statement: No whole-map discard-and-retry: a failing step tries a short fixed ordered list (check, repair locally, retry that piece on its next random stream, simpler shape, substitute, leave out and report) and nothing on the list touches anything outside the failing piece.

The unit of failure is a kernel transaction (a batch), never the map; the pipeline has no restart path (IMPROVEMENTS J-K; D-9); every retry is a rung of the batch's ladder on its own keyed stream (tier 3, keys of §6.1).

References' whole-map retries removed (item 51; J-A51.51): MFCG 12710731 retries all nine stages on an uncuttable polygon continuing one stream (profile-mfcg.md ST-8; 24 restarts in 58 attempts); VG 1.6.9 retries a failed build on the failed seed's next generator state (4 of 27 attempts); NG 1.2.2 rebuilds from seed + 1 on any exception (never observed firing).

Every stochastic step has a declared, bounded, deterministic ladder; every rung taken writes a report line with its cause code and tier (§5.4); the ladder path is replayable from the printed stream key.

Tier 0 feasibility by construction: S1 guarantees river descent, S2 derives stage budgets from demand, S3 sites relative to the river and reserves castle, plaza and institution precincts before any fabric is cut.
Invariants police validity, not regularity: FTG's sheared minority of quads and NG's wedge class are kept.

Every output-changing limit is a work limit, never a time limit, and scales with its scope: each stage declares limits on counts of kernel calls, proposals, candidates, skeleton events and recursion depth as laws over its batch scope's counts, not fixed numbers per rung.
WorkUnit = 'plots' | 'buildings' | 'households' | 'landHa' | 'frameCells' | 'latticeNodes' | 'faces' | 'vertices'.

WorkLimitLaw { counter: string; unit: WorkUnit; perUnit: number; floor: number; log2?: boolean }; limit = floor + perUnit × count(unit, scope); with log2, floor + perUnit × ⌈log2(count)⌉ (recursion depths).
WorkLimits = WorkLimitLaw[]; carried as StageDecl.workLimits (§4.12, §14); coefficients are rows of workLimits.json (§7.6).

count(unit, scope) reads only model values committed before the batch runs (request population via S2 demand and stage quotas, Allocation records, the scope's land area, frame cells or lattice size), never a measurement; a scoped re-run (edit, regeneration, replay) gets exactly the limit its scope had in the full run.
A kernel call that reaches its count returns E_WORK_LIMIT (§3.1), handled as F-WORK (§5.2); the same inputs take the same rungs on every machine.

Work-limit coefficient = 99.9th percentile of measured work per unit on B-CITY-lite × 1.5, computed by the spike or milestone that builds the stage and recomputed whenever the stage's code changes; a change that moves output is a declared shift (§6.4).

Confirmation at M1 then every nightly cost-model run (§13.2): F-WORK hit rate per stage flat across each population band — the rate at the band's top exceeds the bottom's by at most 1 per 1 000 batches. Pre-decided fallback: raise the failing counter's perUnit to the measured 99.9th percentile at the band's top × 1.5 and re-run the sweep.

Wall-clock time is read only by @plat/api's worker host, never by a model package (§6.5); it may postpone or resume a lazy tier (F-BUDGET-TIME) and writes telemetry, never changes what is computed; a tier computed late hashes exactly like one computed at once. §12's millisecond budgets are reporting targets and cost tests, never output-changing limits (J-DET-3, J-DET-25).

Retries are not rerolls: ladder retries (tier 3) draw from the stream key's attempt component, which restarts at 0 with the same cap for every reroll of the scope entity; New random advances the reroll component (§6.1, §7.1), so every reroll has its full ladder.

New random change check: after re-derivation compare each scope entity's content digest with its value before the event; unchanged → advance its reroll (for a rung, the rung's counter, §6.1) once more and re-derive, up to reroll.maxAdvance times; still unchanged → keep the original reroll (nothing changes, not even lineage) and report "no alternative within the ladder". Advances run on the dry run's overlay (§7.1), only the chosen result commits; the event stores the rerolls actually used so replay repeats neither the comparison nor the advances (J-DET-20).
CONTENT DIGEST: the Merkle node of an entity's subtree (§6.2) computed with identity (address, lineage) and lifecycle left out — kinds, geometry and attributes only. Names used: "content digest".
reroll.maxAdvance: a table value, default 3 (maximum extra reroll advances when New random leaves content unchanged).

For a regenerate with rung (item 28) the content compared is the rung's own derived result before and after with identity left out (composition's wings, towers, courts; plan's rooms, walls, openings, roles, units); for an unstored rung both results are derived on the dry run's overlay, the one before read from the elaboration cache when that entry is current (ElaborationChunk, §2.9), neither stored; for an edited rung the stored composition's subtree (§6.2) is compared; an unstored rung lies outside the model subtree, so the building's own content digest could never show the re-roll (J-A28.61).
owner_raw: V02 buildings / V03 interiors (rung content), mechanism determinism

statement: B-EDIT minimal scopes: New random on a block holding one plot, a plot with a one-building row site plan, a one-cell district, a ruined building, a person whose every attribute path is locked, and the plan.roles rung of a one-room plan either changes the scope's content or reports it — never a silent no-op, never an identity change without a content change.

Requested features counted by delivery tier: tier ≤ 3 full, tiers 4-5 degraded, tier 6 omitted; acceptance counts a tier-6 omission of a requested feature as a failure with the bars of §13.5's requested-feature delivery row (§15.2); "no restart path" is a design property, not an acceptance number.

The seven tiers: 0 feasibility by construction; 1 constraint check (typed KernelResult/invariant, nothing committed); 2 local repair (deterministic geometric fix: attract, widen, merge, re-inset, re-claim, re-site); 3 bounded local regeneration (next attempt inside current reroll, ≤ 3 attempts per reroll); 4 simpler primitive (bent cut → straight cut on mean normal → perpendicular mid-run cut; skeleton → sampled medial axis for spine readers / plain roof for roofs); 5 substitution (uncuttable block → court, green or landmark plot, NG's rule); 6 documented omission (feature dropped for this entity, reported, never silent).

Tiers 2-5 run inside the transaction on the overlay; tier 6 commits without the feature; no tier re-runs another stage or re-rolls outside the failing entity's scope because every retry draws from (entity lineage, concern, reroll, attempt) and nothing else reads that stream (§6.1).

FAILURE LADDER / RUNG / TIER: a ladder is the declared ordered list of fallbacks of one failure class; a rung is one step of it; a tier (0-6) is the rung's kind in the seven-tier scale. Names used: "ladder", "fallback ladder" (F-LIGHT, §8.4), "rung", "tier", "ladder use". Note: "rung" is also the ladder-of-detail/elaboration rung (§2.9, item 28) and the population rung (TOWN…METROPOLIS) — three meanings of one word.

Failure class table: each row fixes its class's detection, the order of its rungs (each deterministic from the stream key) and its test; a row marked † names in brackets the section that states how its rungs are computed.

F-NUM precision failure of an optional chain (kernel): detection E_OUT_OF_RANGE, E_BELOW_MIN_EDGE, E_BELOW_MIN_ANGLE, E_SELF_INTERSECT on an optional chain (growth proposals, optional lanes, decorative lines), warnings W_SNAP_PASSES, W_ACUTE_CORNER; ladder: re-propose from the next attempt stream → reject the chain with a report line; mandatory chains never fail for precision (§3.6): E_OUT_OF_RANGE on one is a bug aborting the batch with its stream key; E_LOCKED goes to the dry run (F-EDIT). Test: B-FUZZ at §13.8's sizes against §13.1's bar (O3 a); 0 mandatory chains rejected on B-CITY.

F-CUT bent cut fails (S8, S10): detection E_NOT_TWO_CROSSINGS or a child failing simple/min area/min width/min angle; ladder: reflex pre-cut (a face with a reflex vertex deeper than the band's plot depth split there first, and at antenna roots) → re-plan in the working frame turned by k × 36°, k = 1, 2 (item 39; §4.6 step 8 (a); fresh cut.t draws on the attempt component) → straight cut on the mean normal → the always-succeeding cut perpendicular to the longest side run at its midpoint, clipped to the face's own component, foot sliding along the run until §3.6's contact rule passes (W_CUT_SLID; J-Fredteam-1) → substitution (court, green, landmark or a joined plot for the largest unplaced class of the district's allocation, never live roster state, §4.7) only for faces ≤ 2 × the band's upper block area. Test: on 10^5 random concave and holed faces the ladder ends in ≤ 6 kernel calls and the face count never decreases; court/green residue share reported per district (soft band ≤ 5 %); NG signature regression (§13.5). Baseline: MFCG 19 skipped cuts, 3 of 16 cities restarted.
F-CUT constants: frame turn 36° per attempt, 2 turns; substitution only for faces ≤ 2 × band's upper block area; ≤ 6 kernel calls per ladder; residue soft band ≤ 5 %.

F-CORRIDOR (S9): a face below its class minimum width or area after corridorUnion; ladder: absorbSliver (merge across a partition edge, else keep the face as residue; a structural edge is never deleted) → downgrade the offending lane to alley width → retype the lane invisible and log. Test: B-CITY 0 faces below class minimum width and area; 0 structural edges deleted.

F-OUTLINE (S1: coasts, lakes, islands, sky-island outlines): a displaced closed outline self-intersects or loops; ladder: clamp the displacement → repair by non-zero union → type each resulting loop (islet / pond / absorbed), reported. Test: §13.2's outline stage property test.

F-RIVER (S1, S3, S1's water operator §7.3): descent stalls in a sink, the carve would exceed carveMaxCm, the course leaves the frame before the core, or no crossing site in the core band; ladder: carve the sink deeper up to carveMaxCm → re-trace from the last good knot → move the inlet along the frame edge (attempt) → move the centre to the bank (S3) → declare "no crossing", route arterials to the bank road, report; a requested river island whose branch separation fails is reported "not built"; inside an edit the re-trace is confined to the edited reach and the inlet and centre rungs are not offered (§7.3's S1 rows); a moved course knot is never re-traced away from the user's position (§7.3 (b) 1). Test: 1 000 seeds × {river, coast+river} (WaterSetting spelling, §13.3) × rung: river within the core when requested = 100 % (MFCG baseline 7 of 10 attempts fail at size 80).

F-CONTOUR (S1): a contour level set crosses a shore edge; ladder: the coast construction of §4.2 S1 → clip every contour to the land faces in vector space before emission (always succeeds), reported; never an abort path. Test: steep-coast, cliff and spit fixtures: 0 contours crossing water; 0 S1 aborts.

F-SITE (S3): every candidate fails slope/land/flood tests, or polycentric nuclei closer than the separation floor (§4.2 S3 (6)); ladder: relax the slope threshold one step → the largest land component's centroid band → report; nuclei: re-site the later nucleus (≤ 3) → merge the two under one enceinte with a cross wall, reported. Test: corpus sweep over relief characters; twin-town fixtures (walls apart by the floor, or one enceinte with a cross wall).

F-ROUTE (S4; S5b at k ≥ 2 and in every epoch via S4's router §4.4; S4's local operator §7.3): E_NO_PATH, or an approach cannot meet a pinned bridge deck within the class's minimum radius; ladder: another crossing site on the reach within its search band (one S1 or S3 emitted, a site no way uses yet; river and canal decks; a moat deck is fixed at its gate §4.3; deck perpendicular to local flow) → one bridge at extra cost (a new deck whose two deck_end vertices one L0 batch of two same-level shore splits places, nothing cleared, before the way's L1 batch lays its span; inside an operator whose water is not yet inserted only sites the deck, §4.2 S1 (5)) → relax the slope limit one class → route to the nearest reachable junction and mark the destination unserved in the report (MFCG only logs, O16). Test: scripted requests on 100 seeds with pathological sites; O4 (a): 100 % of through-roads at a named destination or reported; road and deck agree on 100 % of crossings.

F-BUDGET-STAGE (S5): S5d's area test (the stage's grown area against its plot demand at the bands' plot areas); ladder: one bounded top-up before the next stage (widen the stage boundary by the shortfall at the stage's measured plot density, grow only the added ring, recompute the trace) → accept and report the shortfall; the exact plot check after S10 feeds F-SITING. Test: §13.2's B-CITY wealthLevel sweep.

F-WALL (S3 stage 1, S5a, S7): trace self-intersects or crosses the core; a closed trace does not close or an open trace has an end not anchored on shore, bank or cliff; fewer arterial crossings than N; a non-gate way reaches the trace; gates ladder: two gate routes crossing the stage-1 boundary at one point → re-draw the later gate pick (≤ 3) → drop it and report (§4.2 S3 (7)); trace ladder (fixed before growth, gates pinned): re-offset with larger radius → topology-preserving union-simplify (booleans §3.7) → anchor open ends by attraction onto nearest shore, bank or cliff (shared stretch carrying bank and wall, §3.6), adding water gates where the waterfront policy requires a quay wall → divert excess arterials to the nearest gate as lanes → add posterns and report when N cannot be met (N = 0: a declared sealed circuit, harbour gate still built, §4.2 S3 (7)) → cut a way that reaches the wall at the setback band and prune the outer stub, reported. Test: B-CITY gates on arterials 100 %; main gates = N; roads leaving each walled stage = its gate count; 0 non-gate crossings; 100 % quays reachable without crossing a wall except at a gate. MFCG baseline: sealed at 0 main gates, no fallback.

F-CASTLE (S3, S7): compactness < 0.75 or claim overlaps water or plaza; at S3 when the bailey is sited, before the trace welds (§4.8), inside the reservation, in MFCG's order (item 45): thinness bloat (5 % steps while the claim's nearest boundary vertex lies within castle.minInnerM of its centroid, up to the band's top) → equalise toward regularFit (§3.4; ≤ 20 passes, each moving every free vertex 20 % toward target; repaired at compactness ≥ 0.75, unrepaired when a pass gains < 0.001) → re-site (reported) → keep without a bailey (reported). Test: §4.8's castle acceptance; O8 (d).

F-PLOT (S10; re-cuts of §7.1 plot join/split and §4.11's ladder; S11 cluster packing, item 70): frontage < min, wedge angle < 12°, landlocked, or a cluster structure with no door on a footpath reaching an access edge; ladder: per-frontage regions (block skeleton downgrade → reflex pre-cut partition) → merge into neighbour → insert an alley for access, or a covered passage under the front building where §4.6 allows (item 30), rung skipped on the underground arena (II.7.3 U2) → typed residue (court/vacant); a cluster structure without a connected door re-packed once at the packer's next free site, else dropped and reported, its households re-housed by §4.7's overflow pass, never omitted; a plot too narrow for a trunk and one structure depth takes the hovel arrangement, reported; a hidden plot passes with an access chain through passage, alley and court faces. Test: every plot ≥ 1 access edge (100 %), every hidden plot its chain, 0 landlocked buildings, same after every re-cut, every cluster structure with its own door on a connected footpath. NG baseline ≈ 42 % frontage-less leaves (courts by construction, item 42).
Minimum plot wedge angle 12°.

F-SITING (S10a band-range re-homing §4.5 (5); S10b; S11 overflow pass): eager allocation cannot place a class's demand in its affinity district; S10a re-homing finds no district for a household filling no dossier population (housed at nearest range, J-A72.50); a post-build request (§7.7) finds no plot inside the hard rows; S11's overflow pass finds no residential building with room. Ladder: reconcile inside the district's allocation (JOIN at block granularity → whole block → district edge; cross-district moves only in S7b's reconcile and S10a's re-homing) → item's soft rows to weight 0 → reduce the manifest lowest-priority classes first, never a dossier-backed item (item 20: goes to its first closest option — fewest hard rows failed, then best score — failed hard rows reported, never omitted, §7.7 precedence), report naming each unplaced item's blocking hard rows and closest options; an unhousable household takes the last rung alone (manifest reduced, reported with refusing capacities, no re-cut after S11), never one filling a dossier population (§7.7 item 2; §4.7 re-provides via the dossier request, which always places, J-A20.42); decided eagerly, never by lazy placement order, never silently. Test: O18 (f) 100 % institutions on a plot meeting their requirement; §4.5 S7b (3) acceptance; derived-complete digest across district orders (§6.5 (9)); every dossier-backed element placed (§5.3); every S2 household housed or reported, every dossier-population household housed (§13.2 T19-4).

F-SITEPLAN (S11; terrain operator §7.3): setbacks leave no rectangle ≥ the class minimum, or after a terrain stroke a row footprint's fall exceeds skirtMaxCm; ladder: on slopes above skirtMaxCm stepped wings first → lower coverage one step → next arrangement (compound → detached → hovel → tents row where the class allows) → vacant plot typed yard, reported. Test: O17 (f) (§15.2); 0 renderer fallback rectangles.

F-PLAN room programme does not fit its wings — plan rung (BuildingGenerator.plan, §2.6, stage 3, staged — row is its hook), per building, and every step of a re-cut along the interior ladder (item 28 (f), §7.3). Tier 0: storey allocation places household units first at their ladder row's unit form, falling to the next poorer form down to the single room, then trims the rest to wing capacity soft rooms first, reported. Tier 1: §13.2 plan bars fail on the overlay (hard room missing, room unreachable, unit without own door onto circulation or street, piece below minimum area, seed or fixed ring refused by tileRings/transientArena — E_DEGENERATE detail seed/fixed/overlap). Tier 2: merge under-size pieces, slide a cut to its neighbour's minimum, answer a refusal by the ring refused (a kept room leaves the kept set and is re-cut, address carried by §6.3 re-match; a stair bay or chimney stack re-placed by §2.6 step 3 at the next candidate of its filtered order, deterministic, no stream; no further candidate → tier 6: chimney omitted with hearth room kept, stair bay's upper storeys unreached and the building flagged; a seed ring, passage room or composer's room refusal is a bug aborting the rung with its stream key, J-A28.73); swap two rooms' storeys. Tier 3: storey layout re-run on next attempt (≤ 3, plan.layout, §6.1). Tier 4: bisect on the wing's axes. Tier 5: soft room absorbed into neighbour or a generic room, never a household unit. Tier 6: a hard room omitted and reported, never a household unit (capacity bounded upstream by §2.6; a rung that cannot cut that many single rooms is a bug aborting the rung, J-A28.51). Nothing outside the building touched. Test: §13.2 B-PLAN: hard rooms 100 %, every household housed in own unit with own door, every room reachable, stairs stacked, walls equal the wing rings.
owner_raw: V03 interiors (plan rung staged; this row is its hook) / determinism

statement: F-UNDER underground plot under excluded ground: a plot sample (vertices, frontage midpoint, 1 m sample of its rear line) lies in an excluded ground face (water, harbour, wall strip, gate, keep, reservation, surface footprint: II.7.3's list), read by pointLocate on the ground PlatKey, never a write; ladder: band depth → band's lower depth → class minimum depth → a vacant run, reported; a network run needing more fall than the ground gives is re-routed toward the nearer outfall, never trenched (II.7.2). Test: 0 committed underground faces with a sample in an excluded face (CI: 1 m sample grid by pointLocate); fixtures §13.2.
owner_raw: V04 underground (staged; row is its hook)

statement: F-VOID underground system or undercity cannot be laid: a system's extent finds no admissible ground in its depth band (no stone cells, no soluble or volcanic rock, cover below minCoverM); an undercity neighbourhood's void below minimum capacity (UndercityRule minHouseholds, mainChamberM2) or without a lifeline (II.7.5 condition 4); ladder: smaller extent inside the band → system omitted, reported; undercity: fewer neighbourhoods inside the 1-3 bound, each dropped neighbourhood's allocation re-placed by S7b's reconcile → no undercity, reported — never a household dropped (S7b (7)). Test: §13.2 T65 fixtures: undercity only where a void source exists and a lifeline reaches it; bound on 500 seeds per rung; population whole.

statement: F-SKELETON (S1, S11, S13a, plan rung): output validator fails (non-planar, non-monotone faces, inconsistent heights) or the skeleton's work limit (events processed) reached — E_WORK_LIMIT, never a timeout; each reader takes its typed downgrade: spine readers (label spines §9.3, S1's coast simplicity clamp §4.2 S1 (2), plan rung's room-label spines and room lights §2.6) → sampled medial axis; roofs → plain roof (no ridge or hip lines, roof kind plain, heights unchanged); near-rectangular footprints never reach this row (exact OBB roof is primary, §3.8); the regions reader (S10) takes F-PLOT's ladder. Test: §13.1 ladder-coverage fixtures.

F-LABEL (S13b view side): the spine is shorter than the text at minimum size, or an unresolved collision at priority; ladder: §9.4's seven rungs, each counted in the report; placement is view data and never changes the model (§9.1). Test: §9.4's acceptance by B-ZOOM (§13.4).

F-LIGHT (item 68; view: tile worker and compositor, outside model packages): no GPU context, a lost context, or the pass over its frame budget (§12.5); ladder: GPU field → half-resolution light buffer → vector pass (§8.2 shadowPass) with glow sprites; each rung counted in view telemetry, never an error and never a model change; exports, stills and goldens always take the CPU reference (§8.4). Test: §13.4's fallback run renders a frame on every rung; the CPU reference byte-identical across engines (§6.5 (9)).

F-WORK operation count reached (any stage, ladder or kernel call): E_WORK_LIMIT — a declared count reached (candidates, proposals, kernel calls, skeleton events, recursion depth), each the stage's law over its batch scope (§5.1 (5)); ladder: the stage's declared coarser rung, entered by the count, never by time (fewer candidates, larger cells, shallower recursion) → report work_cut with the count; the map is valid and identical on every machine. Test: time dilation (§6.5 (9)) per-stage digests byte-identical; work-cut rate per stage reported on B-CITY; hit rate flat across each band.

F-BUDGET-TIME (reporting and scheduling only; @plat/api worker host outside model packages): wall-clock watchdog; postpone or resume a lazy tier (cancel-and-resume only); telemetry records time_over; never a model change. Test: a tier postponed and resumed hashes like the eager tier; per-stage timing against §12 in CI telemetry on reference hardware.

F-EDIT constraint conflict (S0, edits): detection list — a drawn way crosses a locked entity; a targeted assignment names a locked entity; a map event without EditBase.dossier that would close, remove or re-designate a dossier-backed element (§7.7 item 2); an assignment not honourable within drift bounds; a post-build placement (assignment, placeAt, rejectSite re-placement) no plot satisfies inside the hard rows, or a user's placeAt over its disruption budget; a plot join/split that would remove an occupied building (item 31); a plan edit leaving a room below minimum area or unreachable, a plan edit or setRoomUnit leaving a unit without its own door, a hand relet above §2.6 capacity; a hand edit whose capacity re-homing cannot place its excess; a heights edit leaving a base wing spanning a passage below two floors (Passage.headroomCm, item 30); a warp breaking an invariant or carrying a locked/pinned point-anchored record out of its host face; an effective scope holding protected entities whose fate is not kept; undo/redo whose target has dependent live events, or undo of a creation event, a dossier event or an epoch that carried one; a water edit's new channel ⊕ bank setback meeting a locked/pinned way, wall, finer entity or reservation; a moved course knot whose carve exceeds carveMaxCm; a map event that would change a dossier-owned value (name/kind of a dossier-named element or quarter, knownTo, concealment, front or powers weights, an assignment's state, a collective count outside its range, an adjust of a dossier-bound population or a dossier-supplied slice value; reason dossier-owned, J-A20.77); an addUndergroundAccess whose closure ends in a refusal (terrain rules out every basement form, connector route over its bound, underground stages not built; item 66); an authoring declaration contradicting a lock or a dossier fact (item 101); a Works edit leaving a plot without access or occupants unhoused (item 67); a table cell outside its column's declared range (jitter.minM among them); a host provider's output passing §2.9's cap; an upgrade's pack copy passing that cap (§7.5). Ladder: the dry run returns the conflict as an action (per case: the refusal with reason and the map's own alternative — label display text/visibility, viewer knowledge key, a count inside the range; nearest lawful basement form or the refusal naming its cause; lock/dossier fact with closest acceptable declarations (item 20 (g)); nearest valid position; blocking lock; closest sites with failed hard rows and disruption over budget; rejectSite / placeAt; vacate first or demolition as a fate; fate list to confirm; dependent events to undo first (never a dossier event or an epoch that carried one); unassign or rejectSite+placeAt in place of undo of a creation/dossier/epoch; Re-derive from S3 for a reservation; provider and size or pack with "keep the old model"), decided by §7.7's precedence order; never silently resolved. Test: B-EDIT sequences and conflict fixtures: 0 planarity violations, 0 lost faces, 0 silent re-binds.

F-REDERIVE coarse re-derivation invalidates finer content or crossings (§7.3's local operators: S1 water and terrain, S4, S5, S6, S7): detection — a plot, footprint or yard in new water, in a new corridor, across a moved wall band or outside its new cell; a way that new water ⊕ bank setback will meet off a deck (found before insertion); a deck span no longer over water; a crossing site whose bank vertices no longer stand on a shore of its reach. Ladder — plots and buildings: re-cut along the new boundary (ids by anchor rule §6.3) → re-fit its site plan (F-SITEPLAN) → demolish what still conflicts with a lifecycle event caused by the edit. A way new water will meet off a deck (decided in the L1 batch of S1's water operator or a carve, before L0 insertion): a kept way (arterial, sole connection of streets beyond to a gate or plaza per §4.11, or a way that crossed the changed water on a deck) is re-routed through a deck within the detour bound (re-routed length between nearest pinned nodes ≤ 1.4 × old length); every other way is cut at the bank setback, each land part stays a way (the part keeping the old anchor keeps the address, the other is fresh), a stub shorter than the district's minimum block width ending at the setback is removed. A deck over land: Bridge becomes a tombstone (demolish, cause the edit), span stays as an ordinary segment of the way's class (the higher of the two joined where it was a separate bridge way) or leaves with the way; deck and deck_end rows removed (removeEdges on ChainRef('deck', bridge) and its two VertexRef('deck_end', bridge, i)), demotion takes bank vertices to the way's level and clears kernel pins (§2.2 rule 3). A site over land: its deck_end rows removed and its record tombstoned (§2.7). Every re-cut, demolition, re-route, cut and pruned stub listed in the fate report with its lifecycle event; a locked or pinned entity is never demolished, re-routed or cut — its conflict returns as F-EDIT. Test: the coarse-edit oracle, §7.3 item 7 (v).
Detour bound: a kept way's re-routed length between its nearest pinned nodes on either side of the water ≤ 1.4 × the old length.

Every invariant declares a scope: batch-local (evaluated on the batch's touched faces plus their one-ring and on the records it created, changed or removed), stage-end (once when a stage or its scoped re-run completes), save and load (when a document is written or verified), CI-only (test harnesses); only batch-local ones run per batch.

An edit's dry run (§7.1) evaluates its batch-local and stage-end invariants once on the scratch overlay and the commit reuses that result (the overlay is committed as validated): one validation per edit, not two.

For an edit whose operators chain several batches (§7.3 item 3) the batch-local rows are evaluated once after the chain's last batch over the union of the chain's touched faces, their one-ring and touched records (a river move places decks' bank vertices in an L1 batch before its L0 batch inserts water, so the deck row holds only at the chain's end); the kernel invariants (first row) still hold at every batch, so each chained batch keeps every way and enceinte one connected chain (§7.3 (b) 3).
The kernel invariants (§3.10) — batch-local, checked on the commit record's faces, edges and role keys (§3.3, §3.10).
Class floors: minimum width / area / angle per class (never minEdge used as a face floor) — batch-local, on touched faces.
No footprint overlap — batch-local, touched footprints against the spatial index.

A basement lies inside and is smaller than its ground storey's wings; a basement other than a crawl space never under the flood band or below the water table (§2.6 terrain gate, item 29); a crawl space (kind 'crawl') only where the lowest terrain sample under its footprint lies above the water table (§2.6 requested-mode ladder, item 66); a basement never joins a tunnel — a cellar stair to one is an AccessPoint (II.7.3). Batch-local, touched buildings.

Every dossier-backed element (assignment with existence 'dossier', §7.7) is live and placed on every map, or present as its ruin while its assignment's state is ruined (item 80: use closed, building standing in ruined existence); a delete never removes it, F-SITING never drops it, a rejection re-places it, no map event closes, removes or re-designates it (§7.7 item 2), no epoch step closes it or leaves it without its building (§4.11 Dossier content across epochs). Scope: batch-local (assignments touched), stage-end (each epoch event: every dossier-backed assignment), save; checked by the assignment index against live placements.

Coherence (item 20 (h) (iii); §7.7): no derived fact contradicts a dossier fact — every dossier record the map carries is placed or present as its ruin; every dossier count met within its tolerance (population by §4.11's roster tolerance); every dossier kind, name and membership unchanged on the element its binding key names; realm-level trade facts are the trade slice's (§7.7 layer 2). Stage-end: every derivation, each dossier event and each epoch that carries one; checked by the dossier facts by binding keys (Document.dossier) against the named elements.
The stored binding (Document.dossier, §7.7, item 74) equals the binding rebuilt by folding the log's dossier events — load and CI-only, compared row by row.

A stored plan's storeys tile the extents of the wings that reach them — at the ground storey with the span ring of each passage a wing spans, the passage room (stage-3 contract's fourth rung, §2.6; J-A30.23): each exterior wall segment on an extent's edge, each room ring simple and within its wing's extent or the span ring, no overlap, no gap (§3.10's seed-tiling row, per storey). Batch-local: buildings whose stored composition the batch wrote or carried.

Interior ladder (item 28 (f), §2.6): in every stored plan, and every cached plan at derivation, each household unit has its own entry door onto circulation (corridor, stair hall or landing) or the street and never opens through another unit's room; a re-cut along the ladder changes no wing ring, stair core, entrance, hearth, chimney stack, passage room or basement ring — the shell's leaf digest (wings, heights, entrances, roof, basement), rings read with the composition-role vertices a stored plan's re-cut adds removed (§2.6, J-P48 (1)), is byte-identical across it. Scope: batch-local (a stored plan re-cut, §7.3); at derivation on the transient arena for a cached plan (F-PLAN tier 1). Checked by the room graph walked door by door per unit; shell digest before and after.

No building houses more households than its capacity: Building.households ≤ capacity(b) (§2.6's one capacity function) after every committed change — generation fill (§4.7), relet (§4.11) and every change §2.6's capacity rule lists, whose excess §4.7's overflow pass re-homes inside the causing event (J-A28.23, J-A28.46). Scope: batch-local (buildings whose wings, heights, class, plot builtBand or household count the batch wrote, and re-homing receivers); stage-end (S11 per district after the overflow pass; each epoch event; a §7.6 table edit's re-derived set).

A live-in dwelling stays among its building's households: Building.dwelling, where present, names one of Building.households and is present only while its use is a live-in class's (§10.2 liveIn; J-A28.29), after every committed change. Stage-end (S11 per district after overflow; each epoch; every edit at its dry run).

A mutation's kept parts keep their addresses and its added parts are minted from the causing event (§4.7 S11, §6.3); after a plot join or split the party walls agree on both sides and every plot keeps its class minimums (item 31). Batch-local: plots of the mutation or re-cut and their one-ring.

Declared means held (item 101, §7.2): no re-derivation, scoped re-roll or epoch moves or removes an entity its declaring event pinned; only a later declaration, an unpin or its declaring event's undo changes it. Batch-local (every re-derivation's scope), checked by the scope's declared set before and after by address.

Epoch rows (item 31, §4.11): no occupied building removed by a band change (redevelopment first vacates via item 17's relocation); across the epoch the ladder's rungs 1-2 change no frontage edge and shrink or re-cut no building shell toward a poorer band (shell = wings, heights, entrances, roof, basement, rings read without composition-role vertices); their only geometry is rung 1's yard buildings (densify/thin … infill) and rung 2's densify … back_court split or thin … back_court reversal; every other change of a plot ring or building shell carries the lifecycle event of its step (rung-3 event, designation or renovation mutation (item 18), any ConversionOp — decline, terrain-and-water, island, carve, wallToWay, contractWall — or the growth step's own changes); every plot's geometry band ≥ its floor (max(field band, geometryFloor), J-A31.75). Stage-end (each epoch event), checked by touched plots' frontage edges and shell subtrees against pre-epoch values.

Works (§4.11, item 67): at no stage of a Works is a plot left without an access edge (old line kept as a pending bound until its clearing stage, new line in place before occupants move in); occupants rehoused by item 17's relocation before demolition or conversion begins; a Works' drawn stage is derived from its record and the week, never stored (§6.2). Batch-local (Works an event started, changed or cancelled, and their plots); stage-end (each epoch).

Decline and staged layers (§4.11, II.6, II.7): a cleared building's footprint face persists; no EvolutionStrategy plan contains demolish on a tunnel; every island in state floating has supported area > 0; U1 (sewer part 0; U1-U3 are its rules, J-A65.42): every underground plot's frontage rows on the kerb of exactly one navigable open tunnel run, access rows ⊆ frontage rows; U2: underground L1 carries tunnel chains only, no way chain and no alley face on L1 or L3; U3: every underground building's frontage side on its plot's frontage edge; ≥ 1 access point per underground neighbourhood; every AccessPoint.ground.at in public ground, a yard, outside ground (a mouth) or a surface building — a cellar_stair only where II.7.3 admits one (undergroundAccess.prob > 0 at its band, or a secret plot), a basement access only in its building's basement (item 64); never in water or a wall strip; no committed underground plot sample in an excluded ground face (F-UNDER); underground stages' commit records show 0 writes on the ground PlatKey, each writes only its own system's part except the far link_end vertices the connection stage places, keeps or strips by one transaction per part (§3.4). Scopes: batch-local (U1, U3, trace face, island area; surface exclusion); stage-end (U2, access rows, tunnel-demolish lint over an engine plan); CI-only (cross-arena write count).
owner_raw: V04 underground / V05 sky / pipeline II.6-II.7

statement: Basement accesses (II.7.3, item 64): an access of source basement only where its building's basement ring lies within UndergroundRule.access.reachM of the open element it reaches (open navigable tunnel kerb, underground building's side or rear wall, another system's open gallery or chamber); a building with a concealed use holds its accesses knownTo 'secret'; an access's stored state is open, locked or bricked, and reads collapsed only while its element is closed (II.6). Batch-local; checked by kernel read services on the element's part (J-A12.32).

Underground systems and undercity (item 65): undercity only where a void source exists and a lifeline reaches it; never more neighbourhoods than the rung row's maxNeighbourhoods (TOWN rarely 1, CITY 1-2, METROPOLIS ≤ 3); every underground building's heights under its chamber's ceiling less ceilingClearCm; every UndergroundLink typed, carrying knownTo, one end a link_end vertex of one part and the other of the other, never a vertex two parts share. Batch-local and stage-end (undercity stage; connection stage).

Closures (§7.3 item 9, item 66): every piece a closure created is named in its event's closure record, every named piece exists, and a generated connector is reachable end to end inside its system's depth band. Batch-local (the closure's batches).

Every plot has ≥ 1 access edge; every building has exactly one main entrance on the footprint side facing its plot's frontage access edge (court or path from the street gate for a set-back building, passage or court for a hidden plot, its footpath for a cluster structure; §2.6 rule 1; items 29, 50, 70), a side or rear entrance only where the plot has an access edge beyond the frontage (§2.6 rule 2); a hidden plot (Plot.exposure = 'hidden', §2.5) is reachable by a chain of access edges through passage, alley and court faces to a public corridor, an access edge on a sealed passage (Passage.sealed) skipped so a sealed plot reads sealed (item 30; J-A30.71; walk uses faceNeighbours §3.4). Batch-local and stage-end (S10, after every join/split and §4.11 re-cut).

Concealed institutions (§4.7, item 63): every institution or assignment with concealment other than none is placed in one of its allowed modes — underground only in an underground allocation (II.7.3, S7b (6)) or undercity neighbourhood (II.7.5), front with its front's building built to the front's template, hidden on a hidden plot — and its concealed rooms reachable only from its concealed entrance or its front's service side, never through public rooms. Stage-end (S10b, S11 per district); batch-local (buildings an edit re-fits).

Informal clusters (item 70): every cluster structure has its own door on a footpath face connected to one of its plot's access edges; every pair keeps its row's fire gap; each structure's households lie within its row; no cluster on a plot whose geometry floor is middle or above while that stock stands, nor in a district whose band range excludes the squalid band (§4.5). Batch-local.
No way centreline crosses a footprint; no way crosses a reservation (§4.2 S3). Batch-local.
Walls are not crossed by ways except at gates. Batch-local.

A way crosses water only on a deck, and a deck only over water: every way-role edge whose two side faces' L0 parents are water belongs to a Bridge's deck span (edges between its two deck vertices, carrying deck; fords included) or to a harbour work; every deck span crosses a water face with both ends on its banks; a wall trace crosses water only at a water gate. Batch-local, by index (§2.2 rule 2); covers S1 river decks, S3 moat and canal decks, S5a outer-moat decks, a carve's decks and S7's harbour furniture; §13.2's harbour fixtures include a two-arm mole and a detached breakwater.

HARBOUR WORK: a way of class pier or quay whose connected set of pier and quay edges meets land in at most one L0 land face (a pier, mole or breakwater arm rooted on one shore; a detached breakwater touching none, §4.8) — it stands in the water rather than crossing it; a pier or quay way joining two land faces across water crosses on a deck like any way; checked by one walk of connected pier/quay edges counting distinct L0 land faces (a few hundred edges at most).

NF-P5: no lane crosses a wall strip, and no L3 band, setback, glacis, tower or gatehouse face is cleared or split by an L1 or L2 batch — in every generation batch and every edit batch except for enceintes whose wall-strip parts the edit's chain declares it rebuilds (S10's step (0)) or removes. The dry run of every chained edit computes that declaration (each enceinte "rebuilt" or "removed") and every batch carries it; the check reads the declaration, never a list of edit kinds. Declaring edits: a tree-scoped re-derivation of a scope holding wall-strip faces (§7.3 item 2); S7's operator (drawWall, moved trace vertex, re-traced run, gateToJunction); S1's water operator for every strip its L1 batch changes (§7.3 (b) 3, 7, 8); a carve for every strip its batches (1)-(3) change and its step 4 re-derives (§4.11); as removals wallToWay, contractWall (§4.11) and an enceinte's delete. A lane still never crosses a strip (J-DET-39). Checks: touched lanes against setback and wall edges; removed/changed L3 faces against declared enceintes; a CI registry test fails when an edit operator or conversion that can write a wall strip's L1 lines or L3 parts has no declaration path; §13.2 fixtures: a canal carved across a wall between two towers and a river move cutting a glacis line commit with 0 violations, a drawWay lane across a strip is refused.
Footprints ∩ (wall band ⊕ setback) = ∅ on both faces of every wall. Batch-local.

Every building's wing rings (and a stored composition's composed wings) pass §2.6's wing rule 4 after every carry, in generation and in edits; checked by rule 4's tiered test (≈ 0.06-2.7 µs a building). Batch-local.
Water ∩ footprints = ∅. Batch-local.
Every built bridge within ± 10° of the channel normal, measured on the deck and on the way; a site has no span and is outside every deck row (§2.7). Batch-local.
Exclusive land uses never overlap. Batch-local, touched land-use faces.

Every LightSource (§2.7, item 68) stands in its host's faces on its host's arena (a door light, standing on its footprint ring, within half a lattice diagonal of that ring's nearest edge, either side; §2.2 rule 3, §7.4), its height within its rule row's band; no light lit on a building whose Works stands before its finished stage (record kept, unlit). Batch-local; pointLocate on the host's PlatKey (door light: squared distance to the nearest edge ≤ ½ cm² in exact integer arithmetic).

Reference integrity: every reference out of a touched record (people, relations and uses included: a dependent's carer resolves; a building's use and a use's buildings resolve both ways, §2.7) names a live id; every reference into a record the batch removed is carried over (§6.3) or reported as an orphan. Batch-local via the reverse-reference index.
Identity: every fresh address differs from every live and tombstoned address, and no two live entities share a lineage key (§6.3); O(1) at mint against the identity set.
Every length field carries a unit (§2.1); at schema write and §2.1's lint.
Every stored geometry reference resolves; no geometry carries a dead entity (§3.10). Stage-end and save, via the kernel's reverse indexes.

Every gate joined to the network and the plaza; the roads leaving each walled stage equal its gate count (its N main gates, plus a harbour gate of §4.2 S3 (7) where one was placed — a sealed town's or the detour guard's); an outer enceinte's gates ≥ its arterial crossings; a coastal town's harbour joined to its plaza through a gate, crossing a moat only on a deck (§4.2 S3 (11)). Stage-end (S7), one graph search per enceinte.
Every gate and weld vertex on its trace; stage 1's trace within its distance bound of the stage-1 boundary (§4.2 S3 (9)). Stage-end (S5).
Every baseLane portal matches one S8 lane end and vice versa, spaced by the portal gap (§4.6 (7)). Stage-end (S8), Seam records against lanes' end vertices.
Every quay reachable from the town without crossing a wall except at a gate. Stage-end (S7, S9), one graph search.
No branch re-joins its parent within k segments (§4.4). Stage-end (S5), per growth stage.
A sealed enclosure only when declared. Stage-end (S7), per trace.
Contours never cross a shore — a check of F-CONTOUR's clip construction, never an abort path. Stage-end (S1).
Names unique within their kind's scope (§9.6); a new entity never renames an existing one; a generated name changes only by one of §6.3's draw cases. Stage-end (S13a), per naming run.

Neighbourhood character (§4.5, item 72): one district per district-defining dossier instance; every building's prosperity-driven state inside its district's band range; a shared building's partition weights sum to one over its powers and over its sectors; the character vector and band range recomputed from committed state equal the maintained ones. Stage-end (S12c; each epoch's character step); load (the recomputation); checked against the dossier's district-defining instances, bands against ranges, vector recomputed from lots (J-DET-12).
Every requested feature (river through the core, N gates, a harbour when coastal, …) delivered, degraded or omitted and reported with its tier (§5.1 (7)). Stage-end, via the report's requested list.
Containment complete: building ⊂ plot ⊂ block ⊂ district, 100 %. Stage-end, per-batch containment counters summed, not a model walk.
The canonical document validates against its schema (Recipe.salts keyed by rerollable concerns only, §6.1); the recorded digests are the maintained model and records roots (§6.2). Save, at write.

Load: the decoded snapshot's roots and chunk hashes pass §2.9 step 3's checks (a frozen view: chunk hashes only, §2.9 step 2), by §2.9 step 3's recomputation before the first edit or §6.2 (iii)'s off-edit-path one; and the replayed model and records roots equal the recorded ones (verification replay, §2.9).

CI-only: a full recomputation of the model tree's and records tree's roots from their leaves equals the maintained root (§6.2), on every B-CITY generation and B-EDIT sequence (the digest-maintenance oracle); digests equal across platforms, under time dilation, under district permutation (derived-complete digest) and replay = session (§6.5 (9), §7.3 item 7).
Label collisions are not a model invariant: placement is view data; its "0 collisions" is tested by B-ZOOM (§9.4).

Hard invariants abort the batch, which rolls back to the previous arena version while its ladder continues; soft ones (statistics bands) go to the report; CI counts hard violations per 1 000 cities and requires 0 (O3 b).

Cost rule: validating a batch costs O(touched faces × log n), never O(model); per-edit validation time for a fixed scope flat from TOWN to METROPOLIS within ± 20 % (cost test §13.2: TOWN → CITY at M2a; TOWN → METROPOLIS at M2b, which measures METROPOLIS, generated from M1 on, §16). Pre-decided fallback: an invariant whose batch-local check breaks the flat cost moves to stage-end scope — still hard, checked later in the same stage.

GenerationReport { outputVersion; stages[] { name: StageId; work: Record<string, number> (operation counts against declared work limits); attempts; ladderUses[] { cause; rung; tier 0-6; entity: Id; key (stream key textual form, §6.1) }; invariants[] { name; scope 'batch'|'stage'|'save'|'ci'; pass; count } }; requested[] { feature; delivered 'full'|'degraded'|'omitted'; tier; entity?; cause? }; requestedVsBuilt: Diff[]; autoResolved[] { param; value; reason; layer: OverrideLayer }; unserved: Id[]; unplaced: Id[]; dossier[] { element; state 'placed'|'rejectedSite'|'blocked'; site?; rules? (failed hard rows); closest? }; changes: ReportEntry[]; kernel { engine (§3.7); warnings: Record<string, number>; downgrades; workLimitHits } }.

Kernel warnings counted in the report: W_ATTRACTED, W_STRETCH_SHARED, W_WEDGE_ROUTED, W_SNAP_PASSES, W_ACUTE_CORNER, W_SLIVER_RETYPED, W_HEIGHT_CLAMPED, W_CUT_SLID (§3.1; F-CUT's foot slide, J-Fredteam-1).

ReportEntry = { seq (causing event); epoch (0 before the first); change? { changeId; reason? } (item 75, a dossier event's DossierChange) } & one of: { kind 'reject'|'lapse'|'place'; element; site } | { kind 'open'|'close'|'relocate'; use; from?; to? } | { kind 'mutate'; plot; mutation (index into EditBase.mutations) } | { kind 'disruption'; overBudget } | { kind 'rename'; id; from; to (an epoch's district rename past identity hysteresis, §6.3 case (5), item 72) } | { kind 'works'; works; op 'start'|'cancel'|'finish' (item 67) }.
Telemetry { stageMs: Record<StageId, number>; timeOver: StageId[]; verifyMs? } — session-only, never saved, never in any digest.

The report is a derived cache: rebuilt by every derivation and by the verification replay on load, saved only in the document's derived section so the panel can show it before verification finishes, and excluded from the canonical form and every digest.
The report records stream keys only for ladder uses (any rung from tier 2 up, retries at attempt > 0 included), not for every stream used; every ladder use is replayable from its printed key.
Timings are telemetry: measured by the worker host outside the model packages, shown by the UI; nothing saved or hashed contains a millisecond.
The same GenerationReport object is the UI's compact dismissable panel (O16) and the API's report(doc).

A dossier event's or a positive placement's own consequences (what moved, was joined or vacated, why) are that event's disruption report (EditBase.disruption, §7.3 item 4, §7.7), stored in the event; the report's dossier list is the standing state shown after any derivation.

The changes list is the report's account of what moved — every placement, rejection and lapse (§7.7), every use opened, closed or relocated (§4.11, item 17), every mutation record (§4.7 S11), every disruption report (§7.1), each naming the event whose record holds the detail; recomputed in seq order by the whole report (derived, never stored); it is what §11.2's report.changed delivers (the entries appended since its last delivery) — the host's one account of every move, closing and reopening (J-A22.75); an entry a dossier event caused names its changeId and reason (item 75) and nothing flows back (J-A20.81); an epoch's renames and each Works' start, cancellation and completion are entries (items 72, 67).

A dossier the port refuses — population outside the ladder, below the 1 500-person floor or above the 120 000 cap, E_RUNG_UNAVAILABLE (§7.7 item 15, item 81; J-A81.01) — makes no model (or at an absorb no event) and nothing in the report; the refusal is the port's result (§14), never a report entry.

BATCH-LOCAL / STAGE-END / SAVE / LOAD / CI-ONLY: the five invariant scopes (report encodes 'batch'|'stage'|'save'|'ci'). Note: GenerationReport's scope enum has four values ('batch','stage','save','ci') while §5.3 names five scopes (load has no enum value).
DOSSIER-BACKED ELEMENT: an assignment with existence 'dossier' (§7.7) and the element it places; also called "dossier element", "dossier-backed item", "dossier record".

DOSSIER-OWNED value: a value the dossier supplied which no map event may change (refusal reason 'dossier-owned'): name or kind of a dossier-named element or quarter, knownTo, concealment, front or powers weights the dossier set, an assignment's state, a collective count outside its range, an adjust of a dossier-bound population or of a dossier-supplied slice value (§7.7 item 11; J-A20.77).
Text defect: "what moved, wasjoined or vacated" — missing space ("was joined").

The same seed always makes the same town on any computer; the stability promise excludes a release that changes an early step (towns built on it change and the release says so stage by stage); an edited town keeps its edits across such changes because addresses are permanent and separate from random streams.
RNG engine: xoshiro128** per stream (four 32-bit words; period 2^128 − 1; fast in JS, no BigInt).
Keys are mixed from structured components, never from strings (K-6 / R-1 kept); no string is built on the generation path.

Seed key (128 bits) derived once from the seed by four 32-bit-lane finalisers with distinct salts (all Math.imul); entity key = mix of seed key, lineage hash (§6.3) and arena key (layer and part, §2.2), computed once at mint and cached in the arena beside the lineage hash.

Town-level draws (S0's feature draws, terrain noise, per-document furniture — compass and emblem, §9.5) use the town root's entity key: the seed key mixed with the fixed town lineage (ground arena, no parent, creation epoch 0, index 0), so they depend on the recipe alone and never on docId. Paint programs and furniture pass the reserved stage id STAGE_VIEW (0xffff) to the one mixer (§14 Rng.stream).

Stream key = one finaliser round over the entity key combined with the packed components (stage id u16, concern id u16, reroll u16, attempt u8, epoch u16, salt u16); its four words seed the state directly (all-zero state replaced by a fixed nudge); a stream is created once per derivation and continued, and a second request in the same derivation returns the same stream. Textual form for reports only: S11/siteplan@plot:7kq2m9x4c1b0a/arrangement[/r=1][/a=2][/e=0], rendered from the same components.

Stream key budget ≤ 0.1 µs per key (string paths measured 0.73 µs); measured by the M0 (d) determinism spike over a B-CITY city; pre-decided fallback: derive a batch's stream keys in one vectorised pass over a typed array (output-neutral, no golden moves).

SEED KEY / ENTITY KEY / STREAM KEY / TOWN ROOT / RENDER KEY: the three key levels of the RNG (seed → entity → stream), the town root's entity key for town-level draws, and the render key (low 64 bits of the entity key).
Component lineage: the entity's stream identity, its lineage key (§6.3); a surviving entity keeps it, so nothing that survives is re-rolled.
Component concern: what the draw is for (registry, 0146-0147); streams are never shared across concerns.

Component reroll: the scope entity's New random count, an absolute number stored in its identity and written into the regenerate event as an explicit per-entity map (the rerolls actually used, §5.1 (6)); children draw with their derivation unit's reroll, so New random on a block changes that block's plots and nothing else.

Stage-3 rungs (item 28) are their own derivation units, one reroll counter per regenerate.rung value: wings, rooms, plan, plan.layout, plan.roles, plan.furnish (coarsest first); their streams (plan.* and the composition's concerns) carry S11's stage id (for an underground building, the underground stage's S11 run, II.7.3), which a transient arena's batches carry too (§3.3); each counter is absolute, advanced only by a regenerate naming its rung, stored in that event's map under <building id>#<rung>; a rung's reroll is the count as the log gives it, never a field of the elaboration record (§2.8), so a replay rebuilds it and the cache can be dropped any time (§6.2).

A stage-3 concern's stream mixes the counters of its own level and every coarser level through the one mixer (§14 Rng.stream): coarser counters folded into the building's key, one finaliser round per level in rung order, and the concern's own counter is its reroll component — plan.program reads #wings, #rooms, #plan; plan.layout those and #plan.layout; plan.roles those and #plan.roles; plan.furnish all six; the composition's own concerns (stage 3's, appended when stage 3 registers them) read #wings, and at rooms also #rooms. A finer re-roll leaves coarser streams unchanged (layout keeps wings, entrances, stair core; roles move no wall); a coarser one re-rolls everything below (J-A28.61).
A user's reroll count (a rung's counter included) is capped at 32 767; rerolls from 32 768 up are reserved for the faithfulness references (§7.3 item 7 (iv)).

Component attempt: the ladder's retry number (§5.1), restarting at 0 inside each reroll; its cap declared per concern in the registry: 3 for every geometric ladder (tier 3), 8 for the naming re-draw of §9.6 (a repeated name re-draws on its own stream before taking a distinguishing suffix).
Component epoch: e for draws made by epoch e (epoch 0 is the original town).

Component salt: a per-concern number in the recipe (default 0) bumped by rerollLayer(concern) (§7.1), for rerollable concerns only. A concern can be rerollable only if it is not a geometry concern and a registered stage or paint program reads it (StageDecl.streamKeys entry or paint program); the rerollable set is exactly naming, render.instances, style.jitter, style.crowns, style.compass, naming.emblem (the last two read by the compass furniture program and the emblem generator, §9.5); naming.quarter and style.random are registered non-rerollable (a new setStyle re-draws the random style, §8.2), as is every geometry concern (whose reroll is regenerate). rerollLayer's concern type is generated from the registry; the recipe's initial salts are keyed by the same type and its schema refuses any other key (§2.9); a CI test fails when a rerollable concern has no reader (J-DET-22).

A town-wide rerollLayer sets the concern's town salt; an ids-scoped rerollLayer of naming re-draws only the listed entities' names, each with the per-entity salt the event carries; every other name draw takes its salt by §6.3's draw case (town salt for an entity with no predecessor, the salt its naming record holds for a changed naming input), so a name's salt is never in the model digest: the event that set it holds it and the naming record caches it (§2.8).

Label candidates are geometric (S13a, §9.3) and label placement is a deterministic greedy over a total order (S13b, §9.2), so no draw reads a labels stream and none is registered: "reroll the labels" is not offered; re-placing a label is moveLabel.

Draws keyed by an ordinal rather than an entity — the roster's prefix-stable roster/<class>/<ordinal> draws (§10.2) — use the class's registry entry as the derivation unit and the ordinal as the creation index, through the same mixer.

Concern registry: adding a concern is a reviewed change to a registry file; concern ids are u16, append-only, never renumbered (adding one changes no other key); each entry declares its reader stages, whether it is rerollable, and its attempt cap.

Initial concerns: terrain.noise, terrain.controls, water.coast, water.river, water.islands, water.delta, site.centre, blueprint.features (S0 per-rung feature draws, §4.2), intent.surprise (§7.7), gate.pick, reserve.plaza, reserve.castle, reserve.precinct, reserve.water, roster (+ roster/<class>/<ordinal>), route, growth.heading, growth.branch, growth.mainroad, growth.curvature, district.seed, district.type, alloc.district, alloc.block, field.chance, cut.t, cut.side (retired), cut.arc, cut.width, cut.farSideAlt (retired), plot.width, plot.join, plot.vacancy, plot.bounds, siting, siteplan, siteplan.template, heights, material, greenery, fields, crop, forest, hinterland.outside, hinterland.decor, pin.centrepiece, pin.decor, pin.stall, people, content/relations, naming, naming.quarter, naming.emblem, warp.jitter, epoch.transform, island.place, sewer, style.jitter, style.crowns, style.compass, render.instances, style.random (random-style draw of §8.2: creation index = setStyle event's seq, attempt 0-2), render.stampTiles.

other generators on the called stage's concerns keyed the same); undercity neighbourhoods on plot.*, siting, siteplan, heights from their own lineage; gate.pick a trade partner's bearing where the dossier gives none (item 77, keyed by the partner's key hashed as derivation unit); hinterland.outside a listed deposit's bearing where the dossier gives none (§7.7 DR19, item 88, staged); alloc.district dispersal's controlled random share (§4.5, item 72); naming an epoch's district rename (§6.3 case (5)); every chance entry of §7.7's derivation table (item 20 (h)) names a concern of this registry or none.

CI test: every stream key and every lineage hash in a B-CITY city and in a sky-island fixture (two islands carrying districts, underground tunnels) is distinct; birthday bound negligible (2^128 for stream keys; ≈ 3 × 10^-10 per city of 10^5 entities for 64-bit lineage hashes; §6.3's collision rule covers even that) — the test guards the encoder.

Draw helpers: u32, float01 ((u32 >>> 8) · 2^-24), int(lo, hi), bool(p), normal() (Irwin-Hall of 12 uniforms; no transcendental in the RNG layer, G-R12; NG roof jitter's 6-uniform pseudo-normal is a style-time helper), bell4() (folded bell |(u1+u2+u3+u4)/2 − 1| on [0, 1], mean 7/30 — the stop test's draw), mean3() (three uniforms averaged; §4.6 position and corner draws), fuzzy(f), weighted(table), deck(table) (draw without replacement, MFCG's deck selection idea). Helpers draw uniforms only; every power of a draw ((e_hi/e_lo)^g, 4^u) goes through dmath.pow (§6.5 (3)).

Decoration (instance model §8.10): trees, scatter, crowns, roof detail and hatch phase keyed by the entity's render key — low 64 bits (words 0 and 1) of its entity key (§8.1 item 5) — and the instance ordinal, never by LOD band; nothing re-scatters with zoom; nothing stored except the user's instance overrides (instance events, §7.1) and the current positions of positional overrides in the entity's override table, which a warp or vertex move carries with the ground (§7.4).

Enter creates a new document with seed (seed + 1) mod 2^32 (Seed is u32, §2.9) and the same recipe (params, intent, districtIntent, entry mode, table pins, packs) without edits, locks, map assignments or salts; the dossier is kept: the creation prefix holds one creation assign event carrying its DossierRef per live dossier-backed assignment, as the dossier's live events leave it (each live dossier setAttr written into the copy's Assignment field: name, function, shapeClass, knownTo, drift), without placed, target or use (item 20 (c), item 22 (d), §7.7 One path); rejections and positive placements (map edits) are not carried; when the current document has edits the app first warns and offers to save (J-DET-53).
Seed-exact parity with the references is ≈ 0 by evidence and not a goal (docs/CONFIDENCE.md §1).

model = G(outputVersion, base, log): a pure function; base = the canonical recipe (§2.9 Recipe: every model-affecting input that is not an event) or a rebased state; the log folded in order (§7.4); its one declared read-ahead is the log's creation prefix (events at positions 0…k flagged creation, §7.1), taken in before the base derivation: S2 reads its assign events as fixed rows (§7.4; J-A22.74) and the stage owning each drawn declaration of a skeleton's prefix reads it as that stage's constraint (§4.1, item 101; J-A101.41).
CREATION PREFIX: the log's events at positions 0…k flagged creation; read ahead before the base derivation.

Tables, presets and styles a host supplies are not in the recipe: they arrive as logged editTable, editPreset and setStyle events whose content is copied into the log (§6.5 (8), §7.6); packs a later adjust adds are named by that event and belong to the document's pack set (§2.9).

Nothing else reaches the model: no wall clock (operation counts, §5.1 (5)); no host text engine (label placement S13b is view data derived per zoom stop from names, LabelEntity records and bundled fonts' metrics, not in the digest); no viewing order (lazy stages only under §4.1's laziness contract, tested by the derived-complete digest §6.5 (9)); no worker timing (results merge in lineage order, §6.3); one boolean and offset engine per output version on every host (§6.5 (7)); no host code (host provider outputs read from hostContent on replay, §6.5 (8)); no installed pack (every pack resolved by content hash, §2.9); no machine preference read at run time (user-global preferences folded into the recipe at creation, §7.6); no host seed (a dossier-bound document's seed is the port's one-way derivation from the host's seed, §14, item 85, written once at creation; the host's seed never enters a digest, document or link, §6.4); no pointer (cursor sun §8.4 and pointer-driven views transient, never stored, logged or hashed, item 68; an underlay image §9.5, item 101, is view state the model never reads).
Two machines or browsers produce identical model digests (O2 a); two renders of one model are pixel-identical at a given backend, DPR and style version.

The model digest is a Merkle digest over the eager model's content only; the eager model = everything the city LOD draws plus the town-level Allocation and FieldBands records (§4.5, §4.7); lazily derived content (close-ups, people, stage-3 compositions) enters the digest when an edit materialises it.
EAGER MODEL: everything the city LOD draws plus the town-level Allocation and FieldBands records; MODEL DIGEST: the Merkle root over it.

leaf(record) = H128(kind ‖ id ‖ lineage ‖ parent ‖ existence ‖ flags ‖ attributes in schema order ‖ digests of the faces and chains it owns); node(n) = H128(tag(n) ‖ children's digests sorted by address id); root = node(model) per layer: site (terrain raster, fields, L0 water); network (ways, junctions, walls, gates, towers); districts (district → block → plot → buildings, yards, households, pins, Passage records); hinterland; content (Allocation, FieldBands, institutions, factions, relations, Use records, Rejection records, MaterialLedger, Works records, LightSource records, staged ConditionOverlay, DepositSite and PowerRelation records — empty in the base); names and LabelEntity records; closeups (edited close-ups only); underground (UndergroundSystem, Tunnel, Gallery, Chamber, UndergroundLink, AccessPoint — plots under districts via the pseudo-district and undercity neighbourhoods); sky (SkyIsland records; districts under districts, arenas under plats); identity (tombstone ids, supersededBy links, lifecycle event block); plats (per arena and level, the kernel's level digests).

Geometry hashed once by the kernel per level: each arena keeps a digest per level over its level-n route (vertices, roles, face owners and kinds of level ≤ n, never arena slots), updated along each commit record's dirty set (§3.3); finer Steiner vertices belong to the finer level's digest; per-level digests read each vertex's and edge's current birth level (promotion moves a vertex into the coarser digest, demotion back out; kept finer content keeps its leaves through a coarser re-derivation); an entity's leaf takes the digests of the faces and chains it owns (FaceRef, ChainRef), so no coordinate is hashed twice; coordinates in canonical order (level-n ring from its lowest-then-leftmost vertex of level ≤ n, finer vertices skipped); integers as 32-bit lanes, doubles as IEEE-754 bit patterns (−0 → +0; NaN refused by the schema), strings UTF-8; no text serialisation on the digest path; no byte-order dependence.
H128 = MurmurHash3 x86 128-bit variant (public-domain algorithm in 32-bit ops; own implementation tested against published vectors), seed 0 — specified exactly, as H32 is (§13.6 (2)).

Hashed: names and LabelEntity records (text, candidates, pinned, hidden). Excluded from the model digest: provenance, derivation records and naming records (provenance digest §2.8; persisted records form the records digest); style, view, derived, hostContent, dossier (binding and carried facts, §2.9 — rebuilt from the log's dossier events and checked against that fold at load; §7.7, item 74) and telemetry (§2.9); the lighting (light pass, height-and-normal buffers, light maps, §8.4, item 68); label placement decisions (S13b); close-ups never edited (pure function of district committed state, sub-seed, strategy, params; enters under closeups at first edit, §7.4).

Digest maintenance: at every batch commit the kernel re-hashes the leaves of touched records and the nodes on their paths to the root — O(touched × depth) — never by serialising the model (§3.3); the tree is built by the generation run in a session and, for a loaded document, by the load's one full recomputation from the decoded snapshot under the model packages of the document's own output version (§2.9 step 3; the snapshot stores only the root), so every edit maintains a complete tree; memory counted in §12.8's entity-store line; the canonical text serialisation (sorted keys, integer coordinates, floats as shortest round-trip strings) used only for golden files and exports.
CANONICAL TEXT SERIALISATION: sorted keys, integer coordinates, floats as shortest round-trip strings; used only for golden files and exports (distinct from the canonical document form of §2.9).

Records digest: the persisted derivation and naming records (§2.8) form a second Merkle tree — leaf H128(id ‖ record kind ‖ fields in schema order ‖ each cited slice as (table, version, kind, key, hash)); one node per static-index partition (§3.3) plus one town node, each over its records sorted by address id; a root over the nodes; a record belongs to its entity's partition node (district, or the partition outside districts), records of entities belonging to no partition (ways, walls, water bodies, districts) to the town node; maintained like the model tree (a batch re-hashes each rewritten record's leaf and node; a batch moving an entity between nodes — re-parent across districts, district merge or split, outskirtToDistrict — moves its records' leaves and re-hashes both); root finalised when read, stored as recordsDigest, recomputed by every in-window load (§2.9 step 3) with the model tree; memory counted with the model tree's (§12.8); leaf encoding belongs to the file schema, not an output version (records are stored inputs), so any version checks it; a schema transform changing a record column (§7.5) checks the old root and writes the new.

Records digest recomputation measured ≈ 4 ms at CITY and ≈ 11 ms at METROPOLIS for ≈ 10 900 derivation and 3 500 naming records at CITY (≈ 29 300 and 9 500 at METROPOLIS), synthetic schema-shaped workload on the reference machine, two runs within 0.1 ms (docs/validation/bench/fixall_det_r5_recordsdigest.out) — PLAUSIBLE until M0 (d) times it in the engine, under the same 150 ms bar.

The records digest is not a model digest: goldens, the locality checks of §7.3 item 7 (ii)-(vi) and the bridge's convergence read the model digest alone; replay = session and truncation identity compare both (§6.5 (9), §7.3 item 7 (i)) (J-DET-49).

Digest bars decided before any golden is signed: maintenance ≤ 5 % of each batch's own time at CITY; root finalisation at a stage end ≤ 5 ms at CITY; full recomputation of the root from its leaves ≤ 150 ms at CITY, records tree included — used by the CI oracle and every in-window load. Measured ≈ 31-34 ms at CITY and ≈ 95-101 ms at METROPOLIS for the model tree (+ ≈ 4 / ≈ 11 ms records tree), synthetic workload (docs/validation/bench/fixall_det_r4_loaddigest.out) — PLAUSIBLE until M0 (d).

Pre-decided fallbacks (none moves a golden, the root being a pure function of the leaves): (i) maintenance over 5 % — leaves re-hashed at the next coarser batch boundary (per district instead of per block and plot), root at every stage end unchanged; (ii) root finalisation over 5 ms — layer nodes maintained at every commit, root finalised only when read: at save, end of a verification replay, export, an API digest request, each stage end of a CI golden run.

Fallback (iii) full recomputation over 150 ms: the CI oracle recomputes per run one subtree per layer chosen by the run's seed (all covered across nightly runs) and compares with the maintained node; the load's recomputation leaves the edit path: a copy-on-write checkpoint of the decoded state at h₀ (§7.4 checkpoints), working state editable at once, model and records trees recomputed from the checkpoint in the generation worker between edits; each edit made meanwhile keeps its touched set (§7.4) and its leaves are re-hashed on the new trees in log order when it finishes; roots at h₀ compared with model.digest and model.recordsDigest as in §2.9 step 3; a mismatch is a corrupt cache — the replay's state replaces the working state at the head and the interim edits are re-applied in log order as "take the replayed town" does (§2.9 step 4), fates recomputed, differences reported; until roots match nothing is reported verified, "trust the saved town" and step 4's keep shown disabled ("checking the saved copy…"), and save, export, an API digest request and a bridged client's comparison with a rebase's stateDigest wait (edits do not); a mismatch withdraws the keep for good — a corrupt cache is never a base (J-DET-40, J-DET-45); a New random meanwhile computes its scope's content digests from the scope's own leaves (§5.1 (6)).

Histories, not states (item 22 (c); J-A22.71): the map is a function of the seed, the ordered history of dossier events and the map's own edits; replaying the same history reproduces the same map; two players reaching the same dossier by different histories may hold different equally valid maps (continuity chosen over path-independence; each dossier event is a least-disruption mutation of the map that stood, §7.7; the document keeps the whole history, §2.9). A dossier event's draws are keyed by the plots it touches and its own seq (§6.1, §6.3) — or, for a trade partner's or deposit's bearing, by that element's binding key — never by the dossier's values, so one history gives one digest on every host (§6.5 (9) history test). Item 20 (h)'s derivation is this same fold: the derivation table's rows (§7.7) read only delivered dossier facts and committed state.

Works records (§4.11) are model data in the digest; a Works' drawn stage at any week follows from record and week, never stored or hashed (scrubbing weeks changes no digest). A LightSource is model data; its lighting is view. A district's character vector and band range (§4.5) are pure functions of committed state, recomputed on load, never hashed; its identity, pressure and nameHistory depend on the epochs lived through and are model data in the digest, written by generation, epochs, dossier events and (identity only) a setAttr override (§2.5; registry row §2.8); the dials' inputs are recorded (circumstance slices in the recipe and each EpochInputs; dossier facts in the log) so a load's recomputation reproduces the field (J-DET-12; J-A72.61).

The elaboration cache is outside both digests (item 28 (c); J-A28.62): a click-derived rung (a neighbourhood's wings, a building's plan) is a pure function of the building's committed state and own streams (§4.1, §2.6); its cached result and elaboration record (§2.8: rung state and digest of inputs) sit outside the model and records digests, beside the report in the non-canonical blocks (§2.9); a click logs and writes nothing a replay must reproduce; a rung's absent/current/stale state is recomputed from the recorded input digest at load and after every batch touching the building; a click's derivation enters a digest only when an edit materialises it (the first plan edit stores the composition, §2.6); rung reroll counters are not cache state (absolute in regenerate events under <building id>#<rung>); a re-cut of an unstored plan along the interior ladder never takes the cache as its prior — its prior is committed state (the as-built plan carried step by step, §7.3's row), so occupants changing twice between clicks derive the same plan either way (§6.5 (9)); a stored plan is re-cut inside the event changing its inputs (§7.3, §7.4) (J-A28.71, J-A28.72).
ELABORATION CACHE / ELABORATION RECORD / RUNG STATE (absent, current, stale): the non-canonical cache of click-derived rungs and its record. Also "elaboration chunk" (ElaborationChunk, §2.9).

Every entity has two identities: an address everything points at (edits, locks, assignments, pins, labels, households, exports, the host) and a lineage that keys its random streams; they start equal and separate only when an entity is re-derived.

Lineage key = (arena key — layer and part, §2.2 —, derivation unit's lineage hash, stage, creation epoch, creation index, derivation unit's reroll[, dup]); lineageHash is its 64-bit hash, cached in the arena.

Derivation unit per kind (declared per stage in the registry): the town for S4 routes (destination order) and S6 districts (seed order); the growth stage for S5 ways (acceptance order); the L1 cell a way split, for new cells (split ordinal); the cell for S8 blocks and lanes; the block for S10 plots and alleys; the plot for S11 buildings, yard parts and households; the household for people (member ordinal); S6's run for Seam records (creation index by the run's lowest-then-leftmost vertex); the S5c growth run, the district's S8 run (baseLane portals) or the creating edit for portals; the parent surface district for an undercity neighbourhood (II.7.5; its district's lineage continues its parent's); the system for its galleries and chambers (II.7.6; part in the arena key); the connection stage's run for links (creation index by the pair's canonical order); the host for a light source (its light rule row and ordinal along the host as creation index, item 68); the target for a Works (start week as creation index, item 67); the creating edit event (seq) for anything a user draws or builds; otherwise (cells and junctions of a growth commit, walls, water bodies, bridges, greenery) the stage run that created it. Creation index = deterministic creation order of the unit's run or the stage's declared canonical order (faces and vertices: lowest-then-leftmost lattice point).

DERIVATION UNIT: the entity whose derivation run created an entity (whose reroll children draw with); CREATION INDEX: deterministic creation order within that run; LINEAGE KEY / LINEAGE HASH / "lineage": the stream identity. Also used: "stream identity".
