Address id = kind:token, prefixed <layer><part>/ outside the ground layer (the island's slot on the sky layer, the system's part on the underground layer, the sewer network's part 0 written bare: sky2/plot:…, under/tunnel:…, under3/gallery:…); a part number is part of the address and never reused (§3.4, J-A65.31); for a generated entity the token is the base-32 form of its lineage hash at creation (13 characters); for a user-created one the hash of the creating event's seq and its ordinal — closure pieces (§7.3 item 9, item 66) and sugar-expansion entities (§7.1, item 101) are user-created entities of their event, ordinals in the closure's dependency order and the expansion's order; the address is opaque: the parent is a field, never parsed from the id (J-DET-1).

Never reused; one collision rule: minting runs after succession matching; a fresh entity whose natural address equals a live address, a tombstone or an address its own batch retires takes suffix ~k with the smallest free k; a fresh lineage key equal to a live entity's outside the batch's re-derived set (a survivor, e.g. a locked plot) takes the smallest free dup component; entities the batch itself replaces are not collisions (so a faithful Regenerate (keep settings) re-mints their lineage keys, matches by anchor and reproduces them exactly); collisions resolved in the batch's canonical order (records sorted by lineage hash); an address an undo withdraws (§7.4) is free again but only the same derivation (same unit, lineage and reroll — a redo or repeated New random) can mint it.

Carry-over when a scope is re-derived (regenerate, Adjust, re-derive from Sk, a §7.3 local operator, template replacement, migration, an epoch): an entity not re-derived (outside the invalidation set, a fixed input — locked, pinned, edited or assigned §7.2 — or merely re-parented) survives: keeps address and lineage; only its parent field and a reparent lifecycle event change. Survivors in this sense: the kept parts of a designation mutation (§4.7 S11); rooms a stored-plan re-cut keeps along the interior ladder (item 28 (f)); the standing fabric of an epoch (vacant, derelict, ruined, cleared or reused building; neglected, breached or superseded enceinte; silted, caved-in or sealed tunnel; waning or settled island — state a lifecycle change); a reuse … build successor on a cleared trace succeeds at the trace's address (supersede); regrowth on an old plot re-uses the plot's address; raiseIsland mints the island's arena key and lineage from the town's lineage, slot index and epoch (item 8; J-A8.61); a use keeps its own address as it moves (anchor: plot address and role) while the building it leaves keeps its own (item 17); a mutation's added parts are user-created entities minted from the causing event's seq and ordinal; a dossier-backed assignment is a fixed input so its element survives every re-derivation of the ground under it (§7.7).

A re-derived entity is matched to fresh entities by its anchor: the fresh entity of the same kind and class family whose anchor lies nearest within the kind's hysteresis radius succeeds it — takes the old address and the old generated name with its naming record (references re-bind; §7.3 item 4 decides which overrides move) and keeps its own fresh lineage (New random really re-rolls); a carry event records the lineage change and the same batch re-owns the successor's faces and roles under the address (setOwner, retypeEdges, §3.4); an old entity with no successor becomes a tombstone in the archive (§2.8) whose supersededBy names the fresh entity covering its anchor point, if any; a fresh entity with no predecessor keeps its fresh address; lifecycle events are written only for changes (existence, flags, lineage change, supersession, re-parenting), so an exact re-derivation leaves the model digest unchanged (J-DET-2).
SURVIVE / SUCCEED (successor) / TOMBSTONE / supersededBy / carry event / reparent / resurrect: the carry-over vocabulary.

Names follow the address and their inputs: a generated name (text and short form) is handed to a successor with the address and its naming record (§2.8: naming slices its last draw consulted and its salt), as a lock or assignment is; S13a draws a name only in five cases: (1) an entity with no predecessor, town salt; (2) every unedited name under a town-wide rerollLayer(naming), new town salt; (3) entities an ids-scoped rerollLayer(naming) lists, each with salt one above the largest its name has been drawn with, advancing once more when equal to the old name up to reroll.maxAdvance, event storing salts used; (4) an unedited generated name whose naming inputs changed, with its record's salt — runs whenever S13a runs over the entity: after an adjust of the pack list (pack or corpus added/removed/selected/deselected, §7.6), an editTable or editPreset changing a naming slice, an upgrade's mapping (§7.5), a frozenImport rebase (§2.9 step 2, over every unedited name), the event ending the name's protection (unlock, unassign, undo/redo/revert removing the holding setAttr, lock or assign, §2.8 dormant record), any re-derivation reaching S13a; compares every cited slice with the current effective tables, a changed or unresolvable slice re-draws; (5) at an epoch, a district whose identity row changed at its character step (item 72): unedited generated name re-drawn on its naming stream with the renaming epoch's component and its record's salt, the old text moved to District.nameHistory (§2.5); a protected name (setAttr, lock, assignment, dossier naming claim, item 82) never re-drawn; listed in the epoch report (§5.4) and stored in EditBase.renames without confirmation (J-A72.62).

Each field of a culture or ancestry row is its own naming slice (§7.6) and a name's record cites only the fields its draw read, so selecting another corpus for one field re-draws exactly the names from that field; a carried name is kept exactly while its naming inputs are unchanged; a change of the features a grammar guard reads (a district that lost its gate) is not a naming input and renames nothing (§9.6); only case (5) renames a district at an epoch and only past its identity's hysteresis; every draw uses the entity's naming stream (keyed from its entity key with the case's salt and the attempt) and writes the naming record anew.

Renames of case (4) are confirmed like fates: the dry run lists each (old and new text) in the edit's fate report, the edit commits after the user confirms (an action whose dry run lists any returns confirm, a frozenImport rebase included), the confirmed renames stored in EditBase.renames (§7.1); a replay or receiving client re-draws identically; one computing different renames reports a mismatch under §7.3 item 4's rule; a user-set name (setAttr), a locked name path and an assigned name are never re-drawn while protected, each keeping its naming record dormant for the event ending the protection (§2.8); when carrying or a re-draw brings two equal names into one uniqueness scope (§9.6, e.g. a district merge joining two lanes of the same name) the entity whose address sorts later re-draws on its own stream and the rename is listed in the fate report (J-DET-37, J-DET-46).

Matching is by distance, never by quantised cell: candidate (old, fresh) pairs within the radius and of the same class family are sorted by (distance, old id, fresh id) and assigned one-to-one greedily in that order.

Anchor table (kind: anchor; radius; class family): plot — highest-class frontage (way address, start offset along the way); 0.5 m along the same way or its successor; use family (residential, commercial, institutional, agricultural). building — footprint centroid; 0.5 m; building class family (table row). block, cell — centroid; 2 m (block), 5 m (cell). district — seed feature's address; same feature; district kind family. way — end junctions' addresses, else overlap ≥ 50 % of length; way class family. junction, gate, tower, pin — position; 1 m (junction, pin), 2 m (gate, tower); kind. bridge — deck midpoint on the same river (water body's address or successor); crossing.searchBandM (default 120 m, §4.2 S1 (5)); kind (bridge, ford). enceinte, water body, greenery, land use — overlap ≥ 50 % (IoU); kind. household, person, label — (plot address, ordinal); (household address, ordinal); target address. use — (plot address, role), a relocation moves it by its event (item 17); use class family. room of a stored plan — centroid within its wing per storey; 0.5 m in the wing's frame; any role (item 28 (f)). entrance ('entrance', building, i, §2.2 rule 7) — carried with its wing by carryWings (§2.6), re-matched by (wing, side, offset); half the side's length; entrance role. passage (item 30) — (front plot address, kerb end midpoint); 0.5 m along the same kerb; one family. access point (II.7.4, items 12, 64) — (element's address, position of its ('access_point', id) vertex); 1 m; AccessPoint.kind. tunnel, gallery — end junctions else overlap ≥ 50 % in own part; Tunnel.kind / system kind. chamber — floor face centroid in own part; 2 m; system kind. underground link — its two ends' element addresses; same pair; UndergroundLink.via. undercity neighbourhood — parent surface district's address and void system's part. light source — (host address, light rule row, ordinal along host); 1 m from recorded point; light kind. Works — (target address, start week). condition overlay, deposit site, power relation (item 88, staged, empty in the base) — binding key (§7.7 item 12). sky island — its slot key (raiseIsland; J-A8.61). seam (NF-P6) — its two districts' addresses and first chain's address. portal — position; 1 m; portal kind (baseLane, growth, edit).

Split through an anchor: the child left of the directed cut keeps the id (§3.6 (5)); a household's address survives a re-derivation of its plot by succession (plot address and ordinal), so a person's key (household address, member ordinal, birth epoch, §10.3) is stable wherever the household is; when S1's water operator re-sites an edited reach's crossings (§7.3 (b) 2), each old deck is succeeded by the re-sited deck nearest its old midpoint within the band, keeping name, assignment and its way's reference.

Measurement (M1, B-EDIT-lite): 1 cm perturbations of every vertex keep ≥ 99.9 % of addresses; pre-decided fallback: building and plot radii double to 1 m and an IoU ≥ 0.5 test joins the class-family check.

One matching routine hands addresses on in every re-derivation (scoped regeneration, Adjust, Re-derive from Sk — from S1 the whole town, a local operator, template replacement, epochs, migration, the upgrade mapping of §7.5): point-anchored kinds (plots by frontage offset, buildings, blocks, cells, junctions, gates, towers, pins, bridges, passages by kerb end, access points) through a uniform grid per (kind, class family) with cell = hysteresis radius, candidates in the 3 × 3 neighbourhood, pairs sorted by (distance, old id, fresh id) and assigned greedily; overlap-anchored kinds (ways and tunnels without matched end junctions, enceintes, water bodies, greenery, land use) take candidates from the kernel's spatial index (§3.3) and compute overlap on those only; a sky island matched by its slot and a staged dossier record by its binding key, no distance read.

Matching budget ≤ 2 µs per re-derived point-anchored entity and ≤ 20 µs per overlap-anchored one (median), included in §12.6's scope costs; measured (Apple M1, Node 24; docs/validation/bench/fixall_det_r2_match.out): 0.60 µs per entity for a 450-building district regeneration, 0.59 µs for a 30 000-entity CITY re-derivation (0.38 µs when unrelated), 0.59 µs for an 80 000-entity METROPOLIS mapping at 2 m radius; measurement M0 (d) then M1 on B-EDIT-lite and a Re-derive-from-S1 fixture; pre-decided fallback: matching per static-index partition (district first, leftovers across partitions) — a declared shift (§6.4) since a boundary entity can take a farther in-district candidate.

JOIN and SPLIT (item 31 (c); J-A31.73): a joined plot takes its address by the anchor rule from the member whose frontage anchor it keeps; other members become tombstones with supersededBy = the joined plot, members is history; its lineage continues the lineage key of its largest member by area (ties by address id) — the exception to J-DET-2 — so its buildings' and yard parts' streams continue; the epoch component keeps an epoch's re-cut distinct (owner: modifications of the original seed, not new rolls). A SPLIT keys each child by the parent's lineage key with the child's index as creation index; the child keeping the parent's frontage anchor keeps the address, the others take fresh addresses; every child takes the continued lineage; a later SPLIT resurrects a member whose anchor matches — the one permitted reuse of a tombstoned id, recorded as a resurrect event (safe since a JOIN's member ids were never given to another entity) — taking its address from the tombstone, lineage from the parent and child index, builtBand (§2.5) from the rung-3 event that re-cut it, never from the tombstone's last record; only an undo restores that record exactly (§7.4).

A tunnel record split by a stretch conversion (II.6, J-A11.43) follows the split rule with the centreline's first vertex as frontage anchor (part holding it keeps the address, other parts minted from the causing event's seq and ordinal, every part continues the tunnel's lineage with its part index); a block's Frontage record (§2.5) the same split cuts at a stretch end follows the same rule (part holding the record's first kerb edge in centreline order keeps the address; every other part — two where the record spans a whole interior stretch — minted from seq and ordinal; each continues the lineage with its part index; an undo restores the one record, §7.4); a mutation continues lineage; only a re-derivation takes a fresh one (New random and every successor matched in a re-derived scope: Adjust, Re-derive from Sk, §7.3 local operator, template replacement, migration, what an epoch re-derives) (J-DET-2, amended so).

Dossier bindings never re-key (item 74): a dossier re-binding re-points a binding row of Document.dossier and never re-keys a map address (records keep ids, lineage, geometry); a dossier name change carrying no receipt is a removal plus an addition (§7.7), and the addition mints nothing until the solver places the new element, from its placing event's seq.

docId (a UUID) minted when a document is created, kept on save, re-minted on clone and save-as; addresses are document-scoped (a clone keeps them); at the API and bridge boundary every id is rendered <docId>/<id>; exports carry addresses and a supersedes table (tombstone → successor).
Workers merge results in lineage order, never arrival order.

Scope of stability: (1) independent concerns — adding or changing a concern changes no other concern's draws; a naming input change re-draws only the names citing it; (2) scoped rerolls — New random changes nothing outside its effective scope (§7.3); (3) upstream changes — a change to stage k's code or tables changes stage k's outputs and what derives from them: a declared cascade shift (§6.4, §13.3), never silent; stages upstream of k and independent of it stay byte-identical; (4) edited documents — stability across such changes comes from carry-over by anchor and migration (§7.5), never from stream keys.

Identity fixtures: minting and matching within budget; B-EDIT fixtures for drawBoundary, district merge and split, outskirtToDistrict, regenerate around a lock, a course-knot move that re-sites a bridge (bridge keeps address and name), New random on a district (matched successors keep names; only entities without a predecessor draw one), a district merge joining two equal lane names (later address re-draws, reported), the recycling case (a superseded assigned building whose creation slot is reused) — 0 duplicate ids and 0 silent re-binds; naming-input fixtures are §13.2's.

Output version (o<k>): the observable output of the model packages; bumps exactly when a release declares a shift (any stage digest moves on the golden suite, §13.3); a release changing no output keeps it (documents, links, goldens stay valid); every document and link names the output version it replays under.
Generator version = the code build, informational (bug reports), never a replay key; schema version = the file format (§7.5).

Preview flag: links and documents made before output version 1 (fixed at M4's exit, §16) carry preview: true (in a link &pv=1) and the app shows §13.3's preview notice; the flag disappears from output version 1 on.
Table versions: each rule table separately, pinned in the recipe; a table change that changes output is part of an output-version bump; a user override carries its base row's hash (§7.6).

Pack versions: each setting pack by id, version and content hash, in the recipe or in the adjust event that adds it (§2.9's pack set); shipped packs belong to the output version like its tables (each retained version's chunk carries its own); a non-shipped pack's content travels in the document; a pack a later version stops shipping is copied into the document by the upgrade to that version (§7.5); a selected user corpus is a non-shipped pack user:<content hash> (§2.9).
Style version: style sheets; changes pixels, never the model digest; carried in a link for pixel identity.
VERSION AXES: output version, generator version, schema version, preview flag, table versions, pack versions, style version.

Permalink format: carries the canonical recipe, never a pointer to machine state: ?o=<output version>&s=<seed, base 36>&z=<rung> when the recipe is the version's defaults apart from seed and rung (watabou's one-line link kept); otherwise &r=<base64url of the deflated CBOR recipe delta> (params with preferences folded in, intent, districtIntent, entry mode, rerollable salts keyed and schema-checked as Recipe.salts, table pins and packs differing from shipped ones, packs by id, version, hash); &l=<base64url deflated CBOR log> when the town has a log (edits, locks, assignments, style edits, undo and redo; a blueprint's assignments are log events, §7.7); &st=<style id@version> when not default; &pv=1 preview.

A link is emitted only when it can rebuild the same town and picture on any machine: every pack of the pack set (a corpus once selected and later deselected included) is shipped with the link's output version; the base is the recipe (a rebased town is not seed-reproducible before its rebase); hostContent is empty; the style sheet is shipped; the whole URL fits in 2 000 characters.

Otherwise the app says which condition failed ("this town uses the setting pack X, which is not built in"; "this town uses your own name list X" — also when deselected; "this town uses content from the host program Y"; "this town was kept from a saved copy and cannot be rebuilt from a link"; "too many edits for a link") and offers the .plat file, or &doc=<ref> when the host configured a document resolver with publish (DocResolver, §11.5); the document carries pack content and host outputs (§2.9); preset=<id> never appears — an edited preset elsewhere cannot change the town (J-DET-50, J-DET-17, J-DET-35).

CI: link → recipe → link identity; the model digest built from a link equals the session's; refusal cases: a recipe naming a non-shipped pack; district names from a user corpus selected after creation (user:<hash> named only by an adjust); a town that selected such a corpus, deselected it, saved and reloaded; a document with a host provider's output; a town rebased by keeping the saved town after a forced load mismatch — each link refused, and the .plat file opened by a library lacking pack, corpus and provider replays to the session's digest (select-then-deselect: corpus content stays in packs while the first adjust names it; rebased town reopens as the kept town from its base state).

Retention of old output versions: the browser library ships the current output version's model packages and the two previous ones (N−1, N−2) as lazily loaded, tree-shakable chunks (@plat/*-o<k>; an embed may leave them out); the Node CLI replays any published output version by installing that exact package version; inside the window a document or link replays exactly; outside it a document opens as a frozen view (§2.9 step 2) checked by chunk hashes only, labelled "made with o5; not verified by this version"; a link opens under the current output version with a visible notice ("made with o5, shown with o8; differences are expected") and the exact-replay CLI command; nothing changes silently; the same window bounds what the browser can undo by replay (an upgrade, a rebase onto an older version, §7.4) — outside it the undo is withdrawn with the CLI command shown.

Measurement (M3a): each retained output version adds ≤ 150 KB gzipped to its lazy chunk; the golden suite replays under N−1 and N−2; pre-decided fallback: the browser window shrinks to N−1 (the CLI keeps every version).

Goldens (§13.3 builds the tooling from M1): stage-isolated goldens keep, per seed and stage, the previous output version's frozen upstream outputs; a release computes each stage's digest by running the new stage code on those frozen inputs, so only stages whose own code or tables changed can differ, each needing a shift record; end-to-end goldens are re-signed only with a cascade record; both records and the protocol are §13.3's.

DECLARED SHIFT / SHIFT RECORD / CASCADE RECORD / CASCADE SHIFT: a release's declared change of a stage's output (shift record per changed stage; cascade record to re-sign end-to-end goldens). Names used: "declared shift", "declared cascade shift", "declared golden shift", "shift record", "cascade record".
Topology lives on integer centimetres with exact predicates (§3.2).
Fields, costs and weights are IEEE doubles; + − × ÷ and Math.sqrt are exact by specification; every other real function goes through dmath, the vetted fdlibm port (§3.1; D-23).

Lint allowlist: in model packages and every adapter or provider whose output reaches the model, the only Math members allowed are abs, floor, ceil, round, trunc, sign, min, max, sqrt, imul, clz32, fround plus arithmetic operators; the allowlist also covers view code whose output reaches a bit-compared digest — @plat/labels, every implementation of ObstacleSource and RoleIndex (§14) and functions they call, the S14 builder code writing the display-list columns they read (bbox, geometry ranges and GeomTable, layer, z, symbol extents from style sizes — a rotated symbol's extent uses dmath), §8.10's instance function with every function it calls (stamp, grid and line layouts, per-instance look draws, density edge test; run by model-format exporters and override resolution in the generation worker, positions compared byte for byte by §13.3), and the CPU reference light pass of §8.4 with every function it calls (item 68; the GPU implementation, held by a tolerance, stays outside, J-A68.62); CI finds that code as the import closure of those implementations, column writers and the instance function from the TypeScript program, so a joining module is linted unlisted; the rest of @plat/render (paint programs, backends, compositing) stays outside (pixels compared by visual regression, §13.3, §13.4).

** allowed only with a literal integer exponent 0-4, rewritten by the build into multiplications; every other power goes through dmath.pow (S1's river-width law w0 · acc^0.4 is dmath.pow(acc, 0.4)). Forbidden: Math.random, Date, performance, timers, crypto.getRandomValues, DOM access, locale-dependent string operations (toLocaleString, localeCompare, Intl), Array.prototype.sort without a comparator, and any dependence on object-key or Map iteration order beyond insertion order; the lint also enforces §3.2 (8)'s division rule (ratio()).

The lint scans the dossier port's adapter boundary (item 73): no module of plat/ outside @plat/port's adapter folders names a key of the host's dossier — the adapter's key list (§14) is the scan's input — so the host's vocabulary lives in one folder.

Vendored dependencies are scanned: every third-party library a kernel adapter imports is vendored at a pinned version and passes the same allowlist scan at each version change; an audit record (library, version, scan result, each exception with its wrapper) is kept in @plat/kernel; a library that fails (e.g. calls Math.hypot) is patched or wrapped in its adapter before adoption.
Every sort uses a total-order comparator with an id tie-break (the OS ObjectMap key-order hazard cannot occur).
Pool workers follow §3.3's overlay-and-merge protocol, merging in lineage order (§6.3); no result depends on arrival order; no model package reads time (§5.1 (5)).
One boolean and offset engine per output version on every host (D-14): no host may silently run a different engine; changing the engine is an output-version bump with a declared shift.

Host providers: a host-supplied table arrives as an editTable, editPreset or setStyle event whose content is copied into the log with provenance host (§7.6); host code registered as a provider (ContentProvider, §14) passes a double-run check at registration (same request twice in two fresh workers returns identical digests); its results are recorded in the document's hostContent block keyed by (provider id, version, input hash) and read from there on replay (§2.9, §11.4), so the document replays without the host; setting packs follow the same rule through the packs block (§2.9).

Determinism tests (CI) part 1: cross-host — identical digests on Node x86 / arm64, Chromium, Firefox, WebKit, workers on and off, pool sizes 0-3; time dilation — golden suite under a shim scaling every clock read × 10 and × 0.1 gives byte-identical per-stage digests; derived-complete digest — every district's S10, S10b, S11 and S12b and the hinterland unit's (S12b named explicitly), derived for 50 METROPOLIS seeds in three random orders with pool sizes 0-3, give identical digests (laziness contract §4.1); op-order determinism (§13.2) and placement digests (§13.3); headless = UI (O11 f).

replay = session: replaying base and log gives the session's model digest and records digest on every B-EDIT sequence (§7.3 item 7 (i)), including the naming-collision fixture, sequences with undo and redo from several sessions, edits made during load verification under both choices of a forced mismatch (§2.9 step 4), and edits made before a records mismatch, re-applied (§2.9 step 3).

truncation identity: a B-EDIT sequence folded with its undone pairs kept and with them truncated gives the same model and records digests (§7.4), including a redo followed by a user-created entity (same address in both folds), a setAttr(name) + undo pair, a lock + unlock pair and a naming rerollLayer + undo pair each around a corpus selection (freeing event re-draws by §6.3 case (4), listed, confirmed, stored; naming records restored with names, §2.8), and a corpus selection + undo, truncated, saved, reloaded and redone, its pack still in packs (§2.9).

links and documents without their inputs (§6.4's pack, user-corpus, provider and rebased-town cases); checks under the recording version — a keptSnapshot-rebased CITY document upgraded across a test output version whose field driver and digest leaf encoding differ from from's opens editable after a reload and replays to the session's digest; a frozen view of a fixture written by a test build labelled o(N−3) opens with no mismatch message, one with a chunk's bytes altered reports damage and refuses the frozenImport rebase (§2.9 steps 2-3, §7.5); the double-run check of registered providers (8) and the distinct-key test of §6.1.

click-order identity (item 28): for 50 CITY seeds every district's wings and every clicked building's plan derived in three random click orders under elaborate 'click' and 'view', cache dropped to absent between runs, give identical model and records digests and byte-identical cached results per (entity, rung, input digest) across hosts; a layout re-roll leaves wings, entrances, stair core byte-identical and a roles re-roll every ring and opening position; the interior ladder (item 28 (f)) — a building whose occupants' band and household count change twice between clicks (a hand relet and an epoch band fall) gives the same plan with a click after each change and with one click at the end, and again with the cache dropped; its shell's leaf digest unchanged by every re-cut; a return to the as-built band and count gives the as-built plan exactly (§7.3's canonical prior).

history determinism (items 20, 22): same seed and same ordered history of dossier events, rejections, positive placements and edits gives one model digest on every host; two histories reaching one dossier give two valid maps whose difference is confined to their events' disruption sets (§6.2, §7.7; fixtures §13.2's). session-history independence (item 52; J-A52.61): for 20 seeds, a seed's model digest generated first in a fresh process equals its digest after 50 other maps and every view toggle and zoom stop (no render draw touches a model stream; Enter's successor is (seed + 1) mod 2^32, not stream state; no cache keyed by anything but its content — §8.10's stamp tiles built with the product and content-hashed); provenance: in MFCG 12710731, VG 1.6.9 and NG 1.2.2 the renderer's leftover stream state seeds the next map and tree-spacing tiles are cached per session; Dwellings (itch 17195045) resets its generator from the clock for some houses; Fantasy Manor 1.0.0 build 890 seeds from the page's load time.

dossier fixtures (item 83, T73-8): the same B-DOSSIER-lite fixture (§13.2) and seed give the same model digest on Node x86 and arm64 and in the nightly five-engine run; works stages (item 67): a Works' drawn stage at week w is a pure function of record and w — reached directly or by scrubbing forward and back, byte-identical, no digest moves; lighting (item 68): the CPU reference light pass gives byte-identical light for the same model, lights, view and time on the five engines, the GPU pass within §13.4's tolerance, flicker a pure function of render key and view time (§8.4); skeleton round trip (item 101): a map's declared subset exported as a skeleton (§11.1) and re-imported under its seed reproduces its model digest; a clerk's transcript of tool calls, replayed, gives the session's digest; one declaration made on the canvas, through the tool API and in a skeleton file gives one event (the elegance bars scheduling these are §13.2's).

Second implementations: the WebAssembly accelerator of §3.7 (J-K8) compiles a hot loop from the same integer algorithm as the TypeScript loop it replaces and must reproduce its integer outputs byte for byte (cross-implementation test: golden suite with accelerator on and off, identical per-stage digests); output-neutral, moves no golden; the TypeScript loop stays in every bundle. The Clipper2-WASM engine (§3.7's pre-decided fallback) is a different engine: replaces the arrangement engine as the single engine on every host (7) with a declared golden shift (§3.7, §13.3), pinned and vendored (4), named in the report (§5.4); its determinism test is (9)'s cross-host one (J-DET-28).
MODEL PACKAGES: the packages whose output is the model (linted by the allowlist); also "model package(s)". DMATH: the vetted fdlibm port.

Every user change is recorded in order as a small event on the permanent address of what it changes; the town is always a starting point plus the list of events, applied the same way on screen and on reopening; anything touched is protected (regeneration around it keeps it); a change reaching something the whole town depends on is announced first with which edits are kept, moved to their nearest match, or left with nothing to attach to; otherwise regeneration is local and everything outside the chosen area stays byte-identical.

EditBase { seq (from the document's nextSeq; never reset; survives rebase; an event an epoch carries in EpochInputs.dossier takes its seq when the epoch is appended, §7.7 item 6; J-A22.76); author 'user'|'host'|'epoch'|'migration'; session (authoring session per document and author, §7.4 — its undo and redo stacks; never read by the fold); group? (one undo step); renames?: Rename[] (§6.3 case (4) confirmed renames); dossier?: DossierRef (set by @plat/port on every event a dossier change generates through the host door, §11.4; binding key opaque to the module); dossierChange?: DossierChange (set with dossier: the change envelope — id, source, week, cause, element, operation, reason, §7.7 item 13, item 75); proposedBy?: 'clerk' (item 101; author stays the user; exports' provenance reads it, §11.1); closure?: ClosureRecord (§7.3 item 9, item 66); creation?: true (set by generate on the blueprint's, creation dossier's and skeleton file's events at positions 0…k — the creation prefix; never an undo, redo or revert target, never truncated, §7.4); mutations?: MutationRecord[] (§4.7 S11, item 18); disruption?: DisruptionReport (dossier event, positive placement or relocation consequences as the dry run listed them) }.
Rename = { id; from; to } — the name's text before and after as the user saw them.
DossierRef = { element: string (the binding key of §7.7, item 74); version?: string (the host's product line) } — the module reads it, never writes it.

PointsForm = { points: PointCm[] (declared anchors: one seed, two to four corners, a source and a mouth, a shore point, or a brush's or lasso's samples); levelCm? (water's level form); sizeM2? (a harbour basin's size) } — item 101 (i): the minimal declaration of a shaped thing; the event stores the derived shape, resolved, as its geometry.

Cardinal = 'N'|'E'|'S'|'W'; Locus = { rel 'in'|'on'|'at'|'near'; target; side?: Cardinal } — a roster line's or place's locus ("in <quarter>", "on the harbour", "at <gate>", "north side of <square>", "near <place>"; item 16's relation templates as hints).
RosterLine = { name; cls: BuildingClass; locus?: Locus; element? (with a dossier connected: the binding key of the dossier element the line places) }.
RungKey = string `${Id}#${rung}` — a stage-3 rung's reroll counter in a regenerate event's map (<building id>#wings … #plan.furnish, §6.1).
DisruptionReport { cost; budget (the request kind's row, §7.7); overBudget; moved[] { use; from; to | null }; joined: Id[][]; vacated: Id[]; mutated: Id[]; why[] { id; rule } }.
EditScope = { ids: Id[] } | { ring: PolygonCm; key: PlatKey; level: Level } — resolved to the effective scope at dry run and stored resolved.
EditFate = { id; fate 'kept'|'carried'|'orphaned'|'discarded'; to?; reason }.
FieldStroke = { path: PointCm[]; radiusCm; falloff 'linear'|'cosine'; amount (relative Δ: field units, or cm for terrain); water? 'locked'|'follow' (terrain only; default 'locked', §7.2, §7.3) }.
lock / unlock { ids; paths? (attribute-level locks) }.
pin / unpin { ids } — only ever an explicit user action, never emitted by viewing.
moveVertex { key: PlatKey; at: LatticePoint (position before the move); sig: VertexSig (role signature, §2.2 rule 5); to: LatticePoint }.
moveCourseKnot { water; ordinal (knot ordinal in WaterBody.controls, §2.3); at: PointCm (before); to } — a river's control knot is S1's recorded input, not an arena vertex.
warp { key: PlatKey; fromLevel 0 | 1 (1 default; 0 also moves water and coast); strokes: WarpStroke[] } — one staged warp session committed on Apply.
drawWay { points; class: WayClass; widthCm; from?: PointsForm (two points: route derived by S4's router at the dry run, §4.3) }.

drawWater { kind: WaterKind; add: PolygonCm[]; subtract?; line?; widthCm?; from?: PointsForm (lake: one point and a level; river: source and mouth; harbour: sea level, shore point and size) } — add rings unioned, subtract rings = land brush (islands).
drawWall { points; kind: Enceinte['kind']; closed; from?: PointsForm (two or more points: run derived along ridges and contours by S5a's trace) }.
placeGate { enceinte; at: PointCm; expansion } — sugar (item 101): a gate declared by one point on its enceinte.
drawGreen { polygon; kind: Greenery['kind']; densityPerHa? }.

drawBoundary { polygon; district?; kind? (district-kind row steering a points form's snap); from?: PointsForm (one seed, two to four corners or a lasso: grown along block edges) } — snaps to whole L1 cells.
quarter { boundary (resolved at dry run); from?: PointsForm; kind (district-kind row); name?; band?; district?; expansion } — sugar (item 101).
roster { lines: RosterLine[]; expansion } — sugar (item 101).
group { name; quarters: Id[]; expansion } — sugar (item 101): a region label group on §9.1's quarter tree.
drawFootprint { polygon; cls?; use?; heights?: Partial<Heights> }.
build { plot; cls; use?; footprint?; heights? }.
moveFootprint { id; deltaCm: VecCm; rotateCdeg? }.
swapUse { a; b }.
fill { scope: EditScope; arrangement: SitePlan['arrangement']; cls? }.
setAttr { id; path; value } and setAttrMany { ids (resolved at dry run); query?: Query (kept for display); path; value }.
paint { target 'roofKind'|'roofColour'|'wallColour'; ids (resolved under the brush); brush: BrushPath; value }.
paintGround { region; cover; colour? } — a style region (FTG's texture brush), outside the model digest.

instance { entity; ordinal?; point?; op 'add'|'move'|'remove'|'restyle'; to?; style?: Partial<InstanceStyle> } — for an ordinal-addressed event the dry run fills point with the instance's generated position; InstanceStyle is §8.10's.

delete { id }, merge { ids }, split { id; cut: PointCm[] }, join { ids } — on plots split and join are item 31's splitting and fusion; delete never removes a dossier-backed element — it becomes rejectSite (§7.7).

rejectSite { element (dossier-backed assignment or its placed member); site (the plot); op 'reject'|'lift' } — item 20 (b): a rejection, never a removal; its lapse is written by the epoch or dossier event that causes it (§7.7).

placeAt { plot; element? (dossier-backed element or member pinned here); designation?: Designation (§4.7 S11); lift?; from?: PointsForm (one point: the plot derived) } — item 20 (g): positive placement; lift frees the plot.
setEntrance { building; op 'add'|'move'|'remove'; index?; role?; wing?; side?; offsetCm? } — item 29: the main entrance may be moved along the footprint side §2.6 rule 1 puts it on, never removed.
drawPassage { plot; from; to; widthCm } — item 30 (c): a covered passage under the front building's ground storey as §2.5's passage face; sealing and reopening are convert ops (§4.11).

drawTunnel { points; kind: Tunnel['kind']; widthCm?; headroomCm?; system? (item 65: a gallery of that system, in its part; absent: a sewer network tunnel, part 0) } — items 11, 12: a tunnel chain on the underground arena, never a drawWay (U2 forbids); width and headroom default to II.7.2's profile row; navigable derived (§2.7).
drawChamber { system; polygon; floorCm? } — item 65: a chamber of an underground system in its part (II.7.6).
addLink { a; b; kind: UndergroundLink['kind']; via } — item 65: a link between two elements of different parts (II.7.6); its knownTo by setAttr.
addUndergroundAccess { building; target? (an element, else the closure's target order II.7.6); kind? } — item 66: an access from a building's basement, a closure edit (§7.3 item 9).

placeAccess { kind; role; ground: PointCm; element (tunnel, gallery, chamber or underground building it reaches, II.7.4; an older event's tunnel reads as element, §7.5) } — item 12 (d): a new AccessPoint opening at ground, its access_point vertex placed on element's kerb or wall at the nearest point; its underground end moved by moveVertex, its opening by setAttr on ground.at (re-hosted by pointLocate, ground.host rewritten, refused as F-EDIT outside II.7.3's admitted ground); removed by delete.
setRoomRole { building; storey; room; role: RoomRole } — re-derives what hangs off roles (windows, door kinds, furniture), moves no wall.

moveWall { building; storey; wall; deltaCm } — slides a partition wall along its normal (mergeFaces then splitFace on the rung's transient arena, §3.4); both rooms re-checked against their rows' minimum area — F-EDIT when one falls below.

splitRoom { building; storey; room; cut: [PointCm, PointCm]; roles? } (splitFace); mergeRooms { building; storey; rooms: [Id, Id]; role? } (mergeFaces, refused across a wing joint; one room, surviving role chosen or given, removed wall's openings dropped).

setOpening { building; storey; wall; at?; kind 'door'|'arch'|'open'|'none' } (an entrance's door moves with its entrance via setEntrance, never removed here); setWindow { building; storey; wall; at?; op 'add'|'move'|'remove' } (exterior walls only).
moveStairCore { building; core; bay: Polygon } — moves the bay on every storey it serves; each storey's partition re-runs around it, plan.layout kept where the wing is unchanged.

setRoomUnit { building; storey; room; unit? } — item 28 (f): the household whose dwelling unit the room belongs to (§2.6 Room.unit); absent for shared, service or circulation rooms; F-EDIT when it would leave a unit without its own door onto circulation or the street.

revert { id } — "reset to generated": one undoable event applying, in reverse log order, the inverses of every logged event whose target is this entity (its own edits only, never a creation or dossier event, §7.4); ctrl / cmd+click (§14's keymap, MFCG's ctrl-click reset).

regenerate { scope: EditScope; mode 'keep'|'newRandom'; rerolls: Record<Id | RungKey, number> (absolute, per scope entity; with rung the rung's counter: the rerolls actually used, §5.1 (6)); rung? 'wings'|'rooms'|'plan'|'plan.layout'|'plan.roles'|'plan.furnish' (item 28: New random on one rung of one building, advancing that counter only; absent: the whole scope); discardEdits?; fates: EditFate[] }.
adjust { param; value; fromStage: StageId; fates } — Adjust, and Re-derive from stage k.
setField { field 'prosperity'|'density'|'greenery'|'terrain'; stroke: FieldStroke } — a relative Δ; the stroke list is composited once (§7.2).
assign { assignment: Assignment } / unassign { id }.
moveLabel { id; placement: Placement } / hideLabel { id; hidden } — LabelEntity.pinned / hidden, model data (§9).
setLayer { layer: Layer; spec: Partial<LayerSpec> }.

editTable { table: TableId; ops: RowOp[]; provenance? 'host'; fates? (confirmed fates of §7.6's fallback re-derivation from the table's first reader stage) }; editPreset { preset; ops; provenance?; fates? }; setStyle { ops; provenance? }.

rerollLayer { concern: RerollableConcern (generated from the registry, §6.1); salt (town-wide: the new salt; 0 with ids); ids? (naming only); salts?: Record<Id, number> (with ids: per-entity salts actually used, §6.3) }.
convert { op: ConversionOp (§4.11) }.

startWorks { target; kind: Works['kind']; startWeek? (default the document's week); change?: WorksChange (the hand change the Works shows — build, convert, join, split or delete — folded at once at this event's position under its seq, author and session, carrying no EditBase fields of its own, §4.11 (1); absent only for a repair, decay or clear of the target) } / cancelWorks { works } — item 67: a timed Works on the weekly clock (§4.11; J-A67.72).
placeLight { kind (a light rule row's kind); point; host? (default the entity under the point); heightCm? } — item 68: a hand-placed LightSource (§2.7).
closeup { district; strategy: FabricStrategyId; params } — logged before the first edit inside a close-up (PART II).
epoch { epoch; inputs: EpochInputs } — an epoch is an event in the log (§4.11).

rebase { reason: RebaseReason; stateDigest: Hash128; version (the output version whose model packages computed stateDigest — the document's output version from this event on; a frozenImport sets it to the library's current version, §2.9 steps 2-3); at (the log head its state materialises: the previous event's seq, or h₀ when kept after edits during load verification, §2.9 step 4; any other value refused with E_REBASE_AT, nothing appended, §14) }.
upgrade { from; to; mapping: MigrationMap (§7.5); baseDigest? (with a rebased base: base.state's model root under to, checked by later loads, §2.9 step 3, §7.5) } — undoable.
undo { of (seq of the event undone, or of the first event of its group) } — applied at the head through the same fold (§7.4); redo { of (seq of the undo it reverses) }.
RowOp = { op 'set'|'insert'|'delete'; rowKey; field?; value?; baseRowHash?: Hash64 } — rows by stable key, never by position.
WarpKernel = 'displace'|'liquify'|'relax'|'bloat'|'pinch'|'equalize'|'swirl'|'jitter'; WarpStroke = { kernel; centre; radiusCm; innerRadiusCm?; strength; dragCm?: VecCm }.

WithoutBase<E> = an event's own fields member by member, EditBase fields removed; WorksChange = WithoutBase<Extract<EditEvent, { t: 'build'|'convert'|'join'|'split'|'delete' }>> (J-A67.72: exactly these five kinds; its EditBase fields are the wrapping event's).

Ownership note: Designation and MutationRecord are §4.7 S11's, RoomRole and Entrance §2.6's, ConversionOp §4.11's; Works, LightSource and UndergroundLink §2.7's (rules §4.11's, §4.7's, II.7.6's); AccessPoint II.7.4's; DossierChange §7.7's; ClosureRecord §7.3 item 9's.

No event stores a VertexId, HalfEdgeId or FaceId (§2.2 rule 5): geometry is addressed by entity address, by lattice point with a role signature (bound by resolveVertexAt, never by distance alone), by a water body's address with a course-knot ordinal (§7.4's moveCourseKnot row), or by a ring; undo and redo are events like the rest (§7.4): the log only grows, which lets a host store it (§11.3).

The named actions (G-R4; O16-core) are separate operations with distinct semantics, never one flag. Regenerate (keep settings): re-derives the scope with each entity's recorded inputs and unchanged rerolls (§7.3): faithful, byte-identical when nothing upstream changed; used after a lock or a drawn constraint.

New random — always on a scope (a block, a quarter, a building's rung, a person, or a rerollable layer such as the trees via rerollLayer); an unscoped new town is only the empty state's action before anything is declared (§7.3 item 10, item 101); advances the reroll of every scope entity by one, written as an absolute map (replay exact; blocks at different rerolls each move on); an unchanged scope entity advances again under §5.1 (6)'s check.

A designation change is neither: assign, unassign, a setAttr on a plot's use or class, a relocated use and a dossier event run §4.7 S11's mutation of the standing design toward the new designation's template (kept parts kept, additions and subtractions recorded) — never a re-derivation, never a re-roll (§7.3 item 8, item 18); a click on a stale elaboration rung re-derives it the same way from its canonical prior (§7.3's table: the stored plan, else the as-built plan carried along §2.6's interior ladder — never the cache; item 28, item 28 (f)).

Adjust re-solves with a changed parameter; locality promised only for parameters the control registry (§7.8) lists as consumed at S10 or later or that carry a spatial scope (a district's density, a block's granularity); a parameter consumed earlier (seed, rung, water setting and side, walls, castle option, gate count, planned ↔ organic, wealth level, the recipe's pack list) has no local operator and is offered as Re-derive from stage k: everything from Sk down re-derives with carry-over (§6.3) after the user confirms the edit-fate report.

Same kind, new seed is Enter's successor (new document with seed + 1 keeping the recipe and the dossier, §6.1); per district (PART II) it is New random on the district; Surprise me is a new document whose intent is drawn from the intent.surprise stream of a fresh seed and written into its recipe (§7.7).

Warp is MFCG's staged edit: strokes in a warp session preview on the L1 overlay at interactive rate (vertex moves and a redraw of affected tiles, no invariants, §8.8); Apply commits one warp event holding the strokes in order (committed only on Apply); Discard drops them; on Apply and every replay each stroke is applied as its operation to the geometry current at that log position, never as stored displacements: the operation computes a displacement field over the vertices under the brush and the kernel's warp(field, fromLevel, region) applies it with §3.6's whole-step validation, halving, re-seating, sliding and held vertices (the dry run lists held entities), re-deriving locally any face then failing a class floor, logged; point-standing records move with their host face and every moved footprint, trace and deck is re-based (§7.4); a fromLevel = 0 warp moving water hands the moved shores to S1's water operator as its new water (§7.3 (b) 1).

Warp kernels vs MFCG tools: displace (drags vertices by dragCm: full weight inside innerRadiusCm, falling linearly to 0 at radiusCm); liquify (displace with a smooth cosine falloff over the whole radius); relax (Laplacian relaxation toward equal edge lengths); bloat (each L1 cell under the brush grows about its centroid by strength, neighbours yielding); pinch (each L1 cell shrinks about its centroid); equalize (each cell moves its vertices strength × 20 % toward regularFit's targets, §3.4 — MFCG's tool is its castle routine, §4.8, item 45); Rotate → the rotation view key (§2.9): whole-map rotation about the frame centre as view state, never a vertex operation; model north (+y) unchanged; compass view key trueNorth (default) or free; exports apply rotation per §11.1 (J-DET-15); Measure → the measure tool of §9.5, view data, no model event; swirl (our local rotation about the brush centre); jitter (seeded random displacement from warp.jitter).
equalize moves vertices strength × 20 % toward targets per application.

Pointer samples resampled along arc length to spacing ≥ minEdge, simplified with a topology-preserving Visvalingam at minEdge; a self-crossing stroke split into simple runs before insertChain (§3.4); drawWater's add rings unioned by the boolean engine and subtract rings a land brush (island = subtract ring inside an add ring; overlapping sea shapes union — FTG's method); rivers and canals take a line and width; drawBoundary selects L1 cells whose area lies ≥ 50 % inside the drawn polygon, the district boundary becoming those cells' boundary; the dry run shows the snapped boundary before commit (J-DET-14); a drawWay of class bridge across a river face places its Bridge by §4.2 S1 (5)'s drawn-bridge rule, S4's operator routing the ends to its deck (§7.3).

drawFootprint places a hand-drawn footprint (concave allowed, simple) on the plot containing it — spanning several plots proposes their JOIN in the dry run; on unplotted land (green, residue, field) creates a plot around it with access to the nearest way, or returns a conflict if none reachable — the host plot's site plan re-fitted around it as a fixed slot (buildings no longer fitting listed in the fate report); build places a building of a class on a plot (site plan picks the footprint when none given) — §4.11's build(...); moveFootprint moves or turns a footprint, leaving its plot re-homes it with both site plans re-fitted; swapUse exchanges two buildings' uses, households and assignments atomically, footprints staying (two relocateUse conversions under one event, item 17); a use is opened, closed or relocated by hand via convert openUse/closeUse/relocateUse, the building persisting vacant or converted; fill forces an arrangement on the scope's plots and re-runs S11 there.

setEntrance adds, moves or removes a side, rear, yard or service door under §2.6's rules and never removes the main entrance (movable only along the §2.6 rule 1 side); setAttr(basement) overrides the derived basement decision (an edited attribute); drawPassage reserves a covered passage face (§2.5) giving the plots behind their access rows; convert sealPassage/openPassage sets Passage.sealed; Passage.headroomCm and Passage.frontBuilding are derived (S11 writes them with the spanning wings' spans; a heights edit of a spanning wing re-derives the headroom; the event making the front building a footprint trace or tombstone clears frontBuilding) and have no edit kind.

setAttr(knownTo) hides or reveals a place's name and purpose for §9.2's label policy; a knownTo the dossier set is dossier-owned and a map setAttr of it is refused (F-EDIT dossier-owned; §7.7 items 7, 11; J-A20.77), while a label's display text and visibility (§9.1) and a viewer's knowledge key (§11.3) remain map-side choices (item 30); a front's concealed programme (item 63) is edited through setEntrance and the plan events.

The plan events edit a building's stored plan storey by storey, the first storing the composition (§2.6), each dry-run against §13.2's plan bars on the overlay, so a move leaving a room below its row's minimum or unreachable, or a unit without its own door (item 28 (f)), returns F-EDIT, never a silent repair; a building's household count is changed by hand through convert relet (§4.11) within §2.6's capacity, marking an unstored plan stale and re-cutting a stored one inside the event (§7.3); an edit lowering a building's capacity below its households re-homes the excess by §2.6's capacity rule, each move among its fates (§7.3 item 4); a click on a building or neighbourhood logs nothing (item 28 (c)).

paint sets roof kind, roof colour or wall colour on every building whose footprint centroid lies under the brush path (ids resolved at dry run and stored); paintGround records a ground-cover region in the style (pixels only); the tree brush is a batch of instance events on the entities under the brush (§8.10), one undo step; painting trees where no green entity exists first logs a drawGreen (a wood on open land, a yard_planting in a yard); instance events also carry close-up presentation edits (II.4); field brushes are setField strokes (§7.2); the terrain brush's water mode chooses locked (default) or follow.

A lock with paths fixes chosen attributes of a person (name, age, role …); New random on a person re-derives it with a new reroll keeping locked paths; relations and schedules are not re-derived by a person reroll (town-wide, §10); setAttrMany edits many entities at once (job, workplace, schedule, household relocation) from a query resolved to ids at dry run and stored (replay never re-runs the query), one undo step.

Every generated element is editable; every rule table and preset is editable (§7.6), by a user through the preference layer and by us through new table versions; edits are first-class events that persist (the log, §2.9), undo (§7.4; undo/redo are log events so they work in a shared document), survive regeneration (§7.2-§7.3) and migrate (§7.5); the generator repairs around them locally (§7.3, F-REDERIVE); the preference and override layer sits above the defaults (§7.6); the entity registry (§2.8) declares each type's edit kinds with their undo path and lifecycle row; its completeness test is §13.2's (§2.8).

terrain: setField(terrain) with water 'locked' or 'follow'; drawWater (hollows and lakes); setAttr on site features; setAttr on geology — an override of S1's value (§2.3), re-deriving the underground systems that read it (II.7.6's caverns).
water, coast, rivers: drawWater, moveVertex on shores and coasts, moveCourseKnot on a river's control knots, setAttr (bank class), delete.
ways, junctions, bridges: drawWay (class bridge for a new crossing), moveVertex, warp, split, merge, delete, setAttr (class, width, surface, name; a bridge's kind).

districts: drawBoundary (points form, item 101), quarter (sugar), merge, split, setAttr (kind, name, per-district intent DistrictIntent §7.7 layer 2, identity — an override of the derived identity, item 72; §4.5), regenerate, adjust; setAttr(fabric) + regenerate is a stage-2 template replacement; derived with no edit kind: the character vector and band range (§4.5), pressure (written only by epochs), nameHistory (written by §6.3 case (5) and by a dossier rename, §2.5); an undercity neighbourhood (II.7.5) is a district like any, with convert clearUndercity.
reservations (§2.5): setAttr on a market's rank (principal or secondary, item 24) — a Re-derive from S3 with its fate report, §4.2 S3 (12)'s batch taking the edited rank as a fixed input (J-A24.71).

blocks, plots: split and join (item 31: least-disruption re-cut of §4.7 S10 (7) with S11's mutator, neighbours fixed, undo exact, §7.4), merge, fill, setAttr (use, owner, knownTo; tenure — derived from owner and band, the edit an override kept like knownTo, item 70; a cluster's structures are buildings and a re-pack is its plot's regenerate; frontJitterCm — 0 or in [jitter.minM, jitter.maxM], footprint re-fitted by S11's mutator with neighbours fixed, item 43; a block's reach — open, passage or gated — re-deriving the block's interior by S10 (7)'s re-cut with neighbours fixed, J-A30.72; never builtBand or builtProsperity (derived, written only by §4.11's floor paragraph paths, J-A31.44, J-A31.71); never fieldBand (written only by a derivation reading the current field and by the epoch's re-banding, §2.5, J-A28.29); never exposure (derived from access rows); never a block's due (written only by §4.11's ladder)), regenerate, lock, assign, placeAt, rejectSite, drawPassage, convert (plotToGarden, amalgamate, subdivide, densify (infill, back_court), thin (infill, back_court), sealPassage, openPassage; §4.11).

buildings: drawFootprint, build, moveFootprint, swapUse, paint, setAttr (class, heights, roof, basement, knownTo, condition — an edited attribute §4.11's rung 1 then leaves as set, §7.2, J-A31.76), setEntrance, delete (a generator-added building only; a dossier-backed one becomes rejectSite), convert (demolish, abandon, decay, ruin, clear, rebuild; vacate, reoccupy, reuse; openUse, closeUse, relocateUse, mutate; relet within §2.6 capacity, item 28 (f); §4.11), startWorks / cancelWorks (item 67), addUndergroundAccess (item 66), assign, regenerate with rung, the plan events (item 28; setRoomUnit), lock on a room's path (plan/rooms/<id>); derived, no edit kind: nextEntrance (written by §2.6's entrance derivation and setEntrance), reusedAs (convert reuse), formerUses (use conversions closing or moving a building's use), predecessor (reuse … build), each base wing's spans (written only by S11 building or re-fitting a passage's front building, cleared by S11 or the event making it a footprint trace or tombstone, §2.6), each slot's frontage (§2.5 BuildingSlot: from the designation template, re-derived by S11's mutator) and unhoused (written by every run of §4.7's generation fill, cleared by the designation mutator).

walls, gates, towers: drawWall (points form, item 101), placeGate (sugar), moveVertex, setAttr, delete, convert (wallToWay, gateToJunction; neglect, breach, dismantle, contractWall, §4.11); derived, no edit kind: an enceinte's supersededBy (written by contractWall).

uses (§2.7): convert (openUse, closeUse, relocateUse), swapUse, setAttr (specialisation; a concealed use's concealment, front, knownTo, item 63 — dossier-owned where the dossier set them; concealmentSource written with concealment — edit for a map value — no edit kind of its own), assign / unassign and the assignment's pinned (§7.7); a use's address moves with it (§6.3).

institutions (§2.7): setAttr (knownTo, name, concealment, front, powers), assign / unassign (§7.7); a dossier-set value (a dossier-named institution's name or kind, knownTo, concealment, front or powers, its assignment's state (item 80), a claimed quarter name (item 82)) is dossier-owned — a map setAttr returns F-EDIT dossier-owned and changes nothing, while a label's display text and visibility (§9.1) and a viewer's knowledge key (§11.3) remain map-side choices (§7.7 items 7, 11; J-A20.77).

tunnels, galleries, chambers, links, access points (II.6, II.7; staged, editable in the base): galleries are drawTunnel with its system and chambers drawChamber, each in its system's part (J-A65.71), edited like tunnels (moveVertex, setAttr on kind, depth, width and knownTo, delete, convert silt, caveIn, seal, reopen and flood, II.6, item 65; a gallery's walkway derived by II.7.5, no edit kind); links: addLink, setAttr (kind, knownTo), delete; a buried old town is convert raiseGrade (II.7.6); tunnels: drawTunnel, moveVertex, setAttr (kind, widthCm, headroomCm — navigable re-derived, §2.7), delete, convert (silt, caveIn, seal, reopen) — a tunnel's condition is no setAttr path (reads existence and closure; a condition change is the matching convert, J-A11.21); the profile preset is II.7.2's network choice, not a tunnel field; access points: placeAccess (from public ground), addUndergroundAccess (from a basement, a closure), moveVertex on the access_point vertex, setAttr (kind, role, state — open, locked or bricked, a collapsed reading never set — knownTo, item 64; ground.at re-hosted by pointLocate, refused as F-EDIT outside II.7.3's admitted ground), delete; setLayer on underground is the CITY / METROPOLIS visibility toggle (§7.8); J-A12.71.

sky islands (II.6; staged, editable in the base): setAttr (area, altitude, state), lock, convert (resizeIsland, settleIsland, fallIsland, refloatIsland, raiseIsland); recipe.layers.islands is an adjust re-deriving from S7b (§7.8).

terrain and water conversions (§4.11, item 25): convert (reclaim, siltReach, shiftCourse, digCanal — the slow conversions the evolution engine will schedule, usable by hand now), repaired through S1's terrain or water operator or the carve (a marsh's reclaim by the terrain operator §7.3 (a); a foreshore's reclaim, siltReach and shiftCourse by the water operator §7.3 (b); digCanal by the carve §4.11); derived, no edit kind: LandUse.reclaimed (written by reclaim, §2.3).

works (§4.11, item 67; J-A67.71): startWorks, cancelWorks, setAttr on the Works (startWeek, its duration within its WorksTable row) — its stage at a week derived, never set. lights (§2.7, item 68; J-A68.72): placeLight, setAttr (kind, heightCm, colour, intensity, radiusCm; point — re-hosted by pointLocate on its host's PlatKey, refused as F-EDIT off its host), delete, lock; derived lights (lit windows, the plan rung's room lights) have no edit kind; the view's light keys (§2.9) are not logged.

greenery, trees: drawGreen, tree brush, instance, setAttr, delete. fields: setField (prosperity, density, greenery); setAttr on the town's FieldBands (an explicit re-banding) — both authorial: the blocks they re-derive past τ take the new field as their built state and their plots' builtBand (§7.2, item 31). names, labels: setAttr (text; a label's displayText, §9.1, cleared by revert), moveLabel, hideLabel, rerollLayer(naming) town-wide or on chosen ids, group (region label group RegionGroup, §9.1, sugar, item 101; renamed by setAttr, removed by delete); a name the dossier gave or claimed is dossier-owned, its label's display text a map-side choice (item 20 (h)).

layers, style: setLayer, setStyle, paintGround; view keys are not logged (§2.9). people, households: setAttr, setAttrMany, lock with paths, regenerate (person scope), pin; a household's building and dwelling unit (§2.7, item 28 (f)) follow relet and item 17's relocation (§4.11, §10.3), never a bare setAttr. close-ups (stage 2): every kind above on close-up entities after closeup; instance for presentation edits. rule tables, presets: editTable, editPreset (§7.6). history: epoch, convert, rebase, upgrade, undo, redo; the dossier events — assign, unassign and setAttr with EditBase.dossier and EditBase.dossierChange set, produced by the dossier port and folded in the host's order (§7.7, items 73, 75); the creation prefix's assign events carry EditBase.creation (§7.4).

Every event is validated before commit on the scratch overlay: the schema, the batch-local and stage-end invariants of its scope (§5.3), and the edit-fate report of its effective scope with its case-(4) renames (§7.3 item 4); for a chained operator (§7.3 item 3) the whole chain runs on the overlay so the report lists every re-sited bridge, re-routed or cut way and re-based building before commit; for a declaration's points form the derived shape with its handles; for an area declaration (quarter, fill, roster) the plots, households and buildings it will hold — the count the ghost's badge shows (§9.5; item 101 R14); for undo or redo, §7.4's independence check; conflicts come back as actions (F-EDIT), never silently resolved; a warp that would break an invariant is halved and reported.

An E_KEPT conflict (the edit would cross or clear finer content an earlier stage made, or content outside a coarse edit's clear region, §3.3) is offered with one resolution: start the re-derivation at the stage that made that content (for a wall's band parts or a margin band's part, S10's step (0) for the wall strips of the touched run or for the scope's side of the touched stretch, §4.7, §7.3 item 2); a host's bridge commands map onto these events (§11.3).

A dossier event or positive placement is dry-run like any edit: its disruption (every moved use, joined or vacated plot and mutated building, each with the causing rule) computed against the request kind's budget row (§7.7) and stored in EditBase.disruption; a dossier event over budget still lands (dossier authority absolute) and is reported over budget; a user's positive placement over budget, or one no plot satisfies inside the hard rows, returns F-EDIT with the closest acceptable sites (§4.7 S10b); a join or split of plots that would remove an occupied building returns F-EDIT "vacate first" (item 17's relocation) unless the user confirms the demolition as a fate (item 31); a map event without EditBase.dossier that would close, remove or re-designate a dossier-backed element returns F-EDIT with rejectSite and placeAt offered (J-A20.75); a map event changing a dossier-owned value returns F-EDIT dossier-owned with the map-side alternative named where there is one (§5.2).

The authoring toolkit (owner: "come up with an elegant set of tools for both an ai clerk and a user where a dedicated user can build it or emulate it"): declare, then derive — authoring is a set of DECLARATIONS, each one of the events above or sugar over one, with one dry run, one fate report, one commit and one undo; the rules derive everything undeclared (item 20 (h) applied to human input): a declared fact stays fixed like a dossier fact until its author changes it (§7.2; §2.8's factTier reads it declared); a declaration is refused only where it contradicts a dossier fact or a lock (reason and closest acceptable declarations, item 20 (g); F-EDIT); every other infeasible declaration is bent by its dry run to the nearest lawful one, named in one line (item 101 R2); emulating a city = declaring intent, bones and programme (L0-L2), building it = declaring the fabric too (L3-L4).

The twelve tools in five layers (author may stop at any layer; everything below derived): L0 intent — T1 intend (the recipe's intent at creation, §7.7 layer 1: site, size, form, era and style, prosperity, walls; afterwards the Adjust and Re-derive events of the basic panel's controls, its sliders, §7.8); L1 ground and bones — T2 ground (setField(terrain), warp, drawWater (points and level forms), moveCourseKnot), T3 wall (drawWall points form, placeGate), T4 road (drawWay with class; across water a bridge; points form), T5 quarter (quarter); L2 programme — T6 place (placeAt point form, assign, build, drawFootprint), T7 roster (roster); L3 fabric — T8 fill (fill, setField density/greenery/prosperity, drawGreen; its three variations §7.3 item 10), T9 shape (split, join, drawFootprint, moveFootprint, setAttr, setEntrance, paint, the plan events), T10 hold (lock, pin, revert, regenerate keep or New random on a scope); L4 finish — T11 name (setAttr(name), moveLabel, hideLabel, group), T12 dress (setStyle, setLayer, paintGround; furniture §9.5, exports §11; the underlay is view state).
owner_raw: determinism (tool home; UI surfaces V09, V10)

statement: A new capability adds a parameter to an existing tool, never a thirteenth tool (§13.2's elegance bars).

Sugar events are logged as themselves (one undo step, one fate report) and expanded at their fold into the events they stand for by the sugar expansion table (sugar.json, §7.6) at the version the event records (expansion), so replay and upgrade expand exactly as the session did (§7.5); what an expansion creates is minted from the sugar event's seq (§6.3). placeGate(enceinte, at) = a short through-way stub of the enceinte's gate class crossing the trace at at, square to it, so S7's operator builds the gate (a gate also arises wherever a declared road crosses a wall, §7.3's S7 row); quarter = a drawBoundary (kind's size band and snap), a whole-neighbourhood assign naming that kind as its function (read by §4.5's character as a dossier kind, a declared kind winning over an emergent identity), a setAttr(name) and, when a band is given, a setField(prosperity) stroke moving the boundary's mean to the band's centre; roster = one assign per line (class, name, locus as PlacementCriteria hints) in one group solved together by §4.7 S10b's solver in one dry run in claims-first order, a line the rules cannot honour listed with its closest options and not committed; with a dossier connected a line must name a dossier element (RosterLine.element) and expands to its placeAt, a line naming none returns F-EDIT dossier-owned with the dossier's unplaced elements offered; group(name, quarters) creates a named region label group over §9.1's quarter tree nodes.

drawBoundary, drawWater, drawWall, drawWay and placeAt take a points form; the dry run derives the shape with the operator that builds that class and stores it resolved in the event's geometry fields (no replay or later derivation re-derives or moves an accepted shape): a quarter grows from its seed along block edges to its kind's size band by §4.5's grower (two to four points give its far edges; a lasso its outline), snapped to street centre-lines, water, walls and ridges, never through a block, the kind steering the snap (harbour hugs the shore, manor prefers high dry ground, market centres on a square); a lake fills S1's basin to the declared level; a river runs source to mouth by S1's water operator; a coast and harbour take a sea level and one shore point with a basin size, quays by §4.8's harbour rules; a wall follows ridges and contours between points by S5a's trace, closing when ends meet; a road joins two points by S4's router with its class (§4.3); a place takes the plot its point selects (the plot under it, else the nearest lawful one by §4.7 S10b) and S11's site plan. The derived shape keeps four to eight handles by default (more on demand); dragging one is a new declaration of the same kind on the same entity (drawBoundary with the district's id, moveVertex, moveCourseKnot); the authoring surface's feature snap (§9.5) is visible and escapable and resolved into the event's points before the dry run; the kernel's attraction (§3.6) applies to every insertion and is never escaped; a brush is many seeds and a lasso many points: one event kind per thing.
Derived shapes keep four to eight handles by default.

The canvas (§14's reference UI), the clerk's tool API (over §11.2's embedding API) and the skeleton file (§11.1 — ordered declarations imported as the log's creation prefix and read ahead by their stages, §4.1, §7.7) produce identical events; a clerk's proposal is a dry run shown as a ghost; accepted, it commits with proposedBy 'clerk' and the user as author (J-A101.74); the clerk never bypasses the dry run or the undo, never writes a dossier fact, and reads only what its viewer may know (§9.2); the tool API and these events are the base's; the built-in clerk and plots on a bridge deck are staged (Staged by the owner's roadmap).
owner_raw: determinism (surfaces: V09 application, V10 clerk, §11.1 skeleton)

statement: DECLARATION / SUGAR EVENT / POINTS FORM / HANDLE / GHOST / CLERK: authoring vocabulary of item 101.

Protection: a locked entity (or locked attribute paths) is a fixed input — regeneration never changes it and re-derives dependants around it; a pinned entity keeps its existence and position, other attributes may re-derive; an edited attribute implicitly pins that attribute and the entity's existence against Regenerate and New random (IMPROVEMENTS O9) unless the user chooses discard edits in scope, only by confirming the fate list (§7.3 item 4), recorded in the event; an assigned attribute is held at its assignment within the drift bounds (§7.7).

A dossier-backed element (existence 'dossier') has its existence held on every map: a map delete is recorded as rejectSite (§7.7); a map event that would close, remove or re-designate it is refused as F-EDIT (§7.7 item 2's list); a regeneration under it re-places it by §4.7 S10b's solver when its plot goes; its position is not held unless the assignment is pinned or a positive placement pins it; a positive placement (placeAt) pins its element or designation to its plot and is kept by every re-derivation and dossier re-application that can honour it, reported when one cannot.

Every finer face under a locked or pinned entity is a fixed input too; under a warp or smoothing step the kernel holds its route vertices as §3.6 states, so "keeps its position" holds for plots, blocks and buildings (which carry no vertex roles); the dry run lists the held entities; when protections and inputs meet, §7.7's precedence order decides.

Every entity an authoring declaration made, placed or shaped is held without a lock: the declaring event pins it (existence and position; other attributes may re-derive) — a drawn feature is locked besides, a placed or assigned thing held as placeAt and assignments hold it, a quarter's boundary and a points form's derived shape pinned by their event, a hand-placed light by placeLight — so Regenerate, New random, every scoped re-roll, an epoch and every later derivation keep it (§5.3's declared row), the regenerate brush skips it, the fates list names it kept (declared) (§7.3 item 4); its author changes it by a new declaration (handle drag), by unpin, or by undoing the declaring event; a skeleton's declarations are held the same way (§4.1); the pieces a closure edit created (§7.3 item 9) are held while the creating edit is live.

Drawn constraints (ways, water, walls, greens, district boundaries, footprints) enter the plat through insertChain as mandatory chains with their roles (§3.6) after §7.1's resampling; locked by default; apply at their log position: inserted into the current state and, for the coarsest faces its chain touches, its class's local operator (§7.3) re-derives the affected scope — drawn water via S1's water operator (re-sites crossings on moved reaches, re-routes ways using them), drawn ways via S4 and S5 (arterials re-route to reuse them), drawn walls via S7's run re-trace, drawn boundaries via S6's regrouping, drawn greens via S12 on covered faces, drawn footprints via S11 on the host plot; session and replay run the same code at the same log position in the same canonical insertion order (same digest, §6.5).

The old rule "insert before the stage that would create the class" survives only as the explicit action Rebuild around my drawings: it moves the drawn constraints into the recipe as constraints of their stages, regenerates the town, shows the diff as a migration does (§7.5) and commits as a rebase (reason drawnConstraintsRebuilt) (J-DET-6).

Field brushes: a stroke is a relative Δ over the driver field (FieldStroke); the field is the driver field plus the stroke list composited in log order and clamped once at the end, so undo removes a stroke and re-composites exactly (a per-stroke clamp is not exact: +0.3 then −0.3 on 0.9 would give 0.7); a stroke re-derives every block whose plot samples moved — against the samples their DerivationRecord holds (§2.8) — by more than τ = 0.01 of the field's range, same τ on replay; bands move only as §4.5 states (a stroke in one quarter never re-bands another); an epoch keeps the stroke list and re-composites it over its new drivers; a brush is authorial: the blocks it re-derives take the new field as their built state (S10 and S11 read it; plots' builtBand set to the band they are re-cut for), so the static base behaves as before item 31, whose geometry floor governs wealth change over epochs only (§4.11; J-A31.72); an epoch never re-derives a block by τ — it acts on survivors only through §4.11's ladder bounded by the floor.
Field re-derivation threshold τ = 0.01 of the field's range.

Terrain brush: edits the heightfield raster under S1's terrain operator (§7.3 (a)) with the same stroke list and single clamp (to the declared relief limit, §2.3); water mode locked (default): stroke masked (Δ zero) on every cell whose centre lies in a water face or within one cell of a shore or bank edge, and under footprints, bands and decks of locked or pinned entities; land cells near the sea keep §4.2 S1 (2)'s floor (a lowering stroke cannot sink the coast); water bodies, courses and widths unchanged; dry run shows masked cells; follow: stroke may change bed and bank cells; every reach whose bed cells changed is re-traced by S1's water operator (§7.3 (b)), re-siting crossings and re-routing ways; in both modes the terrain operator re-bases every building, wing, tower, gate, wall vertex, bridge and pier whose terrain samples changed, re-runs drainage locally, re-evaluates terrain-reading field drivers (authorial like a brush) so the town stands as a reload would compute (J-DET-24), and re-derives the basement decision of every building whose terrain gate changed (§2.6, item 29).

Effective scope: regenerate(scope) finds the coarsest faces covering the scope at its level; that set (possibly larger than the drawn area) is the effective scope, shown before commit and stored in the event as the resolved EditScope; for a chained edit, the union of every chained operator's scope; for a designation change, dossier event, positive placement or relocation (item 8), the plots the placement and mutation touched (the site, its joined neighbour if any, each displaced use's new site) bounded by the request kind's disruption budget (§7.7), except a dossier event over budget, whose scope is its least-disruptive placement's touched set, reported over budget (§7.7 item 5).

Stored compositions, spanned passages and re-homed households (§2.6): the edit storing a composition (and every event whose re-cut of a stored plan establishes J-P48 (1) for its new walls) holds the faces sharing an edge J-P48 (1) splits and the row neighbours' wing rings its carry changes; an edit whose batches change a Passage face (L3) or move one of its vertices holds the passage's front building when its stored composition has a wing spanning the passage; an event changing a spanning wing's heights or making its building a footprint trace or tombstone holds the passage it spans, rewriting headroomCm or frontBuilding; an edit lowering a building's capacity below its households holds that building, the buildings §2.6's capacity rule re-homes into and, where §4.7 re-provides a dossier household's housing, the plots its dossier request touches, bounded as a dossier event's scope is.
