Seam exception: a district-scoped re-derivation's effective scope also includes its bounding ways' chains and Corridor records, the half-corridor strips on both sides and the junction wedges at the vertices its batches insert or remove on those spines — on a neighbour's side only II.1 (3)'s neighbour step, one corridor_split edge and the one kerb vertex it lands on (promoted) or adds —, the neighbouring cells, plots and footprints whose rings pass through those vertices and the wing rings of their buildings (§2.6), all changed only by those vertices (a promoted vertex returns to its level when the lane goes, §2.2 rule 3), and the Seam records it is party to (§4.6, II.4).

Tree scoping (L1 cells and below): every unprotected finer entity under the effective scope is discarded and the refinement stages re-run for those faces — recorded inputs and unchanged rerolls for Regenerate (keep settings), advanced rerolls for New random; the batch's rederivesFrom and kept finer content follow §3.3; sound by over-invalidation; the primary mechanism.

The L3 parts S10's step (0) builds on both sides of an L1 edge two face sets share without corridors (§4.7) are cleared by a re-derivation from S8, S9 or S10 inside its scope; a scope holding wall-strip faces, or faces bordering the settlement perimeter or a reservation boundary two districts share, re-runs step (0) for its own side's parts after its S8 and S9 (first when it re-derives from S10), before its plots: bandUnion restricted to the scope's faces, cross edges ending on the shared edge by attraction onto the other side's vertices, and the scope's plot, alley and furlong lines ending on the re-laid band's inner edge; the other side is never written; so a Regenerate (keep settings) of a perimeter district lays the same backland part, and of the hinterland (S12 row) the same headland, byte-identical to the one-click result. Measurement (M2a, B-EDIT): Regenerate (keep settings) of a perimeter district, a walled district and the hinterland on B-CITY-lite seeds is byte-identical; pre-decided fallback: cover both sides of every shared stretch the scope borders (other side's parts and fronting blocks re-derive from S10 with the scope, declared in its effective scope) (J-DET-29).
S13a re-derives label candidates inside the scope and draws names only in §6.3's draw cases; the display list, tiles and label placement update as §8.1 item 4 and §9.2 state.

Replay mode (load verification, migration, undo beyond the scoped records, the undo of an upgrade after a reload) folds the log through exactly the session's code path: every model stage, S13a's scoped delta included, runs at its event's log position (name uniqueness resolved scope by scope in log order, §9.6; moveLabel, hideLabel and setAttr(name) address LabelEntity records and names S13a creates mid-log); only the view stages wait: S14 and S13b run once at the end (J-DET-21).

L1 and L0 are not per-face refinements (S4 routes across the frame, S5 grows a town-wide queue, S6 grows districts across cells, S7 traces an enceinte), so each has its own local operator with pinned boundaries; an operator may chain others (S1's water operator chains S4, S5, S6, S7): the chain's batches commit in the order stated, each operator draws from the operated entity's lineage under its own stage's concerns, and the whole chain runs in the dry run first (§7.1), so session and replay run the same chain at the same log position; an edit with no local operator (a parameter consumed early, §7.1) is Re-derive from stage k.

S1 terrain (terrain brush in either mode, site features, a marsh's reclaim, item 25): operator (a) — masked stroke, local drainage, terrain-reading field drivers, exact re-basing of what stands on the changed ground, slope re-sampling; in follow mode (b) for every reach whose bed changed; pinned: all water in locked mode, the heightfield outside the stroke, every way's geometry; beyond: in follow mode Re-derive from S1 when a course leaves its drainage basin or F-RIVER needs its inlet or centre rung (§5.2).

S1 water (drawWater, a moved shore or coast vertex, moveCourseKnot, a warp from level 0, the terrain brush in follow mode, siltReach, shiftCourse and a foreshore's reclaim): operator (b) in §4.11's order — new water, crossings, routes, wall runs and the chain's footprint as data; one L1 batch clearing the footprint's partition content, re-laying kept ways through their decks, re-tracing crossed wall runs and cutting lesser ways; one L0 batch inserting the water through the vertices that batch prepared, both declaring the footprint as clear region; then S5, S6, S7, tree scoping and F-REDERIVE; pinned: reaches and coasts outside the edit, every way, wall and district not named in (b), every finer face outside the footprint less the seam exception at its boundary; beyond: Re-derive from S1 when the course leaves its drainage basin or F-RIVER needs its inlet or centre rung.

S4 (drawWay of an arterial, a moved arterial vertex, a moved destination, the castle placed or resized, a deck re-sited or removed by S1's water operator): re-route only the arterials whose corridors meet the edit region or whose destination or deck moved, each between its nearest pinned nodes (junctions of degree ≥ 3 or destination nodes) on either side of the region, over S3's lattice, every deck a fixed graph edge; pinned: their endpoints and every spine outside the region; beyond: a gate-count change (a destination added or removed) re-derives from the stage picking those gates — S3 for stage 1 (§4.2 S3 (7)), S5 of its stage for a later enceinte (§4.4).

S5 (drawWay of a secondary, a deleted street, a secondary now crossing water off a deck): regrow only inside the affected L1 cells from the proposals whose origins lie there, under S5c's legality (water only on a deck); pinned: the cells' boundary spines; beyond: none.

S6 (drawBoundary, district merge or split, outskirtToDistrict, land vacated or covered by a moved channel): regroup and re-type only the districts touching the region, the grower restricted to their cells, turn skips and picks from district.seed keyed by each grower's seed lineage and turn (§4.5, §6.1; item 47), so unchanged cells regroup as before; then re-lay the margin bands: along every L1 edge without corridors whose sharing changed (moved perimeter stretch, a reservation boundary two districts now share) S10's step (0) lays the 2 m band on both sides, and where a merge or conversion ends the sharing it removes both parts; blocks fronting such a stretch on either side (neighbour's or hinterland's included) re-derive from S10 and join the effective scope shown in the dry run; pinned: every other district and every block fronting no changed stretch.
Margin band width 2 m (S10's step (0)).

S7 (drawWall, a moved trace vertex, wallToWay, gateToJunction, a river crossing an enceinte moved; a declared way of a class above lane crossing an enceinte — a placeGate's stub or a declared road, item 101): re-trace only the run between the nearest unaffected towers on each side, with water gates where the course now crosses and a gate at each declared crossing (a lane across a strip stays refused, NF-P5; J-A101.76); re-cut the strips' setback and glacis lines along it; re-derive the strip blocks' S10 step (0); pinned: the rest of the trace, its gates and strips; beyond: Re-derive from S7 when the enceinte kind changes.

A carve (canal, moat or basin drawn by an edit, digCanal among them; §4.11): §4.11's way rule (pinned decks for arterials and sole connections, cuts for the rest) and footprint in its declared batch order, the channel inserted with the footprint as clear region (§3.3); pinned: every way and finer face outside the carve's footprint (§4.11: channel ⊕ (attractCm + bank setback) united with every L1 cell that buffer, the way rule and the wall re-trace touch — (b)'s footprint follows), less the seam exception; beyond: if the clear region cannot be kept, §3.3's pre-decided fallback: a declared town-wide re-derivation with the fate report.

S8-S11: per cell, block and plot (tree scope, item 2; wall-strip blocks and the scope's side of every shared margin band from S10's step (0)); pinned: the other side of every shared edge. S12: the covered hinterland faces and greenery entities; the hinterland unit re-lays its headland parts along the perimeter by step (0) first (item 2); pinned: the districts' side of the perimeter.

A designation change (assign/unassign, setAttr use or class, openUse/closeUse/relocateUse, a dossier event, placeAt, the re-placement a rejectSite causes; item 18): §4.7 S10b's solver for the site, then §4.7 S11's mutator on each placed plot (the inverse mutation on reversal); a displaced use re-placed by the same solver, one displacement level (§4.7 S10b); pinned: every plot outside the touched set, every locked part, the plots' faces beyond a joined neighbour; beyond: none (a JOIN the mutator needs is a join of the two plots, chained as item 3 states).

A plot fusion or splitting (join/split, item 31): S10 (7)'s re-cut of the members with their neighbours fixed, under the band's target, then S11's mutator on the new plots (an occupied building kept, or the edit refused, §7.1); pinned: the block's other plots and every neighbour's ring; the members' party-wall vertices on the fixed side.

A click on a stale elaboration rung (item 28; no event), the re-cut of an unstored plan along the interior ladder among them (item 28 (f)): BuildingGenerator.plan from its canonical prior — committed state, never the cache (§6.2): the stored plan where one exists, else the as-built plan (the class's programme at the plot's builtBand row with the template's households.built clamped into [1, capacity], §2.6, §10.2) carried along §2.6's interior ladder one row or one household at a time, in §2.6's order, to the occupants' current band and household count, each step §2.6's re-cut rule (FIXED set, re-derived set, kept-room rule, J-A28.26) with draws keyed by the step (§6.1); the cache holds any step already derived and is only a memo (§6.2); the wings rung likewise through compose with the stored or as-built wings as prior; pinned: everything (a click writes only the cache).

CANONICAL PRIOR: the committed-state prior a rung re-cut starts from — the stored plan, else the as-built plan carried along the interior ladder; never the cache. AS-BUILT PLAN: the class's programme at the plot's builtBand row with households.built clamped into [1, capacity].

A change of a building's plan inputs while its plan is STORED (a relet, a household moved in or out — §4.7's overflow pass, §2.6's capacity re-homing, item 17's relocation, §10.3 —, an occupants' band change at an epoch, a designation mutation; item 28 (f)): §2.6's re-cut rule run inside the changing event from the stored plan as prior, around its edited and locked rooms as fixed inputs (§7.2), one ladder step per row or household crossed, recorded in EditBase.mutations and listed as fates (item 4); an unstored plan is only marked stale (§2.8) and waits for the click (J-A28.72); pinned: the shell (wing rings read without composition-role vertices, entrances, heights, roof, basement) and every room outside the wings whose demand changed.

An edit whose prerequisites are missing (addUndergroundAccess and the other instances of item 9 (d), item 66): the closure (item 9) — its generators in dependency order on the overlay, each through its own stage's operator, as one event whose batches commit together (item 9 (a)); pinned: everything outside the closure's pieces and their clear regions.

Staged layers (II.6, II.7): a ground edit re-derives the underground blocks whose recorded ground cells its clear region covers (II.7's declared reads), a tunnel edit the blocks its edges bound, an island edit its own arena; the underground's and an island's reroll writes only its own arena (their seam exception is empty); each underground system's edit and reroll writes only its own part (§3.4, item 65) and the far link_end vertices of the links ending on it, an undercity neighbourhood's only its void system's part and its links' far ends, and a closure's underground pieces the part II.7.6 gives each; pinned: the ground arena under an underground edit, every other arena and part less those far link ends.

(a) Terrain operator: 1 Stroke — the stroke list composited on the heightfield and clamped once (§7.2) with locked mode's mask; 2 Drainage, locally — priority-flood filling and flat resolution (§2.3) on the stroke's bounding box dilated by 8 cells, ring cells' levels fixed as spill heights, the box doubling until no ring cell's filled level changes (at worst the whole hydrology grid, S1's own cost, §12.4); filled levels go into the drainage arrays (flowDir, flatRank, flowAccum) only, never the stored heights (a brushed hollow stays a hollow and drains to its spill point); accumulation re-propagated downstream along D8 from the box; a new hollow deeper than the lake threshold is reported ("a hollow: draw water to make it a pond or a lake"), never turned into water. Test (B-EDIT terrain fixtures): arrays equal a whole-grid re-run's; pre-decided fallback: re-run drainage over the whole hydrology grid (frame and margin; ≈ 16-17 ms at CITY, §2.3, §12.4), output-neutral.
Local drainage box: stroke bounding box dilated by 8 cells, doubling until stable; whole-grid fallback ≈ 16-17 ms at CITY.

(a) 3 Fields — the terrain-reading drivers (elevation above the flood line, low and damp ground, §4.5) re-evaluated on the dilated box; blocks whose plot samples moved beyond τ re-derive as for a field brush (§7.2), matching a reload (§2.9); inside an epoch event (a reclaim the engine schedules, §4.11) the re-evaluated drivers only mark due blocks for §4.11's ladder and re-derive nothing by τ. 4 Re-basing, exact — every entity on a changed sample re-based by §2.6's per-entity datum step (the function S11 and S7 call): a wing's baseCm = max(samples) + plinthCm with its foundation skirt; a row footprint whose fall now exceeds skirtMaxCm re-split into stepped wings (F-SITEPLAN's first rung; footprint face and address unchanged); towers and gates from samples under their footprints; the wall's base profile (each knot whose sample changed takes the new value; a trace vertex whose sample changed and carries no knot gains one, §2.2 rule 5); a bridge's deckCm and a pier's deck height from bank elevations plus the clearance row; a user-edited baseCm kept (fate kept, listed; J-DET-24); every building whose terrain gate changed re-derives its basement decision by §2.6 (a cellar under a raised water table becomes none, a slope past the class threshold a walk-out cellar), an edited basement kept (item 29). 5 Slopes — every way whose spine crosses changed cells re-samples slopeP95; a way now steeper than its class's limit is reported with an offer to re-route it (a regenerate through S4's or S5's operator), never re-routed silently. 6 Water — in follow mode, (b) runs for every reach whose bed cells changed.

(b) S1's water operator runs in §4.11's carve order — prepare the finer structure the new water will meet, insert the water, re-grow what it displaced — because a coarse insertion may meet finer geometry only at vertices an earlier batch of the same edit placed (§3.3); both geometry batches declare the chain's footprint as their clear region under §3.3's clearing and preparation rules (as the carve's batches (1)-(2) do); §4.11's terrain and water conversions (item 25: silting, course shift, foreshore reclamation) run through this operator as local repair, their new water or land being (1)'s data; a marsh's reclamation runs (a), digCanal the carve.

(b) 1 New water as data (nothing committed), by trigger: moveCourseKnot — the course between the moved knot's neighbours recomputed through the knots by §4.2 S1 (3)'s control-polyline construction with the moved knot fixed (an edited knot is implicitly pinned, §7.2), width and depth from accumulation, shores = course buffered by width; a carve beyond carveMaxCm returns F-EDIT with the nearest position along the drag within it. A follow terrain stroke — each reach whose bed cells changed re-traced by descent from the nearest pinned upstream point to where the new course first meets the old (or its outfall), F-RIVER's re-trace rungs confined to the reach; knots re-sampled at the control spacing with fresh ordinals, except an edited knot the new course must pass within half a control spacing of, else F-EDIT offering to discard that edit. drawWater — the drawn rings (add unioned, subtract removed; a line buffered by its width), a drawn river's or canal's course being its line. A moved shore or coast vertex, or a level-0 warp — the shores as the move leaves them (the stroke's field applied to the reach's L0 shore and coast vertices, the rest of the brush moving land at level 1 by §3.6's warp first), the course recomputed as their centreline, knots re-sampled; nothing re-traced (the user's shore authoritative, §2.3). The changed reach is where new shores differ from old; an edited coast stretch has its sea side re-lowered and contours clipped (F-CONTOUR); new shore segments take bank class and kind by §4.2 S1 (7).

(b) 2 Crossings, routes, wall runs and footprint as data: siteCrossings (§4.2 S1 (5)) on the changed reach (sites perpendicular to new flow, ends on new banks); each old deck there (built bridge or unused site) matched to its successor site (new site nearest its old midpoint within the search band, §6.3's bridge row); kept ways (F-REDERIVE) re-routed by S4's router over S3's lattice between their nearest pinned nodes — new channel ⊕ attractCm impassable except across a deck, every site a candidate deck and fixed graph edge, the way's own successor site preferred within the detour bound; F-ROUTE's rungs decide (an extra-bridge deck sited now); a deck built at every site a route uses; the one at an old deck's successor site takes the old bridge's address, name and assignments when its way uses it; every other new site stays a site (two bank vertices, no span) that (4) inserts with the shores; a way whose old deck lay on the changed reach but which the new water no longer meets keeps its geometry and (9) turns that deck into an ordinary segment; every enceinte run the new or old course crosses re-traced between its nearest unaffected towers, a water gate where the new course crosses and none at the old; the footprint computed last: with B = (new channel ∪ changed old channel) ⊕ (attractCm + bank setback), the exact union of the L1 cells that (i) B meets (vacated land and cells S6 re-assigns); (ii) border a stretch (3) cuts, prunes or replaces, or that a kept way's new route crosses; (iii) border the old run of a re-traced wall or a stretch of its setback, glacis or intervallum line (3) removes with it (between the feet of the perpendiculars from the run's end towers), or meet the re-traced run ⊕ (half its band + setback, + glacis or berm on the field side); these are the carve's footprint rules (§4.11); the fate report lists exactly the protected entities inside it.

(b) 3 One L1 batch — structure first: declares the footprint as KernelTx.clearRegion and clears it by §3.3 rule 1, structural finer edges only as it re-lays or cuts them; inserts each kept way's new route and removes the replaced stretch (every way one connected chain, §3.10), placing at the new bank points the two deck_end vertices of each deck it crosses under a fresh Bridge (§6.3's matching hands it the old address when (4) removes the old span), the edge between carrying deck beside way (the L0 batch adds none); replaces each crossed wall run by its re-traced run, the water gate's two bank vertices carrying ('gate_end', gate, 0 | 1) under a fresh Gate (§2.2 rule 7) whose record (7) builds, and removes the old run with its strips' setback, glacis and intervallum stretches through their StretchRef (§2.2 rule 5), ends placed by splitThrough at the feet of the perpendiculars from the run's end towers; by F-REDERIVE's way rung cuts every other way the new channel ⊕ bank setback meets, and every way but a kept way at a gate that the new strips will meet, the part not keeping the old anchor handed to a new way first by retypeEdges' rekey on its StretchRef (§3.4); splits every other structural edge of any level that the new banks will cross and that is no way (settlement-perimeter or district-boundary stretch L1; setback or glacis line outside a re-traced run L3, NF-P5's faces) at its two bank points, each carrying an anchor contact name (§2.2 rule 7), removing the stretch between; prepares the map's border line at its two bank points without cutting it (§3.3 rule 2); what the chain may not move (a locked or pinned way, wall or finer entity in the new channel ⊕ setback or a new strip, or a reservation there) returns to the dry run as F-EDIT (Re-derive from S3 offered for a reservation).

(b) 4 One L0 batch — the water: declares the same footprint and clears nothing (§3.3 rule 1); removes the changed reach's old shore stretches (removeEdges on each StretchRef between the points where the new shores leave and rejoin the old, §3.4) and inserts the new ones through the vertices (3) prepared (deck_end, gate_end and contact-name vertices listed in KernelTx.prepared, promoted to L0 with contact names stripped, §3.3, §3.6); each deck's span now lies across the water in S1 (5)'s form (no L0 edge crosses water, §2.2 rule 7), each old Bridge address passes to its successor (§6.3); each unused new site's two deck_end vertices placed on the new shores as S1's L0 batch places a site's; an old shore stretch shared with a quay or riverside wall keeps its way or wall row and is demoted to L1 with its L0-only vertices; a deck left over land keeps no L0 edge: where its deck_end rows are L1 (a deck a carve, outer moat or earlier water edit prepared, an F-ROUTE deck sited inside one of these included) its bank vertices take L1 at once; where L0 (placed by S1, S3, S4's or an edit's added deck on standing water, or an edit's new site) they keep L0 with no L0 edge at them until (9) removes the rows (§2.2 rule 3), so the L0 view stays land and water only; the new shores split the finer faces they cross, which keep their owners until (6)-(8) re-own them (§3.3 rule 3); the batch meets no finer edge but the prepared vertices; the old decks' and sites' bank vertices on the changed reach leave with their shores, except the deck of a way the new water no longer meets; tree scoping (8) and F-REDERIVE (9) act only inside the footprint and item 7 (ii) checks byte identity outside it less the seam exception.

(b) 5 S5: lesser connections re-grow inside the cells whose ways (3) cut, from the proposals whose origins lie there, under S5c's legality (water only on a deck). 6 S6: each land face of the footprint that (4) split from a pre-edit L1 cell takes the district (or hinterland, or wall_strip typing) of the pre-edit cell holding the larger part of its area; a cell merged across a removed boundary stretch joins the district holding its larger part only where the stretch was removed on land (a cut way) and no boundary re-separates the parts; vacated land joins the district across its longest boundary unless a wall or arterial separates them (then the next longest; ties by id), or the hinterland; every L1 face whose L0 parent is now water leaves the district face set it inherited (§2.2 rule 4) for the water body's faces; perimeter and district boundaries re-typed on the L1 edges between face sets; margin bands follow the S6 row. 7 S7: re-cuts the strips' setback, glacis and intervallum lines along each re-traced run from the feet (3) left, closing them on the new banks, builds the furniture (towers at its vertices; the water gate's Gate record at the new crossing, banks naming the two gate_end vertices; none at the old); strip blocks' band parts from S10's step (0) in (8). 8 Tree scoping: S8-S12b re-derive every cell of the footprint, vacated land included, by item 2 (shared-edge parts too; strips (3) and (7) changed re-run step (0), declared for NF-P5) with succession by anchor and fresh addresses for new faces (§6.3); the height samples the edit changed run (a) 2-4 on what stands outside the footprint. 9 F-REDERIVE removes every deck and site left over land and lists every re-route, cut, pruned stub, succession and demolition in the fate report with its lifecycle event. The deck invariant (§5.3) is evaluated once after (9) over the chain's touched faces; the kernel's invariants hold at every batch (J-DET-23).

The dry run lists every protected entity in the effective scope — locked, pinned, edited or assigned; declared (listed kept (declared)); a closure's created piece (with the event that created it); hosting a pin; the target of a pinned label placement; housing a pinned or edited person; an edited close-up entity — with its fate: kept (fixed input); carried (to its anchor-matched successor, §6.3, after the class-family check — an override moves with the address only if the successor's class family accepts the attribute, never by id alone); orphaned (no successor: the edit stays in the log, listed in the document's orphan table, re-attachable); discarded (only with "discard edits in scope", recorded as supersede events).

A chained edit's report also lists its unprotected consequences (bridges re-sited or removed, ways re-routed, cut or pruned, buildings re-based or demolished) with their lifecycle events; every edit's report lists the households §2.6's capacity rule re-homes (each with its relocate event, from and to), the residential slots §4.7 builds to re-provide a dossier household's housing with the uses that re-provision displaces and the plots it joins, and the names it re-draws by §6.3 case (4), old and new text side by side; the user sees counts and the list and confirms every fate other than kept and every rename; an action whose dry run lists a rename returns confirm even when its scope holds no protected entity (§11.2); confirmed fates and renames stored in the event (EditBase.renames).

A replay or receiving client compares an event's stored fates and renames with those it computes only when it folds the event under the output version that confirmed them — the from of the first live upgrade after the event, else the document's own output version — and reports a mismatch when they differ; folded under a later version the recomputed values are applied: the upgrade names those events once in its diff (MigrationMap.changedConfirmations, §7.5) and no later load re-reports them; the upgrade's undo, replaying under from, compares them again.

Regenerate (keep settings) re-derives the kinds that persist a derivation record (§2.8) — plots, blocks, buildings — with their recorded inputs, so it reproduces an untouched entity byte-identically even after an epoch or a field edit elsewhere moved the current inputs (re-deriving with current inputs is Adjust); kinds without a derivation record (ways, districts, walls) re-derive from their current upstream state, which only an explicit edit or an epoch changes; the provenance rebuilt by their last derivation or the verification replay holds what they read (§2.8); every generated name keeps its naming record.

The dependency graph is the audit: Provenance.deps (every entity records what it read) serves (a) as the audit of item 7 and (b) as an optimisation for Adjust — invalidating exactly the closure of a changed parameter or table slice — only where the oracle has proven that stage's declarations complete; elsewhere tree scoping applies; both routes leave the same records because a re-derivation reproducing an entity's leaf digest keeps its old derivation record (§2.8).

Oracle (every B-EDIT sequence) (i) replay = session: replaying base and log in log order gives the session's model and records digests (§6.2) on sequences mixing drawn features with later attribute edits, epochs, rebases, undo and redo; among them the naming-collision fixture (two scoped regenerations in different districts whose new ways draw the same street name, then a moveLabel on the second way's label and a setAttr(name) on the first: replay's names, LabelEntity records and digest equal the session's) and a corpus selection and a naming-row edit with their case-(4) renames stored and recomputed equal.

(ii) Outside the scope byte-identical: every entity outside the effective scope keeps its leaf digest; the oracle computes the seam exception from the batches' commit records (changed faces per level, portal roles added or removed) and checks each excepted neighbour cell, plot, footprint and wing ring (stored composition's rings included) equal to its prior ring after removing those vertices, and for an edit storing a stage-3 composition or re-cutting a stored plan each face and wing ring §2.6's composition rule (1) adds to its scope equal to its prior ring after removing the vertices that rule inserted, with the composition role rows present. (iii) Content: content and relation digests outside the scope unchanged.

(iv) Faithfulness: Regenerate (keep settings) by byte identity; New random per regenerated scope against K = 50 independent from-scratch generations of the same scope (same context, rerolls 32 768 + i, i = 0 … K − 1): for median plot area, frontage width, density and attached share, the rank of the regenerated value among the K (references below it plus a uniform draw from 0 … t over the t equal references, from the campaign's own stream; exactly uniform on 0 … K for a perfect regenerator); the nightly campaign judging the ranks (size, test, calibration) is §13.2's (O9 c).
Faithfulness reference count K = 50; reference rerolls 32 768 + i.

(v) Coarse edits: terrain-brush (both modes), course-knot, drawn-water, moved-shore, level-0 warp, drawn-way and drawn-wall sequences end with 0 hard invariant violations, 0 decks and 0 sites over land, 0 off-deck crossings, 0 wings off §2.6's datum rule, 0 footprints in water, an event for every demolition, cut and re-route, every arterial at its destinations or reported unserved, every bridge that still has a site within the band keeping its address and name; a river move across a street grid commits (no E_LEVEL or E_KEPT) with decks on kept ways and cuts on others, every face outside (b)'s footprint byte-identical; a pond drawn inside a block and a river bank widened into its riverside blocks between two bridges each commit with no E_LEVEL or E_KEPT and byte identity outside; a river moved across a wall between two towers commits likewise (every indexed role unique per ordinal, Gate.banks on its two gate_end vertices, no anchor contact name left, 0 NF-P5 violations); a river moved across the settlement perimeter leaves 0 district faces outside it; a course-knot move replayed after an upgrade that changed S1's knot count binds by address and ordinal or is reported orphaned, never another body's knot.

(vi) Shared-edge identity: Regenerate (keep settings) of a perimeter district, a walled district and the hinterland byte-identical to the one-click result; after outskirtToDistrict, drawBoundary and a district merge every L1 edge two face sets share without corridors carries a margin band on both sides and no other edge carries one. (vii) Mutations and dossier events: a designation change, relocation, plot join or split, dossier event, positive placement, rejection, a relet with the stored-plan re-cut it runs, a plan edit or rung re-roll, a closure edit with its undo and the deletion of its edited thing, and a sugar event with its expansion are edits under (i)-(iii): byte identity outside their touched set, the same record on every host, and A → B → A by the inverse mutation byte-identical when nothing else changed (§4.7 S11 rule 5; fixtures §13.2's).

Designation changes are mutations, not re-derivations: where an edit changes what a plot is for (assign, unassign, setAttr on a plot's use or class, openUse, closeUse, relocateUse, a dossier event, placeAt, the re-placement a rejectSite causes) the engine does not discard the plot's finer content and re-run S11: it runs §4.7 S11's designation mutator, which keeps every part still fitting the new designation's template, adapts, converts, adds and subtracts the rest as a recorded MutationRecord drawn from the plot's siteplan.mutate stream (§6.1), and joins a neighbour only when the template's size budget needs the land (a join chained as item 3 states); effective scope those plots' faces; fates are item 4's (a locked part kept, never subtracted); reversal applies the inverse record (§7.4); tree scoping remains the path of Regenerate (keep settings) and New random on the same plot.

Closure rule (owner: "if a user edits a building to have an access to the underground, it generates all the necessary pieces"): an edit whose target lacks its prerequisites is expanded at its dry run into its closure — the minimal set of pieces making it lawful, in dependency order (each piece's prerequisites first); an edit kind that can imply prerequisites declares its closure generators in the entity registry (§2.8), in order, each naming the stage operator it calls; a kind declaring none is never expanded; the closure is the edit's ONE event: its batches (each one level of one arena, and on the underground layer of one part — §3.3, §3.4, §4.1) run in dependency order on the dry run's overlay and commit together (whole or not at all).

Closure seed and locality: every piece draws from the edited entity's and its target's lineage streams under the calling stage's concerns keyed with the event's seq (§6.1), minted from the event's seq and its ordinal in dependency order (§6.3; J-A18.43's pattern): one edit at one log position of one seed always yields one set of pieces; effective scope = the pieces and their clear regions; byte identity outside (item 7 (ii)).

Closure record, undo, ownership: the event stores EditBase.closure (created pieces in dependency order, and reused existing pieces — a connector already dug, another cellar); undo removes exactly the created pieces and restores what they replaced (§7.4), nothing reused touched; a later delete of the edited thing (the access point) removes the created pieces nothing else now uses (a connector a second access shares stays, named among that access's reused pieces); a basement the closure created returns to §2.6's derived decision unless edited since; pieces held while the edit is live (§7.2); a closure creates map facts only, never a dossier fact (item 20 (h)); a closure that would change a dossier-owned value is refused dossier-owned (§5.2).

Closure instances: addUndergroundAccess(building, target?) is the first; its generators are II.7.6's pieces (J-A66.41): the basement by §2.6's requested-mode ladder (the request overrides the probability, never the terrain gate: a full cellar, else a half cellar or walk-out on a slope, else a hatch to a crawl space, else a refusal naming the gate); the target in II.7.6's order; the dug connector; the minimal private underground where none exists; the access point; the plan reservation (the basement plan's stair, ladder or hatch, its rung marked stale, §2.8); the links. A clandestine front lacking its concealed door (§4.7, item 63; the setAttr setting a placed use's concealment to front, acting on the use's building; T66-5) and an undercity neighbourhood an edit leaves without a lifeline (II.7.5 condition 4, item 65; a drawBoundary adding one on the undercity's part or a split of one, acting on that neighbourhood's District, whose lineage keys the lifeline's draws) are closures too — a concealed door by §2.6's entrance rules (§4.7 Concealed institutions (4)), a lifeline by II.7.6's target, connector, access and link pieces; every later edit kind implying missing prerequisites declares its generators the same way; the closure rule and the edit kind are the base's; addUndergroundAccess's underground pieces run once the underground stages exist (II.7.4; staged), until then its dry run returns F-EDIT naming the staged layer (§5.2).

Closure failure: a generator that cannot produce its piece ends the expansion; the dry run returns F-EDIT with the nearest lawful form its ladder reached or the refusal with its reason (§5.2), and nothing commits.

ClosureRecord { created: { id; piece 'basement'|'target'|'connector'|'system'|'access'|'reservation'|'link'|'door' }[] (dependency order); reused: Id[] } — EditBase.closure; read by undo, by a later delete and by §5.3's closure row.
CLOSURE / PREREQUISITES / CLOSURE GENERATORS / CLOSURE EDIT / closure record.

Scoped re-rolls and variations: every re-roll is scoped (regenerate newRandom on a scope — a block, a quarter, a building's rung — or rerollLayer on one rerollable layer); an unscoped new town is only the empty state's action before anything is declared; a derived fill (a fill, T8's brush, a scoped New random) offers three variations: its dry run derives the scope at its next three distinct rerolls on three overlays (§5.1 (6)'s check advancing a variation equal to the current scope's or an earlier variation's content to the next unused reroll, within reroll.maxAdvance), the ghost shows them side by side; the accepted variation commits as that regenerate with its absolute reroll map, the others leave nothing; declared entities are kept in every variation (§7.2).

The log is an ordered fold: each event applies to the state its predecessors produced, through the same code path interactively and on replay; nothing is hoisted; epochs, rebases, upgrades, undo and redo are events like any other.

The one read-ahead is the creation prefix: the base derivation's S2 reads the log's creation events (the blueprint's and creation dossier's assign events at positions 0…k) as fixed rows before it runs, and each stage reads a skeleton's drawn declarations there as its constraints (§4.1, item 101; J-A101.41); folding those events afterwards records the generation run's placements and places nothing a second time (§4.2; J-A22.41, J-A22.72, J-A22.74).

A creation event belongs to the base derivation it feeds, not an edit of the map it made: never an undo, redo or revert target — the undo key and revert skip it, and an undo(h, of) naming it returns F-EDIT offering unassign for a blueprint assignment and rejectSite and placeAt for a dossier element (§5.2) — and never truncated; a blueprint assignment is removed by unassign (§7.3 item 8's mutation), a skeleton's declaration by a later declaration or a delete, a dossier element only by a dossier event (§7.7 item 2).

Every later dossier event (EditBase.dossier set, §7.7 item 1) is no undo, redo or revert target of a map event: revert skips it, an undo(h, of) naming it returns F-EDIT offering rejectSite and placeAt for each dossier element it placed or re-designated (a dossier unassign leaves none to offer); an epoch that carried one in EpochInputs.dossier is refused as an undo target the same way, because undoing either would change dossier content without a dossier instruction (item 20 (c)).
"case (4)" in the lifecycle table = the event runs §6.3's case (4) for the name it frees or whose inputs it changes, the rename listed, confirmed and stored (§7.3 item 4).

lock / unlock / pin / unpin — create: UI or API on any address, optionally on attribute paths; read: entity flags (derived from the log); persist: log; regenerate: a fixed input, dependants re-derive around it; a lock on a name path keeps the naming record dormant (§2.8); an unlock that frees the name runs case (4); undo: inverse event; undoing a lock that frees a name runs case (4); an unlock that re-drew a name keeps the former name and naming record in its undo record, which its undo restores; migrate: address mapped (§7.5); an orphaned lock re-imposes its last geometry as a drawn constraint unless the user drops it.

setAttr / setAttrMany / paint — create: UI / API, a bulk query resolved to ids at dry run; read: entity attributes, flags.edited, editedPaths; persist: log; regenerate: an input override at the stage computing the attribute (a name: S13a keeps it and never re-draws while edited, naming record dormant; a district kind: S6 reads it as fixed; heights and roof: S11); implicitly pinned; a plot's tenure and a district's identity are overrides of derived values kept until reverted (items 70, 72); a change of a front's designation runs S11's mutator on the front, the concealed use persisting and its concealed rooms re-fitted (item 63); a setAttr of a dossier-owned value never reaches the fold (dry run refuses); undo: inverse (old values in the undo record); undoing or reverting a setAttr on a generated name returns it to unedited with its dormant naming record and runs case (4), the replaced text kept in that event's undo record; a setAttr of heights or class that re-homed households keeps their former buildings in its undo record; migrate: attribute names schema-versioned with a rename table; unmappable → orphan, reported.

moveVertex / warp — create: vertex handle stored as lattice point + role signature / staged warp session with Apply; read: geometry; persist: log — the operation (arena key, strokes, fromLevel; a moveVertex's at with its VertexSig); per-vertex displacements only as a verification record; regenerate: the kernel's whole-step validation, halving, sliding and holding (§3.6); kernel-pinned vertices move (pins constrain smoothing, simplification and cutting); what stands on the ground carried and re-based; moved water to S1's water operator; undo: undo record — moved vertices, re-derived faces, former birth levels and flags of promoted and demoted vertices and edges, former points of displaced records, former wing rings, basement rings and stored compositions, former bases of re-based entities, households §2.6's capacity rule re-homed with former buildings; migrate: the operation replays at its log position; a moveVertex binds by resolveVertexAt (exact point, else signature match within the rebind radius, else orphaned and reported).

moveCourseKnot — create: dragging a river's control knot; read: WaterBody.controls (§2.3), the knot's path controls/<ordinal> in editedPaths (implicitly pinned); persist: log (water body's address, knot ordinal, at, to); regenerate: S1's water operator, every later re-trace keeps the moved knot; undo: the replaced scope of the whole chain and the knot's former position; migrate: once the water body's address is carried, binds (1) the knot with that ordinal if within the rebind radius of at — half the body's control spacing (§4.2 S1 (3)); (2) else the body's nearest knot within the radius, ties by ordinal; (3) else orphaned and reported; never another body's knot.
Course-knot rebind radius = half the body's control spacing (§4.2 S1 (3)); the moved-knot re-trace tolerance in §7.3 (b) 1 is also half a control spacing.

drawWay / drawWater / drawWall / drawGreen / drawBoundary — create: drawing tools with resampling, snapping (first-crossing split, attraction) and validation at the authoring boundary; their points forms (item 101); read: entities with existence = built, author user; declared, so held; persist: log (geometry is the payload; for a points form the derived shape stored resolved, never re-derived); regenerate: at its log position through its class's local operator, chained operators included; undo: the replaced scope of the whole chain; migrate: the same geometry replays at its log position under the new version.

drawTunnel / drawChamber / addLink / placeAccess (items 11, 12, 64, 65; J-A12.71) — create: the underground tools (II.7; staged, editable in the base); read: the Tunnel or Gallery record and its chain, the Chamber record and outline, the UndergroundLink record and its two link_end vertices (each in its system's part), the AccessPoint record, its state, knownTo and access_point vertex; persist: log (geometry payload); regenerate: at its log position — a drawn tunnel through II.7's network stage (chain on the underground arena, navigable derived) and the underground stage re-deriving the blocks its edges bound; a placed access point by II.7.3's access rules, its ground host found by pointLocate, nothing on the ground written; a gallery or chamber through its system's stage on its own part, a link between two parts' vertices one part per batch (§3.4); an access point's underground end by moveVertex and its opening by setAttr on ground.at (refused as F-EDIT outside admitted ground); undo: the replaced underground scope, a moved opening's former ground.at and host; migrate: the same geometry replays; an access point whose element is unmapped is orphaned and reported.

addUndergroundAccess (item 66) — create: a building's context action; the API; read: the AccessPoint and its closure's pieces; the closure record; persist: log (building, optional target and kind, closure record); regenerate: at its log position, the closure's generators in dependency order, pieces held while live; undo: created pieces removed and what they replaced restored, reused pieces untouched, a created basement back to its former state; a later delete of the access removes only created pieces nothing else uses; migrate: replays at its log position; an event whose building is unmapped is orphaned and reported.

placeGate / quarter / roster / group (sugar, item 101) — create: the authoring tools (§7.1's toolkit), the clerk's tool API (§11.2), a skeleton file (§11.1); read: the entities its expansion made, declared so held; persist: log — the sugar event itself with its expansion version, one undo step, one fate report; regenerate: expanded at its fold into its events by sugar.json at the recorded version (§7.6), what it creates minted from its seq; undo: the whole expansion's scope as one step; migrate: the recorded expansion version replays; an upgrade whose expansion table changed maps the event as it maps the events it expands to, listed once in its diff (§7.5).

startWorks / cancelWorks / setAttr on a Works (item 67) — create: the Works tools (§7.1); an epoch's step (§4.11); read: the Works record, its stage at a week derived from it; persist: log — the event with the change it wraps (the epoch's own for an epoch's Works); regenerate: §4.11's Works — a startWorks folds the change it wraps at once at its position (§4.11 (1); J-A67.72) and creates the Works that shows it (the change of ownership at its start and stages derived from record and week); a cancelWorks ends it by §4.11's rule; undo: the wrapped change's inverse and the Works record, with the plots and buildings its start changed; migrate: the record replays; its stages follow the output version's WorksTable.

placeLight / setAttr / delete on a light (item 68) — create: the light tool (§7.1); read: the LightSource record (§2.7); persist: log; regenerate: a hand-placed light is declared (§7.2): survives a regeneration by its anchor (host's address, rule row, ordinal, §6.3) and follows its host's lifecycle (§2.8: removed with a demolished host, unlit on an abandoned one); rule-placed lights re-derive with their host's faces (§4.7, §4.11); undo: inverse, exact; migrate: by its host's address; a light whose host is unmapped is orphaned and reported.

drawFootprint / build / moveFootprint / swapUse / fill — create: building tools (§7.1); read: building and plot entities; persist: log; regenerate: S11 re-fits the host plot(s) with the footprint as a fixed slot; fill re-runs S11 on its scope with the forced arrangement; undo: undo record; migrate: replays; a footprint whose host plot is unmapped re-creates a plot around it.

delete / merge / split / join / convert (the ladder kinds relet, densify, thin, subdivide, amalgamate; the decline kinds; tunnel and island kinds; use kinds; sealing kinds; terrain and water kinds of §4.11; the underground layer's flood, raiseGrade, clearUndercity, II.7.5-II.7.6) — create: context actions; the evolution engine's plan (§4.11); read: lifecycle events with cause; persist: log; regenerate: structural ops on the plat (§3.4): a district or way split/merge with dependants re-derived; a plot join or split is item 31's fusion or splitting (S10 (7)'s re-cut with neighbours fixed, S11's mutator, no occupied building removed unless confirmed); convert = retypeEdges plus lifecycle events; decline conversions change existence and the drawing (§2.8), credit or debit the material ledger (§4.11), a reuse … build succeeds at the trace's address; tunnel conversions change existence and closure (condition reads them, §2.7; J-A11.21) and close or reopen the frontage plots on the run (II.7.3); island conversions resize an arena or archive it (fallIsland lays the ruin face through the carve path); use conversions open, close or relocate a Use with detail.from/to and mutate buildings by S11; relet sets a building's household count within §2.6's capacity (item 28 (f)) — households added minted from the event, leaving households go by item 17's relocation — marks an unstored plan stale and re-cuts a stored one inside the event, no shell geometry changed; densify/thin … infill add or clear yard buildings by S11's mutator; densify/thin … back_court re-cut the plot's yard by S10 (7) with neighbours fixed, adding or removing a rear row and its passage face (§4.6, §4.11); subdivide and amalgamate are rung 3's re-cuts, whose hand forms are §7.1's plot split and join; sealPassage/openPassage set Passage.sealed, change no geometry, vacate or reoccupy the plots behind it (item 30); siltReach, shiftCourse and a foreshore's reclaim run S1's water operator, a marsh's reclaim its terrain operator, digCanal the carve; a split or join of a chain carrying a profile (a way's width, a wall's base, a tunnel's invert, a shore's bank kind or class) goes through retypeEdges' rekey on the part's StretchRef (§3.4) — each part gets a cut knot carrying the sampled value, a join knot dropped only where the joined profile is unchanged (§2.2 rule 5) — and the event writes both records' returned profiles; undo: members resurrect with former rings, records and builtBand, tombstones return to live, both records' former profiles; a decline or tunnel conversion's former state and ledger rows; a fallen island's arena restored from the archive and its ruin face removed through the carve path's inverse; a reuse … build undo returning the address to the trace; a use conversion's former use and building links; a relet's former count, household links and stored plan; a ladder conversion's former rings, records and passage face; a terrain or water conversion's replaced chain scope with §2.3's records; a mutation's inverse record; migrate: same.

regenerate / adjust / re-derive from Sk — create: the named actions on an area, district, block, plot or person; read: report entry, the fate list; persist: log — resolved scope, mode, absolute rerolls used, confirmed fates and renames; regenerate: §7.3; New random's content check (§5.1 (6)); a pack-list adjust and any re-derivation reaching S13a run case (4) for unedited names citing a changed slice; Adjust re-derives with the current field and sets builtBand in its scope, listed in the fate report, while Regenerate (keep settings) keeps it (item 31); undo: the effective scope's faces, entities (names and naming records included), lifecycle events and tombstones, O(scope) — an undo restores former names, never re-draws them; migrate: the scope replays; fates and renames recomputed and compared under §7.3 item 4's rule.

assign / unassign (a dossier event among them, EditBase.dossier set) — create: assignment dialog / host API / the host door (§11.4); read: assignment fields, flags.assigned, a dossier-backed assignment's existence 'dossier'; persist: log; blueprint and dossier-at-creation assignments at positions 0…k flagged creation, read ahead by S2; regenerate: §4.7 S10b places (claims-first at positions 0…k, least-disruption order after the city is built) and §4.7 S11 mutates each placed plot, the record in EditBase.mutations; an assigned name keeps the naming record dormant; an unassign leaves the plot vacant (closeUse) and frees the name, running case (4); a dossier-backed element's existence is held (§7.2); undo: the inverse mutation from the undo record (§4.7 S11 rule 5) and the former placements — for an event neither creation nor dossier (no undo targets); migrate: addresses and criteria; unmapped members re-solve around mapped ones (§7.7); a dossier element re-binds by its DossierRef.

rejectSite / placeAt (item 20 (b), (g)) — create: the map's "delete" of a dossier-backed element; the "make this place X" action; read: the rejection record and the plot's pin (§2.8, §7.7) — model data; persist: log; regenerate: rejectSite — the element re-placed by §4.7 S10b's solver at the event's position and the site excluded while the rejection holds; the hold lapses (site eligible again) by §7.7's lapse rule (item 3), the lapsing event writing the lapse into the record inside its own touched set, never as a log event of its own (J-A20.74); placeAt — the plot pinned to its element or designation, honoured by every later placement and re-application that can, reported when one cannot; undo: inverse (lift); the re-placement's scope restored from the undo record; an undo of a lapsing epoch that carried no dossier event restores the hold, while an undo naming a lapsing dossier event or an epoch that carried one returns F-EDIT; migrate: by the site's and element's addresses; an orphaned rejection or pin is reported.

setEntrance / setAttr(basement) (item 29) — create: building tools (§7.1); read: Building.entrances, Building.basement (§2.6), editedPaths; persist: log; regenerate: edited attributes — a moved main entrance and an added, moved or removed door are fixed inputs of the site plan, carried with the wing (§2.6) and re-fitted around by S11's mutator on a designation change (a house that becomes a shop gains its street door, a shop that closes keeps its door as a house door, §4.7 S11); an edited basement is kept through terrain changes (§7.3 (a) 4); undo: inverse; migrate: with the building's address; an entrance whose wing is unmapped re-placed by §2.6's rules and reported.

drawPassage / sealPassage / openPassage / setAttr(knownTo) / setAttr(reach) (item 30) — create: context actions on a plot, block, building or institution; read: the passage face and its Passage.sealed bit (an access row on a sealed passage face reads sealed), Block.reach, Plot.knownTo / Building.knownTo / Institution.knownTo; persist: log; regenerate: the passage face and the rear plots' access rows are fixed inputs of S10's re-cut; an access row on a sealed passage is skipped by §5.3's reachability walk and the plots behind it decay as vacant under §4.11's ladder; a setAttr of a block's reach re-derives its interior by S10 (7)'s re-cut with neighbours fixed (J-A30.72); knownTo is read by §9.2's label policy only (no model geometry changes); a knownTo the dossier set is dossier-owned and refused (J-A20.77), a dossier event setting one writes it as any dossier fact; undo: inverse; migrate: by address; a passage whose building is unmapped is reported.

plan events (setRoomRole, moveWall, splitRoom, mergeRooms, setOpening, setWindow, moveStairCore; item 28; setRoomUnit, item 28 (f)) — create: the plan tools on the building band (§8.5); read: the stored composition's plan (§2.6), a room's unit; persist: log; the first plan event stores the composition; regenerate: a fixed input to the rung's re-derivation — a stored plan whose inputs change is re-cut inside the changing event around the edited rooms from the stored plan as canonical prior; an edited unit is kept while its household lives in the building and listed as a fate when it leaves; carryWings carries the rooms with the wings; undo: the former storey; migrate: by the building's address and the room's anchor (§6.3), else orphaned and reported.

regenerate with rung (item 28) — create: New random on one elaboration rung; read: the rung's counter (§6.1; the event's map under <building id>#<rung>); persist: log; regenerate: the rung re-derives with its advanced counter under §5.1 (6)'s content check comparing the rung's own derived result, identity left out (an unstored rung is outside every digest, §6.2); re-rolling a finer rung changes no coarser stream: plan.layout keeps wings, entrances, stair core; plan.roles every wall and opening position; undo: the previous counter; the rung's cached result recomputed, never stored in the record; migrate: replays.

builtBand (a plot attribute, item 31; not an event kind: its paths) — create: the writers §4.11's floor paragraph lists (J-A31.44); read: §4.11's ladder; S10 and S11 through the manifested band max(field band, geometryFloor) (§4.7 S10 (2), S11); persist: the plot's attribute columns (§2.9), in the leaf digest; regenerate: Regenerate (keep settings) keeps it; Adjust and a brush reset it in their scope (authorial, §7.2; J-A31.72); an epoch writes it only through §4.11's writers (a rung-3 event; rung 2's back court for the new rear plots it creates, which take their stock's band; a completed upward refurbishment, which raises it), so a standing plot's builtBand is lowered only by a rung-3 event; undo: restored by the undo record of whichever event wrote it; migrate: a document written before the attribute existed gets builtBand = the band its plot's DerivationRecord.band holds (§7.5).

fieldBand (a plot attribute, item 28 (f); not an event kind: its paths) — create: every derivation that reads the current field (generation, Adjust, a brush's re-derivation past τ) and the epoch's re-banding after S6 (§2.5, §4.11); read: §2.6's interior ladder, ClassRules.pick and the plan rung's recorded inputs (§2.8); persist: the plot's attribute columns (§2.9), in the leaf digest; regenerate: Regenerate (keep settings) keeps it; Adjust and a brush set it in their scope; an epoch re-bands it; undo: restored by the undo record of whichever event wrote it, an epoch's among the entities it replaced; migrate: a document written before the attribute existed gets fieldBand = the band its plot's DerivationRecord.band holds (§7.5).

setField (brush) — create: prosperity / density / greenery / terrain brush; the terrain brush's water mode; read: the stroke list; the composited field or heightfield; persist: log (strokes); regenerate: field strokes — blocks whose inputs moved beyond τ re-derive; terrain strokes — S1's terrain operator (§7.3 (a)), in follow mode with the water operator; a brush is authorial and sets builtBand in the blocks it re-derives; undo: the stroke leaves the list; the field or heightfield re-composites (exact) and the operator re-runs on the stroke's region; the households §2.6's capacity rule re-homed restored to their former buildings from its undo record; migrate: strokes are geometry and replay.

editTable / editPreset — create: tables editor, presets dialog; read: the override layer (§7.6); persist: log — row operations by key with the base row's hash, the fallback's confirmed fates, renames; regenerate: entities whose derivation record, naming record or provenance cites a changed slice hash re-derive; a changed naming slice runs case (4) for exactly the unedited names citing it; a predicate table, or a kind whose recorded slices are unavailable, re-derives from the table's first reader stage with fates (§7.6); undo: inverse row operations; re-derived entities (renamed names with former naming records among them) restored from the undo record, never re-drawn; the households its capacity re-homing moved restored; migrate: a row that changed or vanished in the new table version → orphan, reported and kept.

instance (and the tree brush) — create: tree tools (a batch of instance events), instance handles; read: the entity's instance set with its overrides; persist: log; regenerate: applied by ordinal while the entity's lineage is unchanged since the event (no carry or supersession after its seq) and the ordinal's generated position lies within 0.5 × the spacing of the recorded point; otherwise re-matched by position to the nearest unclaimed instance within 0.5 × the spacing (a superseded entity's overrides move to its supersededBy successor), else orphaned and reported (§8.10); undo: inverse; migrate: ordinals geometry-stable only under the same lineage; otherwise re-match by position.
Instance re-match tolerance: 0.5 × the instance spacing (ordinal kept when its generated position lies within it; else nearest unclaimed within it).

rerollLayer — create: "reroll names / trees / decoration / compass / emblem" (§6.1's rerollable concerns); names also on chosen ids; read: the effective salt (the recipe's initial value set by the log's town-wide rerollLayer events; for an ids-scoped naming reroll the per-entity salts in the event); persist: log — absolute salts (with ids, those used after §6.3 case (3)'s advance); regenerate: naming — S13a re-draws every unedited name (town-wide) or the listed entities' unedited names, uniqueness by §9.6; instances, crowns, jitter: display only; compass and emblem: furniture only (§9.5); undo: the previous salt; for naming, the previous names and naming records from the undo record; migrate: replays.

revert (reset to generated) — create: ctrl / cmd+click, context action; read: the entity's own logged edits; persist: log (one event); regenerate: the inverses of the entity's own events applied in reverse log order at the revert's position; edits to other entities stay; a name it frees runs case (4); undo: inverse — re-applies them; migrate: follows the entity's address; an event whose target no longer maps is reported.

moveLabel / hideLabel — create: label handles; the dry run refuses a placement whose box at its stop meets another pinned label's box there, returning the nearest free position (§9.2); read: LabelEntity.pinned / hidden (model data, in the digest, §6.2); persist: log; regenerate: honoured by S13b (§9); the LabelEntity exists at the event's log position in session and replay, S13a running per event (§7.3 item 2); undo: inverse; migrate: follows the target address; unmapped → orphan.

setLayer / setStyle / paintGround — create: UI, style dialog; read: style state (canonical, outside the model digest); persist: log; regenerate: no model re-derivation; the display list rebuilds; undo: inverse; migrate: style schema versioned.

people: pin, setAttr, lock with paths, regenerate a person — create: an explicit action or edit only, never viewing; read: the pinned or edited fields, everyone else derived; persist: log; regenerate: pinned and edited people are fixed inputs, re-homed to the household that inherits their household's address (§6.3), else orphans reported (§10.3); undo: undo record; migrate: person-table version recorded per household; person keys map through the household's address; orphans reported.

closeup (stage 2) — create: logged before the first edit inside a close-up; read: the close-up's entities, a refinement level of the district; persist: log (strategy, params) and the edits after it; regenerate: a pure function of the district's committed state, sub-seed, strategy and params; a base re-derivation of the district re-derives its close-up with carry-over, re-matches presentation instance edits by position and reports orphans; undo: undo record; migrate: replays.

epoch — create: grow(doc, inputs) (§4.11) or a circumstance-schedule entry; read: the derived EpochRecord, lifecycle events with cause; persist: log; regenerate: §4.11's incremental path at its log position — each plot's fieldBand re-banded after S6 (§2.5), regrowth-first siting, the survivors' ladder bounded by the geometry floor (its rung-1 relet marking unstored plans stale and re-cutting stored ones inside the epoch, item 28 (f)), the use step, the decline lottery, the island and underground laws; every live rejection re-checked by §7.7's lapse rule (item 3); a dossier change the host sends with the epoch rides in EpochInputs.dossier and is applied at §4.11's step (e), one sent between epochs folding at its own log position (§7.7 item 6; item 22 (e)); the epoch carries its absolute week (item 76), the Works it starts are records whose stages the week derives (item 67), its character step recomputes each district's vector, moves identities past their hysteresis, writes the pressures and renames by §6.3's case (5) (§4.5, item 72); undo: the faces and entities it replaced (O(epoch scope)) with the identities, pressures and names it wrote; migrate: a multi-epoch document upgrades by replaying the whole ordered log with a per-epoch diff, or stays pinned to its output version.

rebase — create: keeping the saved town on a mismatch; Rebuild around my drawings; editing a frozen import (a frozenImport rebase runs case (4) over every unedited generated name and returns confirm with renames listed; keeping the old model at an upgrade needs none — the document stays at its own output version, §7.5); read: the document's base; persist: the base state and the event (version names the output version that computed stateDigest; at the log head the state materialises — h₀ when kept after edits during load verification, §2.9 step 4; events before at stay in the log, §2.9); regenerate: replay starts from the rebased state, checked against its root of record for the replay's output version (§2.9 step 3), and folds the events after at; other clients: see Rebases on other clients; undo: the previous base; migrate: the rebased state migrates by the schema chain; an upgrade checks it under from against its root of record and records its root under to as baseDigest (§7.5); not seed-reproducible.

upgrade — create: explicit, after the diff (§7.5); read: the document's output version; persist: log with baseDigest for a rebased base and the saved packs in its mapping; regenerate: §7.5 — a rebased base checked under from and re-rooted under to; every pack to stops shipping copied into packs first; the mapping hands names on with addresses and runs case (4) for unedited names whose naming slices the new tables changed, listed in the diff; earlier events' fates and renames recomputed under to and differences listed once in the diff; undo: the undo record is upgrade.from — undo replays base and log before the upgrade under that version (a rebased base checked against its root of record for from) to exactly the pre-upgrade digest; in session the pre-upgrade checkpoint makes it instant; outside the browser's version window the undo is withdrawn there with the CLI command shown; migrate: —.

undo / redo — create: ctrl / cmd+Z, ctrl / cmd+shift+Z, the API's undo(h) / redo(h), a host's doc.apply; read: each event's live or undone status, derived from the log; persist: log (of); regenerate: after the independence check — undo restores its target's scope from the target's undo record; redo re-applies the target at the head, its lifecycle events citing the target's seq and its minted addresses the target's own; a result freeing a name runs case (4); undo: an undo is undone by a redo, a redo by an undo (exact inverses); migrate: replays; a target's record is rebuilt under the new version by the replay.

host provider output — create: a host-registered provider's answer after the double-run check (§6.5 (8)); read: the document's hostContent block; persist: hostContent keyed by (provider id, version, input hash); regenerate: read from hostContent on replay, never re-requested; undo: removed with the event that first requested it; migrate: replays without the host.

A rebase event is a no-op for a client whose base it already is; a replay from the recipe folds an undone rebase and its undo as a no-op pair, every event between them undone (a whole-town event is undoable only as the latest live event); undo: when the previous base is the recipe (always kept in a rebased base) the undo restores it and replays the kept log; when it is an earlier rebased state, that state is the undo record held in the undo section under its cap; past the cap, or when the replay would need an output version outside the browser's window, the undo is withdrawn with a notice (the CLI replays any version, §6.4); a redo re-installs the rebased state, which the undo keeps under the same cap (past it the redo is withdrawn with a notice).

Rebases on other clients of a bridged document: a keptSnapshot rebase whose at lies behind the client's head and whose stateDigest differs from the client's root at at installs the snapshot at at from the doc.load bytes the client kept and re-applies the events after at through the fold (fates recomputed, differences reported, undo records rebuilt; §2.9 step 4); one whose stateDigest equals that root changes nothing; any other rebase behind the head (a hand-built log) is a reported no-op; a load whose log already holds a keptSnapshot rebase at model.seq with stateDigest = model.digest takes model as that base without asking.

Undo never removes an event from a shared log (a host stores it and it only grows, §11.3): { t: 'undo'; of } and { t: 'redo'; of } are appended at the head and applied through the same fold, identically by every client and every replay (J-DET-16).

Sessions: an authoring identity per document and author, not per app start; @plat/api mints one (128-bit random value in base 32, outside the model packages) the first time an author edits a document and reuses it on every later open: an unshared document stores it in view state (view.keys['session'], outside every digest, saved with the file, §2.9), so a reload or reopening continues the same undo and redo stacks; a file made without one (CLI or link) mints it on first edit; a client attached to a host bridge takes the session the host assigns in doc.load (§11.3) and never writes the view key; the session enters the log only as EditBase.session; the fold never reads it (an undo names its target by of), so sessions decide which event the undo key picks, never the model (J-DET-34).

Each session has its own stacks; undo targets the session's latest live event other than a creation event, a dossier event or an epoch that carried one — live unless an undo targets it and no later redo re-applies it; a group counts as one step and of names its first event; redo targets the session's latest undo whose target is still undone; a new event from the session clears its redo stack; an unshared document has one stored session (linear undo continuing across reloads); a session with the owner role (the app's role for an unshared document) may name any live event (undo(h, of), §11.2), which is how an earlier session's events are undone.

Undo record: every committed event keeps the inverse event when exact; otherwise the faces, entity records, lifecycle events and tombstones its effective scope replaced, the former birth levels, split flags and stripped contact names of the vertices it promoted, and the former levels and flags of the vertices and edges it demoted or unflagged (§2.2 rule 3; CommitRecord.promoted, demoted, unflagged); and always the addresses it created, changed or removed (its touched set), so undo costs O(scope); undo restores the target's scope from the record and withdraws the addresses the target minted (§6.3); redo re-applies the target at the head from its stored resolved payload (scope, absolute rerolls, confirmed fates), reproducing its result exactly; an edit whose capacity re-homing moves households (§2.6) keeps the former records of the buildings moved out of and into and, where it re-provides a dossier household's housing (§4.7), the plots the re-provision touched (the site with the residential slot, its joined neighbour, each displaced use's new site), restoring them with the households on undo.
TOUCHED SET: the addresses an event created, changed or removed (kept for every event); UNDO RECORD: the inverse event or the replaced scope; LIVE event: one no undo targets without a later redo.

Independence: an undo is applied only if every live event after its target is independent of it — the later event's touched set and effective-scope faces are disjoint from the target's touched set and from the target's effective-scope faces dilated by one ring of adjacent faces at the coarsest level either touches; otherwise the dry run returns F-EDIT listing the dependent events and their authors; the session may undo its own dependent events first, and an owner may undo through a chain — never through a dossier event or an epoch that carried one, so a target one of them depends on stays live; a redo is checked the same way against the live events after its undo; every client folds the same events in the host's order on the same state, so the check agrees everywhere; an undo or redo whose check fails at its log position (only in a hand-built log) is a reported no-op, identically everywhere; a whole-town event (upgrade, rebase, Re-derive from S1) is undoable only while it is the latest live event.

The check also holds a later live event dependent on its target when the target changed an input that event's derivation read: for an editTable or editPreset, when an entity the later event derived (one in its touched set whose leaf digest a stage, S13a's delta, a re-cut or a rung wrote — marked apart from addresses merely set) cites in its derivation record, naming record or provenance (§2.8) a slice whose hash the target's row operations changed (recomputed by §7.6's slice kinds); for an adjust (a parameter, a Re-derive from stage k or the pack list) and a town-wide rerollLayer of naming, whenever the later event derived any entity; an undo or redo whose target is one of these counts as one; an event deriving nothing depends on no such target; so an input change is undone through its dependants or stays, the state after a permitted undo is the fold of the log without its target, and no derivation record cites a slice the effective tables no longer hold; the check costs the later events' touched sets and records' slice references, kept for every event.

Fixtures (B-EDIT, §13.2): an editTable on a heights row followed by a build on a plot the edit did not touch, an adjust followed by a drawWay, and a town-wide rerollLayer(naming) followed by a scoped regeneration drawing a name — each later event reported dependent, and once it is undone first the target's undo gives the model and records digests of the log without the pair; an editTable followed by a build whose derivation cites none of the changed slices is independent, and the target's undo gives the digests of the log without the target.

Undo records kept for the session and saved in the file's undo section (the last 64 events or 20 MB, whichever is smaller; rebase and upgrade records as their rows state), so undo survives a reload; a client with no record for a target (joined later, or the record left the cap) rebuilds it by replaying from its nearest checkpoint before the target or from the base and says it is slow; the replay keeps full records only for the events later undo events target (found by a pre-scan of the log) and touched sets for all; the replay is deterministic, so every client reaches the same state.
Saved undo section cap: last 64 events or 20 MB, whichever smaller (fallback 16 events).

When an unshared document's undo targets the event immediately before it, the engine may drop both from the log and hold the target on the session's redo stack; a redo re-appends the target with its original seq and advances nextSeq by one (the seq the kept log's redo would have spent), so every later event and every address a later user-created entity mints from its event's seq is the same in both logs; the canonical nextSeq (§2.9) never moves back; an undo removes its target's lifecycle entries and tombstones and a redo re-inserts them, both citing the target's seq (§2.8), so lifecycle block, archive and model digest of the truncated log equal those with the pair kept; the truncated target is held on the redo stack in the saved undo section (UndoRecord.redo, §2.9) so a redo after a reload re-appends it, and the packs it names stay in packs while held; a B-EDIT property test over random sequences folds each both ways (§6.5 (9)'s truncation cases among them) requiring equal model and records digests and equal addresses; a document attached to a host bridge never truncates.

Copy-on-write checkpoint (arenas chunked per district, cost only the chunks changed since the previous one) whenever replay cost accumulated since the last passes 80 ms at the session's rung, and before every epoch, rebase and upgrade, so any replay from a checkpoint stays ≤ 100 ms; a load taking §6.2 (iii)'s off-edit-path recomputation also takes one at h₀.

Measurement (M2a): undo of a CITY district regeneration ≤ 30 ms; undo memory ≤ 25 % of the model's working set after 100 edits; (M3a) the host-and-three-clients convergence test of §11.3 with interleaved undo and redo from every client; pre-decided fallback: the saved undo section shrinks to 16 events and checkpoints are taken every 40 ms of replay cost.
The enumeration test checks that every EditEvent kind — undo and redo included — has an exact inverse or an undo record (O9 d); save → load → save is byte-identical over the canonical form (O9 a).

Seven kinds of record hold a world point and move with the ground they stand on: Pin.point (host: Pin.host's faces); Decoration.point (the L3 face containing it); the current position of a positional instance override (a move's to, an add's point, for a line layout the recorded generated point) held in the entity's override table (§8.10); a pinned label's Placement anchor and spine (its target's faces, or its target's corridor for a way, §9.1); LightSource.point (host: the face its host stands on on its host's arena — building footprint face; half-corridor strip of a way or bridge; square's face; gate's footprint; pin's host face; gallery's band; chamber's floor; a junction light's tunnel band faces (junction wedge and half-corridor strips); the faces of the underground element an access point's access_point vertex lies on for the light at its foot; a castle's inner ward, bailey and gatehouse footprint; a decoration's face; any other hand-placed light's host face; of several faces the one pointLocate returns); AccessPoint.ground.at (II.7.4; host: the ground face its ground.host names or stands on); the rings and lines of Works.before (§2.7, item 67; host: its target's plot face, or for a join or split the plot whose face holds the point).

After the kernel's commit the edit layer takes every such record whose host face has a moved vertex (the commit record's moved list, §3.3) and computes its new point from the move: the point's mean-value coordinates in its host face's outer ring before the move applied to the ring after it (+ − × ÷ and sqrt only, §6.5), rounded to the lattice; a record whose new point lies outside its host face, or nearer its boundary than its clearance (a pin's footprint radius, Decoration.keepClearCm, half an instance spacing, a label's box, a light's sizeCm; none for an access point's opening), is re-seated at the nearest lattice point of the host face inset by that clearance, ties by (y, x) (never a door light); if the inset is empty a generated pin, decoration, light or access point is re-placed by its placement rule in its host (§4.7 S11, §4.7 Light sources, §4.9, II.7.3) and a user's record (an override, pinned label, user-placed or edited pin, hand-placed light, an edit-placed access point) is orphaned and reported; a Works' kept rings and lines are drawn history: each point takes its mean-value image wherever it falls, never re-seated, re-placed or orphaned.
