A door light (standing beside its door on the footprint's ring, on the side §4.7's Light sources (4) draws) keeps its fraction of the ring edge nearest its point — the foot of its point on that edge clamped to [0, 1]; the nearer of two edges by squared distance, a tie to the edge first in the ring's order — its new point that edge's two end vertices where the move leaves them blended at that fraction (the mean-value image of a boundary point; + − × ÷ only), rounded to the lattice, so it stays within half a lattice diagonal of the moved facade whether the warp slides or turns it, the rounding never accumulating; never re-seated; goes with its ring edge even for a locked or pinned entity.

A record of a locked or pinned entity (a door light excepted) is held like a held vertex: the warp's whole-step validation requires it to stay inside its host face at its clearance and halves the step otherwise (§3.6); the dry run lists it. A building's stored wing rings — with a stored stage-3 composition's rings, its plan's points (rooms, wall ends, bays, columns) and tower centres, and the building's basement ring — are carried with its footprint face in the same pass by §2.6's wing-carrying rule, and the whole-step validation includes §2.6's check through warp's recordCheck, halving the step when it fails: the basement's ring within its ground storey's wings (an unedited basement failing it re-derived by §2.6's basement decision, an edited one failing the step); for a stored composition its composed wings uniting to the moved face, its rooms inside the moved face united with the span rings of passages its wings span (J-A30.23), tower centres inside or on it. Every entity whose footprint, trace, deck or pier the move carried is re-based by §2.6's datum step (§7.3 (a) 4), a user-edited base kept; the undo record keeps every former point, wing ring, basement ring, stored composition and base; a replay recomputes the same by replaying the same operation; stamp and grid instances are world-anchored patterns, not displaced (§8.10); B-EDIT warp fixtures are §13.2's (J-DET-31; J-A68.73).

Each ask is a scripted B-EDIT scenario reporting its locality share and invariant results (§13.2); "expressible" counts working, measured edits: add a district → drawBoundary (S6 regroups covered cells; S8-S11 where the class band changed); delete a district → merge into its neighbour (S6 re-types; S8-S11 where the band changed); add roads → drawWay (S4 or S5 local operator; S8-S11 in split cells); remove roads → delete way (S5 regrows the merged cell or S4 re-routes; S8-S11); move / remove labels → moveLabel, hideLabel (LabelEntity.pinned/hidden only; 0 other model changes; S13b re-decides the labels whose boxes meet it); set district colours → setStyle (a thematic row keyed by the district's address; style only, 0 model changes); add / delete vertices → split (a way at a point), merge (edges), moveVertex (L1 edit; S8-S11 in touched cells); place the castle → setAttr(castle, site) (S4 re-routes the castle street; S7 re-traces when the castle is on the enceinte; cells under old and new reservations re-derive); size the castle grounds → setAttr(castle, baileyArea) (reservation resizes; cells re-derive; S7's run when on the enceinte); farms in chosen areas → setAttrMany (land-use faces under a drawn region → arable; S12 on those faces); draw walls → drawWall (S7 re-traces the run or adds an enceinte and cuts its strips; F-REDERIVE on plots in the new strips); draw bridges → drawWay class bridge across a river face (Bridge by §4.2 S1 (5)'s drawn-bridge rule; S4's operator lays the ends through its deck, pinned; deck row holds); drag points in the sea → moveVertex on the coast L0 (S1's water operator: moved coast is the new water, contours clipped, decks re-sited, footprint cleared, kept ways re-laid, others cut; S5 and S6; F-REDERIVE).

migrate(doc, to) has two parts; (1) the schema chain — a sequence of pure, versioned transforms over the document format, forward only; a document whose schema is newer than the running library opens read-only with a message (view and export).

The upgrade (a new output version) is an explicit, undoable upgrade event: the base and the whole ordered log (epochs included) replay under the new output version into a new model; a rebased base is checked then re-rooted — before the replay base.state is decoded under from and its model root compared with its root of record for from (§2.9 step 3; a mismatch refuses the upgrade with a message, the document staying at from), and the replay decodes it under to; the upgrade records the model root of that decoded state as baseDigest, which every later load under to checks.

The mapping: entities of the old model are matched to the new by kind, anchor within the kind's hysteresis radius, class family and, for faces and chains, overlap (IoU ≥ 0.5), through §6.3's matching routine and budget; a matched entity hands its address to its successor, and edits follow it only through §7.3 item 4's class-family check; nothing is matched by string equality.

The fates and renames of the events before the upgrade are recomputed under to; the events whose recomputed values differ from the confirmed ones are named in changedConfirmations and their differences shown in the diff, once (§7.3 item 4).

Packs the new version stops shipping: before the upgrade commits, every pack of the pack set (§2.9) that to does not ship and packs does not hold is copied into packs from from's shipped copy (in the browser where from is the document's own version inside the window and its retained chunk carries its shipped packs, §6.4, and in the CLI), and the mapping names it in packsSaved; a copy that would pass §2.9's 2 MB cap is an F-EDIT conflict naming the pack and its size, nothing committed, the one resolution offered is keeping the old model (removing the pack cannot help, the pack set keeping every pack the log ever named, §2.9); such a town stays at its output version; once that version leaves the browser's window it opens as a frozen view whose frozenImport the same cap refuses (§2.9 step 2), viewable and exportable, and the CLI still replays it exactly (§6.4).
Pack/host-content cap: 2 MB (§2.9's cap).

An unmatched edit is a reported orphan, kept in the log and listed in the orphan table, never silently bound to another entity; an orphaned lock re-imposes its last geometry as a drawn constraint (a drawFootprint, drawWay, drawBoundary or drawWater event appended at the upgrade's position) unless the user drops it, so a locked building stays where it was; a diff (entities changed, orphans, changed confirmations, statistics deltas, and a per-epoch diff for a multi-epoch document) is shown before commit.

The upgrade's undo record is its from output version, not a stored copy of the old model: undoing it replays the base and the log before the upgrade under from (the retained N−1 or N−2 chunk in the browser, any published version in the CLI, §6.4), reproducing the pre-upgrade model exactly, digest included (a rebased base checked against its root of record for from, §2.9 step 3); within the session the checkpoint taken before the upgrade makes it instant; when from has left the browser's window (library updated twice since) the undo is withdrawn there with a notice and the CLI command; the upgrade's diff stays viewable (J-DET-18).

The user may instead keep the old model: the document stays at its output version while inside the retention window (§6.4); outside it the document opens as a frozen view whose one edit is a rebase (§2.9); FTG's "no way to regenerate old towns with new features" and "cannot be undone" are the weaknesses answered (J-DET-44, J-DET-54).

MigrationMap { orphans: Id[] (targets of logged edits left without a successor, kept in the log, listed in the orphan table); packsSaved: { id; version; hash: Hash128 }[] (pack-set packs to does not ship whose content this upgrade copied into packs); changedConfirmations: number[] (seqs of events before the upgrade whose fates or renames recomputed under to differ from the confirmed ones) } — what the upgrade computed and showed; a replay recomputes it and reports a difference as for fates; address hand-offs are recomputed by §6.3's matching on every replay, never stored (the upgrade event stays small); its renames are EditBase.renames.

Upgrade tests (M3a): golden suite replays under N−1 and N−2; a corpus of edited documents upgraded across one output version keeps 100 % of edited entities or reports each orphan (O9 e); an upgrade undone (in session and after a reload) restores the pre-upgrade digest exactly; a METROPOLIS document's saved size does not grow with its upgrades beyond the upgrade events; a keptSnapshot-rebased CITY document upgraded across a test output version whose field driver and digest leaf encoding differ from from's opens editable after a reload and replays to the session's digest, and the upgrade undone restores the pre-upgrade digest; a document using a pack to stops shipping holds it in packs after the upgrade and reopens with it once from has left the window; a document whose such pack copy would pass 2 MB gets the F-EDIT conflict with only "keep the old model" offered and commits nothing; an upgraded document whose pre-upgrade corpus selection renames differently under to lists that change once in the diff and reloads with no mismatch report, while a divergence forced under the confirming version is still reported.

Schema transforms of items 11, 12, 17, 20, 28, 29, 30, 31 (pure, forward-only, checking the old records root and writing the new, §6.2): a plot without builtBand gets it from its DerivationRecord.band and its value companion from the record's field sample (exact for every document without an epoch; for one with epochs the band its last derivation read); fieldBand is that same band; a building's single entrance becomes entrances with one main entrance at that vertex (ordinal 0, nextEntrance 1), its basement derived at first load by §2.6 (an absent decision, never random); every building's use becomes a Use record (§2.7) with the building as only member and no formerUses; a building's households filled from its households' Household.building in address order, the retired occupants list dropped (J-A28.29); condition kept and reusedAs absent; a block's reach open (the parity presets' value); each plot's exposure derived at first load by §4.6's rule from its access rows (no older document has a passage, so no base wing carries spans), its knownTo and its buildings' defaulting from that exposure — an institution's optional knownTo stays absent and reads its plots'; a stored tunnel without headroomCm takes II.7.2's profile row for its kind and the network's preset, navigable derived; an older assignment gets existence 'map' and pinned false, its use linked at first load to the Use its member's building received; Composition.lod admits plan with no data change; a stored plan written before Room.scope and Room.unit gets each room's scope from its role's programme row (circulation for corridors and stair halls) and each room's unit at first load by §2.6's rule (one household: the whole shell is its unit); an elaboration cache is non-canonical and dropped at upgrade; no rejection, positive placement, DossierRef or Passage exists in an older document, so none is invented.

Schema transforms of items 20 (h), 63-72, 74-82 and 101: a use, institution or assignment without concealment reads none, no front; an assignment without state reads active; an AccessPoint without state reads open, its knownTo derived at first load by II.7.3's rule, its source neighbourhood, and its under built from the older tunnel reference as part 0 and that tunnel; a placeAccess event's tunnel reads as its element, and so does the tunnel of an older convert event's underground decline op (silt, caveIn, seal, reopen; DeclineOp, §4.11 — flood is new and has no older form); a plot without tenure derives it at first load (item 70); a district without identity takes its character step's derived one at first load (§4.5), pressure 0, no nameHistory; an older recipe's character entries become its districtIntent entries field for field (wealth, density, age, function mix, planned / organic, greenery, fortification, building scale; the entry without a district the town-wide default); an older district record's stored character is dropped, the derived CharacterVector recomputed at first load (J-A72.21); a document without nextUndergroundPart takes 1 (part 0 the sewer's, §2.9); a Terrain without geology reads ordinary (§2.3); Document.dossier rebuilt from the log's dossier events at first load (item 74); an older event has no dossierChange, proposedBy, closure or points form, none invented; an older epoch event without a week takes its predecessor's week + round(52 × years) (§4.11's EpochInputs.week rule; the first epoch's predecessor week 0; item 76; J-A76.72); model data a later output version derives that an older document never held (Works records, rule-placed lights, the underground layer's other systems, galleries, chambers, links and undercity, clusters) appears only by an upgrade to that version, whose diff lists it, never by the schema chain.

A placeGate, quarter, roster or group event records the sugar.json version it was expanded with (expansion); every replay under the document's own output version expands it at that version (session and replay make the same events); an upgrade whose output version changed an expansion re-expands the event under to and hands its entities on by §6.3's matching like any re-derived scope; events whose expansion changed are named in the diff with the other changed confirmations (MigrationMap.changedConfirmations), once.

effectiveParams = defaults(pinned table versions) ⊕ packs ⊕ preset ⊕ userGlobal ⊕ documentOverrides ⊕ log events, each layer a sparse delta with provenance; setting packs recorded in the recipe, or in the adjust that adds them, by id, version and content hash (§2.9); the UI shows which layer set a value and the report lists auto-resolved values with reasons (O16 a-b).
OVERRIDE LAYER / OverrideLayer: the layers defaults, packs, preset, userGlobal, documentOverrides, log events (GenerationReport.autoResolved[].layer is typed OverrideLayer).

Preferences are folded in at creation: packs, preset, the user's global preferences and document overrides are copied into the recipe's params delta (shown as "from your preferences"); a later change to the machine's preferences never changes an existing document; applying them is the explicit action "apply my current preferences", logged as one adjust per changed parameter with its locality class.

A pack's content is §10.4's; its place in the pack set, retention in packs and a user-uploaded corpus as a pack are §2.9's; adding or removing a pack (selecting or deselecting a corpus included, §10.4) is an adjust of the recipe's pack list (param 'packs'): a Re-derive from the pack's first reader stage with the fate report (§7.1); when the pack changes a naming slice (a grammar row, or the corpus a culture or ancestry row field names) S13a re-draws exactly the unedited names citing a changed slice, listed for confirmation (§6.3 case (4)); a replay resolves every pack by hash from the document first (§2.9); a link is emitted only when every pack of the pack set is shipped, so never for a town whose history selects a user corpus (§6.4).

Every rule table is versioned JSON: a map from a stable row key to a row whose cells carry { value, unit, provenance: { source, date, note }, calibratable, extension?: { over, mode } }; each table's schema declares its readers (the stages consulting it) and its slice kinds (row, weights, bracket, thresholds, match — §2.8).

The editable table registry enumerates: size ladder, stage regimes, way widths, granularity, class rules and class families, heights, wall spacing, greenery, drivers, naming, style sheets, the dependency graph, S0's feature probabilities, the work-limit coefficients (§5.1 (5)); relation templates, supply edges and designation templates (§10.2, §4.7); room-programme rows and layout patterns (§2.6, §10.2); the interior ladder's rows — households per shell, unit forms, shared and staff rooms, circulation and room-size bands per band (§2.6; item 28 (f)); the decline table and the survivors' ladder with durations per rung by direction and stock replaceability, churn caps, orderings, the middle-band designation and each rung's manifestation column (§4.11, §4.5; item 31); the class table's replaceability column (§10.2); hidden-share rows (§4.6); the island rule and sewer existence law (II.6, II.7); UndergroundRule and TunnelProfileRow (II.7.2, II.7.4); the disruption budget rows (§7.7); the entrance and cellar columns of the designation templates (§10.2, read by §2.6); RosterTables.basementGate (§10.2); prosperity.bands (§4.5); market.siting (§4.2 S3 (12)); FarmModeRow (§4.9); reach weights (§4.6); knowledge.admit (§9.2); cut.bendMode and cut.flattenM (§4.6); castle.minInnerM, wall.smoothPasses, the gates' waterfront share, district.growthRate (§4.2, §4.4, §4.5, §4.8); jitter.maxM and jitter.minM (§4.7 S11; jitter.minM's declared range starting above attractCm); the class-mix table and prestige rows (§4.7 S10b, §10.2); cluster rows and tenure defaults (§4.7 S11, §10.2); quarter identities, significance, power and sector links and band ranges with the dials' weights (§4.5, §10.2); the concealment column and cover table (§10.2, read by §4.7); underground system rows, UndercityRule, LinkRule, basement-access rows (II.7.3-II.7.6); WorksTable with its calendar row (§4.11); LightRule (lights.json; §4.7, §8.4); the palette's role values on the owner-opened targets (§8.2); sugar.json (§7.1); the dossier row sets tables/dossier/* (§14).
owner_raw: determinism (tables owned by the sections named)

statement: A naming slice of a culture or ancestry row is one field of it: a SliceRef of kind row with key <rowKey>/<field>, hashed over that field's value and, for a corpus field, the named corpus's content hash (a slice's hash changes when the corpus behind it changes); a naming draw cites only the fields it read, so a set on one corpus field (a user corpus pack's binding among them) changes exactly the names drawn from that field; every other slice stays a whole row, weight vector, bracket, threshold set or match set (§2.8) (J-DET-48).

Emulation first (owner: "based in our base of MFCG and FTG emulation first"): every rule's DEFAULT reproduces what MFCG or FTG does where they have the behaviour (§1.4's tiebreaker chooses where both do); extensions are layered above as data-driven tendencies with a chance or a weight, or options, never fixed laws or orders; a cell's provenance.source names where its value comes from in §17.1 (6)'s grammar — ref:⟨reference⟩ ⟨behaviour⟩ for an emulated default (or its (code) form with its P-id, item 62), otherwise own, architecture ⟨date⟩ or another of its values; an extending cell carries extension { over 'MFCG'|'FTG'|'both'|'none'; mode 'chance'|'weight'|'option' }; the parity presets MFCG and FTG (the presets §13.6's side-by-sides run) set every extension cell's chance or weight to 0 and its option off (hidden-plot share, supply edges, upwind rows, island and sewer rules, the ladder's tendencies among them); with a parity preset on, B-REF's parity rows (§13.5) hold on the references' own behaviour; with the default preset the extensions run at their table values (§13.5's test).

Reading rule for absolutes: where the document says a settlement "always", "never" or "first … then" does something, it means "by default, as a table value that can be changed per region, era and setting"; an engineering invariant (planarity, "never re-rolled", "never stored", a work limit) is not a settlement rule and stays absolute.

The interior ladder's rows (§2.6, item 28 (f)) are defaults in the same sense (a region, era or class may change what a band's households share and how small a poor unit gets); neither reference draws an interior, so the parity presets leave the plan rung alone: with no epoch and no relet every residential building houses what §4.7's generation fill gives it (at least one household, never above capacity), so the static baseline is unchanged.

No corpus content enters the design by the emulation rule except the palette bands the owner released on 2026-09-27 (item 69; §8.2's palette targets), whose role values carry provenance corpus with that release as evidence; the corpus phase re-signs every other table value through §13.9.

Where the reference's behaviour is a VALUE that differs from our default the cell carries presets?: { MFCG?: CellValue; FTG?: CellValue }, each with its own provenance (ref:⟨build⟩ ⟨behaviour⟩ (code) and its P-id where read in code); a parity preset resolves every cell in one order: its own presets entry; else for an extension cell 0 for a chance, weight or number and off for an option; else the cell's default; a categorical option cell has no neutral value, so the table schema refuses one without an entry for each parity preset; rows carried this way: cut.bendMode and cut.flattenM (§4.6 step 5 — MFCG preset straightFirst and 8 m; FTG reads the default); jitter.maxM and jitter.minM (§4.7 S11 — MFCG 4.8 m and 2 m; FTG reads 0, no recession, since no front-recession fact of the FTG client has been read, J-A43.71); the compound enclosure (§4.7 S11 — extension over 'both', its parity value stated there and read by both presets; no third preset for NG 1.2.2, whose §13.6 comparison compares fabric, J-A44.71); the light rows (§4.7, §8.4); §13.5's parity rows run under this resolution (T23-1).

An override records { op, rowKey, field, value, baseRowHash }; when a newer table version changes or removes that row the override is reported as an orphan — kept, not applied — with the old base row, the new row and the user's value side by side; an insert whose key already exists is an orphan too.

A table edit changes the hashes of the slices it touches and exactly the entities whose recorded slices cite a changed slice re-derive (audited by the oracle, §7.3 item 7); recorded slices read from persisted DerivationRecord.slices for plots, blocks, buildings (§2.8), from persisted NamingRecord.slices for every generated name (a naming-table edit re-draws exactly the unedited names citing a changed slice, in a rebased document too), and from the provenance rebuilt by the last derivation or verification replay for every other kind; fallback — where neither exists (a kind without a derivation record in a document rebased from a kept snapshot or a frozen import) and for a row inserted into a table read by predicate (changing its match slice) — Re-derive from the table's first reader stage with the fate report, its confirmed fates stored in the editTable or editPreset event.

Host tables arrive as editTable, editPreset or setStyle events whose content is copied into the log with provenance host (source, date, version), so a document replays without its host (§11.4); users edit through the tables editor and presets dialog (preference layer); we change the system through new table versions — a declared shift whenever output changes (§6.4); the corpus phase replaces values and updates provenance without code changes; the default path with no edits is byte-identical to the shipped defaults (O10 h).
Three input layers above the parameter vector, all persisted in the recipe; a pointer names one as "§7.7 layer n", while "§7.7 item n" names the dossier contract's item n.

"§7.7 layer n" (the three input layers: intent, character, constraints/assignments) versus "§7.7 item n" (the dossier contract's items) — a disambiguation convention for two numbered lists in one section.

Intent (outcome targets; Intent type): form archetype, size as population / area / buildings with a tolerance, water setting and coast side, gate count, wall rings, planned ↔ organic, wealth level and gradient direction, era and region preset, defence level, density; Expansion (intent → ≈ 200 internal parameters) is a pure function held in data: each intent field maps to internal parameters by { param, fn 'const'|'linear'|'smoothstep'|'table', args } rows (tables interpolate linearly) evaluated in a fixed order.
Rows are continuous: no rounding and no comparison inside a continuous control; a discrete outcome is a probability drawn per entity or a discrete control that declares itself (§7.8).

Expansion examples: wealthLevel ∈ [0, 1] → field.characterOffset = lerp(−0.3, +0.3), granularity.joinMaxBonus = 2 · wealthLevel (fractional part = probability a candidate plot takes one more join, drawn from plot.join), greenery.parkPer1000 = lerp(0.1, 0.8); item 71's class mix reads wealthLevel itself (no expansion row), moving every band row's weights toward larger classes in a rich town and smaller in a poor one, cuts staying the town's own (§4.7 S10b; J-A71.42); planned ∈ [0, 1] → growth.headingSigma = lerp(20, 5) degrees per 100 m of street, growth.crossroadProb = lerp(0.02, 0.15), avenues.probability = smoothstep(0.3, 0.7, planned) per eligible tier-1 way.
Every internal parameter is documented (unit, range, effect, provenance, consuming stage) and reachable in the advanced panel (O10 a); the registry test proves 100 %.
Surprise me draws every intent field from its declared range and weights on the intent.surprise stream of a fresh seed and writes the drawn intent into the recipe, so the town's link reproduces it.

For a dossier-bound map the port's creation half fills the intent from the dossier by the derivation table (item 10; wealthLevel from the dossier's prosperity word); the filled values are map facts (item 9) and stay editable.

The per-district intent DistrictIntent (wealth, density, age, function mix, planned / organic, greenery, fortification, building scale), supplied automatically per district and overridable, is the input shaping a district's generation; a district's character is item 72's derived profile (CharacterVector, §2.5), read from what was built and naming the district (§4.5), never an input; the circumstances are one CircumstanceSlice per entry of a timeline dated in weeks (§4.11's week; for a dossier-bound map the host's campaign week, item 76) that schedules epoch events: an epoch happens only as an epoch event in the log (§7.1, hook 8), proposed by the app at a timeline entry or by the port at §4.11's cadence; the timeline's first entry is the creation slice S0 reads (§4.2); the season is read from the week through §4.11's calendar row, never stored; an epoch's population target and terrain events ride its EpochInputs; a government's kind names its lordship (§10.2); the slice carries activity scalars (market, harbour, main-street, default 1) the prosperity field's kernels read under decline (§4.11); the recipe's feature set holds layers.islands, II.6's model setting (§7.8).

DISTRICT INTENT (input, DistrictIntent) vs CHARACTER (derived, CharacterVector, item 72) — distinct concepts; older recipes' "character" entries became districtIntent (§7.5). CIRCUMSTANCES / CircumstanceSlice / TIMELINE (CircumstanceTimeline).

The typed slices are read by item 72's dials and terms (§4.5) and by S2 and S3 (§4.2); each is recipe data at creation and epoch data afterwards; the port fills them from a dossier, and standalone the blueprint and our own rows fill them by the same rules, so every reader sees the same fields with or without a dossier.

Trade partners in order: the dossier's named neighbours and partners its trade links name, each keyed by binding key (item 12); with none, one derived partner per through route of the settlement's access row (source 'derived'); standalone, one per external bearing the blueprint requests, else per through route of its access intent. Weight: a partner's listed trade links (a named neighbour with none counts one), zero for a hostile relationship or a suppressed economy (a rival's or cold-war partner's listed links kept, as SettlementForge keeps them), normalised to Σ = 1, derived partners sharing equally. Mode: where the site has navigable water, partners in weight order take sea (harbour) or river (docks) until their weights cover the water fraction of all toll and duty income (income rows the port marks water — port duties, river tolls — over all it marks water or road — gate and road tolls), the rest road; with no such income the water fraction is the site's default (1/2 harbour town, 1/4 river town; our own values, calibratable); without navigable water every partner is road. Bearing: the realm block's true bearing when sent (source 'realm'); else a draw on gate.pick keyed by the partner's key (§6.1), uniform over the arc the site admits for its mode (open water for sea, upstream and downstream reaches for river, the land arc for road). Road partners' bearings are among S3 (4)'s requested external bearings; every partner's bearing and weight feed TradeFlow (per-gate and harbour weights, dominant bearing), derived from the slice, entrepot and road-and-gate geometry at §4.3. North first: when true bearings arrive for a map drawn on derived ones the port first turns the geo anchor's bearingDeg (§11.1) to fit the derived gates to them (no geometry moves) and moves gates or roads only for the residual, as a dossier event under item 5's least-disruption budget (J-A77.72).
Default water fraction of trade: 1/2 for a harbour town, 1/4 for a river town (own values, calibratable).

Economy shares over §10.2's RosterTables.sectors, Σ = 1: with a dossier its income sources mapped to sectors by the port's revenue rows (a revenue with no sector — rents — drops out and the rest renormalise; J-A78.71); standalone the blueprint's economy setting, by default an even mix amplifying no class (J-A78.72); read by item 72's economy dial (§4.5) at creation and each epoch past its hysteresis (§4.11) and by S2's town-level character (§4.2 S2, §10.2); the shares are read, never modelled (D-10, D-32).

One standing per power: with a dossier standing = its power ÷ the settlement's total, its kind by the port's category-and-name rows (military and arcane powers included, §2.7), governing and secret from the dossier; standalone the governing power the government row names and the established religion (§10.2), 0.6 and 0.4 (own defaults, calibratable); appliedStanding starts at standing and moves only past the dials' hysteresis at an epoch (§4.11); the base reads standings, never materialised factions (Faction stays the module's, §10.1); an arcane standing is honoured whenever a dossier states it and, standalone, arises only under a magic circumstance above none (D-3).
Standalone power standings: governing 0.6, established religion 0.4 (own defaults, calibratable).

The undercity setting (auto by default) is require when the dossier lists a subterranean district-scale record (placed as a neighbourhood assignment II.7.5's existence test must host) and forbid when the blueprint or the host's circumstances rule one out; disorder (0-1, default 0) is the lawlessness II.7.5's size law reads (the blueprint's setting, a timeline entry's over epochs); the dossier's crime scalar never fills it — it reaches the undercity through §4.6's staged crime term alone (item 88; J-A88.41, J-A88.73), so crime is counted once.
Constraints: pins and assignments (layer 3).

Intent (Recipe.intent, §2.9) { form (a forms-catalogue row); population?; areaHa?; buildings? (the size: any of the three); tolerance (relative); water: WaterSetting (§13.3's one spelling); coastSideCdeg?; gates?; wallRings?; planned (0-1); wealthLevel (0-1); wealthGradientCdeg?; era (era and region preset row, §10.2); defence (0-1); density (0-1, the density control §7.8) }.

Assignment { id; granularity 'building'|'neighbourhood'|'dispersed'|'feature'; target? (one building/plot, one district, or for feature the way, bridge, quay or pin a named-feature claim names, item 16); dispersed? { count; kind: BuildingClass | string; criteria }; criteria? (a building or neighbourhood assignment's own soft rows: a naming claim's location phrase); claim? { kind 'name'; bias: { identity (a quarter identity row §10.2); weight }[] } (names and biases, never zones); name?; function?; shapeClass?; drift: DriftBounds (± area %, ± floors, allowed layouts and roof kinds, class family — read against §4.7 S11's designation template, item 19); precedence 'overClassRules'; placed? (solver's placements, persisted with the event); existence 'map'|'dossier' (dossier: exists on every map the module returns, item 20); dossier?: DossierRef; state 'active'|'ruined'|'removed' (item 80: written only by dossier events through item 14's rows; a map assignment stays active); memberState?: Record<Id, 'ruined'|'removed'>; use? (the Use record, moves with it, item 17 (d)); pinned (stays under epochs and re-applications, the town adapts); knownTo? 'public'|'local'|'secret' (item 30 (d); a dossier fact when set; §9.2 reads it); concealment? 'none'|'front'|'hidden'|'underground' (item 63); front? (a front the dossier names; absent: §4.7's cover table picks) }.

PlacementCriteria = RelationRule[] — per-assignment overrides of the class's relation rows (§10.2, §4.7 S10b): nearM → a near row, minSpacingM → an avoid row on the assignment's own members, frontageClass → a frontage row, districts / districtKinds / prosperityBands → band-class filters; PlacementSolver, PlacementRequest and PlacementResult are §4.7 S10b's — the one solver every placement path calls (item 16).

Rejection { element; site; seq (the rejectSite event); held { epoch; populationTarget (the target in force when made: the last folded epoch's EpochInputs.populationTarget, else the population the recipe resolves to at S2) }; lapsedAt? (seq of the epoch or dossier event that lapsed it) } — model data in the digest (§2.8 lists it); the solver reads it as PlacementRequest.rejected while lapsedAt is unset.

DisruptionBudgetRow { kind 'dossier'|'positive'|'relocation'|'assignment'; weights { displacedUse; join; subtractedPart; vacated }; budget; displacementDepth } — a rule table (§7.6); defaults displacedUse 1, join 2, subtractedPart 0.5, vacated 1, budget 6, displacementDepth 1 (own values, calibratable).

DistrictIntent { district? (absent: town-wide default); wealth?; density?; age?; functionMix? (Σ = 1); planned?; greenery?; fortification?; buildingScale? } — each 0-1; absent field derived; the input a district is generated from, never item 72's derived CharacterVector (§2.5).

CircumstanceSlice { era (era and region preset §10.2; its row carries the public-lighting density, item 68); biome (§4.9 climate rows); government: Government['kind'] (its row forces the seats §10.2); threat (0-1: the defence level's source at creation, item 10 DR2; the evolution engine's over epochs); disorder (0-1, default 0, item 65); undercity 'auto'|'require'|'forbid'; magic 'none'|'low'|'high' (item 68; none by default under D-3); landscape { fertileLand; mines; quarries; fishing; logging } (S0 landscape toggles §4.2); activity { market; harbour; mainStreet } (default 1 each); trade: TradePartner[]; entrepot; economy: EconomyShares; powers: PowerStanding[] }.

CircumstanceTimeline { entries: { week (§4.11's week); populationTarget?; slice; events?: EpochInputs['events'] }[] } — Recipe.circumstances (§2.9): entries in week order, the first the creation slice; applied only through epoch events (§7.1).

TradePartner { key (binding key or standalone name); mode 'road'|'river'|'sea'; weight (Σ = 1; 0 for hostile); bearingCdeg; relationship? (the dossier's word); source 'dossier'|'derived'|'realm' }; Sector = a row key of §10.2's RosterTables.sectors (trade, taxes and tolls, crafts, agriculture, extraction, fishing, finance, religion, military, magic, crime); EconomyShares = Record<Sector, number> (Σ = 1); PowerStanding { key; kind: Faction['kind']; standing (Σ = 1); governing; secret; appliedStanding (moves only past hysteresis at an epoch) }.

DerivationRow { row (DR1 …); family; covers (the §2.8 registry kinds and attribute paths the row derives); inputs (digest fields in the order read); rule (the section whose rule derives it); chance (a §6.1 concern or 'none'); bar (the coherence bar it holds, item 11) } — tables/dossier/derivation, provenance own.

DossierBinding { line (the SettlementForge line, item 73); rows[] { dossierKey (binding key); entity (the address carrying Identity.dossier, §2.8, §6.3); kind; since { seq }; rebound? { from; seq; receipt }[] }; factHash: Hash128 (of carried); absorbed[] { seq; week | null; factHash; changeIds } (every absorbed state newest last, item 5's convergence report) }; CarriedFacts = Record<binding key, the dossier fact's fields as the port's digest holds them> — the "previous dossier" item 1's diff runs against.

DossierChange { changeId (host's event, outcome or decree id; else a Hash128 of (element, op, week)); source 'event'|'pulse'|'decree'|'regeneration'|'edit'|'diff'; week | null (§4.11's dating rungs; null: applied finished without transition stages); cause? { kind; ref?; author? }; element { kind 'settlement'|'institution'|'power'|'notable'|'resource'|'condition'|'trade'|'quarter'|'government'|'deity'; key }; op 'add'|'remove'|'state'|'attr'|'tier'|'population'|'prosperity'|'power'|'rename'|'reopen'; before?; after?; fate?; reason? (shown beside the map's rule in the disruption report); receipts (receipt fields found, item 13) } — EditBase.dossierChange.

ReceiptRow { row (F1 … F22); element kind; op; receipts (in precedence order: the first present decides cause, fate and week); response 'assign'|'unassign'|'setAttr'|'status'|'rebind'|'epoch'|'converge'|'none'; dating 'receipt'|'arrival' } — tables/dossier/receipts, provenance own, the SettlementForge line in its header; StatusRow { status; fates? (keyed first, item 14); response 'open'|'wear'|'dial'|'smaller'|'removed'|'ruined'|'none' } — tables/dossier/status.

Precedence: lock > dossier existence > assignment > user-drawn geometry > rule tables > defaults — the one order for every meeting of protections and inputs (§7.2, §5.2 F-EDIT); S10-S11 apply it to assignments; a targeted assignment on a locked entity (or locked attribute path) is an F-EDIT conflict returned as an action (unlock, choose another target, or keep the lock); the dispersed solver never places a member on a locked entity; a host that must override a lock sends an unlock first, and the log records it (J-DET-11).

Dossier existence (with every dossier-owned value, item 11) sits below the lock and above every assignment, drawn shape and rule: a dossier-backed element is never removed by anything on the map and never placed on a locked entity — it takes the best unlocked site the hard rows allow and, when no site passes, its first closest option (fewest hard rows failed, then best score, in §4.7 S10b's order) with the rows it fails reported (F-SITING), never omitted (J-A20.71).

A blueprint's assignments and edits, every element of a dossier a new document starts from (the port's creation half, §14, item 73, builds that blueprint and prefix through the derivation table, item 10, the recipe's seed derived one way from the dossier's, §14, item 85) and the declarations of a skeleton file imported as a new document (§11.1, item 101) become assign and edit events at log positions 0…k, the assign events flagged creation (S2 reads them ahead as fixed rows, J-A22.74: the dossier's elements counted in S2's demand, their land claimed eagerly at S7b and placed claims-first by S10 (3), J-A22.72; a skeleton's drawn declarations read ahead by the stages that make what they declare, §4.1); every assign event (blueprint, dialog, host bridge or host door §11.4) is placed by §4.7 S10b's one solver for its scope (claims-first at 0…k, least-disruption order after the city is built) and applied by §4.7 S11's designation mutator, so an assignment gives the same town whichever way it arrived and never re-rolls what stood there.

When a member of a dispersed assignment is superseded without a successor, only that member is re-placed, with every mapped placement as a fixed point (minimum spacing measured from them); nothing still mapped moves.

An assignment is a stable identity that moves with its use under §4.11's use step unless pinned (then it stays and the town adapts); members are added only by an event changing the count or criteria, then placed with existing members fixed; every move, closing and reopening is reported (§5.4 changes, §11.3).

One way (owner: "the map does not edit the dossier … This module only takes input from SettlementForge and returns back the map"): SettlementForge → map module → map; the dossier enters through §11.4's host door as dossier events (assign, unassign, setAttr with author 'host', EditBase.dossier and EditBase.dossierChange set) in the host's order; the module never writes to, patches or proposes a change to the dossier and the bridge has no message that does (§11.3); map edits live in the map's own document (§2.9), which the host may store as an opaque artifact; nothing flows back.

The port produces the events (§14, item 73): SettlementForge sends whole dossiers and no change list, so the port diffs the incoming dossier against the dossier facts the map carries by binding keys (Document.dossier.carried, item 12), writes one DossierChange per changed element (item 13), dates it by §4.11's dating rungs (item 76) and emits its events.

The map never asks (owner: "it is one directional"): a gap in the dossier is the map's to fill by the derivation table (item 10), never a request — no message, report or field asks the host for a fact; the doors (§11.4) and the port declare OPTIONAL inputs used when present (HostContext, §14), never a required one beyond what the dossier holds today.

Ignore-list: the port never reads a host's own map-side layers (urbanFabric, mapEdits, fogSessions, every worldState.spatialLedgers.* sub-ledger, the spatial substrate included), its derived reads (district profile, map profile, causal state, system state, capacities, daily life, threat profiles, the spine), its generation log (simulationTrace), aiOverlays, generationCoherenceReceipt, its generation sliders (config.priority*), its NPC social groups, and prose beyond a description seed the clerk may read (item 101); the campaign's frozen spatialDigest is the one campaign fact the optional realm block may carry (§14); the adapter reports every key it dropped (ignored_key, §14). Reasons: a host's map memory would make its map program the base (against the owner's rule that what we build stays the base); the sliders' effect already sits in the institutions and income shares (reading them would count it twice); SettlementForge's own district names (in its news) are never matched to our districts (owner, J80 Q6; J-A86.72).

Everything the dossier specifies (buildings, institutions, assignments, named features) is a dossier-backed assignment existing on every map the module returns, live or (when the dossier lists it ruined) present as its ruin (item 14): F-SITING never drops it, delete never removes it, only a dossier event removes, adds or re-designates it; a removal (state removed) leaves the plot vacant through closeUse for item 17's rules to re-use; the dossier's population is a dossier fact — a count the households filling it honour (they are map facts, derived and housed through the roster's demand, §10.2).

A map event (appended without EditBase.dossier by a user or a host's map edit) that would close, remove or re-designate a dossier-backed element is refused as F-EDIT with rejectSite (move it) and placeAt (designate the plot for something else, the element re-placed): an unassign; a setAttr of its use or class; a convert closeUse of its use or mutate of its plot to another designation; a conversion emptying or removing the building housing it (vacate, abandon, decay, ruin, robStone, clear, demolish); a plot join or split whose fate would demolish that building; a map delete is recorded as rejectSite (item 3); a relocateUse or swapUse moves it and is not refused (J-A20.75).

An epoch is bound by the same rule without being refused by it: no step of an epoch closes a dossier-backed use or leaves one without its building — §4.11's Dossier content across epochs relocates it first or keeps it in its building wherever a step would close it or empty or remove that building — so every dossier-backed element is live and placed (or present as its listed ruin) after every epoch (§5.3's row); elements the generator added on its own (filler houses, trees, lanes) may be deleted on the map with local repair, and whatever the dossier needs of them (housing for its population, a demanded class) is re-provided elsewhere by the same solver (J-A20.72).

A map "delete" of a dossier-backed element is the rejectSite event: the site excluded (Rejection; PlacementRequest.rejected), the solver re-places the element by the least-disruption order (§4.7 S10b), surroundings repair locally (§7.3), same seed; the rejection is not permanent (owner: "it is not permanent because if a settlement grows or declines that might be appropriate to put something there"): it holds while the settlement stays in its state and lapses (site eligible again, the element staying where it is) at the first epoch event folded after it whose populationTarget differs from held.populationTarget by more than the roster tolerance (§4.11; item 76; J-A76.43, J-A76.71), or at the first dossier event folded after it whose effective scope holds the site's block; the lapsing event writes lapsedAt inside its own touched set (no event logged for the lapse); an undo of a lapsing epoch that carried no dossier event restores the hold (J-A20.74, J-A20.41); a user lifts a rejection with rejectSite op 'lift'.

Positive placement (owner: "maybe you want a specific place to be something"): placeAt pins a dossier-backed element, an assignment member or a designation the generator controls to a chosen plot; the solver honours it when the hard rows allow (joining plots and mutating buildings by §4.7 S10 (7) and S11, relocating whatever was there by the least-disruption order), else F-EDIT with the blocking rows and closest acceptable sites; it never creates or deletes dossier content, persists until the user lifts it or the dossier removes the element, and draws on siting keyed by the plot and the event (§6.1).

A dossier change after the first map mutates the CURRENT map, never reshuffles: the solver's least-disruption order (vacant or under-used plots first, then a use that can move within the same district, one displacement level, then a join only when the new use needs the land — §4.7 S10b) finds the site, S11's mutator adapts buildings, a removal vacates; households the dossier adds fill standing shells first by relet up to §2.6's capacity before any new plot (item 28 (f), §4.11), plans re-cut per §7.3; positive placements and the map's other edits are honoured first as pins and protected entities (§7.2) and the dossier event applied around them; an edit it can no longer honour is reported and orphaned, never dropped silently (J-A20.73); its disruption (every moved use, joined or vacated plot and mutated building with its causing rule) is computed in the dry run against the request kind's DisruptionBudgetRow, stored in EditBase.disruption and shown as its fate report; the budget bounds the search (the first rung of the order that fits is taken) and the effective scope, never the dossier's authority: an event no rung fits within budget still lands at the least-disruptive site, reported over budget (J-A22.73); everything outside the disruption set keeps its exact geometry and identity (oracle §7.3 item 7 (vii)).

A host restoring an earlier dossier state sends it as a dossier change like any other; the port diffs it, and because §4.7 S10b's least-disruption order takes vacant plots first and §4.11 prefers a building's formerUses, an element removed then restored returns to its own vacated building and an element added then withdrawn leaves the plot it took — the map converges to its earlier state wherever nothing else changed; the residue is reported and the report names the earlier absorbed state the dossier now equals (state_matches_absorbed, by the binding's absorbed hashes, item 12); no rewind of dossier events exists; a dossier event stays no undo target.

The map is a function of the seed, the ordered history of dossier events and the map's own edits (§6.2); the same history replays exactly; two histories reaching one dossier may give different valid maps (continuity over path-independence; owner: the seed should "respect the previous layout prior to the addition or subtraction", J-A22.71); a brand-new map from an existing dossier has every element present from the start (One path); inside the evolution stage the same rules apply; a dossier change the host sends with an epoch rides in EpochInputs.dossier and is applied at §4.11's step (e) after the use step and ladder and before siting (J-A22.42); one sent between epochs folds at its own log position and mutates the map the last epoch left (item 22 (e)); the events an epoch carries take their seq from nextSeq when the epoch event is appended (the epoch's own first, then the carried events' in the host's order), so their draws and minted addresses are keyed as a standalone event's (§6.1, §6.3); they fold only inside the epoch and are never undo targets, nor is the carrying epoch (§7.4) (J-A22.76); the port groups a host's changes by §4.11's cadence (item 76): an element change folds at its own week as a standalone dossier event in the host's order; a population change or typed-slice change rides the epoch the cadence schedules, in its EpochInputs.

A dossier may designate an institution hidden or secret and, for a clandestine one, its concealment and front (item 63): Assignment.knownTo, concealment and front are then dossier facts; the solver prefers hidden plots through the class's relation rows (§4.6, §4.7 S10b; item 30), places a front and the function it hides as one item by §4.7's concealment rule, and §9.2's label policy reads them; a raid or discovery is a dossier event applied as a least-disruption mutation (the front may close, the hidden function relocate, a passage be sealed; items 17, 22, 30); a map delete relocates by rejectSite; a map setAttr of a dossier-set knownTo, concealment or front is refused as dossier-owned (item 11; J-A20.77, superseding the override clauses of J-A30.71 and J-A30.72); the drawing's display stays the user's (a label's display text and visibility §9.1; each viewer's knowledge key §11.3); where the dossier sets no such value it is a map fact edited as §7.1 lists.

The port's creation half is the base's (M1, exercised by the frozen dossier fixtures of §13.2 — items 83, 84 — never by a live host); its absorb half lands with this contract at M3a; its wiring to a live host bridge is the owner's SettlementForge stage (§11.4, §14, Staged by the owner's roadmap; item 73); no door opens the other way (the host's simulator never reads the map's geometry, J86, §11.4); records and rows the port will fill when a host supplies them are declared schema-complete and empty in the base: ConditionOverlay, DepositSite, HistoryHint, PowerRelation and the dossier-backed Person (§2.7), and the impairment, hinterland, crime, custom-weight and legitimacy rows (§10.2) (item 88); everything else in this contract (events, records, precedence, rejection, positive placement, budget, continuity, items 9-16) is the base's, exercised today through the dialog, the API and the fixtures.

Owner: "whatever the dossier doesn't provide, the rest of the map code must compensate. it is one directional. only the dossier is the source of immutable truth while the rest can be constructed at whim. better if the rest of the map code coherently derives things from the dossier and in accordance with our rules".

Every fact is either a dossier fact (a record or value the dossier supplies, carried under its binding key, immutable on the map, changed only by a dossier event) or a map fact (everything else: positions and geometry, plots, buildings and their classes, the households filling the dossier's population, lot assignments, prosperity values, the settlement-level trade direction and partners' derived bearings, a collective record's count inside its range, names the dossier does not give, each district's character), generated, regenerated, edited and replaced freely subject only to items 10 and 11; dossier facts by kind: the settlement's name, tier word and population; each dossier-backed element's existence, state (item 14), name, kind and membership and, where given, knownTo, concealment and front; a collective record's count range; each quarter's name (item 16); the typed slices' dossier-sourced values (partners, relationships and listed links, income shares, power standings, the government); the conditions; for every field §2.8's factTier derives which tier holds it (never stored; J-A20.23), read by §7's edit rules (item 11), §9.2's reader, §11's exports and the API through which any clerk reads (§11.2); an author's declarations (item 101) are map facts factTier reads as declared, held until the author changes them and never above a dossier fact (a contradicting declaration refused as dossier-owned with the closest acceptable alternatives, item 20 (g)) (J-A20.76).
DOSSIER FACT vs MAP FACT (and declared map fact): the two tiers of fact; factTier (§2.8) derives the tier per field.

A map fact the dossier does not supply is derived from what it supplies by the design's rules before any recourse to chance; the derivation table is an INDEX: one row per map-fact family — the dossier inputs it reads (the port's DossierDigest fields, §14), the section whose rule derives it (stated there, never here), where seeded chance enters (a §6.1 concern or none) and the coherence bar it never contradicts (item 11); a row's inputs are read in the order written (a host's optional input when present (HostContext, §14), then the dossier's, then the blueprint's own), the rule's default when none is present; a missing input never becomes a request; standalone the blueprint and our own roster are the inputs of every row (the same rows: connecting a dossier changes inputs, not rules); tests run the rows from M1 on frozen dossier fixtures and blueprints alike (§13.2, items 83, 84); the rows are data (DerivationRow; tables/dossier/derivation, provenance own), each naming the §2.8 registry kinds and attribute paths it covers; §13.2's totality test proves every map-fact family of the registry is covered by a row and every row's chance names a registered concern or none (item 20 (h), item 83's vocabulary test).

DR1 the site (relief, coast and its side, river course and inflow, lake, marsh): inputs the realm cell's terrain, river and coast (optional); site.terrain, site.access, the water deposits, site.culture; rule S0's site request (tables/dossier/site), S1 (§4.2); chance blueprint.features, S1's terrain.* and water.*; bar: a coastal dossier has a coast, a riverside one a river, a port one a harbour basin.

DR2 walls, enceintes and gates: inputs realm gates (optional); walls.records, walls.citadel, walls.flagged, site.access, population, site.threat; rule the access row's gate counts, S0's walls and castle toggles, S3's gate law (§4.2), wall furniture (§4.8); chance gate.pick; bar: walls exactly when the dossier lists a wall institution; gate count inside the access row; a citadel record gives a citadel.

DR3 trade partners, weights, modes, bearings: inputs realm partners (optional); economy.partners, economy.tradeLinks, toll and duty income rows, site.access; rule layer 2's trade fill, road partners' bearings read by S3 (4); chance gate.pick keyed by the partner's key; bar: a hostile partner carries no trade, a rival's listed links kept, a bearing never moves on an unrelated change. DR4 trade flow (per-gate and harbour weights, dominant bearing): inputs DR3's slice, entrepot; rule TradeFlow (§4.3); chance none; bar: weights sum to one; a harbour town's harbour carries the sea share; a derived partner is marked derived.

DR5 districts (count, kinds, boundaries, identities): inputs population; quarter claims (item 16); district-scale records; site.culture (forms weights); power seats (DR11); rule S6's typing and grower, item 72's identities (§4.5); chance district.seed, district.type; bar: every quarter name on at most one district and on exactly one unless reported waiting (item 16); each district-scale record on a neighbourhood of its own; no district named for a social class.

DR6 prosperity field and each plot's band: inputs wealth.label (to intent.wealthLevel by tables/dossier/wealth), economy and power slices, quarter hints; rule the field with item 72's dials (§4.5); chance field.chance; bar: population-weighted mean band within one band of the wealth row's band. DR7 households (count, sizes, bands): inputs population, wealth.label, the rung, the housing record's range, economy slice; rule S2's roster (§4.2, §10.2); chance roster (ordinal draws); bar: members sum to the population within the roster tolerance, residential building count inside the housing record's range, every household housed. DR8 class mix inside a neighbourhood: inputs DR6's field, intent.wealthLevel; rule S10b's class mix (§4.7, item 71); chance siting; bar: the larger classes' share monotone in the value within a band row.

DR9 institution instances (collective count, each instance's class and band): inputs institutions[].kind, .count, .districtScale, population, wealth.label; rule S2's per-capita rows clamped into the record's range (§4.2), DR24's class, its distribution (§4.5 (3)), S11's templates (§4.7); chance roster (ordinal draws); bar: count inside the record's range; a singular record placed once. DR10 positions: inputs class, tags, facets, forbidden, the landmarks naming it, chains and dependencies, the power association, knownTo; rule S10b's one solver claims-first from the creation prefix (§4.7; One path); chance siting (keyed by assignment and member), alloc.district (a dispersed class's controlled random share per district, §4.5); bar: every dossier-backed element placed (item 2); a hard row never broken silently.

DR11 power seats and turf: inputs powers[] (standing, governing, controlled), government; rule §10.2's government rows (seat classes) and §4.7 S10b's faction-turf attractor rows, weighed by item 72's significance (§4.5); chance none (ties by address); bar: the governing power's seat is the government's seat institution. DR12 a district's political alignment: inputs DR10's lots, class-to-power rows (§10.2) with Institution.powers overrides, the power slice; rule item 72 (§4.5); chance none; bar: shares sum to one per district, a shared building counts once. DR13 a district's economic role: inputs DR10's lots, the class-to-sector column (§10.2), economy slice; rule item 72; chance none; bar: a building serving two sectors counts once, partitioned. DR14 names the dossier does not give: inputs the dossier's names (protected), site.culture; rule §10.4 with item 72's dominant components; chance naming, naming.quarter; bar: no generated name repeats a dossier name within its kind.

DR15 buildings (class, footprint, storeys, heights, materials, entrances, basements): inputs the use's class and plot band (DR6, DR10), site.culture (a template-family row); rule S11's designation templates (§4.7, item 19), §2.6; chance siteplan, siteplan.entrance, heights, material; bar: a material never changes a shape. DR16 hidden plots, passages, fronts: inputs facets, criminal categories, covert impairments, the crime scalar (§10.2 staged crime row, item 88); rule the hidden share with its staged crime term (§4.6), the concealment rule (§4.7, item 63); chance siting (front pick); bar: a clandestine record's public views show only its front. DR17 the underground (sewers, accesses, undercity): inputs population, sanitation records, subterranean kinds, crime scalar, the blueprint's disorder, undercity; rule II.7's feature law, II.7.5 with §4.6's staged crime term; chance blueprint.features, sewer; bar: the underground mode only with a navigable run; a required undercity exists. DR18 informal clusters and camps: inputs DR6's field, the rung, slum claims; rule the cluster rows (§4.7, item 70), shanty staging (§4.5); chance siteplan; bar: never on a standing plot floored at the middle band or above.

DR19 the hinterland (land uses, bearings, sizes): inputs the realm cell's resources (optional), site.deposits, economy.foodImportPct, site.isolation, site.terrain; rule S12a and §4.9, foodImportPct through §10.2's staged hinterland row (PortRows.hinterland, item 88) scaling §4.9's farmland once the port fills it; chance hinterland.outside (a deposit's bearing keyed by its key); bar: every listed deposit has its land use. DR20 knowledge of places: inputs facets, covert impairments; rule item 30's defaults (§4.6), item 63 (§4.7); chance none; bar: a covert fact never reaches a public view. DR21 transition timing: inputs the change's week (§4.11 rungs), the calendar row's season, conditions; rule the Works (§4.11, item 67); chance works (epoch's Works: start offset then duration keyed by target lineage with the epoch's week and epoch component; a dated change's or scheduled edit's Works: duration alone keyed by target lineage with its start week); bar: the stage shown at week w depends only on the record and w. DR22 persons beyond the notables: inputs households (DR7); rule derivePerson (§10.3); chance people; bar: a person derives from its key alone. DR23 rung and frame: input population; rule §1.1's size ladders, §3.2 (9)'s frame rule; chance none; bar: the rung is the population's; a dossier below the floor or above the cap is refused (item 15). DR24 a record's class: inputs its name, kind, category, tags, a demotion or upgrade receipt; rule the class rule (item 12); chance none; bar: a kind without a class row takes its category's generic class, reported, never refused.

DR25 a collective record's state over its members: inputs the record's state and severity band; rule the distribution rule (item 14); chance siting (keyed by the assignment, the event's seq as creation index); bar: the affected share equals the severity band's share.

The derivation obeys four rules, proved by §13.2's coherence bars on the design's own dossier events and by the port's bars on the frozen dossier fixtures (item 83), checked at run time by §5.3's coherence rows: (a) no derived fact contradicts a dossier fact (counts, kinds, existence and state, membership, realm-level trade facts — each table row's bar); (b) a dossier change re-derives exactly the dependent map facts (rows whose inputs it changed) inside its disruption set by item 5's least-disruption mutation, never a re-roll; (c) the derivation reads nothing beyond the seed, the ordered dossier history and the map's edits (item 6); (d) nothing derived flows back (item 1); the rules bind the DERIVATION (generation, re-derivation, every dossier event); a user's edit of a map fact (a prosperity stroke, a moved building, a renamed lane) stands; an edit that WOULD alter a dossier fact (a rename of a dossier-named element or quarter, a change of its kind or class, a setAttr of a dossier-set knownTo, concealment, front, state, a collective count outside its range, an adjust of a dossier-bound population or dossier-supplied slice value) is refused as F-EDIT dossier-owned, the map-side alternative offered where one exists (label display text §9.1; a count inside the range).

SettlementForge keys most records by NAME and gives most institutions no id at birth, so the map binds its own stable addresses (§6.3) to the dossier's keys in the document's dossier block (§2.9: DossierBinding and CarriedFacts), written by the port at creation and every absorb; the KEY LAW is stated here and applied by the port's adapter (§14), the only code reading SettlementForge's fields.

Binding keys: settlement → settlement:<id> (the dossier's own id, stable across reloads, same-seed regeneration and section rerolls; a new id is a new dossier and a new map; receipt rename-settlement renames the title label only); institution → inst:cat:<catalogId>, else inst:uid:<localUid>, else inst:name:<slug(name)> (SettlementForge's anchor precedence; #k appended for a collective record's k-th member; two records of one key told apart by order in the dossier, reported duplicate_key; receipts demotedFrom with fate demoted_by_disaster, promotedFrom with upgraded_by_reconstruction: row kept, record re-classed by its new name); power → power:id:<faction.id> when authored, else power:<slug(name)> (receipt rename-faction); notable → npc:<id> (a successor's replacedNpc links its row to the one replaced); condition cond:<id>; resource res:<key>; quarter quarter:<slug(name)>; government government (no receipts).

slug is the line's own name normalisation applied by the adapter (a name key agrees with the catalogue key the line writes at birth); class is read apart from identity (DR24): a record's class comes from its current NAME when a demotion or upgrade receipt is present (its kept catalogue key naming the old kind), else from its catalogue kind, else from its name, category and tags; a kind with no class row takes its category's generic class, reported unmapped_kind, never refused (at M1 the rows cover M1's classes); re-binding only on a receipt of the table: a name change without one is a removal plus an addition, reported rename_without_receipt (J-A74.73); a power's controlled-institution list resolved to binding keys through the stable part the line stores (slug of the institution's own id, else of its name) against the current roster, never through the catalogue key; DossierRef.element is the binding key and DossierRef.version the SettlementForge line; Identity.dossier carries the ref on the entity (§2.8; J-A20.22); a re-binding re-points a binding row and never re-keys a map address (§6.3); the model digest does not cover the block (the model carries each entity's current key in Identity.dossier, and carried holds dossier facts the map does not draw, e.g. a notable's role, whose change must not change the digest); binding rebuilt from the log's dossier events at load and must equal the stored rows (§5.3); factHash is the hash of carried (J-A74.71).

Every event a dossier change generates carries its DossierChange in EditBase.dossierChange so the disruption report, LifecycleEvent.cause and §5.4's changes say why (host's reason beside the map's rule, item 22 (b)); SettlementForge records a change only through scattered receipts (stamps, capped history lists, decrees, a news feed), so the port reads them through the RECEIPT TABLE (ReceiptRow; tables/dossier/receipts): per change kind the receipt fields in precedence order (the first present decides cause, fate and week by §4.11's dating rungs) and the response; the design states the ten rows the survey's verification corrected and F22 (item 87's undo row); the others — F6 reopened, F7 population, F9 prosperity, F10 power standings, F11 government, F12 conditions, F13 resources, F16 deity, F17 notables, F19 a confirmed table event, F21 a reroll — are data rows of the same type, their completeness §13.2's vocabulary totality test (item 83); a change no rung dates is applied finished without transition stages, reported unreceipted_change.

F1 institution added (a new binding key; createdByEventId or an add-institution decree; _worldPulseTierAdded, _worldPulseEconomyBuilt or _worldPulseFounded with outcome ids and foundedAt; the fate founded_by_flourishing writes nothing else, dated by arrival alone) → an assign with existence dossier placed by S10b's dossier request; an addition under a key carried as removed or ruined is a REOPEN (F6, item 14); a missing foundedAt never reads as "stood since the founding". F2 removed (worldPulseFate and _worldPulseInactive FIRST — closure fates hollowed_out, abandoned, bankrupt, closed_for_want_of_custom, shuttered, abolished, disbanded, captured_by_local_powers, abandoned_with_the_settlement under status remnant — then status removed with removedByEventId, or a remove-institution decree) → item 14's removed: unassign, closeUse, plot vacant. F3 reduced or converted (fates privatized, downsized, reduced_to_watch_post, survives_as_remnant; demotedFrom or promotedFrom) → setAttr of the designation in place (item 18 mutation); demotion or upgrade is also F15's re-binding. F4 impaired or restored (visible impairments[], state impaired derived) → physical types (capacity, infrastructure, access, supply) one condition step per severity band; non-physical (legitimacy, influence, wealth, staffing, corruption) the institution's own dial term only (§4.5 (6); J-A88.42). F5 ruined (status ruined with destroyed_by_disaster, remnantReason and the calamity's targets; never destroyedByEventId, the settlement's) → item 14's ruined. F8 tier moved (a tierHistory[] entry, or a bare tier change with none) → rung re-read at the next epoch's target (§4.11); the tier word re-titles the map (item 15). F14 trade (_cutRoutes, _userRoutes, a route link, tradeLinks, a partner's relationship; rival's or cold-war partner's links kept, only hostile or suppressed economy carrying none) → the trade slice at the next epoch. F15 rename (rename-settlement, rename-faction, rename-npc; for an institution only demotedFrom or promotedFrom) → item 12's re-binding; without a receipt a removal plus an addition, reported. F18 decree (decrees[] applied with tickRef; the week's decreeCauses[]) → the decree's own change rows; a decree whose verb binds no world effect expects no change. F20 settlement ended or born (destroyedByEventId on the root; lifecyclePatch; memberBirths) → an END is an epoch ruining every building by the decline hooks (§4.11); a resettlement of the same site is the SAME map regrowing on its old plan by item 8's regrowth-first order (owner, J80 Q4; J-A75.72); a member birth is a new dossier and a new map. F22 host undid a change (incoming fact hash equals an earlier absorbed state's) → item 5's forward convergence, reported state_matches_absorbed.

SettlementForge never deletes a record, so an assignment carries state written only by dossier events through StatusRow rows (tables/dossier/status), keyed on the fate word and inactive flag BEFORE the status (a bankrupt shop never kept open as a smaller designation): absent or active → open; impaired (derived from visible impairments) → open, physical types wear the building one condition step per severity band, non-physical reach the institution's own dial term only (§4.5 (6)); remnant with privatized, downsized, reduced_to_watch_post or survives_as_remnant → a smaller designation in place (item 18 mutation); remnant with a closure fate (F2's list) or removed → removed: unassign, closeUse, plot vacant (item 2); ruined, destroyed, destroyed_by_disaster, ruined_by_decree → ruined: PRESENT as its ruin, use closed, building ruined (§2.8 existence), counted present by §5.3's dossier row; vacant (an empty seat) → no physical change. A listed ruin stays on the map as its ruin (never contradicted by a map showing it open or gone); an epoch keeps it as it stands — the decline ladder never robs, clears or rebuilds its building (§4.11's exemptions) until a dossier event changes its state; a reopen (to active) re-opens its use in its own former building first (S10b's dossier request ranks it first, §4.7), repaired by a Works where item 67's clock runs (§4.11) and at once otherwise; a collective record's state is distributed over its placed members: the affected share = the severity band's share (all members when no severity), members chosen on siting keyed by the assignment with the dossier event's seq as creation index, recorded in memberState; the record's state stays active while any member is.

A dossier whose population lies below 1 500 is refused by the port (E_RUNG_UNAVAILABLE, naming the village product, PART III) while no village product is registered: §1.1's clamp to a 1 500-person TOWN applies only to a blueprint request carrying no dossier; a dossier above the 120 000 cap is refused the same way (E_RUNG_UNAVAILABLE naming the cap, nothing absorbed); both refusals hold at creation and every absorb (§14's creation and absorb); §1.1's clamp to the cap serves only a request without a dossier; inside the ladder the population chooses the rung (§1.1) at creation and at each epoch's target (§4.11); the dossier's own tier WORD is a dossier fact and the map's title word (§9.5) — a "city" of 5 001 people is drawn on the TOWN rung and still titled a city; a bare tier change with no history entry fires row F8 like any tier receipt.

Dossier population floor 1 500 persons (TOWN floor) and cap 120 000 (metropolis cap); a dossier outside [1 500, 120 000] is refused with E_RUNG_UNAVAILABLE while no village product is registered (floor side).

SettlementForge picks its quarters by a name test at generation and never refreshes them, so a quarter enters the map as a NAMING CLAIM, never a zoning: a neighbourhood assignment with claim set, carrying the quarter's name, a kind bias from the quarter rows (tables/dossier/quarters: Market → market identity; Religious → temple; Noxious Trades → craft with noxious rows; Waterfront → docks or riverbank by its phrase; Government → the seat's district; Mages' → arcane identity; Artisan → craft; Shadows → a low band and larger hidden share; Wealthy and Common Residential → band biases; Roadside Shrine → a shrine claim with a soft edge row; the village quarters Alehouse & Common, Fishing Landing, Woodcutters' Ground one row apiece), and its location phrase as SOFT rows in criteria ("Downstream/downwind" → downstream, downwind; high-ground phrases → highGround; "Central" and "Village centre" → nearCentre; water phrases → nearWater; "Between market and residential" → nearMarket; "At the forest edge" → toward the wood land use; "Isolated area (safety concerns)" → far from the centre; "Old town or slums" → the oldest stage and a low band; "At the settlement edge" → the edge; "Spread throughout" → no district; "Eastern district (traditional)" → a soft east row at low weight, a placeholder dropped on the owner's word); at creation S6's typing reads the claim's bias and rows as soft terms (§4.5); the district whose emergent identity best matches the claim carries the name (protected as an assigned name, §10.4, kept past item 72's hysteresis); when no district matches above the claim floor the name waits, reported, re-matched at each epoch, never forced; an ABSENT quarter is never a fact; SettlementForge's own district names (its news) are never matched; a landmark string the roster already demands becomes a NAMED-FEATURE claim (granularity feature: the way, bridge, quay or pin it names — a notice post among the pin kinds, §2.7; tables/dossier/landmarks); nothing is created for a string alone.
Quarter naming-claim floor = 0.5 of a perfect match (own value, calibratable).

A whole-neighbourhood assignment sets the district's intent (layer 2) and its class mix — overriding the class-mix table's weights inside the district (§4.7 S10b, item 71) — while every building stays individually diversified by the class rules within the drift bounds (read against §4.7 S11's designation template, item 19, passed to BuildingGenerator.compose); a district-defining dossier institution is such an assignment with existence dossier, one district per instance (item 72, §4.5); assignments are events (persist, undo, migrate) and take precedence over class rules (O10 e); stable addresses for districts, neighbourhoods, plots and buildings are §6.3's.

Forms catalogue (should-have; the schema is the must-have hook): a form is a row { id, constraints, growthProgramme, signature } — constraints (site request, wall rings, plaza position, planned flag, gate count band), a growth programme (stage regimes and branch tables, §4.4), a morphometric signature (radial share of arterials, orthogonality index, street-density profile, block-area CV, enclosed share); initial rows: organic, bastide-grid, linear-street (growth anisotropy a = 8 along the main road, §4.4), radial, hill-acropolis, bridge-town, port-quay-parallel, monastic-close, island-city (shore destinations, §4.2 S3), confluence, twin-town, polycentric (two or three nuclei, §4.2 S3), citadel-and-port (item 101: a walled upper town on high ground over a walled lower port — two nuclei of §4.2 S3, the upper on a hill site primitive with its own enceinte, the lower on the quay front with its own, one arterial joining them); forms compose by growth stage (an organic core with a planned extension); O10 (g)'s classifier runs on the signature vector.

The control registry declares for every control its output metric (density → buildings per ha; wealthLevel → median plot area and greenery share; greenery → private green share), range, consuming stage (the earliest stage reading it), locality class (local — consumed at S10 or later, or spatially scoped: Adjust is local — or re-derive from Sk — the action shows the fate report first), continuity class (continuous or discrete, with a discrete control's levels) and a documentation anchor linked from the control as context help; the same registry fields (label, range, unit, output metric, consuming stage, locality class, continuity class, anchor) generate @plat/docs' reference pages.

Islands: at TOWN and every village rung the control is disabled with the reason "islands only at CITY and METROPOLIS (II.6)"; at CITY and METROPOLIS it is the model feature recipe.layers.islands (off / on; consuming stage S7b; locality re-derive from S7b; discrete), the sky layer's visibility a separate view control (LayerSpec.visible, §8.4; no model effect) that shows the islands a settlement has and never creates one. Sewers: one control with two meanings by rung — at TOWN a model feature (auto / on / off; consuming stage S0; locality re-derive from the network stage, confined to the underground arena; discrete), at CITY and METROPOLIS a view control (the underground layer's LayerSpec.visible; no model effect) — hidden by default at every rung (II.7.1); both rows carry locality class and anchor in the registry and sit in the advanced panel outside the basic panel's count; elaborate (item 28) is no control: per-viewer view state (§2.9) deciding when a pure rung is derived, never what.

CI sweep: each continuous control over 21 evenly spaced steps × 50 seeds at TOWN and CITY (METROPOLIS nightly): monotone — the mean of the control's metric moves in the declared direction between adjacent steps, a reversal of at most 2 standard errors allowed; continuous — no adjacent step moves the mean by more than ε = max(3 standard errors, 3 × the median adjacent change of the mean); per seed — at most 10 % of seeds jump by more than 5 × the median per-seed step at any one step; the formula is fixed now, the standard errors and medians are what the M1 sweep measures; continuous controls are smooth maps with no thresholds inside (VG's "1 vs 0.999" is the failure); discrete controls (walls on/off, form) declare their effect in the report.
