Transient arenas (J-A28.31): the composition rungs - a stage-3 compose() and the plan storeys, one at a time (§2.6) - partition rings that are no plat faces (rooms cut into the L4 arena would enter its index partitions and the model digest on every click, so a click would change the model, §4.1, §6.2); they cut on a TRANSIENT ARENA: a one-level scratch subdivision on the world lattice under §3.2 numbers, §3.6 insertion rules and §3.10 invariants, opened for one derivation call and gone at its end.

statement: type TransientKey = { transient: true; owner: Id (the entity whose derivation opened it); n: number (per call, never persisted) }.

type ArenaKey = PlatKey | TransientKey - what KernelTx.key and CommitRecord.key name, what resolve, pointLocate and faceNeighbours accept; resolveVertexAt, signature and sampleProfile read a plat role rows and take a PlatKey.

transientArena(owner: Id, seed: Ring[] (world lattice rings, counter-clockwise, tiling: interiors pairwise disjoint, two rings meeting only along sides or at vertices; tiled wings share each joint vertices by §2.6 wing-carrying rule 1, while a vertex one ring has on another side splits that side), fixed: { ring; owner }[] (counter-clockwise, faces made before any cut and never cut, each inside one seed ring - a room never spans a joint between wings - interiors pairwise disjoint, a ring coinciding with its seed ring allowed: a stair core bay, a hearth chimney stack, a spanned passage room (item 30), a composer room (a hall, a tower round room: §2.6 Composition.rooms) less any stair bay or chimney stack in it (§2.6 contract of stage 3) and, on a re-cut, the rooms §2.6 interior ladder keeps (item 28 (f))), workLimit: number): KernelResult<TransientKey> - E_DEGENERATE (detail seed | fixed | overlap) names the offending vertex (for overlap, a vertex of the offending ring); the construction moves nothing.

readBack(key: TransientKey): { faces: { ring; holes: Ring[]; owner: Id | null; fixed: boolean }[]; edges: { a; b: LatticePoint; left: number; right: number | outside (face indices in this result); seed?: { ring; side } (the seed ring whose side the edge lies on with that ring interior on its left - for a joint, whichever of its two rings lies on that side - and which side by that side first vertex index); joint: boolean (on a side two seed rings share) }[] }.
release(key: TransientKey): void - ends the transient arena; no slot of it outlives release.

Transient arena opening: its L0 faces are the seed rings then the fixed rings, each a face of its own, inserted as exact topology the way §3.9 load inserts stored chunks: a lattice point two rings share is one vertex, a side two rings share is one edge (the wall at the joint between two wings - an interior wall, never a party wall, §2.6), a vertex within the hot pixel (0.71 cm) of another ring side splits that side there, and no attraction moves any of them; an input ring breaking minEdge, clearance or simplicity is refused with E_DEGENERATE (detail seed or fixed) naming the vertex, which F-PLAN tier 1 takes (§5.2), so a planner places an anchor on a wall or at least minEdge from it.

Transient arena overlap refusal: seed rings that overlap, and a fixed ring that crosses a seed ring side, lies outside the seeds union or overlaps another fixed ring, are refused with E_DEGENERATE (detail overlap): two crossing input sides are refused where the construction meets them, and it then labels every face with how many seed rings and how many fixed rings contain it by the booleans winding walk (§3.7), so a face inside two seed rings, a face inside a fixed ring and no seed ring or inside two fixed rings, and a fixed ring whose inside is more than one face are found exactly, in one walk.

The seed clip (tileRings): a caller whose wings overlap (§2.6 rule 4 (iii)) passes them clipped to tile: the faces of one overlay of the storey rings on the arrangement (§3.7 boolean machinery), each face going to the first ring in the order passed (§2.6 clip order) that contains it and each ring faces united; each ring is thereby minus every ring before it (a covered ring has no piece; one cut in two has two), and every ring carries each crossing vertex the overlay placed on its sides, so joints are shared sides vertex for vertex; the overlay moves no vertex where rings keep §2.6 composition contract (at least attractCm apart except at joints). A piece left with a hole (earlier rings inside a later one without reaching its sides) is refused (E_DEGENERATE, detail overlap, naming a vertex of the hole), because a seed is one ring. §2.6 clip order puts a contained wing after its container, and a composed tower wholly inside a wing before that container only where an earlier overlapping wing carries its cut to the container sides, so the refusal marks a caller bug (F-PLAN, §5.2).
The opening exact insertion is the one way edges enter a transient arena other than through its face partitioners, as §3.9 load is for a stored plat (J-A28.34).

Fixed edges: the seed and fixed rings edges are the arena FIXED EDGES: mergeFaces refuses to delete one (E_STRUCTURAL) and absorbSliver never deletes one (a sliver bounded only by fixed edges stays a face, W_SLIVER_RETYPED, §3.6); no writer moves a vertex there - a wall moves by mergeFaces then splitFace at its new line (the plan moveWall, §7.1), so warp is not offered - which makes §3.10 seed-tiling row hold by construction.

Transient arena op set: its batches are §3.3 transactions with the transient fields (either op form, the caller workLimit); its writers are the face partitioners splitFace, connectHole, radialSplit, ringBand, mergeFaces, absorbSliver, setOwner; booleans, offsetFace, insetRing, obb, lir, sideRuns, skeleton, faceNeighbours and area2 are services on its faces; insertChain, splitThrough, removeEdges, clearFiner, retypeEdges, claimSubFace, corridorUnion, bandUnion, warp and pinVertices are NOT offered on it.

A transient arena has no static partitions (its dynamic grid serves every query), no stage ranks, no kept content, no role rows beyond the owners the caller sets, no PlatKey and no entity; it is never persisted (§3.9), digested (§6.2) or frozen (§3.3); no slot of it outlives release. readBack returns rings and edges as values in §3.3 canonical order, so the caller records (plan storeys, rooms, walls, openings, §2.6) depend on the input rings and op sequence alone, whichever worker cut them.

A caller may plan its cuts on a coarser module of its own (the plan rung wing-local module, a table row, §2.6): the module is the planner grid, never a second lattice - every point enters through snap and the placement rule, so a cut ends lie on the fixed edges within the hot pixel of their input sides and the tiling holds exactly.
Transient arena opening costs O(seed vertices) and each op what the list states, on tens of vertices per storey; §12.7 stage-3 rows count it.

The input sides are the arena routes (J-A28.34): a side of a seed or fixed ring as passed is an INPUT SIDE; no split changes it; it is the route of every fixed edge on it (as a plat coarser route is the route of Steiner vertices a finer batch places, §2.2 rule 3); the arena grid holds it as one route-edge item, its box the side padded by the hot pixel (§3.3). That route is read by placement and by its grid item and is never the unit of an answer: a query and readBack return each arena edge as its own item (a grid hit on an input side expanding into its pieces meeting the box), keyed by §3.3 canonical key on that edge own endpoints (every vertex of the arena being of its one level), so no two edges share a key and an edge on more than one input side needs no choice.

Every vertex a face partitioner places on a fixed edge (a cut end, a ray, a band cross edge) is placed by §3.6 placement rule against the input side that edge lies on, never a sub-edge an earlier split left: test (i) reads that side line, and on an edge lying on several input sides it reads each (a joint lies on two; a fixed ring side along a seed side on two; a fixed ring side along a joint - a kept room, or the passage room, a span ring both seed and fixed, §2.6 - on three; two fixed rings sides back to back across a joint on four). So every vertex on a fixed edge stands within the hot pixel of the line of each input side it lies on, and a kept ring vertices meet the split test when it re-enters.

A re-cut is the same call (item 28 (f); J-A28.33): the plan derived again for new occupants under §2.6 interior ladder opens a fresh arena from the same seed rings (the shell item 31 geometry floor fixed, §4.11), passes as fixed the rings §2.6 re-cut rule fixes (stair core bay, chimney stacks, passage room, composer rooms, each less a bay or stack it holds, and the rooms the ladder keeps) and cuts the rest; after item 18 mutation the seeds are the mutated shell rings, and a room is kept only where its seed ring (its wing extent at that storey, clipped to tile) is unchanged (§2.6 kept-room rule).

Kept ring re-entry: a kept ring re-enters exactly on the lattice points it left with and keeps its polygon (every vertex unmoved and in order; any vertex a new wall adds lies within the hot pixel of one of its sides). Its vertices on a seed ring side or another fixed ring side lie within the hot pixel of that side line, so the construction splits the side at each. The only geometry beside it that can differ is such a side straightened (by at most the hot pixel) where an unkept wall ended on it, so the exact insertion accepts it unless that straightening brings the side within minEdge of one of its vertices, which is refused as above (J-A28.34).

Nothing of an earlier cut is edited, because no arena outlives its call: the model derives the plan as a chain of least-disruption steps (§2.6 canonical chain, J-A28.26; §7.3), each step its own open, cut and read-back, counted by §12.7 plan row. The seed rings never change with the occupants, so the interior changes while the shell cannot; §3.10 seed-tiling row holds on every re-cut as on the first cut. The unit-door rule of §2.6 (its §5.3 check) reads readBack edges: a door edge has the unit room on one side and a circulation face or outside on the other.

statement: Attraction (GEO-3; J-K2): insertChain processes each chain of a batch in the batch order (canonical for a declared op set, issue order in a callback-form stage, §3.3) in five steps. Its CANDIDATES are: (a) the vertices and edges of level <= the batch level; (b) the finer vertices lying on those edges routes where the chain ends on or joins such a route (a neighbour plot-line end on the kerb where II.1 (3) neighbour step lands its corridor_split edge; a close-up kept fabric beside a new junction); (c) in a batch declaring a clear region, its prepared vertices (KernelTx.prepared, §3.3 rules 2-3). Nothing finer is a candidate.

Promotion by attraction: a finer vertex of (b) or (c) that a chain vertex lands on, or a chain segment is routed through, is promoted to the batch level (§2.2 rule 3; W_PROMOTED, listed in the commit record), its finer edges kept. A (c) promotion clears the vertex split flag (it is a vertex of the new coarse chain) and strips an anchor contact name (its work done); a (b) promotion keeps the flag (the vertex still lies on the edge it split), and removing the promoting chain later returns it to its level by demotion (§2.2 rule 3; J-K28). A clear-region batch never shares a finer edge (§3.3 rule 2).

Obstacles: kept geometry, and inside a clear region every finer vertex and edge other than the prepared contacts, is an obstacle: a chain crossing it or coming within attractCm of it returns E_KEPT or E_LEVEL (§3.3). A chain is inserted run by run; the part already inserted counts as existing geometry for later parts, so a chain doubling back near itself attracts onto itself like any other edge.

insertChain step 1 Snap and decimate: every point passes snap (§3.2 (7)); consecutive points closer than minEdge are decimated - the later dropped unless its index is in opts.pinned or it is a knot (§3.4); two such protected points closer than minEdge merge at the first, reported, and a merged knot vertex carries both ordinals (a step in its profile). A chain that touches or crosses itself is split into simple runs.

insertChain step 2 Vertex attraction: a chain vertex within attractCm of an existing vertex moves onto it (nearest; ties to the smaller lattice position, y then x). Otherwise, within attractCm of an existing edge (nearest; ties by the edges canonical keys, §3.3), take the exact foot on that edge: if the foot lies within attractCm of one of the edge endpoints, the vertex moves onto that endpoint (the nearer; ties y then x), because a split there would leave a sub-edge shorter than minEdge; otherwise it moves onto the edge at the foot placement point by splitThrough - a Steiner vertex if the edge is coarser. Worked example: vertex (20, 20) beside edge (0,0)-(1 000,0): 28.3 cm from (0,0) (not vertex-attracted), 20 cm from the edge, foot (20,0) 20 cm from (0,0), so it moves onto (0,0). Chain vertices attraction brings within minEdge of each other merge, the later into the earlier, as in step 1.

insertChain step 3 Segment and stretch attraction: a chain segment passing within attractCm of an existing vertex is routed through it. Where a segment runs within attractCm of an existing edge over a stretch (near-parallel approach, or a crossing shallower than minFaceAngle) the stretch is shared: the chain joins the edge where the stretch begins, follows it and leaves where it ends, the shared edges gain the chain roles (W_STRETCH_SHARED). A join or leave point within attractCm of an endpoint of the edge moves onto that endpoint (as step 2); any other join or leave point is placed by the placement rule; a stretch whose join and leave points would lie closer than minEdge collapses to one contact point, handled by step 2.

insertChain step 4 Crossings: remaining crossings computed exactly, placed by the placement rule and resolved by iterated snap rounding (<= 3 passes; each pass leaves a planar arrangement, so an unconverged result still commits, reported W_SNAP_PASSES; sub-centimetre re-routes of Steiner vertices are snap-rounding re-routes with the same guarantee).

Wedge routing (step 4): two consecutive crossings closer than minEdge lie on the two arms of an acute corner (the clearance invariant forbids any other way) and are resolved at that corner instead of cutting a sliver off its tip (W_WEDGE_ROUTED): when the corner is the existing arrangement (two crossings along one new segment) the chain is routed through the corner vertex; when it is the chain own (two crossings along one existing edge) the chain corner vertex moves onto that edge at the placement point of its foot. The chain moves at most minEdge / (2 tan(theta/2)) for a corner of angle theta: 0.47 m at the 30 deg junction floor, 1.2 m at the 12 deg plot floor. An optional chain that would move more than attractCm this way is rejected with E_BELOW_MIN_EDGE.

insertChain step 5 Re-walk: only faces incident to touched edges are re-walked; face records, owners, parents and stage ranks are updated - a kept face is re-parented into the new face that contains it (§3.3); the commit record lists them.

The placement rule (GEO-3, GEO-35; J-K17): every new vertex on an existing edge (a split foot, a stretch join or leave point, a crossing) is placed at the lattice point nearest its exact position among points that (i) lie within 0.71 cm of the existing edge route at the edge own level (one index item, §3.3), so that edge moves no more than its hot pixel; (ii) lie at least minEdge from the endpoints of the edge being split and, for a crossing, from the endpoints of the crossing segment; (iii) keep every vertex and edge around the split at least minEdge from the new vertex and from every edge incident to it (clearance, checked in the index); ties y then x. The search runs outward from the exact position, never beyond attractCm, charging each candidate to the work count.

Placement rule behaviour: the nearest lattice point qualifies almost always; it fails only where a vertex already stands between minEdge and minEdge + 0.71 cm from the edge (a gap a previous rounding or a warp can leave) and a point rounded towards it would bring it inside minEdge; then a qualifying point lies a few cm along the edge (a point about 5 cm along the hot-pixel band is at least minEdge from it). Measured (fixall_kernel_r2_attract.out C): 200 000 crossings next to a vertex 25-26 cm from the crossed edge - plain nearest rounding leaves 1 361 edges shorter than minEdge; the placement rule leaves none, moves a crossing at most 0.84 cm and keeps it within 0.71 cm of the crossed edge.

Placement rule fallback: if no candidate qualifies, the incoming vertex moves onto the nearer endpoint of the edge (a crossing routes its segment through that endpoint) and the new segments re-enter step 3; each re-route lands on an existing vertex, so the loop ends within the work limit.

W_PLACED reports every vertex the placement rule places away from its nearest lattice point: a new, re-seated or sliding vertex seated at a qualifying non-nearest point, and an incoming vertex moved onto the edge endpoint because no candidate qualified. Snap rounding is the same rule for points on no existing edge (nearest lattice point).

Placement bound drift (J-K32): the rule gives every vertex it places, re-seats or slides onto a coarser edge §3.10 placement bound; a later same-level change of that route (a split, promotion, demotion or dissolution, §2.2 rule 3) moves no finer vertex and may leave one farther off: one promotion in ten leaves another finer vertex up to about 1.25 cm from its new route edge, a same-level split about as often, and successive changes up to about 1.36 cm after two and about 1.49 cm after three or four (fixall_kernel_r4_checks.out A, fixall_kernel_r5_checks.out B). Nothing reads that standing distance but the index, whose route-edge boxes cover it (§3.3).

Existing geometry wins: an incoming chain vertex moves at most sqrt(2) * attractCm = about 36.8 cm (onto an edge endpoint from beside the edge), or by the step-4 corner bound at an acute tip; no existing vertex moves; an existing edge moves only by its hot pixel (<= 0.71 cm) where a vertex is placed on it.

No edge shorter than minEdge can be created: every edge a batch creates is one of four kinds, each >= minEdge: (a) a chain segment between consecutive chain vertices (decimation and merge rule); (b) a sub-edge of a split existing edge (placement rule (ii)); (c) a chain segment ending at a split point or crossing ((ii) again for a crossing segment own endpoints, and the merge rule when the chain previous vertex is an existing vertex beside the split); (d) the span between two crossings (resolved at the acute corner by step 4). Clearance holds by steps 2-3 for every new vertex and segment and by (iii) for every placed vertex.

Measured (fixall_kernel_r2_attract.out A-B): over 400 000 vertices dropped in the attraction band of random lattice edges, 0 sub-edges shorter than minEdge (shortest 25.50 cm; 5 729 moved onto an endpoint; largest displacement 36.72 cm); on cut endpoints of Chaikin x2 spines with 7.9 m median segments (fixall_kernel_r2_attract.py B), 6.38 % attracted, displaced p50 12.9 cm and at most 26 cm, shortest resulting edge 25.6 cm. Constructive fixtures: §13.1.

Chain classes - mandatory: coast, shore, bank, river, wall trace, arterial, band and kerb edges, plot lines, user-drawn geometry cannot fail for a precision reason: after attraction and placement no precision error is left, only §3.1 non-precision codes can reject one, and a corner below minFaceAngle commits with W_ACUTE_CORNER.

Chain classes - optional: growth proposals, optional lanes, decorative lines are also rejected with E_BELOW_MIN_ANGLE; with E_BELOW_MIN_EDGE when the chain collapses below one edge after decimation or when wedge routing would move it more than attractCm (step 4); or with E_SELF_INTERSECT where their role requires a simple ring: a proposal that cannot be inserted is not a street. The F-NUM ladder of §5.2 applies to optional chains; mandatory chains never reach it.

Clearance: attraction and the placement rule maintain §3.10 clearance invariant for insertions, and warp checks it for moves. Consequence stages rely on: a setback smaller than minEdge collapses to zero (a building front drawn 10 cm behind the kerb lands on the kerb), so a stage wanting a visible setback draws at least minEdge (§4.7).

Roles on shared stretches (GEO-4): when a chain shares an edge (by stretch attraction or an exact collinear overlap) the edge role set gains the chain (role, entity, level) row: never a duplicate edge, never an overwrite. A wall pulled onto a river bank is one edge carrying bank and wall; a quay on a shore carries shore and way.

Slivers (GEO-4): a face below its class floor (width or area, never minEdge) is resolved by absorbSliver: it merges into the neighbour across its longest shared boundary whose edges carry only partition roles; if every candidate boundary carries a structural role, no edge is deleted and the sliver stays as a face of kind residue owned by the neighbour across its longest boundary (W_SLIVER_RETYPED). A street, wall, shore or border can never lose a stretch to sliver repair; mergeFaces across a structural edge returns E_STRUCTURAL.

splitFace contact semantics (GEO-6): a cut is a polyline whose interior lies in the face open interior and which touches the face boundary exactly at its two endpoints, decided by exact orient2d on lattice points, never a parameter-space epsilon.

splitFace rule 1: each endpoint is a boundary vertex or a point on a boundary edge inserted by splitThrough; with attraction, an endpoint within attractCm of a boundary vertex lands on it, and so does an endpoint whose foot on a boundary edge lies within attractCm of that edge endpoint (step 2).

splitFace rule 2: any other contact is E_NOT_TWO_CROSSINGS: the cut passing through or within attractCm of a boundary vertex, grazing a reflex vertex, running within attractCm of a boundary edge anywhere but where it arrives at an endpoint, overlapping a boundary edge, or crossing the boundary more than twice. splitFace never lets attraction bend a cut into a pinch; the stage ladder picks another cut (§4.6).

splitFace rule 3: an antenna (a dangling chain inside the face - a cul-de-sac spine, a dead-end lane) counts as boundary: a cut may end on it (a declared T-junction, the natural end against a dead-end street) and may not cross it.

splitFace rule 4: a cut from the outer ring to a hole does not split the face; it is connectHole(face, cut), whose post-condition is the same face count and one hole fewer (the slit of §4.6); a violation is E_HOLE_CONTACT.

splitFace rule 5: the two children are returned in canonical order, the face left of the directed cut first, so an anchor lying exactly on the cut belongs to the left child (the tie-break of the anchor rule, §6.3).
splitFace rule 6: a face exported area boundary omits its antennae, so a GeoJSON ring never retraces a slit (§11).

Moves - warp and smoothing (GEO-10, GEO-35, GEO-5 (c)): warp(field, fromLevel, region) applies a displacement field to every vertex of level >= fromLevel inside the region. Shared boundaries are single vertices, so streets, blocks, plots and footprints under a brush move together; vertices of level < fromLevel stay fixed (a street warp does not move the coast unless fromLevel = 0). Smoothing committed geometry is a warp whose field the smoother computes (§3.4), under the same rules.

A move batch keeps nothing (J-K27): E_KEPT governs insertion and clearing only (§3.3); a move batch rederivesFrom is the first stage of §4.1 order (J-K33); what a move may not displace is decided by the held set, what it may not break by the whole-step validation.

Held vertices (GEO-5 (c)): before the step the kernel computes the HELD SET: (1) every vertex of the geometry a locked or pinned entity references resolve to (§7.2) - the level-n route vertices of every ring of its FaceRef faces (outer rings and holes), of its ChainRef and EdgeSetRef edges, its VertexRef vertices - and of every finer face nested in its faces (§7.2 makes every finer face under a locked or pinned entity a fixed input); (2) closed downwards by level: the two endpoints of every coarser edge carrying a held Steiner vertex are held, so that edge does not move and its held vertex keeps its place; each round adds endpoints of a strictly coarser level, so closure ends within four rounds. The field is zero at every held vertex and the dry run lists the held entities, so a locked plot, block or building keeps every corner although none carries a vertex role.

Kernel-pinned vertices under warp: gates, junctions, portals and the vertices smoothing, simplification and cutting keep move with everything else unless held, because a warp is the user explicit move and every entity names its vertices by role (§2.2 rule 5), so a moved gate is still its gate.

Deck and water-gate ends held: a bridge deck_end vertices and a water gate gate_end vertices are held unless fromLevel = 0, because the step that made the crossing fixed it across the water (§2.7): a deck perpendicular to the flow, a water gate wall edge bank to bank - whatever level its bank vertices have (L0 for a deck and an edited water gate; L1 Steiner vertices on the shores for one the trace made at generation, which would otherwise slide along the shore under a street warp and skew the gate edge, §2.2 rule 7; J-K35); with fromLevel = 0 the banks and the crossing move together.

Vertices on fixed routes slide (J-K18): a route is FIXED when its edge is of level < fromLevel or both its endpoints are held. A vertex of level >= fromLevel on a fixed route and not held (a street ending on a shore, a bridgehead, a riverside junction - level-1 Steiner vertices on L0 edges under §7.1 default fromLevel - a neighbour footprint corner on a locked plot line) moves only along that route: its displacement is projected onto the route direction at the vertex, the projected point kept at least attractCm from the route endpoints and from every held vertex on it, and the vertex is seated at the lattice point the placement rule chooses for that point ((i) within 0.71 cm of the route, (ii) >= minEdge from the route edge endpoints and its neighbours on the route, (iii) clearance), never the plain nearest lattice point, so the slid vertex keeps §3.10 placement bound and a slide beside a vertex 25.0-25.7 cm from the route commits. A brush over a quay road drags its junctions along the quay instead of halving to a no-op against the shore (fixture §13.1).

Re-seats (J-K17): each Steiner vertex on a moved coarser edge is re-seated at the lattice point the placement rule chooses for its projection onto the moved route, (i)-(iii) read on the moved geometry (two roundings stack here as on insertion); where no lattice point within attractCm of the projection qualifies, the step fails validation and halves. Measured (fixall_kernel_r3_checks.out A): over 200 000 re-seats beside a vertex 25.0-25.7 cm from the route, plain nearest rounding breaks minEdge or clearance in 12.9 % of cases and the placement rule in none, moving the vertex at most 4.3 cm along the route and keeping it within 0.71 cm; constructive case: a kerb warped to run (0,0)-(1 000,9) past a vertex at (517,30), 25.35 cm from it, with a plot-line end re-seated at that vertex foot - plain rounding lands 24.999 cm away and fails, the placement rule lands 25.999 cm away and the step commits.

Order within a step (J-K30): re-seats and slides read vertices that may be moving in the same step, so they are placed one at a time in canonical order by each vertex lattice position before the step (y, then x), each reading the vertices already placed at their placed points and every other moved vertex at its rounded target (a re-seat or slide rounded target = nearest lattice point to its projected point); the whole-step validation then checks the result. The order is a function of positions alone, never slots (§3.3). Measured (fixall_kernel_r4_checks.out B): for two Steiner vertices re-seated onto one warped route with projections 25.0-26.5 cm apart, the two possible orders place different points in 6.8 % of pairs.

The split flag under moves (J-K26): a step clears the split flag (§2.2 rule 3) (b) of every vertex it moves, EXCEPT a Steiner vertex re-seated onto its coarser edge route and a vertex sliding along a fixed route (both still lie on the route of the edge they split; dissolving either restores that edge exactly; a re-seated Steiner vertex keeps its flag so a later clearFiner dissolves it and the next derivation meets the clean coarser edge); and (b-prime) of every flagged vertex it does NOT move that is of the same level as a run it split (a same-level split foot or crossing, or a vertex promoted onto that run) when the nearest vertex of that level or coarser beside it along that run moves in the step (re-seat or slide included): the run line moved from under it. A Steiner vertex of a coarser run keeps its flag (re-seated with that run). So a warped same-level T-junction or crossing becomes a shape vertex of the warped chains, and removing the lane that ended there never straightens the warped spine. The commit record lists the (b-prime) vertices in unflagged; the edit undo record restores their flags (§3.3, §7.4).

Whole-step validation (GEO-10, GEO-35): each target is rounded to the lattice (re-seats and slides by the placement rule, in the order above) and the whole step is validated: every edge incident to a moved vertex (including edges between two moved vertices and edges at re-seated or sliding Steiner vertices) >= minEdge and tested against the index for crossings; every unmoved vertex tested against the triangles swept by the moved edges; no two vertices on one lattice point; no held vertex moved; the clearance invariant holds; and the edit layer recordCheck passes - every held point record inside its host face at its clearance (§7.4), every building whose footprint the step moves valid under §2.6 wing-carrying rule, decided by §2.6 rule 4 tiered test after the kernel own checks pass, stopping at the first failing building in address order.

Whole-step failure: the step strength is halved globally - deterministic, at most 8 halvings, after which the step is a reported no-op. The commit record lists every moved vertex (§3.3) and §3.10 minEdge row checks the new and moved edges it names, so a pinch or swirl that would shorten an edge to 10 cm, or stack two vertices on one lattice point, halves instead of committing.
Faces a committed move step leaves below a class floor are re-derived locally, each by its own batch whose rederivesFrom is the stage that makes that face, and logged.

The named brushes of §7.1 are displacement fields supplied by the edit layer (a moveVertex: §3.4); a whole-map rotation is a view transform, never a vertex operation, because it would re-snap every vertex in the arena.

One geometry engine on every host (GEO-9, DEF-2; J-K4): booleans, buffers, per-edge insets and bands are built on the kernel own arrangement - the machinery of insertChain on a scratch overlay - and no second geometry engine ships (one exception: the pre-decided M0 fallback).

Boolean algorithm: overlays both operands rings, labels every face with its winding numbers (a breadth-first walk from the unbounded face adding each crossed edge ring orientation), keeps the faces the operation and fill rule select (non-zero or even-odd, declared per call), and removes the edges separating two kept faces; an empty result is E_DEGENERATE with detail empty.

Buffer algorithm: the union of per-segment strips and per-vertex join discs: round joins as chords of at most 2 cm sagitta (about 27 chords per full circle at a 3 m radius), square ends where declared (gates, bridgeheads); where the half-width varies along a stored chain it is sampled from the chain knot profile at each segment two ends and the segment strip is the trapezoid between them (§2.2 rule 5).

Every engine output takes and returns integer coordinates and is produced by the same insertion rules as every other chain, so it obeys the same attraction, placement, minEdge and clearance (GEO-35) with no re-snap round trip, and on every host it is the same TypeScript code producing the same integers - no host can compute a different town.

The kerb, defined once (GEO-20): for an L1 face F, kerb(F) = F minus the union of buffer(spine_i, half-width_i) over F bounding spines, each half-width sampled from the width the spine linear entity declares - a way width profile (§2.4); on the underground layer a sewer tunnel corridor half-width = widthCm / 2 + wallCm (half its bore plus its wall; Tunnel.widthCm, II.7.2 profile row), and another system gallery = Gallery.widthCm / 2 + Gallery.wallCm (§2.7; defaults from its system row, II.7.6) - with round joins on the union convex side and square ends where declared; the union concave corners (block corners at junctions) are sharp by construction.

corridorUnion commits exactly the kerb geometry at L2: the kerb rings as kerb edges; the spine inside the band (already an L1 edge) splits it into two half-corridor strips; a corridor_split edge from each junction vertex to the kerb corner separates the junction wedge; on a side where the spine passes straight through a junction vertex (a T-junction whose street arrives from the other side) there is no kerb corner and no wedge: one corridor_split edge from the vertex to the foot of its perpendicular on that side kerb separates the half-corridor strips of the spine two sub-edges (§2.2 rule 1) - the edge II.1 (3) neighbour step inserts alone into a finished neighbour strip; the faces outside the band are the built blocks.

Kept faces inside a kerb: a finer face an earlier stage made inside F is kept (§3.3): it must lie wholly inside one resulting L2 face, and a kerb or corridor_split edge that would cross one or come within attractCm of it returns E_KEPT. The one-click order leaves none inside the faces S9 bands (a wall band, setback and glacis parts are built after S9 inside their own L1 strip faces, §4.7 S10 (0), §4.8), and a strip ends at the corridor of the way through each gate, so every gate passage stays open by construction.

kerb is also a read-only service on the faces of an open transaction overlay: S8 plans every cut on kerb(F) of the current L1 faces, inserts each accepted lane at L1 in its own district transaction and recurses on the children kerbs; S9 then commits corridorUnion for those L1 faces - the same function on the same inputs - so the block S8 cut and the block S9 keeps are one face (tested, §13.2). Because a way width is a knot profile, the T-junction S8 inserts into a crossed spine (§4.6 step 7) adds a vertex that carries no knot and changes no half-width, so both sides of that contract read the same widths.
corridorUnion takes a set of L1 faces and re-derives only those, which is also how an edit re-derives the corridors around a changed street.

Insets: the per-edge half-plane inset of the 2017 idea survives only as insetRing, for a uniform inset of a face whose convexity is checked exactly (E_NON_CONVEX otherwise; an inset larger than the inradius returns E_DEGENERATE with detail collapsed and the last non-empty distance); per-edge distances on any face use the buffer difference (offsetFace), so a concave, mixed-class face (the usual organic-growth face) has one correct construction, and a 2 deg kink between a 6 m and a 3 m half-width no longer lets the wider offset govern about 86 m of the narrow edge.

Wall bands, glacis, tower and gatehouse footprints use bandUnion with the band role: the wall chain (already an L1 edge) splits the band, so a band is a FaceRef of per-side L3 parts and never straddles its L1 edge.

The same functions on every arena (J-A12.31): kerb, corridorUnion and bandUnion take the arena from the transaction key (§3.3) and a chain from its (role, entity) row, so they run on the sewer network part of the underground layer (part 0, §3.4) on tunnel chains as on the ground way chains; a sky island arena needs nothing of its own (its ways are ways).

Sewer part bands: corridorUnion over part 0 L1 faces commits each tunnel band (its bore plus a wall each side) as its two half-corridor strips with a junction wedge at every tunnel junction, and the faces between bands as that part built blocks (level mapping §2.2 rule 1; which blocks are plotted and how deep, II.7.3); the band outer ring, the tunnel external wall, is the kerb edge every underground frontage plot lines end on (§4.7 S10 frontage-first cut on that kerb), so a plot stands flush against the wall by construction (item 12; frontage rule and invariants II.7.3 U1-U3 and §5.3).
owner_raw: kernel (plotting rules owned by II.7.3 / V04)

statement: One cut for every underground part (item 65; J-A65.32): on the other systems parts corridorUnion commits each gallery or walkway band from the half-width its Gallery record declares (as for a tunnel); faces between the bands are that part blocks (which are plotted: II.7.5, II.7.6, as II.7.3 decides for the sewer). A CHAMBER - a void wider than a band (a cavern hall, a quarry chamber, an undercity main chamber) - is a closed chain carrying the structural chamber_wall role (§2.2 rule 7), inserted by insertChain (closed) at the part L1 (§2.2 rule 1 underground mapping), so the chamber floor and the rock around it are separate L1 faces; its outline declares no half-width (as a shore), so its own edge is the kerb a plot on the floor may end on; a walkway across the floor is a gallery chain banded by corridorUnion; S9-S11 then cut the floor faces as a ground L1 face. A place where two parts meet is a record, never a band (§3.4). No arena-specific band operation exists.
owner_raw: kernel (systems owned by II.7.5-II.7.6 / V04 underground)

statement: Oracles, not fallbacks (J-K19): Clipper2 (compiled to WebAssembly, run in Node) and polygon-clipping are dev dependencies of @plat/testkit only; no product bundle loads either unless the M0 speed fallback fires. Because our engine attracts features closer than attractCm and the oracles do not, B-FUZZ splits every boolean and buffer case by what our engine reports.

B-FUZZ unattracted cases: the operation reports no W_ATTRACTED, W_STRETCH_SHARED, W_WEDGE_ROUTED or W_PLACED (nothing moved beyond the hot pixel): our result and each oracle must have equal face counts after both are snapped (zero-area faces dropped) and a symmetric-difference area of at most perimeter x 1 cm, the perimeter the summed boundary length of both operands.

B-FUZZ attracted cases (thin, near-collinear and near-touching inputs §13.1 random family and constructive set include): our result must pass every hard invariant of §3.10, and its symmetric difference from each oracle must be at most perimeter x sqrt(2) * attractCm (about 36.8 cm), the farthest any boundary point can move under attraction, placement or wedge routing (a wedge-routed tip sweeps at most half a minEdge per unit of arm length); face counts not compared (merging features closer than attractCm is the designed difference).

The harness draw count (keeping the strict comparison from being vacuous) is §13.1. There is no runtime fallback, so no host produces a different model hash and no fallback path needs a budget (SCL-22). The generation report names the engine that ran - the arrangement engine, plat-arrangement@<version> (§5.4); an engine change: §6.5 (7).

M0 (a) confirmation: (i) differential correctness on 10^6 fuzzed and constructive inputs per operation - 0 crashes, 0 invalid outputs, and the split oracle agreement; (ii) speed: S9 corridor bands over the CITY face set against §12.4 S9 row and one district <= 3 ms on reference hardware, and S11 geometry share against its §12.4 row on B-CITY-lite S11 workload. S11 geometry share = every kernel call S11 makes for one plot (base outline builder frontage-band intersection or OBB/LIR fit (§2.6, §4.7), per-edge setbacks by offsetFace, the yard partition splits and the footprint insertion into the block L4 batch) - the geometry part of S11 single §12.4 row, whose remainder is S11 rule evaluation (designation template, heights, materials, entrance), so this bar cannot pass while the stage misses its row. Criterion (i) has no fallback: a failure is a kernel bug fixed before M1.

M0 speed fallback: if (ii) fails after one optimisation pass, the shipped engine becomes Clipper2 compiled to WebAssembly as the only engine on every host: outputs still enter the arena through insertChain (attraction, placement, minEdge, clearance hold); WebAssembly becomes a stated requirement of the embed contract (§11); a host that cannot instantiate it receives §11.2 E_ENGINE_UNAVAILABLE - never a different town; the switch is a declared golden shift whose shift records name every stage reading a boolean, buffer, inset or band (S1 outline repair, S3 reservations, S8 kerbs, S9 corridors, S10 step (0) wall and margin bands, S11 footprints, S12b greenery faces). Clipper2 does not reproduce the arrangement engine integers, so §6.5 (10) cross-implementation byte-identity test applies to the WebAssembly accelerator only, and Clipper2 determinism check is §6.5 (9)-(10) cross-host digest identity.

No WASM kernel (DEF-13; J-K8): the kernel is TypeScript on every host. M0 (a) measures its per-op costs against §12.4 rows - insert + snap + attract + re-walk per growth proposal (S5), splitFace per bent cut (S8), and the band and S11 costs.

What an M0 per-op miss triggers, per hot loop after one optimisation pass: (a) miss by more than 2x: that loop only is compiled from the same integer algorithm into a WebAssembly accelerator behind the kernel facade; (b) miss by up to 2x: the measured cost is carried into its stage row of §12.4; if that pushes the row over budget the accelerator is built as above, otherwise the measured cost replaces the row figure as a declared budget amendment (recorded in §12.4 and the M0 record, critical path re-summed); (c) an accelerated loop that still misses, or a re-summed critical path above its rung p95 (§12.3), re-declares the model budget at the measured p95 as a D-18 amendment for the owner veto - the same path the fusion gate uses (§16).

The WebAssembly accelerator must pass §6.5 (10) cross-implementation test byte-identically on the golden suite (§16 M0 exit names this rule), and the TypeScript loop stays in every bundle, so a host without WebAssembly is slower and never different.

Skeleton decision (DEF-3; J-K5): built in-house (§3.1); it never writes an arena: roof ridges and hips are derived per building and cached by (entity, content revision, roof construction) - never by id alone (§8.1 (5), LC-23, N-19), so a setAttr on floors or a re-fitted footprint changes the revision and so the roof - and label spines are derived per face (§9). A stage wanting skeleton-derived topology inserts the validated arcs through insertChain like any chain. A skeleton failure can degrade a roof, a label or one stage partition, never the plat.

Skeleton reader roof: the roofs not taking the exact path (quad wings failing the convex near-rectangle test, irregular or notched outlines - institution shapes - and stage-3 irregular wings); downgrade: a PLAIN ROOF.

Skeleton reader spine: the hole-aware skeleton graph as a medial axis - label spines (§9.3), the local feature size S1 coast simplicity clamp reads (§4.2 S1), and each room label spine and light point when the plan rung draws a storey on the building band (§2.6, §8.5, §11.1; item 28) - the plan rung only skeleton use: it takes no wall from the skeleton, so a failure degrades a room label or light and never a room (J-A28.32); downgrade: a SAMPLED MEDIAL AXIS.
Skeleton reader regions: S10 per-frontage regions of a block (§4.7 S10 (4)); downgrade: the stage own exact construction, a REFLEX PRE-CUT PARTITION (§4.7, §5.2 F-PLOT).

Skeleton numeric contract (GEO-8): exact rational event times are impossible (edges move at unit speed, so event times involve lengths sqrt(dx^2 + dy^2)); event times computed in doubles with + - x / sqrt only (identical on every IEEE engine; no transcendental), on coordinates relative to the polygon bounding-box corner. Input is pre-cleaned (collinear merge, minimum angle 5 deg); holes supported. Events closer than 1 mm in offset time and 1 cm in position are coalesced into one multi-edge event; ties broken by the input vertex index in the ring, canonicalised to start at its lowest-leftmost vertex.
Skeleton work limit: 4 * (n + r) + 64 events for n vertices and r reflex vertices (a correct run needs at most about n + r); exceeding it is E_WORK_LIMIT, a count and never a timeout.

Convex near-rectangles take the exact path (J-K21): the CONVEX NEAR-RECTANGLE TEST - a footprint wing that is convex (every turn non-negative by exact orient2d on its lattice vertices), whose four OBB corners are each matched by a footprint vertex within 30 cm and whose area >= 0.97 of its OBB - gets its ridge or apex exactly, independent of sub-cm snapping, so a 1 cm edit cannot flip a micro-ridge (after snapping only 33 % of rotated squares keep a single apex, GEO-8).

Exact roof constructions: a hip roof ridge ends half the OBB minor extent in from each short side, its hips running from the four matched vertices to the ridge ends; a gable roof ridge lies on the wing ridgeAxis line (§2.6: for a rect, the OBB axis parallel to the side it names; for a quad, the line joining the arc-length midpoints of the two side chains it names, sides delimited by BaseWing.corners) and ends where that line meets the footprint boundary; a pyramid apex is the OBB centre. Every roof line lies inside the footprint (endpoints do; hip ridge end or apex at least half the OBB minor extent inside the OBB, far more than the <= 30 cm a convex footprint matching all four corners can fall short; a segment between two points of a convex polygon lies inside it), so VIS-11 crossing hip lines cannot occur.
owner_raw: kernel (roof kinds owned by §2.6 / V02 buildings)

statement: Convexity is what makes the exact path true: a 20 x 10 m rectangle with a 3 x 2 m notch at x = 1-4 m on a long side (area 0.970 of its OBB, all four corners present) has a reflex vertex and so takes the skeleton (fixall_kernel_r2_attract.out D).

Roofs are taken wing by wing, by BaseWing.kind (§2.6): rect wings (base outline builder rectangles and L/T compositions) are convex, so most roofs take the exact path; a quad wing (a row house cut to a curved frontage) takes it when it passes the test and the validated skeleton otherwise - no path asserts a party-wall side is straight, so a quad whose bent side (the lot cut one bend) fails the test takes the skeleton; polygon wings keep the pyramid, cone and dome constructions.

Skeleton post-condition validator: every result checked before any use: (1) planarity - no two arcs cross (exact orient2d on nodes rounded to the millimetre in bounding-box-relative integers); (2) exactly one skeleton face per input edge, monotone along that edge direction; (3) heights consistent - each node offset time equals its distance to the supporting lines of its faces within 1 cm, and times increase along every arc away from the boundary; (4) the graph is connected with exactly h independent cycles for h holes (a tree only with no holes).

A validator failure, or E_WORK_LIMIT, takes the reader downgrade, reported W_DOWNGRADE: a plain roof is the footprint drawn and exported without ridge or hip lines, its heights unchanged (MFCG own behaviour when its gable pass fails); a sampled medial axis is a Voronoi of boundary samples at 1 m via d3-delaunay, pruned by clearance. Never a crash, never a roof line outside its footprint, never unvalidated output.

Skeleton M0 (a) confirmation: runs §13.1 skeleton fixtures and the B-CITY-lite corpus of irregular footprints and district and water faces. Pass: 0 crashes; 0 validator failures on the fixtures; downgrades <= 0.5 % and work-limit hits <= 0.1 % on the corpus; <= 20 us median per footprint.

Skeleton pre-decided fallback: if the corpus bar fails after one repair pass, the downgrades become the default paths - convex near-rectangular wings keep exact OBB roofs, every other roof is plain, every spine reader takes the sampled medial axis and S10 the reflex pre-cut partition - and the skeleton leaves the product (kept in the testkit for comparison); nothing else changes, because the readers are the only readers of skeleton output.

Geometry in the document (SCL-11, kernel part): the snapshot geometry (§2.9) is one block per PlatKey, never one per level; a boundary seen by several levels (a kerb, a plot line, a shore) is written once.

Snapshot vertices: live vertices in slot order (slots compacted on save; nothing outside the kernel stores a slot and no output depends on slot numbers, §3.3, so renumbering is free), coordinates as delta + zig-zag varint Int32 pairs, with their current birth levels (after any promotion or demotion, §2.2 rule 3) and flags.
Snapshot edges: one (origin, destination, birth level) triple per edge pair, the level being the current one (the lowest among the edge rows, §2.2 rule 3); next, prev and twins not stored.

Snapshot roles: (edge or vertex, role, entity, level, ordinal) rows, entities as document ids - the rows of every role §2.2 rule 7 registry marks indexed, the knot roles among them, included (an edit anchor contact names never reach a snapshot: the batch that promotes them strips them, §3.3 rule 3), so every entity-held vertex and every chain profile survives the round trip without a stored position (§2.2 rule 5).

Snapshot faces: per level, one (boundary half-edge, owner, kind, stage rank) row per face; parents not stored. The stage rank is persisted because the kept-content rule (§3.3) must decide the same way after a reload as in the session that made the face.

No per-level digest is stored (§2.9 step 3). The ordinal and stage-rank columns - 2 bytes per role row, 1 byte per face - are about 0.45 MB raw at CITY, almost all zero ordinals and a handful of repeated ranks that the document compression removes; §2.9 document-size test measures the result at M1.

Chunks: the block is written as content-addressed chunks (§2.9). Per arena the LEVEL-<=1 ROUTES are one chunk: every vertex of birth level <= 1 and every L0-L1 edge as one (origin, destination, birth level) triple between its level-<=1 endpoints, with its roles of level <= 1 and the L0-L1 face rows (no finer Steiner vertex part of it). Each static-index partition (§3.3) is one chunk holding the vertices belonging to it by §3.3 rebuild rule, its edges of level >= 2 (every district boundary is an L1 edge, §2.2 rule 1, so each lies in one partition), the STEINER SPLITS its batches made on L0-L1 edges (each as the coarser edge route endpoints and the split vertex, by lattice point, with the split vertex level), the finer roles those batches added to the coarser edges sub-edges, and its face rows of level >= 2.

Cross-chunk references: every reference to a vertex another chunk holds is its lattice point, never (chunk, index): a vertex is unique per lattice point in its arena (§3.10); a vertex on an L1 edge two partitions share (the foot of a wall- or margin-band cross edge, §4.7) is written in the chunk of the partition with the smaller key and named by its lattice point from the other.

Chunk load order: the kernel inserts the level-<=1 routes, then each partition chunk in partition-key order - its splits first, sorted along each coarser edge by position, then its vertices and edges - resolving lattice-point references through the one-vertex-per-lattice-point index; the rebuild then yields the same arena and per-level digests (they read routes, not slots), and save -> load -> save holds chunk by chunk.

Chunk rewrite locality: an edit that renumbers one partition vertices rewrites that partition chunk alone (an item whose partition changes, §3.3, rewrites both chunks); the level-<=1 chunk only when it changes a level-<=1 route, promotes a vertex into one, or demotes a vertex or edge out of one; and when it changes a level-<=1 route edge, also every partition chunk holding a Steiner split on that edge, because each split names its route edge by the edge endpoints (J-DET-36) - the partitions whose faces border the edge, which an edit changing a coarse route (a carve or water edit footprint, a seam amendment two districts) mostly re-derives anyway, and which §2.9 rebased-size test at M2a counts, with §2.9 block-group fallback pre-decided.

Load: the kernel rebuilds next/prev by sorting each vertex outgoing edges by exact angle (quadrant, then orient2d), re-walks faces level by level, recovers each face parent from its boundary edges and rebuilds the role reverse index and the static index partitions: O(E log d), deterministic. The per-level digests are recomputed from the rebuilt arena within the load digest check (§2.9 steps 2-3).

Pre-decided fallback for §2.9 open-to-editable bar: each L2-L4 static index partition is rebuilt at the first query that reads it instead of at load - output-neutral, because every query result is sorted by its canonical key whichever structure holds an item (§3.3).
Entities carry no slots (§2.2 rule 5), so the entity table needs no remapping on load. The round-trip test is §13.1; the compact twin carries the same block (§11.1).
Invariant - lattice and range: every coordinate is a lattice point inside the range invariant. Class: hard. Checked: at snap. How: by construction (§3.2 (7)).

Invariant - minEdge: no edge shorter than minEdge, whichever writer made or moved it (insertion, boolean, buffer, offset, smoothing, warp). Class: hard. Checked: batch-local. How: the commit record new edges and moved edges - every edge incident to a vertex in its moved list, Steiner re-seats and slides included (§3.3, §3.6).

Invariant - clearance: every vertex lies at least minEdge from every edge outside its one-ring (edges incident to it or its neighbours); acute corners inside the one-ring governed by minFaceAngle and the class floors. Class: hard. Checked: batch-local. How: new, placed and moved vertices and their incident edges against the index.

Invariant - one vertex per lattice point: no two vertices share a lattice point. Class: hard. Checked: batch-local. How: by construction for insertions (coincidence is attraction); the moved vertices against the index for a warp or smoothing step.
Invariant - simplicity: faces simple except declared antennae; no two edges cross. Class: hard. Checked: batch-local. How: touched faces.

Invariant - nesting: every face of level n+1 has exactly one parent at level n, and each of its boundary edges is of level n+1 or a sub-edge of a level-<=n edge. Class: hard. Checked: batch-local. How: touched faces and re-parented kept faces, by index - never by coordinates.

Invariant - placement bound: every vertex a batch places, re-seats or slides onto a coarser edge lies within 0.71 cm of that edge route at the edge own level when placed (a later same-level change moves no finer vertex, §3.6); on a transient arena every vertex placed on a fixed edge lies within 0.71 cm of the line of each input side the edge lies on - its route, which no split changes and no writer there moves, so the bound stands for the arena life (§3.4). Class: hard. Checked: batch-local. How: the placed, re-seated and sliding vertices.

Invariant - level consistency: every edge birth level is the lowest level among its role rows; no vertex is coarser than every edge and vertex role at it; a vertex finer than an incident edge lies inside that edge run - its incident edges coarser than it are exactly two, of one level, with identical rows of that level (§2.2 rule 3). Class: hard. Checked: batch-local. How: the commit record new, changed, demoted and removed edges and the vertices at them, and its promoted and demoted vertices.
Invariant - held vertices: no vertex of a warp or smoothing step held set moved (§3.6). Class: hard. Checked: batch-local. How: the commit record moved list against the held set.

Invariant - prepared contacts: a clear-region batch met finer geometry only at its KernelTx.prepared vertices, promoted exactly those, stripped their anchor contact names, and shared no finer edge (§3.3, §3.6). Class: hard. Checked: batch-local. How: the commit record promoted list against the resolved prepared set, and its new edges birth levels.

Invariant - kept content: no finer face made by a stage before the batch rederivesFrom - nor, in a clear-region batch, any finer face outside the region - was cleared, crossed, split or re-owned (moves keep nothing, §3.6). Class: hard. Checked: batch-local. How: the stage ranks and region test of the commit record removed and changed finer faces (§3.3).

Invariant - role consistency: every role the registry declares linear (way, wall, shore, tunnel ...) forms, per entity, the connected simple chains or rings the entity declares; no structural role is lost by an absorption or merge. Class: hard. Checked: batch-local. How: the commit record role keys.

Invariant - stored references resolve: each FaceRef, ChainRef, EdgeSetRef, VertexRef held by a live entity finds geometry; every indexed role of §2.2 rule 7 registry other than a knot role finds exactly one vertex or edge set per ordinal (a link two link_end ordinals each in the part its end names, §3.4); every ChainProfile knots lie on its chain in ordinal order with at least one knot per ring; no geometry carries a dead entity. Class: hard. Checked: stage end, save. How: the reverse indexes.

Invariant - frozen base complete: at every pool freeze, after the freeze rebuilt each static partition whose grid or tombstone set was not empty (§3.3 pool step 1), every level dynamic grid and every partition tombstone set is empty - every item lives in a static partition the copy carries. Class: hard. Checked: at the freeze, at every pool size. How: two counts per level, O(levels), after the rebuild.

Invariant - index levels and freshness: a batch wrote no index of a level coarser than its own, except the promotions and demotions it made, and left no static item of what it deleted, re-levelled, changed or moved to another partition unfiltered - each tombstoned in the partition its home entry named and its successor in the grid of its current level (§3.3). Class: hard. Checked: batch-local. How: the commit record index writes against its level and its promoted and demoted lists; each deleted, re-levelled, changed or re-partitioned item that had a static copy found in the tombstone set of the partition that held it (in a pool worker, the overlay set for that partition).

Invariant - pool scope: no district overlay wrote outside its district scope; no two overlays, and no concurrent eager write, touched one base record. Class: hard. Checked: at the pool merge. How: the overlays copied-record lists against each other and against the live arena changes since the freeze (§3.3).

Invariant - arena isolation: a batch wrote only the arena its key names, and no vertex, edge or face of one arena references a slot of another - the arenas (the ground, each underground part, each sky island) share no topology and every cross-arena link is an entity id, a link between two underground parts included (§2.2 rule 2; services read any arena by key, §3.4). Class: hard. Checked: by construction; debug-build assertion. How: each slot passed to an op or service checked in a debug build against the key and version it was stamped with (§3.4); the multi-arena stages property tests, the underground reroll-isolation fixture and its per-part twin among them (§13.2).

Invariant - seed tiling on a transient arena: the union of its faces equals the union of its seed rings as inserted, and every fixed edge (a seed ring or fixed ring, §3.4) survives every batch, so the rooms of each storey tile exactly the seed rings §2.6 passes - at and above ground, the extents of the wings reaching the storey (a wing ring, or above ground its ring union the span ring of the passage it spans), clipped to tile, plus on the ground storey every spanned passage span ring; below ground, the basement ring (§2.6 plan rung steps 4 and 6) - with every outer wall on a seed-ring side, whether cut once or re-cut under §2.6 interior ladder (item 28 and 28 (f)); a stored plan carried rooms tile its storeys carried seed rings the same way. Class: hard. Checked: at the open; batch-local; at readBack; at a stored plan carry. How: at the open, §3.4 overlap test (no two input sides cross, no face inside two seed rings, each fixed ring one face inside one seed ring and no other fixed ring); the commit record removed edges against the fixed edges (none); at readBack, area2 summed over faces against area2 summed over the seed rings as inserted, and every face ring inside one seed ring by orient2d; for a stored plan carried rooms (§2.6 carry check (4), §5.3), a transient arena opened with the carried shell seed rings, formed as the plan rung forms them, and that storey rooms as fixed rings, as §2.6 carries them: the §3.4 overlap test, then the faces area2 sum equal to the fixed rings (no face outside a room), the arena then released.
Invariant - face corners >= minFaceAngle. Class: soft for mandatory chains (W_ACUTE_CORNER), hard for optional chains. Checked: batch-local. How: touched corners.
Invariant - Euler characteristic per level: V - E + F = 1 + components. Class: hard. Checked: CI (B-FUZZ, B-EDIT). How: whole arena.

The §3.10 rows are the kernel part of the §5.3 invariant suite. Batch-local checks read only the commit record faces, its moved, promoted and demoted vertices, its changed and demoted edges and their one-ring, so a batch costs O(touched), never O(model) (SCL-1); whole-arena checks run at stage end, at save or in CI; the freeze check runs once per freeze and the pool check once per merge in O(overlay size). Class floors are the stages invariants, stated as §3.2 (2) says (GEO-35).

Nesting admits no exception (J-A30.31): a passage under a building wing (item 30) is an L3 face of kind passage in one parent (§2.5 Passage, cut by S10 along one side line of the front plot, §4.6, §4.7 S10 (9), by splitFace or claimSubFace as any alley face); the wing overhead is a composition ring (§2.6), never a plat face, so no footprint straddles it and no level is crossed; the rear plots it serves carry their access rows on the edges they share with it, and §5.3 reachability walk crosses passage, alley and court faces through faceNeighbours (§3.4). A passage is never an L1 way (its L2 corridor would cut the footprint above and split the block; S10 never writes L1, §4.1).
owner_raw: kernel (Passage record §2.5; plot model §4.7 / V01, V02)

statement: A sealed passage (item 30 (e)) keeps its face and its edges; the seal is Passage.sealed, the one bit of the passage record (§2.5), from which the sealed access edges and the plots exposure sealed are read (§4.6); its geometry is unchanged.
A building rooms (item 28) are never plat faces: they are cut on a transient arena (§3.4), so no clicked building plan enters an arena, an index partition or the model digest.
Defined term lattice point: the integer-cm world grid point; every persisted coordinate is one.
Defined term hot pixel: the 0.71 cm (sqrt(2)/2 cm) tolerance square a lattice-placed point may deviate from an exact line; also the padding of route-edge boxes.
Defined term range invariant: |x|, |y| < 2^23 cm.
Defined term minimum edge: 25 cm minimum edge length.
Defined term attraction distance: 26 cm.
Defined term minimum face angle: 5 deg = 500 centidegrees.
Defined term class floors: per-class minimum width, area and angle of faces from the stage tables.
Defined term transaction: an atomic batch of kernel ops at one level.
Defined term birth level: the level an item currently belongs to (lowered by promotion, raised by demotion).
Defined term kept content: finer faces made by a stage ranked before rederivesFrom (or, in a clear-region batch, finer faces outside the region); obstacles never cleared or re-owned.
Defined term clear region: the footprint of a coarse insertion into finished fabric, shared by a declared sequence of single-level batches.
Defined term prepared contact: a vertex a preparation batch placed where a coarse chain will meet finer geometry.
Defined term contact name: an anchor vertex role row placed by splitThrough without an ordinal, stripped by the coarse batch.
Defined term commit record: per-batch result listing the dirty set and moved/promoted/demoted/unflagged items.
Defined term declared form: op set applied in canonical order.
Defined term callback form: ops issued by fn and applied in issue order.
Defined term canonical order: stable key sort (op kind rank, lineage key, op index) for ops; canonical item key (y, x) for query results.
Defined term overlay: a copy-on-write layer over an arena.
idents: one overlay of all the rings (boolean arrangement, seed clip)

statement: Defined term frozen base: the read-only arena copy sent to pool workers at the freeze.
Defined term scope (district): faces, edges and vertices a pool overlay may write.
Defined term static partition: flatbush packed index partition with tombstone set.
Defined term dynamic grid: per-level uniform grid index with O(1) insert/delete.
Defined term tombstone: item key (kind * 2^32 + slot) filtered from a static partition.
Defined term home column: per-slot partition number (Plat.indexHome).
Defined term route edge: a maximal run of a level sub-edges between vertices of that level or coarser; one index item.
Defined term Steiner vertex: a finer vertex placed on a coarser edge.
idents: finer vertex on a coarser edge

statement: Defined term promotion / demotion: lowering / raising a vertex or edge birth level (§2.2 rule 3).
Defined term split flag: flag on a vertex that split a run; cleared by promotion or moves (J-K26).

Defined term kernel pinned flag vs held vs opts.pinned: three distinct notions: kernel pinned flag (set only by pinVertices; kept by smoothing, simplification, cutting; not by warp); held vertex (warp field zero: locked/pinned entity geometry, deck and gate ends); opts.pinned (chain indices exempt from decimation).
Defined term stretch: part of a chain between two of its vertices.
Defined term knot / profile: ChainProfile knots carrying a varying width along a chain.
Defined term arena: one planar subdivision (a plat or a transient arena).
Defined term transient arena parts: seed rings, fixed rings, fixed edges, input sides, joints, seed clip.
Defined term chain class: mandatory (never fails for precision) or optional.
Defined term antenna: a dangling chain inside a face.
Defined term slide / re-seat: placement-rule seating of a vertex moving along a fixed route / a Steiner vertex on a moved coarser edge.
Defined term whole-step validation: validation of a whole warp step with global halving.
Defined term sliver / residue: a face below its class floor; kept as residue when bounded by structural edges.
Defined term kerb: F minus the union of spine buffers; also the kerb edge role.
Defined term corridor parts: half-corridor strip, junction wedge, built block, corridor_split edge, band.
Defined term chamber: a closed chamber_wall chain enclosing a void wider than a band.
Defined term oracle: Clipper2 / polygon-clipping used only for CI comparison.
Defined term accelerator: a WebAssembly compilation of one hot loop behind the kernel facade.
Defined term arrangement engine: the kernel own boolean/buffer engine.
Defined term skeleton uses and downgrades: roof/spine/regions and their downgrades plain roof / sampled medial axis / reflex pre-cut partition.
Defined term convex near-rectangle test: convex, four OBB corners matched within 30 cm, area >= 0.97 of OBB.
Defined term snapshot block and chunks: one geometry block per PlatKey written as content-addressed chunks.
Defined term frame: the map rectangle; arena = frame + margin.
Defined term work limit: operation-count budget per transaction.
Defined term placement rule: lattice-point choice for vertices placed on existing edges ((i)-(iii)).
Defined term attraction: moving new geometry onto existing geometry within attractCm.

The plat is the single spatial truth: every area (sea, river, district, block, plot, yard, footprint) is a face and every line (street, alley, wall, shore, plot line) an edge, in integer centimetres, refined in five coarse-to-fine levels so a change at one level touches only what lies under it. Plain-words restatement of §2.2.
Every record carries provenance (which rule, which random stream) and a lifecycle history (generated, edited, pinned, built, converted, demolished). Plain-words restatement of §2.8.
Three model layers exist from the start (underground, ground, sky), so the owner-staged sewers and floating islands need no change of the model.
Every model length is an integer number of centimetres (i32); world centred on (0,0), +x east, +y north (as FTG, _critic-ftg.md F1), inside the arena frame of §3.2 (9).
Twice-areas and ring orientation are §3.2 (6)'s exact integer predicates; directions are §3.2 (5)'s (reference, not restated).
Heights are centimetres; angles, where stored, are i32 centidegrees, named ...Cdeg or typed Cdeg (§2.8 type list).
A length field carries its unit either in its name (...Cm, ...M) or in a unit-branded type (Cm, M, CmArray, ChainProfile of Cm); a schema lint refuses any length field with neither (O6 (a), G-R14).

layer ∈ {underground, ground, sky} is a field on every geometric entity and every display-list item, with z: i32 (order inside the layer) and elevationCm: i32 (base elevation: an island's altitude; a sewer's negative depth).
Each layer has its own arena or its own parts (G-R11): the ground; one per underground system (the sewer network's is part 0; item 65); one per sky island; keyed by PlatKey (§2.2 rule 2).
Per-layer toggles, shadows and export hang off the one layer field; a layer's drawing and export settings are its LayerSpec (§8.4), edited by setLayer (§7.1).
The base populates only the ground layer; underground and sky are schema-complete and empty until their staged stages run.

Layer (unqualified) means one of the three model layers; the toggleable drawing groups of §8-§9 (labels, cadastral outlines, trees, annotations, thematic style overrides) are display-list groups selected by `semantic`, never a fourth model layer.

Address id `kind:token`, prefixed with its arena outside the ground layer (sky2/plot:..., under/tunnel:..., under3/chamber:...): underground part 0 keeps under/, a further underground part n takes under<n>/, a sky island's part n takes sky<n>/. Edits, locks, assignments, pins, labels, households, exports and hosts point at it.
The lineage key (keying random streams), the anchor rule with its hysteresis radii, survival and succession, the JOIN rule and the one collision rule are §6.3's (LC-1, LC-29, GEO-34) — referenced.
In memory addresses are interned u32 handles, held by the kernel's owner and role tables; in the document they are strings.
The parent is a field (Identity.parent, §2.8), never parsed from the id; no record outside the kernel stores an arena slot (§2.2 rule 5).

The underground layer holds a family of systems, each in its own arena part (PlatKey; J-A65.31): part 0 = the sewer network's tunnels and, along its navigable runs, the underground neighbourhoods' blocks, plots and buildings (II.7.3); each further part = one system of II.7.6 (catacombs, caverns, quarries and mine voids, vaults, buried old town, or dug private passages) as an UndergroundSystem record with galleries, chambers and links (§2.7); the undercity's neighbourhoods in the part of the void they occupy (II.7.5).
An underground part number is allocated once and never reused (Document.nextUndergroundPart, §2.9).

Underground records live on under/ and under<n>/ prefixes and are populated only when the owner-staged network and underground stages run, or, for a dug system, when an access edit or an undercity lifeline's closure makes one once those stages exist (§7.3 item 9 (d), II.7.4; item 66).
Underground level mapping is §2.2 rule 1's; depth is elevationCm (negative below the ground datum, II.7.3, II.7.6).

Whether a layer exists is decided by what the model holds, never by a layer's visibility (item 14): Features.sewers for the network at a rung and Features.underground for the layer as a whole (§2.9, II.7.4).
Cm = integer centimetres (number); a number becomes an arena coordinate only through snap() (§3.2 (7)), in every build.
Level = 0|1|2|3|4: L0 land/water; L1 way skeleton; L2 kerbs, corridors, blocks; L3 plots + residue; L4 footprints + yard parts.

PlatKey = { layer, part }: part 0 = the ground, or the underground layer's sewer network; underground parts >= 1 = one arena per further system (catacombs, caverns, quarries and mine voids, vaults, buried old town, dug passages — II.7.6), each number allocated once at creation and never reused (§3.4; counter nextUndergroundPart §2.9); sky parts 1-3 = one arena per sky island (§4.2, II.1).
VertexId, HalfEdgeId, FaceId = arena slots: kernel-internal, valid within one batch (rule 5).
Plat { key; frame; lattice; vertices; halfEdges; roles; faces[5]; index[5]; indexHome; version } — the per-arena planar structure.
Plat.frame is set at creation and replaced only by the frame growth of an epoch's upward rung crossing (§3.2 (9), §4.11; J-A81.41), which only grows it.

Plat.lattice is fixed for the arena's life; §3.2 (1)'s range bound is taken at the population cap and the extreme aspect so a grown frame keeps every old lattice point. LatticeSpec { unitCm 1; minEdgeCm 25; attractCm 26; minFaceAngleCdeg 500; rangeCm 8,388,608 (2^23) } — meaning in §3.2 (2), classes in §3.10.
vertices: x, y (Int32Array), out (one outgoing half-edge), level (Uint8: birth level; lowered by promotion, raised by demotion — rule 3), flags (Uint8: pinned | steiner | split | free slot).

Vertex flag `pinned` is set only by pinVertices (§3.4) and cleared when a batch strips the vertex's last vertex role row other than knot rows (rule 3 (b)); `split` is rule 3's, its clearing under moves is §3.6's.
halfEdges: origin, next, prev (Int32Array); twin(h) = h ^ 1 (allocated in pairs); level per pair (h >> 1) = the edge's birth level, always the lowest level among its role rows (rule 3).
roles: RoleTable — (role, entity, level, ordinal) sets on edge pairs and vertices, with a reverse index (rule 7).

faces: one LevelFaces per level; index: one LevelIndex per level (§3.3); indexHome: per slot the static index partition (numbered across the levels) whose build holds it, -1 if none, written by every build, read to tombstone (§3.3); version: bumped by every committed batch.

LevelFaces { outer; holesStart; holes; kind (Uint16); owner (interned entity handle); parent (level-1 face containing it; -1 at L0); stage (Uint8: rank in §4.1 order of the stage whose batch created or last re-owned the face — the kept-content rule, §3.3); nextOfOwner; ownerHead: OwnerTable }.

RoleTable { edgeFirst; vertexFirst (first slot of each set, -1 if none); kind (Uint16 interned RoleName); entity; level (batch level that added it); ordinal (Uint16; 0 unless registry declares role indexed, rule 7); nextInSet; nextSameKey; head: RoleHeadTable }.

RoleHeadTable and OwnerTable are typed-array hash tables (J-K22): open addressing, linear probing, capacity a power of two kept at load <= 0.5 (doubled and re-inserted in slot order when exceeded), fixed integer hash of the key words, deletion by backward shift (no tombstones); lookups only — nothing iterates a table — so its layout never reaches an output.
RoleHeadTable { k0 entity handle; k1 = role << 16 | ordinal; first (first role-row slot, -1 empty); count }; OwnerTable { owner (interned handle); head (first FaceId, -1 empty); count }.

LevelIndex { static: PackedIndex[] (one per arena at L0-L1; one per district plus one outside districts at L2-L4); dynamic: UniformGrid; tombstones: Set per static partition of keys (kind * 2^32 + slot; kind = vertex, route edge or face) tombstoned since its build, filtering that partition's hits only; when a set empties is §3.3's }.

RoleRow = { role; entity; ordinal? } — a row a writer adds; its level is always the adding batch's (rules 3, 7); an `anchor` contact name is given without ordinal, the kernel allocates it (§3.3 rule 2). RoleKey = { role; entity; ordinal } — a row's identity without level.

Geometry references (the only forms by which an entity, seam contract, edit event or API scope refers to geometry, rule 5): FaceRef {owner, level} = faces whose owner at that level is the entity; ChainRef {role, entity} = ordered edge chain carrying (role, entity) (way spine, wall trace, tunnel); EdgeSetRef {role, entity, ordinal?} = unordered edges (frontage, access, party walls, one gate opening); VertexRef {role, entity, ordinal?} = the vertex (junction, tower, gate, entrance, portal, deck end, water gate's bank end, weld end); StretchRef {chain, from, to: VertexRef|LatticePoint} = chain edges between two vertices, batch-local, never stored in an entity record.
LatticePoint = { x: Cm; y: Cm } — a position in an arena; which records may hold a vertex's position is rule 5's.
VertexSig { v: the vertex's own (role, entity, ordinal) rows sorted; e: the structural (role, entity) rows of its incident edges sorted, deduplicated }.

ChainProfile<T number|string> { knotRole (registry knot role: width_knot, base_knot, invert_knot, bank_knot, shore_class_knot ...); values[i] belongs to the chain vertex carrying (knotRole, entity, i): an authored value in the attribute's unit or a cut knot's exact sample; interp 'linear'|'step' } — never an array indexed by chain vertices.
Rule 1: everything with a boundary is a face; everything linear is an edge chain.
L0 faces are land and water only: land components, sea, lakes, river reaches, islets, ponds, moats.
Terrain contours and drainage lines are raster products (§2.3), never plat edges or faces, so no L1 face straddles two L0 parents and no drainage antenna enters a face ring.

The arena's outer ring (frame plus context margin, §3.2 (9)) is one L0 chain carrying the structural `margin` role on the arena's Terrain entity, written first by S1 before any water, so every L0 face has a boundary; a sea or river reaching it shares its stretch (§4.1).

L1 faces: coarse blocks (regions between way spines) and the wall strips S7 cuts beside each trace (§4.8). L1 edges: way spines (centrelines), wall lines, the wall strips' setback and glacis lines (role `setback`), shorelines inherited from L0, the map border, the settlement perimeter (a district_bound chain, §4.5) and district boundaries.
The map border is the frame rectangle, role `border` on the arena's Terrain entity, written first by S3's L1 batch after S3's L0 batch (§4.1).
District boundaries are always L1 edges — a spine, a wall line, a reservation boundary, a shore or the perimeter — so every finer face lies inside one district.

L2 refines each L1 face into one half-corridor strip along each spine edge (road reserve on that side, width = the way's half-width), one junction wedge at each corner and the remaining built block(s), built by corridorUnion (§3.7), so every L2 face nests in exactly one L1 face.

A Corridor entity is the FaceRef of the half-corridor faces on both sides of its spine; a Junction is the FaceRef of the wedges around its vertex; a Square is a corridor face of class `square` (G-R11).
