A site becomes a bridge only when a way uses it (as FTG turns only crossing road proposals into bridges gated by 40 m; MFCG one bridge per street crossing, 1–4 per city): the way S4 or S5 routes through the two vertices lays the span (its own L1 edge between them carrying structural deck role beside way); the Bridge becomes built with that way; S7 builds its furniture (§2.7, §4.8); no L0 edge crosses the water, no deck splits a reach's L0 face, every bridge has one structure (§2.2 rule 7; J-I12); S4 routes to a site's ends as a fixed graph edge (§4.3), so "bridges within ±10° of the channel normal" holds by construction

A site no way uses by the end of S5 stays a site: two pinned bank vertices and a record — no span, way or furniture; not drawn, named, labelled or exported (S13a names a bridge once built; renderers and exports draw deck spans only); outside §5.3's deck rows; an epoch's growth (§4.4, §4.11), a drawn bridge (§7.4) and F-ROUTE's move rung (§4.3) may use it later

A deck where no site stands, on standing water — F-ROUTE's extra-bridge rung (§5.2) in S4 at generation (after S1 and S3 committed every shore), in S5b at k ≥ 2 and in every epoch (§4.4), or in S4's operator in an edit moving no water; or a drawn bridge with no site within crossing.snapM (20 m, half the minimum spacing) of where it crosses the channel centreline — is placed by one L0 batch of two same-level shore splits before the way's L1 batch: splitThrough at L0 on each shore at the deck's bank point, perpendicular to local flow, carrying the deck_end row of a fresh Bridge (over: 'added'), pinned; a street end already within attractCm of that point (vertex carrying a way row) is attracted and promoted (§3.6); any other bank point keeps attractCm from every vertex on the shore's route, map border crossing included; nothing cleared; finer faces whose rings run along the shore gain the vertex (§3.3 same-level-split); the way's L1 batch then lays its span through the two vertices

A deck placed before its water exists is built by the batches of the operator that inserts the water (a carve's kept way §4.11; an outer moat's arterial via S5a's carve path §4.4; a kept way of S1's water operator §7.3 (b) 3; and a deck F-ROUTE's extra-bridge rung sites inside one of these); inside such an operator the rung only sites the deck, as data, with the operator's other crossings (§7.3 (b) 2): its two deck_end vertices placed on the way's new route at the new bank points under a fresh Bridge by the operator's L1 batch (§7.3 (b) 3; §4.11 batch (1)) and promoted to L0 by its L0 batch when the water is inserted through them (§3.3; §7.3 (b) 4; §4.11 batch (2)); no shore split runs
S1 (6) Harbour candidates: coast faces with depth ≥ threshold

S1 (7) Bank classes (COV-FTG-H06): every shore segment classed bay/headland/straight (WaterBody.shoreClass, §2.3) by signed curvature of the shoreline smoothed over 200 m (thresholds in a table); bank kind beach/rock/cliff/quay/marsh drawn from a per-class weight table (our own weights) conditioned on slope and exposure (G-R5) so bays tend to beaches and headlands to rock and cliff; class kept per segment for §8's shore decoration
S1 (8) Water faces enter L0 with shore/bank edges; land components by flood fill (MFCG's land-component build), every one given uses later (O14 g)

Shore setback (COV-FTG-H07): table shoreSetback per bank kind — plots: beach 6 m, marsh 10 m, rock 3 m, cliff 5 m from the edge, quay 0 m (quay plots front the quay way); fields 10 m — read by S10 and the hinterland unit (§4.9); the band is typed shore greenery or commons
S1 (9) Drainage stays queryable

S1 (10) Resources (COV-FTG-B09): SiteResources rasters on the terrain grid — stone from slope, rock class and cliffs; ore from relief × fBm propensity (hills only); timber from forest propensity (slope and soil class; realised as woods by the hinterland unit §4.9); fish from water adjacency and reach width; clay from low damp river flats; fertile land from gentle, dry, non-rock ground; S0 landscape toggles clamp a kind to zero or raise its floor; S2's resource gates and S12a's outside sites read these rasters

Geology flag (Terrain.geology, §2.3; item 65; J-A65.49): the S0 toggle's value, or for auto the feature table's geology row at S0's relief class — P(soluble) plain 0.10, rolling 0.20, hilly 0.30, mountainous 0.30; P(volcanic) plain 0, rolling 0.02, hilly 0.05, mountainous 0.10 (our own rows, calibratable, extension) — read against one uniform S0 draws on blueprint.features before any other stage: soluble below P(soluble), volcanic at or above 1 − P(volcanic), else ordinary; recorded in autoResolved with reason (§5.4); a sky island's terrain takes ordinary, as do the parity presets (no reference has an underground); only II.7.6's cavern rule reads the flag; quarry voids read SiteResources.stone (item 65, II.7)
Restart-free by design: a requested feature infeasible on the drawn site is adjusted inside S1's own ladder (F-RIVER, §5.2), never by regenerating the whole map

S2 Programme (roster demand side; O7): from population (or derived from area or buildings by size tables) — the dossier's population and circumstances when bound to a dossier, the blueprint's own as the dossier's stand-in when none (§7.7 derivation table; item 20 (h)): households by wealth band (band set of §4.5, default shares FTG's captured lifestyle distribution; item 27); institutions (markets: one principal and secondaries by size; temple, churches per capita, guild halls, inn, mill on water, tannery; seats the government circumstance forces, §10.2, COV-FTG-B13); building demand per class from our own dependency tables run as §10.2's sequential, prefix-stable roster, with resource gates read from SiteResources ("no farmland → no farms, shops instead")
Outside classes (farmsteads, mills, quarries, lumber yards, fisheries, mines) are demanded by S2, sited by S12a and placed on the outside plots the hinterland unit builds (FTG-7)

Markets by size (item 24; emulation baseline MFCG's central plaza doubling as market, later wards adding secondary plazas rarer since 0.9.2; FTG places market squares by district rules, two in its captured city): the market class row (§10.2) demands N_markets: the principal (min 1 at every rung) and secondaries — firstAtPopulation 10 000 (the CITY floor) and perCapita one per 12 000 inhabitants beyond it (our own rows) — plus (our extension) one per growth nucleus beyond the first in a polycentric form (S3 (1)) and the town-level character's mercantile shift; at TOWN a secondary market drawn with secondaryChance 0.15 rather than by count

A market is a Reservation of kind market with a rank (§2.5): the principal is sited by S3 (12); every secondary is a district claim of S7b (§4.5 S7b (3)) except a polycentric nucleus's plaza, which S3 (12) ranks secondary (S3 (1)); each has its market district (§4.5); the market hall's and market trades' rows read a market's rank (§10.2); churches demanded per capita (MFCG spawns several); the sequential roster keys each market by ordinal, so an epoch's suffix may add a secondary market, which the epoch's S7b claims by the same rule (§4.11)

Hinterland demand decided with the town's (item 26; FTG-7): §4.9's farm table turns population into farm households and arable land, fuel and timber rows into wood burned and built with — farmsteads (none under §4.9's perimeter and rivers farm modes, whose farm households are housed in the town; a mode depending only on rung, climate row, S0's relief class and S1's resources), coppiceHa and managedWoodHa demanded here; outside classes' produces and supply edges (§10.2) carry them into need propagation; hinterland unit sizes fields and woods to them under §4.9's mode and extent rules

Demand in plot counts (FTG-2; J-P6): stage demand is plot counts per class × band: n(c,b,k) = class demand × band shares × stage k's quota share; residential band shares = roster's household wealth shares (shifted by the town-level character, which S2 reads from the circumstances' economy slice — its sector shares — so one input drives the roster and the economy dial; §10.2, item 72); workplace bands from the class row's lifestyle band

Stage land A_k = Σ_(c,b) n(c,b,k) · plotArea(c,b) / plotShare(regime_k), plotArea = plot area of the granularity table's band centre (§4.7; footprints and coverage not in the formula) — for a residential class the expectation over class-mix weights at the band centre (§4.7 S10b, item 71); plotShare = measured share of stage land that is plots: dense core 0.62 (MFCG gross lot cover inside wall 0.60–0.65 at sizes 40–250, CONFIRMED), gapped rings 0.55, ribbon 0.45 (PLAUSIBLE)

plotShare measurement: M-1 #5 (FTG face recovery on decoded road graphs) measures FTG's land share inside road-graph faces (FTG's client captured 2026-09-25 receives no lot or plot; subdivision server-side, item 49), bounding its plot share from above; M1 measures B-CITY's own per regime; fallback: if S5d's top-up fires on > 10 % of B-CITY seeds at a rung, plotShare rows refitted from B-CITY's measured share per regime by one scripted pass with a declared golden shift (§13.3)

Stages and walled share (MFP-6; J-P5): stage rows per rung (era-calibratable): TOWN 2 stages — walled core 0.90, ribbon 0.10; CITY 3 — inner walled 0.55, outer walled 0.33, ribbon 0.12; METROPOLIS 4 — inner 0.30, middle 0.30, outer 0.28 (all walled), ribbon 0.12; FTG's cul-de-sac suburb regime only by era or form preset or shanty toggle; share inside outermost wall ≈0.9 TOWN, ≈0.88 CITY and METROPOLIS (anchored on MFCG's 0.87–0.92 inside the wall at 40–250 with shanty off, CONFIRMED); FTG's ≈20 % walled preset reachable as a preset row; corpus phase recalibrates
yearsPerStage = 50 (a stage-row column; our own, calibratable): each growth stage stands for that many years of the town's age, the age II.7.6's catacomb rule reads

A staged history (item 88; J-A88.42): when the dossier port fills the staged Recipe.history (HistoryHint, §2.7, §2.9; empty in the base), stage count K′ = min(K, max(1, ⌈ageYears ÷ yearsPerStage⌉)): stages 1..K′−1 keep their rows, every later walled stage's share folds into stage K′−1 and the ribbon stage stays last (at K′ = 1 the one stage takes every share); only rules naming a scar's type read it: a fire or flood scar (a RaiseGrade.cause) by II.7.6's buried old town, any other type by none; the creation week shows a finished town (J-A67.47); empty, K is the rung row's

S2 output: Roster (demand by class with area/frontage requirement classes, district affinities, wealth bands) and StageQuotas[] (plot counts per class × band, land area and regime per stage: dense core → gapped rings → ribbon, plus optional suburb; FTG's zonal gradient, R4)

S2 need propagation (item 16 (b); with §10.2's supply edges): after the sequential roster produces the manifest, S2 walks the supply graph: for every manifest building whose class has a hard supply edge, count providers within reach — site resources SiteResources provides (farmland → grain; timber, stone, ore, fish, clay; §4.2 S1 (10)), harbour and gates for import resources (§4.7 S10b), manifest producing classes (produces) — at one provider per perConsumers consumers; where short, the highest-priority producing class receives its next building through its own roster/<class>/<ordinal> draw (prefix-stable; propagated demand a monotone function of the manifest entering the sequential run as a perOther floor), to a table depth (default 3: brewery → maltings → farmstead); a resource no class produces and no site provides takes the roster's substitution (no farmland → no farms, shops instead) and is reported as an import; hinterland food, fuel, timber rows are the outside classes' edges (§4.9, item 26); propagated buildings demanded here, allocated by S7b and S10a, placed by S10b, whose supply distances score the chain's siting (§4.7)
Need-propagation depth default 3 (brewery → maltings → farmstead); one provider per perConsumers consumers

S3 (J-P26) decides everything the first enceinte depends on in one construction — gate routes solved first, stage-1 boundary is the travel-cost level set over them, gates where routes cross it, castle weld and moat placed on the trace pulled from that boundary (no later stage recomputes a boundary they were fixed on) — and commits in two batches, L0 (every water body it carves with its decks) then L1 (land reservations), before S4 commits a single way

S3 (1) Centre(s): candidate centres on a coarse lattice inside the frame's middle third scored by a rule table — distance to a crossing site, to the harbour candidate, slope, elevation above the flood line, wind exposure, distance from the frame, a controlled random term; best is the centre (nucleus the main plaza (2), gate routes (5) and field T (6) are rooted at); it is not by law the market (principal site chosen at (12), the plaza itself by default; may be a bridgehead, harbour, gate or main street; item 24; J-A24.41)

The site is placed relative to the river (G-P14), so "no river through the core" cannot occur when a river is requested; the invariant is checked at S3 and repaired by moving the centre, never by re-rolling

Polycentric forms (IMP-9): twin-town and polycentric form rows site k = 2–3 nuclei (candidates inside the frame's middle half), each scored the same way, each with its own share A_1,i of stage 1's land (a form-row share), own main plaza (2) and own gates (4); principal market sited at (12) among every nucleus's candidate sites; the plaza of a nucleus that does not win it is a secondary market when the roster's count allows (S2), ranked and committed with the principal at (12)

Nuclei separation floor: sep_ij = τ(a₁)·(R_i + R_j) + (outer setback + glacis)_i + (outer setback + glacis)_j + g, R = √(A_1/π) equal-area radius, g one ribbon plot depth (30 m), τ(a) tip factor of the anisotropic level set: table 1.2 at a = 1.3 and 1.4 at a = 1.8 (above executed 1.13–1.18 and 1.24–1.34; receipt fixall_pipeline_r2_levelset.out), τ = a for any other a (safe bound); form row's separation band from that floor to 400 m beyond it (≈ 800–1 200 m for two 29 ha nuclei at TOWN); ground between nuclei grown as an extramural regime in S5

S3 (2) Main plaza of every nucleus: area band TOWN 0.25–0.45 ha, CITY 0.35–0.6, METROPOLIS 0.45–0.8 (anchored on MFCG's 0.32–0.58 ha at sizes 40–250 and red team's 0.36–0.54 ha); compact 4–6-vertex polygon at the nucleus aligned to contours, compactness ≥ 0.8; its vertices are the attach points arterials end at (plaza acts as MFCG's roundabout)

S3 (2) Temple or cathedral precinct adjacent to the main plaza by score, sized from its institution row; markets not planned here (principal at (12), secondaries S7b claims except a polycentric nucleus's plaza, ranked secondary at (1)/(12); item 24)

S3 (2) Harbour basin: a template shape (rectangle, semi-octagon, semi-hexagon, L wide or narrow) scaled to port demand at the chosen harbour candidate; canals along a least-cost line between two water bodies, each carrying decks of S1 (5)'s form at spacing row canalDeckSpacingM (150 m inside the predicted built extent, 600 m outside); planned polygons here — the lattice sees them as reservations and water (water impassable except along its decks); committed in (10) and (12)
S3 (3) Lattice and costs: S4's candidate lattice and its edge costs (§4.3) built here once over the planned water and reservations of (2)

S3 (4) Gate count (MFP-4, COV-MFCG-E04; J-P24): N₁ per nucleus = the request, or round(1 + 0.47·√A_ha) with A the stage-1 land — reproduces MFCG's 5/8/12 gates at sizes 40/80/130 from walled areas 58/220/548 ha and 18 at size 200 (receipt fixall_pipeline_mfcg_fits.out)

Waterfront reduction (J-A46.41): where the nucleus's pick contour runs along a sea or lake shore for at least gate.waterfrontShare of its length (0.1; our own, calibratable) the land law's N_land becomes N₁ = 2 + ⌊0.75·(N_land − 2) + ½⌋ — 4/7/10/14 where the land law gives 5/8/12/18, never more than N_land (provenance ref:MFCG 12710731 coastal gate reduction (code), P11: coded law counts mesh cells 2 + ⌊0.75 × inner cells ÷ 12⌋, recorded 3/4/5/7 gates at sizes 26/39/51/80; this is its metric restatement); a requested N₁ is taken as given; a river takes water gates, not this reduction

Sequential nested gate picks from the gate.pick stream on the pick contour (the level set of stage 1's land in the terrain-only field, a = 1, used only to score candidates): pick i scores the contour's candidate points by angular gap to earlier picks, nearness to a requested bearing (site request bearing or the bearing of a road partner of the trade slice — item 77 (b), §7.7 DR3), terrain (saddles and valley exits up, steep ground down) and a jitter, so a smaller N is always a prefix of a larger one

Each pick carries a bearing: the requested bearing it serves or, when none requested, the least-cost outward direction from the pick to the frame; a bearing's trade weight — read by (12) and §4.7 S10b's trade rows — is its gate's weight in TradeFlow.gates (§4.3, computed at (7); J-A77.41, J-A77.42), read from the circumstances' trade slice (§7.7 layer 2; items 72, 77); a polycentric nucleus's first picks are forced at the bearings of its adjacent nuclei

The harbour pick (J-P45): when the town has a harbour and N₁ ≥ 1, L* = the path to the harbour's destination node (13) in the plaza-rooted Dijkstra tree over (3)'s lattice (computed once here; the tree (5) routes gates with) from the plaza of the nucleus nearest the harbour — least-cost lattice path, wall ignored; when that node lies outside the pick contour, that nucleus's first unforced pick is forced at L*'s first node beyond the contour, after any polycentric forced picks (nested-prefix property and N unchanged); if no unforced pick is left (N₁ taken by polycentric forced picks: a nucleus under about 10 ha between two neighbours whose law gives N₁ = 2, or a twin town's requested N₁ = 1) no pick is forced, forced picks stay, and (7)'s detour guard applies unconditionally; the forced pick's bearing is the least-cost outward direction to the frame; its gate route's inward part is L*'s own prefix (a walled port has a main gate on its harbour side; harbour route (11) leaves through it)

Harbour pick measurement (M1): the committed harbour route (11) against L* on every B-CITY walled coastal seed, p99 of the ratio ≤ 1.5, and ≤ 1.5 on every §13.2 walled coastal fixture; pre-decided fallback: the detour guard of (7)

Water gates added where the river crosses the boundary (not counted in N); N = 0 produces no main gate and no external arterial through the wall — a harbour outside the stage-1 region still gets the harbour gate of (7); the sealed circuit is reported and the extramural stages are folded into the walled stage

S3 (5) Gate routes solved (not committed): for every pick the route from its plaza's attach point through the pick to the frame at its bearing — plaza-rooted Dijkstra tree to the pick, heap A* beyond — on (3)'s lattice with S4's cost function (§4.3); an island town routes to its landings; a polycentric pair gate to gate; S4 commits exactly these routes and reuses the plaza-rooted tree for its plaza-anchored routes (§4.3); the harbour ↔ plaza route is not among them and never enters T's road set; it is solved in (11) (J-P35)

S3 (6) Stage-1 field and boundary: the one travel-cost field T of §4.4 S5a computed here — multi-source Dijkstra from the plaza(s) over (3)'s lattice with road multiplier 1/a₁ (a₁ = stage 1 regime row: walled core 1.3) on lattice edges of (5)'s routes; each node records its source nucleus (polycentric T partitioned by nearest source); t_1,i chosen so nucleus i's nodes with T ≤ t_1,i hold its land A_1,i (exact to one cell); stage-1 boundary is that contour, Chaikin-smoothed and resampled

If two nuclei's regions come closer than their setbacks, glacis and g, the later-scored nucleus is re-sited to its next candidate (≤ 3 attempts); if still too close, the two are merged — one enceinte around their union and a cross wall along T's partition line (an open wall chain anchored on that enceinte at both ends, a gate where the inter-nucleus route crosses it) — and the merge is reported

S3 (7) Gates on the boundary: each gate is the first point at which its solved route walked outward from its plaza reaches T = t_1 (on the boundary by construction); keeps the pick's identity, ordinal, bearing and route; two routes crossing the boundary at one point cannot both be gates: the later pick re-drawn from its next candidate (≤ 3 attempts), then dropped and reported (F-WALL)

The harbour gate: one gate of kind water, not counted in N, carrying a way like a quay-access water gate (§4.8), reported, placed where L* first reaches T = t_1 (so the trace pins it and the harbour route leaves through it) — (a) for a sealed town (N = 0) whose harbour destination node lies outside {T ≤ t_1}; (b) as the detour guard, for a town with gates whose best gate-bound harbour route (solved as data on (3)'s lattice, stage-1 boundary impassable except at the gates just placed) is longer than 1.5 × L*, applied when M1's harbour-pick measurement fails and, whatever it finds, when the harbour's nucleus had no unforced pick left to force
With the gates placed, §4.3's trade flow derives its gate weights, the harbour's share and the dominant bearing — reading no route — which (12) and S10b's trade rows read (§4.3 Trade flow; J-A77.42)

S3 (8) The castle (MFP-3, COV-FTG-G09): when requested or drawn, the castle bailey sited by defensibility (height + water on ≥ 1 side + control of the main route, O8 d), restricted by the castle option to inside/on/outside the stage-1 boundary, under a hard filter that no (5) route crosses the claim or, when water is within reach, the castle-moat band planned with it by (10)'s rule: 5–7-vertex polygon on a jittered circle, area band TOWN 1.0–3.0 ha, CITY 1.5–3.5, METROPOLIS 2.0–5.0 (anchored on MFCG's plain-size castles 1.3–3.4 ha), compactness ≥ 0.75 (MFCG's threshold, checked and repaired here by §4.8's rule before the trace welds)

on_enceinte castle placed across the boundary so exactly two of its vertices lie on it — the weld vertices — and the bailey's outer arc (its boundary between the welds on the outside) becomes the stretch of town wall the castle shares (9); the castle's town-side gate fixed now at the midpoint of the bailey side with the least-cost path to the plaza (for on_enceinte, among the sides of its town-side arc), so the castle street is a routable destination and a ring castle moat can carry its deck

S3 (9) Stage-1 trace: for a walled stage 1 the registered EnceinteStrategy traces the enceinte by S5a's rules (§4.4): boundary pulled to defensible ground within the 40 m band with gates and weld vertices pinned, then pinned-vertex smoothing and topology-preserving simplification; between the weld vertices of an on_enceinte castle the trace is the bailey's outer arc itself, one wall carrying both enceintes' wall roles (§2.7 Castle.cityWeld); pull and simplification treat the water planned in (2) and an inside/outside castle's planned ring moat as water, never crossed (§4.4), so no channel (10) carves can cut the trace; S5a commits this trace unchanged for k = 1; an unwalled town keeps the boundary itself as stage 1's boundary

Trace test: every gate and weld vertex lies on the committed trace exactly (lattice equality); the trace departs from the boundary by ≤ 40 m everywhere except along an on_enceinte castle's shared stretch (bailey's own outer arc, may bulge up to the bailey's width beyond the boundary)

S3 (10) Water carvings and their decks → the L0 batch (GEO-19; J-P36): carved into L0 before S4, seen as water by every later stage: harbour basin and canals of (2) with their decks; a castle moat when water is within reach — around an inside/outside castle a ring band around the bailey outside its curtain's outer half-band and a berm with one deck at the castle gate perpendicular to the moat; for an on_enceinte castle only its outer arc: the channel along the shared stretch between the welds outside the trace's outer half-band and a berm (the city moat's own stretch there when the town has one, one channel at the wider of the two width rows; otherwise a channel clipped at each end by trace ⊕ (outer half-band + berm), ending against the town wall's berm beside each weld), while the bailey's town-side arc takes its castle template row's townSide (§4.8) and its castle gate needs no deck

City moat when moat is inner or all: a channel of the era row's width along the (9) trace outside its outer half-band and a berm (table 2–5 m), with one deck at every main gate and at a harbour gate (7), where the gate's route (for a harbour gate, the route that placed it) crosses the channel, perpendicular to it

Decoration ponds: the pond row of §4.9's decoration table (count by rung and biome), sites scored on hollows, flow accumulation and damp ground, each ≥ pondClearM (150 m) beyond the predicted built extent {T ≤ t_K} and ≥ 30 m from every (5) route and planned canal

No castle moat crosses the city trace (a ring surrounds a bailey the trace keeps off; an outer arc runs beside the trace), so §4.4's rule that the trace crosses water only at a river's water gate holds with every castle option; (8)'s hard filter keeps every solved route off a planned castle moat, so no castle moat needs a deck except at a ring moat's castle gate; every deck has S1 (5)'s form and two states
When a moat was carved, T is recomputed once over the new water (≈4 ms at CITY) for stages k ≥ 2; stage 1's boundary is never re-derived from it

S3 (11) The harbour route (J-P35): once the L0 batch commits, the harbour ↔ plaza route is solved on (3)'s lattice with committed water impassable except along decks, every reservation of (2) and (8) impassable and (walled stage 1) the (9) trace impassable except at gates; a harbour inside {T ≤ t_1} or of an unwalled town routed by heap A* from the plaza of the nucleus whose partition holds it; a harbour outside is reached through a gate: one multi-source Dijkstra from every gate's exit (the far bank vertex of its moat deck where (10) carved a city moat, the gate itself otherwise) over the lattice outside the trace finds the serving gate (least cost; ties by gate ordinal; a harbour gate competes, with N = 0 the only gate) and the branch at once; the harbour route = that gate's inward street, passage and moat deck (S4 re-solves through the deck, §4.3) and the branch; crosses a moat only on that gate's deck, adds no road through the wall (roads leaving the walled stage stay N, plus a harbour gate); data committed by S4 outside T's road set; costs one heap search of the castle street's size inside S3's §12.4 row (PLAUSIBLE); fixtures §13.2 walled coastal harbour fixtures

S3 (12) Principal market (item 24; owner: "the central market does not actually have to be central"): before the L1 batch, with gates, trace and harbour route fixed, the principal market's site is chosen by the trade-convergence score over candidate sites — rule table market.siting (§7.6; our own rows) with a controlled random term of share 0.1 from the reserve.market concern (§6.1)

Market siting candidates and score terms (defaults): main plaza of each nucleus — plaza carries rank 'principal', attach points are the market's: kind 1.0, routes 0.5 × fraction of gate routes (5) rooted at it; each gate inside or outside — a flanking square around the gate route's stretch just inside/outside beside the gate plaza (§4.8): kind 0.3 inside or 0.15 outside, trade 0.6 × gate's trade weight; town bridge's landward ends (13) — flanking square around the bridge approach S4 routes to the deck's bank vertex: kind 0.35, traffic 0.5 × fraction of arterials whose bearings lie across the river; harbour's landward attach (11) — flanking square between basin attach point and harbour route: kind 1.0, trade 0.6 × min(1.5, p ÷ portRef); busiest inward street — middle third of the street of the gate of highest trade weight, flanking square astride it: kind 0.25, trade 0.4 × that gate's trade weight; slope, flood band and wind exposure enter as (1)'s site penalties

Port demand fraction p = share of manifest buildings whose class requires 'coast' (§10.2); portRef = the table's reference port, median p over B-CITY's harbour seeds — a stored cell of market.siting (§7.6) computed by running S0–S2 alone on every B-CITY harbour seed; a scripted pass sets it at M1 and re-runs whenever a shipped roster row changes (new value shipped as a table-version bump with declared shift §13.3); a contract test recomputes the median and fails on a stored value that differs (§13.2); 0.12 (PLAUSIBLE) until the M1 receipt

Defaults compared (before penalties and random term; J-A24.43): single-nucleus town — plaza 1.5 (kind 1.0, routes 0.5), a gate ≤ 0.9, bridgehead ≤ 0.85, busiest street ≤ 0.65, so an inland walled town's plaza wins and the default reproduces MFCG; port — harbour 1.0 + 0.6 × min(1.5, p ÷ portRef): 1.6 at the median port, 1.3 at half the median, equal to plaza at p = ⅚ portRef, so the principal market leaves the plaza for the harbour in at least half of port seeds before penalties — the share §13.2's T24-1 and §13.7's row require (measured at M2b with §13.7's re-tune fallback); stays on the plaza where trade is mostly overland; parity presets pin the plaza by setting every other kind weight to its off value (item 23)

A flanking square is a market reservation of the principal row's area band (the plaza band of (2)) laid astride its way's stretch, that way passing through it as an arterial passes a gate plaza (§4.8): impassable to every other route except at its attach points (the two points where its way enters and leaves and the midpoint of each flank, where a side street may end as at a plaza); S4 places width_knot vertices at those two points (§4.3) so the square reads as a widening; chosen site, score and runners-up recorded in the report; setAttr on the reservation's rank or a drawBoundary moves the market by hand (§7.1)

The L1 batch: plazas, precinct, a flanking principal market's square and the castle bailey enter L1 as barrier faces carrying the reserved role: no way crosses them (S4, S5) other than a flanking market's own way; S8 does not cut them; the claimed entity is built inside them (§4.7, §4.8); every other claim larger than a block is S7b's (§4.5 S7b (3)), every secondary market among them except a polycentric nucleus's plaza

S3 (13) Destinations are typed entities: plazas' attach points and a flanking principal market's; each gate and its bearing (an external bearing per gate for a walled town; an unwalled town derives bearings by the same law on its own land); the town bridge — the crossing site nearest the centre when a river passes through the stage-1 region (scored at (1)), connected in town (§4.3) — every other site a bridge only when a route (S4) or growth proposal (S5c) uses it (S1 (5)); the harbour (its destination node = basin's landward attach point; route (11)); the castle's town-side gate; the precinct

Island towns (FTG-19): when the settlement's land component does not touch the frame, external destinations are shore points — the harbour, one landing per requested bearing (shore point nearest the bearing with best deep-water score) and a ferry point — and O4 (g) counts landings as the external connections

Dossier-backed elements at creation (item 22 (d); §7.7; J-A22.41): a brand-new map from an existing dossier holds every dossier element from the start: the blueprint's assignments and the dossier-backed elements enter S2's manifest as fixed rows — one (class, ordinal) each at the head of its class, present at every population, never withdrawn by the roster's arithmetic (prefix stability holds) — S7b allocates them before the roster's free demand in each rank of its order (§4.5), S10 (3) claims them, S10b's generation request places them (§4.7); the log's positions 0…k assign events (§7.7) record these placements as the generation run's own (place nothing a second time); replay reproduces them because the base derivation reads the same creation prefix (§7.4); a dossier element arriving after creation is a dossier request on the current map (§4.7 S10b, §7.7); one arriving with an epoch's inputs a mutation at that epoch (§4.11)

S0's sewer feature (item 14; II.7.1): toggles.sewers ∈ {auto, on, off}; at TOWN auto resolved by the feature table's P(sewers) row — II.7.1's law of the request's population and the intent's wealthLevel — drawn from blueprint.features with the other auto features, recorded in autoResolved; at CITY and METROPOLIS the rung row fixes existence on and a requested off hides the underground layer instead, reported in requestedVsBuilt (II.7.1); resolved value Features.sewers, which every dependant reads from the model (II.7)

S4 candidate lattice: built once at S3 (depends only on frame, terrain, water, reservations) and reused by S3's pick contour, gate routes, field T, S4's routes and every S5a boundary; a jittered hexagonal point set at ≈25 m spacing, adjacency known by construction (six neighbours per point, jitter bounded so no edge crosses another; no Poisson sampling, relaxation or triangulation)

Edge cost = length × (1 + k_slope·slope²) × waterCrossingPenalty (impassable except along a pinned crossing deck — a site or built bridge) × reservationPenalty (impassable inside a reservation; plaza and castle reached only at attach points and gate) × wallCrossingPenalty (only at gates) × existingFabricCost (epoch > 0: crossing a built face costs by its class, so growth reuses streets) × landValue

At epoch 0 S3's plaza-rooted Dijkstra tree gives every plaza-anchored route; a tree path that crosses a claim or water S3 added after the tree (castle bailey, a moat) is re-solved by heap A*, as are routes without a plaza end and every route at epoch > 0 (with existingFabricCost)

S4 commits the gate routes solved at S3 without re-solving: each split at its gate into inward street (plaza attach ↔ gate, primary) and outward arterial (gate ↔ frame edge at the bearing, through), so roads leaving the walled stage = N (plus a harbour gate) and each gate carries one road out and one street in (MFCG's gate identity; MFP-4)

Where S3 carved water across a solved route (the city moat just outside each gate) S4 re-solves only that stretch, from the last lattice node before the channel to the first beyond it, through the gate's deck, which continues the gate passage straight across the moat perpendicular to it

S4 remaining routes: the town bridge (each of its two ends to the nearest arterial on its bank in town); a site outside the boundary a route uses reached through the nearest gate, never a new wall crossing; every other site stays a site unless S5's growth uses it; the castle street (castle's town-side gate ↔ plaza, across the castle-moat deck when there is a moat); the precinct's frontage ↔ the plaza side it faces; canal decks inside the boundary ↔ the nearest arterial; harbour ↔ plaza and island gate ↔ landing were solved at S3; a polycentric town's gate-to-gate route between adjacent nuclei joins their plazas through both nuclei's gates; for a merged pair it crosses the cross wall at its gate

One graph, then one smoothing (GEO-16): all routes solved first on the lattice; the arterial graph is the union of lattice edges they use, each with its multiplicity; split into chains at every node of degree ≠ 2 and every pinned node (gates, attach points, deck ends, landings); junctions closer than 8 m merged on the graph; each chain simplified (Visvalingam) and smoothed (Chaikin × 2, then curvature-limited to the class's minimum radius) once with end nodes pinned, inserted into L1 once as a spine — a mandatory chain carrying the way role (§3.6) whose attraction folds any residual near-duplicate within 26 cm into a shared stretch — so routes sharing a run become one street, never braided near-duplicates

Class and width from multiplicity and betweenness on this graph (width table keyed by class, class by betweenness; O4 c); where a way's width varies along it (widening at a market or gate) S4 places width_knot vertices at the class-change junctions (insertChain opts.knots, §3.4), so width is a knot profile on the spine (§2.2 rule 5)
Junction rules: minimum crossing angle 30° (else deflect); Y → T conversion where the acute arm can be bent within its class curvature limit (G-P5)

Decks are fixed edges of the graph: smoothing never moves their vertices; each approach curve stays within the class radius; a river/canal deck approach that cannot meet the radius takes F-ROUTE's ladder (§5.2) — another site on the same reach within its search band, then an extra bridge placed as §4.2 S1 (5) — while a moat deck stays fixed to its gate, whose passage it continues straight; every deck a route uses becomes a built bridge when the spine lays its span through its two bank vertices (§2.7)
S4 test: on B-CITY no two spines run closer than their class separation for more than one step length; every deck's way angle within ±10° of the channel normal

Result: through-roads continue to the context margin with their bearings (O14); MFCG's radial gate → plaza legibility (streets converge on the plaza) with real metres and terrain (O4 a, d); later growth stages add main roads through S5b (§4.4), which runs this router incrementally with every existing arterial fixed, under the same F-ROUTE ladder; S4's local operator for edits is §7.3's

Markets as destinations (item 24): a flanking principal market is on its way already — S4 commits that way through the square between its two attach points and places a width_knot at each (the square a widening of the street profile, §2.2 rule 5); a side street may end at a flank's midpoint attach as at a plaza; every other market (the plaza when it carries the principal rank, S7b's secondary markets) is reached as a plaza or claim is, at its attach points; no market re-roots the plaza-rooted tree or field T (J-A24.41)

Trade flow (items 72, 77; J-A77.41, J-A77.42): TradeFlow declared and derived here — in two parts at generation: gates, harbour and dominantBearingCdeg at §4.2 S3 (7) as soon as gates and bearings exist (read no route), and ways after S4 commits the routes — and both again at each epoch (§4.11), from the circumstances' trade slice (CircumstanceSlice.trade: partners, bearings, modes, fill; §7.7 layer 2) with the gates' and roads' geometry; a derived record — Document.derived.tradeFlow (§2.9) caches it, rebuilt on load, never canonical; draws no random number

interface TradeFlow { gates: {gate: Id; weight: number}[] (with harbour Σ = 1); harbour?: number (water partners' share when the town has a harbour); dominantBearingCdeg: Cdeg (weighted circular mean of partners' bearings, item 72 (a)(3)); ways: {way: Id; weight: number}[] (absent ways weigh 0) }

Partners to gates: a road partner goes to the land gate whose bearing lies angularly nearest its bearing (ties by gate id) — the gate S3 (4) picked for that bearing; a river or sea partner to the harbour, else the water gate on its river, else the nearest land gate; a gate's weight sums its partners' weights, normalised with the harbour's to one (the bearing's trade weight S3 (4), (12) read); with no partner every gate weighs the same and the harbour nothing

Ways' trade weight: sums the weights of every gate and the harbour whose S4 route to the plaza (§4.2 S3 (5), (13)) follows it; main streets in from the busiest gates carry the most; a way on no such route weighs 0; §4.5's trade-position component and its gate and main-street kernels read these weights (item 72)

Without a dossier the blueprint's external bearings and the intent's trade setting fill the slice (§7.7 layer 2), so a standalone town has the same record; a user's gate or road edit re-derives it with the geometry

Two-point roads (item 101 (i)): a drawWay declaration in its points form (two points and a class, or more points for a free-hand line, §7.1) is routed at its dry run: each consecutive pair joined by this router on the lattice with the class's costs and existingFabricCost (prefers existing streets and plot lines), each point snapped to the nearest lattice node or existing way vertex (the author's snap, §9.5, resolves points first); chain smoothed and inserted as S5b inserts a main road (§4.4); a stretch across water takes a deck by S1 (5)'s crossing rule — its preview draws a bridge; the dry run returns the derived route as the declaration's resolved shape, stored resolved (§7.1), pinned nodes the handles; no later derivation moves it (item 101's R13)

Each growth stage k runs four sub-steps; stage 1 commits the boundary, gates and trace S3 fixed (§4.2 S3 (6)–(9)); a stage k ≥ 2 takes its boundary first, then its main roads, then its trace, so every gate lies on the boundary it was picked on

S5a boundary (FTG-5, COV-FTG-D26; J-P7): boundary of stage k is a level set of network travel cost T(x) — least cost from the plaza(s) over the S3/S4 lattice, a lattice edge inside an arterial's corridor costing ρ_road per metre and any other edge ρ_off per metre, both times the slope term; water impassable except along decks; reservations impassable

Anisotropy ratio a = ρ_off/ρ_road, a stage-regime and form row: walled core 1.3, walled rings 1.8, ribbon 4, suburb 3, linear-street form 8 (our own values); FTG's measured road/non-road 90th-percentile radius ratio 1.26–1.65 on its two captured cities is the calibration target for extramural stages (B-REF, §13.5); a controls the wide-versus-elongated balance of ribbons and suburbs

T is one field: computed at S3 (≈4 ms at CITY), recomputed once after S3's L0 batch only when a moat was carved; S4's remaining routes and the harbour route are not in its road set; each S5b's new main roads re-settle T incrementally only at nodes whose cost they lower, so no stage computes a new field (SCL-3)

Stage 1's boundary is S3's contour and S5a commits S3's trace unchanged; for k ≥ 2 the boundary is taken from T as it stands when stage k begins (before its own S5b): t_k chosen so the land of {T ≤ t_k} ∪ the enclosure of stage k − 1 equals the land of stages 1…k from S2 (lattice nodes sorted by T, cell areas accumulated; exact to one cell) — the union keeps stages nested even where a moat raised T just outside the previous wall — boundary is that region's outer contour, Chaikin-smoothed and resampled; S5b then picks and routes primaries on it; their re-settlement serves stage k + 1 onward

S5a trace (GEO-18, FTG-8): for a walled stage fixed before the stage's secondaries grow (stage 1 by S3; k ≥ 2 right after S5b) by one rule set, the registered EnceinteStrategy: boundary → pulled to defensible ground within a 40 m search band (local ridges, slope breaks, river banks: a cost-surface path around the town with a penalty for leaving high ground), gates pinned where arterials cross the boundary (stage 1 S3's gates; k ≥ 2 every crossing of an S4, earlier-S5b or this stage's S5b arterial), an on_enceinte castle welded through its two weld vertices (shared edge one wall; MFP-3) → pinned-vertex Laplacian smoothing in 3 passes (wall.smoothPasses, a wall-table row; provenance ref:MFCG 12710731 three pinned smoothing passes (code), P12; J-A46.43), gates, weld vertices and the two shore anchors of an open chain never moving → topology-preserving Visvalingam (kernel simplify §3.4: minimum segment 20 m, no interior angle < 100°; a removal that would make the trace touch itself, cross water, enter a reservation or move a pinned vertex is refused) → inserted on L1 through insertChain as a mandatory chain carrying wall role, gate vertices carrying wall_gate; on a shore or bank the trace is attracted onto the outline (shared stretch one edge carrying both roles, §3.6)

A second castle on an outer enceinte (the citadel of §4.2 S0) is sited by §4.2 S3 (8)'s rules against its stage's boundary and entered as an L1 barrier face in that stage's trace batch, with its gate and any moat deck

Water and the waterfront (COV-MFCG-C07; J-P25): the trace never crosses water except at a water gate where a river passes: its two vertices on the river's banks carry ('gate_end', gate, 0|1) and the Gate names them in banks (§2.2 rule 7, §2.7); a generated gate's bank vertices are the trace's vertices on the shores, placed by S5a's L1 trace batch after the water exists (L1 Steiner vertices on L0 shores, or L0 shore vertices where the trace attracted); an edited gate's (§4.11, §7.3 (b) 3) are promoted to L0 by the water's batch (§3.3 rule 3); every water gate names its bank vertices the same way; both kinds held under a warp unless fromLevel = 0, as a deck's are (§3.6; J-K35)

On a coast or river bank the trace may be an open chain whose ends are anchored on a shore, bank, cliff or another enceinte; its enclosure is closed by the L0 shoreline for every "enclosed" and "sealed" test

waterfront row: open (default — MFCG's coastal wall stops at the water; FTG's captured wall an open 17-tower chain bank to coast: no wall along quays and beaches), quay_wall (a wall along the waterfront), sea_wall (a full wall); under either wall a water gate stands at every quay access, so every quay stays reachable through a gate

placement 'aroundStage' traces only the stage's new ring, as an open chain anchored on the previous enceinte (FTG's "around stage lots"); nothing grown later crosses the trace except at a gate; S6 treats it as a barrier; if an inward pull would leave the stage's land short by more than the S5d tolerance the pull is capped at the smoothing step (reported); F-WALL's ladder is §5.2's

Outer moats: when moat is all, S5a carves stage k's moat (k ≥ 2) right after committing its trace, through §4.11's carve path; its way rule meets only arterials (each just outside one of the stage's gates; secondaries not yet grown), so every way is kept with a deck and nothing cut: the L1 batch places each deck's two pinned bank vertices on its arterial where the channel's banks will cross it (deck_end rows of a fresh Bridge, built with that arterial as its way, §2.7), the span between carrying deck (the arterial re-routed between the gate and its next pinned node beyond the channel where it would meet the channel more than 10° off its normal, as §4.3 re-solves S3's moat stretches); the L0 batch inserts the channel (era row's width, outside the outer half-band and a berm) through those prepared vertices, so each span becomes its deck perpendicular to the channel and continuing its gate's passage; S7 builds bridge furniture (§4.8); S5c treats the moat as water; nothing finer than L1 exists yet so the carve clears nothing; the innermost enceinte's moat is S3's

S5b main-road step (FTG-4; stages k ≥ 2 and every epoch stage): N_k = the gate law of §4.2 S3 (4) on the land inside the stage's enceinte with its waterfront reduction where the stage's boundary runs along a sea or lake shore for ≥ gate.waterfrontShare of its length (walled; J-A46.42), or one primary per mainRoadSpacingM of boundary (unwalled; 450 m at CITY); existing arterials cross the new boundary c times; when N_k > c S5b spawns N_k − c radial destinations on the boundary by nested picks (largest angular gaps first, terrain-scored like gates) and routes each with the incremental S4 router (§4.3) from the nearest junction on an existing primary outside the previous enceinte (never through an inner wall) to the frame at its bearing, under S4's F-ROUTE ladder (§5.2), extra-bridge rung included (its L0 batch of two same-level shore splits precedes the L1 batch)

S5b crossings become stage k's main gates; posterns only for an explicitly requested remainder; an outer enceinte never gets fewer gates than arterials cross it; a request below that is raised and reported (a requested gate count applies to the innermost enceinte, MFCG's semantics)
S5b test: primary length per km² and the share of gates on primaries in band from TOWN to METROPOLIS; each epoch stage whose N_k exceeds its crossings adds ≥ 1 primary

S5c growth of the secondaries: inside the boundary a priority queue of proposals grows streets FTG-style (CONFIDENCE C5): each proposal {origin junction, heading, curvature, goalHeading, class, remainingSegments, branchCounter, priority}, lowest priority first; step length by class (secondary 25–40 m, lane 15–25 m; FTG's district streets persist at (L + 0.5)/2 ≈ 25–30 m, where our tables start)

Division of labour with the bent cut (MFP-2; J-P4): in walled regimes S5c grows only the arterial-connecting secondary network at district scale — proposals seeded at arterial junctions and gate plazas, separation floor 120/160/200 m at TOWN/CITY/METROPOLIS, destination bias toward other arterials — and every lane and finer intramural street comes from S8's recursive bent cut, inheriting the wall's and shore's direction (MFCG street-signature targets §13.5); in extramural regimes (ribbon, suburb, unwalled rings, ground between polycentric nuclei) growth works at block scale as FTG's does

Heading model (FTG-17, FTG-6; J-P8): ou, a mean-reverting curvature walk κ ← ρ·κ + (1 − ρ)·κ_goal + s·√(1 − ρ²)·ξ per step Δs, ρ = e^(−Δs/ℓ), κ_goal = (θ_goal − θ)/L_r, s from headingSigma (degrees per 100 m); organic defaults 20° per 100 m, ℓ = 90 m, L_r = 250 m; planned 5° per 100 m; at organic defaults a 600 m street's net turn p50 21°, p90 50°, 0.1 % beyond 90°, per-30 m-step turn p95 11.4°, p99 14.9° with Gaussian tails (receipt fixall_pipeline_ou_heading.out, 4 000 streets per setting); radiusHold: ring proposals keep curvature 1/r about the centre with small s (ringed preset); gridLock: headings snap to the preset's grid table (american); CI tests the drift distribution per preset
Branching after n segments with a per-class probability, perpendicular ± jitter (FTG's Continue) or tangential to the centre (FTG's Curve around origin, the ringed preset's ring branch)

Destination bias, switchable per class and preset: a proposal that can reach an unserved destination or existing spine within ≈1.5 step lengths turns toward it; off for suburb offshoots and ring proposals

Legality (GEO-37): minimum separation from parallel spines = the regime's separation; same clearance to shores, wall setback bands, reservations and the stage boundary: a proposal within max(minimum block depth of the regime, separation/2) + half its corridor of any of them and within 30° of parallel is deflected or rejected (no strip thinner than a plot depth); a proposal meeting a shore or reservation at ≥ 30° ends there; a wall never crossed except at a gate — a proposal reaching the setback band stops there; snap to a junction within 0.35·step

Crossings follow the preset's crossing matrix (proposal class × crossed class → stop in a T, cross with a materialised crossroads, or deflect): organic crosses only a lower-or-equal class collinear within 6° (rare crossroads, O4 b); ringed crosses radials with rings; american crosses on the grid

Water in S5c: a proposal whose class row allows a bridge (secondary and lane by default) meeting a river or canal bank within 0.35·step of a site's bank vertex snaps to it and continues across that deck to the far bank vertex, building the bridge (§2.7) — sites' 40 m spacing playing FTG's minimum distance between bridges; any other proposal meeting water ends there as at a shore; slope ≤ class limit
Junction rules as §4.3 with T-preference in organic regimes; junction-degree band a preset row: organic 4-way 0–15 %, ringed 20–45 %, american 40–80 %

Between stages: prune dangling secondary chains shorter than one block width; trim only S5-grown provisional spines running beyond the boundary (FTG-18); S4 and S5b arterials never trimmed; the boundary becomes the next stage's start

S5d capacity check (FTG-2): right after S5c the stage's new coarse faces are priced: built land per face = face area − corridor reserve of its spines (declared half-widths) − reservations; each face's band is the driver-only prosperity field at its centroid (S6 pass 1's kernels) cut by provisional cut points computed as §4.5 computes the recorded bands, over land grown so far (S6 records the town's FieldBands once over all stages); if land per band falls short of Σ n(c,b,k)·plotArea(c,b)/plotShare by more than 5 % in total, one top-up runs: the level set grows to cover the shortfall, S5a re-traces only the affected arc between its pinned gates, S5c grows the added rim — except along a moat: a moated arc is never re-traced, so a moated stage's shortfall moves to the next stage's quota (last stage's to the exact check), reported; a remaining shortfall goes to the exact check after S10 (§4.7) and to the F-SITING reconcile, reported (F-BUDGET-STAGE, §5.2)
S5d test: §13.2's B-CITY wealthLevel sweep

Stage regimes (StageRegime rows per rung, era, form): dense core (walled, stage 1) block-depth floor 30–45 m (applied by S8), separation 120–200 m (district-scale secondaries only), a 1.3, ou bias on, lanes from S8, T-preference; walled rings (walled stages ≥ 2) 45–70 m (S8), 120–200 m, a 1.8, ou bias on, courts and rear lanes (S8); ribbon (default extramural, outside the last enceinte along arterials) plots directly on the arterial, depth band 30–50 m, starting beyond the outer setback/glacis (MFP-9), density falloff by a distance-to-gate kernel, a 4 (MFCG's outskirts: 71–85 % of extramural buildings within 100 m of a gate road); suburb (FTG C10; preset, era row or shanty toggle only, MFP-6) final regime outside the last enceinte, 40–60 m, separation 80 m, a 3, offshoots, bias off — optional perimeter lane (FTG-20: previous enceinte's outer boundary offset by setback and glacis, typed lane, broken at arterials) seeds offshoots at a 60–90 m spacing row besides arterial seeds; offshoots grow as cul_de_sac/lane proposals without destination-bias termination, no infill below the band; plots directly along offshoots with small lots, a per-plot density Bernoulli from the distance-to-gate kernel leaving gaps; calibration references FTG's 83 cul-de-sacs, 30.00 m suburb streets, 14.70 m lot outlines; american/ringed presets on request, gridLock/radiusHold, crossing matrix and junction band per preset; fixture: ringed on a flat site gives ≥ 3 closed rings with radius CV ≤ 10 % and ring × radial crossroads
The alternatives rejected for this construction are recorded with J-P4 and J-3

Fusion risk gate (O4 f): S4 + S5 + S8 infill ≤ 100 ms at CITY on reference hardware; infill block-area and junction-degree distributions inside the NG-measured bands on the same district shapes and MFCG's street-signature rows (orientation coherence at 60/120/250 m, wall and shore alignment by distance band, T/Y share, intramural dead ends, blocks per ha, lots per block) inside their bands (§13.5); M0 measures it before anything else is built (§16); fallbacks: on time failure extramural growth stops at secondary (lane infill-only everywhere) and the gate re-runs; on statistics failure infill constants recalibrated against NG vertex captures and MFCG size-sweep exports (spike M0-b) before M1; neither changes the architecture; repeated at M1 on B-CITY-lite's river, coast and relief configurations with M1's pre-decided fallbacks (§16; IMP-13)
Fusion gate time budget: S4 + S5 + S8 infill ≤ 100 ms at CITY on reference hardware

Markets and T (item 24): T keeps its root at the plaza(s) whatever site the principal market takes; an off-centre market is a destination the routes already serve; stage boundaries and gates are the centre's (J-A24.41); a secondary market S7b claims in a later stage seeds that stage's district typing and prosperity kernel (§4.5), never its growth

Arable reserve (item 26; off by default): when the farm table's reserveArable is on (§4.9), S5c's legality adds one soft term in extramural regimes (ribbon, suburb, unwalled rings, ground between polycentric nuclei): while fertile land left outside the built extent (SiteResources.fertile cells of frame and margin outside the boundary) is below the arable demand S2 recorded (arableReserveHa), a proposal onto a fertile cell is priced by reserveArable.penalty (default 3, a cost multiplier), so growth prefers poorer ground; a shortfall S5d then finds is reported (F-BUDGET-STAGE), never repaired by a restart; off, the term is absent and growth ignores fertility, as both references do (J-A26.43)

Perimeter: S6's one L1 batch first inserts the settlement perimeter — the last stage's boundary offset outward by the ribbon regime's block-depth band top (50 m) and rounded (FTG C17) — as a chain carrying district_bound, closed against the arterials, shores and frame it meets; every coarse face outside belongs to the hinterland pseudo-district, every face inside to a grown district, so the hinterland's faces are fixed before any district is typed and no later stage splits a district face to make hinterland (§4.9)

Margin band (J-I9): along every L1 edge two face sets share without a way — the perimeter, and any reservation boundary two districts share (a reserve seam run, II.1) — S10's eager step (0) (§4.7) lays a band of half-width 2 m (2 m each side; a table value ≥ the residue class's minimum width), split by the edge into one unbuildable L3 part per side typed residue with its side's ground role (on the perimeter a backland strip inside and a headland outside), so the pooled districts and the hinterland unit never write the edge they share (§3.3 pool step 3): their plot, alley and furlong lines end on the band's inner edge inside their own set

Margin band lifecycle: a regeneration on either side re-lays its own side's part (§7.3 item 2); an edit that moves the perimeter or changes which face sets share an L1 edge without corridors (drawBoundary, a merge or split, outskirtToDistrict, a moved channel) re-lays the band on both sides of every such stretch and removes it where the sharing ends, through S6's operator (§7.3's S6 row)

District grower (CONFIDENCE B9): seeds = the sited features (every market — principal's reservation and each secondary's claim, one market district per market, item 24 — harbour, gates, castle, temple precinct, river banks, the bridgeheads (both landward ends of every bridge carrying an arterial, the town bridge among them), parks) plus a density-guided remainder, N_d seeds in all; a grower (MFCG 12710731's district-builder idea) claims adjacent coarse faces of the L1 skeleton in round-robin turns: on each turn it skips with probability 1 − rate(kind) — district.growthRate table, one row per seed kind: gate, castle and bridgehead 0.1, riverbank 0.5, every other kind 1 (provenance ref:MFCG 12710731 growth rate by seed kind (code), P13; J-A47.41) — otherwise absorbs one admissible neighbour drawn uniformly

Admissible neighbour: the shared edge passes the edge test (no arterial of class ≥ primary, no wall trace, no water, no reservation boundary) unless the seed kind allows it, and the grown patch passes the patch test (area within the district band, compactness ≥ 0.5, no hole); a hole check → split

Grower rounds: a round gives every unfinished grower one turn in seed-id order; a grower with no admissible neighbour is finished; growth ends when every grower is; each turn's skip and pick draws come from district.seed keyed by the grower's seed lineage (its feature's; a remainder seed's first face) and the turn number, so §7.3's S6 operator re-grows a scoped regroup by the same turns; faces no grower could claim (enclosed by barriers or band tops) seed further districts in face-id order, grown by the same turns (MFCG 12710731's leftover rule)

A district whose area ends below the band's floor merges into the neighbour with the longest shared edge, except one grown from a seed whose rate is below 1: it keeps at least its seed face, so the rates set its size (small gate, castle and bridgehead wards behind §13.5's MFCG anchors row, 2.4–17.6 ha at size 40; J-A47.42); arterial barriers and the count law are ours (J-A47.41)

One law for count and band (MFP-10): N_d = round(3.5·√(A_ha/10)) seeds over the settlement's land A (FTG's 10 ha anchor in its middle; MFCG 12710731's ⌊√(city cells)⌋ matched in metric terms on its size sweep), band [0.5, 1.5] × A/N_d, so mean district √(10A)/3.5 — ≈7 ha at 60 ha, ≈14 ha at 250 ha, ≈22 ha at 600 ha

A district's faces is a FaceRef (§2.5): its L1 faces and every face nested in them (§3.3 pool step 3); after S8 cuts lanes the finer faces inherit the district through parent (§2.8), so containment is 100 % by construction (O11 b; §5.3's containment row checks it)

Quarters (MFP-10, VIS-4; J-P2, J-P28, J-I1): after typing S6 builds §9.1's quarter merge tree (QuarterNode) once per model: repeatedly merges the adjacent pair with the smallest cost — combined area, plus 1 000 ha when their kinds are of different families (central + market, docks + riverbank, gate + ribbon, craft + craft … share a family), plus 10 000 ha when a wall or water barrier separates them — until one root remains, ties by id; quarters are the tree's cut at min(N_q, L) nodes (after L − min(N_q, L) merges, L = number of districts; every district stands alone when N_q ≥ L; QuarterNode.cityCut; N_q can exceed district count at TOWN)

N_q = round(1.37·B^0.267), B the roster's building count: least-squares fit of MFCG's district counts on its size sweep (9/12/18/22/24 districts at 1 475/5 242/13 091/31 951/48 379 buildings), giving N_q = 9–10 at TOWN (1 200–1 500 buildings), 13–14 at CITY (4 500–6 000), 17–18 at METROPOLIS (12 000–15 000) (receipts fixall_pipeline_mfcg_fits.out, fixall_pipeline_r2_quarters.out); S13a names every node of the tree; the quarters are the city-band label unit (§9.4)

Typing (G-P5; MFP-7; J-P1): a data-driven scorer per district kind reads the roster's remaining demand per class, the kind's relation rows (RosterTables.districtKinds[].relations, §10.2 — item 16's templates: docks at the harbour, gate wards at gates, central → market/merchant, a market kind at every market reservation, noxious crafts downstream and downwind, near the castle → military/administration, waterfront → docks) and a random term; faces typed greedily from the largest with a mixed-use floor (no single-use district unless requested, R5)

Kinds are feature-named; wealth is not a kind — "the rich quarter" is a description the naming engine derives from the prosperity field (§10.4) — so no district is zoned residential or by class; the district's identity, read after placement from its character vector, names and describes it (item 72); the kinds stay this typing, which later stages read

A staged power relation (item 88; J-A88.42): when the dossier port fills a staged PowerRelation (§2.7; empty in the base), the scorer gains one soft row between the S6 kinds the quarter-identity rows name for its two powers (the kind of each identity row whose power is that power's PowerStanding.kind; §10.2; §7.7 layer 2): an adjacent row for an alliance, an avoid row for a rivalry or feud (any other pair type none), weight relation.adjacencyWeight (0.3; our own, extension, 0 in parity presets) × its strength

Shanty districts (FTG's rule as the default; items 27, 23): a shanty/squalid kind is admitted only when the roster's average band (household shares' mean over the band set) is poor or squalid, and only once the settlement's first half is built (shanty.trigger, shanty.afterStageShare 0.5; provenance ref:FTG shanty rule); where admitted it replaces the typing of the districts of lowest mean pass-1 band among the districts of the stages whose cumulative quota share (§4.2 S2's stage rows) exceeds shanty.afterStageShare (a district's stage is its growthStage, §2.5), as many as its demand fills, and takes the cluster row (§4.7 S11, item 70; FTG's tents row in parity presets)

Our preference that shanties lie outside the enceinte is the shanty kind's extramural relation row — soft, extension: true, weight 0.6, zero in the parity presets — a tendency not a law (J-A27.43); the shanty toggle (S0) forces the kind on where FTG's trigger would not fire; MFCG's "one prominent feature per named type" survives as the district's namingFeature; a district's fabric is bent-cut unless a template is requested (II.1, II.2)

Prosperity field (owner: prosperity is a gradient and a band; AM-6): P(x) = Σ_i w_i·kernel_i(x) + characterOffset(district) + ε(x), clamped once to [0, 1]; driver kernels from a table: distance decay to the plaza and every market (principal at the row's full weight, a secondary at the secondary row's, item 24), to main streets, gates, water and harbour (+); elevation above the flood line and upwind (+); low, damp, downwind, flood-prone (−); walls (−); attractors at reserved institutions (castle, precinct, plaza); the three dials' driver terms and the district pressure (item 72); ε a low-frequency fBm from the field's own sub-stream with a declared share (default 0.15); smoothed by a Gaussian of one block width (σ ≈ 60 m at CITY); stored per coarse face and as a raster

Field mechanism (budget §12.4): 32 m cells over frame + margin; each driver kernel splatted within its radius (or one distance transform per driver class); the Gaussian an O(N) three-box blur; computed in two declared eager passes (LC-2): pass 1 at S6 — first the driver kernels existing after S5 (the kernels S5d uses; S6's typing reads this driver-only state), then after typing the district-type term characterOffset(district), which completes pass 1 (S8's block bands read pass 1 complete); pass 2 at S10a (§4.7), adding kernels around noxious trades, prisons, middens and institutions the block allocation placed; S10 onward reads pass 2

The band set (item 27): one named, versioned table prosperity.bands (BandSet; §7.6), read by every rule table keying a row by band: granularity and the designation templates (§4.7; site-plan table folded into them, J-A19.41), greenery (§4.9), hidden-plot shares (§4.6), island supply law (II.6), ladder rows (§4.11), the interior ladder's rows read at the occupants' band (§2.6, item 28 (f)), the roster's household and lifestyle rows (§10.2); default set six bands in order: squalid (FTG squalid, MFCG slum, share 0.011, reads poor/dense with §4.7 S11's hovel and cluster rows — FTG's tents row in parity presets); poor (poor, slum, 0.011, poor/dense); modest (modest, craftsmen, 0.217, modest); comfortable — the middle band (comfortable, craftsmen, 0.435, interpolated between modest and prosperous); prosperous (wealthy, merchant, 0.217, prosperous); rich (aristocratic, patriciate, 0.109, rich); weights 1/1/20/40/20/10 (provenance ref:FTG lifestyle distribution)

MFCG's ward-class shares 0.70/0.17/0.07/0.07 of the open-source model's 30 class-typed ward-deck entries for craftsmen, slum, merchant, patriciate (receipt research/findings/os-model.md) are the anchor of §13.5's built-land share per band group, never a district typing (J-P1)

Band interpolation: a rule table may carry rows for some bands only; a band without its own row takes the linear interpolation along the value between the nearest rowed bands' centres (how the four granularity rows serve six bands and how class-mix weights §4.7 S10b item 71 are read at a plot's value); an end band takes the end row

Middle band: the band §4.11's geometry floor bounds a once-richer plot's manifested geometry to (item 31: the shell, never the interior, which follows its occupants' band through §2.6's interior ladder, item 28 (f)); designated per settlement as the band that holds its median household under the roster's wealth shares (comfortable under defaults: cumulative 0.239 after modest, 0.674 after comfortable); recorded on FieldBands.middle at S6 with the cuts and moved only as they move (J-A27.42, J-A31.45); each settlement's middle its own

The continuous gradient between and within bands is our extension; a parity preset keeps the reference's tier count and shares and sets the interpolation's blend to a step at each cut (item 23; J-A27.41)

Bands (LC-6, FTG-2): cut points computed once per town so the share of built land in each band equals that band's share of the plot land the roster demands (household wealth shares × the band's plot areas, S2) — capacity and demand agree by construction — recorded as the town's FieldBands (§2.5) with the band set's ids in order and its middle; move only by an explicit setAttr on that record (re-derives every block whose band changes) or by an epoch; a field brush (§7.2) never moves them; a block keeps its recorded band unless its value crosses a cut by more than the hysteresis (0.02), so a replay reproduces the session's bands; a block whose band changes past the hysteresis at an epoch is marked DUE for §4.11's survivors' ladder (item 31)

Bands used only where a table needs a class; continuous rules (coverage, plot size, greenery share, building scale) interpolate linearly between band rows along the value, so quarters blend at their edges

Over time (LC-12): an epoch re-evaluates the drivers with new circumstances; surviving plots keep their built state and change only through §4.11's explicit, rate-limited transformation events — the survivors' wealth ladder, whose rungs a DUE block climbs by duration and by its stock's replaceability, bounded by the geometry floor (item 31); under decline the field contracts toward the survivors' core (§4.11)

The owner rule clause by clause (AM-6): continuous field P(x); predictable drivers: the kernel table; controlled random component: ε with its declared share; banded only where a table needs a class: FieldBands; continuous rules interpolate: §4.7, §4.9; dynamic over time yet predictable: epochs move drivers, survivors transform by rule; editable: the brush and setAttr on FieldBands

The density field and the greenery propensity field follow the same construction with their own driver tables and FieldBands; each field's district-type term applied after typing as the last step of its pass 1

S7b Allocation and district claims (after S7; LC-2, FTG-1, FTG-3): everything deciding content decided once for the whole town before any lane is cut: (1) Town → districts: roster demand per class × band allocated to districts — and for outside classes (farmsteads, mills, quarries, mines, lumber yards, fisheries) to the hinterland pseudo-district (§4.9) — by capacity (built land per band from pass 1) and affinity (kind relation rows §10.2, adjacency to features, resource sites from SiteResources), greedy in a declared order (institutions, large workplaces, households; classes by priority then id; districts by score then id) from the town's alloc.district stream derived from the town's lineage on demand (no allocation record stores a stream key; §2.5, §6.1); a bounded reconcile (≤ 3 rounds) moves counts between districts before any placement; result persisted as one Allocation per district and one for the hinterland

S7b (2) Sub-districts (COV-FTG-E02): a class carrying a cluster tag (trade group) whose allocation in a district exceeds a threshold share gets a SubDistrict; S10a gives it a contiguous group of blocks sized to its allocation, so industries clump inside their district as FTG's sub-districts make them

S7b (3) District claims (J-P41): every item larger than one block — institutions whose requirement exceeds the district's upper block area (e_hi², as §4.6's stop test defines it), the district's share of the park and green quota (§4.9), area-bearing assignments, a castle's esplanade — sized from its requirement table and cut out of the district's coarse faces other than its wall_strip faces by claimSubFace (within = that face list, §3.4) at the best siting score, entered as a Reservation; S8 cuts around it as a hole (the slit exists), S10 keeps only sub-block claims, S12b builds parks only on reserved faces or residue

No S7b claim takes strip ground, as no S8 cut does (§4.6): a strip's ground is the band, setback and glacis S10's step (0) builds, where the hard invariant "footprints ∩ (band ⊕ setback) = ∅" leaves a claim nothing to stand on; only S7's gate plazas use a strip's setback zone (§4.8); a castle's esplanade is therefore claimed beyond the bailey's outer strip, so the spacer reads as glacis, then green (§4.9)

Step 7 ends in the model (GEO-21): each junction end extended along its arrival direction from the kerb to the crossed spine and inserted there as a T-junction (splitThrough §3.4), so the L1 face splits and the lane joins the street graph, junction census, betweenness and R3; NG's "stop half the crossed road's width short, square caps" is the renderer's stroke rule, produced by S9's corridor union and junction wedge; a cut end meeting a dead end or hole follows §3.6's contact semantics (antenna end → T-junction; hole joined by connectHole §3.4); an end arriving at a wall strip's setback line (no spine) stays there square to the line as a lane ends at a reservation; an end at the intervallum is a T-junction like any other

Seam portals (J-P32): when the crossed spine bounds the district (an arterial or boundary secondary) the T-junction's vertex lies on a chain two districts share, so S8 records it as a baseLane portal with its SeamAmendment in the shared Seam record of that boundary run (II.1), which both districts' contracts read; a planned end inside the portal gap of an existing portal on that spine — max(6 m, 2 × the wider lane's width), a table row — slides along the spine out of the gap toward the side keeping its arrival within 85–95°; if neither side does, the cut takes its next ladder rung; so two districts' lanes never meet at one boundary vertex (the crossroads step 10 forbids) and each portal vertex carries exactly one lane

When a re-derivation removes a lane, its end vertex loses its portal role (removeEdges on its VertexRef, §3.4) and is dissolved; its portal and amendment leave the Seam record, so the spine reads exactly as before the lane, and the neighbour step's reversal restores the neighbour's kerb (II.1 (3))

A district's effective scope — its own faces plus this seam exception (the chains, corridors, strips, wedges, neighbouring rings and Seam records its lane ends touch) — is §7.3 item 1's; every other entity of every other district stays byte-identical, and the locality oracle checks exactly that (§7.3, II.4)

Step 8 transaction and ladder (GEO-23): before step 1, on any face with a reflex vertex deeper than the band's plot depth (L- and C-shaped faces, faces wrapped round a cul-de-sac antenna), a reflex pre-cut splits the face perpendicular to the reflex vertex's longer run, and antennae are split off at their roots (FTG's fix for internal corners); then splitFace(F, cut) as a transaction; reject if either child violates minEdge, min angle or the class's minimum block width

Cut ladder, each rung under an operation-count work limit: (a) a turned frame — re-plan steps 2–7 in the working frame turned by 36° (attempt k turned by k × 36°; ≤ 2 more frames, ≤ 3 in all), drawing afresh from cut.t for steps 2 and 4 on the stream key's attempt component (§5.1 (6)) (P7; NG retries like MFCG in frames turned by 36° up to ten times, then NG leaves the face whole and MFCG restarts the whole city — ours bounded, restarts nothing, D-9; J-A39.41); (b) the straight cut from A along the mean normal (average of start run's inward normal and far run's outward normal as found in the unturned frame; start run's inward normal alone when step 5 found no far run); (c) the always-succeeding cut — straight, perpendicular to the longest run through its midpoint, clipped to F's own component by boolean intersection; when §3.6's contact rule refuses it (interior within attractCm of a shallow reflex vertex or touching an antenna) its foot slides along the longest run in steps of 2·attractCm, alternating sides of the midpoint (first toward the run's lower (y, x) end), each candidate re-clipped and re-tested under the rung's work limit, until the contact rule passes (for k shallow reflex vertices at most 2k candidates fail; a run too short to hold one passing candidate is a face below the band's block width, which step 1 already types a block); the slide draws nothing and is reported as W_CUT_SLID with its step count (J-Fredteam-1); (d) substitution — F becomes a court, green or landmark block chosen from the district allocation's pending claims (NG's substitution rule, K6) — only for faces ≤ 2 × the band's upper block area; a larger face reaching (d) is cut by (c) again (that slide, never a repeat of a refused cut); no rung restarts anything above F
Every district reports the share of its built land left as court or green by substitution (soft bound ≤ 5 %), so MFCG's "empty areas inside city walls" cannot return silently

Step 9 width (COV-NG-N20): one scalar per lane w = w_lo + Δw·min(1, L/L_ref)^p, Δw = w_hi − w_lo, [w_lo, w_hi] the cut class's metric width band (alleys 2–3 m, lanes 3–5 m), L final kerb-to-kerb length, L_ref the district OBB's major extent, p one draw per district on cut.width with ln p uniform between ln 0.5 and ln 2 (p = 0.5·4^u; powers by dmath.pow §6.5 (3)) — longer cuts wider, saturating at the band's top (P8; free-end term withdrawn as a drawing artefact; J-A40.41); in a walled regime a cut exceeding the lane length band is typed secondary; never narrower than a lower class (O4 c); template roads take fixed per-district widths (II.2)

Step 10 continuation (J-P11): a cut may continue across an existing lower-or-equal-class street when collinear within 6° (the rare crossroads) — only inside its own district, never across a district-boundary edge (GEO-42)
Step 11 recurse on both children with their own sub-streams

Deep-interior rule (IMP-8, GEO-25; J-P15): when recursion stops and a block's local thickness exceeds twice its band's plot depth, the district's band row chooses the interior now, in S8, by target shares: court (hollow block, perimeter plots around a shared court), back_lane (lane spine through the middle, parallel to the longer frontage), through_alley (alley spine joining two opposite frontages), rear_plots (second row reached through the front row); defaults poor court 0.35, back lane 0.25, through-alley 0.30, rear plots 0.10; modest 0.45/0.30/0.15/0.10; prosperous 0.65/0.15/0.05/0.15; rich 0.75/0.10/0/0.15 — our own values, calibrated at M-1 on NG's hollow-block frequency and MFCG's inner-lot removal; rows keyed by §4.5's band set (a band without a row interpolates, item 27); lanes and alleys chosen here inserted as L1 spines in S8's own district batch (S10 never writes L1), so no sibling block left stale
Keep-test: the court share of deep blocks within band per class (§13.5)

Hidden plots and reach (item 30): a court or rear_plots interior is reached from the public way by the block's reach, drawn with the treatment and recorded beside it (Block.reach, §2.5); S10 builds what it names: open — an open slot between two front buildings, an alley face (§4.7 S10 (9)) or the L1 spine of a back_lane or through_alley (the references' every-plot-fronts-a-street baseline and the parity presets' only value, item 23); passage — a covered way under a front building: an L3 face of kind passage (alley-as-face) of width passage.widthM (2.4–3.5 m by band) S10 cuts along one side line of the front plot the rule picks (widest frontage in the middle third of the run) from the kerb to the court or rear row; front plot keeps identity and its footprint ends at the passage's edge; S11 gives its building a wing spanning the passage at every storey above ground (BaseWing.spans §2.6; plan rung reserves the cells, item 28); chosen only where the front row is continuous (arrangement row), else reach stays open; gated — an opening in a frontage enclosure (PlotBound gate of a compound's wall or gatehouse arch, §4.7 S11) into a private court, chosen only where arrangement is compound or detached
