The arable reserve (reserveArable, default false): when on, S2 records arableReserveHa and S5c prices growth onto fertile ground while the reserve is short (§4.4) — the hinterland kept clear of suburb growth only when demand requires it, only as a tendency

Hinterland test: 100 % of outside-class buildings on outside plots with occupants; farmland per capita ± 20 % of the era row and equal to the farm classes' area; wood area against the fuel and timber rows with the import share reported (bars §13.2)

Farm modes (item 26; provenance ref:FTG farmland modes, keys ours; J-A26.43, J-A26.44): FTG has four farmland settings — three layouts Farmsteads, Around perimeter, Around rivers — and Default picking by size and landscape, climate presets overriding; FarmModeRow {rung; relief: plain|rolling|hilly|mountainous; land: fertile|poor; mode: fill|perimeter|rivers; riverBandM} per rung × landscape — S0's relief class and the fertile share (SiteResources.fertile ≥ 0.4 on at least half the cells: fertile, else poor) — plays Default: fill (FTG Farmsteads: farmsteads whose households live on their land, filling remaining countryside from the perimeter outward, lots larger where land plentiful; each lot a count-driven outside plot with driveway); perimeter (no farmsteads; farm households in the settlement, demanded as households of their band and allocated by S7b with the town's; fields close to the settlement ring by ring outward from the perimeter along the main roads until arable demand met; remaining frame in landscape uses); rivers (as perimeter but fields only within riverBandM, default 300 m, of a river's banks on both banks; no river → reads as perimeter; band short → remaining fields laid as perimeter beyond the band, shortfall reported, never a failure)

Farm mode defaults: fill at TOWN and CITY on plain or rolling fertile land, perimeter at METROPOLIS and wherever the land is hilly, mountainous or poor; ClimateTable row's farmLayout rows|perimeter|rivers is FTG's climate override (arid → rivers, cold → perimeter — FTG's Desert and Polar presets; temperate rows leaves the rung × landscape choice); the mode depends only on rung, climate row, S0's relief class and S1's resources, so S2 reads it before it demands farm plots; the hinterland's derivation record carries it; the field-system preset lays fields inside every mode; the village rungs take fill (PART III)

Count-driven outside plots (COV-FTG-I03, COV-FTG-B09): the hinterland allocation (S7b) lists the outside classes — farmsteads (under fill), water and wind mills, quarries, mines, lumber yards, charcoal burners, fisheries, lodges — and the decorations; sites seeded by score on SiteResources — the outside classes' relation rows (§10.2), the same rows the placement solver reads: quarries on stone, mines on ore, lumber at the woodland edge, fisheries on the shore, water mills at a reach with fall, windmills on exposed high ground, farmsteads on fertile land near a lane — with a clustering term (a seed's score rises for each seed of its own kind within the cluster radius; FTG's rule); S12a fixes the seeds; the hinterland unit's S10 divides the outside land into exactly that many lots by a weighted Voronoi (power diagram with area targets) clipped to the land; each lot an outside plot (L3 in hinterland blocks) with its yard and a driveway face to the nearest way corridor (VG's lonely houses); edge orchards (S7b (4)) are lots of their allocated area in the first ring beside their district; the unit's S10b places allocated outside classes and, under fill, the farm households

Crops and livestock (COV-NG-VS27): every field face takes crop and livestock from the era/region crop table (our own rows) under a rotation scheme (three-field by default: winter grain, spring crop, fallow per furlong, each field's slot from its furlong index); pastures take livestock; the lit preset's field textures read these attributes

Hinterland decorations (COV-FTG-I12): decoration table rows {kind, count by rung and biome, placement score, trail: yes/no, keepClearCm} places ponds (small closed outlines from S1's routine, carved at S3), copses (wood faces), stone circles, ruins (outline footprint in the ruined lifecycle state), wayside shrines (one per through-road by default) and boundary stones at the margin crossings — sited by S12a, built by the hinterland unit; a row with trail links its decoration to the nearest way corridor by an L3 path face; fields and woods keep back by keepClearCm; our own rows and counts, calibratable

S12b Greenery (after S11; O19; owner ruling AM-1): a rule family reading the prosperity value, the district kind and the greenery propensity field, never leftover space; the same rule family as coverage and plot granularity: every share a band row of §4.5's band set (a band without a row interpolates, item 27), the value for a plot interpolated along its prosperity value, so greenery blends at quarter edges; rows are defaults with provenance "owner ruling + O19 answers", all calibratable (J-T, §13.7), scaled by the rung's RungProfile.greenery (park area per 1 000 inhabitants ×, the edge-green or orchard probability, the private-green shift; §1.1, AM-4)

S12b writes only inside its own faces (§4.1): its L3 batch lays parks and groves on its own reserved green faces and residue, then its L4 batch types yard-planting parts; avenue and street-tree rows are Greenery entities along its own half-corridor strips (Greenery.along §2.7) that write no plat edge; the hinterland's rows are the hinterland unit's

Greenery rule table: yard planting by plot class (reads site plan, value; every plot): row → rear kitchen garden (≥ modest) else bare/midden; compound → formal or kitchen garden + orchard part; detached → garden; hovel → bare, pen or midden; cluster → bare ground, paths, a midden (item 70); institution → forecourt/churchyard · formal gardens (value): compound plots, share rising from 0 at the modest band's centre through 0.3 at the prosperous centre to ≥ 0.6 in the rich band → formal_garden yard parts (grid) · parks and ornamental grounds (value, institutions, greens): rich or planned districts 0.4–0.8 ha of park per 1 000 inhabitants of the district, only on S7b reserved faces or residue ≥ 0.3 ha; palace/cathedral close/monastery an ornamental claim of 0.5–2 ha → park, garden faces owned by the institution or commons · avenues (way class, value, planned flag): tier-1 ways (through, primary) bounding or crossing rich or planned districts; prosperous districts with probability 0.5 (the district's greenery stream) → avenue rows at 8–12 m spacing in each qualifying district's own half-corridor strip (a boundary way gets a row on each side whose district's rule fires) · street trees (COV-FTG-I09): secondary streets in prosperous and rich districts with probability 0.3 → one row at 10–14 m in the half-corridor strip of the wider side (by corridor half-width; ties: the side left of the way's direction), planted only by that side's district · edge green or orchard: modest districts touching the perimeter, S7b draws the choice — green/commons claim 0.1–0.3 ha inside the district at its edge, or an orchard 0.2–0.5 ha as a hinterland row in the first ring beside it; green built by district S12b, orchard by the hinterland unit's S10, both owned by the commons · churchyard: every church/temple plot a churchyard part ≥ 30 % of the plot's yard · market green: an unpaved market square (era table) → market_green · castle esplanade (MFP-11): an inside or inner castle, a 20–40 m green spacer between bailey and town · poor quarters: yard planting on ≤ 15 % of plots; a tree by the well (a pin rule at squares and wells) · hinterland ring supply: orchards ring 1, commons ring 3, coppice ring 4 (hinterland unit) · ambient scatter (COV-FTG-I09): pasture, meadow, commons 0.5–2 single trees per ha by biome row, clumped by a cluster process, each unit on its own land-use faces · shoreline band (COV-FTG-I09): round ponds and lakes where the bank is not quay or beach, a 5–15 m tree band, each unit on its own faces · trees at render: every green entity instanced by §8.10's layouts (ranked tile stamp for areas — wood 3–5 m, garden 4–6 m; jittered grid for orchards 6–8 m; jittered line for avenues and street trees at their spacings and hedgerows 8–12 m) keyed by entity and instance ordinal from render.instances/<entity> (§6.1); positions independent of LOD band; crown diameters in metres consistent with building sizes; species from the entity's mix; never stored; overrides are instance events (§7.1)

greens toggle (MFP-11): on — the park row fires in every band at a floor rate (0.1 ha per 1 000 inhabitants in modest districts, 0.05 in poor) and one park district seeded per 25 000 inhabitants regardless of wealth (MFCG grows park districts independently of wealth); off — parks and park districts not generated, yard planting and every other row unchanged; auto — the feature table (§4.2 S0); the resolved mapping written to the report

Park layout (COV-MFCG-I03, COV-MFCG-G03): a park's inside laid by a PartitionRecipe (§4.6): a radial fan of groves with alley-width paths when its compactness is ≥ 0.7, otherwise a semiFan from the vertex at its longest edge (MFCG's rule), plus a perimeter path (FTG's); groves are grove L3 faces and paths L3 path faces (fan gaps and perimeter band), not ways, so S12b never writes L1 after S9; formal gardens use a grid

Species and climate (COV-FTG-I11, COV-FTG-I15): a ClimateTable row per biome (temperate-deciduous, temperate-coniferous, mixed, maritime, arid, cold — biome a circumstance, §7.7) sets the ground-cover role, the tree-species mix with separate inner and outer shares for woods, the default field system and farmLayout, the default roof form and pitch, and the scatter densities; Greenery.species carries each entity's resulting mix, which the crown symbols and orchard kinds read; our own rows

Greenery acceptance (O19): (a) Spearman(prosperity, private green share) ≥ 0.7 within ± 5 points of the table mean, σ ≤ 8 across seeds; (b) public-green rule satisfaction ≥ 95 % and park/green area per 1 000 inhabitants within its band, reported; (c) 100 % of greenery typed and owned or common, untyped leftover green = 0; (d) tree scatter NN p1 above the canopy threshold and a pair-correlation per class; (e) ≥ 10 000 trees within a 16 ms frame at district LOD (per rung and tier in §12.7); (f) greenery control monotone and continuous (§7.8); (g) city-zoom greenery passes the legibility check and no option coupling drops the layer; restraint at city zoom is §8.5's; the grove tag and VG's dramatic forest kept as options; trees a layer toggle

The owner rule clause by clause (AM-1): trees and greens here and there (poor-quarter tree-by-the-well pin, edge greens, street trees, ambient scatter); parks (park row with per-capita band and the greens toggle); artificial landscapes (formal gardens, orchards, avenues, ornamental grounds: their rows); placed by rules reading prosperity and district type (every row's reads column and interpolated band rows); rich quarters gardens, parks, tree-lined ways; modest a green or orchard at the edge; poor little; yard planting follows plot class; same rule family as coverage and granularity

One more member of the family (AM-10): II.6's island supply law is a band row of this family: supported area and altitude interpolate along the prosperity value between band rows exactly as coverage, granularity and greenery do, read the same field, and are zero below the supporting threshold; its rows are II.6's IslandRule

Gardens over epochs (item 31): yard rows read the plot's manifested band for the yard parts that exist (S11's yard partition is geometry, bounded by §4.11's floor) and the field value for what is planted in them; rung 1's densify … infill builds over the garden part and thin … infill re-gardens it, re-running the yard-planting row for that plot alone (§4.11)

S13 is two parts (§9.1): S13a (model; eager for every district) draws names from the naming concerns only in §6.3's cases (a successor keeps its predecessor's name) — quarters (every node of §4.5's merge tree), districts, ways, landmarks and water, with short forms — builds each labelled thing's LabelEntity with candidate spines and anchors (§9.3), numbers addresses, and writes each district's one-line description from its venue mix, features and prosperity (§10.4; COV-FTG-E10); S13b (view) places labels per zoom stop (§9.1, §9.2; GEO-29), so the first paint is complete and the same for every viewer without any placement entering the model

S14 builds the columnar display list — the city band eagerly for the first paint, finer bands on demand per district, a transient list per drawing export, a DisplayDelta after every edit (§8.1, §8.9, §11.1); S15 is the optional module (§10), never in the one-click path

Names and descriptions from character (items 67, 70, 72): since S13a follows S12c (§4.1), a district's naming and one-line description read its identity and character vector beside its venue mix, features and prosperity (§4.5, §10.4; item 72); an informal cluster takes one place name and one label, never one per structure (§4.7, §10.4; item 70); a building's description reads its Works stage at the drawn week (§4.11 Which week is drawn: the document's week unless the viewer's week key names another) — "being built", "being demolished", "ruined since …" (§4.11, §10.4; item 67)

The one built path — add a growth stage (GEO-27, LC-12, FTG-4, FTG-14): grow(doc, epochInputs) appends an epoch event to the log and runs at that log position (§7.1, §7.4) on the persisted model with the epoch sub-stream: S2 (delta demand = the suffix of the sequential roster between old and new population, §10.2 — prefix-stable, no survivor's use withdrawn by arithmetic) → S5 for the new stage when a residual remains after the regrowth-first order (S5a boundary grown from the previous one and, if walled, trace and gates; S5b main-road step; S5c with built-face legality; S5d) → S6 (districts extend over new faces, existing districts keep ids; drivers re-evaluated with new circumstances, brush strokes kept as Δ) → S7 (new enceinte's furniture) → S7b (allocation of the delta demand in regrowth-first order — old plan's vacancies, ruins and traces first, new faces only for the residual) → S12a (outside sites for new outside classes; the hinterland unit builds their plots) → S8–S13 on new faces only (S10–S12b in the derivation pool over a copy frozen as §3.3 step 1)
S5c's proposals cross water only on a deck — a built bridge or a site the proposal builds (§4.4) — so an epoch's growth uses the crossing sites S1 and S3 left unused

Built-face legality (GEO-27): in an epoch a growth proposal may not cross a face holding footprints unless it runs along plot boundaries or back lanes (§4.3's existingFabricCost applies to S5c too, pricing a route along plot lines far below one through buildings) or a declared demolish conversion is chosen at its table cost (by building class and age), recorded as events; plots cut by a new corridor are re-cut through the conversion path — buildings that still fit kept, others demolished with lifecycle events — never re-derived from scratch

Survivors — wealth ladder and geometry floor (LC-12; owner 2026-09-26; item 31): surviving plots and buildings keep their built state; a re-evaluated field never re-derives them and never removes an occupied building; it acts only through the explicit, recorded, rate-limited events of the wealth ladder — three rungs by the time a block has spent in its new band and by what its standing stock allows — drawn from …/epoch=e streams (ladder's own draws on epoch.transform; a rung-3 re-cut's plot.* and siteplan concerns keyed by the block's and new plots' lineage with the epoch component, §6.1 — no new concern)

The engine scheduling the ladder is the owner's staged evolution stage (DEF-8); the base carries now the due mark, the table, the operators, the floor and the edit kinds, each usable by hand (§7.1) and undoable (§7.4); with no epoch nothing here runs, so the static baseline is unchanged (item 23): neither reference evolves (MFCG fixes granularity by ward type, FTG by lifestyle tier at generation; FTG's "regenerate area" is a re-roll, which this ladder never is)

The trigger — a band change past the hysteresis marks the block DUE: after S6 re-evaluates the drivers each block's band is read again against FieldBands with hysteresis 0.02: a block whose value crossed a cut by more than it is marked due — Block.due = {band, since, epochs} (§2.5): the band it must meet, the epoch of the crossing, the epochs spent in that band counted up at every later epoch — until its stock meets the band or the band changes again (a new mark; a flicker inside the hysteresis marks nothing); mark per block, memory per plot (builtBand); "the neighbourhood grew poor" is the aggregate of its blocks' marks and plots' records, never a district switch (J-A31.43)

The rungs act through operators the base already has — item 18's designation mutator (mutate §4.7 S11), item 17's use step, item 30's passage choice (§4.6), S10 (7)'s join-and-split law in incremental form (§4.7) — as LadderOp conversion events, so no occupied building is demolished by a band change and nothing re-rolled (J-A31.41)

Rung 1, at every due epoch — use, occupancy, condition. Growing poor: relet raises a building's household count within §2.6's capacity (J-A28.23), the roster's households (with a dossier, those filling its population, §7.7 item 2; item 20 (h)) and item 17's relocation filling them (§10.3); the interior follows the occupants down §2.6's interior ladder (item 28 (f)): the plan rung re-cuts the programme for the new count inside the unchanged wing rings (one household with staff rooms → lodging house → tenement of one-family apartments off a corridor → single rooms) inside the relet event for a stored plan (§7.3 stored-plan row; J-A28.72), otherwise when next clicked (unstored rung stale, §2.8); F-PLAN never drops a household (§5.2); outbuildings convert to dwellings and workshops, sheds and hovels infill the yard (mutate toward the field band's use and specialisation columns; densify … infill inside the manifested band's yard rows); the garden is built over (§4.9); condition steps down Building.condition kept → worn → neglected (§2.6; rendering classes §8.2, never a shape change, item 19); the roof is lost only by the decline ladder's decay after the last household left (vacate; derelict state of §2.8's ladder)

Rung 1 growing rich: renovation and extension by mutate's adapt and add steps toward the richer template (item 18); households re-united (relet down to the row's built count; the interior re-cut back up the ladder removes what the subdivision added and restores the earlier plan where nothing else changed, §2.6); infill cleared once its households are re-homed and the garden reclaimed (thin … infill; infill whose households cannot be re-homed within the epoch's churn cap waits); condition restored; use, condition and interior read the field band; geometry reads the manifested band

Rung 2, after the ladder table's duration in the band — tenure and yards: the holding fragments or consolidates without its front changing; growing poor, the yard becomes a back court of rear plots reached by a new passage (densify … back_court) where §4.6's passage choice allows and the manifested band's row carries a rear-plot or hidden share — a middle-floored plot's yard is infilled, not cut into tenements; growing rich, a back court cleared and re-gardened (thin … back_court: uses relocated by the use step, households re-homed — item 17's relocation, or a relet up in a standing shell within capacity — buildings vacated, then rear buildings cleared (clear) and the passage sealed, item 30; a court whose households cannot be re-homed within the churn cap waits); big houses change class keeping shells (mansion → tenement, inn, workshop, chapel) by mutate (item 18)

Rung 2 keeps every frontage and every main shell; its one plot-line change is densify … back_court, which splits the yard off the plot into rear plots and a passage face by S10 (7)'s incremental re-cut — the front plot (the child keeping the frontage anchor) keeps its address and builtBand, every child's lineage continued by §6.3's SPLIT rule (the parent's key with its child index), rear plots taking their new stock's band as builtBand — admitted only as above, never on a middle-floored plot; a court thin has emptied and cleared is vacant, so its rear row returns to the front plot's garden by rung 3's amalgamate (J-A31.40)

Rung 3, on vacancy, ruin, a destructive circumstance event or redevelopment only — the geometry follows: a vacant or ruined plot's ring is re-cut to the band: growing poor, an abandoned or ruined mansion's plot split into row houses or tenements (subdivide), or the fallen house's plot re-cut and rebuilt as lodgings; growing rich, a buyer joins two or three worn small plots and replaces their houses with one large building (amalgamate, then rebuild or build); redevelopment is a composite the engine issues in order — purchase (the plots' uses closed or relocated by the use step under item 17's rules — a dossier-backed use relocated, never closed; a pinned assignment or lock stops it), vacancy (vacate), then the re-cut and new stock — so the invariant holds at every step (J-A31.47)

Rung 3 re-cut is S10 (7)'s law in incremental form: the due block re-cut with its neighbours fixed (§7.3: the block is the effective scope with its seam exception), under the band's granularity target, fusing by S10 (7)'s orderings and splitting by them, every survivor's plot byte-identical, the new plots' buildings by S11's mutator from the empty design, their residential classes by S10b's class mix at the new stock's value (item 71); slums arise where stock was small and cheap, or from rungs 1 and 2 inside big shells; a mansion district grows poor as tenements behind grand fronts, never as a cleared slum (owner quote)

Asymmetry (owner: "much easier for a poor neighborhood to grow rich and merge plots"): rung durations are rows of the ladder table (WealthLadderTable in @plat/tables, §7.6, §14; our own rows, calibratable §13.9; tendencies per region and era, item 23), keyed by direction and by the stock's replaceability — a column of the template rows of the class table (§10.2) read at the plot's builtBand row: immediate (tents, sheds, hovels), short (cottages and poorer-band row houses), long (prosperous-band row and detached houses), ruin_only (manors, halls, institutions) (J-A31.42); default rows — years in the band before rung 2 rich/poor: immediate 0/0, short 0/10, long 10/20, ruin_only 10/30; rung 3 growing rich fusion after purchase and vacancy: immediate in the due epoch, short after 10 years in band, long after 30 years, ruin_only on vacancy, ruin, destructive event or redevelopment only; rung 3 growing poor splitting: every row on vacancy, ruin, destructive event or redevelopment
Every duration in years is read on the weekly clock: the years a block has spent in its band = (the epoch's week − the week of the epoch that marked it, from its EpochRecord) ÷ 52

Churn (J-A31.46; J-A76.44): the table's churn cap rows bound every epoch per kind — geometry (rung-3 re-cuts and rebuilds), fabric (the decline lottery's strikes), use (the use step's relocations) — as a share of a district's plots (or uses) per decade scaled by the epoch's years (a fraction of a year allowed; the scaled cap's fractional part the chance of one more, drawn on epoch.transform keyed by district, kind and epoch; no new concern) and a maximum per block per epoch; defaults 0.05/0.10/0.10 per decade and 2 plots per block (the former "10 % of a district's plots per decade" is the fabric row); candidates beyond a cap wait in address order; item 17's cap and the lottery's bound are rows of this one table

Geometry floor (owner quote on middle-class floor): each plot persists builtBand and builtProsperity — the band and field value its present stock was built for (§2.5; in the model digest §6.2; never recomputed from the field, J-DET-12) — and derives, never stores, geometryFloor = min(builtBand, FieldBands.middle) by the band order (the settlement's middle band for stock built at or above it, the stock's own band below it — a hovel cannot read poorer than a hovel; only replaced upward); the plot's manifested band = max(field band, geometryFloor), manifested value = max(field value, floor value), floor value = middle band's lower cut or builtProsperity when the floor is the built band

Block-level read (S10 (2)'s granularity rows, II.3's dispatch) takes the block's manifested band as max(block band, the floor of its standing plots' area-weighted median): plots ordered by geometryFloor in band order (ties by address), the floor at which their cumulative area first reaches half their total; a plot-level read takes the plot's own (J-A31.43)

Every change other than a rung-3 event reads the manifested band and value for what is BUILT — S10 (2)'s granularity rows, S11's template geometry columns (size budget, structures, storeys, heights, frontage, court and garden; J-A19.43), the yard partition (§4.9), II.3's block dispatch — and the field band and value for who is there and how it fares — households, condition, specialisation, room programme, labels and descriptions (J-P1: "the rich quarter" still a description of the field); the interior has no floor (item 28 (f)) — shell keeps its floor while rooms follow occupants down §2.6's interior ladder to single rooms off a corridor at the poorest; between the rich and the middle manifestation it cycles freely and reversibly through rungs 1 and 2 with no frontage change and no shell falling toward a poorer band (renovation may extend a shell, item 18); the middle band is each settlement's own (J-A31.43)

What writes builtBand (J-A31.44): generation (the plot's band at S10); a rung-3 event, to the band of the new stock (an amalgamate that builds nothing — a thinned rear row or cleared plot returned to its neighbour — keeps the builtBand and builtProsperity of the member whose frontage anchor the joined plot keeps, §6.3 JOIN); rung 2's densify … back_court for the rear plots it creates only; the hand edits of rung 3's kind (rebuild, demolish then build, amalgamate, subdivide, fill, a replace close-up (II.4), a New random of the block); the authorial re-derivations that re-derive the stock (a field brush's or FieldBands setAttr's re-derivation and Adjust, §7.2, §7.4); and a completed upward refurbishment — a mutate whose result meets a higher band's shape template raises builtBand to that band; nothing else lowers it: rungs 1 and 2 never lower a standing plot's builtBand; wealth change over epochs lowers it only through rung 3

builtBand lifecycle: Regenerate (keep settings) keeps it (a recorded input, §2.8); a member a split resurrects takes it from the rung-3 event that re-cut it, not from its tombstone (§6.3); a document written before the attribute existed gets builtBand = its plot's DerivationRecord.band and builtProsperity = its recorded sample, exact for every document without an epoch (§7.5 migration); the floor draws no random numbers; with no epoch the manifested band equals the field band everywhere

Lineage survives, so the seed survives (J-A31.48): fusion and splitting continue lineage by §6.3's JOIN and SPLIT rule (J-A31.73), so one seed with one history gives one town; an undo returns the former plots exactly from the undo record's rings and records (§7.4); every ladder event is a mutation continuing lineage; only a re-derivation takes fresh lineage (§6.3 succession rule; owner: "It's not new rerolls its modifications and variations to the original seed")

The epoch's order (engine's loop on the base's path): before S2 — rung profile read at the epoch's population target (The rung at an epoch), dials' applied standings and shares move past their hysteresis (The dials' inputs over epochs), TradeFlow re-read from the epoch's trade slice on current geometry (§4.3; item 77); after S2's delta demand: (a) S6 re-evaluates drivers and bands, re-bands every live plot's fieldBand against its own column by §4.5's rule (§2.5; J-A28.29) — before any rung reads the field band, former values in the epoch's undo record — and marks due blocks; (b) the use step (item 17) closes, opens and relocates uses; (c) when the target fell, the roster's suffix leaves in reverse ordinal order — a building whose household count falls but not to zero takes a relet down (unstored plan stale, stored plan re-cut in the event), vacate only when its last household leaves; the decline lottery draws per building, deciding whose households leave first, and strikes fabric by exposure (item 28 (f) with item 8; J-A28.45); (d) the ladder runs its rungs on due blocks under the churn cap; (e) dossier events arriving with the epoch's inputs (EpochInputs.dossier, in host order) applied as mutations at that epoch — S10b's dossier request and S11's mutator (§4.7, §7.7; item 22 (e)), never a re-roll (J-A22.42); (f) siting places the delta in the regrowth-first order from its step (0) — a relet up in a standing shell before reoccupy of a vacant one (J-A28.45); (g) a residual grows a stage (S5); (h) every live placement rejection (§7.7, item 20) re-checked by §7.7's lapse rule (J-A20.74, J-A20.41), the epoch writing lapsedAt inside its touched set; a lapsed site eligible from the next placement on; (i) the character step (item 72): §4.5's S12c on the grown town — character vector, identity (past hysteresis, re-typing a kind its identity row names), band range re-derived, clamped excess added to pressure, a district whose identity changed renamed by §6.3's epoch case — and TradeFlow re-derived on grown geometry; (j) every physical change of (a)–(g) shown on the ground by a Works started inside the epoch's span, and every Works finished more than works.retainWeeks before the epoch's week retired (item 67)

Each epoch step's events cite the epoch; the whole is one epoch event's fold (§7.4); a dossier event between epochs is applied at its own log position by the same request and mutator (§7.7); a dated one — between epochs or carried by an epoch — keeps its dossierChange (§7.1, item 75) and starts its Works at the change's week

Regenerate, Adjust and the derivation record: a transformed entity's DerivationRecord is updated; every other plot keeps its record, so Regenerate (keep settings) on an untouched block reproduces it byte for byte; re-deriving it with the new field is the explicit Adjust (authorial); siting across epochs places only delta demand in the regrowth-first order

Test (M4): on a town with walled, ribbon and suburb regimes, adding a stage re-rolls 0 survivors, adds ≥ 1 primary when its gate law asks for one, and replays from the log to the session hash; the ladder's, floor's and epoch order's hook tests are §13.2's (item 31), as are the Works', the clock's and the character step's (items 67, 72, 76)

ConversionOp is defined here once as one union: the base's own kinds (wallToWay {enceinte, widthCm?}; gateToJunction {gate, square?}; outskirtToDistrict {region {ring, key}} — no stored slots §2.2 rule 5; demolish {id}; rebuild {building, cls} — whole replacement a ruin or redevelopment calls for (rung 3), never a designation change; build {plot, cls, footprint?} — as §7.1's build event; carve {kind canal|moat|harbour_basin, polygon}; abandon|decay|ruin|robStone|clear {building} (clear: removed to a footprint trace); plotToGarden {plot}; contractWall {enceinte, trace}) plus LadderOp (item 31), DeclineOp (item 8), UseConversionOp (item 17), TerrainWaterOp (item 25), HiddenOp (item 30 (e)) and the underground's own kinds (item 65: RaiseGrade II.7.6, ClearUndercity II.7.5, declared there); §7.1's convert event carries it; build is §7.1's build event

LadderOp = relet {building, households: rung 1, the household count the roster fills within §2.6's capacity (J-A28.23); stored plan re-cut inside the event, unstored goes stale and re-cut on click, along §2.6's interior ladder} | densify {plot, as: infill (rung 1: sheds, hovels, a workshop in the yard, garden built over) | back_court (rung 2: rear plots reached by a new passage)} | thin {plot, what: infill|back_court — inverse: infill cleared and re-gardened (§4.9) after uses relocate and households re-homed (item 17's relocation or a relet up within capacity) and buildings vacated; back court likewise, passage sealed} | subdivide|amalgamate {plots: rung 3 only, on vacated plots: S10 (7)'s incremental law; §7.1's plot split and join are the hand forms}; each a mutation with an undo record (§7.4), usable by hand (§7.1)

wallToWay(enceinte) = retypeEdges(ChainRef('wall', enceinte), add ('way', the new ring road), remove 'wall'): the wall chain becomes the spine of a primary way with a ring-road width on the same edges; the wall strips' setback and glacis lines removed, strips merge into the faces beside them, band, tower and gatehouse faces cleared with the rest of their finer content; S9's corridorUnion re-derives the ring road's corridor there; towers removed; gates become junctions with a square option

wallToWay clearance (GEO-38): the new corridor needs half its width on each side of the old wall line; where the half-band plus setback on a side is narrower, plots meeting the new corridor are clipped along its edge — a plot keeps its id when its frontage anchor survives (O8 g) — and footprints that no longer fit are demolished with lifecycle events (cause convert:wallToWay)

carve — a canal, moat or basin added by an edit, or an outer moat by S5a (§4.4): the dry run decides every way's fate and the carve's one footprint before any batch runs; S = channel ⊕ its bank setback; every way whose corridor meets S takes a fate by class (J-P30), recorded as lifecycle events with cause convert:carve

Carve fate kept with a pinned deck: every through and primary way, and any other way that is the only connection of the streets on its far side to a gate or the plaza; its deck (S1 (5)'s form, perpendicular to the channel) and its re-route solved in the dry run by §7.3's S4 local operator — between the way's nearest pinned nodes on either side of S, on S3's lattice with existingFabricCost (keeps near its old line), through the deck as a fixed graph edge; a way already meeting the channel within ±10° of its normal keeps its line and only its stretch across the channel changes; the old stretch between the re-route's ends is the way's replaced stretch; S7's rules give the deck its Bridge (events: altered on the way, built on the bridge)

Carve fate cut: every other secondary, lane, alley, cul_de_sac, track and path: its stretch inside the channel ⊕ max(bank setback, 1 m) removed, so every cut end lies ≥ 1 m from the channel, and a remainder that now dangles shorter than one block depth is pruned (events: altered, demolished); quay and pier ways cut the same way and, where they met the new water at ≥ 30°, extended from the cut end to the new bank as a quay or landing

Other crossings (J-I13): a wall trace S crosses has its run (trace between the nearest unaffected towers on either side) re-traced as data in the dry run with a water gate where the channel crosses (as §7.3 (b) 2 re-traces a run a moved river crosses); the run's strip-line stretches alongside it (inner setback line, glacis line or the moat's inner bank which stays, and the intervallum where the era row has one) between the feet of the perpendiculars from the run's two end towers leave with the old run and S7's operator re-cuts them along the re-traced run from those feet (batch (3)); every way the re-traced run's new strips (new run ⊕ (half band + setback, + glacis or berm on the field side)) will meet — other than a kept way through a gate of the run — takes the cut fate at the strip's boundary (as drawWall cuts ways its new strips meet, §5.2, §7.4), and every plot inside the new strips is re-derived with the rest of R; a locked or pinned way, wall or finer entity, or a reservation, inside S or a new strip returns to the dry run as an F-EDIT conflict (lock > drawn geometry; Re-derive from S3 offered for a reservation, §5.2), as for S1's water operator

The footprint (J-P34): C = the set of L1 cells that (a) the channel ⊕ (attractCm + bank setback) meets; (b) border a removed stretch, a pruned remainder or a stretch the new strips' cuts remove; (c) border a kept way's replaced stretch or are crossed by its new route; (d) where the channel crosses a wall, border the old run or the strip-line stretches batch (1) removes with it, or meet the re-traced run ⊕ (half band + setback, + glacis or berm on the field side); R = ⋃ C exactly; R is the carve's one clear region: batches (1) and (2) declare it as KernelTx.clearRegion, step (4) re-derives exactly its cells, the fate report lists exactly the protected entities inside it; locality checks (§3.3 clear-region confirmation, §7.3's carve row, §13.1 and §16 M3a fixtures, the O18 (g)/O2 (c) perturbation test) require byte identity outside it, less the seam exception at its boundary

By (b)–(d) no plot outside R loses its access (a plot's access edge lies on a kerb of a way it fronts) and batch (1) removes no edge a kept face uses (no E_KEPT); inside R S10 gives every plot an access edge by construction (O5 a), and S8's deep-interior rule and F-PLOT's alley rung act as in any block; wall-crossing fixtures are §13.1's and §13.2's

Carve batch (1) L1, clear region R: clearFiner on R's cells; cut stretches, pruned remainders and kept ways' replaced stretches removed, each through its StretchRef (§3.4) — a way cut in two first hands its far part to a new way by retypeEdges' rekey on that part's StretchRef; each kept way's new route inserted whole across the line the channel will take with its deck's two bank vertices placed at the new bank points (deck_end, pinned) and the span carrying structural deck beside way (every kept way one connected chain through every batch); each crossed wall run replaced by its re-traced run with its water gate's two bank vertices carrying ('gate_end', gate, 0|1) under a fresh Gate (§2.2 rule 7), the old run leaving with its strip-line stretches (each through its StretchRef, ends placed by splitThrough at the feet of the end towers' perpendiculars); ways the new strips will meet cut at the strips' boundaries; every other L1 edge the channel's banks will cross that is no way (settlement-perimeter or other district-boundary stretch, a wall strip's setback or glacis line outside a re-traced run) split at its two bank points by splitThrough, each carrying an anchor contact name (§2.2 rule 7: the entity of the edge's first own-level row, smallest free ordinal — from 2 on an enceinte), the stretch between removed through its StretchRef; the map's border line split at its bank points the same way but kept whole across the channel (§3.3 clear regions rule 2; the arena's outer ring is L0); those deck_end, gate_end and contact-name vertices are the carve's prepared vertices; every cut end ≥ 1 m from the channel, so no way is prepared except at its deck

Carve batch (2) L0, clear region R, KernelTx.prepared = the deck_end, gate_end and contact-name vertices of (1) (J-P40): the channel's ring inserted, attracts onto and promotes the prepared vertices, stripping the contact names (§3.3 rule 3, §3.6); each deck span now crosses the water as the Bridge's deck (§2.2 rule 7); no L0 edge crosses the channel, water body stays one L0 face; any other contact with finer geometry is E_LEVEL or E_KEPT and returns to the dry run

Carve batch (3) L1: each kept quay or pier extended from its cut end to the new bank (end a Steiner vertex on the L0 bank line, §2.2 rule 3); S7's operator re-cuts the wall strips' setback, glacis and intervallum lines along each re-traced run from the feet (1) left, closing them on the new banks, and builds its towers and the water gate's Gate record whose banks name its two gate_end vertices (§7.3's S7 row)

Carve step (4) re-derivation of R (J-P43): S6's operator restricted to R's cells after the L0 batch: each land face of R takes the district — or hinterland pseudo-district, or wall_strip typing — of the pre-edit L1 cell that held the larger part of its area (ties by id); a boundary stretch removed under the water lies between its two bank anchors, so the L0 batch re-separates the land on either bank along the remaining boundary and no land face spans it (a canal across the settlement perimeter leaves the land outside it with the hinterland on both banks — 0 district faces outside the perimeter; fixture §13.2); a block part beside a crossed glacis line keeps its own block's typing; the same rule settles a boundary stretch removed on land (a cut way that carried a district boundary) by the larger part; new strips (3) cut are typed wall_strip and take their district as S7's strips do; channel water faces leave the district face sets they were cut from; then S8–S12b re-derive R's cells by tree scoping (§7.3 item 2) — S8 first — with S10's step (0) for R's faces beside a wall trace, the perimeter or a shared reservation boundary

Where a carve batch adds or removes a junction vertex on a spine that bounds R, the far side takes II.1 (3)'s neighbour step or its reversal; those steps and the Seam records of R's districts are the carve's seam exception, the same set a district's reroll has (§7.3 item 1), which the locality oracle computes from the commit records; a carve costs its footprint, not the town

At S5a nothing finer than L1 exists and the channel meets only the arterials through the stage's gates: every way kept with a deck, nothing cut, R clears nothing (§4.4); every touched entity's lifecycle records the event with its cause

A cut way's far part — records that name a way (J-Fpipe-2): when carve batch (1) hands a cut way's far part to a new way by rekey — and S1's water operator likewise (§7.3 (b) 3) — the rekey moves role rows, knot rows and vertex role rows and no record (§3.4), so the same batch re-points every record naming the way by id along the far part to the new way: Frontage.way (§2.5), Bridge.way of a built deck, Gate.way of a gate (§2.7), Greenery.along.way of avenue and street-tree rows (§4.9; §2.7), Junction.arms at its junctions (§2.4), Tunnel.follows of a main beneath (§2.7), and SeamEdge.chain, Portal.wayId, SeamAmendment.spine of Seam records naming it (II.1); those records lie outside R and change only by that id: the carve's identity exception, admitted by the locality oracle beside the seam exception (§7.3 item 1, item 7 (ii)); every such record equals its prior except the new way's id; every other entity outside R byte-identical

Which part keeps the old address is §6.3's anchor rule (the part keeping the old anchor, §7.3 (b)); the far part keyed by §6.3's SPLIT rule as a split plot's or tunnel's part is (J-A31.73, J-A11.43), continues lineage and keeps the parent's name and naming record without a draw — a street a canal severs is one street on both banks, so S13a draws nothing and label candidates for the new way built inside the carve's S13a delta (§7.3 item 2); a Frontage's class and lengthCm unchanged; the carve's undo restores the one way and every re-pointed record (§7.4)

Carve far-part test (§13.2, with §13.1's carve fixtures): after a canal that cuts a lane and a secondary, §5.3's reference-integrity row holds on every record that named either way, 0 records outside R differ from their prior other than by the new way id, and both parts of each cut way carry one name

Coherence from one seed (owner): epoch N+1 derived from epoch N's persisted state, the inputs and the seed's epoch sub-stream …/epoch=<n>: same town under different inputs has different histories, under the same inputs the same history; nothing that survives is re-rolled (survivor keeps lineage and derivation record, §6.3, §7.3)

The evolution engine is the owner's later stage (DEF-8); its hooks are concrete now: the owner's history (growth, regression, growth again: houses emptied and robbed for stone, plots turned to gardens, a shorter wall ring inside the old one, ruins left standing) expressed with the base's records: the transformation and conversion kinds (abandon, decay, ruin, robStone, plotToGarden, contractWall, LadderOp, DeclineOp), which a user can also apply by hand (§7.1); the lifecycle history on every entity; the epoch streams; the circumstances timeline (§7.7); the sequential roster (a population fall selects its suffix in reverse ordinal order; the decline table's exposure lottery chooses which buildings empty); a ruined building keeps its footprint and heights and draws with the ruin program and the none roof kind (§2.6, §8.2); when and where the engine applies these kinds is its own rule table over …/epoch=e streams

interface EpochInputs {week?: number (item 76: absolute week at the epoch — a dossier-bound map's is SettlementForge's calendar.elapsedWeeks; absent on a standalone call, then previous week + round(52 × years)); years: number (derived from weeks: (week − previous epoch's week, or the creation week) ÷ 52, a fraction allowed); populationTarget: number; circumstances: CircumstanceSlice (§7.7 layer 2); events: {kind; params: Record<string, number>}[]; dossier?: EditEvent[] (host's dossier events, author 'host', EditBase.dossier set, in host order, applied at step (e) (§7.7 item 6); each keeps its EditBase.dossierChange (§7.1, item 75))}

interface EvolutionStrategy {plan(doc: Document, inputs: EpochInputs, tables: TableView, rng: Stream): KernelResult<(ConversionOp | EditEvent)[]>} registered by name (§4.12); base registration 'grow-by-stage' — the path above; the owner-staged engine registers its own strategy and reuses every event kind
The base builds and tests exactly one path — add a growth stage to an existing town — at M4 (G-P13), because it is the same path "regenerate this area" uses

The clock — weeks (item 76, with item 67's Works; owner: "our simulator advances by units of one week"): "our simulator" is the clock that changes the map's inputs — the host's (SettlementForge's) or the staged evolution engine's — never @plat/sim's time view key, which changes nothing (§10.3; J-A76.41)

(1) The week: the map's time is an integer week; for a dossier-bound map SettlementForge's calendar.elapsedWeeks (no conversion; never elapsedMonths, never history.age); creation week the port's HostContext.week (§14) or 0; a standalone map starts at week 0; EpochInputs.week the absolute week at the epoch, years derived from it; a standalone grow call giving years only takes the previous week + round(52 × years) and re-derives years from whole weeks (one clock); a dossier event carries its week in dossierChange.week (§7.1, item 75); the document's current week is derived — the week of the last folded event carrying one — never a stored counter (§2.9); each epoch's week is its EpochRecord's

(2) Dating a dossier change: the port (§14) dates each change it finds by the first rung giving a week: an explicit tick on the change's receipt (foundedAt.tick; lifecycle institutionHistory[].tick; populationHistory[].tick; activeConditions[].triggeredAt.tick; campaign-era historicalEvents[].tick; decrees[].tickRef; calamityHistory[].tick; previousGovernments[].tick; a news tick; the provenance ledger's tick), then the week suffix of the change's outcome id, then HostContext.week, then none: a change with no week applies finished with no Works (§7.7 item 1 reads these rungs; the port counts an undated change in its report)

(3) The season — one calendar (J-A76.42): CalendarRow gives the week of the year (week mod 52) + 1 and its season: a dossier-bound map reads row sf445 (52 weeks; four seasons of 13 weeks from spring; month ends at weeks 4, 8, 13, 17, 21, 26, 30, 34, 39, 43, 47, 52), a standalone map our own default row shaped alike (month ends 4, 9, 13, 17, 22, 26, 30, 35, 39, 43, 48, 52); Works' pauses, §8.2's season rows for a campaign week and the module read it; no second calendar exists (tables/dossier/calendar, §14)

(4) The cadence: the port folds a dossier's discrete changes as standalone dossier events at their weeks, in SettlementForge's order (decrees first), and an epoch at each 52-week boundary crossed — or sooner, when the dossier's population has moved from the last epoch's populationTarget by more than the roster tolerance ± 5 % (J-A76.43; the one number §7.7 item 3's lapse reads too) — carrying the target, circumstance slices, event kinds and that week's dossier events in EpochInputs.dossier; a catch-up batch follows the same rule, gaps allowed; no epoch folded per tick (Works stages derived from the week at any drawing); a standalone map's epochs are its circumstance timeline's (§7.7, dated in weeks) or a user's grow calls

(5) Rates per year (J-A76.45): every chance stated per unit of time is per year, applied over an epoch's span as 1 − (1 − p)^years through dmath (§6.5 (3)); dwell bands and ladder durations in years read as weeks ÷ 52; churn caps scale by years — so epochs a few weeks apart and one a decade long change the town at the same rate; II.6's island slots follow the same rule

interface CalendarRow {id: 'sf445' (dossier's) | 'plat-default' (ours); weeksPerYear: 52; seasons: {season: spring|summer|autumn|winter; fromWeek (week of year, 1-based)}[]; monthEnds: number[] (twelve week-of-year ends)}

The rung at an epoch (item 81 (b); J-A81.41): at each epoch the rung profile is read at the epoch's populationTarget (§1.1's ladder): a crossing of one of §1.1's bands changes the rung's row — its granularity, greenery, layer and budget rows — for everything the epoch builds from then on; standing fabric survives exactly as it survives a growth stage (§6.3)

Frame growth at an epoch (J-A81.31): a crossing upward whose town the frame no longer holds grows the frame to the one §3.2 (9) gives the new target: S1 derives terrain, water and the hinterland's ground on the ring between the old margin and its successor (same terrain field continued; each water body continued across the old margin with inner reaches fixed); the kernel grows the frame by §3.2 (9)'s single-level batches over one clear region — an L1 batch clearing finer content of whole L1 faces beside a lapsing stretch of the old chains or under the new rectangle, an L0 batch replacing the margin chain, an L1 batch replacing the border chain — each raster growing by whole cells, every stored height unchanged, flow fields recomputed over the grown grid; then S4 continues every through-road from its old end to the new margin, S12a sites the hinterland on the ring; the stages owning the cleared faces re-derive them (hinterland unit for the hinterland's; a district's S8–S12b for a district's; on each underground part §3.2 (9) grows, that part's stages for its cleared faces — part 0's network stage its bands by corridorUnion (II.7.2), II.7.3's stage its plots, each other system's stage (catacomb, cavern, quarry, vaults) its own part's bands (II.7.6), II.7.5's stage the undercity's plots; on the buried and dug parts, which no stage re-derives at an epoch, their cleared bands re-laid from kept gallery chains by corridorUnion (§3.7), drawing nothing); every face outside the region, off a deleted stretch and off the ring keeps its ring, owner and nested faces; the frame never shrinks (a declining town keeps its frame and hinterland)

II.6's island gate is one reader of the rung; a dossier outside the ladder — below 1 500, or above the 120 000 cap — is refused by the port (§7.7 item 15, item 81; §1.1; J-A81.01) and never reaches an epoch, so §3.2 (9)'s clamp of the frame's target at the cap serves only growth that carries no dossier

The dials' inputs over epochs (items 72, 78, 79): at each epoch, before S6 re-evaluates the drivers, a power's applied standing (PowerStanding.appliedStanding, §7.7 layer 2) moves to the epoch's standing, and a sector's applied share to the epoch's share, only when they differ by more than dial.hysteresis (0.05, a dial-table row); both are folds over the epochs' slices in log order, so a replay reproduces them and §4.5 (6)'s dials follow the dossier's powers and economy without flickering

Uses across epochs (item 17): a use (shop, workshop, inn, institution) is its own record (Use, §2.7), separate from the buildings that house it: a building references its current use or none (vacant) and keeps formerUses, so a use can close in one building and open in another while the building persists; the base builds the hand path: openUse on a vacant plot or building (the building mutates to the designation by §4.7 S11's operator), closeUse (building stays vacant — first state of the decline hooks — or converts to a named designation), relocateUse (a closeUse here and an openUse there under one event, detail.from and to on the use's lifecycle event §2.8; swapUse is two relocations) and mutate (§4.7 S11) — each with its undo record (§7.4) and reported to a host (§11.3)

The staged engine's use step runs at each epoch after the roster's delta demand and before siting, as the same events: (1) re-score — for every use §4.7 S10b's solver scores its present plot and the best alternative within its catchment (the district and neighbours, serviceRadiusM of §10.2's useRules) against the current field, distribution and supply graph; (2) inertia — a use moves only when the alternative beats the present plot by more than the row's inertia and the row's moveChance draw falls (use.relocate concern on the use's …/epoch=e stream, §6.1); closes only when its catchment's demand (households within its radius against the roster's ratio) has been below closeShare for closeAfterEpochs, or a hard supply edge had no provider in reach for starveAfterEpochs; a dossier-backed use never closes by this rule; new demand opens uses where the solver scores best; (3) cap — at most the churn cap's share of a district's uses relocates per epoch; (4) assignments — a host or owner assignment moves with its use unless pinned (§7.7, item 20 (g)), then it stays and the town adapts; every change reported; (5) traces — a vacated building keeps its former use in formerUses, which a later opening prefers (former inn reopens as an inn first; a dossier element whose assignment returns to active reopens in its former building first, repaired by a Works when dated — item 80) and the naming engine may read (§10.4); (6) concealed uses relocate by these rules like any use, front stays an ordinary business; uses visited in address order; households and postings follow (§10.3)

The epoch-spread mutation (item 18 (c)): across epochs a designation change is issued as a sequence of mutate events over the ladder's rung durations (item 31) — first occupy when the present design is compatible (every kept part, nothing added), then adapt, then extend (the adds), and rebuild only parts that cannot be adapted — same steps and draws spread in time; each event decides and records its step at once (§4.7 S11 step 6) and a Works shows it over the weeks it takes (J-A67.49); the model never changes between events

Dossier content across epochs (item 20; J-A20.75, J-A20.43): no step of an epoch closes a dossier-backed use (assignment existence 'dossier', §7.7 item 2) or leaves one without a building; only a dossier event at step (e) removes, adds or re-designates one; the use step never closes one: where its catchment or supply fails the use relocates to (1)'s best alternative by the solver's dossier request (first closest option where no plot passes the hard rows, J-A20.71) or, where its catchment holds no candidate plot, stays in its building; its moves by (2)'s inertia rule are any use's

Before any other step would empty or remove the building housing an unpinned dossier-backed use — a redevelopment's purchase, step (c)'s vacate, the decline lottery's strike, the growth step's declared demolish or corridor re-cut, a carve, wallToWay's clearance, contractWall, a terrain-and-water repair, fallIsland, a tunnel's closing (II.7.3) or a passage's sealing — the use is first relocated the same way inside the epoch, a relocateUse citing the epoch and counted outside the use cap, the request's scope its catchment less the plots that step empties or removes, widened to the town where that scope holds no candidate plot; a pinned one keeps its building, which the step treats as any pinned entity (§7.2); so the dossier element is live and placed at every step (§5.3's row); a dossier-listed ruin (Assignment.state ruined, §7.7, item 80) is present as its ruin — its use closed, its building ruined — and no step repairs or clears it but a dossier event; a reopening returns its use to its former building first

UseConversionOp = openUse {plot, to: Designation, building?, assignment?} | closeUse {use, leave: vacant|convert, to?: Designation} | relocateUse {use, to (destination plot: a closeUse here and an openUse there under one event)} | mutate {plot, to: Designation, spread?: now|epochs (§4.7 S11's operator; epochs issues steps over the ladder's durations)}; joins ConversionOp

Decline and regrowth (owner 2026-09-25; AM-8): regression is growth read the other way: the population target falls, the roster's manifest shrinks by its suffix (§10.2), the fabric the suffix leaves steps down a ladder of states over epochs — never re-rolled, never removed by arithmetic — until regrowth reoccupies it; steps scheduled by the owner's staged engine (DEF-8); the base carries now, stated once: ladders, decline table with exposure function, salvage ledger, lag rule, regrowth-first siting order (binds the built grow-by-stage path today) and conversion kinds, each applicable by hand (§7.1) and undoable (§7.4); states §2.8's, style classes §8.2's; §6.3 identity rules, §13.2 hook tests, §16 price at M4

The ladders (§2.8 Existence in brackets; every step one conversion, a lifecycle event with its cause): Buildings — occupied → vacant (abandoned: use left, fabric stands) → derelict (decayed: roofless, RoofSpec.kind 'none') → ruin (ruined: walls part-standing, the ruin program) → robbed or cleared (cleared: a footprint trace, material in the ledger) → reused (reused: the trace drawn as the garden, orchard or field it became — Building.reusedAs §2.6 — or a successor building on the old foundations taking the trace's address, §6.3); upward steps at every rung (reoccupy, repair, rebuild, reuse), regrowth uses them first · Walls and gates — in use → neglected (abandoned) → breached or partly dismantled (decayed; gap a StretchRef) → superseded by a shorter inner ring: contractWall traces and builds the new ring inside the old one through S5a's trace step and S7's operator, old ring's record live with Enceinte.supersededBy naming the new one, its line a trace — or becomes the ring road by wallToWay · Tunnels (II.6's condition table) and the underground's galleries and chambers at the same persistence rate (II.7.5, II.7.6; item 65): in use → neglected, silted (abandoned) → partly caved in (decayed) → collapsed or sealed (ruined; Tunnel.closure), never demolished by the engine · Islands (II.6): floating → waning → settled → fallen · Plots — a plot whose last building is cleared or reused merges into a garden, orchard or field (plotToGarden) or its occupied neighbour (amalgamate; §4.7 S10), the plan coarsening where people are few; fields their own layer: a struck farmstead's fields stay worked, LandUse.owner passing to the nearest farmstead or the commons

Decline table (DeclineTable in @plat/tables: editable, versioned rule table with provenance, §7.6; our own rows, calibratable §13.9; rows are tendencies — weights and chance, no fixed order, AM-23): persistence rate per fabric layer use 1.0 · building 0.6 · plotBoundary 0.3 · street 0.08 · wall 0.05 · underground 0.03 · terrainWater 0.005; exposure drivers — kernels over the context vector (§2.5) with weights, §4.5's construction: extramural + ; terrainClass low, damp or flood + ; downwind + ; near noxious kernels of field pass 2 + ; intramural periphery (dist.wall small inside the enceinte, dist.centre and dist.market large) + ; low prosperity + ; resilient core (dist.market and dist.plaza small; attractors at churches, precinct, castle) −; chance share 0.25 of the exposure field (prosperity field's 0.15); dwell bands (years; each drawn once as its step's decay Works duration) vacant → derelict [10, 30]; derelict → ruin [20, 60]; ruin → cleared on salvage demand only; walls one band slower, tunnels two; haul radius 250 m; exemptions: a locked or pinned entity never struck; an assigned entity only through the use-relocation rule (AM-17); the building of a dossier-backed use only after that use is relocated

Strike lottery (the engine's step; the exposure function and table are the base's): for an epoch whose target lies below the manifest, the suffix leaves in reverse ordinal order as step (c) states (relet down while households remain, vacate at the last household; J-A28.45); which standing fabric steps down is drawn without replacement from a lottery over candidates whose dwell band has run (for a building, whose decay Works has run its span; J-A67.46) with weight w = E(x)·rate(layer)·u: E(x) = clamp(Σ_j v_j·kernel_j(x) + ε_E(x), 0, 1) the exposure field computed per epoch on §4.5's 32 m cells from current context vectors and prosperity field with its chance share; rate the layer's persistence row; u a draw from epoch.transform keyed by entity lineage and epoch (§6.1; no new concern); bounded by the churn cap per district per epoch; a weighted tendency, not a law (J-A8.41)

Salvage — the material ledger: robStone, clear, dismantle and demolish credit the town's MaterialLedger (§2.7) by the building's class-table yield (salvageM3 per material, §10.2); build, rebuild, reuse … build and a repair (reoccupy from derelict) debit it by the new class's row from sources within the haul radius; a flow record, never a hard constraint: a debit it cannot cover is built anyway and the shortfall reported (J-A8.45); the lottery's weight for robStone and clear is multiplied by the salvage demand within the haul radius (standing debits of planned building, repairs and a new stage's footprints), so cleared zones appear beside active building and a ruin beyond any demand is left standing

Lag and memory: built extent follows population with a lag on the way down and none on the way up: a fall's households leave at once (step (c)) and standing stock decays by the dwell bands over later epochs; a rise met in the epoch it arrives by the regrowth-first order without a dwell (J-A8.47); memory is the persistence order itself: plot, street, wall lines and traces outlast buildings, so the old plan is there for regrowth to refill

Regrowth-first — built now on the one path: in grow-by-stage S2's delta demand placed in this order, only the residual grows a stage: (0) standing shells whose household count fell below what their occupants' band row houses relet up within §2.6's capacity (relet; J-A28.45); (1) vacant buildings reoccupied (reoccupy); (2) derelict ones repaired (reoccupy, ledger debit); (3) ruins and cleared traces rebuilt or reused on their foundations (rebuild, reuse … build); (4) vacant plots of the old plan beyond the band's vacancy-run share (S10 (8) keeps the share; design's own runs never filled below it); (5) plots S10 cuts on faces the old plan left unbuilt along its street lines inside the last boundary; (6) new faces of a new stage — where Features.sewers is on, the underground crowding hook first sends crowdingShare of the residual's poorest-band households underground (II.7.3 (c), II.7.4, §4.5 S7b (6)); S5a grows the boundary for the residual only; an epoch whose residual ≤ 0 grows no stage and adds no face; S7b allocates the delta first to (0)–(5) as each district's old-plan capacity, only the remainder to new faces (replacing the rule that an epoch placed delta only on new or transformed plots; J-A8.44)
Regrowth-first test: §13.2's T8-2 (M4)

The prosperity field under decline: drivers re-evaluated per epoch (§4.5); under decline the market, harbour and main-street kernels shrink with their activity (§7.7's circumstance slice), and where plots merge the density field falls, so the field contracts toward the survivors' core and may concentrate there — the ladder's amalgamations its footprint on the plan

Islands and the underground over epochs (laws II.6's): each epoch re-reads the rung from its population target and re-evaluates II.6's supply law: an island whose supported area shrinks past the hysteresis is resized (rim plots cleared with lifecycle events, cause convert:resizeIsland); one whose supply falls to zero — or whose settlement has left the CITY band (AM-13) — wanes, settles after its dwell band and falls: fallIsland archives its arena and lays a ruin decoration face (§2.7) over its projected outline on the ground through the carve path's clear-region protocol, every entity under it demolished with that cause; regrowth re-floats a settled island before it raises a new one (J-A10.42); a tunnel silts, caves in and is sealed by the same lottery at the underground's rate, never demolished by the engine (J-A11.41), reopened before a new one is dug

Identity and determinism (decline): a vacant, derelict, ruined, cleared or reused building is a live record with its address and lineage (§6.3); it becomes a tombstone only by demolish or when a reuse … build successor takes its address (supersede, §2.8) (J-A8.42); every draw comes from epoch.transform or, for islands, island.place, keyed by lineage and epoch, so same seed + same timeline → same history of decline and regrowth (§6.2, §7.7)
Emulation note: neither reference has time; with no epoch the static baseline is unchanged byte for byte (§13.3's goldens), every rate a table value (AM-23)

DeclineOp = vacate|reoccupy {building} (occupied ⇄ vacant; reoccupy from derelict a repair: roof restored, ledger debited) | reuse {building, as: garden|orchard|field | {build: BuildingClass}} (Building.reusedAs or a successor on old foundations, Building.predecessor §2.6) | neglect|breach|dismantle {enceinte, stretch?} (old line persists as a trace; contractWall and wallToWay supersede a ring) | silt|caveIn|seal|reopen|flood {element: tunnel, gallery or chamber (II.6's condition table); flood only on a gallery or chamber whose floor lies below the water table; stretch?} (a stretch splits the record first; no engine plan contains demolish on a tunnel; J-A65.48) | resizeIsland {island, areaHa, elevationCm} (outline re-drawn by §4.2's routine from the island's own stream; rim plots cleared or new rim faces grown by the grow path on the island's arena) | settleIsland|fallIsland|refloatIsland {island} (waning → settled (elevation at the floor of its band, districts declined) → fallen (arena archived, ruin face on the ground); a settled island re-floats first) | raiseIsland {allocation} (regrowth: a new island for a sky allocation the count law opened, placed by SkyStrategy, II.6)

Terrain and water change slowly (item 25; engine owner-staged, kinds and hand path the base's): reclamation, silting and river-course shifts are conversions on the one list, the slowest layer of the persistence order, never immutable, applied by hand through §7.1's convert event and in the staged engine drawn at the decline table's terrainWater rate by their own trigger rows; each a typed operation whose repair is an operator the base already has (J-A25.41)

TerrainWaterOp = reclaim {kind: marsh|foreshore, region} (marsh: LandUse faces of kind marsh or a damp or flood band re-typed as land; foreshore: a shallow water margin filled) | siltReach {water, stretch?} (width and depth profiles fall by the row's share; a basin below the harbour's draught loses its harbour use) | shiftCourse {water, from, to} (control-knot ordinals §2.3; the reach between re-traced — a meander cut-off or avulsion) | digCanal {polygon} (the carve, kind canal)

Terrain/water repair: reclaim runs S1's terrain operator (§7.3 (a)) — region raised to the flood line plus the row's margin (reclaim.raiseCm 60), drained by a ditch water body and its LandUse faces re-typed with reclaimed set, as §2.3 states — and for a foreshore S1's water operator (§7.3 (b)) with the filled margin as new shore; siltReach and shiftCourse are S1's water operator on the changed reach (width and depth profiles, shores as buffer, crossings re-sited, kept ways re-routed, F-RIVER's re-trace confined to the reach, §7.3 (b) 1–2), so their footprint, fates and locality are the carve's and byte identity holds outside it; digCanal is carve; every touched entity's lifecycle records the cause (convert:reclaim …); record changes are §2.3's

Terrain/water trigger rows (the engine's step; rows the decline table's terrainWater rows, §7.6): candidates and chance per year — applied over the epoch's span as 1 − (1 − p)^years (J-A76.45) — each × the layer's persistence rate (0.005), drawn from epoch.transform keyed by the water body's or face's lineage and epoch (§6.1; J-A25.42): siltReach — a reach whose accumulation has fallen or a basin whose harbour use closed, 0.02/yr; reclaim — a marsh or foreshore face beside built land whose band's plot demand is short (S5d's shortfall record) and whose district's band is modest or above, 0.03/yr; shiftCourse — a reach whose sinuosity exceeds river.cutoffSinuosity (1.8) or whose flood cells beside it exceed the row's share, 0.01/yr; digCanal only by demand (a canal row of the roster's institutions, a dossier element or a user's edit); each fires at most once per body per epoch; AM-23 tendency; emulation: neither reference has time; MFCG's warp and FTG's water drawing kept as §7.1's edits; nothing runs without an epoch

Hidden plots over epochs (item 30 (e)): a passage can be sealed — sealPassage sets Passage.sealed (§2.5), so the access edges on its face read as sealed; every plot whose only reach passes it takes exposure sealed (§4.6) and its buildings enter the decline ladder as vacant (vacate, cause convert:sealPassage) — and later reopened (openPassage: exposure returns to hidden, buildings reoccupy by the regrowth-first order); both hand edits in the base and the engine's kinds later; hidden plots arise by densification (densify … back_court, rung 2) and vanish by thin … back_court (item 31)
HiddenOp = {op: sealPassage | openPassage; passage: Id (the L3 passage face, §2.5)}; the last kinds of this section the union admits (… | TerrainWaterOp | HiddenOp)

Works (1) decided at once, shown over weeks (item 67; J-A67.41): every physical change (build, extension, demolition, repair, conversion, decay step, clearance) is decided and recorded by the event that makes it (mutator record, conversion, ladder or decline op; §4.7 S11 step 6, J-A67.49), so the log alone determines the model; when that event carries a week (an epoch, a dated dossier change §7.7 item 1, a hand edit scheduled by startWorks §7.1) and works.enabled holds, the event also creates a Works record (§2.7): kind, target (a building, whose added or subtracted wings and storeys are the parts of the MutationRecord its cause.mutation names; or the plots of a join or split — Works.target), start week, duration in working weeks, WorksTable row read, the event and mutation it shows, and what the ground held before that the model no longer holds (removed parts' rings with heights and roof kinds; removed plot lines with treatments); the drawn state at any week derived, never stored per week; an event with no week, an unscheduled hand edit, generation (creation week shows a finished town; J-A67.47) and the parity presets create no Works; a user's build, demolish or convert stays instant unless scheduled; an engine's demolish makes its tombstone at once while its Works draws the demolition from the kept shell; aborting a change is its undo (§7.4), which removes its Works; cancelWorks (§7.1) ends a running Works at once (change stands, drawn finished); a setAttr on a Works moves its start or duration

Works (2) stage at a week: stageAt(works, w): e = the working weeks in [start, w) — weeks the calendar row does not pause for the Works' material in the town's climate (WorksTable.pauses: masonry, stone and brick pause in winter in temperate and cold climates; our own rows) — f = min(1, e ÷ duration); the stage is the kind's latest scheduled stage whose start fraction ≤ f, before for w before the start and finished at f = 1; weeks integers (a stage shorter than a week never drawn); a tent's zero-week duration applies finished in its week; at most one Works runs on a target: a new change on it ends the running one at the stage reached, which the new one takes as its before (a repair begun on a decaying house runs back from DECAYING)

Works (3) durations (item 67 (b); J-A67.43): WorksTable rows keyed by kind × class (or the template's works key §10.2) × size (storeys, footprint) × material give a range of working weeks; duration drawn once uniform in the range × the labour factor of the plot's band (richer, faster), on the works concern (key §6.1; J-A67.61; J-A67.42); defaults (own, calibratable §13.9): hovel or shed 1–2 weeks; small timber house 2–6; town house 8–17; stone house 17–52; manor 52–156; church 520 or more; a cathedral built part by part (choir, transept, nave, towers, each its own Works in programme order; choir in use under a temporary roof while the nave rises); demolition a quarter of its build's range; clearance 1–4; a decay Works the decline table's dwell band for its step × 0.6 for timber and thatch; material a duration row only — time, never shape (§2.6; J-A31.42 stands for replaceability)

Works (4) stages (item 67 (c)–(f)); start fractions per class row; what each draws is §8.2's states rows: build (and each wing or storey an extension or adaptation adds) — STAKED 0 · GROUND BROKEN 0.05 · FOUNDATIONS 0.15 · WALLS RISING 0.25 · ROOF FRAMED 0.75 · ROOFED 0.85 · FINISHED 1; extension — kept building in use throughout; added wing through build stages; at ROOF FRAMED old roof opened where the two join; at FINISHED joint wall opened and wings united; demolition — EMPTIED 0 · STRIPPED 0.2 · ROOFLESS SHELL 0.4 · RUBBLE 0.7 · CLEARED 1; decay (§2.8's ruin ladder downward) — toward decayed: ABANDONED 0 · DECAYING 0.5; then decayed is ROOFLESS, ruined COLLAPSED, cleared or reused OVERGROWN; repair — decay stages backwards under a scaffold to the former state; fire — an instant destructive event (rung 3's trigger): building decayed in its week, drawn CHARRED until a clearance or repair starts; conversion with no geometry step — REFIT 0 · FINISHED 1; ruin stages are the existing ladder's drawn stages (J-A8.46; no new Existence value); target keeps its ladder state from the event on and carries its running Works by Building.works (§2.6)

Works (5) decay Works carries the dwell band (J-A67.46): a vacate (building abandoned) starts a decay Works toward decayed whose duration is its dwell band drawn once; the lottery's decay candidates are buildings whose decay Works has run its span; the strike's decay event (building decayed) starts the next toward ruined the same way; a reoccupy ends it and starts a repair; a building left abandoned or decayed by an undated event (hand edit) gets its decay Works from the next epoch, starting at that epoch's week

Works (6) mutation steps (J-A67.49): a Works shows its event's MutationRecord in the record's order — subtracted parts by the demolition stages first, then adapted parts, then added parts by the build stages — each part's span a share of the duration by its footprint area; kept parts stand; a rebuild is a demolition then a build, one Works; the epoch-spread mutation's events each start their own

Works (7) plots in transition (item 67 (g); J-A67.44): a join or split decided when its event lands (plot rings change then — ownership) and the ground follows the work: each removed boundary line drawn from the Works' kept lines, dashed as pending removal, until the joined plot's build reaches GROUND BROKEN (or a demolition reaches RUBBLE); a new dividing line drawn as stakes, dashed, from STAKED and as its fence or wall from WALLS RISING; item 31's subdivide and amalgamate run through the same stages; access is the event's, so a Works never leaves a plot without access

Works (8) what reads the stage: heights at a stage derived, heightsAt(works, w): WALLS RISING raises the eave storey by storey (eave × storeys reached ÷ floors), no roof before ROOF FRAMED (drawn as a framed roof), finished roof from ROOFED, a demolition lowering them in reverse; stored heights stay the finished building's, so §8.4's shadows and §11.1's 3-D export follow the stage; households an event placed are housed at a week only from FINISHED, and a demolition's have left before EMPTIED (item 17's relocation, J-A17.41): the module's occupancy, lit windows (§10.3) and light sources (§4.7, §8.4) read that; the plan rung of a building in progress draws walls without doors or furniture, of a ruin its fallen walls and open rooms (§2.6); the stage counts among the plan rung's recorded inputs, so a stage change marks a derived plan stale and §8.5's change marker shows it (item 67 (j)); descriptions say "being built", "being demolished", "ruined since …" (§10.4); the city band draws the stage glyph on the footprint, the neighbourhood band walls, scaffolds, frames and rubble (§8.5, §8.2)

Works (9) which week is drawn (J-A67.45): every drawing, export and reader draws the document's current week unless the per-viewer view key week (§2.9) names another — a host setting its campaign week, or a user scrubbing — outside every digest; scrubbing draws every live Works and every Works finished within works.retainWeeks (52) at that week over the current model, forward and back, byte for byte; the full history at an earlier week is the log's replay (§7.4); an epoch retires Works finished more than works.retainWeeks before its week: the record leaves the model, its target's lifecycle event keeps the weeks

Works (10) restraint (item 67 (i); J-A67.48): an epoch's Works start at weeks spread uniformly over its span (the offset the works concern's draw before the duration's, §6.1), so the share of stock under works follows the growth or decline rate by construction; a ConditionOverlay (§2.7; staged, empty in the base; item 88) scales the share of an epoch's changes it starts as Works once the port fills it (a siege stops building); with no epoch and no scheduled edit nothing runs; static baseline byte-identical (item 23)

type WorksStage = before|staked|groundBroken|foundations|wallsRising|roofFramed|roofed|finished | emptied|stripped|rooflessShell|rubble|cleared | abandoned|decaying|roofless|collapsed|overgrown | charred|refit

interface WorksRow {key (class id or template's works key §10.2); kind: build|extend|demolish|repair|convert|decay|clear; storeys?: [n, n]; footprintM2?: [n, n]; material? (duration row only; never a shape input); weeks?: [n, n] (working weeks drawn once; absent on a decay row, whose span is the decline table's dwell band × 52); factor? (decay row's material factor: timber and thatch 0.6); stages: {stage: WorksStage; from: fraction}[]}; interface WorksTable {rows; labour: {band; factor}[]; pauses: {material; climate; seasons[]}[]; retainWeeks: 52; enabled: boolean (false in the parity presets)}; WorksTable lives in @plat/tables (works.json, §14), editable with provenance (§7.6); its decay rows read the decline table's dwell bands, never a second number
