interface UndergroundStrategy {derive(doc, tunnels: Tunnel[], allocation: Allocation (the underground pseudo-district's, S7b (6)), rules: UndergroundRule, ctx, k): KernelResult<{blocks; plots; buildings; access: AccessPoint[]}>} — a Stage registered after the network stage by declared I/O (inputs under.tunnels, the ground plat (read), the fields, the underground Allocation; outputs under.blocks, under.plots, under.buildings, under.access); runs S9 → S10 → S10b → S11 on the underground arena with the underground context; the StrategyRegistry's underground map (§14)

The base's part for the staged row (Staged by the owner's roadmap): RungProfile.layers.sewers and Features.sewers with S0's draw, and Features.underground; the underground LayerSpec hidden by default; the class table's drain, underground, undercity, undergroundAccess and concealment columns and the cover table (§10.2); Tunnel.navigable, Tunnel.headroomCm and the profile table with its wall thickness; the AccessPoint record with its state and knowledge; ContextVector.arena; UndergroundRule's depth scale, vacancy share, crowding share, arrangement restriction and access row; the undercity's existence row and rule (II.7.5); the system rows, link rule and raiseGrade kind (II.7.6); the records UndergroundSystem, Gallery, Chamber and UndergroundLink and the district's parent and outskirts links (§2.5, §2.7), schema-complete and empty; the UndergroundStrategy, UndercityStrategy, UndergroundSystemStrategy and UndergroundLinkStrategy registration slots; the U1–U3 invariants, F-UNDER's ladder row, §5.3's rows for accesses, concealed modes and the undercity, and §13.2's hook tests (T12, T63–T66); the closure rule with addUndergroundAccess (§7.3 item 9, §7.1), whose underground pieces run once the stages exist; staged and not built here: the network, sewer-front neighbourhoods, void systems, undercity and connection stage

II.7.5 plain words: an undercity is not more dwellings along the sewer walls but a place with a void big enough to live in, its own square and streets, its own institutions, and lifelines to the surface; one to three neighbourhoods at most, each the underside of a real quarter above, peopled by the settlement's own poorest and outlawed, trading the town's goods — a shadow of the settlement, never a second one

Existence test (item 65 (b); J-A65.41), four conditions each a rule with values in UndercityRule (own, calibratable, extension): (1) a void large enough to live in — chambers from a source that explains them (II.7.6): a cavern hall, a quarry's gallery system, a catacomb, cisterns and vaults, or a buried old town (the settlement's earlier street level under a raised grade, II.7.6's raiseGrade); a void's capacity = floor area of one connected cluster of its chambers and galleries ÷ m2PerHousehold (40 m² with its walkways); (2) its own public space and streets — a chamber ≥ mainChamberM2 (400 m²) as plaza and black market, and galleries or walkways joining its chambers, independent of the sewer's water channel; (3) its own institutions — ≥ minInstitutions (2) institutions of undercity 'preferred' classes placed (black market first, a fence's hall, a criminal guild's seat, a tavern, a forbidden shrine, a fighting pit, a healer), beside its warren of dwellings; (4) lifelines to the surface — food, water and air: ≥ 1 access to the surface (a stair, a basement access of II.7.3 or a link to a system that has one), one air shaft surfacing at a well, grate, chimney or ruin (AccessPoint role air), water from the river, a cistern or a well; and a route outside where the site offers one (an outfall, a cave mouth beyond the walls); a neighbourhood failing any steps down the ladder; II.7.3's sewer-front dwellings along the tunnels leading in are its outskirts, its core the void

Existence and the 1–3 bound (item 65 (c); owner quote; J-A65.41): one rule: an undercity exists in cities and metropolises, and in a large town only where a void source exists — rarely; never below TOWN; rung row RungProfile.layers.undercity (§1.1; UndercityExistenceRow) reads never at THORP, HAMLET, VILLAGE (PART III); law at TOWN with maxNeighbourhoods 1, minPopulation 6 000 (the large town) and chance 0.2 (rare: one draw on sewer); law at CITY with 2; law at METROPOLIS with 3; under law it exists when (i) the rung admits it (and at TOWN its draw comes up), (ii) a void source with capacity for one neighbourhood exists or is predicted, (iii) its household demand H reaches minHouseholds (20) and (iv) conditions 2–4 can be met; where the dossier port supplies the fact (optional input, §7.7) a dossier may require one — then it exists at TOWN and above with at least one neighbourhood, in the vaults under the oldest district where no other void is found — or forbid one; the dossier's word outranks the rule; never more than three neighbourhoods; sewer-front dwellings elsewhere are not part of it and do not count against the bound

Size law: H = min(N × u × (P ÷ P_ref) × (1 + g × disorder) × c, maxBandShare × N_poor) — N the settlement's households; u the undercity share at the reference poverty by rung (TOWN 0.01, CITY 0.02, METROPOLIS 0.03); P the poverty share (households in squalid and poor bands, §4.5), P_ref 0.022 the default roster's; disorder the circumstance slice's scalar in [0, 1] (§7.7 layer 2; 0 where absent), gain g 1; c §4.6's undercity factor 1 + crime.undercityScale × PortRows.crime (item 88; 1 while empty); N_poor the households of those two bands, maxBandShare 0.6 (surface keeps poor households of its own); H households taken from the squalid band first, then poor; joined by the roster's undercity 'preferred' institutions at their table counts and the clandestine institutions whose mode is underground (§4.7)

Neighbourhood count n = clamp(⌈H ÷ householdsPerNeighbourhood⌉, 1, maxNeighbourhoods) (120 households), none when H < minHouseholds; the void's capacity caps both (n falls first, then H); at the default roster and the navigable preset a city holds one neighbourhood and a metropolis two, a poorer or more disordered one up to the bound

Realism or toggle (D-3; J-A65.43): under the sewer's historical preset (realism, the default) the undercity is a modest warren: at most one neighbourhood at any rung, void sources vaults, catacombs, quarries and a buried old town only, shares u × 0.5; the full microcosm with the 1 / 1–2 / ≤ 3 bound and cavern towns rides on the navigable preset (D-3's fantasy toggle)

The allocation (S7b (7), §4.5): where an undercity exists — predicted at S7b, when every void source is predictable: caverns from S1's geology flag, catacombs from the religious rows and their sources' ages, quarries from the stone resource and the roster's predicted stone stock, vaults from the arterials and bridges S4 laid, a buried town from the log or at generation from the history scar II.7.6 reads — S7b creates its Allocation after (6) and before (1): H households (squalid first, then poor), the undercity 'preferred' classes, and the clandestine institutions whose mode is underground (preferring the undercity over a sewer dwelling where both exist); capped by the predicted capacity; ground districts receive the remainder (population whole — nobody added by the underground, c′ (1)); a miss between prediction and built voids absorbed by S10b's plan–fit–reconcile and F-SITING's ladder, reported, never re-rolled

A shadow, not a second city (item 65 (c′); owner quote; J-A65.44): (1) its people and institutions are the settlement's own (the dossier's where one exists); population totals include them; (2) each neighbourhood shadows a surface district: a pseudo-district (District.kind = 'undercity', §2.5) in its void's part, with a parent link to the surface district above the largest share of its main chamber in plan (ties by address) — the district that feeds it; joins §9.1's quarter tree under its parent's quarter node, named as the underside of that quarter by §10.4's undercity naming (J-A65.40), never a rival town; prosperity = the parent's field sampled at each plot shifted by undercityOffset (−0.35), banded by the town's FieldBands (II.7.3's pattern); (3) its economy is the surface's shadow: black market trades the town's goods; S10b's supply edges run to the surface markets, docks and outfalls, measured from each undercity plot along its walkways to its nearest lifeline and on from the lifeline's ground point (the solver's street mode through the lifeline); (4) nothing of its own to govern it — no government, walls, gates, rung or identity of its own; settlement circumstances (disorder, crime, government) drive it; (5) it changes as the settlement changes: at each epoch its size law re-read, a change taking effect only past hysteresis (0.1 of H), a new neighbourhood opening only in its void's free capacity; its blocks follow their parent's due marks through §4.11's wealth ladder (item 31); chambers and galleries flood, collapse or are sealed by II.6's condition table, a chamber's plots following it as II.7.3's follow their tunnel; clearUndercity (the authorities' clearance, by an epoch or by hand) vacates one neighbourhood's plots — households leaving by §4.11's step (c), institutions relocating by the use step — while its chambers stay

Where it lives (item 65 (e); J-A65.44): an undercity neighbourhood lives in the arena part of its void source (a cavern, quarry, catacomb, vaults or buried-town part, II.7.6) — never in the sewer's part 0 (U1–U3 hold there), never in a part of its own (its chambers are its source's; nothing copied between parts, J-A12.43; J-A65.31); the undercity stage runs S9–S11 on that part by the kernel's one cut (J-A65.32): its streets are gallery chains of its own — walkways laid across a chamber's floor and the source's galleries it adopts — banded by corridorUnion; a chamber's floor cut by S10's frontage-first machinery on those walkways' kerbs and on the chamber wall (plots may end on the chamber_wall); the main chamber stays unplotted as its plaza, the black market's stalls its pins (§4.7's market pins); S11 admits row, hovel, cluster (item 70) and institution (UndercityRule.arrangements), carved rooms and repurposed vaults being row cells against the chamber wall; heights ceiling-capped: eaveCm = min(class storey height × floors, chamber's ceilingCm − ceilingClearCm (30)), one floor or more where the ceiling allows, roof kind flat, no sky; every district, plot and building an ordinary record on its part, editable by every edit kind of §7

Its outskirts: the sewer-front blocks of II.7.3 whose tunnel runs lead into the undercity — within outskirtsReachM (150 m) along open tunnels from a link that joins it — belong to its neighbourhoods: each undercity district lists them (District.outskirts §2.5), a link between records in two parts (J-A65.31); their plots, geometry and allocation stay part 0's under U1–U3, and they are named, described and counted with the neighbourhood

Lifelines: the connection stage (II.7.6) realises the undercity's lifelines before any lottery: the nearest candidate access, air shaft and water link are made (open, or secret by the row) first; a neighbourhood left without one fails condition 4 and is dropped, its allocation re-placed by the reconcile, and with none left there is no undercity — each drop reported

Undercity light (item 68 (d′); owner quote: a lot of light sources, no sun or moon): the underground layer has no global light and near-zero ambient; the undercity's rows of §4.7's light table (LightRule, arena underground, system undercity) are the densest of the layer — a light at every door (windows lit by §8.4's derived window lights), along walkways (gallery rows, arena underground) at a spacing tighter than any surface street, clustered in the market chamber and around its institutions, braziers and fire pits in the larger chambers — the fuel by the settlement's circumstances (tallow and pitch, lamp oil; magical lights only where the magic circumstance admits them); every lifeline breaking the surface is a light shaft (§8.4), so its brightest spots at noon lie under its shafts
Undercity emulation (item 65 (f)): no reference generator has an underground: every row here is an extension; the parity presets set maxNeighbourhoods to 0

Undercity order, seed and locality: UndercityStrategy registers after the void systems and the sewer-front neighbourhoods and before the connection stage, by declared I/O — inputs the void systems' parts, the ground plat (read), the three field rasters, the undercity Allocation and the rows; outputs its districts, blocks, plots, buildings and walkways — runs eagerly on the generation worker after the pool's merge (J-A12.46); existence and size draws on sewer keyed by the settlement's lineage; each neighbourhood's streams derive from its district's lineage, itself from its parent's (§6.3), through ordinary concerns (plot.*, siting, siteplan, heights; §6.1); writes only its void's part, so a New random of an undercity neighbourhood leaves the ground and every other part byte-identical, but for the far link_end vertices of its links, which the connection stage re-derives by one transaction on each such part (§3.4)
interface UndercityExistenceRow {existence: never|law; maxNeighbourhoods: 0|1|2|3; minPopulation?; chance? (TOWN 0.2)} — RungProfile.layers.undercity (§1.1)

interface UndercityRule (one editable rule record §7.6; own, calibratable, extension; parity presets maxNeighbourhoods 0) {share: Partial<Record<Rung, number>> (u: TOWN 0.01, CITY 0.02, METROPOLIS 0.03); povertyRef 0.022; maxBandShare 0.6; disorderGain 1; householdsPerNeighbourhood 120; minHouseholds 20; m2PerHousehold 40; mainChamberM2 400; minInstitutions 2; undercityOffset −0.35; ceilingClearCm 30; outskirtsReachM 150; hysteresis 0.1 of H; arrangements default [row, hovel, cluster, institution]; presets: Record<historical|navigable, {maxNeighbourhoods (a cap on the rung row: 1 and 3); sources: UndergroundSystem['kind'][] (historical: vaults, catacomb, quarry, buried; navigable: all); shareScale (0.5 and 1)}>}

interface ClearUndercity {op: 'clearUndercity'; district: Id (one undercity neighbourhood)} — a conversion kind (§4.11's union names it): its plots vacated, households leaving by step (c), institutions relocating by the use step; chambers kept

interface UndercityStrategy {derive(doc, systems: UndergroundSystem[], allocation: Allocation (S7b (7)'s), rules: UndercityRule, ctx, k): KernelResult<{districts; blocks; plots; buildings; walkways: Gallery[]}>} — a Stage registered after the void systems and II.7.3's stage by declared I/O; runs S9 → S10 → S10b → S11 on each neighbourhood's void part; the StrategyRegistry's underground map (§14)

One layer, several systems (item 65 (a); J-A65.31, J-A65.42): the underground layer holds the derived sewer network (system kind sewer, part 0) and beside it systems each an UndergroundSystem record (§2.7) with kind, source, arena part and depth range: catacomb, cavern, quarry (quarries and mine voids), vaults (cisterns, street and bridge vaults), buried (a buried old town), dug (private passages an access edit or an undercity lifeline's closure digs, item 66); each its own arena part of the underground layer (§3.4): sewer keeps part 0, every further system takes the next unused part number when first created — at generation in the stage order, one system per kind; a buried system when a raiseGrade first makes one or at generation from a history scar; a dug system at the first closure needing one (§7.3 item 9 (d)) — stored on the record (UndergroundSystem.part), counted by the document's nextUndergroundPart (§2.9), never renumbered or reused (the number is part of its entities' keys and addresses, §6.3)

One system per kind: two catacomb complexes that meet join, as galleries of one kind may; what passes over or under without meeting belongs to another kind and so another part; inside one part every plan crossing is a junction (§3.4), so no rule lays an element across another of its part without meeting it: a catacomb or quarry laid beside a complex of its kind joins it at a common depth band; a dug connector's path search treats every other building's dug passage as a foundation (step 3); a drawn gallery or chamber that would cross one of its system's at another depth band is refused by its dry run naming the crossing (F-EDIT, §5.2; J-A65.47)

System elements: galleries (Gallery §2.7: a chain at the part's L1 with widthCm, wallCm, headroomCm from its system row, banded by corridorUnion as a tunnel is, §3.7) and chambers (Chamber §2.7: a void wider than a band — ossuary, cavern hall, quarry room, cistern — a closed outline chain carrying the chamber_wall role, its floor an L1 face; J-A65.32), each with its floor elevationCm and its ceilingCm

Depth bands: every gallery and chamber keeps its own depth inside its system row's depthM range (catacombs 3–10 m, vaults 3–8 m, quarries 10–30 m, caverns 5–60 m following the rock, a buried town at its old grade, dug passages 2.5–6 m) and never above the ground less its system's coverM; inside one part depth is per entity (J-A12.45); systems in different parts pass over and under one another; the view groups every part's items into the depth bands of depthBandCm (II.7.3), so the layer draws and exports as one (§8.4, §11.1), a crossing of two parts drawn over and under

The derivations: each system is a registered stage with declared I/O (§4.12; UndergroundSystemStrategy) running after the network stage in the order catacombs, caverns, quarries, vaults — then at generation a buried old town where a history scar makes one — each reading the ground and part 0 through the services only (J-A12.32) and writing its own part; every draw on sewer keyed by the system's lineage and the element's source (§6.1; no new concern); every system gated to TOWN and above (PART III) and by its row's chance per rung — a history scar's buried town by the buried row's scarSeverity instead, drawing nothing; the chances 0 and the scar rule off in the parity presets

Catacombs: from cemeteries' and churchyards' sources: churchyard parts of church and temple plots (§4.9 churchyard row), crypted classes (underground 'preferred': crypts, §10.2) and religious precincts and monasteries; a source qualifies when its ground is not damp or flood (water table of §2.6's gate values) and its age reaches minAgeYears (100) — at generation (K − k + 1) × yearsPerStage for a source built in growth stage k of K (§4.4; yearsPerStage 50, §4.2 S2), replaced by the staged HistoryHint.ageYears when the port fills it (item 88) and by the log's years since its use opened after epochs — and holds a catacomb with the row's chance by source kind and rung (crypted church 0.6; churchyard 0.25 at TOWN, 0.4 at CITY, 0.5 at METROPOLIS; precinct 0.4)

Catacomb extent = ossuary need A = Σ_years servedPopulation × burialRate ÷ 1 000 × ossuaryShare × m2PerBurial — population its source serves (town's population history × the source's share of its religion's temples, §10.2; at generation each growth stage's population at its built share), burialRate 30 per 1 000 a year, ossuaryShare 0.1, m2PerBurial 0.05 — laid as galleries on a grid of gridM (6 m) under and beside the source within reachM (80 m), an ossuary chamber at every fourth crossing, and an entrance stair from the source's building (an AccessPoint of source system); a catacomb as large as its town's dead and as old as its church

Caverns: from geology: where S1's geology flag (Terrain.geology, §2.3) is soluble or volcanic, over the frame's rock (S1's rock, high and mid terrain classes), a cavern system exists with the row's chance (soluble 0.7, volcanic 0.4); soluble rock: galleries along the terrain's drainage lines beneath the rock (§2.3 hydro cells whose flowAccum passes the row's threshold) at the local water table — a gallery below it carries water (Gallery.water) — with a hall where two galleries meet under high relief; volcanic rock: one to three tubes descending from high ground along steepest descent with breakdown chambers; extent capped at maxRockShare (0.1) of the rock area; a gallery meeting a slope's face or a bank opens there as a cave mouth (AccessPoint kind mouth)

Quarries and mine voids: from S1's stone resource and the town's stone stock: volume taken = the wall volume of the stock whose material is stone (§2.6's material rule read as a quantity of stone, never a shape; J-A65.45) and of the enceinte's walls and towers × wasteFactor (1.6); workings laid on the frame's stone cells (SiteResources.stone ≥ 0.5) ranked by stone value, then nearness to the town, within reachM (2 km), under the town first where its own ground holds the stone (as the old quarries under Paris), as room-and-pillar galleries on a roomM (5 m) grid leaving pillarShare (0.35) of the rock; area = volume ÷ headroomCm (250); a working whose cover would be under minCoverM (6 m) is left to the hinterland's surface quarry (§4.9) and laid nowhere underground; a shaft opens at each working's centre (AccessPoint kind shaft); mine voids read SiteResources.ore the same way, only where the roster holds a mining class

Vaults: cisterns and street and bridge vaults: under every bridge approach whose way rises over the ground beyond the banks, under way segments on slopes steeper than vaultSlope (0.12) where a street is carried on arches, and a cistern under the oldest precincts and the castle where dist.water exceeds cisternDistM (400 m) — each a chamber or a short run of vaults under its way or precinct, under public ground only (II.7.3's surface constraint applies)

A buried old town (item 65 ruling 5; J-A65.46): the conversion kind raiseGrade (§4.11's union names it) applied by an epoch (staged engine) or by hand (convert, §7.1): S1's terrain operator raises the region's ground by raiseCm (≥ 200 cm, a storey); the region's ways, plots and buildings at the old grade end on the ground (existence cleared, §2.8) and fresh records of the buried part are the system's elements — each old way's centreline a gallery, each old building's ground storey a chamber, each new record a fresh entity of the buried part minted from the conversion event's seq and ordinal (§6.3), the cleared records keeping their addresses on the ground (an address names its part; no batch writes two, §3.4) — while the ground above is re-derived on the new grade from the old centrelines (regrowth-first §4.11: streets keep their lines, buildings rise on their plots); the conversion records the system it created or extended in RaiseGrade.system, so a replay after a log truncation reads its part number there, as a closure's ClosureRecord.created does (§2.9); an undercity in it walks the old town's streets under the new

Buried town at generation: none exists unless the port fills the staged HistoryHint (item 88) with a fire or flood scar (the RaiseGrade.cause types §4.2 S2 routes here) of severity ≥ the buried row's scarSeverity (0.5): the most severe such scar (ties: the oldest, by yearsAgo) makes one buried system, in the systems' stage order after vaults, gated to TOWN and above — its region the districts whose growthStage is 1 (its sources, §2.7), its galleries that region's way centrelines and its chambers their buildings' ground storeys, fresh records of the buried part (system's lineage children, §6.3), floors laid at scarBaseCm + scarGainCm × severity (200 + 200 × severity) cm below the present grade; the town above generated on the present grade as it stands, no raiseGrade event recorded, nothing cleared, the rule draws nothing (our own rows, calibratable, extension the parity presets turn off); with the hint empty, none

The connection graph (item 65 (d); J-A65.47): a link (UndergroundLink §2.7) joins two elements of different parts — each end one vertex in its part carrying the link_end role (§2.2 rule 7), never a vertex two parts share (J-A65.31) — with a kind (open, gated, secret, collapsed, flooded), a via (breach, stair, shaft, door) and a knownTo; surface links are AccessPoints (II.7.4); the connection stage (UndergroundLinkStrategy) runs last, after the undercity: (1) the undercity's lifelines (II.7.5) first; (2) for every pair of elements of different systems within linkReachM (10 m) in plan and linkDepthM (8 m) in depth — found by reads across parts — one link per pair within linkSpacingM (60 m), existing with the row's chance for the pair of kinds (sewer–vaults 0.6, catacomb–quarry 0.5, any–buried 0.5, sewer–catacomb 0.3, sewer–quarry 0.3, cavern–quarry 0.3, sewer–cavern 0.2, others 0.2; our own); (3) its kind drawn by the row's weights (open 0.3, gated 0.25, secret 0.25, collapsed 0.15, flooded 0.05 — flooded only below the water table); (4) its knownTo secret for a secret link or a link into a building with a concealed use, else local; (5) II.7.3's basement accesses (item 64); a link's kind follows the elements it joins (II.6); every link an edit target (add, delete, setAttr on kind and knownTo, §7.1)

The same engine (item 65 (e)): every system laid by the kernel's one cut (J-A65.32): galleries as chains banded by corridorUnion, chambers as closed outline chains; plots and buildings exist only where a system hosts people — the sewer's frontage (II.7.3) and the undercity (II.7.5); a catacomb's, cavern's, quarry's or vault's chambers carry none unless the undercity takes them; every element an edit target (draw, move, delete, setAttr on kind, depth, width, state and knownTo; II.6's conversions and flood); every rule a data row (§7.6); the seed survives edits (§6.3); the dossier stays the authority for institutions (item 20); every element fades by II.6's condition table

Underground systems' light (item 68 (d′)): catacombs dark but for shrine and ossuary lamps at the chamber altars; caverns dark but where lived in (a glowing-fungus row only where the magic circumstance or the biome allows); quarries and vaults dark but at their shafts and where lived in — §4.7's light table, arena underground and the system kind; every access or cave mouth breaking the surface a light shaft (§8.4)

The pieces an access edit generates (item 66; owner quote; the closure rule — one event whose batches commit together, the record of what it created, exact undo, shared pieces kept — is §7.3 item 9's; J-A66.41): addUndergroundAccess(building, target?) (§7.1) calls generators in dependency order at its dry run, each drawing on sewer keyed by the building's lineage, the target's and the event's seq (§6.1; minted as J-A18.43 mints), so the same edit on the same seed gives the same pieces: (1) the basement — §2.6's basement decision with its probability forced (the request overrides the chance, never the terrain gate): a full cellar where the gate allows, else a half cellar or walk-out on a slope, else a hatch to a crawl space under a raised floor (§2.6's requested-mode ladder), else a refusal naming the gate (F-EDIT §5.2), never silent (J-A29.22); (2) the target — the named element, else the most plausible reachable: an open navigable sewer tunnel or an underground building's wall within accessReachM, then within digReachM (60 m) the nearest open gallery or chamber of a catacomb, cavern, quarry or vaults, or an undercity walkway — ties by plan distance then address

(3) The connector — when the target lies beyond accessReachM: a dug passage, a gallery chain in the dug system's part, routed by the kernel's path search (§3.1) on the frame's grid from the basement ring to the target — cost infinite within foundationClearM (0.5 m) of every other building's footprint, basement ring and dug passage and wherever the water table (§2.6's gate values) lies above the passage's floor, rising with the rock class — inside the dug row's depth range, below the street's services (network coverCm, II.7.2) and above the water table; a route longer than 2 × digReachM is a refusal with the reason

(4) The system itself — where no underground element lies within digReachM (a town without sewers, a village): the minimal private underground, the dug system with one passage to the most plausible outlet by the building's outlet row (default: another cellar of the same owner within reach, a catacomb or cave the site has, the riverbank, the shore, beyond the outermost enceinte; with a concealed use: beyond the walls, the riverbank, the shore, a catacomb or cave) — its outer end an AccessPoint of kind mouth, or a door into the other cellar; the settlement's sewer rows unchanged (a dug passage is no network, Features.sewers untouched) while Features.underground turns true (II.7.4); (5) the access point — II.7.4's record, its kind by the drop (II.7.3 Basement accesses (3)), state open, knownTo by (4), source edit; (6) the plan — the plan rung reserves the stair, ladder or hatch in the basement plan (§2.6, item 28), building's plan rung marked stale; (7) the links — the connection graph gains the new links, typed (open at a dug passage's two ends)

The closure's other instances (§7.3 item 9 (d)) declare their own generators: a concealed front's missing door by §2.6's entrance rules (§4.7 Concealed institutions (4)); an undercity neighbourhood's missing lifeline by the target, connector, access-point and link steps above (II.7.5), run from that neighbourhood's district ring in place of a basement ring, its target the nearest element of another system with an access to the surface (II.7.5 condition 4), keyed by that district's lineage; bars §13.2's T66 group

interface UndergroundSystemRow (one per system kind; own values, extension; every chance 0 in the parity presets) {kind: catacomb|cavern|quarry|vaults|buried|dug; chance: Partial<Record<Rung, Record<sourceKind, number>>> (absent: none; buried row's generation-time town reads scarSeverity instead; never below TOWN); depthM: [n, n]; coverM; gallery {widthCm; wallCm; headroomCm} (kerb reads widthCm ÷ 2 + wallCm, §3.7); chamber {minM2; ceilingCm}; params: Record<string, number> (minAgeYears, burialRate, ossuaryShare, m2PerBurial, gridM, reachM; maxRockShare; wasteFactor, roomM, pillarShare, minCoverM; vaultSlope, cisternDistM; scarSeverity, scarBaseCm, scarGainCm; digReachM, foundationClearM); outlets?: {use: default|concealed; order: (cellar|void|riverbank|shore|beyondWalls)[]}[] (dug only)}
interface LinkRule {linkReachM 10; linkDepthM 8; linkSpacingM 60; chance: Record<sorted pair of system kinds, number>; kinds: Record<UndergroundLink['kind'], number> (kind weights)}

interface RaiseGrade {op: 'raiseGrade'; region: Id[] (blocks or districts raised); raiseCm ≥ 200; cause: fire|flood|rebuild|hand; system?: Id (buried system created or extended, written when applied; its address's under<n>/ prefix carries the part number a replay reads, §2.9)} — a conversion kind (§4.11's union names it)

interface UndergroundSystemStrategy {derive(doc, row: UndergroundSystemRow, ctx, k): KernelResult<{system: UndergroundSystem; galleries: Gallery[]; chambers: Chamber[]; access: AccessPoint[]}>}; interface UndergroundLinkStrategy {link(doc, rule: LinkRule, access: UndergroundRule['access'], ctx, k): KernelResult<{links: UndergroundLink[]; access: AccessPoint[]}>}; stages registered after the network stage by declared I/O (§4.12): the systems in the order catacomb, cavern, quarry, vaults and, at generation, a history scar's buried system, each writing its own part; then II.7.3's and II.7.5's stages; then the connection stage last, writing link records and access points and no geometry but their link_end and access_point vertices, one part per transaction; the StrategyRegistry's underground map (§14)

PART III plain words: the village generator is a separate product staged after the town, with its own ladder (thorp → hamlet → village); this page lists what it would take from the base, the hooks the base carries now, and confirms nothing stands in its way; the base does not pay for it

What the village would reuse unchanged: the kernel and plat (§2–§3); the site model — descent-traced rivers with a carved field, level-set ponds, the coast routine (§4.2) — and, for VG's own order, a RiverStrategy that lays a terrain-independent spline course first (VG's live course runs through 6–7 control points laid before its terrain; COV-VG-WC2) and asks S1 to carve the field to it, which S1's carve step already does; the sequential roster and lazy people (§10); the frontage-first plot machinery and the designation templates (§4.7 S11, §10.2), which already contain cottage, farmstead and detached-in-yard classes; the hinterland presets incl. the VG sector look, orchards and commons (§4.9); the palisade enceinte kind (§2.7); the display list, style sheets, the base's relief tier (hillshade, contour, hachure marks) and the reserved painterly preset slot (§8.2); the document, edits, exports and the API (§7, §11)

Village hook (1) (DEF-15): a density stage before its network (COV-VG-VN-002): the pipeline is the topological order of declared stage I/O (§4.1, §4.12), so a VillageStrategy registers a density StageDecl whose output the network stage declares as an input; VG computes its density before its roads, and the base's S6 order does not bind it

Village hook (2): a palisade before its roads (MN-4, COV-VG-VN-003): on VG 1.6.9 the palisade is built before the roads — the hull of the populated points of a 10 × 10 lattice over the density field, cleaned and smoothed — and the road trackers consult it at every step (steering: a per-type terrain weight plus terms for water, the destination's pull and the wall's push — reader-tier, for the village rung's calibration; provenance row D5, item 61), gates falling where they meet it (profile-village.md N2, P1); the village registers an EnceinteStrategy that builds exactly that from its density stage, and its tracker-steered NetworkStrategy receives the result through the enceintes input every network strategy takes (§4.12)
Village hook (3): a tracker-steered network (VG's roads are steered trackers, not A*) with one through-road and partial driveways, and a "houses along ways" FabricStrategy with no block cutting

Village hook (4) One district (COV-VG-WC4): a village is modelled as one district of kind village (one quarter) covering the settlement; its blocks are the large faces between ways and its plots line the ways, so the containment invariant building ⊂ plot ⊂ block ⊂ district holds unchanged and nothing in §2–§4 needs a village exception

Village hook (5) a size ladder below TOWN: rung rows THORP ≈ 20–80, HAMLET ≈ 80–400, VILLAGE ≈ 400 up to (not including) 1 500 inhabitants (our own rows, calibratable; VG spans ≈ 130–1 700); a request of 1 500 or more is a base TOWN and below 1 500 LadderRouter routes to the village product (§1.1, D-33); a village request's default is not a walled circle (walls a rule keyed on rung); VG's independent tree stream is a keyed sub-stream (already the design); VG's spotlight vignette and grass-tuft look are painterly programs — the hillshade, contour and hachure marks are the base's relief tier (§8.2), built at M2b (§16), so the village adds none (COV-VG-VN-029)

Not-precluded checks (the parity judge's 44/44): the strategy registry admits every strategy above; the level model tolerates nearly empty L2/L3; model time is near-linear in building count; every VG rendering row has a program or a preset slot; terrain-and-water-as-one-picture is the base's own model; what the base does not pay for: tracker steering, the palisade construction, VG's spotlight and painterly look, the palisade look, VG's grammar and its tag vocabulary

Placement and designation (items 16–19): the village reuses the one placement solver with the relation templates and supply edges, the designation templates and mutator (§4.7 S10b, S11; §10.2), whose rows already carry the village classes — cottage, farmstead, mill, smithy, chapel, inn — and the Use record with its relocation path (§2.7, §4.11); a village adds rows, not code

Village rung rows (items 24–27, 30): hidden-share target 0 and reach weights of open only (§4.6; VG's and MFCG's every-house-on-a-way); a market row of min 0 with at most one market — a green or a widened street, sited by §4.2 S3 (12)'s score with the plaza kind absent; farm mode fill (§4.9); band set's cuts computed per village from its own roster shares over its one district (§4.5); §4.11's terrain and water conversions apply unchanged; a concealed institution at a village rung takes the front mode (hidden share 0, no sewer: its fallback chain ends at a front — a working business on an ordinary plot); each is a table row a village supplies, not code

Layers at the village rungs (AM-13): the village ladder's RungProfile rows carry layers.islands = 'none' (§1.1), so II.6's island rule admits no island below TOWN whatever the prosperity or model setting; a village request never creates a sky allocation

No sewers below TOWN (item 14; II.7.1): the village rung rows carry layers.sewers.existence = 'never': a village registers neither the network stage nor the underground stage; a request's toggles.sewers is reported as not applicable in requestedVsBuilt; drainage is gutters and pits — the class table's drain column is read by nothing there

No derived underground below TOWN (items 65, 66; II.7.5, II.7.6): village rows carry layers.undercity.existence = 'never' and derive no catacomb, cavern, quarry, vaults or buried-town system (every II.7.6 system row gated to TOWN and above), so a village's underground layer is empty unless a user asks for an access: addUndergroundAccess (§7.3 item 9's closure, item 66) digs a private passage of kind dug from the building's basement to the most plausible outlet (II.7.6) — the one underground a village can hold, making the layer present without a network (sewers stay never); nothing in II.7 stands in a village's way: every hook is a rung row or a field it leaves empty

A dossier below the town floor (item 81; owner's ruling J80 Q3): a dossier whose population lies below 1 500 is refused by the port (§7.7, item 81: E_RUNG_UNAVAILABLE, naming the village product) while no village product is registered — the dossier's population is a dossier fact and a clamped town would contradict it — so a village-sized SettlementForge settlement waits for the village product's own port path, which registers its rung rows behind the same port (§14) rather than a second one; §1.1's clamp to a 1 500-person TOWN stays for a request that carries no dossier
LodBand = city | district | neighbourhood | building: the four drawing bands; declared in @plat/model so labels and render share it (N-22).
MarkKind = area | ribbon | outline | hatch | glyph | text | instances | shadow | field | shore | light (11 kinds).

MarkTable: one row per mark, every column a typed array (transferable slices); columns kind(1 B), semantic(2), entity(4, interned session-local handle, never hashed), key(8, render key), layer(1)+z(4), lodMask(1), pass(1), group(4, district handle), bbox(16, world cm), geomStart+geomLen(8), revision(4, low 32 bits of §6.2 leaf digest); fixed columns 54 B per mark; named attrs columns 4 B per mark each (heightCm, baseCm, eaveCm, ridgeCm, prosperity, class, block, bankKind, waterKind, exposure, knownTo, concealed, worksStage, worksKind, material, tintKey, ...).
MarkTable.entity is the interned handle: session-local, routes deltas, hit-tests and edits, and is never hashed.
lodMask has one bit per LodBand in which the mark exists; geometry never changes with the band.
pass: 0 fills, 1 casings, 2 bodies, 3 linework and symbols, 4 overlay — the order within a slot.
group = district handle: unit of delivery and invalidation, never of raster caching.
revision column = low 32 bits of the entity §6.2 leaf digest (its inputs content revision): the cache key (LC-23).
GeomTable { rings: Uint32Array ring-start offsets into coords; coords: Int32Array x,y cm pairs }.
FieldRaster { id, originX, originY, cellCm, cols, rows, values Float32|Int16, meaning heightCm | shoreDistanceCm | depthCm | custom }.
StringTable { utf8 blob, offsets }: names and species kinds as one transferable UTF-8 blob.

LabelTable: one row per LabelEntity drawn at the band, all S13b reads, <= 97 B per row plus geometry and text; columns mark, key (2 per row), kind, lodMask, priority, areaM2 (order second key), text, shortText (~0 = none), spines (2 per row, preference order), anchors, breakAt, parent (QuarterNode label row, ~0 at root), pinStop (-1 = not pinned), pinSizePx, pinAnchor, pinSpine, pinSeq (PinnedPlacement.seq: order of the pin pass), knownTo (0 public, 1 local, 2 secret; read by the knowledge filter only), hidden, revision.
LabelTable.knownTo (0 public, 1 local, 2 secret) is filled and read by §9.2 knowledge filter and by nothing else.

InstanceTable: one row per instances mark (§8.10), <= 40 B per row: mark, layout (stamp|grid|line), offset (2, cm), rotationCdeg, spacingCm, species range, overrides range; speciesRows {kind (StringTable row), inner, outer, leafType} <= 16 B per row; overrideRows {ordinal (2), op, x, y, style (2, InstanceStyle), state byOrdinal|rematched|orphaned} <= 32 B per row.

LightTable: one row per light mark (§8.4; item 68), <= 36 B per row: mark, x, y (world cm), zCm (host ground + LightSource.heightCm), intensityCd, radiusCm (§8.4 cutoff), sizeCm (penumbra radius), colour 0xRRGGBB, flags (bit0 fire else magic, bit1 flicker, bit2 lit at drawn week and state, bit3 downward shaft, bit4 underground).

DisplayList { marks, geom, rasters, semantics, strings, labels, instances, lights, salts (Record<RerollableConcern, number>, §6.1 effective salts, type generated from the concern registry), layers: LayerSpec[], bounds, version, surfaceTopCm }.

DisplayList.surfaceTopCm = greatest elevation above Terrain.datumCm that a caster of the city band list writes into the surface layer, a pyramid or the slab list (slab top: island, span mark, deck); it is §8.4 (c) Z, the reach of the global light window; S14 derives it on the city band list; a delta raises it, a full build re-derives it; every other list (finer band, export transient) carries that value, never its own (J-A68.93).
DisplayDelta { version, groups, removed (entity handles), marks, geom, strings, labels, instances, lights, dirty: Box[], surfaceTopCm? (present when the delta raises it) }.

DisplayListBuilder (S14; generation worker, read-only model): build(model, band, groups?) -> DisplayList for full build (generation, load) or one band for named districts (on-demand bands §8.9); update(model, changed handles, band) -> DisplayDelta for edits, scoped regeneration, override resolution (§8.10).

Display list built by S14 from the model through the entity registry (type -> marks per band); backends never read the model; footprint geometry identical in every band (O12 a; O17 i); only marks emitted and programs run change.
field marks carry a world-space raster (terrain height for hillshade and contours, distance to shore for water ramps and foam, depth); cost nothing when no program reads them (VIS-12).

shore marks: chains, one per maximal run of equal attributes along a water face boundary: bankKind (§2.3), waterKind, exposure, shoreClass (bay/headland/straight, §2.3; read by shore programs per-class rows).

exposure = sheltered where the segment bounds a harbour basin, moat, canal or pond or its fetch (longest straight run across water within +/-30 deg of outward normal) < 300 m; river on river and tributary faces; else open (VIS-13).

instances marks carry a face or chain and one InstanceTable row (offset, rotation, spacing drawn by S14 from the entity render.instances stream, species mix, resolved overrides); points generated at raster time (§8.10), never stored.

text marks carry one LabelTable row each so S13b needs only the display list (N-4) — except a room label, set by the plan draw inside its room (building band only), read by S13b only as a protected obstacle (§8.5, §9.2; J-A28.85).

light marks carry one LightTable row: a placed LightSource (§2.7) position, height, intensity, radius, colour, flicker, or a derived light (live-layer window, plan-draw room light, shaft); only the light pass reads them; nothing else draws them but the vector rung glow sprite (§8.2).
A building eaveCm and ridgeCm columns (its wing's, for a wing mark; §2.6) let the surface layer (§8.4) rebuild each roof face elevation from the roof construction without the model.

The city band carries every caster (item 68; J-A68.93): every caster of §8.4 Shadow casters has a city-band mark — a tree line instances mark with an empty city-band rank subset; each base wing of a multi-wing building a caster mark with its Heights drawn by no program; a one-wing building casts by its footprint mark; caster marks of every composition wings and towers and every close-up casters the elaboration cache holds (§2.9, §8.6), added in the DisplayDelta answering the band request, removed with the cache entry, included in every full build, a composed building replacing its base wings; ring blocks (§8.8) and surfaceTopCm read them from the one list the tile worker holds.

Draw order is slot-major across the whole scene (N-7): every mark of slot s draws before any of slot s+1 in every tile; within a slot by pass, then z, then key; slot from (semantic, pass) by §8.2 slot resolution, cached per style version as a (semantic index, pass) -> slot table.

S14 emits one mark per pass an entity draws in, as the registry declares per band: a cased ribbon = pass-1 casing + pass-2 body over one geometry range (~60 B for the second mark, never a second geometry copy; a few thousand extra marks at CITY).
The raised under-copy (slot 11) and projected-shadow union (slot 10) are not marks but per-tile operations over the caster marks, placed by derived entries (§8.2).

Way casings (slot 5) and way bodies (slot 6) are separate slots holding every way class, so every casing precedes every body across the scene (GEO-28); masses, fields, woods and shadows keep their slots after the roads (K16, NG shadow order, MFCG wards after roads). Rasters cached per world-aligned tile (§8.8).

Incremental update: after an edit or scoped regeneration the builder gets the changed handles (§7.3 locality closure) and emits a DisplayDelta: removed marks; new marks for changed entities and dependants (a way when a junction moved; a district ground mark when a block changed); their label and instance rows; dirty boxes = old and new bboxes dilated by the largest cross-tile effect (§8.8). Cost O(changed marks). During a replay the builder is suppressed and runs once at the end (§7.3 item 2; SCL-9).

Cache keys (LC-23): every derived artefact (roof geometry, label spine, footprint mass, instance set, tile raster, glyph run) keyed by (entity key or tile address, content revision, band, style version, roof construction where it applies), never by id alone.

Every render-time hash (multi-colour role index, weathering, stamp tile variant, grid jitter, crown index, colour and scale jitter, hatch phase, roof detail, ruin dash) = RH32(tag, key, salt[, ordinal or cell][, style id]): tag from a fixed render-tag table; render key = low 64 bits (words 0 and 1) of the entity key (§6.1) cached beside the lineage hash; the concern salt (§6.1); style id only for looks (colours, crowns, hatch), never positions; RH32 folds words through MurmurHash3 32-bit finaliser, distinct from §13.6 H32, never reads the interned handle.
Render-tag table: fixed table of tags indexing RH32 calls. (Not enumerated anywhere in §8.)
Render key: low 64 bits (words 0,1) of the entity key; stored in MarkTable.key and LabelTable.key.

Entity key is a pure function of model data, so an unchanged model renders pixel-identically after reload (§6.2) and golden PNGs hold (§13.3); a render rule ordering entities (tint colouring §8.2) uses address order (§6.3).

Display-list size (N-9 c): 54 B/mark fixed + 4 B/mark per attribute column + label, instance tables and geometry; CITY city band ~60 000 marks ~3.2 MB fixed, ~2.4 MB attrs, ~4 MB coords, <= 0.5 MB label/instance/string rows = ~10 MB; undrawn caster marks +54 B each plus coords, slab list 16 B/record + 8 B/outline vertex, both counted on B-CITY at M2b; light rows <= 36 B per light (~0.3 MB for 8 000 lights, PLAUSIBLE until §4.7 light table runs on B-CITY).

The tile worker holds the only full copy; after each transfer the generation worker keeps only entity, bbox, group (24 B/mark, ~1.4 MB at CITY) and the city band surfaceTopCm, which every list it builds for an export carries (§11.1).

An export that draws (SVG, PNG, print, .dd2vtt image) builds its own transient list in the generation worker: SVG writes from it there; a raster export transfers it to the tile worker with its request; each releases it when done (§8.9, §11.1).

Display list built at the drawn week (document current week or per-viewer key week, §2.9; §4.11): S14 writes worksStage from stageAt(works,w), worksKind from the running Works kind (WorksRow.kind), height columns from heightsAt; emits stage marks (dashed footprint, pit, walls without roof, scaffold ring, rubble; §8.2 states) and pending/staked plot lines; on a drawn-week change (clock, view.set {week}, scrub) the generation worker re-emits only marks of targets whose stage or heights differ and lights whose lit bit changes (O(changed Works)); no digest moves (§6.2).
owner_raw: rendering (S14 writing rule); which week is drawn: pipeline §4.11

statement: A mark of a concealed part (concealed room, concealed entrance tick, concealed access point or link down; item 63; §2.6, II.7.4) carries concealed = 1 and the concealed use knownTo; raster draws it only for a viewer whose knowledge key admits that use at the band (§9.2; key joins the tile key §8.8); building mass and public parts carry the building own knownTo and always draw.

A light draws only where its host draws (items 63 (c), 64, 68; J-A63.82): a light mark carries its host mark concealed and knownTo; lights of concealed rooms, lit windows of one, LightSources hosted by a concealed part, AccessPoint or UndergroundLink (II.7.4, II.7.6) and such an access shaft (§8.4 (b)) are taken by the light pass, light-map bake, vector glow and every export lights only where the host draws under the viewer knowledge key; that key joins the tile key and the light-map key (§8.8).

StyleSheet { id, version, family ink|lit|hatched|painterly|graphic, palette Record<Role, Color|Color[]>, symbols (semantic -> band -> Symbolisation), order Record<LodBand, OrderSlot[]>, programs (semantic -> band -> PaintProgram[]), roofConstruction plain|skeletonHip|skeletonGable|fakeGablePerWing (over stored wings §2.6), labels LabelStyle (§9.4), light LightingSpec (§8.4; item 68), raised {on, offsetM, minPx, maxPx, ratio rows}, overrides ThematicRow[], states StateRow[], post PostOp[], budgets Record<LodBand, DetailBudget>, referenceBackend canvas2d }.

StyleSheet.family includes 'graphic', a family named by the type but defined by no preset row or other text of §8 (the presets table lists ink, lit, hatched, parchment/bw-print/night variants, painterly).
StyleSheet.budgets: a DetailBudget per band (type named; its fields are not declared in §8).
Symbolisation { mode model|paper; k (drawn = k x model width); minPx; maxPx; px (paper width at 1x) }.

OrderSlot { slot (row of layer-order table; entries may share a row); semantic (exact or dotted prefix x.*); passes? (absent = every pass); derived? raised|shadow (per-tile raised under-copy or projected-shadow union over the matched marks); reason; recordedAs? (reference step, order parity §8.3) }.

StateRow { kind building|wall|gate|tunnel|island|passage|plotLine|access|gallery|chamber|link; state (Existence value §2.8, Building.condition §2.6, SkyIsland.state §2.7, 'superseded' when Enceinte.supersededBy set, 'sealed' when Passage.sealed set, a WorksStage §4.11 winning over the ladder state while the Works runs, 'pendingRemoval'/'staked' plot lines, AccessPoint.state II.7.4, gallery/chamber system kind + state II.7.6, UndergroundLink.kind II.7.6); worksKind? (matches only a target whose running Works is of that kind, laid as override over the stage row; J-A67.83); bands? (absent = every band the kind is drawn at); paint replace|override; programs }.

Roles (23): paper, road (= paper in ink), ground, court, garden, green, tree, field, verge, water, building, roof, wall, ink, label, shadow, ambience, light, sand, plank, grid, snow, lights. A role never changes meaning across bands or presets of one family; MFCG 13, NG 26, VG 40 reference keys map onto it without loss.

Light roles (item 68): shadow = vector-rung shadow tone (ink at family alpha); ambience = vector-rung night wash and two-tone roof dark mix; light = lit window/light mark glyph tone; lights = vector-rung glow sprite. On rungs 1-2 of §8.4 ladder the light pass computes light over the albedo instead.

Every family carries @night role variants (keyed like tree@autumn), read by the vector rung when the view is night; rungs 1-2 light the day albedo, so a family night look is its day palette under night light.

Contrast matrix (O12 f), pairs that must separate where both drawn (city band unless noted), dE2000 / dL*: road/ground 6/5; ground/building 12/12; road/building 15/15; garden/building, green/building 10; tree/water 10; green/road, tree/green 8; water/road, water/ground 8; wall/water 20; field/road, field/ground 4; court/road 4 (district+); court/ground 3 (district+); ink/road, ink/ground, ink/paper 40/50 (label floor §9.4); ink/building 30/40; ink/tree 25/30.

Contrast checked on every palette when loaded (built-in, user-edited, random) and on rendered city-band images in B-ZOOM (mean CIELAB of pixels whose top mark from the pick buffer has each role, every pair in view); a failing user edit is shown with the failing pair and kept only with an explicit accept-low-contrast flag recorded in the report; MFCG default garden=building (dE 0.6) and tree=water (0.0) are not copied (VIS-2).

Random style (N-26): each role L* within +/-12 of the family shipped value, chroma [0,34] in ink and [0,60] otherwise, any hue, road = paper kept where tied; a style-time draw from stream style.random (§6.1) written into the setStyle event as row operations so replay never re-draws.

Bounded repair: take the first failing pair in matrix row order; raise lighter role L* by 1 (up to 97) or, if at 97, lower darker L* by 1 (down to 3); re-check every pair; stop when all pass or after 100 steps; must pass after sRGB conversion; failed draw redrawn (attempts 0-2); after three failures the family shipped palette is used and the report says so; <= 300 steps (J-R30).

Measured on 2 000 seeded draws per family (amendc_rendering_palette.out): 9-27 % pass as drawn, 96-97 % after the first repair (median 4-12 steps, p95 16-39), 100 % within three attempts; fallback does not fire.
Confirmation at M3b (random styles ship): shipped-palette fallback <= 2 % of 10 000 draws per family; pre-decided fallback: L* window narrows to +/-8 and the run repeats.

Role values (own, calibratable, re-tuned 2026-09-28 onto palette targets, item 69) for ink/lit/hatched: paper F7EAD3 all; road F7EAD3(=paper)/DDCFC1/C4A683; ground E8CFA6/D4B78F/F7EAD3(=paper); court F4DFAC/D8C4A3/B5BC6A; building/roof lit side AE947B/BD855B/B9723D; ink/label 2D2219/2C2218/2C2218; wall 2D2219(=ink)/8B7964/74593D; water 9ABDD1/2DA0D3/71B4D3; green B4CC94/8AB85D/A9B951; garden C4CF96/7BAF43/9DB541; tree 70946A/447F33/5E9434; field F5DEA0/E3BC5D/F3D580; verge D7DEB1/A5BF7C/B7C278; shadow (vector rung) ink at alpha 0.35/0.45/0.40. Every matrix pair passes (receipt amendc_rendering_palette.out; e.g. ink road/ground 8.4/8.9, ground/building 16.7/21.2, tree/water 29.2, court/ground 4.7, ink/building 42.5/48.8; lit ink/building 41.4/46.1; hatched 37.4/40.7); paper luma 235.3 warmth 36, ink luma 35.8-36.3 warmth 20.

ink keeps its character by value steps (one ink, 4-8 roles): eight city-band colours (paper=road, ground, building, ink=wall=label, water, green, tree, field); courts as ground at city band (§8.5); raised under-copy and vector shadows the ink at an alpha; light a value change only (LightingSpec.mono §8.4); no role above CIELAB chroma 34 (field highest 33.3; J-A69.82 re-rules J-R3's 18); walls in ink, courts as ground at city band (J-R28, J-R29 kept).

Palette targets (item 69; owner rule "Adopt the corpus measured color targets"; J-A69.81-84): paper lightness = Rec.601 luma of median sRGB of paper-top-mark pixels, band 226-244, target 235; paper warmth = R-B of that median, 20-50, pinned 36; darkest ink = luma of darkest 0.5 % of pixels, <= 45; ink warmth = mean R-B of those, 15-25 (own tolerance), target 20; plate chroma = mean CIELAB C*ab (D65) over every pixel, 18-70, median 43, ink 20-30 (J-A69.82). Targets, never a palette to copy; the only corpus content in the design; no corpus file read by the program.

Every shipped family paper and ink take the paper and ink targets (J-A69.84): one paper value for all three; ink family other roles keep L* and hue with the least chroma scale whose plate chroma reaches 20, never past 30 (J-A69.82); lit, hatched and reserved parchment and painterly aim at median 43 by the chroma scale nearest it that clips no role in sRGB and puts none above C* 60 (J-A69.83): lit ~29, hatched ~30 today; dependent roles move with them and every contrast pair is re-checked by the bounded repair's L* steps.
Plate figures are a plate model (city-band role shares of a plate-framed render, stated in the receipt), PLAUSIBLE until the measurement render confirms them.

Measurement render: fixed render of ink, lit, hatched at plate-equivalent resolution and framing (golden TOWN and CITY §13.3 framed by §9.5 framing rule at 300 dpi on A3, labels and furniture on, default view, day, no pointer), measured on resolution-stable axes only by own code written from the definitions (no corpus instrument in plat/); each family chroma scale re-found by a scripted sweep at the milestone shipping its four bands (ink M1 and M2b; lit M2b; ink-family variants M3b; hatched M5; §13.4 bar), the sweep re-signing the values; a definitional mismatch re-signed at the reconciliation stage (§13.9), never by opening the corpus earlier.

MFCG parity is judged by style class (the MFCG preset needs no MFCG colours); §17.1 (5) palette audit (no three colours within dE2000 2 of a reference palette) compares with the references' palettes only.

Symbolisation (VIS-1): drawn width px = clamp(k x model width x px/m, minPx, maxPx) in model mode, or fixed paper width at 1x (x device pixel ratio) in paper mode; no length in any reference's private unit; ink rows calibrated on MFCG metre-unit export at matched view scale (MFCG size 40 at 0.816 px/m, 1.23 m/px): walls 7.6 m, towers 15.2 m, road cores 8 m, piers 4.8 m (its SVG's 4 m internal unit: wall 1.9, road 2) (MN-1, MFP-8).
Exaggeration never enters the model, GeoJSON, VTT, glTF or CityJSON (model widths); styled SVG and PNG carry drawn widths.
wall.curtain (city, district; model): k = 3 on band thickness (2.5 m -> 7.5 m), minPx 2, maxPx 12; ~6.1 px at MFCG size 40 (MFCG 6.2).
wall.tower (city, district; model): diameter = 2 x drawn wall width, never below the model diameter; ~12.2 px (MFCG 12.4).
wall.gate (city, district; model): gap in wall stroke = max(model opening, 1.2 x drawn wall), flanked by two square blocks of side 2 x drawn wall; ~12 px blocks.
way.through, way.primary body (all bands; model): k = 1, minPx 1.5; 8 m core ~6.5 px.
way.secondary and lane symbol body (city; model): k = 1, minPx 1.
way casing (all; paper): h = 0.5 px each side (casing = body + 2h).
way.pier and bridge deck (city, district; model): k = 1, minPx 1; 4.8 m ~3.9 px.
building outline at city band (paper): 0.5 px x clamp(s / 8, 1/3, 1), s = median footprint side in px at the zoom stop (MFCG thin lines as a law).
building outline at district band and finer (paper): 0.5 px.

raised under-copy offset (city, district; model): (+0.4 m, -1.0 m) east/north x the class ratio = raised.ratio's first matching row: landmark footprints (building.landmark, slot 12: keeps, temples, churches, halls) 2, farmstead class and outbuildings 0.6, every other building 1 (provenance ref:MFCG raise ratios (code), P15; item 54), read from the mark semantic and class column, no model field; drawn length clamped to [0.3 px, 2.5 px] x the ratio.

informal cluster structure (plot of §4.7 S11 cluster arrangement; item 70), city band: each structure its own small roof mark over the plot footpath web drawn in ground, never closed into one mass across the paths (§8.5 (2) exception); below the 2-px floor a settlement dot; from district band a footprint with entrance tick like any building.
boundary treatment (fence, hedge, yard wall, railing), district and finer, paper: <= 1/2 the building outline weight, never filled, gaps at gates.

entrance tick (Entrance.role §2.6; item 29), district and finer, paper: tick across the footprint edge at the entrance vertex: main 1.5 px at outline weight; side, rear, yard, service 1 px at 1/2 outline weight; at building band the plan door leaf.

frontage treatment (BuildingSlot.frontage §2.5; item 19), district and finer, paper: run along the main slot frontage edge at <= 1/2 outline weight: lean_to and stall as short ticks at bay spacing, shopfront a bar inset 1/2 px, arcade arcs at bay spacing; none, gate, wall draw nothing beyond the boundary treatment.

passage arch (passage face §2.5; item 30), district and neighbourhood, paper: arch glyph on the front building outline (Passage.frontBuilding; none while it has none, §2.6 BaseWing.spans) at each end of the face, 3 px wide at 1x, never below 2 px; face floor takes road; none at city band where the spanning mass covers it (§8.5 (2); J-A30.84, J-A30.87).
minimum feature (all bands): 2 px, met by masses and settlement dots (§8.5), never by enlarging one footprint.
Curtain walls draw after footprints; the wall symbol is clipped on its inner side to the band inner edge minus the setback, overhanging only outward (berm, moat, glacis), never covering a plot.

Dry ditch: the ditch residue on the town side of an on_enceinte bailey (§4.7 S10 (0), §4.8) takes the glacis parts' role in a dry-ditch variant: fill 5 dL* darker than glacis fill and, district band and finer, a short inward hachure along its inner edge; city band the glacis plain fill; the overhang rule covers it.

Paint programs: fill; stroke(width by symbolisation, join, cap); casing(w, h) (ink at w+2h in casing pass, body at w in body pass); bands(N, W, exponent, ramp) (VG water law); raised(offset, classRatio); shadowPass(mode, colour, alpha, penumbraPx); hatch(angle|ridge, pitch, taper); roof(construction, dark = lit x lerp(ambience, shadow, alpha)); crown(library); halo(role rule) (§9.4); glyphAlongSpine; pattern(texture, tintRole, metresPerTile); faceLight(dir); ramp(field, stops); hillshade(sun, strength); contourMarks(levels, mode contour|hachure|grass); foam(widthM, alpha); feather(widthM); outlineMix(factor); tint(method, strength); weathering(amplitude); instances(library) (§8.10); vignette; ruin; trace(kind); vault; symbol(glyph); glow(radiusPx, role); Works programs stake, pit, scaffold(ringPx), frame, charred; underground programs ossuary, cavern, quarry, chamber.

hillshade: Lambert on bilinear-interpolated cell normals of the terrain field, water masked, strength from the shadow role alpha, multiply-composited after fills and way bodies and before buildings and trees, no blur.
foam from the shore-distance field on open segments, half alpha on river, none on sheltered and quay.
feather: three inset vector bands at alpha 2/3, 1/3, 0 toward open ground, no bitmap blur (COV-FTG-I05).
ruin: outline dashed by an entity-keyed pattern, fill at 30 % alpha, rubble stipple: the ruined state program, with the none roof kind (§2.6).
trace(kind): a footprint, ring or centreline as a broken hairline, no fill (a cleared building, a superseded wall old line, a closed tunnel) at district band and finer.
vault: barrel-vault hatch along an underground cell long axis over the flat roof kind (II.7.3).
symbol(glyph): a point symbol for every Pin.kind (§2.7), every AccessPoint.kind (II.7.4) where the point breaks the surface, each end of a passage face (arch, §8.3), and §8.5 change marker.
glow(radiusPx, role): the vector rung light sprite at a light mark (§8.4).

Works programs (item 67): stake (dashed footprint with material-pile glyph in yard); pit (cellar pit or trench: darker ground fill, hachured rim, spoil-heap stipple); scaffold(ringPx) (hatch ring outside footprint walls); frame (roof construction lines without fill: rafters and ridge); charred (blackened roofless shell).

Underground system programs (item 65): ossuary (catacomb gallery band with niche ticks), cavern (natural gallery irregular fill with rock stipple), quarry (worked gallery band with pillar squares), chamber (chamber floor; the undercity's in ground with its buildings drawn as buildings).

On rungs 1-2 of §8.4 ladder faceLight, two-tone roof, hillshade and lit crowns emit the albedo (lit-side tone, no face shading) and write normals into the surface layer, and the light pass lights them once; on rung 3 they light as written (J-A68.87).
Undeclined tunnel draws by Tunnel.kind: main a cased band; drain or culvert a hairline pair; passage as a main with arch glyphs at its ends.

An underground building (on the underground arena) draws its footprint in building, a vault class with the vault hatch, both through the underground layer cut-away (§8.4); access points and gratings are symbols on the ground layer where they break the surface.

A lane's body and casing end square at the kerb of the way it meets; the junction wedge belongs to the higher-class way (GEO-21 renderer half); hairlines and casings in paper px; ribbons and symbols follow the symbolisation table.

Relief tier (VN-029, VN-031; base should-have, optional, off by default): contour, hachure and grass marks extracted per render tile from the terrain field by marching squares over the tile cells plus a margin, resampled evenly along each level line, clipped to land faces in vector space before emission so no contour crosses a shore (F-CONTOUR §5.2; coast §4.2 S1 (2)); hillshade on the same field; VG-specific looks (spotlight vignette, dramatic forest) stay in reserved painterly.

Multi-colour roles (XB17): a role may hold a list; an individual mark (building, roof, tree, stall) takes index RH32(role, key, salt[, instance ordinal], style id) mod n; aggregate fills (block ground, city-band masses, wood fills) take index 0.

Tint (K12): per district a hue from a greedy colouring of the district adjacency graph in address order (§6.3): hue = base + 137.5 deg x colour index, stepped by 30 deg until every neighbour differs by >= 30 deg; method spectrum | brightness | overlay; strength 0-1; applied to roofs of built districts; outlines lerp(ink, tint, 0.3); recomputed when the palette changes; off in ink by default.
weathering: each roof RGB x (1 + u*w), u in [-1,1] from RH32('weathering', key, salt, style id), w = 0.04 (ink), 0.06 (hatched), 0.08 (lit).

Override rows may key roof and wall colours by roof.material and the enceinte wall material; a material is a rendering attribute only (§2.6; item 19): its rows change colour and texture roles, never geometry, so a setAttr of a material re-keys the same marks' look and moves nothing.

Wealth in roof colour (lit default; §2.6; items 19, 23; J-A19.81): roof role keyed by prosperity band, one override row per band of prosperity.bands (§4.5), read from the mark prosperity column banded by §4.5 rule (never builtBand): rich C17C46, prosperous C08051, comfortable BD855B (role value), modest BA8765, poor B48B6E, squalid AF8E78; moved by lit chroma scale; each passes every contrast pair of building (ground, road, garden, green, ink), checked by the loader; material picks the pattern texture and band row its tint; a sheet keying roof colour by material applies it after the band row; an unrowed band takes §4.5 interpolation; ink keeps one roof role, hatched two tones.

View state (§11.3) carries season in {spring, summer, autumn, winter} and weather in {clear, overcast, snow}, selecting override rows: autumn and winter re-skin deciduous crowns (by leafType, deciduous when absent) through role variants (tree@autumn; winter a bare-crown symbol); snow lays the snow role over ground, fields and roofs while road keeps its value; overcast removes the global light direct term (shadows go, ambient and occlusion stay; vector rung projected pass off, raised under-copy stays); model and hash untouched.

Post operations (K07): greyscale, sepia, tint(colour, strength), vignette (on the view), pixelate(cellPx), dotScreen(cellPx, angle), scanline(periodPx, alpha), crosshatchNoise(periodPx, alpha); each applied once to a tile's base picture (slots 1-20), never to labels, live overlays, furniture; by Canvas2D in the tile worker after the base marks (~1-2 ms per 512^2 tile) where the light pass does not run, after the light pass where it does in §8.4 (f) order; cell operations take cells and weights by §8.4 (f) so view and export agree; PNG applies per tile; SVG carries greyscale, sepia and tint as one colour-matrix filter over its lit base (§11.1 SVG wrapper group) and omits pixel operations, listed in the export report.

LiveLayerProvider { id; target base|overlay; readsElaborations?; marks(view, model, region, elaborations?) -> MarkTable }: adds display-list groups that are view data (never hashed); run in the generation worker, called when its view state, the model, the visible region (dilated by one tile) or (readsElaborations, e.g. live.stale) Document.derived.elaborations (§2.8, §2.9) change, so a click writing only the cache (§7.3) re-runs it; delivers a DisplayDelta of group live.<id> (§8.9); overlay marks drawn in tile worker composition step (§8.8), base provider part of the tile key (§8.8).

Shipped live layers: live.selection (overlay); live.stale (overlay: §8.5 change markers, one glyph per building or district whose elaboration record reads stale, outside every digest; J-A28.81); live.favourites (base: view state favourites as thematic override); live.ghost (overlay; item 101: pending dry-run preview — derived shape of a points form, the plots and buildings the declaration would make or move in ink at alpha 0.5, its handles and the anchor of §9.5 count badge — while a declaration is drawn or a clerk proposal waits, removed on commit or cancel, never a model change; R1, R3, R14); live.windows (base; item 68: a light mark per lit window at view hour and drawn week by §10.3 rule, read by the light-map bake §8.4); live.people (overlay, registered by the simulation module: favourite persons positions from occupancy at view hour, one categorical colour per person).

Thematic layers: FTG D7 matchers are override rows keyed by entity attributes (prosperity, use, epoch, owner, material). A row keyed by use or owner skips a mark whose knownTo the view knowledge key does not admit at the band (§9.2 table), drawing it unthemed; a theme legend lists only values drawn; while such a row is active the knowledge key joins the tile key (§8.8) (J-A30.85). A front's building themes as its front; its concealed use (item 63) has no theme colour or legend key for a non-admitting key.

Character themes (item 72; J-A72.81): rows keyed by a district identity, by the share of a power (CircumstanceSlice.powers §7.7) or of a sector among its significance-weighted lots, and by its band range (§4.5) — data override rows like D7's.

Conditions (item 88; staged): a ConditionOverlay (§2.7) drawn as a settlement-wide thematic row: settlement-wide post-operation tint plus a legend row keyed by archetype and severity, no geometry; rows schema-complete and empty in the base until the port fills the records.

StyleSheet.states is a rule table keyed by kind x state, read after an entity programs are resolved: replace draws its programs instead of the entity at the row bands; override lays changes over them; one set per family (ink shown; lit and hatched keep geometry and glyphs with own tones) (items 8, 11, 31; II.6, II.7; J-A8.81).
building abandoned (vacant), all bands: override roof tone lerped 30 % toward ground, no raised under-copy.
building decayed (derelict, roofless RoofSpec.kind none §2.6), all: override no roof construction, outline dashed by entity-keyed pattern, fill at 60 % alpha.
building ruined, all: replace with the ruin program and none roof kind.
building cleared (footprint trace), district and finer: replace trace('footprint'); no mass at city band.

building reused (Building.reusedAs garden|orchard|field, §2.6; J-A8.22), all: replace — face filled as that kind (garden = ground at city band, orchard grid instances, field) with trace('footprint') over at district+; no mass; a successor on old foundations is its own building (Building.predecessor) with its class programs.

building condition worn/neglected (§2.6; item 31), district and finer: override weathering amplitude x2 / x4 and, neighbourhood+, a roof pattern variant with patched courses (texture and colour only, item 19); no change at city band.
wall, gate abandoned (neglected), all: override casing dropped, tone 20 % toward ground.
wall, gate decayed (breached or partly dismantled), all: override gap glyph over each breached stretch; towers of a dismantled stretch as trace discs.
wall superseded (Enceinte.supersededBy set §2.7), all: replace trace('ring'), old line as hairline lighter than a wall under the new ring stroke.

tunnel (II.7) abandoned (silted) / decayed (caved in) / ruined (Tunnel.closure collapsed or sealed), underground layer: override band dashed / band broken at caved stretch with rubble stipple / band as trace('centreline') with closure glyph at each sealed end.
island (II.6) floating / waning / settled (SkyIsland.state §2.7), sky layer: override none / alpha x0.8 / alpha x0.6 with ghost share raised (§8.4); shadow follows elevationCm by itself.
island fallen, ground layer (ruin face): replace ruin program rubble stipple over the ruin face.
passage sealed (Passage.sealed §2.5; item 30), district and neighbourhood: override arch glyph at each end drawn closed (bar across); plots behind take their buildings own rows (vacant, §4.11).
building Works staked (item 67; §4.11), all: replace stake; no mass at city band, stage glyph (§8.5) on the dashed footprint.
building Works groundBroken, all: replace pit over the footprint; stage glyph at city band.
building Works foundations, district+: replace footprint walls as low wall bands (outline weight x2) or a sill frame, no roof; city band a mass at 40 % alpha with the stage glyph.
building Works wallsRising, all: override no roof construction, interior floor in ground, scaffold round walls; heights of heightsAt (§4.11) so shadows grow storey by storey.
building Works roofFramed / roofed, all: override frame without fill and scaffold / roof drawn with scaffold still up; work yard in ground.

building Works emptied / stripped / rooflessShell / rubble (demolition), all: override openings as gaps / frame over bare rafters / decayed row with rubble stipple inside / ruin program as wall stubs with rubble heaps; cleared is the existing row.
building Works decaying (toward decayed), all: override roof with gaps along the ridge, outline dashed at 30 %.

building Works roofless / collapsed / overgrown (decay Works ruin stages, item 67 (f); §4.11 Works (4)), all: as decayed row / as ruined row / replace footprint as grassy mound (green stipple fill, trace('footprint') over at district+), no mass.

building repair Works at any decay-ladder stage (abandoned, decaying, roofless, collapsed, overgrown; worksKind repair; §4.11 Works (4); item 67), all: override laid over the stage row — scaffold round walls, work yard in ground; city band stage glyph (§8.5).
building charred (a fire, item 67), all: replace charred (blackened roofless shell) until a clearance or repair Works starts.
building Works refit (conversion without geometry step), district+: override scaffold along the frontage.
plotLine pendingRemoval / staked (item 67 (g); §4.11 Works lines), district+: replace old boundary treatment dashed / new line as stakes, dashed, until fence or wall stands.

access open / locked / bricked (AccessPoint.state II.7.4; item 64) / collapsed (derived while its element is closed, II.6), ground layer where it breaks the surface and underground layer: override kind symbol / with a bar / filled solid in wall / trace with rubble stipple; a secret one drawn only for an admitting key (§9.2).

gallery by system kind catacomb, cavern, quarry, vaults, buried (buried old town street), dug, or undercity walkway (II.7.5, II.7.6; item 65), with II.6 closure states, underground layer: replace ossuary, cavern, quarry, vault hatch, old street as lane body in ground with buried shells as trace outlines, dug passage as passage tunnel, walkway as lane body in ground; closure states as the tunnel row, flooded in water.

chamber by system kind (ossuary, cavern hall, quarry room, cistern or vault, undercity chamber; II.7.6; II.7.5), underground layer: replace chamber with system fill; flooded in water; collapsed as trace with rubble stipple.

link by UndergroundLink.kind open / gated / secret / collapsed / flooded (II.7.6; item 65), underground layer: replace hairline pair / with gate bar / dashed and drawn only for an admitting key / broken with rubble stipple / in water.

A Works stage named like a ladder state (decay Works abandoned, demolition cleared) takes that state's row; before draws the target prior state and finished the target's own programs — the two stages §8.3 census exempts as undeclined (item 67 (f)).

A row naming a worksKind is the one exception to one row per (kind, state): it matches only a target whose running Works is that kind and is laid over the row its stage resolves without it (J-A67.83), so a repair draws decay stages backwards under scaffold.

No reference draws a declined, worn or hidden state, a building in progress or an underground (item 23): the rows are ours, act only on an entity carrying the state or a running Works; a town never passing an epoch, scheduled edit or hand conversion renders as the references would.
builtBand and the geometry floor (§4.11) are read by no render rule: condition follows Building.condition; labels and descriptions follow the prosperity field (J-P1).

Layer order (data; ink shown; one list for city and district bands), 25 slots: 1 paper; 2 water; 3 ground.block; 4 relief (off by default); 5 way casings (way.*, pass 1); 6 way bodies (way.*, pass 2); 7 river casing and body; 8 shore marks; 9 greens, parks, yard parts by role; 10 projected shadows (vector rung only, derived shadow); 11 raised under-copy (derived raised); 12 landmark footprints (solid ink); 13 building masses/footprints/roof detail; 14 piers and bridges; 15 fields and hinterland land use; 16 trees (wood fills and crowns; woods may cover track casings, K16); 17 boundary treatments (district band); 18 curtain walls; 19 towers and gate blocks; 20 grid; 21 scale bar; 22 compass; 23 labels (composed onto each tile §8.8); 24 title, legend, emblem; 25 live layers, annotations, measure overlay. MFCG recorded order is a subsequence (order parity §8.3); NG 1.2.2 order (item 58 (d)) a subsequence of hatched slots.
