LightingSpec (StyleSheet.light): model field|vector|none (field = light pass every rung; vector = rung 3 by the sheet's choice, hatched; none = MFCG preset); castShadows (true in every shipped family, false under MFCG; J-A68.81); mono (true ink, false lit and hatched); sun SunSpec; moon MoonSpec; ambient {day: ink 1.3, lit 0.85, hatched 1.05; night 0.10; underground 0.02}; occlusion {radiusM 6, strength 0.5}; bounce {radiusM 4, share 0.15}; exposure {nightLux 2 lx drawn at albedo full value; by day E_key derived}; defaultLight? day|night|time (night in the night preset; absent elsewhere); vector {projected drop|prism, penumbraPx}.

SunSpec { mode cursor|fixed|path (family default); admits (modes a viewer sunMode may choose: all three by default, a parity preset only its own); azimuthCdeg, altitudeCdeg (fixed sun 31 500, 4 500 = 315 deg, 45 deg); heightRatio h0 of the cursor sun = 1; discCdeg apparent radius 27; colour; intensityLux 100 000; latitudeDeg path mode default 50 }.
MoonSpec { colour; intensityLux full moon 0.25; phase rows {at 0 new .. 0.5 full .. 1; factor} interpolated; discCdeg 26 }.

(a) Surface layer: the tile worker rasters beside each tile base a surface layer from the same marks (§8.8): per pixel normal, height above the tile datum (tile lowest terrain sample) and unlit coverage. Writers: terrain field marks; roofs as surfaces from §8.6 roof construction (eave, ridge, construction faces; never the straight skeleton directly so §3.8 readers stay three; J-A28.32, KERNEL-C05); flat roofs, walls, towers, gatehouses as prism tops; bridge and pier decks at deckCm; tree crowns as domes to crown height; water at its level; Works buildings at stage heights (heightsAt §4.11; item 67); underground each floor, walls and ceiling.

Occluder slabs hold what one height per pixel cannot — a caster whose covered ground the view draws: a sky island under ghost or offset occlusion, span marks of a building over a passage (§8.5 (2); baseCm column the underside), a bridge or pier deck over drawn water — each a record of the document's slab list (§8.8) with outline, top and underside, so ground beneath is shaded from above and lit from the side, and an island shadow falls from its underside (J-A68.83).

(b) Sources: global light (sun by day, moon at night; LightingSpec.sun, .moon); placed lights = LightSource records (§2.7) placed by §4.7 light table or by hand (placeLight §7.1), each a light mark with height, intensity (cd), radius, colour, flicker; derived lights, never records (J-A68.72): lit windows (live.windows by §10.3 rule at view hour and week), plan-rung room lights (building band §8.5), light shafts (II.7.3, II.7.5, II.7.6: every access, grate, well or opening breaking the surface; downward source at its underground end, intensity = current global light x opening area / 1 m^2, cosine lobe, radius = depth + 4 m).

Hand lantern: the viewer own light (handLantern key, underground only, off by default): 20 cd source 1.5 m above the pointer floor point, radius 6 m, never a record; every light lights only where its host draws (§8.1 item 7; J-A63.82).

(c) Brightness: L = A (x) (a*(1-O)*E_g*c_g + sum_s E_s*V_s*c_s + beta*Spill) / E_key; global E = intensity x max(0, n.l), no fall-off; point light E = I_s*max(0, n.l_s)/d_s^2 x f(d_s/r_s), f(x) = (max(0, 1-x^4))^2 (owner: 'optimal distances and gradients of effectiveness'); c source colour; a family ambient share (day, night, underground); O ambient occlusion = mean over eight directions of sine of the horizon angle within occlusion.radiusM x occlusion.strength; Spill = max(0, B(D) - D) (D direct sum, B blur over bounce.radiusM by three box passes with margin) weighted by bounce.share, never a darkening; E_key by day = E_g*(a + sin 45 deg) exactly (open level ground shows its albedo; palette targets hold on the lit map; a shadow keeps a/(a+sin45): ~0.65 ink, ~0.55 lit; receipt amendc_repair_rendering_r1_light.out (C)); night and underground E_key = exposure.nightLux; mono family replaces bracket colour by its Rec.709 luminance; encoded back to sRGB and clamped.

Visibility V_s along the ray from pixel toward the source over surface-layer heights and the slab list, ray height rising linearly from z with slope m: V_s = clamp(min over the ray of (z_ray - h)/(t*sigma_s), 0, 1); t ground distance; sigma_s the source apparent size as a slope (sun/moon disc; flame radius / distance).

Traversal (one law for CPU reference, GPU pass and light-map bake; J-A68.83): the minimum over constant-height texels via the max-height pyramid each surface layer carries (§8.8: level 0 texels, each level never lower than its four cells, up to one cell per tile; beyond the first ring the ring blocks; heights raised by each datum into one frame); a crossed cell [t_a, t_b] with h_max above z bounds from below by (z + t_a*m - h_max)/(t_a*sigma_s); resolved at level 0 or at the resolution floor l(t_a) = max(0, floor(log2(4*t_a/S))), S tile side at the drawn stop and DPR (point lights one level more on every host once §12.7 bake fallback is taken), else divided into four; a caster within half a tile side resolved to its texel, one at t to a floor cell of side <= t/128, shadow lengthened by at most the cell diagonal sqrt2 x side (<= t/90), never shortened; front-to-back evaluation skips cells whose bound cannot lower the minimum and ends at V_s = 0 without changing the value; every caster met however narrow (receipt amendc_repair_rendering_r2_traversal.out (2)).

Window R: point light = its ground distance from the pixel; global light = R = (Z - z)/(m - sigma_s), Z - z = DisplayList.surfaceTopCm less the pixel elevation, m = max(tan altitude, 1/8) for fixed and path suns (the 8x shadow cap), cursor sun m = (H - z)/|P - G| toward G, R at most |P - G| and = |P - G| where m <= sigma_s; the ray also ends where it leaves the list bounds; a world distance so shadows never depend on the tile grid (receipt (1); 1.33 x side under 15 deg diagonal sun, amendc_verify_rendering_r2_diag.out); slab records within R tested exactly by outlines; R, the floor and resolved cells depend on source, pixel and surface only — never device, rung, frame time, view extent or where a cell is held (receipt amendc_repair_rendering_r3_blocks.out (1): 0 of 672 pixels differ, 3 000 m hill at 7 deg); CPU and GPU differ only by GPU arithmetic and encoding, bounded by §13.4 tolerance; §12.5 and §12.7 cost this and restate none of its terms.

A shadow is one source's absence and a gradient, never one shade: edge softens with source size and distance; a spot reached by other lights on every side has no shadow; spill lifts a shadow, a narrow one most; height-aware (owner point 4): a tall caster's shadow falls on a lower roof wherever the ray passes below the caster top, shortened by that roof height, continuing beyond; a lower caster's shadow never climbs a taller neighbour; length follows source height and distance.

(d) Cursor sun (SunSpec.mode cursor, the default; owner: 'the cursor moves the global light which creates different angles for every shadow'): V view centre on ground, D view half-diagonal in metres, C pointer ground point, u = C - V, s = sunHeight (>= 1, default 1); sun at G = V + s*u, height H = h0*D*s; at s = 1 over the pointer, shadows radial; tip d*h/(H - h) beyond a caster at distance d from G, capped at the view end when h >= H; as sunHeight rises shadows turn toward parallel, the pointer setting bearing (view centre toward pointer) and elevation atan(h0*D/|u|); because H scales with the view, zoom changes on-screen radial shadow lengths; fixed and path lengths never depend on zoom (J-A68.84).

Which sun draws (J-A68.84): SunSpec.mode is the family default and SunSpec.admits the modes offered — a parity preset only its own, FTG fixed and path; per-viewer sunMode (§2.9) chooses among admitted modes, a non-admitted value (the key's cursor default under FTG) draws SunSpec.mode; a drawn cursor sun with no pointer (first map, touch screen, every export, a still, a headless render) or on rung 3 is fixed (315 deg / 45 deg, light from upper left). The pointer is a transient input, never stored, logged or hashed (§6.2).

The moon follows the same geometry at the night view intensity and colour, intensity x the phase row factor at the phase of the drawn week and the time key's day on a 29.53-day cycle from week 0 (own stylisation).

(e) Day and night: per-viewer key light (§2.9): day (default) the sun; night the moon and every point light; time: by path-sun altitude at the time key, night below -6 deg, blended over -6..+6 deg. A sheet's LightingSpec.defaultLight sets the viewer light key when that sheet becomes the drawn style (chosen as stylePreset §11.3, or the document's own style opened by a viewer with no light value) — a view change the viewer can change back; night preset opens at night; §2.9 day elsewhere. By day point lights contribute nothing on ground and sky layers (a lamp post stays a symbol).

Underground there is no global light at any setting: ambient = ambient.underground (near zero), every lux from point lights, shafts and the hand lantern, dense in the undercity and around dwellings below ground by the light table's underground rows (§4.7; II.7.3, II.7.5). How much light a night has is not a style value: it is the light table rows (§4.7) with era, magic and prosperity rows (rich streets and magical districts lit, poor alleys and hidden courts dark).

(f) Light pass — one function, two implementations (J-A68.82): a post operation over the base (slots 1-20) before labels, live overlays and furniture (slots 21-25), which keep day colours so the label floor holds at night (§9.4); the tile worker composes labels and overlay marks into the tile one bitmap (J-R21) and writes their coverage into the surface layer unlit coverage, and the pass leaves a covered pixel at its composed colour (lit (+) composed weighted by coverage).

§8.2 post operations run after the light wherever it runs (J-A68.87): rungs 1-2 the tile worker leaves them off the base and the GPU pass applies them to the lit base after the global term and baked light; an export or still applies them after its CPU reference pass, band by band, before its labels are composed (§8.8); on rung 3 and under a sheet with no light the tile worker applies them after its marks; on every path they act on the base alone (covered pixels keep composed colour); a cell operation (pixelate, dotScreen) takes cells on each tile own grid from the tile corner (partial cells at far edges), averages only the base weighted by 1 - unlit coverage (tile worker and CPU reference taking the coverage of the labels and overlays they will compose, the GPU the coverage the surface layer carries) and puts the average into the cell uncovered share alone (J-A68.91).

CPU reference: runs in the tile worker for every export and still, the goldens and tests, in float64 with transcendentals through dmath, every sum in a fixed order — byte-identical on the five engines (§6.5 (9); J-A68.62).
GPU pass (WebGL2, WebGPU where available) is the main-thread compositor (§8.9) for the interactive view, held to the reference by §13.4 tolerance.

Light map: static lights and occlusion baked per tile (sum over point lights of their terms with visibility, and O) by the tile worker once per light-map key (§8.8): the tile surface key (§8.8 base key, content version over the tile dilated by the largest radius of lights reaching it) + revisions of light marks reaching the tile + drawn week + drawn hour + light key; re-baked by any view switch or edit changing the surface a traversal reads or the lights that draw (model-layer toggle, plotsOnly, storey, depthBand, knowledge key while a concealed mark, a key-gated mark or a light whose host is either lies in the dilated tile; §8.1 item 7); a light enters a tile bake only when its radius reaches the tile, reading the surface of the tile dilated by that radius — thousands of torches cost only what is on screen.

Per frame the global light term (and underground with handLantern on, the hand lantern by (c) law and traversal within its radius; J-A68.92) is evaluated on the GPU over the visible tiles surface layers and pyramids, assembled into one view texture with the first ring positions and ring blocks the global window reaches (§8.8); an export or still (no pointer) draws no lantern; the CPU reference evaluates the lantern only at a test-supplied pointer point, as it evaluates the cursor sun for §13.4 stills.
A fire light's flicker scales its baked term in the view by a pure function of its render key and the view time (J-A68.61); the CPU reference draws it at its mean.

(g) Fallback ladder (F-LIGHT §5.2; J-A68.85): rung 1 GPU pass at tile DPR; rung 2 GPU pass with the global term at half resolution upsampled by surface normals and heights; rung 3 vector pass: projected-shadow pass (shadowPass, drop or prism by vector.projected, vector.penumbraPx) from the fixed or path sun, @night roles with a glow sprite at each light mark, light step for faceLight, two-tone roof, hillshade, crowns. A tier's rung chosen at app start from §8.8 canvas budget and measured frame time (§12.5), lowered at run time on a lost GPU context or three consecutive frames over the pass budget, never raised mid-session; every change counted in view telemetry, never an error, never a model change.

A tier whose GPU pass misses §13.4 tolerance at its milestone transfers surface layers at full precision (height and octahedral normal two components float32 + unlit coverage byte: 13 B per pixel, 3.25 MB per position at 512^2 instead of 1 MB) and pyramids, first-ring heights and ring blocks in 16 bits (whole cm above datum rounded up, 2 B per cell, step widening to ceil(range/65 535) cm only where range > 655.35 m; §8.8 counts them in Q_f); the GPU then reads every height to within one step (1 cm under 655.35 m) versus one byte's square-root step (~0.67 m at 45 m, ~10 px at 1:500 fixed sun); traversal unchanged; re-measured and, still missing, draws rung 3 (J-A68.85).

Every export and still takes the CPU reference; an SVG draws rung 3 vector shadows, or with export option lighting: 'raster' one embedded raster lighting layer from the CPU reference (§11.1); hatched draws rung 3 at every rung (NG 1.2.2 prism pass) while its night lights still come from light marks.

(h) Parity presets (item 23; J-A23.71): MFCG — model none: raised under-copy only (K06), no cast shadow, no night view, no light — our preset's behaviour with no claim about the reference (J-A68.86); FTG — fixed or path sun and a low-intensity moon on the same path, one ambient and the directional term only, every shadow present only under clear or snow weather, one window light at each lit building main entrance (anchor per FTG client captured 25 September 2026, item 50; provenance ref:FTG client ambient-and-directional light (code), P22); hatched — NG 1.2.2 prism pass (one shadow per wing offset by height against the light, trees and pins the same, multiplied at the sheet alpha; at night an ambience wash with a glow per lit building; ref:NG 1.2.2 prism shadow and night glow (code), P23); stage-3 building band under parity presets — per-facet diffuse-and-specular shading from one light with a swept-silhouette shadow as Fantasy Manor build 890 (ref:FM build 890 facet shading (code), P24). No constant of those readings enters a cell; every default row of ours (field model, cursor sun, moon, point lights, ambient, occlusion, spill) carries the extension marker so parity presets switch it off.

Shadow casters (WC5; surface-layer and slab-list writers on rungs 1-2, projected on rung 3): buildings and wings (prism from baseCm to eave and ridge, a wing foundation skirt §2.6 included; a building over a passage also casts span marks (§8.5 (2)) — each a prism from its wing baseCm + passage headroomCm to that wing eave over its span ring, projected from its underside like a bridge deck); towers and gatehouses (prism); curtain walls (band prism); bridges and piers (deck prism over water); trees (crown offset by crown height); sky layers (island outline projected by elevationCm); a Works building at its stage heights (§4.11).

On rung 3 every caster projects along the sun vector from its base elevation (baseCm, FTG-13) onto the ground (exact within FTG-13 plinth tolerance; height-aware receivers are rungs 1-2's); rung-3 shadows unioned per layer and composited once per layer per tile — into the base raster in fixed mode, into a per-tile shadow layer of their own in path mode where the tier canvas budget admits it (§8.8), so a moving sun re-rasters only shadows; drop offsets each footprint by height x cot(altitude) along the sun azimuth; prism draws the swept prism; both from the same heights.

Sun (K05): fixed sun at azimuth 315 deg, altitude 45 deg; path mode sunPath(latitudeDeg, dayOfYear, hour) (solar declination and hour angle with dmath) driven by the view-state time (§11.3; the simulation module clock when it runs), hemisphere by latitude sign; shadow pass reads the path sun quantised to 1 deg (§8.8, N-8); faceLight, two-tone roof, hillshade, lit crown bake read the light step = path sun quantised to 15 deg azimuth and 5 deg altitude on rung 3; on rungs 1-2 those programs emit albedo and normals (J-A68.87); below -6 deg night by (e); shadow length capped at 8 x height near sunrise and sunset for fixed and path suns; rung-3 shadows vector with no resolution setting; rungs 1-2 resolved by (c) traversal to the floor cell beyond half a tile side.

Budget (AM-3; rung 3): the projected pass costs <= 20 % of a tile raster time (vector offsets, one union per layer; penumbraPx two vector rings, not a blur). Measurement: M2b times it on METROPOLIS tiles with prism shadows. Pre-decided fallback: a rung that misses draws drop instead of prism (same heights, one offset polygon per caster), reported.

A moving sun (N-8): in path mode one 1 deg step re-rasters and re-composes the visible tiles shadow layers — <= 20 % of the view settle raster + ~0.2 ms per tile, inside §12.5 settle budget; a newer step cancels an older one's pending tiles (latest wins); a tier with no room for shadow layers re-rasters base tiles within the same budget. Measurement: M2b times steps on METROPOLIS views, one step per frame, on reference and low-end devices. Pre-decided fallback: a tier whose step misses quantises the path sun to 3 deg instead of 1 deg, reported.

Light steps (rung 3): when the path sun enters a new light step, a light-step pass bakes the lit crown sprites for it (§8.10), then re-rasters visible tiles under and over layers (or base without shadow layers) centre-out within §12.5 settle bound, each swapped when ready; never cancelled by a newer light step — the newest waits and starts when the running completes, skipping between, so the view reaches one light step within two settles; 1 deg shadow steps continue beside it; every raster uses its drawn light step (running pass's or last completed) passed as TileRasterOpts.lightStep (§8.9); once complete no tile keeps another step and tiers with and without shadow layers draw the same roof and crown tones. Measurement (M2b moving-sun runs): every pass within the settle bound and crown bake within §12.7 budget. Pre-decided fallback: in path mode faceLight, two-tone roofs, hillshade and crowns hold the sheet fixed sun (only shadows follow the path), reported (J-R54).
Heights of every building, wing, tower and roof are §2.6's (at a Works stage its derived stage heights, §4.11), so the surface layer, the shadows, glTF and CityJSON agree (O17 g).

Bands: city — water; block ground; footprint masses and landmarks; tier-1/2 ways cased and access-critical lanes; symbolised walls, towers, gates; bridges; parks and greens >= 0.3 ha in green; wood fills; fields; quarter labels (city cut §4.5, §9.4), water, major landmarks, gates. district — district names; footprints with outlines, entrance ticks by role and frontage runs (items 19, 29); yards by role; boundary treatments; every way stroked; courts; greens; crowns; way names. neighbourhood — family close-up (§8.2); every named way; addresses; pins; stage 2 composes here (§8.6).

building band: wings and, once its plan rung exists (§2.6; item 28), the floor plan one storey at a time — per-viewer view key storey (§2.9), default ground storey, a basement or upper storey by choice, other storeys' wing outlines faded beneath — with walls by kind, openings and every entrance's door (§2.6 entrance set), windows, stair core, chimneys, abstract furniture by room role, room labels and lights; a clandestine building's concealed rooms, door and way down only for an admitting knowledge key (§8.1 item 7, §9.2; item 63); a plan rung absent draws wings, a stale one its cached plan under the change marker (J-A28.82).
Way tiers: 1 = through, primary; 2 = secondary, quay; 3 = lane, cul_de_sac, alley, track, path; pier, bridge, ford draw with their way.

Continuous zoom selects the band with hysteresis (entered at its threshold stop, left one stop past it); added detail cross-fades across that interval; per-band detail budgets by hardware tier; no feature pops more than once across a zoom sweep (B-ZOOM).

Room labels and lights at building band (item 28; J-A28.32, J-A28.85, J-A28.87): the plan draw sets each room label itself — role (§2.6 RoomRole, a §10.2 row name) along the room label spine (§3.8 spine reader on the room ring; sampled medial axis on a downgrade) at the largest cap height in §9.4 room-label range whose glyph boxes fit within the ring, none below the range (hover still names it); a text mark with no LabelTable row, never an S13b candidate; rooms of a storey never overlap (§3.10 seed-tiling row); S13b reads their boxes as protected obstacles at building band (§9.2).

A lit room (Room.lit §2.6) has one light point at its spine summit (axis point of greatest clearance), a derived light of §8.4's light pass at the building band (vector rung: lights glow in night variants), exported as the storey scene's light (§11.1); a derived plan's chimneys are drawn by the roof construction (§8.6).

Figure-ground contract (MFP-1) (1): every L2 built block filled with ground at every band; at city band yards not subdivided (parks and greens >= 0.3 ha in green; enclosed courts stay ground and take court from district band, keeping ink's eight city tones, N-25; a hidden court reached only through a passage, or a sealed one (§4.6, item 30), reads as a court behind the block masses, never as a paper void), so inside the built area streets and squares are the only road-role voids.

(2) Masses at city band: per block, closed across gaps narrower than 1.5 px at the zoom stop (offset +r then -r, r = 0.75 px x metres per px, in the kernel integer offset, computed and cached per (block, stop, revision) in the tile worker from footprint marks carrying their block column), never across a way corridor drawn at the band (closing clipped by corridors so access-critical alleys stay open); filled building, outlined at the band outline width; party lines between one mass's footprints at 1/3 of that width only where the footprint short side >= 4 px.

A building over a passage (Passage.frontBuilding §2.5) adds a span mark to its block closing: one per base wing spanning the passage (BaseWing.spans, inherited by a composed wing as Wing.spans; a stepped front's quads each) = that wing's span ring (§2.6 cut of the Passage face) so its upper storeys cover the passage at city band (J-A30.84, J-A30.87); S14 emits it at every band with block = the building's, baseCm = spanning wing base + passage headroomCm, heightCm = wing eaveCm - headroomCm (top = eave); only the city band paints it, finer bands read it as a shadow caster alone (§8.4) while the passage floor draws in road under its arch glyphs.

Informal cluster exception (item 70; J-A70.81): a §4.7 S11 cluster plot is not closed into one mass across footpaths: each shack, tent or lean-to its own small roof mark in building with the band outline (below the 2-px floor a settlement dot), footpath web in ground — never an empty block, never a solid mass; other plots of the block keep the closing rules.

(3) A mass smaller than (2 px)^2 that merged with nothing is a 2-px settlement dot in building with an ink rim — a symbol at the centroid, never an enlarged footprint (O12 a 2-px floor). (4) Access-critical lanes drawn as way selection.

Metrics (B-ZOOM, city band, default view, every rung): street-edge recoverability = share of intramural street length (sampled every 2 px along corridor centrelines) with a road/non-road transition within (half-width + 1 px) on both sides >= MFCG value on its size-40/80/130 plain sweep renders less 0.03; MFCG value measured research-side at M-1 (§13.5 <M-1>), the product cross-checked on M1 golden renders within 0.01; road/ground contrast is the matrix's; gross footprint cover inside walls reported beside MFCG's as information, not a target (§13.5).

Pre-decided fallback if recoverability fails at M1: the ink city band adds kerb hairlines (0.25 px, ink) along every open frontage run >= 6 m (detached, compound, hovel, vacant, green frontages) and re-runs the metric (J-R5).

Way selection at city band (VIS-3, N-6): tiers 1-2 always drawn; a tier-3 way is bounded when the footprint-covered share of its frontage >= 0.8 on both sides and its width >= the closing's 1.5 px at the stop; drawn when access-critical (some plot has all its access edges on it and fronts no other drawn way) and not bounded; drawn tier-3 ways take the lane symbol (body = max(model width, 1 px), casing h/2); bounded intramural lanes and alleys stay unstroked gaps; so suburb offshoots, ribbon back lanes, farm tracks, extramural lanes are drawn. Metric: share of city-band plots whose access way is drawn or bounded >= 95 %.
Line greenery (VIS-14): avenues and street trees not drawn at city band; they appear from district band where a crown >= 4 px; check: no tree mark covers a tier-1/2 casing at city band (§8.3; J-R6).

Works stages by band (item 67; owner: 'we should consider things being roofless or other visuals'): a Works building draws its stage at the drawn week by §8.2 states: city band a stage glyph on its mass (scaffold hatch for build, extension, repair; rubble stipple for demolition; ladder rows for decay); district and neighbourhood the stage itself (staked footprint, pit, low walls, walls rising in scaffold, bare roof frame, roof under scaffold, stripped shell, rubble); building band the plan in progress (walls without doors or furniture; a ruin's fallen walls and open rooms, §2.6); a plot boundary in transition dashed from district band (old line until cleared, new as stakes; §4.11 Works step 7); heights and shadows follow the stage (§8.4).

plotsOnly (per-viewer view key §2.9; item 28; J-A28.42) is the cadastral view: at city and district bands every plot boundary (§2.5 cadastral outline group) over block ground and no building mark (masses, footprints, entrance ticks, roof detail off); walls, ways, water, greenery, labels as they are; never the default (default at city zoom is every footprint, MFCG's look, §4.1).

Change markers (item 28; J-A28.81): a building whose elaboration record (§2.8) reads stale (an input of its wings or plan rung changed since derived, §4.1; incl. a Works stage change, item 67 (j)) carries a marker glyph at building, neighbourhood and district bands; a district holding any stale building one marker at city band; drawn by the live.stale overlay (composed without re-rastering, never hashed, read from records outside every digest); vanishes when the click re-derives the rung from its canonical prior (plan: stored plan else as-built along §2.6 interior ladder; wings: stored or as-built) — never from the cache (§2.6, §7.3; J-A28.71).

First paint: the complete city band — S0-S13a for every district and S14 city band — with no S9 block preview on the one-click path (SCL-4; J-R7); lazy work is only what the city band does not draw: yard sub-parts, entrance ticks (entrance set is S11's, §2.6), roof ridges and hatching, street names and addresses (view data §9), crowns and scatter (§8.10), stage-3 rungs (wings and plans) by click or view (§4.1).

Unlit first map (item 68; J-A68.88): the first map is composed without the light (with the raised under-copy); surface layers and light maps follow centre-out within §12.5 settle bound, the view then lit by the fixed sun until the pointer moves (§8.4 (d)); time to first map (§12.5) never includes them.
Proxy thumbnails (§7.8) draw S0-S4 marks in a distinct preview style and are never presented as the map.
The neighbourhood band of every family is the stage-2 render tier (IMPROVEMENTS S5): hatched is NG's family; the stage-2 side-by-side vs NG shows hatched with the ink close-up alongside (VIS-9).

Close-up content (PART II) derived when §4.1's trigger policy says (neighbourhood click under elaborate click; visible tiles under view; II.4) from the district committed state and sub-seed, in the derivation pool (or generation worker when the pool is off); reaches the tile worker as DisplayDelta slices answering the tile band request (§8.9; under click from the elaboration cache §2.9) into the same mark tables and pyramid; an unopened neighbourhood draws the base marks at the neighbourhood band without close-up content.
owner_raw: rendering (tile path); trigger policy pipeline §4.1; elaboration cache model §2.9

statement: Stage 3 plugs in at the building band: marks from BuildingGenerator.compose(...) and plan(...) (taking a Kernel and a BuildingInput with a TerrainSampler, §2.6), derived on a click or under elaborate view for visible tiles (§4.1), kept in the elaboration cache (§2.9: one entry per (building, rung, input digest), held by the generation worker, persisted as non-canonical chunks) — the only cache of derived rungs, no per-session (entity key, revision, lod) memo; a stale rung served from cache until the click re-derives it from its canonical prior (J-A28.71; item 28 (c)); the tile draws the outline until compositions arrive; every other band draws the outline, equal to the union of composed wings by contract (SCL-13), so the footprint hash is the same at every band; the tile worker never runs compose(), plan() or close-up derivation (§8.9).

Roof construction runs per stored wing (VIS-10) by BaseWing.kind (§2.6): rect takes exact OBB ridges with hips from its four corners (BaseWing.corners when sides carry other vertices; a warp-de-rectangled rect is a quad by §2.6 carry rule); quad takes the exact OBB path when it passes the near-rectangle test (§3.8), the validated skeleton otherwise, gable constructions drawing its stored ridge (arc-length midpoints of the two side chains its ridgeAxis names); polygon takes a pyramid, cone or dome; the plain roof (no ridge or hip lines) is the downgrade (§3.8); two-tone lit/shadow faces assigned per roof face by normal against the light (faceLight) for any face set.
The derived-roof cache key includes the construction (§8.1 item 5), so switching ink's hipped roofs to hatched per-wing gables needs no regeneration.

A derived plan's chimneys (Chimney §2.6) rise through the roof at their columns, each a small stack in the roof tone with an ink rim at neighbourhood and building bands; roof detail (§8.10) draws no decorative chimney on a building whose plan rung is not absent (J-A28.85).

A building in progress at the building band (item 67): wings at stage heights (heightsAt §4.11) and, where its plan rung exists, the plan in progress (walls without doors or furniture; a ruin's fallen walls and open rooms, §2.6) from the committed composition, parts §4.11 mutation steps have reached at the drawn week drawn, the rest not; the composition is never re-derived per week; a stage change marks the rung stale via its elaboration record (§8.5 change markers; item 67 (j)).

Export resolution: SVG resolution-free and layered at a declared band (§11.1); PNG and print by §8.8 band-streamed tile assembly at any DPI with labels placed at a zoom stop computed for the export's own scale (§9.2); paper-unit rules keep hairlines at paper width at every scale; symbol widths from the symbolisation table at export scale; VTT exports carry model widths only on a declared grid with exact pixels per cell (§11.1); scale bar accuracy is §9.5's.

Pyramid (N-9 a): zoom stops (ZoomStop) at 2^(1/4) scale steps (four per doubling) cover B-ZOOM 1:50 000 -> 1:500 in 27 stops; stop k has m_k metres per CSS pixel; tiles 512 x 512 device px at the view tile DPR d (device ratio after the tier cap), world-aligned per (stop, d): tile (i, j) covers the world square of side 512 x m_k / d m with corner (i, j) x 512 x m_k / d — stable under panning, shared between views and exports at that stop and DPR; the view settles on exact stops within +/-9 % of requested scale; every settled view has exact hairlines, casings and a collision-free label set (J-R8).
ZoomStop is declared in @plat/model (§14) and defined by §8.8 (its fields are not spelled out in §8; the stop index k and m_k metres per CSS pixel are its content).

Tile content (GEO-28, N-7): a tile draws every mark whose bbox meets the tile dilated by m = the largest of casing half-width, drawn wall half-width, projected-shadow length, largest crown radius, halo width at the stop (for a light map also the largest radius of lights reaching the tile, §8.4 (f)), in §8.1 item 3 order, identical in every tile; each tile clips to its own square (no seams, no casing bar across a junction on a district boundary); fills of one semantic within a tile are one Path2D with non-zero rule; semantics declared seamClose (ground, masses, yard parts, shadow union) get a 1/2-px same-colour stroke underneath (NG seam dilation). Tested by §8.3 junction-mouth and draw-order rows.
seamClose: a declared property of a semantic (ground, masses, yard parts, shadow union) giving a 1/2-px same-colour under-stroke; where it is declared (registry or sheet) is not stated.

Layers of a tile and composition (N-5): the tile worker rasters and keeps a base layer per tile (slots 1-20), then composes base + glyphs of labels placed at that stop (§9.2) + overlay live marks into one bitmap per tile position transferred to the main thread; a label edit or toggle, a selection or a moving person re-composes the tiles it touches (§12.5 composition cost), never re-rasters a base; in path sun mode where the budget admits, the base is rastered as under (slots 1-9) and over (slots 11-20) with projected shadows (slot 10) in their own layer at half resolution (256^2 per tile, bilinear-scaled when composed), so a 1 deg step re-rasters only shadow layers and only a new light step re-rasters under and over through §8.4 light-step pass (J-R21) — the vector rung's machinery.

On rungs 1-2 the tile worker also rasters the surface layer: 4 B per pixel at tile DPR — octahedral normal 2 B, height above tile datum 1 B on a square-root scale to T (h = (v/255)^2 x T; T = 160 m gives ~0.2 m steps at 5 m, ~1.2 m at 100 m; T = 160 m or the tile's own range above its datum rounded up to the metre where greater, carried beside the datum, so no height clamps; J-A68.94), unlit coverage 1 B (coverage of label glyphs, halos, overlay marks composed); and bakes its light map at half resolution (256^2 x 4 B: point-light term in three channels, ambient occlusion in the fourth); both transferred with the composed bitmap (one bitmap per tile position stands, J-R21).

Max-height pyramid (§8.4 (c)): level 0 its own heights; levels 1-9 per cell the greatest height of the city band caster marks (§8.1 item 2) whose outlines (an instances mark dilated by its largest crown radius) meet the cell and of the terrain field samples whose cells meet it, never below the level-0 heights it covers; same writer from the marks; one byte on the height square-root scale rounded up (1/3 of the height byte: 1/12 MB per position).

The GPU pass reads the visible tiles' surfaces and pyramids and, round them, what the global light window reaches (§8.4 (c)): the view holds what its drawn sun can need — cursor sun the largest window a pointer anywhere in the view gives; fixed and path suns their altitude's — so a moving pointer rasters nothing and a sinking path sun adds blocks as a pan adds tiles.

A tile position's ring = its distance in positions from the visible set (greater of two index offsets). The first ring (2(a+b)+4 positions) is held per position from level 0, its heights rastered with pyramid (1/3 MB) from the view band's marks, requested for its districts like a visible tile (§8.9), its shadows completing when the band answer arrives.

Ring block (J-A68.90): the world-aligned square of 2^m x 2^m positions whose indices agree shifted right by m, at the largest order m whose every position lies in ring 2^m + 1 or beyond, held from level max(m + 2, floor(log2(4(r - 1)))), r its nearest position's ring (the level §8.4 (c) floor resolves there) — at most 128 x 128 cells at that level (1/48 MB with levels above, one byte) whatever the order, levels continuing above level 9 (a cell spanning 2^(l-9) tile sides) to one cell per block; cells take the pyramid rule over the city band marks (which the tile worker holds for the whole document and which carry every caster; J-A68.93) with own datum and scale top, so a block cell equals the same cell of any pyramid and no block waits for a band answer.

Slab list: one per document — every slab caster of the city band (§8.4 (a)), each outline, top and underside — held whole by the tile worker, transferred to the main thread with the first surface layer and again with any delta changing a slab, read by the traversal wherever the ray runs within R; memory counted with the display list (§8.1 item 6), held once, not per tile position.

Visible tiles, first ring and blocks partition the window, block count growing with the log of reach: at most 326 first-ring positions and blocks together at the reference view and 437 at any view up to tile DPR 3, for a window reaching the whole frame of any rung to the population cap, blocks together <= B (receipt amendc_repair_rendering_r3_blocks.out (2)) — versus every position held out to R growing with the window square (5 440 positions for 300 m relief under a 15 deg sun at 1:500, amendc_verify_rendering_r2_rings.out); a shadow cast from beyond the view falls inside at full length and where a cell is held never changes its value.

The CPU reference computes its surface from the marks directly into float32 arrays (height and octahedral normal, 12 B per pixel; arithmetic float64) and its pyramids, first ring and blocks in float32 by the same rule, never from an encoding (the GPU pass approximation within §13.4 tolerance).

Tile key (LC-23, N-8) = (stop, i, j, tile DPR d, tile layer base or in path mode under/shadow/over, style version, view-state switches changing the layer's pixels: season, weather, shadows on/off and mode, model-layer toggles, plotsOnly (city and district bands), storey (building band), depthBand (underground layer), knowledge key while a use- or owner-keyed thematic row is active or while the tile holds a concealed mark, a key-gated mark (access and link rows) or a light whose host is either (§8.1 item 7), the drawn week where the tile holds a Works mark, the light key on the vector rung (@night roles), base live layers; for shadow (or base without shadow layers while projected shadows on) the path sun quantised to the tier's sun step (1 deg, 3 deg after fallback); for under and over (or base) of a sheet whose programs read the light, the light step; in fixed mode the sheet sun belongs to the style version). Content version = combination of drawn marks' revisions.

A composed bitmap is keyed by its base key + the stop's label-placement revision + the overlay providers' versions; a DisplayDelta's dirty boxes invalidate every cached tile and ring block they meet at every stop and DPR; in path mode a new 1 deg step invalidates only layers keyed by it and a newer step cancels an older one's pending re-rasters (latest wins); a new light step invalidates its keyed layers, re-rastered to completion by §8.4 light-step pass.

A surface layer and its pyramid are keyed as their tile base; a first-ring position's heights and pyramid likewise (always from level 0); a ring block by (stop, order, indices, tile DPR, level) + the base-key switches changing which casters draw or their heights (model-layer toggles, plotsOnly, drawn week over a Works mark), content version the combination of revisions of city-band marks meeting it; a held block serves any view whose floor at its nearest position is at or above its level, so a pan bringing a position nearer takes the finer block, never a coarser one.

Light map keyed by its light-map key (§8.4 (f)): its tile surface key (content version over the tile dilated by the largest radius of lights reaching it) + revisions of light marks reaching the tile + drawn week + drawn hour + light key; a dirty box invalidates every light map whose dilated tile it meets; a view switch changing a surface or the lights that draw (model-layer toggle, plotsOnly, storey, depthBand, knowledge key over a concealed or key-gated mark or a light hosted by either) re-bakes the light maps reading it; a moving pointer, new sunHeight or zoom inside a stop invalidates nothing cached — only the GPU per-frame terms (global light, hand lantern) move. (Restates §8.4 (f) light-map key content.)

Canvas budget per hardware tier (N-9 b): counted per visible tile position the worker base (1 MB at 512^2) and main-thread composed bitmap (1 MB); next coarser stop's composed bitmaps for gestures (<= 1 MB per visible position); fixed scratch: shadow and post-op buffers (2 MB), crown sprites and glyph atlases (<= 5 MB; with a path sun in lit one crown set per cached light step — drawn step's always, earlier while they fit, §8.10; a set a running export holds counts with that export's canvases, §12.8). P = a x b = (ceil(W*d/512) + 1) x (ceil(H*d/512) + 1); need 3P + 7 MB; 4.25P + 7 MB with path-mode shadow layers (under and over replace base; shadow layer adds 1/4 MB); 4.25P + 7 MB + Q with the light pass on rungs 1-2 (per position surface layer 1 MB and light map 1/4 MB; path-mode shadow layers not held; Q = P/12 + (2(a+b)+4)/3 + B; B = 3.75 MB at DPR 1, 4.25 at 1.5, 4.75 at 2, 5.5 at 3, whatever the window; receipt (2): at most 3.60, 4.09, 4.58, 5.46 MB); 6.5P + 7 MB + Q_f at full precision (3.25 MB per position; 16-bit pyramids, first ring, blocks; Q_f = 2Q; J-A68.89).

Tier ceilings: low 72 MB, mid 128 MB, high 192 MB; tile-DPR caps: low 1, mid 2, high 3; tile DPR = device ratio capped by tier, stepped down 3 -> 2 -> 1.5 -> 1 until 3P + 7 MB fits the ceiling — and with the light pass until 4.25P + 7 MB + Q (full precision 6.5P + 7 MB + Q_f) fits, taking the vector rung where that fails at DPR 1 (J-A68.89); path-mode shadow layers only where 4.25P + 7 MB also fits, else a sun step re-rasters the base.

Worked cases (fixall_rendering_r2_budgets.out; amendc_repair_rendering_r3_blocks.out (5)): reference view 1 440 x 900 CSS px at DPR 2: P = 35, 112 MB (156 MB with shadow layers), mid or high tier; low-end 1 366 x 768 or 1 920 x 1 080 at DPR 1: 43 or 67 MB, inside 72 MB. Lit (base + Q): reference view DPR 2 on high (P = 35, 155.75 + 17 = 172.75 MB), DPR 1.5 on mid (P = 24, 109 + 14.25 = 123.25 MB); low-end 1 366 x 768 lit at DPR 1 (P = 12, 58 + 10.75 = 68.75 MB), 1 920 x 1 080 (P = 20, 92 + 12.75 = 104.75 MB) draws the vector rung; full precision: reference view DPR 1.5 on high (P = 24, 163 + 28.5 = 191.5 MB), DPR 1 on mid (P = 12, 85 + 21.5 = 106.5 MB), low-end vector rung — all PLAUSIBLE until M2b canvas measurement (§12.8). (Arithmetic re-checked: consistent.)

Cached tiles beyond the visible and fallback sets are evicted least-recently-used by bytes; the tier is chosen at app start from the Canvas2D part of bench/calibrate (§12.1) and the host's reported device memory, can be overridden in the advanced panel, and is shown with the tile DPR in the view status (J-R22).

Gestures (SCL-7, VIS-6): during a pinch or wheel zoom the compositor shows the nearest cached stop's composed tiles scaled (labels scale with them); 120 ms after input stops the view animates (<= 150 ms) to the nearest stop and the tile worker re-rasters visible tiles centre-out, swapping each in when ready; panning composites cached tiles and shows newly exposed ones from the next coarser cached stop until rastered; while a gesture runs at most 4 new bitmaps committed per animation frame; at first paint and settle every ready tile committed in the frame it arrives (§12.5).

Print and large PNG (O12 e): horizontal bands of tiles (512 device px high) rastered and composed at export scale; scanlines streamed into the PNG encoder — per-row rule (of PNG's five filter types the one whose filtered bytes have the smallest sum of absolute values, bytes as signed), one zlib stream (CompressionStream in browsers, zlib level 6 in Node), IDAT chunks band by band; §12.7 holds encoding time and fallback; peak canvas memory one band (A2 300 dpi: 7 016 x 512 x 4 B ~ 14 MB); no canvas larger than a tile band; per-layer transparent PNGs use the same path with the layer set restricted.

Lit export (item 68): runs §8.4 CPU reference light pass tile by tile, each export tile over its own window, first ring and ring blocks taken round the export tile as round a view of one position: float32 surface (12 B per pixel, 3 MB) and pyramid, first ring float32 heights and pyramids (8 positions, 10.67 MB), blocks in float32 (4 B per cell) — <= 14 MB plus blocks whatever R; blocks <= 13.1 MB at 1:500 and 300 dpi over the frame at population cap (receipt (3)) and <= 1.7 MB more per halving of the export tile world side (18.52 MB at 1:100 and 600 dpi, amendc_verify_rendering_r3_exportscale.out), never a whole band's surface.

Export block cache: keeps every block the export has computed while they fit in max(16 MB, the tile in progress's blocks) (tile in progress's held, least recently used released first); a cached block serves each later export tile whose floor there is at or above its level; each first-ring position's heights rastered for every band whose tiles it borders; the light-map bake reads the tile dilated by the largest light radius; the export then runs §8.2 post operations (§8.4 (f)) and composes its labels, one band canvas (~14 MB at A2 300 dpi) and one tile window held at a time (§12.8); its transient list carries what first rings, light maps and blocks read beyond the frame; the window's Z is the city band surfaceTopCm the generation worker keeps (§11.1; §8.1 item 6), so a caster beyond the frame edge still shades it.

Warp preview (SCL-9): while a warp brush is held, moved L1 vertices apply to a transient copy of affected ways' and blocks' marks and only tiles meeting the brush dirty box re-raster (frame rate §12.6); Apply commits the warp event (§7.1) whose invariants and re-derivation run then; Discard drops the copy (MFCG staged warp on our event model).

Canvas2D is the reference backend of every shipped preset (ink, lit, hatched and variants), on an OffscreenCanvas in the tile worker through resumable raster jobs; programs render typed-array paths, one Path2D per (program, semantic, variant) per tile, sprites by drawImage; SVG written from the same display list (§11.1).

WebGL2 draws no marks: it composites and, on rungs 1-2, lights — uploads composed Canvas2D tiles, their surface layers and light maps as textures, composites with the view transform, runs §8.4 global-light term (underground, the hand lantern's too) and the composition of the baked light as fragment passes, then §8.2 post operations over the lit base (§8.4 (f)); no stroke tessellation, no SDF text, no look that differs by backend (VIS-7); the lit picture is the CPU reference's, the GPU held to it by §13.4 tolerance (J-A68.82); WebGPU where available runs the same passes.

While the light pass is off or on the vector rung the WebGL2 compositor is the pre-decided fallback compositor: measured at M2b (pan and zoom frame rates of the Canvas2D compositor on reference and low-end devices at METROPOLIS scale, §12.5); enabled for a hardware tier only if Canvas2D misses >= 60 fps (reference) or >= 30 fps (low end).

Text (DEF-6): all text drawn by Canvas2D in the tile worker composition step (§8.8), glyph by glyph at positions from the bundled font's own metrics (§9.2), through a glyph atlas per (face, size, stop): each glyph drawn once into the atlas and copied per placement; SVG writes the same per-glyph positions as the face's glyph outlines by default, or as text in the embedded face on request (§11.1, N-13) (J-R9); measured at M1 against §12.7 label-composition budget; pre-decided fallback: whole words cached as bitmaps per (text, size, stop) in the atlas.

Threads (N-4) (1) generation worker: holds document and model, runs S0-S14; resolves instance overrides (§8.10); runs live-layer providers (§8.2); builds on-demand bands (district, neighbourhood, building bands of the districts a band request names, build(model, band, groups)); writes every export (§11.1); answers the API hit and inView queries (§11.2) from the model and its 24-B index (entity, bbox, group); holds the elaboration cache (§2.9); hands stage-3 compose(), plan() and close-up derivation (§8.6) to the derivation pool — on a click under elaborate click, on the tile worker's band request under view (§4.1).

(2) derivation pool (up to three workers, §4.1): runs the per-district stages at every rung (§12.3) and, on request, compose(), plan() and close-up derivation from the committed state of the district handed; with the pool off the generation worker runs them.

(3) tile worker holds no model and no terrain: holds the display list with label, instance and string tables (the only full copy, §8.1 item 6); rasters base layers and, with the light pass, surface layers with pyramids, first-ring heights, ring blocks and light maps (§8.4, §8.8); runs S13b (§9.2) and decoration instancing (§8.10); composes labels and overlay live marks; runs post operations and every export's CPU reference light pass; answers the main thread's furniture and snap queries; rasters raster exports from the transient list each request carries (§11.1) — all through the queue, everything arriving through the crossing table (J-R23).

(4) main thread: runs the UI, compositing of transferred tiles, pointer hit-testing on hit-test slices, screen-space furniture (§9.5; placement scores and ruler snaps asked of the tile worker), input and, on rungs 1-2, the GPU light pass over transferred textures, re-evaluated per frame while the pointer moves the cursor sun or hand lantern (§8.4 (d), (f)); nothing model-sized reaches the main thread (J-R10).

What crosses (SCL-6, N-4): generation -> tile: display-list deltas (mark columns with key, geometry, field rasters, changed label/instance/string rows incl. candidates, priority, parent node, pinned placement, hidden, knownTo per label; stamp parameters, species mix, resolved overrides per instances mark), each slice copied into a fresh buffer and transferred, generation keeps 24-B index; bound O(changed marks), <= 97 B per label row, <= 40 per instance row, <= 16 per species row, <= 32 per override row + geometry and UTF-8; generation <-> tile (cross-origin-isolated hosts only): mark table as SharedArrayBuffer columns, optional, never required (COOP/COEP); tile -> generation band requests (districts and band that tiles entering the view, then first-ring positions, need and the tile worker lacks; buildings whose rungs and districts whose close-ups the band needs — derived under elaborate view, under click served only from the elaboration cache), copied, <= 4 KB per request; generation or pool -> tile answers (on-demand band marks, compose() wings and rooms, plan() storeys, close-up marks as DisplayDelta slices naming the request), transferred, <= 1 MB per answer; generation -> tile live-layer marks (live.<id>), <= 256 KB per delivery; tile -> main composed ImageBitmaps, per-tile hit-test slices (bboxes + handles), with the light pass each tile surface layer + pyramid + light map, first-ring heights + pyramid, ring blocks, slab list, zero-copy, <= 1 MB bitmap + <= 64 KB slice per tile, + 1 MB surface (3.25 full precision), 1/12 MB pyramid (1/6), 1/4 MB light map; 1/3 MB per first-ring position, <= 1/48 MB per ring block (2/3 and 1/24 at full precision); main -> tile furniture queries (view, stop, <= 16 candidate boxes: compass's eight, title's and legend's four corners) and snap queries (pointer world cm, radius px, stop) with request id, copied, <= 4 KB; tile -> main per candidate box ObstacleSource.coverage record, snapped point from RoleIndex.snap or none, <= 4 KB within one 16.7 ms frame; generation -> tile raster-export requests (PNG, print, .dd2vtt image: frame, scale, band, layers, post ops, export zoom stop (§8.7), sheet id@version or viewer stylePreset sheet with document rows (§11.3), §8.8 view-state switches, shadow sun, light step, lighting rung (CPU reference) with global light resolved to fixed or path sun, the requesting viewer's knowledge key kept until the export completes) carrying the transient list (and for a lit export the city band casters its ring blocks read), request copied, list columns transferred, <= 4 KB + the list (§12.8 export peak); tile -> generation encoded raster streamed band by band + a progress message per band, < 64 B per message; main -> workers view changes, input, API calls (§11.2), copied, small.
Main-thread receive work <= 4 ms per delivery (bitmaps and slices only), measured in B-CITY's browser runs.

@plat/render tile and vector backends (§14): TileAddress {stop, i, j, dpr}; TileRasterOpts {layers; tileLayer base|under|shadow|over|surface|lightMap|ringHeights|ringBlock; block? {order, level}; shadows off|drop|prism (StyleSheet.light.vector.projected); sun? (shadow sun, 1 deg step, read only by the projected-shadow pass); lightStep? (read by faceLight, two-tone roof, hillshade, crowns on the vector rung); lighting? {rung 1|2|3; light day|night; week; hour; reference? {azimuthCdeg, altitudeCdeg}} (item 68); tier low|mid|high; dpr}; TileBackend.begin(tile, list, style, opts) -> RasterJob (fixes the draw sequence, draws nothing); RasterJob {step(deadlineMs) -> boolean (returns after the first draw call ending deadlineMs or more after this call began; true when complete); finish() -> ImageBitmap; cancel(); readonly spentMs}; VectorBackend.write(list, style, {layers, band, frame}) -> string (the SVG writer, generation worker over the export transient list).

The queue passes the view's drawn light step for under, over and base and the shadow sun wherever projected shadows are drawn; an export's jobs get its request's sheet, switches, shadow sun and light step. begin finds every mark whose bbox meets the dilated tile and fixes the draw sequence: native calls in (slot, pass, z, key) order, each a fill or stroke of one batched Path2D (§12.5 per-tile bound), a run of <= 64 sprite draws, or a derived per-tile operation (projected-shadow union, raised under-copy, post operation); the preparing JavaScript reads the clock after every mark and every 64 instances and can stop there; a native call is never split; a derived operation runs whole inside one step — overrun past the deadline at most one native call or derived operation.

Each job owns its canvas and context state and what it reads does not change under it: deltas applied between steps, a removed mark becomes a dead row and an added mark a new row, the tile worker compacts only while no job is live; a job whose tile a delta's dirty boxes meet is cancelled and re-queued; slicing changes when calls run, never which or in what order (whole vs 1-ms slices pixel-identical, §8.3); the queue calls step(8) — step(4) after the pre-decided fallback.

Tile worker queue: between two steps it serves its message queue, then runs one step of the highest class with ready work: 1 furniture and snap queries (answer due within one frame); 2 incoming deltas (edit deltas, band answers, live-layer deliveries) in arrival order, O(changed marks), <= 1 MB per answer; 3 the visible view: S13b at the view stop, on the vector rung with a path sun after a new light step the lit crown bake (one sprite per unit) and §8.4 light-step pass, visible tiles' raster jobs centre-out with compositions and commits; on rungs 1-2 after a tile base its surface layer + pyramid + light-map bake (one light per unit), then the next tile, after the visible tiles the first ring heights then ring blocks nearest first, one block per unit (§12.7 costs); re-compositions for label and overlay changes; 4 exports: S13b at the export stop over its transient list (memo held by the job), crown bake when the request's light step set is not cached (held until the export completes), then band by band raster jobs, surface, first rings, blocks its block cache lacks, CPU reference light pass (64 rows per unit) when lit, composition, read-back (64 rows per step), encoding.

A class runs only while every higher class is empty, one step at a time; within a class the job in progress runs to completion before the next (at most one raster job per class live); a query waits at most one step; a pan or zoom during an export pre-empts it within one step. No starvation: an export waiting 100 ms since its last step runs its next step ahead of class 3 (never ahead of 1 and 2) — at most one step in any 100 ms, <= 8 % of the worker; a settle contains at most two export steps at CITY and three at METROPOLIS (<= 16 and <= 24 ms); a newer sun step or a tile leaving the view cancels its job (latest wins); the export dialog shows progress (bands done of total) and, while class 3 holds the worker, that the export is waiting for the view (J-R46).

Placement and crown bakes are stepped like a raster: S13b (view in class 3, export in class 4) is a PlacementJob whose unit is one decision (§9.2), called with the queue step limit; a crown bake is stepped one sprite per unit; a print's placement over its whole frame runs as a few class-4 steps (§12.7) with queries, deltas and the view served between, every bound holding while an export places labels (J-R51).

Queries to the tile worker: compass, title and legend placement (§9.5) and ruler snapping read the display list (only the tile worker holds it); the main thread asks via query rows; the tile worker answers with ObstacleSource.coverage and RoleIndex.snap over its list — the implementations S13b uses (§14); a query is class 1, waits <= 8 ms plus one native call or derived op, runs in <= 4 ms tile-worker time, answer within one 16.7 ms frame (a city-band tile of a whole-CITY view rasters in ~1.2 ms, §12.5); the ruler keeps one snap query in flight (newer pointer replaces a queued one) and shows the unsnapped point until the answer; furniture placement asked when the view settles, keeping its previous place until the answer (J-R40).

Measurement with the first map (M1 at TOWN and CITY, M2b at METROPOLIS) in B-CITY browser runs: query round trip p95 <= 16 ms during a settle raster and <= 4 ms tile-worker time per query, each tile's longest native call and derived operation logged beside it; exports beside the view are §12.7's run. Pre-decided fallback: step limit falls from 8 ms to 4 ms (step(4)), halving a query's wait and an export step's share of a settle.

InstanceStyle { species? (a species kind of the entity mix); crown? (crown-library index); scale? 0.5-1.5; tone? colour jitter -1..1; leafType? deciduous|evergreen } — what a restyle or add override sets (§7.1).

One instance set per entity, independent of the band: every instances mark (wood, garden, park, copse, orchard, avenue, hedgerow, yard planting, scatter class) has one set of positions in one of three layouts: stamp of a per-class blue-noise tile for areas; jittered grid for orchards (6-8 m); jittered line for avenues and street trees (along the row §4.9 derives in the planting district half-corridor strip at Greenery.along offsetCm from the kerb, no plat edge) and hedgerows along L3 field-boundary chains (8-12 m); S14 draws offset, rotation and spacing (whole cm inside the class range, §4.9: 300-500 cm woods, 400-600 cm gardens) from the entity render.instances stream (§6.1) in the generation worker, carried in the InstanceTable row.

Stamp tiles: per stamped class four toroidal blue-noise tiles of 6 400 x 6 400 cm at reference spacing r0 = 400 cm (~162 points each at the textbook annulus, fixall_rendering_r5_seamstrip.out; ~175-180 at the shipped annulus, PLAUSIBLE until plat/tools/stamptiles/ builds the asset), each point with a progressive rank (void-and-cluster order; every prefix evenly spread; lowest-rank quarter keeps ~1.5-1.8 x r0 between any two points); seam-compatible: one shared border band (points with edge distance e = min(x, 6400-x, y, 6400-y) < r0/2), differing only inside it; an entity of spacing r stamps them scaled by s = r/r0 (a wood at 3 m stamps 48-m tiles, a garden at 6 m 96-m tiles).

No two instances of one stamp lie closer than the entity spacing (less <= 1.5 cm rounding): inside a cell by toroidal spacing at r0; across every seam between any two variants because a non-band point lies >= r0/2 from its cell edges and a band point is present at the same position in the other tile; every band draws a subset (ranks below s_b), so it holds at every band. Measured on five seed sets: 0 pairs closer than r0 across cells in all 256 arrangements of 2x2 cells for all ranks and the rank < 0.6 and < 0.25 subsets, vs 3.5-5 such pairs per 64-m seam for four independent tiles.

A stamp cell's tile variant is RH32('stamp.variant', key, salt, u, v) mod 4 (§8.1 item 5): only the band, ~11-14 % of a tile's points, repeats in every cell; tiles built once when the product is built and shipped; nothing samples or ranks at run time (J-R11, J-R48, J-R50, J-R55).

One construction everywhere: a class's band depends on the class alone, each tile on (class, tile index) and the band; built by plat/tools/stamptiles/ (build-time script) with @plat/kernel poisson module (§14), held to §6.5 allowlist lint; random source rng.stream (§6.1, §14) under key render.stampTiles and §6.1 registry components (J-R42). Sampling: Bridson with k = 50 candidates, all evaluated, in candidate annulus [r0, (1+a) r0] on the torus, a = poisson.annulus = 0.1 (provenance ref:sampler annulus of MFCG, NG 1.2.2, VG 1.6.9, Dwellings (code), P14; item 53; textbook a = 1 the alternative and the value the receipts used); accepted points rounded to integer cm, spacing test exact integer compare of squared toroidal distance with r0^2; first point (int(0,6399), int(0,6399)); active point int(0, n-1) over the insertion-ordered active list, retired replaced by the last; candidate at radius r0 x (1 + a x float01) along angle 2pi x float01 (dmath cos, sin, §6.5), tried in draw order. Band (creation index 4): full toroidal tile cut to points with e < 200 cm in index order. Each tile (creation index 0-3): band points pre-placed (spacing grid and initial active list), sampling continuing over e >= 200 cm, no first point drawn, candidates with e < 200 rejected; tile = band points then own in acceptance order.

Ranking per tile: each point's energy = sum over other points in point-index order of exp(-d^2/(2 sigma^2)) (d toroidal cm, sigma = r0, dmath.exp); the highest-energy point (tie: lower index) removed and given the highest free rank (n-1 first); remaining points subtract the removed point's term in point-index order (removal update: ~1.5 n^2 exponentials, O(n^2), never a re-sum per removal O(n^3): ~53 ms vs ~1.8 ms per tile at 161 points; ~2.2 ms at 178 points); a needed square root is Math.sqrt (exact by spec, §6.5 (2)); crown library shapes use dmath likewise so only sprite rasterisation is engine-specific; a class band and four tiles build in ~19.5 ms at the textbook annulus and ~24 ms at the shipped one (PLAUSIBLE until built); the annulus changes packing density, never construction, seam band or ranking (J-R11, J-R48, J-R50, J-R55; J-A53.81).

Shipped asset plat/assets/stamptiles/stamptiles.bin: per stamped class in registry order its four tiles, each self-contained band points first: point count, then per point x, y int16 cm and rank u16 (6 B per point, ~1.1 KB per tile, ~34 KB for eight classes), header naming asset version, format version, generating script and its constant key words (§17.1 (5)) and the stored H128 of every tile; @plat/render bundles the bytes into both workers' code (no extra host file, §11.2); at worker start each worker takes typed-array views and checks every tile H128 (~0.03-0.06 ms for 8-16 classes; budget §12.7).

Pre-decided fallback when a tile hash differs (damaged bundle): that worker rebuilds the class band and tiles with the same construction at start-up before its first district-band raster (~19.5 ms per class), reported; a rebuilt tile still differing is a determinism defect the census rebuild check (§8.3) fails in CI. Release changes: a new stamped class adds four tiles and moves no stored hash; a construction change (r0, sigma, k, tile side, band width, key words) moves stored hashes and is a render.stampTiles view shift (§13.3); a new spacing needs nothing (a scale).

Stamp: from the row offset o in [0, 6400)^2 whole reference cm, rotation rotationCdeg in [0, 36000) (S14 draws int(0, 35999)), scale s = spacing / 400 cm; R_theta cos and sin = dmath.cos/sin of rotationCdeg x (pi/18000) (a double literal); tile point t of cell (u, v) lies at R_theta . (s . (6400 . (u, v) + t + o)), each coordinate Math.round to whole cm = the instance's world position (read by face test, density test, drawing, override resolution, every export); cells of the rotated scaled lattice covering the face (bbox in lattice coordinates widened by one cell); a point survives if inside the face (exact point-in-polygon with holes on integer cm, §3.2) and, for woods, passes the edge test of a domain-warped density evaluated once per point at its world position in metres; rounding moves a point <= 0.71 cm (spacing kept less <= 1.5 cm); ordinal = (u, v, p), stable under face-boundary edits.

One result on every engine: the whole instance function (stamp, grid, line layouts, per-instance look draws, density test and all they call) is held to §6.5 (3) allowlist lint, so every engine computes the same integer positions and draws and a GeoJSON, glTF or CityJSON file with trees is byte-identical on every host (§11.1; five-engine golden run compares one, §13.3) (J-R52).

Grid: one point per cell (u, v) of the rotated lattice at the row spacing, jittered +/-15 % of spacing in x and y by two RH32 draws over (key, salt, u, v) (tags grid.jitter.x, grid.jitter.y), rounded to whole cm, kept if inside the face; ordinal (u, v). Line: point i at arc length (i + 1/2) x spacing from its start end (the end whose junction address sorts first; for an along row the end at its way's first junction), jittered along and across the same way, rounded; ordinal i. Park paths are L3 path faces drawn by the path program, not instances.

Rank and band thinning (N-10): normalised rank r in [0,1): stamp = progressive rank / tile point count; grid = 32-bit bit-reversal of the Morton interleave of (u, v) / 2^32 (2-D van der Corput); line = bit-reversal of i / 2^32 (J-R25); band b draws r < s_b (city none — the wood, orchard or green fill; district 0.6; neighbourhood and finer 1), so every coarser band is a subset of the finer: an instance keeps its position once visible and appears at most once in a zoom sweep (LC-20, VIS-5).

Per-instance look keyed by (key, ordinal): species drawn by share from Greenery.species (inner or outer share by distance from the edge) picks the crown class; crown index, colour jitter, scale jitter +/-15 % and leafType (from the species when present, else deciduous) are RH32 draws over (render key, ordinal, concern salt); hatch phase and roof detail keyed by the render key; nothing keyed by band or interned handle.

Crown library: 20 crowns per class per style, built once per session from rng.stream keyed by the sheet key (hash of id@version), STAGE_VIEW, concern style.crowns with its salt, and class and index i as creation index (§6.1 structured components; path form a report rendering, §14), drawn as sprites; on rungs 1-2 a crown sprite carries albedo and writes a dome's normals into the surface layer, one bake per style whatever the sun (item 68); on the vector rung a lit sheet bakes per (style, light step): once with a fixed sun, with a path sun again at each light step, in the tile worker as one-sprite units of §8.9 queue; drawn step's set always kept, a set a running export needs held until it completes (class 4), earlier sets kept while they fit §8.8 crown-and-atlas scratch.

Instance edits (LC-20): instance events (§7.1) apply after generation: remove drops the ordinal, move replaces its position, add appends user ordinal u<n> at point, restyle sets InstanceStyle; for an ordinal-addressed event the dry run records the generated position in point. Resolution (generation worker, whenever a commit touches an entity carrying overrides, re-running for that entity only): applies by ordinal when lineage unchanged since the event (no carry lifecycle event, no supersession after the event seq, §6.3) and that ordinal's generated position lies within 0.5 x spacing of point; otherwise (carried successor with fresh lineage, superseded entity whose overrides move to supersededBy, a moved ordinal) re-matches by position to the nearest unclaimed generated instance within 0.5 x spacing (candidates in (distance, ordinal) order, overrides in log order), else kept orphaned and reported (J-R24).

Resolution reads each positional override's current position from its entity's overrides table (§2.7): a move's to, an add's point, for a line layout the recorded generated point — written when the event applies and displaced with the host face by a warp or vertex move (§7.4); for stamp and grid the recorded generated point stays world-anchored; an add stays while its point is in the face (or within 0.5 x spacing of its line), orphaned otherwise; resolved overrides (ordinal, op, position, style, state byOrdinal|rematched|orphaned) cross to the tile worker as InstanceTable override rows (§8.1, §8.9); a tree brush is a batch of instance events (COV-FTG-M04).

Where instances run (N-4): generated per tile in the tile worker from the InstanceTable row, memoised per (key, revision, style version) for the session, never written to the document except as overrides; the generation worker runs the same function on the same shipped tiles for entities carrying overrides and for exports: GeoJSON, glTF and CityJSON exporters call it at the finest band with overrides applied and write each instance's position, species, crown diameter and leaf type (§11.1; VN-158, XB32); the bench computes tree statistics from it (SCL-21); budgets §12.7.

Label model (S13a; in the model hash; persisted): every entity name and short form; a LabelEntity per labelled thing with its candidates; the quarter merge tree (§9.4) and region groups over it (item 101).

LabelEntity { id; target; kind district|quarter|region|way|landmark|place|water|wood|gate|title|annotation|address; text NameRef; shortText?; priority; lod LodBand[]; displayText? (map-side display text drawn instead of the unchanged name, a dossier-owned name above all, §7.7 item 11, item 20 (h); set by setAttr, cleared by revert); candidates {spines Polyline[] in preference order (world cm), anchors {p, dirCdeg?}[], breakAt? allowed two-line breaks}; pinned? PinnedPlacement (model data); hidden? }.

QuarterNode { id; members (districts); children [Id, Id] | null; name NameRef; spine; cityCut (one of the min(N_q, L) quarters of the city cut, §4.5, L = number of districts: the city band's area labels) } — built by S6 (§4.5), named by S13a; every node has its own LabelEntity (kind quarter).

RegionGroup { id; name NameRef (set by its group event §7.1, then like any name); members (QuarterNode ids whose districts are disjoint: an Upper, Lower or Outer City); spine (S13a, from the union of members' faces by §9.3 area rule) } (item 101): a named region label group on the quarter tree; its LabelEntity kind region.

Placement (user placement set by moveLabel §7.1; model data, N-28) { stop (zoom stop §8.8 where placed); sizePx (cap height in display px at 1x, never below the kind floor §9.4); anchor PointCm (point labels: text origin; area/path: spine midpoint); spine? PolylineCm; dirCdeg?; lines? 1|2 (broken at the entity's first breakAt) }. PinnedPlacement extends Placement { seq: the moveLabel event seq; applying writes pinned = {...placement, seq}; a warp or vertex move carrying the pin keeps it; orders the pin pass }.
The title label entity carries the map title text as model data; the title is placed by §9.5 furniture rule (layer-order slot 24), not by S13b's greedy.

What the tree holds (items 65, 72, 82, 101, 70): node and district names from dominant identity and character (§10.4, item 72); a quarter the dossier claims carries its claimed name like any assigned name (§7.7 item 16, item 82) — S13a's naming, never a second rule; an undercity neighbourhood (II.7.5; item 65) is a leaf under its parent district node, named as the underside of that quarter, its labels candidates only while the underground layer is visible (§9.2); the sewer pseudo-district stays a leaf in a family of its own (II.7.3).

A region group (group event §7.1; J-A101.84) names any set of nodes whose districts are disjoint; its label drawn at city band above the city cut (§9.4); removed by delete or re-grouped by a new group; its registry row is §2.8's.
An informal cluster (item 70) has one LabelEntity of kind place targeting its plot — a place name from §10.4, never one per structure — and a named court or yard may take the same kind.
displayText is the drawing's text and nothing else: the reader, the gazetteer and every export give the name, with the display text beside it where one is set (§11.2).

Label view (S13b; never hashed; recomputed per zoom stop and cached, §9.2): which candidate each label uses, its size and glyph positions, the quarter cut, halo roles; pinned placements honoured by the pin pass; a pinned placement moves with its target under a warp or vertex move (§7.4).

Consequences: the model hash does not depend on fonts, viewport or DPR (O2 (a), O11 (f); GEO-29); model hashes and per-stop placement digests compared across Node, Chromium, Firefox, WebKit by §13.3 golden run; moveLabel (sets pinned) and hideLabel (sets hidden) are logged, hashed model events (§7.1); a scoped regeneration re-derives S13a only inside its scope (LC-17). Judgment call J-R12 (placement as view data, own font metrics).

Metrics: @plat/labels parses the bundled OFL font files itself (label faces §8.2, §17.2): cmap, hmtx, kern and GPOS pair adjustments (formats 1 and 2), GSUB single substitutions for smcp and onum, loca/glyf for SVG outline text (§11.1); advance widths and kerning in font units become world metres at a zoom stop; no contextual shaping (Latin faces, ligatures off); glyphs placed and drawn one by one (§8.9) so drawn equals measured on every backend and in SVG.

Font features (N-12): from M1 a PR-tier CI test asserts per bundled label face cmap, hmtx and TrueType glyf outlines and reports whether GSUB has smcp and onum single-substitution lookups for Latin; the label style takes a pre-decided path per face chosen by that test, never by hand: with smcp small caps from the face; without, the family's OFL small-caps cut (IM FELL Great Primer SC, bundled unmodified) measured by the same reader; with no such cut (a user face) small caps synthesised as capitals at 0.75 x cap height with letter-spacing kept; without onum the scale bar uses default figures; the style report names each face's path; census floors (§9.4) run on whichever path is active (J-R37).

Placement is computed per zoom stop (§8.8): at stop k each glyph box in world units = pixel box x metres per pixel; protected obstacles (gates, castle, plaza, bridges, walls — MFCG's measured defect) are their drawn symbol extents at that stop, and plan-draw room labels (§8.5) are obstacles at the building band; between stops the view uses the placement of the stop at or coarser than the current scale (zooming in only shrinks world boxes; crossing below a stop switches to that coarser stop), so zero collisions hold at every zoom.

S13b reads the display list through ObstacleSource and RoleIndex (§14); both implementations, what they call and the S14 writers of the columns they read are under §6.5 (3) allowlist lint, so S13b inputs are bit-identical on every engine and §13.3 placement digests compare across the five engines; a symbol's rotated extent is computed with dmath, never Math.cos or Math.hypot.

Candidate set of a stop is fixed before the greedy runs: every LabelTable row drawn at the band whose layer is visible (LayerSpec.visible §8.4 — a hidden underground or sky layer's district, tunnel and cell labels are not candidates) and that the knowledge filter admits, minus the labels §9.4 rung (5) hands to a quarter at this stop, plus the quarter candidates rung (5) creates (N-11); rung (5) decided from geometry alone and the filter from one byte per row, so the set is known before any collision test.

Knowledge filter (item 30; the label policy's home; J-A30.81): knowledge is separate from geometry — a hidden or clandestine place is always on the map (faces, masses, walls, doors at every band); what is withheld is its name and purpose; every label row carries its target's knownTo (public, local, secret), filled by S14 from the plot, building or institution record (§2.5-§2.7 with §7.7; a plot default from its exposure, §2.5); ways, districts, quarters, water bodies, woods, gates, title, annotations are public; every viewer holds a knowledge key = per-viewer view key knowledge (tier and places, §2.9; default and authority §11.3).

Admission table (row at a stop, band = the stop's §8.5; never at a band its lodMask excludes): public -> at its kind's bands for every tier; local (known to those who grew up there) -> tier public: neighbourhood band and finer only; tier local and secret (or place in places): at its kind's bands; secret (known only to those who were told) -> tier public: building band only (its own view, J-A30.83); local: building band only; secret or in places: at its kind's bands.

The table is data (item 23; J-A30.86): knowledge.admit, a §7.6 rule table keyed by (knownTo, tier) whose one cell is coarsest: LodBand (city = at its kind's bands); read by S13b candidate set, the reader (§11.2), the legend (§9.5) and every picture and interchange export (§11.1); shipped rows = the table above; a region, era or setting may change them; only editTable edits it (a logged event only owner and editor roles send, §11.3), never a style sheet or a viewer's stylePreset.

The loader refuses — and an editTable fails its dry run with invalid (§7.1) — a table in which a public row is not city or a higher tier admits a row at a finer band than a lower tier does (more knowledge never shows less); an edit re-derives no entity (its readers are view passes) and re-places every stop (memo keyed by the table's version).
