The filter is applied before rung (5) and before any pin or collision test, so the local evaluation is unchanged; a withheld row is not a candidate and blocks nothing, its area or way labelled (where rung (5) allows) by its public quarter; a pinned or user-hidden label is filtered the same way; knownTo is model data (setAttr(knownTo) logged §7.1; a dossier-backed place's value is the dossier's §7.7) while the knowledge key is view data, so the model digest never depends on who is looking; the reader (hover and every query kind §11.2), legend (§9.5) and every picture and interchange export (§11.1) withhold the same names by the same table, a reader without a band admitting as at the city band (§11.2); no reference has knowledge or hidden places (item 23): every reference row public, filter admits all.

Concealed parts (item 63; J-A63.81): a clandestine building's hidden function is its own Use record (§2.7) with its own knownTo (default secret); one table withholds its label row, its purpose in every reader and export, and — the one refinement of J-A30.83's 'never its geometry' — the marks of its concealed parts (concealed rooms, concealed entrance tick and door, concealed access down; §2.6, II.7.4), each carrying the concealed use knownTo (§8.1 item 7); a non-admitting viewer sees the building exactly as its front (mass, walls, public rooms, main and service doors, the front's label, every band), no trace of concealed parts; a knowing viewer (tier secret or place in places) sees them all; the building itself is never withheld.

Secret ways down and between systems (items 64, 65): an AccessPoint or UndergroundLink whose knownTo the key does not admit draws nothing and labels nothing; a secret underground place (a guild seat in the undercity, a smugglers' passage) is withheld by the same table; hiding the underground layer hides them all, showing it admits them only by the key.

Which facts are the dossier's (item 20 (h); J-A20.82): the reader (§11.2) gives beside every admitted fact its tier by §2.8 factTier — dossier (immutable on the map; changed only by a dossier event), declared (an author's declaration, held, item 101) or map (derived); the tier never widens what the key admits.

The clerk (item 101) reads only through this reader with its viewer's key — its why answers under §11.2 rule for the oracle (a front explained as its front, a concealed use left out) and its proposals (preview) an editing role's — so it knows and says no more than that viewer may know (§11.2 Knowledge; item 63 (c)).

The greedy: candidates at a stop totally ordered by priority (numeric LabelEntity.priority; default region > quarter/district > water > landmark > place > gate > way > address), then larger target area (areaM2), then id; a candidate takes its first alternate (spines in order, then §9.4 ladder) meeting no placed higher candidate, no obstacle and no fixed pin, else yields; the whole-map greedy is evaluated locally: deciding c first decides (memoised) every higher candidate whose alternate boxes meet c's; the dependency graph is acyclic (strict order), so the result is independent of tile order and viewport.

LabelRows { labels LabelTable; strings StringTable; geom GeomTable } in @plat/model beside LodBand, Role, ZoomStop: the rows S13b reads; the tile worker's display list and each export's transient list implement it; LabelEntity stays the model record S13a writes and S14 reads.

LabelPlacer (@plat/labels, §14): begin(stop, labels, obstacles ObstacleSource, roles RoleIndex, fonts FontMetrics, memo PlacementMemo) -> PlacementJob; place(same) -> PlacementSet (begin then step(Infinity): SVG exports and tests). PlacementJob { step(deadlineMs) -> boolean (returns after the first unit ending deadlineMs or more after the call began; true when complete); result() -> PlacementSet; cancel() (memo entries stay valid, keyed by stop, candidate id and revision); readonly spentMs }.

Placement unit: the rung-(5) test of one LabelTable row; one pin of the pin pass; one step of the local evaluation on an explicit stack (push the highest undecided candidate whose alternate boxes meet the top's, or when all such are decided decide the top, write the memo and pop); or the glyph layout of one placed label; roots in strict order, pins first; stack and memo persist between steps; every decision reads only decided candidates, so step boundaries never change the result (whole vs one unit per step give identical placement digests, §8.3, §13.3); a unit ~1 us average, tens of us at most (overrun one unit); the view job reads the tile worker's list: a delta between steps drops memo entries its dirty boxes invalidate and, when it changes a label row or an obstacle of the job's stop, the job is begun again keeping valid memo entries; an export's job reads its own immutable transient list (§11.1) (J-R51).

Pin pass (N-28): a pinned label shows only in its bands; at its own stop and every finer stop placed exactly as left, before any other candidate: eligible pins (in band, own stop at this or coarser) in moveLabel seq order then label id (LabelTable.pinSeq); each whose box meets no fixed pin becomes a fixed pin (obstacle every candidate avoids); a pin meeting an already fixed pin is hidden at that stop and reported ('pinned label hidden: overlaps pin P at stop k'); a strict-order greedy evaluated locally (deciding a pin decides memoised every earlier pin its box meets); pin boxes are pixel-sized so zooming in only shrinks them: a pin fixed at k meets nothing new finer; a pin hidden at k is fixed again where boxes part; at a coarser stop a pin is not fixed: it keeps anchor and spine and enters the greedy as a candidate at its entity priority whose only alternate is that placement, drawn when clear else hidden and reported ('pinned label hidden at stops coarser than k'); zero collisions at every zoom with pins (J-R26, J-R45).

moveLabel's dry run (§7.1) refuses a placement whose box at its stop meets another pinned label's box at that stop, returning the nearest free position as the conflict's action (the interactive guard); the pin pass is the guarantee because pins also meet without a moveLabel: warp or vertex move carrying them (§7.4), a setAttr rename or ids-scoped rerollLayer(naming) lengthening text (§9.6), a setStyle changing face widths.

Pin test (B-ZOOM §13.4): two pins 20 px apart brought together by a warp, and two brought together by a rename lengthening the earlier pin text — at every stop 0 collisions, the later pin reported hidden where boxes meet, per-stop placement digests (§13.3) identical after a log replay.

Scope: area and way labels for all candidates of the band; addresses and repeated street names only for candidates in visible tiles and their dependency closure; memo keyed by (stop, candidate id, candidate revision) and held per knowledge key, knowledge.admit version and view rotation (a changed key, table or rotation re-places the stop; rotation because §9.3 orders an area label's stored spines by on-screen horizontality, item 55); a stop's placement digest (§13.3) is per (stop, knowledge key, rotation), goldens taken at public tier with no places under the shipped table at rotation 0.

Incremental (SCL-9): after an edit memo entries of candidates whose boxes meet dirty boxes are dropped and re-decided; a change propagates only through candidates whose outcome changes (the priority cascade stops when nothing more moves).
Label placement budget (SCL-10) is §12.7: in the tile worker from the label rows alone (§8.9); an export placement in class-4 steps (§8.9).

Area labels (districts, quarters, regions, places, water bodies, woods; GEO-39): face simplified by the kernel's topology-preserving Visvalingam (simplify §3.4: a removal refused when the new edge would cross another edge of the face or holes, checked in the kernel index) to half the label cap height at the band's coarsest stop; hole-aware straight skeleton (skeleton(rings, 'spine') §3.8, gated by its validator: connected, one independent cycle per hole) as a planar graph; each edge's clearance = smaller event time of its ends; maximum-clearance spanning tree (Kruskal by clearance descending, ties by edge index) drops the lowest-clearance edge of every cycle; spine = longest path of that tree (two linear passes), smoothed (Visvalingam -> centripetal Catmull-Rom) and curvature-limited by §13.7 O13 (a) threshold and fallback; on F-SKELETON the medial axis of boundary samples is processed the same way.

Area candidates in order: the horizontal spine (among the tree's leaf-to-leaf paths the one maximising length plus horizontal extent, over every pair of leaves when <= 64 leaves, else not offered; scored in model coordinates, model north up, so it depends on the model only; provenance ref:MFCG label path choice (code), P16; item 55; J-A55.81); the spine; the spine trimmed to its central 80 %; the OBB-axis straight line; the OBB arc. The construction stays ours: hole-aware, clearance-first, never retried with jittered vertices.

Under a rotated view (rotation view key §9.5) S13b takes an area label's stored spines in descending order of their on-screen horizontal extent — a view-side order of model candidates (memo held per rotation); at rotation 0 the stored order stands.

Path labels (streets — new to all four references —, rivers, walls): along the centreline at district and neighbourhood bands, repeated per segment above 12 em of length, kept upright (flipped when the tangent points left).

Point labels (gates, bridges, landmarks): eight anchor offsets; a leader line when the footprint is under 12 px; with the style's labels.leaders 'always' (default 'small', the 12-px rule) a leader for every landmark label at the city band — the switch the authoring toolkit's T11 name exposes (item 101; J-A101.84; a style value, no model change).

LabelStyle.leaders: 'always' | 'small' (default) — a field of StyleSheet.labels (LabelStyle), named only here; LabelStyle's other fields (faces, floors, halo rule) are cited to §9.4 but LabelStyle is not declared as a type anywhere in §8 or §9.
Addresses: the numbering is model data (S13a: monotone along each way, per side); the numbers are placed as view data at the neighbourhood band.

Legibility floors (display px at 1x): area labels cap height >= 7 px (and <= 14 px, proportional to sqrt(area) within the band); way labels cap >= 6 px; point labels >= 6 px; addresses >= 5 px; room labels cap 5-9 px, each sized in that range by §8.5 plan draw (J-A28.87); region labels (item 101) cap 1.25 x the city cut's largest quarter label and <= 18 px, letter-spaced 0.25 em, city band only; place labels (item 70) as area labels, from the district band; area labels letter-spaced small caps (0.15 em).

F-LABEL ladder, view side (every rung reached counted in the report): (1) preferred spine at size proportional to sqrt(area), never below the floor; (2) short name form; (3) straight label on the OBB axis on one line or two lines broken at a space (at a breakAt position); (4) the OBB arc; (5) the quarter tree (N-11); (6) a declared overflow: <= 20 % of glyph area outside the face, never over a protected obstacle or another label; (7) a legend entry: numbered disc on the face and a row in the legend (§9.5).

Rung (5) quarter tree: decided per stop before the greedy from geometry alone: when none of rungs 1-4 fits the label's own face at the floor at this stop, the label yields to the smallest ancestor QuarterNode (via LabelTable.parent) whose spine fits that node's own name at the floor; the yielding label is suppressed at that stop and reported ('named by quarter Q at stops k..k'); the ancestor's own LabelEntity becomes a candidate once (not again when the stop's cut already labels the node) with the highest priority among yielding members, the node's area and the node's label id, fixing its place in the strict order; it then takes its own alternates (spines and rungs 3, 4, 6, 7); members whose rungs fit keep their labels, ordered against it like any candidate (J-R27).

Quarters (VIS-4, MFP-10): S6 builds the merge tree of districts once per model by §4.5 rule; S13a names each internal node from the grammar conditioned on members' dominant identity (item 72) and kind and on the naming feature of its largest member (§10.4), spine from its union (§9.3); names, spines and the city cut (the min(N_q, L) nodes of §4.5 city cut; fixall_pipeline_r2_quarters.out, J-P28 column; MFCG's label count; flagged cityCut) are model data; the city band labels the city cut; a stop between city and district bands may use a finer cut (finest nodes whose spine fits the floor), view data; the district band labels districts.
owner_raw: rendering (labelling); the merge tree and city-cut count: pipeline §4.5

statement: Region groups (item 101) sit above the tree: each a candidate at the city band with the highest priority of §9.2 order, spine from members' union; the city cut's labels inside it, decided after it, avoid it taking their next alternate or rung (item 101 (g) 'labels re-flow around the change'; J-A101.84); a region that cannot fit its floor at a stop is hidden there and reported, never rung (5)'s quarter substitution; acceptance is read on the default view, which holds no region group.

Halo (VIS-15, N-3): each glyph's halo 1.5 px wide takes the role of the area mark under the glyph centre (display-list index at the label band: ground, road, water, field, green, ...) when the text colour against that role passes the label floor (§8.2 ink/ground row), otherwise ground (which passes by that row in every accepted palette); over masses and woods the halo is the block ground tone (J-R28); shipped palettes keep the local role over paper, road, ground, court, field, verge, green in every family and over garden and water in ink and hatched; ground replaces building and tree in every family and garden and water in lit (fixall_rendering_r2_palette.out); SVG writes the halo as a paint-order stroke per glyph; a palette accepted with accept-low-contrast may fail the floor, the report listing failing pairs; at night (item 68) halos and text keep day colours (composed after the light pass, never lit; halo role read from the day palette even where the vector rung draws @night roles), so the label floor holds in every light and on every rung.

Label acceptance (B-ZOOM; default view of every rung; bundled font): every node of the city cut (min(N_q, number of districts), §4.5) labelled at or above the floor, at matched sizes within +/-1 of the 9 / 12 / 18 district labels MFCG's plain sweep draws at sizes 40 / 80 / 130 (captures/mfcg/exports-sweep-2026-09-25/README.md); 0 protected overlaps; 0 collisions at settled views and during a scripted zoom sweep, pins included; every placed glyph text/halo pair at or above the label floor from rendered pixels (§8.3); overflows, legend fallbacks, quarter substitutions, hidden pins reported; >= 99 % of area-label glyph area inside its face (O13 a); >= 90 % of named streets labelled at the neighbourhood band (O13 b).
Pre-decided fallback if a rung labels fewer than its city cut at M1: the default framing percentile (§9.5) tightens from 95 % to 85 %, enlarging every district on screen, and the check re-runs.
Scale bar: metres <-> feet, major and minor ticks, old-style figures (onum); a 100 m bar accurate to 0.5 % at every zoom (O6 c).

Compass (XB08): procedural 8-ray design with ink and paper halves, rerollable per town: stream keyed from the town root entity key (§6.1, §14 TOWN_ROOT) with concern style.compass and its salt, so a reroll is a logged rerollLayer('style.compass') event and a link or copy draws the same compass.

Compass auto-placement: candidates four corners and four edge midpoints inset 24 px; score = sum over display-list marks the compass would cover (labels x3, protected features x3, buildings x1, ways x1, water x0.2, paper 0) + 0.5 x (1 - distance from view centre / half-diagonal); lowest wins, ties NE, NW, SE, SW, N, E, S, W; re-evaluated when the view settles; covers computed in the tile worker by ObstacleSource.coverage per candidate box via §8.9 furniture query; dragging places and the wheel rotates it (view state §11.3) and pins the compass; view key compass = trueNorth (default: needle at model north whatever the view rotation) or free; the map's own rotation is the rotation view key about the frame centre (§2.9, §7.1: MFCG Rotate as a view rotation, never a model change).

Grid (XB15): kind none | square | hex (pointy or flat) | mesh (triangular); cell size in metres or feet (default a round ground distance ~1/10 of the view short side on a 1-2-5 sequence; for VTT the export declared grid §11.1); colour role grid; fades out below its legibility zoom (cell < 12 px); skip water clips grid strokes out of water faces (on by default for overview grids, off for VTT grids).

Title: text is the title label entity (§9.1); placed in the emptiest corner (NG rule: the corner whose box covers least mark area, the sum of its coverage record from the same furniture query); movable; a dossier-bound map's size word is the dossier's own tier word (a SettlementForge 'city' of 5 001 people drawn on the TOWN rung titled a city; a dossier fact, §7.7 item 15; item 81; J-A81.72); a standalone map's word is its rung's.

Legend (J04): a gazetteer panel — embedded title, numbered districts (always in legend mode; in labels mode only for legend fallbacks), lettered landmarks, scale bar and emblem; numbered and lettered lists honour §9.2 knowledge filter (a non-admitted place gets no number, letter or row, item 30); border none | single | double rule; position any corner (default emptiest corner other than the title's) or free; metric or imperial; label modes labels (default), legend (districts numbered on the map, MFCG Districts = Legend), hidden; plus the symbol key generated from the registry (O12 d); position, mode and border are view state.

Emblem (M06): furniture slot Emblem = { source none|import|generated; svg?; png?; generated? EmblemSpec }; imports sanitised (no scripts, no external references, <= 64 KB); base ships a minimal own generator: EmblemSpec = a field tincture from the palette roles, one of eight partitions or ordinaries (per pale, per fess, per bend, chevron, cross, saltire, chief, bordure) and zero or one geometric charge (roundel, lozenge, mullet), keyed from the town root entity key with concern naming.emblem and its salt (rerolled by rerollLayer('naming.emblem')); off by default; drawn in the legend or a corner (J-R13).
Annotation layer (numbered markers and a separate legend sheet); north arrow.

Measure tool (L10, L08): an @plat/app ruler — click points for a polyline length in metres and feet; area mode for a polygon area in m^2, ha, acres; snapping to way centrelines, face edges and vertices through the display-list index (8 px radius) — RoleIndex.snap in the tile worker via §8.9 snap query answered within one frame, unsnapped point shown until the answer; exact in world cm; a measurement is view data and can be saved as an annotation.

Authoring surfaces (item 101 (i); R3, R4, R14, R16): while a declaration is drawn or a derived shape is selected, the main thread draws handles (four to eight by default, more on request) over the live.ghost preview; dragging one is a new declaration of the same kind on the same entity (§7.1); the feature snap lights the candidate edge (street centre-line, shore, wall, ridge, block edge) within 8 px via RoleIndex.snap as the ruler's, Alt places freely; the snap is resolved into the event's points before its dry run (§7.1), the kernel's own attraction still applying to every insertion (§3.6); the count badge beside the ghost shows what an area declaration (quarter, fill, roster) will hold — plots, households, buildings from the dry run — with plus and minus re-running the dry run at one more or fewer; numbers while drawing (way length, area in ha); all screen-space furniture: never exported, never in the model, never read by the clerk.

Underlay (item 101, T12 dress; J-A101.81): an image dropped under the map to trace: per-viewer view key underlay (§2.9: image, opacity 0-1 default 0.5, frame as a world-cm affine placement with four handles); the compositor draws it first and the composed tiles over it at 1 - opacity, without re-rastering; never exported, never in a digest, never crosses the bridge (§11.3); no model code or clerk reads it.

Framing (A06): the initial view and the default export frame = circle centred on the settlement centre with radius max(outer enceinte radius, 95th percentile of footprint distances from the centre) x 1.08, fitted to the viewport short side (no letterbox); river tails and ribbon tips beyond the percentile outside unless the user frames them; a user frame is view state; furniture sizes are CSS px x a UI scale; device pixels handled by the tiles.

Names come from §10.4's original grammar conditioned on the model (a docks district for its water, a gate ward for its gate, a street for its destination or trade — R16), drawn from the entity's naming stream only in §6.3's four cases; a successor keeps its predecessor's name and naming record with its address (§6.3).

Name uniqueness (LC-17) within its kind — districts, quarters and water bodies per town; ways per district; tier-1 ways town-wide: in a full generation resolved in id order; a later entity repeating an earlier name re-draws on its own .../attempt=n (<= 8), then takes a distinguishing suffix; in a scoped regeneration or edit, entities outside the scope fixed and only inside re-draw; an existing entity is never renamed by another's creation; the locality oracle, comparing against a replay of the same log, resolves collisions the same way; equal names brought together by carrying and features as non-inputs are §6.3's.
Names are rerollable (rerollLayer(naming), town-wide or with ids, §7.1), editable (setAttr) and persisted; the word lists are spell-checked in CI.

Names test (B-EDIT): a block reroll changes 0 names and 0 LabelEntity records outside its scope; placement changes outside the scope counted and reported as view changes; selecting a user corpus renames exactly the unedited names drawn from the field it replaces and no other (not the district names drawn through the same row, §6.3).

Names from character, places and claims (items 70, 72, 82): district and quarter node names follow identity and character (§4.5, §10.4; item 72); a district whose identity changes past its hysteresis at an epoch re-draws its unprotected name by §6.3 epoch case, the old name kept in District.nameHistory which the reader shows as a former name, resolved by the uniqueness rule; an informal cluster takes one place name drawn once for its plot (§10.4; item 70), its structures unnamed; a quarter name the dossier claims (§7.7 item 16; item 82) is protected, re-matched only past the identity hysteresis; a map-side display text a user sets belongs to the label (LabelEntity.displayText), never to the name.
native .plat: §2.9 format and canonical form; byte-identical round trip tested in §13.2; import of our own export (MFCG cannot re-import; FTG export differs from its edit format).

JSON schema: published, versioned, generated from the zod types; entities by id with containment; a plan block per building whose plan rung is not absent with its state (§2.8) on the block (§2.6; items 28, 28 (f); J-A28.84): storeys with rooms (address, ring in integer cm, role, scope unit|shared|service|circulation, and for a unit room the household address), walls by kind, openings (kind, width, the entrance served) and windows; plan units (household address, unit form, entry opening), stair cores, chimneys; output version and supersedes table; every record's fields with tier by §2.8 factTier (dossier, declared, map; item 20 (h)); each event's authorship with the log (item 101 R19); each district's character vector, identity, band range, name history (item 72); each Works with its stage at the export drawn week (§4.11; item 67); each LightSource (item 68); a clandestine building's concealed use and parts (item 63), document formats admitted whole; own schema, never a cell grid; = the API response type.

compact twin: CBOR with typed-array tags; varint zig-zag int32 cm in world coordinates, settlement centre in the header, an encoding of the same schema (FTG-21); used for embeds and sharing; a decoder is part of the library.

GeoJSON (RFC 7946): two variants (N-14): default strict RFC 7946 in WGS84 lon/lat through the geo anchor, and metric by prior arrangement; no crs member; one FeatureCollection per layer; one feature per entity with id (address §6.3), kind, layer, epoch, public attributes; districts included; ways LineStrings with class and model width; faces Polygons with holes without antennae (§3.6 (6)); MultiPolygons for unions; walls, towers, gates and built bridges typed features (crossing site not exported §2.7); boundary treatments LineStrings with treatment (VIS-8); trees per green entity one MultiPoint of instance positions (§8.10 at finest band, overrides applied, integer cm under §6.5 lint, byte-identical) with species[], crownM[], leafType[], or one Feature per tree on request, or none (VN-158, XB32); model widths only; public attributes include lifecycle states (existence, condition, wall supersededBy, tunnel closure, island state; items 8, 11, 31), plot exposure and knownTo, building knownTo, institution knownTo on its buildings (item 30), building entrances as points with roles (item 29), underground building baseCm as depth and eaveCm as ceiling, tunnel invert profile (II.7), market reservation rank (§4.2), building worksStage at drawn week (item 67), access point state (item 64), each gallery, chamber, link with system, kind, depthBand (II.7.6; item 65), district identity and band range (item 72), each lit LightSource whose host draws for the key as a Point with kind, heightM, intensityCd, radiusM, colour (item 68), every property tier as plat:tier (item 20 (h)); name and purpose a key does not admit withheld (feature stays); concealed-use features and secret access or link left out with their lights; a fallen island archived arena not exported (II.6). CI: default file validated by an open RFC 7946 validator and loaded by the scripted QGIS test (O11 d); metric file geometry validity and sidecar schema checked.

SVG: written from a transient display list at a declared band — city by default; district on request after a size estimate; neighbourhood only for a district-sized or smaller scope; groups <g id='layer.ground'><g id='sem.building.footprint'> per layer and semantic; one compound <path> per (semantic, district) with a <metadata> JSON map from subpath index ranges to entity ids; trees one compound path per green entity (crowns at district band, wood outline at city band); text (N-13; text option) by default as outlines (each glyph once in <defs> from the bundled face glyf outlines, quadratic segments as Q; each placed glyph a <use> at S13b's per-glyph position; label text in aria-label and <title>) or with text 'embedded' as editable <text> (curved per glyph; straight as one <text> with per-glyph x) in the bundled face embedded unmodified as @font-face data URI (OFL; no subsetting §17.2) (J-R32); halos by paint-order; hatching compound paths; symbol widths; light (item 68) as vector-rung shadows in <g id='layer.shadow'> and glow sprites, or with lighting 'raster' one embedded raster lighting layer from the CPU reference in <g id='layer.light'> multiplied over the base; colour-matrix post ops as one filter on wrapper <g id='lit'> holding every base layer group, layer.shadow, glows and layer.light, under label groups. Budgets §12.7; CI opens the METROPOLIS file in Inkscape headless (PNG within 120 s) and checks every layer id (O11 h; SCL-14, VIS-18); outline-file Inkscape PNG and embedded-file Chromium PNG each match PLAT's own PNG within §13.4 threshold.
(alias) VectorBackend.write — the SVG writer (defined in §8.9 code) running in the generation worker over the export transient list.

PNG/tiles: §8.8 band-streamed tile assembly at any DPI, rastered in the tile worker from the export transient list and lit by §8.4 CPU reference at the request light setting (fixed or path sun by day, moon and lights at night; no pointer; item 68); transparent background; per-layer transparent PNGs; print presets A4..A2 at 300 dpi; bar O12 (e): A2 at 300 dpi with no canvas larger than one tile band.

VTT: Foundry-class scene JSON and Universal VTT (.dd2vtt) by the profile, one scene set per model layer (ground; sky per island; underground one scene per depth band at that band's depth with every system of the layer in it, II.7.6; item 65) with its elevation, plus one scene per storey of a building whose plan rung exists (item 28); model widths only; grid alignment error 0 px per cell (O11 g); no manual steps on import.

3-D glTF 2.0 binary (D-8): ground as one planar partition (plat leaf faces at the finest committed level, each boundary read once from the arena §3.9, each face once, clipped to terrain cells and draped by bilinear sample, material by role); rivers as sloped surfaces (water level at each vertex = nearest course station, monotone downstream along S1's carved course); lakes, ponds, sea level planes (GEO-40); buildings extruded from baseCm (FTG-13) to eave with roof meshes to ridge per wing; each wing spanning a passage also extruded over its span ring from passage headroomCm above that wing's base to its eave (stepped front quads each), passage open beneath; basement (§2.6; item 29) extruded down from baseCm by its storeys inside its inset ring; underground cell or vault (II.7.3) at its own depth; roof by wing kind as §8.6; foundation skirt to terrain (§2.6); walls, towers, gatehouses prisms; bridge and pier decks at deckCm; trees as instanced crown meshes (EXT_mesh_gpu_instancing, positions from §8.10), one instancing node per (green entity, crown class) with extras: entity address and per instance species, crownM, leafType (XB32); a Works building at stage heights at the export drawn week (item 67); lights as KHR_lights_punctual (point light per lit LightSource: position, colour, candela, range = radius; one directional light for the fixed sun; underground lights in that layer's node; only where host draws for the key). OBJ as a flat secondary (one mesh per entity). Shadows, glTF and CityJSON agree by construction (heights are model data, §2.6).

CityJSON 2.0: transform scale [0.01,0.01,0.01] + translate so every vertex is integer cm (lossless); Building (LoD1.2 solid base to eave; LoD2.2 roof surfaces; over a passage the spanning wings' span-ring prisms from headroomCm above base to eave, passage open), WaterBody, Road (lines with class and width sampled from the width profile §2.2 rule 5), PlantCover, SolitaryVegetationObject (trees from §8.10, one per instance, GeometryInstance of the crown class template with species, crownDiameter, height; XB32), LandUse, OtherConstruction (walls, towers, gatehouses), Tunnel (swept from invert profile and bore), Bridge, TINRelief; basement as a BuildingPart below baseCm, underground cell as a Building whose base is below the datum (items 12, 29); Works building at stage heights at drawn week (item 67); no referenceSystem; geo anchor recorded in root property +platGeoAnchor {latDeg, lonDeg, bearingDeg} defined by PLAT's own CityJSON Extension listed in extensions (DEF-5); CI validates anchor-less file as is and anchored file with the extension schema from the repository.
CSV/statistics: the statistics record per generation with provenance (O6 d); people, buildings, plots; the corpus-calibration input.
permalinks: §6.4 format and refusal rule; &doc= references resolve through §11.5 DocResolver; a document format under Knowledge, offered only to a key of tier secret.

skeleton (item 101): the document's declared subset — a .plat document with no model whose log is the recipe intent and, in log order, every event whose entities §2.8 factTier reads declared (author declarations incl. sugar events, §7.1), each marked creation, so importing makes them the creation prefix of a new document whose stages read its drawn declarations ahead (§4.1, §7.7); with the same seed a skeleton exported and re-imported reproduces the city byte for byte (§6.5 (9) skeleton round trip); a clerk transcript of tool calls is itself a valid skeleton; a document format under Knowledge.
Rotation: picture exports (SVG, PNG, VTT) use the view rotation (§9.5); GeoJSON keeps model coordinates and records the rotation.

Export knowledge (item 30; J-A30.83, J-A30.85): every picture and interchange export takes the requesting viewer's knowledge key with the view state (§11.3): a shared SVG, PNG, VTT scene or GeoJSON carries no name or purpose of a local or secret place the key does not admit (the place, faces and doors stay), none of a concealed use's concealed parts (rooms, door, way down; item 63) or of a secret access or link (items 64, 65), nor their hosts' lights, glows, shafts (§8.1 item 7; J-A63.82); a picture admits at the band it draws (SVG its declared band, raster its export stop band, a storey scene building band); a file without a band (GeoJSON, CityJSON, glTF extras, CSV, scene journal entries) admits as at the city band (§11.2); document formats (.plat, compact twin, JSON schema, permalink) carry every name and are admitted whole or not at all: export offers them only to a key of tier secret (owner and editor roles by default §11.3; a script's by-value exportDocument runs as owner) and refuses any other with API error E_KNOWLEDGE_TIER naming the needed tier; the key governs what the module shows and writes, not what a client loading the document holds — a host keeping a place secret sends pictures and interchange exports, never the document.

Authorship and tiers in every export (items 20 (h), 101 R19; J-A101.82): every model and interchange format carries per record or feature the tier of each fact by §2.8 factTier (dossier, declared, map); every format carrying the log (.plat, compact twin, JSON schema, skeleton) carries each event's author, its proposedBy: 'clerk' where a clerk proposed it (§7.1) and its dossierChange where the dossier caused it (§7.7 item 13); a picture's metadata (SVG <metadata>, PNG text chunk, VTT scene plat object) states the share of its entities in each tier and whether any clerk-proposed event made them.

Inert exports (item 85 (c); J-A85.81): every text node, attribute value and metadata string escaped by its format's rule (XML escaping in SVG and XML text, JSON string escaping, VTT JSON), so a dossier name or another user's edit never becomes active content; the SVG writer emits no script element, no event attribute, no foreignObject and no external reference (fonts and images as data URIs, §17.2); §9.5 emblem imports stay sanitised; the bar (CI runs hostile names through every exporter and asserts inert, well-formed output) is §13.2's.

Display names (item 85 (b)): a host may pass HostContext.displayNames (dossier key -> text; §14) with one export request; the exporter draws those texts for that request only and writes them nowhere else — never into the document, a cache or a later export.

Two GeoJSON variants (N-14): default writes WGS84 lon/lat (RFC 7946 removed crs); geo anchor {latDeg, lonDeg, bearingDeg} places the settlement centre and turns model north by the bearing; an export option remembered per document in view key exportAnchor (§11.3), default (0,0,0) — the conventional no-real-location point; for a dossier-bound map whose host supplies the optional realm block (item 77; §14), the port's realm fit sets bearingDeg (turn of model north fitting derived gates to partners' true bearings, §7.7 layer 2) as the key's documented default, no geometry moving; each model vertex (x, y) in metres rotated by the bearing is a transverse Mercator easting/northing (scale 1 on the central meridian through the anchor, false origin at the anchor) inverted to WGS84 by Krueger's series to fourth order in the third flattening, evaluated with dmath (byte-identical); 7 decimals (~1 cm); exterior rings CCW, holes CW (RFC 7946 3.1.6); GIS ellipsoid distances match model distances within 1 + (d/R)^2/2 (<= 3.1e-6, <= 5 cm at the farthest corner of the largest frame, ~15.7 km at aspect 2, §12.2); foreign member plat records the anchor, whether default, the document id and output version; metric variant (RFC 7946 §4 prior arrangement) writes x east, y north in metres from the settlement centre with 2 decimals, no crs, in <name>.metric.geojson beside sidecar <name>.metric.json (origin, unit, axes, document id, anchor if set) (J-R31).

Where exports run: every export(h, fmt) runs in the generation worker (holds the document, §8.9). Model formats (.plat, JSON schema, compact twin, GeoJSON, glTF/OBJ, CityJSON, CSV, permalinks) read the model and §8.10 instance function (Exporter.write(doc, null, opts)) — except the JSON schema's plan blocks, which carry every stored plan and the derived plans the exporting session's elaboration cache holds, each with its rung state (§2.8), so which derived plans a JSON export carries depends on what was clicked (cache non-canonical, §2.9; J-A28.86).

SVG needs a display list and label placement at the export's own stop (§8.7) while the generation worker keeps only a 24-B index: the SVG exporter builds a transient list for the export's band and frame with DisplayListBuilder.build(model, band) (~4 us per building at the city band), runs S13b there at the export stop through @plat/labels with @plat/render's ObstacleSource and RoleIndex over that list (the code the tile worker runs, export frame as the visible region of §9.2 scope, so placement equals the tile worker's and §13.3 digests test the code both run), writes the file and releases the list (time §12.7; list = §12.8 export-time peak); a district-band SVG's list is counted in the size estimate shown before writing (J-R41).

Raster formats (PNG, print, .dd2vtt scene image) use a transient list built the same way for the export band and frame (including the live layers its layer set names, as their providers stand at the request), transferred with the raster-export request (§8.9) carrying the look and view state at the request (sheet, §8.8 switches, shadow sun, light step); in the export class the tile worker runs S13b at the export stop over the list with the export frame as visible region, bakes the request's crown set when not cached (lit, path sun) and holds it until completion, rasters every tile with the request look by §8.8 band-streamed assembly, streams bytes and a progress message per band back, releases the list; the generation worker wraps the VTT scene around the image; the export shows the model, look and view state as requested, whatever is edited meanwhile; export dialog shows bands done out of total (J-R47).

A lit export's transient list also carries what its light reads beyond the frame: its band's marks over the frame dilated by one export tile side (first rings) and by the largest light radius, and the city band's casters over the frame dilated by §8.4 (c) largest window R (its ring blocks); R takes Z from the city band surfaceTopCm the generation worker keeps (never the transient list's own), the frame's lowest terrain sample and the export's sun; casters' rows at most a whole city band's (~1.9 KB per building) count in the export-time peak and size estimate (§12.8).

CityJSON extension: root properties outside core named with leading + and defined by an Extension listed in extensions (whether a validator rejects an undeclared one not executed, PLAUSIBLE, so PLAT declares its one); @plat/export ships schemas/cityjson/plat.ext.json (type CityJSONExtension, name Plat, own version, versionCityJSON 2.0) whose extraRootProperties define +platGeoAnchor as an object of exactly three numbers latDeg [-90, 90], lonDeg [-180, 180), bearingDeg [0, 360); extraAttributes, extraCityObjects, extraSemanticSurfaces empty; an anchored file lists extensions {Plat: {url, version}} (url where each release publishes the schema); an anchor-less file (default) has neither property nor member; CI validates both with the extension schema from the repository (no fetch); a change bumps the extension version with the exporter output version (§6.4).

Measurement at the CityJSON exporter milestone (M3b, D-8): the anchored file passes the CityJSON validator with the extension. Pre-decided fallback: the anchor moves to a sidecar <name>.geoanchor.json beside <name>.city.json (three numbers, document id, output version, checked against its own JSON schema like the metric GeoJSON sidecar); the CityJSON file carries neither property nor member; the report says so (J-R43). CityJSON is built for its lossless integer-vertex encoding (J-R14).

Identity in every export (LC-1, LC-28): every export carries entity addresses (§6.3) and the document supersedes table (tombstone -> successor) so an outside tool can follow an entity across re-derivations; ids cross the API and bridge boundary as <docId>/<id>.

dd2vtt profile (DEF-4) scope: a rectangle or district chosen by the user, default the current view snapped to whole grid squares; one scene image <= 8 192 px a side at the declared grid (default 1 square = 5 ft = 1.5 m at 100 px, ~123 m); larger scope split into a grid of scenes aligned to grid lines, or the user lowers pixels per square (>= 50); dialog shows the choice before writing; exact pixels per cell (0 px error, O11 g).

dd2vtt fields: format 0.3; resolution {map_origin {0,0}, map_size in squares, pixels_per_grid}; line_of_sight polylines in grid units from building footprint edges (minus door openings), enceinte faces, yard walls and hedges (fences and railings do not block), cliffs; objects_line_of_sight empty; portals: doors at every entrance of the entrance set (§2.6; item 29: main, side, rear, yard, service, each 1.2 m wide) and gates (opening), each {position, bounds [two points], rotation, closed true, freestanding false}, a concealed door only for an admitting key (item 63); lights (item 68): every LightSource lit at the export drawn week and every lit window at the export hour (§10.3), {position, range in squares (radius), intensity 1, color, shadows true}, on the underground layer its shafts — each only where its host draws for the key; environment {baked_lighting true, ambient_light of the export light setting}; image: scene PNG (base64) rendered by §8.8 at pixels_per_grid without the grid drawn, lit by §8.4 CPU reference at the export light setting.

dd2vtt per layer: one file per model layer (underground one per depth band, II.7.3), elevation in the file name and in a plat extension object; coordinates exact to the grid (O11 g). Per storey (item 28): a building whose plan rung exists exports one scene per storey at its elevation: line_of_sight from walls minus openings, portals from every opening and entrance, stair core a named portal on both storeys' scenes; lights one per lit room (Room.lit) drawing for the key (concealed room only for an admitting key) at its spine summit (§3.8 spine reader; medial axis on downgrade; §8.5), {position, range = room diameter in squares, intensity 1, color = the lights role's, shadows true}; walls keep cm positions and only the scene grid snaps. Foundry scene JSON: same geometry as walls (c: [x0,y0,x1,y1] with movement and sight types; doors flagged), same lights, background image file, grid size and distance units, journal entries from the gazetteer.

PlatApi (DocHandle {readonly id}, document lives in the generation worker): generate(bp, {onProgress?}) -> DocHandle; open(bytes, {readOnly?, session? (host-assigned, §11.3; else stored session minted on first edit, §7.4)}) -> DocHandle (.plat or CBOR twin, bytes transferred); edit(h, e | e[]) -> ApplyResult (event may carry fates); regenerate(h, scope, 'keep'|'newRandom', {discardEdits?}) (§7.1 Regenerate and New random); adjust(h, param, value) (§7.1 Adjust or Re-derive from Sk); confirm(h, token, fates, renames?); cancel(h, token); preview(h, e | e[], {view?}) -> PreviewResult (item 101: the dry run alone, ghost drawn as live.ghost; an editing role's call); undo(h, of?) (appends an undo event for the handle's session §7.4; of only for the owner role; a conflict lists dependent events); redo(h); query(h, q) -> QueryResult (<= 64 KB per page, paginated; names withheld by the knowledge key); view(h, target, opts?) -> ViewHandle; setView(v, patch Partial<ViewState>); export(h, fmt, opts?) -> ArrayBuffer (transferred); report(h) -> GenerationReport; subscribe(h, handler) -> Unsubscribe; close(h); registerProvider({id, version, moduleUrl}) -> ok | refused nondeterministic|origin (§11.4 door (4): module loaded into generation worker, derivation pool and the double-run check's two fresh workers §6.5 (8); origin refused when neither the embedding page's nor on the embed origin allowlist §11.3; a call of the page's own or a script's, no bridge message makes it; J-A85.83).

ApplyResult = {ok; logHead (§11.3); changed (addresses whose records changed)} | {conflict; actions ConflictAction[]} (§7.1 dry run: nearest valid position, blocking lock, stale base ...) | {confirm; token; fates (first 1 000; rest by query fates); renames (case-(4) renames §6.3, §7.3 item 4); counts per fate; scope EditScope resolved} (§7.3 item 4: nothing committed until confirmed).
ConflictAction { kind moveTo|unlock|unassign|reroute|stale|invalid; target?; at? PointCm; message }.

PreviewResult = {refused; reason role} (a viewer's preview: nothing computed) | {ok|conflict; actions? (on conflict); fates (first 1 000); renames; counts {plots, households, buildings, byFate} (§9.5 count badge); shape? PolygonCm | PointCm[] (a points form's derived shape resolved as the event would store it, §7.1); bent? (one-line reason a declaration was bent to the nearest lawful one, R2)}.

Query kinds: gazetteer {text?, kinds?, page?}; people {type?, race?, gender?, profession?, workplace?, ageRange?, household?, district?, page?} (COV-FTG-C13); hit {view, x, y}; whereIs {person, day, hour}; relations {person, up, down} (family tree COV-FTG-C11 from the relation store); inView {view} (features-in-view list, COV-FTG-A24; non-visual route J-S19); fates {token, page}; why {id, path?} (item 101 oracle: the rule, its inputs and alternatives weighed, from provenance and §2.8 derivation records; filtered under the caller's key).
@plat/api/node: the same API over worker_threads plus by-value helpers for scripts and tests: generateDocument(bp) -> Document; exportDocument(doc, fmt, opts?) -> Uint8Array.

API knowledge (item 30; J-A30.83, J-A30.85): query answers of every kind (gazetteer, people, whereIs, relations, hit, inView, why) and hover list every entity in scope with its kind, address, geometry, but withhold the name and purpose (use, or institution kind) of a place whose knownTo the view key does not admit under §9.2 table, marking the row withheld: true; a person's withheld workplace or household given by address only, the profession withheld with it where it is the place's use; a view-bound reader (hit, inView, hover) admits at its view's band (secret place at building band); a band-less one (gazetteer, people, whereIs, relations, every export without a band) admits as at the city band.

Oracle under the key (items 63 (c), 101 (d); J-A101.85): a why answer is filtered by the same table (band-less: city band) and never says more: (1) why on a non-admitted place gives address and kind only, withheld: true, no rule, input or alternative; (2) in any other answer a rule, input or alternative that is such a place (relation target, supply edge end, alternative site) given by address and kind only, withheld; (3) a non-admitted concealed use is left out of every answer (its relation and supply rows, lineage draws, concealed parts and the alternative sites its pair was scored at name nothing and are not counted; why on one of its parts answers empty, as for an address the document does not hold); (4) a front's why for such a key is the front's own — the oracle's answer for the front class alone at that plot (hard rows it passes, soft rows scored there, closest acceptable sites that class alone would take), evaluated from the same tables over the committed model, read-only — so the front reads as the front; an admitting key reads the pair's derivation whole.

preview is an editing role's call (as edit, §11.3 roles): a viewer's preview is refused (refused, role) with nothing computed, since a preview returns the dry run's fates, renames, counts and shape unfiltered; fates pages and a confirm result go only to an editing role and are not filtered (confirm needs lists back unchanged; an editing client holds the document it loaded, for which the key is no secrecy boundary, §11.1); a content provider (§14) answering through query gets the same filtered rows; a host holding the dossier knows every place already (§11.4); a viewer learns one only by the host raising its key (§11.3), never by asking; a concealed use is left out for a non-admitting key in every kind of answer by (3), the front's rows standing.

API tiers (item 20 (h)): every row of every answer marks each fact with its tier by §2.8 factTier (dossier, declared, map), and a why answer names for a derived fact the derivation table row that made it (§7.7 item 10), keeping fixed facts apart from derived ones; a label's display text is given beside the name (§9.1).

Confirming fates: an action whose dry run (§7.1) must be confirmed under §7.3 item 4 — protected entities in its effective scope (Re-derive from Sk, Adjust of an early parameter, a regeneration over locked, pinned, edited or assigned entities, discard edits in scope) or case-(4) renames (§6.3), including an unlock, unassign, undo, redo or revert freeing a name — returns confirm with every protected entity's fate, every listed rename and token = H128(document logHead || canonical bytes of the event without fates and renames); nothing committed; confirm(h, token, fates, renames) commits when the token is current (logHead not moved) and lists equal the dry run's; if state moved it re-runs the dry run and returns a fresh confirm (a changed list never committed silently); resubmitting through edit with fates and renames filled is the same operation (commits when a fresh dry run computes the same lists, else returns confirm) — how a host bridge carries a confirmed action (§11.3); discard edits in scope is a new request (regenerate discardEdits true) with its own confirmation; cancel drops the token (J-R33).

Clerk's tool API (item 101 (b), (d); R10, R19; J-A101.83): the tool API a clerk (the host's own, as SettlementForge's will be, or the staged built-in one) drives is this API with nothing added: declarations are §7.1 events and sugar events through edit; the reader is query; the oracle is query why (from provenance and §2.8 derivation records: rule, inputs, alternatives weighed — closest acceptable sites of §4.7 S10b, rows a derivation fell back through §7.7 item 10); a proposal is a preview (dry run fates, renames, counts, derived shape drawn as a live.ghost in the viewer's view, nothing committed) the user accepts as an edit carrying proposedBy 'clerk' or drops (J-A101.74, §7.1); a bridged host's clerk asks via §11.3 preview message (J-A101.86); a clerk is a client like any other with a role and knowledge key from its host (§11.3): never bypasses dry run or undo, never writes a dossier fact (dossier-owned refusal stands, §5.2), reads and says only what its viewer's key admits; its transcript of edit calls is a skeleton (§11.1).

API crossings: generate in blueprint, out handle and progress events, copy, < 64 KB, < 1 KB per event; open in document bytes, transfer, document size; edit/regenerate/adjust/confirm/undo/redo in events or a token with fates and renames, out ApplyResult, copy, < 64 KB per batch (longer fate lists by query fates pages); preview in events, out PreviewResult (ghost reaches the view as a live.ghost delivery §8.9), copy, < 64 KB, time §12.6; registerProvider in id, version, module URL, out ok or refused with reason, copy, < 1 KB, module loaded once per worker, check's two runs §6.5 (8); query out one page, copy, <= 64 KB; view out composed tile bitmaps and hit-test slices (§8.9), transfer, <= 1 MB + 64 KB per tile; export out file bytes, transfer, format's size; subscribe out ApiEvents (doc.changed, view.changed, report.changed — the changes entries of §5.4 GenerationReport appended since last delivery, a dossier event's entries naming its changeId and reason, §5.4; item 75; items 17-22), copy, < 64 KB.

The headless path runs the same worker code and its model hash equals the browser's (text not in the model, §9.1); ids cross the boundary as <docId>/<id> (§6.3); the derivation pool uses transferred copies, never SharedArrayBuffer (§3.3), so no embedding host needs cross-origin isolation for generation; the tile worker's optional shared columns (§8.9) remain the only use of shared memory.

Engine (§3.7, SCL-22): the product bundle has no WebAssembly dependency; if M0 triggers the kernel's pre-decided fallback (Clipper2-WASM as the single engine), WebAssembly becomes an embed requirement and a host without it receives API error E_ENGINE_UNAVAILABLE from generate and open (not a kernel result, §3.1).

Bridge transport: BridgeTransport { send(msg); onMessage(h) }; shipped WindowPostMessageTransport (iframe hosts; fixed target origin; incoming origins checked against the embed allowlist and — item 85 (d) — the message's source window checked to be the embedding window it was bound to) and MessagePortTransport (any relay: extension content script, SharedWorker, chat-bus relay; COV-FTG-N06); envelope {plat: 1, type, session, seq, re?, logHead?, body} — re on every reply (query.result, preview.result, export.ready/export.refused, doc.applied/doc.rejected) is the seq it answers (item 85 (d)); host messages before the module sent ready are queued and delivered in order, never dropped.

SettlementForge's configuration: the module in an iframe on its own origin speaking through WindowPostMessageTransport (item 85 (e)); a worker or a service remains the configuration for other hosts (J-A85.82); the bridge is the module's boundary with a host program, SettlementForge in its owner-staged phase included: messages carry data only (dossier events in, map document and report out), never code, so no message registers a content provider (§11.4 door (4); J-A85.83); the module stays a separate program in its own bundle loaded in a worker, iframe or service (item 21 (d); §17.3; J-A21.81).

Bridge vocabulary (FTG-22): host -> PLAT: doc.load {bytes | ref, role, session}; doc.apply {baseLogHead, events}; view.set {patch}; export.request {fmt, opts}; query {q}; preview {events, view?: boolean} (item 101 (b): a clerk's proposal; J-A101.86; true draws the ghost as live.ghost in this client's own view, standing for §11.2 ViewHandle; false or absent computes the dry run alone). PLAT -> host: ready {outputVersions, schemaVersion}; doc.changed {baseLogHead, events} (a local user's proposed events); doc.applied {logHead}; doc.rejected {reason stale|invalid|role|version, currentLogHead, conflicts?}; view.changed {patch}; entity.selected {id, kind}; export.ready {bytes} or export.refused {error, message} (incl. E_KNOWLEDGE_TIER); query.result; preview.result {result} (PreviewResult; viewer answered refused); report.changed {entries} (dossier event entries name changeId and reason; never a request back; item 75). Module-tier: sim.advance {hours} (§10.3).

One way (items 20, 22; J-A20.81): no PLAT -> host message writes, patches or proposes a change to the host's dossier: doc.changed carries map-document events only, report.changed the map's report; no message addresses the dossier; a dossier change reaches the map as doc.apply events with author 'host' and EditBase.dossier set (§7.1, §7.7, §11.4), in the host's order (the ordered dossier history of item 22 (c)); the host stores the returned document as an opaque artifact of the map (item 20 (d)).
logHead = a 128-bit hash of (document id, edit-log length, hash of the last event), in hex (own term, FTG-22).

Convergence: the host holds the canonical document and log; a client sends its user's edit as doc.changed against its baseLogHead; the host accepts only when that base is the current logHead (appends, advances logHead, fans doc.apply to every client incl. the sender), otherwise doc.rejected stale; the client applies pending doc.apply messages, re-runs its own events through the dry run on the new state and resends, or shows conflicts; an action needing confirmed fates (§7.3 item 4, §11.2) is sent only after the local user confirmed, as an event with fates and renames; if state moved, the client re-run returns a fresh confirmation instead of resending; every other client replays it with those fates, reporting a mismatch if it computes different ones; all clients apply the same events in host order on the same output version, so every model hash is the same (§6.2) — after a load mismatch once the owner has chosen (§2.9 step 4).

Convergence test (M3a): a host and three headless clients applying 1 000 interleaved random events — undo and redo from every client and one owner undo through a chain among them — converge to one model hash with 0 lost accepted events; and one forced load mismatch settled by an owner keep while two editors edit on the replayed town: all four converge to one model hash, the editors events re-applied on the saved town.

Version handshake: on doc.load the client compares the document's outputVersion (§6.4), not the generator version, with the output versions it can replay (announced in ready); when it cannot, it opens the snapshot read-only (role drops to viewer, says so) as §2.9 step 2 frozen view — checked by chunk content hashes only, labelled 'made with o<k>; not verified by this version', never reported as a mismatch — and never replays under another version silently.

View state over the bridge: the document's view keys (§2.9 view section, outside the model hash; each last-writer-wins by (Lamport counter, session id)) travel as view.set/view.changed; time set by view.set {time} and advanced by module-tier sim.advance {hours} (§10.3); per-viewer keys knowledge (§2.9; admitted by §9.2 table), elaborate (§4.1), storey, depthBand, plotsOnly (§8.4, §8.5), light keys light, sunMode, sunHeight, handLantern (§8.4; item 68) and drawn week week (§4.11; item 67) travel the same way; the pointer moving the cursor sun and the underlay image (§9.5) never cross the bridge.
owner_raw: model §2.9 view keys (the travel rule is this unit's)

statement: The host's clock (item 67; J-A67.82): the clock the design calls the simulator's (the one whose weeks move the map's history) is the host's: its advance reaches the map only as dossier events and epochs, which the port dates and groups by §4.11 week and cadence (§7.7 items 1 and 6; §11.4); a host shows its campaign's current week by view.set {week}; the module's time key counts hours and never moves the map (§10.3).

A viewer's knowledge defaults from its role — owner and editor secret, viewer public; the host may set any viewer's key by view.set; a client never raises its own tier above the one its role or the host gave it, so a player learns a secret place when the game master says so (J-A30.82).

Style is canonical; the preset a viewer looks through is not (N-15): the document style (§2.9 style: sheet and version, row operations, ground-cover regions) changes only through logged setStyle events carried in doc.changed/doc.apply, sent only by owner and editor; view key stylePreset is a per-viewer preset choice (a player looking at lit while the document is drawn in ink): never writes setStyle; replaces the document sheet for that viewer only, the document's own rows (thematic overrides, ground-cover regions) applying on top where the preset has the roles they name, the rest listed in that viewer's style dialog (J-R34).

Roles: owner | editor | viewer, given by doc.load — for SettlementForge by the audience table of the port's host glue (DM, co-DM, player, anonymous; §14, item 85 (f)), never a model rule; a viewer's client never emits doc.changed (edits disabled in the UI and dropped by the bridge) and emits only the view changes the host allows; the host enforces roles too; the host assigns one session per user and document and passes it on every load; a bridged client never mints a session or writes the session view key (§7.4).

Bridged load verification: load verification (§2.9 step 3) runs while the client's user edits; on a mismatch only an owner client may keep the saved town (a rebase sent like any event; J-DET-42); every other client takes the replayed town as its working state, reports the mismatch, records its root at h0 and keeps the doc.load bytes (<= 3 MB at CITY, §2.9 size budget; counted in §12.8) until settled or its session ends; when the owner's keptSnapshot rebase arrives it installs the saved town from them and re-applies the events after h0 (§2.9 step 4); under §6.2 (iii) its comparison of its root with the owner's stateDigest waits for its load's recomputation, a client still verifying stops, and a client loading after the owner's choice takes the saved town as its base without asking.

Bridge logging (LC-31): every model change over the bridge is a doc.apply of EditEvents logged one to one — a host's own commands with author 'host' (§7.1 EditBase); no bridge command changes the model any other way; undo and redo are EditEvents (§7.4) travelling as doc.changed/doc.apply, the envelope session = their EditBase.session; a client never truncates a bridged log; a provider output refused at §2.9's cap returns the requesting edit as doc.rejected {invalid, conflicts}.

Host inputs (DEF-11) only through four doors: (1) blueprint fields (seed, rung, population, intent, districtIntent §7.7 layer 2, circumstances, assignments) to generate; (2) logged edit events through the API or doc.apply — a dossier change arrives as such events with author 'host' and EditBase.dossier set (§7.1), in host order, mutating the current map under §7.7 dossier contract (items 20, 22); a dossier's local/secret designation is one such input (Assignment.knownTo §7.7, read by §9.2); the module never writes to the dossier (§11.3); (3) tables, presets and styles as editTable, editPreset or setStyle events, content copied into the document with provenance host (source, date, version), so it replays without the host; (4) a ContentProvider (§14) registered by registerProvider (§11.2; the embedding page's own call or a script's, the bridge carrying data never code; item 21 (d); J-A85.83), accepted only after a double-run check (runs twice on the same input and stream; byte-identical outputs else refused), every output recorded in the document's hostContent block keyed by (provider id, version, input hash) and read from there on replay; an output passing §2.9's cap on pack data and host content refused at the call. A document never needs its host to replay; host code is made deterministic by the check and the record.

A dossier comes through the port (items 73-87; §14): for a dossier, door (1)'s blueprint and the log's creation prefix and door (2)'s events and epochs are produced by @plat/port (§14, item 73); the host passes the whole dossier and, when it has them, the optional HostContext fields (week, realm block, audience, display names, product line) and nothing else; SettlementForge's map comes through doors (1) and (2); door (3) stays open to it as to any host; door (4) is in-page embedders' and scripts' (registerProvider loads code into the workers), while SettlementForge's bridge (iframe on its own origin) carries data never code (J-A85.83).

The port refuses a dossier whose population lies below 1 500 with E_RUNG_UNAVAILABLE naming the village product while none is registered (§7.7 item 15; item 81), and one above the 120 000 cap the same way naming the cap (§1.1; J-A81.01); §1.1's clamp serves only a request carrying no dossier.
owner_raw: determinism §7.7 item 15 (with scope §1.1 for the cap)

statement: Door (2)'s events carry the element binding key in EditBase.dossier.element (§7.7 item 12; item 74) and the change envelope in EditBase.dossierChange (§7.7 item 13; item 75), dated and grouped into epochs by §4.11 week and cadence.

Optional only (item 20 (h) (iv); J-A20.79): every field these doors accept beyond what the dossier holds today is optional (a stable id, a location hint, a class); what the dossier does not give the map derives by §7.7 derivation table; no door, message or report asks the host for a fact; what a host's data the module never reads is §7.7 item 1's list (item 86); the port's adapter reports every key it dropped; a host's own undo arrives as a dossier change and converges by the solver's order; the port's report names the earlier absorbed state the dossier now equals, state_matches_absorbed (§7.7 item 5; item 87).

No door opens the other way (owner, J86 Q2; J-A73.81): the host's simulator never reads the map's geometry — the module writes no geometry, layout or district read for the host (the plan's door 1, closed); because the map follows from its seed with the ordered dossier history (§7.7 item 6), a canonical-only geometry export could be added without redesign, and only on the owner's explicit word; the port's wiring to a live host bridge is staged (Staged by the owner's roadmap); the port itself is §14's, its creation half built at M1 and its absorb half at M3a (§16).

Decision: the product contains no hosted service; for multi-client use a host (a VTT module, a web page, or SettlementForge in its owner-staged phase) is the store (§11.3) and owns accounts and access (J-R15, J-R16).

DocResolver { resolve(ref) -> ArrayBuffer; publish?(bytes, access private|link|public) -> string } configured by the embedding app; &doc=<ref> links produced only when a resolver with publish is configured, else the app offers the .plat file and, for a small edit log, the inline compressed log of §6.4; access levels are the resolver's; the reference app ships a file resolver (local files and inline logs) and no network resolver.

Reference machine: Apple M1 (4P + 4E cores) MacBook Air (MacBookAir10,1, fanless), 16 GB, macOS 14.7, Chrome stable, Node 24 — where every MFCG, FTG, NG bar was recorded and mechanisms timed (redteam-scale §7); capture record captures/mfcg/2026-09-21T11-25-32/meta.json holds CPU, 8 cores, arm64, Node v24.12.0 but no memory or Chrome version; model, memory, OS read from the same host 2026-09-25 (fixall_rendering_r2_host.out, N-27 b); fanless: every timing batch starts after 30 s idle, runs <= 60 s with bench/calibrate before and after; a batch whose two scores differ > 5 % is re-run.

Low-end device (O12 b >= 30 fps clause; the low hardware tier): Intel Core i3-10110U (2 cores, 4 threads, UHD 620), 8 GB, Chrome stable — or any machine whose calibration score is within +/-15 % of it.

Calibration benchmark bench/calibrate (fixed inputs): 5-octave fBm over 256^2 cells, a bucket-queue priority flood over 256^2, a 20 000-node Dijkstra, a 100 000-element typed-array sort, and in browser runs a Canvas2D raster of 32 fixed tiles (~40 ms; the part that also picks the hardware tier at app start, §8.8); every score stored with host CPU model and cores, memory, OS, Node, browser name and version (UA client hints) (N-27 b); CI divides every timing by (runner score / reference score) before comparing with a budget; the reference score is stored with the goldens.

Where each budget is measured (N-27 a): model budgets in Node 24 (worker_threads for the pool) on every tier and in the nightly tier (§13.8) again inside Chrome's worker on the same seeds and sizes; where the two differ by more than +/-15 % the Chrome figure is checked (the product runs in browsers) and both reported; frame, tile, first-map and label budgets measured in Chrome (Playwright, GPU on); p50 and p95 over B-CITY seeds per rung and water setting.

Timing on shared runners: a CI timing that gates a budget (cost-model sweeps §13.2, first-map, settle and query runs §12.5, §8.9, export runs §12.7, pool comparison and max-clause outlier re-timing §12.3) is taken in the timing phase: last in its tier, alone on the runner, batches <= 60 s with bench/calibrate before and after, re-run if scores differ > 5 %, pool size recorded with every timing; timings taken beside other suites (nightly B-CITY with the invariant suite, B-FUZZ, B-EDIT §13.8) screen and never gate, a flagged generation re-timed in the timing phase (§12.3); the phase costs <= 20 min of the nightly budget: sweeps and first-map runs are nine sizes x five seeds in Node and Chrome (~1-2 min generating), re-timing at most 20 generations x 3 runs per rung (<= ~3.5 min at band tops) (J-R49).
Confirming milestones: each budget of §12.3-§12.8 names the milestone that confirms it and the pre-decided change taken if it misses.

Budgets never change output: a missed budget is reported, never answered at run time by computing something coarser (F-BUDGET-TIME is reporting-only, GEO-2); pre-decided changes are configuration decisions taken once at a milestone and reported, none changing the model.

Matched MFCG reference per rung (rung bands, targets, buildings at target and frame areas are §1.1's; frames §3.2 (9)): TOWN MFCG size 40 (plain options, seed 555001), 1 475 buildings / 58 walled ha, MFCG generation 57 ms; CITY size 80, 5 242 / 220, 131 ms; METROPOLIS size 130, 13 091 / 548, 156 ms; METROPOLIS above its target up to the 120 000 population cap (<= 35 000 buildings, frame <= 153.6 km^2, <= 12.4 x 12.4 km): size 200 (a stress comparison), 31 951 / 1 274, 236 ms.

Buildings at the target derived at ~3.4 persons per building for the core plus hinterland (PLAUSIBLE); the default request of a rung is its target population (building count range §1.1); a band's bottom and top are its population ends at 3.4 persons per building (in buildings: §12.5's table).

Within a rung the frame scales with requested population (§3.2 (9)); at the cap the square frame is 12.4 km (19.8 km with margins); at extreme aspect 2 it is 17.5 x 8.8 km and |x| <= 1.40 x 10^6 cm with margins (~6x headroom under §3.2 2^23-cm range, §3.2 (1)); requests outside the ladder routed or clamped by §1.1 LadderRouter; a dossier below 1 500 or above the 120 000 cap refused by the port (§7.7 item 15; §1.1; item 81; J-A81.01).

statement: Matched counts from the MFCG size sweep (captures/mfcg/exports-sweep-2026-09-25/README.md); MFCG GeoJSON export in metres, only its SVG in the 4 m internal unit (road 8 in JSON, 2 in SVG); the 15 392-building size-80 city of earlier exports (shanty, river, coast on) and the 13 349-36 480 size-80 counts of the MFCG profile are stress comparisons, not the CITY bar.

Primary configuration: one generation worker plus the derivation pool (up to three workers, §4.1) for per-district stages (S10 plots, S10b placement, S11 site plans, per-district greenery), the hinterland unit on the generation worker concurrently, merged in district lineage order (§4.1, §6.3); the single-worker column is the pre-decided fallback on the low tier, in hosts forbidding extra workers, and at every size where the pool measures slower or fails the digest check.

Model budgets (pool p50/p95; per building at p95; MFCG at matched size; ratio at p95; single-worker p95): TOWN 78/100 ms, 75 us, 57 ms (39 us), 1.8x, 115 ms; CITY 262/300 ms, 58 us, 131 ms (25 us), 2.3x, 400 ms; METROPOLIS 624/800 ms, 59 us, 156 ms (12 us), 5.1x, 1 000 ms.

Per-rung cost laws (p95; every size inside a band; fitted by the cost-model tests §13.2): pool TOWN <= 20 ms + 60 us x buildings; CITY <= 40 ms + 50 us x B; METROPOLIS <= 100 ms + 52 us x B (at the 35 000-building cap <= 1.9 s); single-worker TOWN <= 20 ms + 71 us x B; CITY <= 40 ms + 69 us; METROPOLIS <= 100 ms + 67 us; table rows are the laws at 1 333, 5 200, 13 460 buildings (per-building 75, 58, 59 us); the p50 column is §12.4's critical path (pool frozen copies with static index partitions, S12c and S11 light placement included, J-A72.82); §12.5 adds the first frame. (Arithmetic re-checked: consistent.)

O3 (d) bars (docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md: model time p50/p95/max per size class within TOWN <= 100 ms, CITY <= 300 ms, METROPOLIS <= 1 s) are read over every size a rung builds, checked against the laws; max clause: no generation takes more than 1.25 x its own law, T_i <= 1.25 x L(B_i); p50 has no own law, claimed wherever p95 holds. Values (fixall_rendering_r3_budgets.out): TOWN p95 46 ms / 92-110 ms / 196 ms at bottom/default/top, p95 bar holds up to B <= 1 333 (~4 500 people), max at top 246 ms, max bar up to B <= 1 000 (~3 400), single worker up to B <= 1 127 (~3 800); CITY 187 / 265-340 / 481 ms, B <= 5 200 (~17 700), 601 ms, B <= 4 000 (~13 600), single B <= 3 768 (~12 800); METROPOLIS 559 / 724-880 / 1 920 ms, B <= 17 300 (~58 800), 2 400 ms, B <= 13 460 (~45 800), single B <= 13 433 (~45 700). (Arithmetic re-checked against the laws: consistent.)

Declared for the owner's veto: every plot, site plan and building stays on the one-click model path at every size (J-R7, J-I2, J-R38; owner's plot-model ruling) rather than O3 (d) bars held across each band: bars met for p95 up to the table's sizes and missed above — by up to 96 ms at the TOWN top (196 ms), 181 ms at the CITY top (481 ms), 0.92 s at the METROPOLIS cap (1.92 s) — and met for the max up to the fifth column's sizes; holding bars at band tops would need p95 <= 27 us (TOWN), <= 30 us (CITY), <= 26 us (METROPOLIS) per building (MFCG's range, §12.9), reachable only by taking plot and site-plan detail off the one-click path; reversal cost high as a mechanism, nil as a reading (reading at targets alone would report met and hide the miss); D-18 and §15.2's O3 (d) row refer to this.

Law confirmation: cost-model sweeps (§13.2, §13.8: every band's bottom, target and top, five seeds each) in the timing phase, at M1 for TOWN and CITY, M2b for METROPOLIS; pass: at every size the p95 of T_i / L(B_i) <= 1.10, each generation read against the law at its own building count. Pre-decided fallback: a miss re-declares the law at the measured p95 as a D-18 amendment for the owner's veto (§12.5's path) and the tables here and in §12.5 are re-derived.

Which configuration is primary: at the same milestones the timing phase runs every sweep size with the pool (three workers) and a single worker (pool size 0) on the same generations (B-CITY-lite 50 seeds x 4 water settings, paired), and the golden run generates 200 seeds at pool sizes 0-3; the pool is primary at a size when (a) it passes the sweep rule against the pooled law, (b) its p95 is below the single worker's on the same generations, (c) model digests are identical for pool sizes 0-3 on the 200 seeds. Pre-decided outcomes: (c) fails or single faster at all three sizes of a rung -> single-worker column becomes that rung's declared budget, tables restated, O3 (d) reported missed by the difference; (b) fails at one or two sizes only -> each size range runs the configuration faster at the nearest measured size (switch at the midpoint in buildings), chosen at S0 from population / 3.4 (§12.2), configuration not output (§3.3 step 5), each range budgeted by its law; only (a) fails -> pooled law re-declared at measured p95 as a D-18 amendment, pool stays primary where (b) holds. A pool exactly at its law passes (a): default CITY 265-340 ms vs single 351-454 ms (J-R18, J-R44).

Max clause on confirmed outliers: the nightly B-CITY run (1 000 seeds x 4 water settings per rung, §13.8) screens it, recording every generation's T_i / L(B_i) with pool size; each generation over 1.25 re-timed three times in the timing phase (alone, at its pool size, calibration before and after) and a confirmed outlier when the median of three re-timed ratios exceeds 1.25; when more than 20 generations of a rung exceed 1.25, the 20 highest are re-timed and the flagged count reported; pass: no confirmed outlier; same rule at confirming milestones (M1 TOWN and CITY, M2b METROPOLIS). Pre-decided fallback: a confirmed outlier re-declares the max clause at the largest confirmed median ratio (e.g. 1.4 x law) as a D-18 amendment and the max columns re-derived (J-R56).
