Declared trade (MFP-5, N-2): a per-building cost of ~58-75 us at p95 (§12.3 laws at 1 333, 5 200, 13 460 buildings) chosen over matching MFCG's 12-39 us because PLAT builds what MFCG does not (heightfield with hydrology, frontage-first plots with yards and party walls, site plans with heights, roster siting, greenery by rule, collision-checked labels), which D-7 ranks above speed; consequences are the two misses declared for the owner's veto (model time above §12.3 sizes; first map above §12.5 knee, O12 (g)); reversal would drop plot and site-plan detail from the one-click path, forbidden by the owner's plot-model ruling (J-R17).
display list: the renderer-independent columnar list of marks S14 builds from the model per band, read by every backend and export; backends never read the model.
mark: one row of the MarkTable - one drawn thing in one pass at the bands of its lodMask, with a kind of 11 MarkKinds.
band (LodBand): one of the four drawing levels city | district | neighbourhood | building, chosen per zoom stop with hysteresis.
render key: the low 64 bits (words 0 and 1) of the entity key, cached beside the lineage hash; the only entity identity RH32 reads.
RH32: the render hash RH32(tag, key, salt[, ordinal or cell][, style id]) folding words through MurmurHash3's 32-bit finaliser; distinct from §13.6's string hash H32.
drawn week: the week the display list is built at - the document's current week or the per-viewer key `week` (§2.9).

concealed mark: a mark of a concealed part (concealed room, concealed entrance tick, concealed access point or link down) carrying concealed = 1 and the concealed use's knownTo, drawn only for a key that admits it.
caster: a mark whose heights shade others (§8.4 Shadow casters); every caster has a mark in the city band's list, drawn or undrawn there.
slot: a row of the style's layer-order table; draw order is slot-major across the whole scene, then pass, z, key.
pass (MarkTable.pass): 0 fills, 1 casings, 2 bodies, 3 linework and symbols, 4 overlay - order within a slot.
role: a palette entry a style sheet maps semantics to; a role never changes meaning across bands or presets of one family (23 roles).
family: a style lineage (ink, lit, hatched, painterly, graphic) sharing roles, geometry and glyphs; a preset is a sheet of a family.
preset: a shipped style sheet a user or viewer selects (ink default, lit, hatched, parchment, bw-print, night, painterly reserved; the parity presets MFCG and FTG).
style sheet: the data file (StyleSheet) mapping (semantic, predicates, band) to paint programs over roles and a symbolisation table; the document's style is canonical (§11.3).

paint program: a named drawing operation of a sheet (fill, stroke, casing, bands, raised, shadowPass, hatch, roof, crown, halo, glyphAlongSpine, pattern, faceLight, ramp, hillshade, contourMarks, foam, feather, outlineMix, tint, weathering, instances, vignette, ruin, trace, vault, symbol, glow, Works programs, underground programs).
symbolisation: drawn width = clamp(k x model width x px/m, minPx, maxPx) in model mode or a fixed paper width in paper mode; exaggeration never enters model exports.
contrast matrix: the role pairs with minimum dE2000 / dL* that must separate wherever both are drawn; checked at load and on rendered images.
label floor: the ink / road, ink / ground, ink / paper contrast row (dE2000 >= 40, dL* >= 50) every text / halo pair must meet.

palette targets: the owner-released corpus bands (paper luma 226-244 target 235, paper warmth 20-50 pinned 36, darkest ink <= 45, ink warmth 15-25, plate chroma 18-70 median 43, ink 20-30) a rendered plate must land in.
plate model: the city-band role shares of a plate-framed render used to predict plate figures until the measurement render confirms them.
measurement render: the fixed render (golden TOWN and CITY framed by §9.5 at 300 dpi A3, labels on, day, no pointer) on which palette targets are measured.
random style: a style-time palette draw from style.random within +-12 L* of the family value, written into setStyle as row operations and repaired in bounded L* steps.
states table: StyleSheet.states, the rule table keyed by kind x state read after an entity's programs resolve; replace or override rows.
layer-order table: the 25-slot order of the sheet per band (1 paper ... 25 live layers); slots 1-20 are the base raster.
slot resolution: the load-time mapping of every emitted (semantic, pass) to its most specific OrderSlot; a missing or tied candidate refuses the sheet.
live layer: a LiveLayerProvider group of view-data marks (never hashed) delivered as live.<id> deltas; overlay ones compose without re-raster, base ones join the tile key.
thematic layer: override rows keyed by entity attributes (prosperity, use, epoch, owner, material; identity, power and sector shares) recolouring marks as data.
raised under-copy: MFCG's Raised - a dark copy of each footprint offset by a class ratio beneath it; not a shadow, not sun-dependent, identical by day, night and on every rung.
cast shadow: one source's absence under the lighting model, height-derived and graded (penumbra, spill).
projected shadow (rung 3): the per-layer vector union of casters projected along the sun (drop or prism) with penumbra rings; slot 10.
lighting model: the one model of light (global light, placed and derived lights, shafts, hand lantern; brightness law; visibility traversal) stated in §8.4.
global light: the sun by day, the moon at night (LightingSpec.sun/.moon); no fall-off; never underground.
placed light: a LightSource record (§2.7) placed by §4.7's light table or by hand (placeLight), drawn as a light mark.
derived light: a light that is never a record - lit windows (live.windows), plan-rung room lights, light shafts.
hand lantern: the viewer's own underground light (20 cd, 1.5 m above the pointer's floor point, radius 6 m), never a record, never exported.
surface layer: the per-tile raster of normal, height above the tile datum and unlit coverage written from the same marks as the base, read by the light pass.
slab list: one per document, the slab casters (sky islands under ghost/offset, span marks over a passage, bridge/pier decks over water) as outline, top and underside, tested exactly by the traversal.
visibility V_s: clamp(min over the ray of (z_ray - h) / (t sigma_s), 0, 1) along the ray toward the source.
traversal: the one law (CPU reference, GPU pass, light-map bake) resolving the ray minimum over constant-height texels through the max-height pyramid and ring blocks.
max-height pyramid: per surface layer, level 0 its texels and each level above the greatest height of the four cells beneath, to one cell per tile, continued by ring blocks.
ring block: the world-aligned square of 2^m x 2^m positions beyond the first ring, held from level max(m + 2, floor(log2(4(r - 1)))) from the city band's marks.
resolution floor: l(t_a) = max(0, floor(log2(4 t_a / S))), the coarsest pyramid level a cell at distance t_a is resolved at; floor cell side <= t/128, diagonal <= t/90.
window R: the ray's reach - a point light's ground distance, or for the global light (Z - z) / (m - sigma_s) with Z from surfaceTopCm and m >= 1/8.
cursor sun: the default sun standing at G = V + s u over the pointer's ground point with height H = h0 D s; radial shadows at s = 1, near-parallel as sunHeight rises.
light pass: the post operation over the base (slots 1-20) lighting albedo per pixel, with a CPU reference (exports, stills, goldens, tests) and a GPU pass (the interactive view).
CPU reference: the float64 light-pass implementation in the tile worker through dmath, byte-identical on the five engines; the reference every GPU result is held to.
GPU pass: the main-thread compositor's WebGL2 / WebGPU implementation of the light pass for the interactive view, held to the CPU reference by §13.4's tolerance.
light map: the per-tile half-resolution bake of the static point lights' terms with visibility and the ambient occlusion.
light-map key: the tile's surface key (content version over the tile dilated by the largest light radius) + the reaching light marks' revisions + drawn week + drawn hour + the light key.
cell operation: a post operation over cells (pixelate, dotScreen) taken on each tile's own grid, averaging only the base weighted by 1 - unlit coverage.
the fallback ladder (F-LIGHT): rung 1 the GPU pass at tile DPR, rung 2 the global term at half resolution, rung 3 the vector pass; never raised mid-session.

parity presets: MFCG (model none: raised under-copy only, no light) and FTG (fixed or path sun, moon, ambient + directional, window lights at main entrances), whose rows switch off every `extension` default.
light step: the path-mode sun quantised to 15 deg azimuth and 5 deg altitude, read by faceLight, the two-tone roof, hillshade and the lit crown bake on rung 3.
figure-ground contract: at the city band every built block is ground, footprints are masses, streets and squares the only road-role voids; small masses become settlement dots.
mass: a city-band block closing of footprints across gaps narrower than 1.5 px (offset +r then -r, r = 0.75 px x m/px), never across a drawn way's corridor.
span mark: one per base wing spanning a passage, that wing's span ring; painted at the city band, a caster (slab) at every band.
settlement dot: a 2-px building-role symbol with an ink rim at the centroid of a mass smaller than (2 px)^2 that merged with nothing.
street-edge recoverability: the share of intramural street length with a road / non-road transition within half-width + 1 px on both sides; bar MFCG's value - 0.03.

bounded (way): a tier-3 way whose frontage is >= 0.8 footprint-covered on both sides and at least 1.5 px wide at the stop; access-critical: some plot has all its access edges on it and fronts no other drawn way.
stage glyph: the city-band symbol of a Works stage on its mass (scaffold hatch for build, extension and repair; rubble stipple for demolition; the ladder's rows for decay).
plots-only view: the cadastral view (per-viewer key plotsOnly): every plot boundary, no building mark, at the city and district bands; never the default.
change marker: the live.stale overlay glyph at a building whose elaboration record reads stale (one per district at the city band), vanishing when the click re-derives the rung.
first map: the complete city band on screen after one click (S0-S13a and S14's city band), composed unlit; its time is the model law + F(B).
zoom stop (ZoomStop): one of 27 scales at 2^(1/4) steps covering 1:50 000 - 1:500; stop k has m_k metres per CSS pixel; placement and tiles are per stop.
tile DPR: the device pixel ratio after the tier's cap, stepped down 3 -> 2 -> 1.5 -> 1 until the canvas need fits.
world-aligned tile: tile (i, j) at (stop, d) covers the world square of side 512 x m_k / d from (i, j) x that side; shared by views and exports.
base layer: the tile worker's raster of slots 1-20; composed with placed glyphs and overlay marks into one bitmap per position; under / shadow / over in path sun mode.
first ring: the 2(a + b) + 4 tile positions around the visible set, held per position from level 0 with heights from the view's band.
canvas budget: the tier's canvas need 3P + 7 MB (4.25P + 7 MB with shadow layers; 4.25P + 7 MB + Q lit; 6.5P + 7 MB + Q_f at full precision) against ceilings low 72 / mid 128 / high 192 MB.
hardware tier: low | mid | high, chosen at app start from bench/calibrate's Canvas2D part and device memory; overridable; shown with the tile DPR.
per-row rule: PNG filtering choosing, per row, the filter type with the smallest sum of absolute filtered bytes read as signed.
block cache: a lit export's cache of computed ring blocks within max(16 MB, the tile in progress's blocks), LRU.
transient list: the display list an export builds in the generation worker for its band and frame (plus a lit export's beyond-frame casters), released when done.
raster job: a resumable tile raster (RasterJob) whose draw sequence is fixed at begin and run by step(deadline); pixel-identical whether whole or sliced.
draw sequence: the native calls in (slot, pass, z, key) order - batched Path2D fills or strokes, runs of <= 64 sprite draws, derived per-tile operations.
queue class: the tile worker's priority classes 1 queries, 2 deltas, 3 the visible view, 4 exports; one step of the highest non-empty class between message services.
generation worker: holds the document and model, runs S0-S14, exports, live-layer providers, on-demand bands, the elaboration cache and the API's hit and inView queries.
tile worker: holds the only full display list; rasters, composes, bakes light, runs S13b and instancing, answers furniture and snap queries; holds no model or terrain.
reference spacing r0 = 400 cm: the spacing the stamp tiles are built at; an entity of spacing r stamps them scaled by s = r / r0.
border band: the points within r0/2 of a stamp tile's edge, shared by the class's four tiles so any two tiles meet seam-compatibly.
progressive rank: void-and-cluster order of a stamp point; normalised rank r in [0, 1) selects band subsets r < s_b.
candidate annulus: Bridson's candidate ring [r0, (1 + a) r0], a = poisson.annulus = 0.1 shipped (textbook a = 1).
removal update: the ranking's O(n^2) energy update subtracting a removed point's term from every remaining point in index order.
world position: a stamp point's integer-cm position R_theta (s (6400 (u, v) + t + o)) rounded; read by the face test, density test, drawing, override resolution and every export.
ordinal: an instance's stable address - (u, v, p) for a stamp, (u, v) for a grid, i for a line, u<n> for a user add.
crown library: 20 crowns per class per style built once per session from rng.stream (sheet key, STAGE_VIEW, style.crowns, class, index), drawn as sprites; lit sets baked per light step on rung 3.
override resolution: instance overrides apply by ordinal when lineage is unchanged and the ordinal lies within 0.5 x spacing of point; else re-match by position; else orphaned and reported.

model vs view (labels): names, LabelEntity records, the quarter tree and region groups are model (S13a, hashed, persisted); which candidate, size and glyph positions are view (S13b, never hashed, per stop).
LabelEntity: the model record of one labelled thing (12 kinds) with text, short text, priority, bands, display text, candidates, pin and hidden flag.
QuarterNode: a node of the district merge tree (built by S6, named by S13a) with its own LabelEntity (kind quarter) and the cityCut flag.
city cut: the min(N_q, L) quarter-tree nodes flagged cityCut whose labels the city band draws.
region group: a named set of quarter nodes with disjoint districts (an Upper, Lower or Outer City) made by a group event; its label drawn at the city band above the city cut.
pinned placement: a user placement (stop, sizePx, anchor, spine, dirCdeg, lines) set by moveLabel plus the event seq; model data.
display text: a map-side drawing text replacing the name on the label only; the name stays unchanged (dossier-owned names above all).
knowledge filter: the per-row admission test (target knownTo x viewer tier -> coarsest band) applied before rung (5) and any pin or collision; the label policy's home.
knowledge key: the per-viewer view key `knowledge` {tier public | local | secret, places}; view data, never in a digest.
admission table: knowledge.admit, the §7.6 rule table keyed by (knownTo, tier) whose cell is the coarsest admitted band; edited only by editTable.
fact tier: §2.8's factTier of a fact - dossier (immutable on the map), declared (an author's declaration) or map (derived); read here by the reader, exports and the API.
the greedy: candidates totally ordered by priority, area, id; each takes its first alternate meeting no placed higher candidate, obstacle or fixed pin; evaluated locally.
placement unit: one S13b decision step - one rung-(5) test, one pin, one local-evaluation step or one glyph layout.
pin pass: the strict-order greedy fixing eligible pins (own stop at or coarser) by moveLabel seq then label id; a pin meeting a fixed pin is hidden at that stop and reported.
interactive guard: moveLabel's dry run refusing a placement whose box meets another pinned label's box at its stop, returning the nearest free position.
horizontal spine: among the skeleton tree's leaf-to-leaf paths the one maximising length + horizontal extent (<= 64 leaves), scored in model coordinates.
maximum-clearance spanning tree: Kruskal over skeleton edges by clearance descending; the spine is its longest path.
F-LABEL ladder: (1) preferred spine, (2) short name, (3) OBB axis one or two lines, (4) OBB arc, (5) quarter tree, (6) declared overflow, (7) legend entry; every rung reached counted.
legibility floors: minimum cap heights - area 7 px (<= 14), way 6, point 6, address 5, room 5-9, region 1.25 x the largest city-cut label (<= 18).
halo: each glyph's 1.5-px outline in the role under its centre when the text passes the label floor against it, else in ground.
furniture: screen-space map elements (scale bar, compass, grid, title, legend, emblem, annotation layer, north arrow) drawn over the composed tiles; view state.
feature snap: the authoring surface's 8-px snap to a street centre-line, shore, wall, ridge or block edge via RoleIndex.snap; Alt places freely.
count badge: the badge beside the ghost showing an area declaration's plots, households and buildings from the dry run, with plus and minus.
underlay: a per-viewer traced image under the map (opacity default 0.5, affine frame); never exported, hashed, bridged or read by model code or the clerk.
framing: the initial view and default export frame - the circle on the settlement centre of radius max(outer enceinte radius, p95 footprint distance) x 1.08 fitted to the short side.

model formats: exports that read the model and the instance function (.plat, JSON schema, compact twin, GeoJSON, glTF / OBJ, CityJSON, CSV, permalinks) as opposed to picture formats (SVG, PNG, print, the .dd2vtt image) that need a transient list.

document formats: the formats that carry the model and every name (.plat, compact twin, JSON schema, permalink; the skeleton's row names itself one), admitted whole only to a key of tier secret (E_KNOWLEDGE_TIER otherwise).
geo anchor: {latDeg, lonDeg, bearingDeg} placing the settlement centre and turning model north; default (0, 0, 0); remembered in the view key exportAnchor.
skeleton (format): the declared subset - a .plat with no model whose log is the recipe's intent and every declared event, each marked creation; a clerk transcript is one.
inert export: every exported text escaped by its format's rule; SVG with no script, event attribute, foreignObject or external reference.
confirm token: H128(logHead || canonical bytes of the event without fates and renames); confirm commits only while current and the lists equal the dry run's.
oracle: query({kind: why}) - the rule, inputs and alternatives behind a fact, from provenance and §2.8's derivation records, filtered under the caller's key.

clerk: a client (the host's own assistant, or the staged built-in one) driving this API - declarations via edit, reading via query, the oracle, proposals via preview; holds a role and knowledge key from its host.
logHead: 128-bit hash of (document id, edit-log length, hash of the last event) in hex - the bridge's concurrency token.
host bridge: the module's data-only message boundary with a host program (BridgeTransport; envelope {plat, type, session, seq, re?, logHead?, body}); the host is the store.

doors: the four host input routes - (1) blueprint fields to generate, (2) logged edit events (dossier changes), (3) table / preset / style events, (4) a registered ContentProvider after the double-run check.
double-run check: at registration a provider runs twice on the same input and stream; outputs must be byte-identical or it is refused.
reference machine: Apple M1 MacBook Air (MacBookAir10,1, fanless), 16 GB, macOS 14.7, Chrome stable, Node 24 - the machine every budget names.
low-end device: Intel Core i3-10110U, 8 GB, Chrome stable, or any machine within +-15 % of its calibration score; the low tier.
timing phase: last in its CI tier, alone on the runner, in <= 60 s batches bracketed by bench/calibrate, re-run on > 5 % drift; the only timings that gate.
cost law: a rung's p95 budget as fixed + per-building terms (TOWN 20 ms + 60 us B, CITY 40 + 50, METROPOLIS 100 + 52 with the pool).
max clause: no generation takes more than 1.25 x its own law, T_i <= 1.25 L(B_i); judged on confirmed outliers.
first-frame law: F(B) <= 20 ms + 10 us x B for the reference viewport; the first map = model law + F(B).
reference viewport: 1 440 x 900 CSS px at DPR 2, worst tile alignment P = 35 positions.
knee: the building count above which the first map exceeds one second (~14 200 buildings pooled; ~11 400 single-worker).
settle: the visible tiles re-rastered at a new stop, centre-out, <= 150 ms (CITY view) and <= 250 ms (METROPOLIS view).
replay law: V = M(B) + sum c(e) + S14(B) + 5 ms - a replay's cost as a sum over the log; the reference verification mix (300 edits, CITY) ~ 1.4 s p95.
export-time peak: the transient list (~1.9 KB per building at the city band) plus the file being written, counted on top of a rung's working set; one export at a time.
entity-store line: the CITY memory remainder (~34 MB) for the compact entity store with digest trees, bridged load bytes, rasters, overlays, undo records, memos and runtime baselines.
declared trade: the ~58-75 us per building at p95 chosen over MFCG's 12-39 us because PLAT builds terrain, plots, site plans, roster siting, greenery and collision-checked labels (D-7).

statement: Ground: real heightfield in metres; water flows downhill; rivers reach the sea; coasts agree with contours.
Demand: population → own tables decide houses, workshops, inns, churches, institutions and their land before any street.

Markets, castle, large precincts reserved; main roads to gates solved first; first wall follows edge measured along them with a gate where a main road crosses; later wall rings traced before enclosed streets; rivers/moats/canals bridged where roads cross; strip along every wall free of houses and lanes.

Streets: main roads between real destinations; inside walls lanes by the bent cut (one bend, arriving square) = recipe of Neighbourhood 1.2.2 restated in metres, its recordings the test; outside walls FTG-style side streets along main roads.

Districts named for market, gate, harbour, castle; merged into named quarters at city zoom; shaped by a prosperity field (smooth gradient) rising near centre, markets, high dry ground; falling near tanneries, walls, damp low ground.
Plots: blocks divided from street frontage into parcels; rich quarters join plots (courts, gardens), poor split them and get alleys.
Buildings: each plot gets a site plan (row house with party walls, manor behind yard with outbuildings, detached house, hovel); every building stores heights; shadows on by default (§8.4).

Finishing: towers, bridges, harbour, fields and woods sized to population, greenery by rules reading prosperity, names and curved labels never covering a gate or keep; rules are data tables readable, editable, later calibrated.

One display list draws a clean ink map (default, MFCG family), a textured lit map (FTG-like) or a hatched close-up (Neighbourhood-like) on one drawing path; exports SVG, PNG, GeoJSON, VTT scenes, 3-D; large print in background.

First picture always the complete map, never a rough preview, light following within a moment (§8.5): under 1 s for every town and city and metropolis up to ~48 000 people; ~2.3 s at the 120 000 cap (§12.5).
Model build meets improvement-plan speed bars 100 ms, 300 ms, 1 s in 19 runs of 20 up to ~4 500, 17 700, 58 800 people (§12.3); larger towns slower; both misses declared for owner veto (D-18).
Every element and rule table editable; names, functions, shapes assignable to buildings and quarters.

Edits are events on permanent addresses; survive regeneration and version upgrades; undo works multi-user and after reopen; local repair not re-roll; moving a river or dragging ground changes nothing outside the blocks the edit names beforehand; names follow things and change only after confirmation.
Saved town editable once a quick fingerprint check passes; full check from recipe runs in background (§2.9).
Same seed same town on every machine; adding decoration kinds, re-rolling a block or growing never reshuffles existing; a release changing a step declares it stage by stage.
No whole-map retry: every failing step has a short bounded fallback ladder; the report states per requested feature delivered in full, simplified or left out.
Riskiest part (grown streets + bent-cut lanes fit within the speed budget) measured first in a spike and again on real terrain/water at the first milestone.
Every acceptance number says whether it checks a rule, compares with a measured MFCG/FTG number, or shows the town is better.
Owner judges side-by-sides through a written blind protocol at matched sizes; an unrated milestone keeps building but never claims 'at parity' or 'mastered'.
First product milestone is a viewable town; editing directly after (owner ranks editability first).
Effort about 185.5–248.5 expert person-weeks (§16).

statement: A town has several markets: one principal market where trade meets (usually the plaza), secondary markets and churches by size (§4.2).
Every rule's default reproduces MFCG or FTG where they have the behaviour; extensions ride as table values with a weight, chance or option (§7.6).
A building gets several doors when its plot gives it a lane or yard; a cellar where class, ground and wealth say (§2.6).
Some plots hide behind passages and courts (reachable, unseen from any street); a place's name can be known only locally or secretly while the place is always drawn (§4.6, §9.2).
Assignments obey relation and supply-chain rules through one placement solver; a building whose designation changes mutates instead of re-rolling (§4.7).

Quarter wealth change: stock persists — use and occupancy change first, tenure and yards later, geometry only on vacancy, ruin or redevelopment; a plot's geometry never reads poorer than the middle band once built to it or above (§4.11); interior has no such floor — shells re-cut for households from one family with staff rooms down to single rooms off a corridor (§2.6).
Decline and regrowth, floating islands, sewers and underground neighbourhoods, slow terrain change are hooks the base carries for the staged engines (§4.11, II.6, II.7).
SettlementForge's dossier is the authority: the map never edits it; a map delete of a dossier element is a placement rejection the solver re-places; a dossier change mutates the existing map (§7.7).
The module stays private for now, a separate program talking to its host through data alone (§11.3, §17.3, D-22).

statement: Hidden institutions: a thieves' guild can work behind a tavern or funeral parlour; the map shows only the front (§4.7).

Some cellars open onto sewers; below cities the underground can hold catacombs, caves, old quarries, vaults, a buried old town and at most 1–3 undercity neighbourhoods; adding a way down builds everything it needs (II.7, §7.3).
Buildings shown half-built, half-demolished or falling into ruin, week by week (§4.11).

Day and night: by day the pointer is the sun, shadows by real heights (a tall tower shades a low house, never the reverse); by night torches and lanterns light streets; magical lights only where magic is on (§8.4).
Default ink map shows moving shadows gently in its own ink; only the MFCG-imitating setting draws none; the owner is asked to confirm or keep MFCG's raised look with shadows one switch away.

Constructive degeneracies: random sampling rarely hits exact degeneracy (a line across a 2²⁴ frame holds ≤2²⁴ of 2⁴⁸ lattice points; collinear probability ≤2⁻²⁴), so each degenerate class is built on purpose.

Regular-fit fixtures (item 45): regular n-gons n=3…12, radius ≥5 m, rotated and snapped → every target within 1 cm and compactness within 10⁻³ of the n-gon's; vertex-order rotation and reversal give identical targets bit for bit; thin rectangle (1:3 or thinner) below compactness 0.75, targets on a square; a side split into many short edges leaves the centre unchanged; <3 vertices, zero area, vanishing first component → E_DEGENERATE (detail fit); doubles identical under §6.5 (10) cross-implementation test.
Sampler fixture (item 53): every accepted point lies within [r₀, (1+a) r₀] of its active point, beside Poisson min distance ≥ r.

Underground-parts fixtures (item 65): two systems crossing in plan without meeting commit in two parts with no crossing vertex, each passing hard invariants; a link record resolves one vertex per part; a transaction handed a slot of another part asserts in debug; corridorUnion over a gallery gives its kerb at widthCm÷2 + wallCm; a chamber outline at L1 separates floor from rock and S10's frontage cut lands on the floor.
notes: Heading "Fixtures added by amendments c" is narration.

statement: Invariants on B-CITY: the §5.3 suite by scope (batch-local per batch, stage-end per stage, save/load per document, CI-only incl. §5.3's digest-maintenance oracle on every B-CITY-lite city) — 1 000 seeds × 4 WaterSettings (§13.3) × 3 rungs nightly; 50 seeds per rung in PR tier (§13.8); all three rungs from M1. Each invariant has id, severity, report count, CI threshold: hard = 0 per 1 000 cities; soft within band.

Statistics record: core record O(n), emitted by every generation within 4 ms at CITY (§12.4): counts per entity kind and class; areas per class and band; fixed-bin histograms per district and band (plot area, frontage, depth, footprint area, storeys); way length per class; junction-degree histogram; turning per 100 m on ways resampled at 10 m; walled share and built extent; ladder uses per cause and rung; every requested feature's delivery tier (§5.1 principle 7); stage timings. Bench metrics (detour index, Moran's I, KS distances, junction runs, orientation coherence, wall alignment, figure-ground on renders (§8.5), tree NN and pair-correlation from §8.10 scatter) via stats(doc, {level:'bench'}) on demand or in bench, never on the one-click path.
notes: A mechanism (stats API) homed in the testing section; §14 should declare its package; canon to check its producer/consumer ends.

statement: Cost-model tests: each stage timed on nine sizes (bottom, target, top per rung: 1 500/5 000/9 900; 10 000/20 000/29 900; 30 000/50 000/120 000 inhabitants), five seeds each, nightly (METROPOLIS reported from M1, gating from M2b); log-log slope of time vs declared work measure (work-limit laws §5.1 (5), §14) ≤ 1.15 for linear stages and ≤ 1.25 for n log n; §12.3 per-rung cost laws fitted on the same runs.

Work limits follow population: each run reports per stage the F-WORK hit rate (work cuts per 1 000 batches); CI fails when the rate at a band's top exceeds its bottom by > 1 per 1 000 — then §5.1 (5)'s pre-decided coefficient fallback applies and the sweep re-runs. Index work fitted against commits × level size (§3.3).

The budgets these runs time and their measurement rules are §12's: per-edit cost and validation flatness across rungs (§12.6), memory per rung (§12.8), first map by size (§12.5), pan-and-zoom during an A2 300-dpi export (§12.7), model max clause on re-timed outliers (§12.3), simulation occupancy at M4b (§12.7), all in §12.1's timing phase.

Document tests: entity registry path test fails when a type is missing from any path (generation, digest, render, export, persistence, edit, undo, migration; O11 a); export→import→export byte-identical over the canonical form (O9 a, O11 c); document-size test per rung ≤ 320 B per building at CITY (§2.9).
notes: This is the base's mechanised wiring check; volumes' new entity kinds must join it (V-volumes).

S8's working block equals S9's committed block (Hausdorff 0; §3.7). Stored market.siting cell portRef equals the median port-demand fraction recomputed by S0–S2 alone on every B-CITY harbour seed from M1 (§4.2 S3 (12); J-A24.43). Per-stop placement digests of §13.3 are S13b's contract test; a stop placed whole and one unit per step give identical digests (§8.3, §9.2). Stamp-tile asset hash and rebuild tests and view-data contracts are §8.3's; shipped stamp tiles pass §8.3's seam check (§8.10).

Stage property tests (part 2): heights on 100 % of buildings, wings, towers, wall runs; on hilly goldens and after every terrain stroke 0 wings whose baseCm differs from highest terrain sample + plinth (user-edited bases excepted; §2.6, §7.3 (a)); 0 E_KEPT on the one-click path over B-CITY; every gate and weld vertex on its trace; stage 1's trace within 40 m of its boundary except along an on_enceinte castle's shared stretch; 0 lanes crossing a wall strip and 0 L3 band faces split or cleared (NF-P5); 0 S7b claims meeting a wall strip; seam exception (NF-P6) on New random of 20 districts per B-CITY-lite city; union rule on curved-street row fixtures with quad wings incl. oblique rear lines (bent party-wall chains, corners recorded, ridge at arc-length midpoints); decks on 100 % of way–water crossings incl. moats and canals; harbour fixtures (two-arm mole, detached breakwater) pass the crossing invariant; a quay way across a river without a deck fails it (§5.3).

Harbour and crossing fixtures (§4.2 S3 (11)): walled coastal harbour outside the stage-1 region with/without moat:'inner', sealed with N=0, and a polycentric coastal town with no unforced pick left — harbour served, 0 non-gate ways reaching the trace, every way–moat crossing on a deck, roads leaving = N main gates + harbour gate (§4.2 S3 (7)), harbour route ≤ 1.5× plaza↔harbour least-cost lattice path with wall ignored, one main gate on the harbour side (§4.2 S3 (4)); river town with unused crossing sites — 0 site furniture/marks, every built bridge span the way's own L1 edge; an epoch building a site; a drawn bridge 15 m from a site builds it, one 30 m from every site adds a deck by one L0 shore-split batch, crossing invariant throughout (§4.2 S1 (5)); canal across the perimeter — 0 district faces outside, both banks hinterland; castle:'on_enceinte' with water, with/without city moat — 0 trace–water crossings off a river's water gate, outer-arc channel beside shared stretch, town side dry-ditched or plain by row; every seam edge typed; a way-less shared reservation boundary typed reserve (II.5).

B-EDIT and the locality oracle: §7.3 item 7 (i)–(iii), (v) and (iv)'s byte identity of Regenerate (keep settings) run once per sequence (at its end and at one seeded random position), never per edit. Fixtures: re-parenting set (drawBoundary, district merge/split, outskirtToDistrict, regenerate around a lock, id recycling); terrain-brush sequences in both water modes; course-knot, drawn-water, drawn-bridge sequences with §7.3 item 7 (v) assertions; table weight edits and row insertions; drawn features mixed with attribute edits; epochs and rebases; an epoch after 20 edits and a Re-derive from S10 after 20 edits at pool sizes 0 and 3 with identical digests, every freeze empty; undo/redo from several sessions and §6.5 (9) truncation, naming, version-pinned cases (§7.4); undo after reload of an unshared document undoes the pre-reload event; New random on minimal scopes (§5.1 (6)); naming-collision replay (§7.3 item 7 (i)); B-EDIT-lite identity (≥99.9 % of addresses kept under 1 cm perturbation, §6.3); §7.3 item 7 (vi) shared-edge identity; Regenerate (keep settings) of a block with a rich compound (formal garden grid, orchard edges on the house wall) byte-identical to one-click.

B-EDIT carried-content fixtures: warp over a square keeps its fountain, over a yard keeps a user-moved tree, one halved by a pinned pin (§7.4); warp and moveVertex over a lit street with an inn carry every street light, the inn's door light (keeps its fraction of the nearest footprint edge, never re-seated, through two warps), a hand-placed light on a pin and a junction light on a tunnel in their host faces by §7.4's rule, passing §5.3's light row; a light pushed inside its sizeCm clearance re-seated; one whose inset empties re-placed when generated, orphaned and reported when hand-placed; an access point's opening carried in its ground host; a building under a demolition Works keeps rings at mean-value images unre-seated; undo byte for byte and replay reproduce them (§7.4; J-A68.73).

§2.6's test: warp and moveVertex over a built block with an L house, overlapping T, curved row of quads and a holed footprint — every wing union equals its footprint face (integer equality), carried rings simple, roof lines inside footprint, de-rectangled rects turned quads, neighbouring plot re-fitted onto a shared party wall adds its corner to the wing ring, undo byte for byte, replay reproduces; a building with a hand-built stored Composition (composed wings each base wing cut in two, court on the hole, tower centred on a corner and one inside, rooms in one wing) — composed wings unite to the moved footprint after each move, rooms inside, tower centres inside or on, wings reach every storey the base wings reach with ≥ their area (§2.6 stage-3 storey rule), undo byte for byte; stage-3 intake runs the same test with every fixture building's composition stored (§2.6).

Load verification fixtures (§2.9 steps 3–4): an edit within 100 ms of editable state on an edited CITY document with a forced mismatch (one moved footprint, recorded digest recomputed) — the edit applies at once; after either choice session digest = fresh-load replay digest and that load reports no mismatch; open-to-editable time vs T(B); snapshot with one moved footprint and unchanged model.digest (chunk hash rewritten or not) → corrupt cache, loaded by replay, never verified or offered as saved town; under forced §6.2 (iii) 'trust the saved town' and a save wait for recomputation, mismatch withdraws the keep; altered naming record → corrupt cache when recordsDigest left, else reported as records mismatch, meanwhile edits re-applied, then verified, later corpus selection renames exactly what a never-saved session renames; an Adjust during load verification in an epoch-grown town reports no records mismatch after save/reload; a drawBoundary moving surviving blocks, saved and reloaded, reports no corrupt cache.

Naming-input fixtures (§6.3): a selected user corpus and an edited naming row rename exactly the unedited names citing the changed slices (listed in the fate report, stored in the event), fresh and rebased, every other name byte-identical, 0 duplicate ids, 0 silent re-binds; a re-sited bridge keeps its new name; editTable of one naming grammar row renames exactly citing names; replacing a culture row's street corpus leaves district and quarter names byte-identical; a frozen fixture with a changed naming row imports with renames listed, and a later New random renames nothing outside its scope; canal across a wall and river move cutting a glacis commit with 0 NF-P5 violations; lane across a wall strip refused (§5.3).
20-epoch test (M4): a TOWN with ≈30 % churn per epoch keeps heap ≤ 1.3× and document ≤ 2× those of a freshly generated town with the same live entities.
The thirteen MFCG asks of §7.4 as scripted scenarios, each reporting its locality share, invariant results and re-run cost against §12.6.

Faithfulness campaign (O9 c; §7.3 item 7 (iv)): each nightly run draws n = 800 regenerated scopes (400 block, 400 district, seeded; topped up with New random on B-CITY-lite if a kind has < 400); for each, K = 50 from-scratch references with rerolls 32 768 + i (i = 0…49, unreachable by users); for four statistics (median plot area, median frontage width, density, attached share) rank r = count below + uniform tie draw in 0…t (campaign's own stream), exactly uniform on 0…K; ranks binned into 10 bins ⌊r·10/(K+1)⌋, χ² per statistic, campaign fails when Holm rejects at family-wise 0.01 (smallest p < 0.0025). Cost ≈40 800 scope generations (800×51), ≈12.5 CPU-min (20 400×≈6.6 ms + 20 400×≤30 ms) within the nightly budget.

Calibration of the campaign (executed; docs/validation/bench/fixall_scope_r3_o9c_n800.py → .out; fixall_scope_r2_o9c_power.out): statistics correlated; at ρ=0.8 n=400 catches +0.25 sd bias in 92.2 % and 0.8× too-snug in 95.2 % of nights → hence 800. At n=800 a perfect regenerator fails 1.0 % on continuous (31/3 000 at ρ=0.8; 15/1 500 at ρ=0) and 1.4 % (14/1 000) on tied discrete; +0.25 sd bias and 0.8× snug caught 2 000/2 000 at ρ=0 and 0.8 (95 % lower bound 99.8 %); 0.6× snug and 1.5× loose 500/500; at ρ=1 bias 99.3 %, snugness 99.7 %; without randomised tie-break a perfect regenerator fails every campaign on a tied statistic (fixall_verify_scope_o9c_rank.out).
notes: Rationale-grade evidence (why 800) — J-S30 carries the reasoning; candidate to move to the rationale file with a pointer (shrink: restatement/narration).

statement: Campaign diagnosis and retry: a failing statistic's histogram names the fault (hump = too snug, U = too loose, slope = bias). A failed campaign is re-run once with the next campaign seed (perfect regenerator fails two in a row with p ≈ 1–2×10⁻⁴; a fault of the sizes above is declared on its first night with p ≥ 0.996 at ρ ≤ 0.8, ≥ 0.985 at ρ=1). A second failure is a regeneration defect entered in known-defects.json and M3a does not exit until fixed (§16).

Control sweeps: §7.8's statistical monotonicity and continuity — 21 steps × 50 seeds at TOWN and CITY nightly, METROPOLIS in the milestone tier; the population control's sweep reports F-WORK hit rate per stage, flat across each band.
Option-interaction matrix: every pair of toggles rendered and diffed; no option silently disables another (O12 c).
notes: Principle (11) requires every toggle and preset combination; this is pairwise only — edge-catalogue check.

statement: Golden suite: 12 seeds × {TOWN, CITY, METROPOLIS} × 4 WaterSettings {none, coast, river, coast+river} stores per stage its stage-isolated digest (new code on previous output version's frozen upstream outputs, §6.4), entity counts, core statistics record and one PNG per LOD and preset; per shipped preset's label style a per-stop placement digest.

Declared-shift protocol: a release matches or declares a shift record for every stage whose isolated digest moved (stage, cause (rule-table change, fix, new concern), seeds and statistics moved, expected direction, output version created) and a cascade record for every re-signed end-to-end golden (each downstream stage moved only through its inputs; a downstream stage whose isolated digest moved needs its own shift record). An undeclared move fails CI; a statistic moving against its declared direction fails until the record says why; only declared stages re-signed; untouched stages byte-identical (O2 e); a same-seed output change never rides silently (owner non-negotiable 10).
Golden records are product files inside plat/ (so §17.1 (3)'s path rule and the gate never collide).

WaterSetting = 'none'|'coast'|'river'|'coast+river' — the one spelling of a water setting for B-CITY, the golden store and every record. A seed in a record is a Seed (u32, §2.9) written as its decimal string; permalinks write it in base 36 (§6.4).

ShiftRecord: id; release (generator version); outputVersion (o<k>, null for a view shift S13b/render.stampTiles); stage: StageId|'S13b'|'render.stampTiles'; cause {kind: table|fix|concern|engine|feature|calibration|baselineShift; ref (table id@version, issue, concern id, CalibrationRun id, baseline id); note}; seeds [{seed, rung, water, before, after: Hash128}]; statistics [{metric (core-record field or §13.5 metric id), rung, before, after, expected: up|down|none|any}]; tiles? [{tile, before, after}] (render.stampTiles only; seeds empty); d5SeedsChanged; milestone; date; author.
CascadeRecord: id; outputVersion; upstream (ShiftRecord ids); downstream [{stage, before, after (end-to-end), isolatedUnchanged: true}]; seeds; date.

MilestoneRecord: milestone; date; outputVersions; shifts; cascades; parity (plat/goldens/parity/<milestone>.json ParityReport, §13.5); d5 {status: D5Status; record: plat/goldens/d5/<milestone>/record.json} | null; knownDefects {opened, closed}; exitCriteria [{id, result: pass|fail|fallback-applied, evidence}].

Golden store layout: plat/goldens/store/o<k>/ (per seed and stage frozen upstream outputs, digests, counts, statistics, placement digests); PNGs content-addressed in plat/goldens/png/ (large-file storage); plat/goldens/shifts/o<k>.json (shift and cascade records creating o<k>); plat/goldens/shifts/view/<release>.json (view shifts); plat/goldens/milestones/<milestone>.json (exit records). Golden CLI refuses a record with a missing field; @plat/docs release-notes generator reads only these and plat/docs/known-defects.json. docs/validation/shifts/<milestone>.md and docs/validation/d5/<milestone>.md are research-side copies generated by research/baselines/mirror_records.py; no CI job reads them; hand edits change nothing.

Placement digests (§9.1's cross-engine promise): for every golden town, every shipped preset's label style and each of B-ZOOM's 27 zoom stops, S13b places the band's area and way labels at public tier with no places at view rotation 0 (digest per stop, knowledge key, rotation; J-A55.81) — and for one golden CITY also at secret — for all candidates and the addresses and repeated street names of the default view's visible tiles; the digest hashes per candidate in id order the label id, chosen alternate (or yielded), ladder rung, size and every glyph's position and angle as exact IEEE doubles. Placement and its feeding renderer code are held to §6.5 (3)'s allowlist lint; the rest of @plat/render is compared by visual regression (§13.4). PR tier compares on Node x86; nightly on all five engines with workers on/off; an engine difference is a determinism defect.

View shift: a placement digest moving while every model digest holds needs a ShiftRecord with stage S13b and outputVersion null, bumps no output version (placement is view data, §9.1), and bumps the style version of every shipped sheet whose placements moved (style version carries pixel identity, §6.4). Stamp-tile asset stored hashes (§8.10) are kept with placement digests; an asset moving a stored hash while model digests hold is a view shift with stage render.stampTiles, outputVersion null, bumping style versions of sheets drawing stamped classes; an asset only adding a new class's tiles needs no record.

From M1: output-version stamp, shift/cascade/milestone records and stage-isolated golden tooling built at M1, not at hardening (§16); every milestone from M1 writes its MilestoneRecord; a milestone cannot exit with an undeclared shift.

Preview links: until M4's exit fixes output version 1, every permalink and document made by the app carries §6.4's preview flag and the app shows the preview notice ('preview: made with output version oN; a later release may draw this seed differently and will say so'); the link carries its o=. Retention of output versions N−1 and N−2 (§6.4) built and replay-tested at M3a; afterwards links inside the window replay exactly, outside open with §6.4's notice.

Nightly cross-platform golden run (Node x86/arm64, Chromium, Firefox, WebKit; workers on/off; pool sizes 0 and 3; §13.2 contract tests cover 0–3) is the reproducibility proof: identical model, derived-complete and placement digests per stage on every engine; from M3a the strict GeoJSON of one golden CITY seed (coast+river) with its trees (§8.10 integer-centimetre instance positions, species, crown diameters, leaf types) byte-identical on every engine, workers on/off (§11.1).

Amendments c in the goldens: nightly run also holds §6.5 (9)'s session-history independence test (item 52) and B-DOSSIER-lite fixture digests (T73-8). New mechanisms reach goldens only by declared shift: the milestone first placing LightSource records (item 68) writes an S11 shift record with cause feature (records join every model digest, §6.2); class mix (71), informal clusters (70), concealed pairs (63), character step S12c (72) write theirs at their landing milestones (§16); generation makes no Works (T67-5) so transitions move no golden. Lighting, its buffers and light maps are in no model digest (§6.2): changing the light pass is a paint-program change bumping the style version of every sheet it draws (§6.4), PNGs re-signed through visual regression (§13.4), never a model shift (J-A68.01).
notes: Narration heading ("Amendments c in the goldens").

statement: Visual regression: Playwright renders the golden suite per preset, LOD and backend; SSIM/pixelmatch against stored PNGs with per-preset threshold; §8.3 draw-style census per preset; a 'no fills' and a 'no outlines' render must remain legible (R13).

B-ZOOM (1:50 000 → 1:500, default view of every rung): legibility floors; no feature popping more than once (footprint hash identical across bands); §8.3's checks (hairline fidelity, decoration stability, role continuity across band switches, no tree mark over a tier-1/2 casing, no casing pixels in junction mouths, contrast matrix on the city band); §9.4's label checks (incl. §9.2 pin-pass fixture); §8.3 draw-order census and render-key identity; §8.5 figure-ground metrics; §8.2 role-continuity per family from the milestone shipping its four bands (§16).

App harness scripted tasks (O16 c; Playwright on §12.1's machine): share a view link, export a layered SVG, change the coast side, see five variants of one kind, recover from a mistaken regenerate, measure a street with the ruler, find a named building through the gazetteer — each passes in the stated number of UI actions (one where a reference needs a detour; recovery = one undo) with every app response ≤ 1 s, on every PR.

Accessibility: axe-core on every screen and panel of @plat/app reports 0 serious or critical violations; every control reachable and operable by keyboard alone with visible focus; every scripted task passes keyboard-only; gazetteer list/search and 'features in view' list reach every building, plot, district and pinned person without the canvas.
notes: g item 112 (colour-blind-safe maps) is routed to units it names — may add an accessibility bar here (F-MISSING check by canon).

statement: Input scheme: every binding of the default keymap.json (§14) fires its action while the map has focus and none while a text field has focus; a user-edited keymap round-trips through save and load.

Light-pass bar (item 68): GPU pass vs CPU reference on golden day and night stills with the cursor sun at nine fixed pointer positions — per pixel of each lit tile absolute difference per 8-bit channel ≤ 2 at the 99.9th percentile and ≤ 0.5 on average (provenance 'architecture 2026-09-28'; J-A68.02), from M2b (day) and M3b (night). Pre-decided fallback: a tier whose GPU pass misses takes §8.4 (g)'s full-precision surface (traversal unchanged) and is re-measured; still missing → that tier draws rung 3 of §8.4's ladder and the miss enters known-defects.json. B-ZOOM runs legibility floors, §9.4 label checks and §8.2 contrast matrix on night and day views, labels composed after the pass (§9.4), and checks each fallback rung draws a legible map (a forced rung-3 run per preset).

Palette acceptance bar (item 69; §8.2; J-A69.01): on §8.2's fixed measurement render every shipped family lies inside its targets — paper luma and warmth, darkest-ink luma and warmth, plate chroma (ink 20–30; other families inside the band at §8.2's scale) — measured by our own code from §8.2's definitions, no corpus instrument in plat/; in B-ZOOM from the milestone shipping each family's bands (ink M1, lit M2b, ink-family variants M3b, hatched M5). A family outside a target fails; §8.2's scripted chroma sweep re-finds that family's scale and the bar repeats — re-signing role values by their own rule, never the targets (the owner's, §13.7).
notes: g item 112 (colour-blind-safe maps) touches palettes — canon routes whether this bar gains a CVD clause.

statement: First-five-minutes test (item 101 (f′); J-A101.03): at the M2a and M3a exits, 5–8 casual game masters new to the product each get a generated town and complete without help a quarter task, a place task, a dress task (style change + compass) and one scoped re-roll keeping their declarations, within five minutes; passes when every participant or all but one completes all four, each failure recorded with task and step. An exit criterion of the MilestoneRecord; no review reading replaces it. Pre-decided fallback: a task ≥2 participants fail gets its tool's first-screen placement and first-use hint revised (§14 contract) and re-run with new participants before exit.

The same sessions settle three UX questions with pre-decided fallbacks: touch editing (two participants per session on a tablet; every tool takes touch; if they fail where pointer users pass, touch kept for L0–L2 (intend, ground, wall, road, quarter, place, roster) and L3–L4 pointer-only, stated in the guide); a preview-first clerk (where a clerk is connected proposals arrive as previews; if slow, an apply-then-undo mode offered as a user setting, off by default, each applied proposal shown with its one undo, never silent); declared means held (if the re-roll surprises participants, each re-roll shows a visible keep/change toggle on declared entities in scope).
notes: Three "left open" UX questions resolved by pre-decided fallbacks (not deferral). V10 clerk proposal modes must agree.

statement: The parity CLI in @plat/testkit reads only baselines.json (our numbers-only measurements of the references, generated research-side by scripts under research/baselines/ from the captures, committed into plat/packages/testkit/baselines/ (§17.1 (4))) and our B-CITY outputs, reporting every metric against its band; it never opens captures/, research/ or reference/.

Baseline: id; metric; unit; reference 'MFCG'|'FTG'|'NG'|'VG'|`corpus:${string}` (corpus rows arrive through §13.9); referenceBuild (required: itch build, FTG server date + create-request hash, NG/VG build); capture; script; date; matched? {rung, mfcgSize?, ftgSize? BIG_TOWN|BIG_CITY|CITY|METROPOLIS, population?}; role target|weakness|descriptive; values {p10?, p50?, p90?, n, seeds} | {bins, histogram, n, seeds}.
notes: ftgSize enum here includes CITY; RungProfile.matched.ftgSize (§1.1) is BIG_TOWN|BIG_CITY|METROPOLIS — enumeration mismatch between two types for "FTG size" (agreement check).

statement: ParityReport (written by the parity CLI per run; read by milestone exits, §13.9 CalibrationRun and release notes): runId; date; outputVersion; generatorVersion; baselines (Hash128 of baselines.json read); rows [{metric, baselineIds, role, rung, preset?, band {lo?, hi?, ksMax?, direction? above|below, margin?}, ours {p10?, p50?, p90?, ks?, n, seeds}, verdict pass|fail|reported (descriptive always reported), note?}]; summary {pass, fail, reported}.

Each milestone's parity report stored as plat/goldens/parity/<milestone>.json and named in its MilestoneRecord; the CLI refuses a row without referenceBuild, capture, script or date; a new reference build never overwrites a row — it adds a row (id gains the build) and is a declared baseline shift in the milestone's shift record (e.g. VG changed geometry for the same seed between builds 19251041 and 19365073 = VG 1.6.9). Rows hold numbers, units and provenance only — no names, colours, grammars or code.

Band rule: target rows pass when ours lies in [p10×0.9, p90×1.1] of the reference seed spread (single-value baseline ±15 %); distributions pass when our KS distance ≤ 1.25 × the reference's own seed-to-seed KS at p90; weakness rows one-sided (beat the reference in the declared direction by the stated margin); descriptive rows gate nothing. When M-1 re-measures a baseline (five seeds per matched MFCG size; FTG's new captures) the band is recomputed by the same rule with provenance 'M-1 ⟨date⟩'; a recomputation turning pass into fail is declared in the shift record. Thresholds no reference can set are §13.7's.

⟨M-1⟩ rule: a reference number marked ⟨M-1⟩ is measured by M-1 (§16 lists every such measurement); if M-1 cannot measure it (capture lacks the feature or not reproducible across seeds) the cell becomes descriptive, gates nothing and enters known-defects.json with the reason; the parity CLI reports an ⟨M-1⟩ cell without its baseline row as fail, never pass.

Matched sizes (§12.2, §13.6): TOWN ↔ MFCG size 40 and FTG BIG_TOWN; CITY ↔ MFCG 80 and FTG BIG_CITY; METROPOLIS ↔ MFCG 130 (FTG per D-31). MFCG numbers from its plain-option size sweep (walls, citadel, plaza, temple on; shanty town, parks, river, coast off; JSON export in metres, internal unit 4.00 m). Curves measured after both sides resampled at 10 m arc-length steps.
notes: Restated in §1.1 table and §12.2 — canonical home to rule.
