χ̃(D) is §4.5 (2)'s function evaluated with allocation rows as instances (J-V1.1): S7c reads it over the greedy rows, later readers over committed rows; each row (cls, band, count) = count instances (household row = count residential instances); significance §4.5 (1) σ with size = 1, rank and patronage as §4.5 (1) (dossier's where the row carries a dossier element); (1) lot mix, (2) political alignment (partition §4.5 (7) at current applied standings), (4) economic role exactly as §4.5 (2).

χ̃ (3) trade position: frontage = length of every way chain on the boundary or inside the district's L1 faces at S7c (S4 arterials and S5 secondaries, part 0 only; each side of a chain counted once for the owning district) x the way's trade weight (§4.3 TradeFlow), over the town's largest such sum; tradeBearingCdeg as §4.5 (2).

χ̃ (5) relations: mainRoad = share of that frontage on through and primary ways; anchors from S3 and S7b reservations; contribution c = the district's share, by count, of the anchor's allocation-level suppliers: for each supply edge of the anchor's class, S7b (1)'s district supply term (g 105 (g)) binds the anchor's allocation to the nearest district by centroid distance whose allocation holds the provider class (a sky pseudo-district at its island land centroid's world point, V05 §3.20 (12)(b)); c = share of those bindings landing in D. Placed vector keeps §4.5 (2)'s plot-level c.

χ̃ is draw-free, never stored, recomputed on demand from eager records, equal on every host; provisional identity = §4.5 (4) identity rule on χ̃ (source emergent/dominant/plain, or dossier's where dossier-defined, QUARTER included); readers S7c weights, S9b square-type split, replace dry-run ghost, fabric WhyProvider; every other reader (hood-pin identity factors, panel, title subtitle) reads the placed vector S12c writes.

T-V1-2: on B-CITY (a) χ̃ lot-mix shares within 0.08 (half L1 distance) of placed vector for >= 90 % of districts; (b) χ̃ over greedy vs reconciled allocation within 0.08 for >= 95 %; fallback (a): size = class median footprint over median plot (§4.7 S11 templates at band) instead of 1, check repeats; (b) V1-3.3.7's fallback.

S7c per district in lineage order on the generation worker as S7b (1)'s allocation hook: (1) fabric path edited (setAttr held §7.2) or set by a declaration read ahead (skeleton quarter with fabric, BCR-35): keep it, compute templateLandM2, next; (2) hinterland kind or underground arena (underground, undercity): bent-cut (hinterland has §4.9's recipe; underground close-ups never take a replace fabric, II.1); sky districts run this inside their unit run; (3) build DistrictContext on pre-claim template face and χ̃ over greedy allocation; (4) eligible set E = bent-cut ∪ rows whose requires hold; (5) weights, bent-cut 1 - 0.5 x intent.planned; (6) one uniform on fabric.select picks by cumulative weight in table row order; (7) write D.fabric and fabricParams = row params defaults (per-district parameter draws in S8 on hood.template); (8) templateLandM2 to reconcile; (9) report stage2.fabric (D, E with weights, choice, land).

Pre-claim template face at S7c = D's largest L1 face that is not a wall strip, an S3 reservation, an intramural garden (g 106 (b)) or another district's; templateFaceAreaM2 = its area less the expected area of the claims the greedy allocation gives D (all counted against this face, conservative); inscribedRadiusM and faceObb the pre-claim face's; S8 re-tests on the committed face and a failure there is F-TEMPLATE's under the land cap; every factor a hood.constants cell.

Eligibility: ring law inscribedRadiusM >= 2.5 x eLo + w_tpl [elig.ringELo] (w_tpl at band upper end); plaza law templateFaceAreaM2 >= 6 x plaza area [elig.plazaFaceMult] and inscribedRadiusM >= plaza half-diagonal + eLo; spine law faceObb.minorM >= 2 x eLo + w_tpl and majorM >= 3 x eHi [elig.spineEHi]; portals n usable on template face boundary; waterShare/wallShare seam share >= value and longest run >= 3 x eHi [elig.runEHi], wall counts only walled stretches (full, parapet, an enceinte closure arc = earlier ring's curtain), other barrier closure arcs never count (g 106 (a)(c)(f), BCR-30 (b)); noIntervallum: enceinte has no intervallum (§4.8 era row) or run is parapet; landmarkSigma: reservation in face with class σ >= value (character.anchorSigma 5 default); bridgePortal: bridge landward-end portal on face boundary; slopeMeanPct: slope.meanPct >= value; crossingPairs: two usable portal pairs whose chords cross inside face at >= 45° [elig.crossAngleDeg]; arenas: ground for every row, sky for all but quay, wallside, bridgehead.
A district with no template face (every L1 face a wall strip, reservation or intramural garden) has E = {bent-cut}.

Weight w_r = select.base x κ(D) x Π(1 + gain x value) x (1 + plannedGain x intent.planned) x fabric.extensionWeight; κ(D) = select.kind[D.kind] (1 when absent); sky-* kinds read the ground counterpart (V05 §2.4): sky-temple temple, sky-palace castle, sky-island the town's richest ground kind (ground district with highest pass-1 mean, ties by address), sky-prison and sky-tower none (1). fabric.extensionWeight (stage-2 switch) 1 default, 0 in MFCG and FTG (parity presets lay every district bent-cut, the M4 output), 1 under NG whose ng.fabric replaces the product by the four NG rows' select.ngOdds (kept only when eligible, every other row 0).

stepped row weight further x min(2, slope.meanPct / 8) x (1 + terrace.askGain x asks), asks 1 when terrace.asks holds, terrace.askGain 1 (ours, extension); a terraced ward may still be organic. Every row with plannedGain > 0 carries {of shade, gain -0.5} on shade.meanShare (g 102 (a)(d), ours, extension); street row carries {of chain, gain 1} (1 when an incompatible chain runs alongWay a tier-1 way through D; g 104 (h)(3) as revised).

S7c never names or assigns a quarter: a quarter name arises only through item 72's identity rows past threshold or a dossier or author declaration (g 107 (e)); a street's trade name only through WayNamingContext.trade.

Default hood.templates select rows (ours, own, calibratable; J-V1.4) base / kind factors / terms / planned gain / requires: bent-cut 1.0 / - / - / (-0.5) / always; street 0.25 / market 1.5, gate 2, craft 1.2 / mainRoad 2, chain 1, shade -0.5 / 1 / spine law, portals 2; square 0.10 / market 3, central 2 / trade 1, shade -0.5 / 1.5 / plaza law; ring 0.05 / - / shade -0.5 / 3 / ring law; quay 0.8 / docks 2, riverbank 1.5 / sectors.trade 1 / 0 / spine law, waterShare 0.2; wallside 0.4 / gate 1.5 / shade -0.5 / 0.5 / spine, wallShare 0.2, noIntervallum; crossroads 0.3 / market 2, central 1.5 / trade 2, shade -0.5 / 1 / plaza, portals 4, crossingPairs; landmark 0.6 / temple 2, castle 1.5 / identity religious 1, shade -0.5 / 0.5 / ring, landmarkSigma 5; bridgehead 0.5 / riverbank 1.5 / trade 1 / 0 / plaza, bridgePortal; stepped 0.5 / - / - / 0 / spine, slopeMeanPct 8; park 0.02 / park 40 / shade -0.5 / 1 / plaza (green mode).

Confirmation (M5, B-CITY): share of non-bent-cut districts 15-35 % at CITY default preset; S4 (b) classifier separates templates at >= 90 %. Fallback: all non-bent-cut bases scale by one common factor to 25 % (declared shift); classifier failure: failing pair's weaker row base halves and its distinguishing parameter (ring count floor 2; street control offset 0.2) raised, classifier re-runs.

One uniform on fabric.select keyed by the district's own lineage key with reroll forced to 0: New random never re-draws fabric (II.4 'same kind, new seed'); a declared quarter, merge/split elsewhere or S6 renumbering never moves another district's draw (anchor rule); merge/split successor inherits anchor predecessor's key; edit-minted district keys by creating event seq lineage; nothing else moves when one district's weights change.

Standalone auto: NG 1.2.2 random-template odds bent-cut 0.7, street 0.3, square 0.1, ring 0.1 (select.ngOdds; ref:NG 1.2.2 code; code-neighbourhood.md §2.0), kept only when eligible; a context row (quay with water edge, wallside with wall edge) joins at in-town weight x 0.7 [auto.contextFactor] in the default preset; under NG (ng.fabric on) only the four NG rows; draw on blueprint.features.

hood.fabric EpochParticipant {id hood.fabric, step afterGrowth, order 40, stage S9b, run} (after underground participants 10-30; V06 §2.1). A new growth stage's S5-S13 run carries both hooks; the participant covers (1) a district the epoch created outside S7b's hook takes S7c's rule; (2) every block in EpochScope.recut (rung-3 op re-cut or redeveloped) re-typed by S9b (rungs 1-2 keep content, no scope); (3) districts a raised part in scope.raised crosses: derived readings recomputed on read and close-up chunks marked stale, hood pins re-derive over committed plots; no op, no plot removal, no re-homing (V06 §3.19 (7)-(8) clearing runs before); (4) nothing else: survivors keep fabric and content. Inputs EpochContext.doc, scope.recut, scope.raised; outputs setAttr ops of district.fabric, block.content, block.squareType in EpochOps.ops drawn on ctx.stream(S7c or S9b, entity) (epoch.transform). Item 102 (e) shade drift reaches it via the field; standing blocks never re-type.

templateLandM2(D,r) = sum over r's seeds on S7c's context (land.* cells): plaza (carved or green) its A at greedy inhabitants, void plaza its A (corner claims); spine: expected course length x w_top (secondary band top); main or cross spine 1.15 x faceObb.majorM [land.spineFactor]; parallel spine the longest run of its seam type (<= majorM); contour series ceil(e_fall / s) x majorM (e_fall face width along slope.fallCdeg, s terraceSpacingM) plus, when the two-flank test holds, thalweg length x path class width; through street majorM less plaza long side; ring: Σ 2π r_k x w_top over expected series (u 0.5, spacing factor at bell mean) with r_k + eLo + w_top/2 <= inscribedRadiusM - eLo; landmark precinct rings course lengths x w_top up to landmark.maxRings; fan: most portals x ½ minorM x fan class width; bent-cut 0.

Reconcile: S7b (1)'s bounded reconcile (<= 3 rounds) with each district's capacity per band = pass-1 built land less under-deck strips plus owned deck-plot capacity (BCR-4 (b), BCR-39) less expected dispatch land less templateLandM2 (template land taken from bands in proportion to their built-land shares in the template face); households that don't fit move in S7b's declared order to the first district whose capacity holds them; institutions and workplaces never move for a template; nothing else about S7b changes.

S8 honours the reservation: plaza A capped at plaza land reserved; ring series ends when laid corridor area would pass ring land reserved x (1 + 0.10) [land.ringSlack]; contour series likewise with land.ringSlack (one series slack); spine laid by its law (clip can only shorten); a row failing on the committed face bends by F-TEMPLATE, a substitute only when its templateLandM2 on the committed face <= land reserved, else to bent-cut, keyed never re-drawn.

The draw is made once on the greedy χ̃ (J-V1.38). T-V1-12 reports households unplaced per template class with a stress fixture forcing each class to 100 % of districts in turn. Fallbacks: T-V1-12 fails -> spine factor 1.25, ring slack 0, re-measured; T-V1-2 (b) fails -> reconcile's re-homing replaced by one re-run of S7b (1)'s greedy pass on reduced capacities (same stream, fabric choices kept).

Kinds and rows offered (T-V1-6 counts): market square, crossroads, street (its market is its reservation, item 24); central square, crossroads; gate street, wallside; docks quay; riverbank quay (plotRow: NG planned river bank), bridgehead (NG-VC-3); temple, castle landmark (ring round precinct); craft, sprawl, suburb street; park park (green-mode plaza sized by §4.9 parks row, fan of 2-4 paths); shanty bent-cut only (item 70); hinterland, underground, undercity excluded (own recipes); sky kinds excluded from T-V1-6 (drawn in unit run with V05 fabricHint).

A template is seed geometry plus the bent cut on everything else (NG structure, CA-2): S8 lays the row's seed primitives in the template face before §4.6's recursion runs on every face; no template has a subdivision algorithm of its own.

Template face = D's largest L1 face by area that is not a wall strip, reservation, intramural garden (g 106 (b), never built land) or another district's, ties by face order (§3.3 canonical order), read by S8 on committed faces after S7b (3); other faces take the bent cut alone. Holes (S7b claims, landing claims (sky or ground landing yard V05 §3.10 (4)), a locked plot's face in a re-derivation, a V1-3.5.12 fixed input, every under-deck strip) stay holes: seeds avoid them (strip crossed only through an open span); §4.6 holed laws cut faces containing them; a strip crossing a face boundary-to-boundary cuts it and the template face is the largest piece measured without the strip; a held retaining wall is a line, not a hole.

(a) Portal usable when its vertex lies on a chain bounding the template face and class lane or above; rank through 5, primary 4, secondary and quay 3, lane 2, others 1; gate +2, bridge +1 (part-0 gate, never an aqueduct wall arch or raised gate; part-0 deck over water); raised ramp/stair end an ordinary junction by carried class; aqueduct end never a portal. A landing attach vertex (sky island or ground landing S8 destination, BCR-V5-20) ranks as gate (+2 on lane) and must be reached by a seed or lane; on the ground its destination lane (first cut from attach to nearest way by lane rule) is laid first in D's S8 transaction before the seeds and then treated as any spine.

(a) Anchors: portal:best = pair maximising (rank_a + rank_b) x min(1, abs(ab) / (0.7 x faceObb.majorM)) [anchor.spanShare], ties by portal id; pair:1, pair:2 = two usable pairs whose chords cross inside the face at >= 45° [elig.crossAngleDeg] maximising summed ranks, pair:1 higher, ties by ids; portal:gate / portal:bridge highest-ranked gate / bridge portal; axis = template face OBB major axis ends projected onto boundary (virtual; used when too few usable portals and in a standalone unit run).

(b) Template street width w_tpl, one per district, drawn once on hood.template (creation index 0): lerp(0.8 x top, top, u), top = upper end of secondary width band (§4.6 step 9) [tpl.widthLow 0.8]; it is the row's streetWidthM parameter (draw its default, secondary band its range; T8 'more' edits it); every seed way takes w_tpl and class secondary; path fan (park) takes path width; lanes the bent cut adds keep §4.6 step 9's law.

(c) Seeds inserted in the district's S8 transaction (callback, L1) in row order, each by insertChain of its course clipped to the face kerb (§3.7 single kerb function); an end meeting a spine becomes a T-junction by splitThrough (§4.6 step 7); on a district-boundary spine a baseLane portal with its SeamAmendment and portal-gap slide (II.1 (3)); an end at a hard seam or unit border stops on the setback/margin line, square to it; a later seed may end on an earlier one.

(d) Validation per seed on the overlay before commit: every segment >= minEdge; every interior turn <= 60°; clearance from face boundary >= eLo/2 except within eLo of ends; no crossing of another seed except a row's declared crossing or plaza ring; no hole contact (§3.6 attractCm) except a strip crossed through an open span; no run within eLo/2 of a held retaining wall along more than eLo (crossing at >= 45° allowed, takes a stair or ramp interval); every created face >= the band's minimum block width (§4.6 step 8). Failure is F-TEMPLATE's.

(e) After the seeds §4.6 runs on every face exactly as on a bent-cut district (stop test through recursion; holed laws; deep-interior rule); seeds are spines: lanes end on them as T-junctions so plots front seed streets. (f) Every seed draw on hood.template keyed by the template face's cell with the seed's creation index, except ring courses on cut.arc (§6.1, II.2): each seed its own sub-stream.

Main and cross spines: chord A to B, one control point at midpoint displaced perpendicular δ = (m3 - ½) x 0.3 x abs(AB) (m3 = §6.1 mean3); polyline A-c-B resampled into n = 3 + floor(5u) segments, each interior point displaced by (m3 - ½) x ½ x segment length; with probability (n-1)/n, 4 - floor(n/2) corner-cutting passes (¼, ¾) (ref:NG 1.2.2 main street course code; code-neighbourhood.md §2.1) in metres; each end's last leg re-aimed to arrive at the crossed spine's run within 85-95° (final leg >= eLo/2, square to chord); cross spine δ <= 0.05 x abs(AB).

Parallel spines: longest contiguous boundary run of that seam type (water or wall) on the template face, offset inward by onEdge = unbuildable band (§4.2 S1 (8) shore setback or wall strip inner setback line) + w_tpl/2, or plotRow = band + dBar + w_tpl/2; clipped; longest piece kept if >= 2 x eHi; one corner-cutting pass; each end continues by a square leg to the nearest way on the face boundary within 2 x eHi (T-junction), else stops at the setback line (reported dead end).

Contour series (stepped row, series true; J-V1.60): level lines of the unlevelled terrain (marching squares over the face's box) at z_k = z_pole + k x Δz, z_pole terrain at face pole of inaccessibility, Δz = s x slope.meanPct/100, s = terraceSpacingM (default 2 x dBar + w_tpl, range [1.5 x dBar + w_tpl, 3 x dBar + w_tpl], T8 more); level k street = longest component inside face inset by eLo (holes excluded), simplify at eLo/4, one corner-cutting pass, ends continued by square leg, kept when >= 2 x eHi; grows 0, +1, -1, +2, -2 ... until a level leaves the face or abs(k) reaches terrace.maxLevels (15, reported); a level within 0.6 x s [terrace.minGapShare] of the previous street on its side is clipped there. Level 0 must lay else F-TEMPLATE (rung 1 nothing to redraw, rung 2 offset level 0 by ± eLo/2 along the fall, + first, rung 3 row fallback). Each street secondary at w_tpl with terraceIndex (rank from lowest, 0); without series a contour spine is level 0 alone; bent cut runs cross lanes down the fall line (§4.6 step 1 slope term), V1-3.6 (3) steps them where steep, each retaining wall crossing a stair or ramp; creation index ordinal x 64 + f x 32 + (k + 16).

Ravine two flanks (J-V1.64): when the level line at z_pole has >= 2 components each >= 2 x eHi inside the inset face, S8 first lays a path-class thalweg seed (creation index ordinal x 64) along the valley line (flow line of greatest accumulation from S1 drainage), ends continued to boundary, stepped by V1-3.6 (3) where steep; face split along it (splitThrough), each flank (f = 0 holding the pole, f = 1 other) takes its own series with z_pole at its own pole; a flank below the spine law size takes none. With a stream the water is a seam, each flank its own district, no ward-edge wall on the water run (hard; BCR-42). A generated viaduct across the ravine (item 110 (b), CITY and METROPOLIS) is a strip in each flank face; thalweg passes under an open span.

Ring primitive: II.2 states the courses (hexagons one phase, radial bell ringJitter x spacing, three corner-cutting passes to 48 vertices, spacing law, outside-in bands with slit first, staggered radials, centre rule); V01 fixes: (1) centre c: centroid if inside face at >= eLo from boundary else pole of inaccessibility; landmark: centroid of the anchoring reservation (qualifying, highest σ, ties larger area then id); (2) radius budget R = distance from c to nearest boundary point less eLo.

Ring radii: s1 = eLo + u(R - eLo) (u on cut.arc, index 0); r1 = s1/2; one growth factor per district g = 1 + f (f folded four-uniform bell §6.1 bell4 on cut.arc index 1); s_k = s1 x g^(k-1), r_k = r_(k-1) + s_k (NG 1.2.2 geometric law, which II.2's spacing sentence now states, BCR-38; J-V1.37); ring k laid while its jittered smoothed course lies wholly inside the face inset by eLo + w_tpl/2 and laid corridor area stays within ring land reserved; first misfit ends the series (no clipped ring; NG-GQ-5 truncation removed).

Landmark precinct rings (J-V1.70): a precinct ring round each qualifying reservation in σ order up to landmark.maxRings (2): course = outline offset outward by dBar + w_tpl/2 (insetRing negative inset), three corner-cutting passes, 48 vertices; a circle of radius circumradius + dBar + w_tpl/2 only when circularity 4πA/P² >= landmark.roundTol 0.9; laid when wholly inside face inset by eLo + w_tpl/2 and >= 2 x eLo from every ring laid; each takes its own fan (2-4 portals); a later ring's fan may end on an earlier ring; precinct rings draw nothing.

Ring width w_tpl, class secondary, each ring a closed chain, one Way per ring. Faces and order: centre face, annuli (one hole each), outer band; bent cut runs outer band first, then annuli outside in, then centre, each band its own face and cell (radials stagger by construction). A radial end landing within the portal gap max(6 m, 2 x wider lane width) of the other band's end slides along the ring toward the side keeping 85-95° arrival; neither side -> next ladder rung (§4.6 step 7; a ring never carries a crossroads). Through radials (fabricParams.ringRadials = 1; NG-GQ-1; J-V1.53): each band's first radial after the slit continues the outer band's nearest end (portal-gap rule lifted for that pair); 0 default and NG's.

Ring centre rule: when §4.6 step 1 stops the centre face as one block, S8 marks it ringCentre and S9b gives it a square, green or manor block at equal odds among feasible (V1-3.5.6); where greenery rows allow neither greens nor trees, a square (innermost ring encloses a plaza, II.2 plaza loop).

Plaza size A = clamp(SquareRow[type].m2PerInhabitant x inhabitants, minM2, maxShareOfFace x templateFaceAreaM2) x fabricParams.plazaScale (default 1, range 0.5-2), rounded to lattice, at S8 at most the plaza land reserved; NG preset sizes by tag (ng.plazaByTag). Green-mode plaza A = clamp(parks rate x inhabitants, park.minM2 3 000 m² (0.3 ha floor), park.maxShareOfFace 0.4 x templateFaceAreaM2), parks rate §4.9's row at D's value (0.4-0.8 ha per 1 000).

Carved plaza: shape coin (rectangle or round at even odds on hood.template; ref:NG 1.2.2 square plaza code), rect, round; rectangle aspect 1 + bell4 when > 1.2 else 1, long side along face OBB major axis (J-V1.5); round = regular polygon max(8, round(2πr / wMin)) sides, r = sqrt(A/π). Site: centroid (pole of inaccessibility if centroid nearer than half-diagonal + eLo to boundary); crossing (cross spines' intersection); bridgeEnd/gate: near side on the portal's boundary kerb centred on portal, always on land. Fit inside face inset by eLo (near side excepted) clear of holes; else area x 0.8 (<= 3 times), then centre moved toward pole in steps of eLo/2 (<= 4); else F-TEMPLATE. Insertion: plaza ring one closed L1 chain with square role owned by Reservation kind plaza stage S8; through street: two straight spines (δ = 0) from short sides' midpoints (round: axis points) to face boundary; centrepiece by S11.

Green-mode plaza (park row): as carved but ring owned by Reservation kind park (S8), S9 types face green, S12b plants by §4.9 parks row (BCR-10); fan paths arrive at its ring; no centrepiece; its HoodPlace is a green.

Void plaza (fabricParams.squareVoid = 1; COV-VG-VN-179, IMPR S4): nothing carved in S8; S9b picks the void junction (among D's junctions inside the template face with >= 3 part-0 arms, nearest the face pole, ties by id) and writes each block with a corner vertex there voidCorner {junction, radiusCm 1.2 x sqrt(A/π)}; S10's claims-first step (§4.7 S10 (3)) claims per block the sub-face within that radius of the junction and within dBar of the frontage as residue kind square (paved, commons, road role); void square = corner claims + junction corridor inside the disc; centrepiece at the junction's wedge centroid (S11).

Fan primitive: from a plaza or ring to between portals[0] and portals[1] usable portals not already joined by a seed, in rank order, each new bearing >= 45° from every chosen one; each fan spine is §4.6's two-leg cut with start and far side forced (leaves the anchor run square nearest the portal bearing, corner by step 4 law on hood.template, arrives square at the portal's spine, step 5 flatten test, step 6 fillet); w_tpl and secondary, or path class for a path fan.

Template rows (card; seeds; fabricParams; fallback): bent-cut (Organic; NG area; -; -; -); street (Main street; spine main portal:best to portal:best; streetWidthM; bent-cut); square (Square; plaza centroid carved coin type by V1-3.5.3 rule at site, through; plazaScale 1, squareVoid 0, streetWidthM; bent-cut); ring (Rings; ring centroid law; ringJitter 0.15, ringPasses 3 (II.2), ringRadials 0, streetWidthM; square, bent-cut); quay (Quayside; spine parallel water, onEdge when kind docks or band >= prosperous else plotRow; quayOnEdge 0/1, streetWidthM; street, bent-cut); wallside (Wall-side; spine parallel wall (walled only), plotRow; streetWidthM; bent-cut); crossroads (spine cross pair:1, pair:2, plaza crossing carved rect crossroads; plazaScale 1, streetWidthM; street, bent-cut); landmark (Around the church; precinct rings <= landmark.maxRings, fan per ring 2-4 secondary; streetWidthM; bent-cut); bridgehead (plaza bridgeEnd carved rect bridgehead, fan 2-3 secondary; plazaScale 1, streetWidthM; square, bent-cut); stepped (Terraces; contour series, ravine thalweg + series per flank; streetWidthM, terraceSpacingM; bent-cut); park (Green; plaza centroid green round, fan 2-4 path; plazaScale 1; bent-cut).

Four NG rows emulate NG 1.2.2 (area = base bent cut; street, square, ring restated in metres); seven context rows ours (extension true): NG-VC-3's planned templates (junction, park, river bank, bridge, port) plus II.2's context features; the square row's default is carved (NG 1.2.2's own, J-V1.6, BCR-20, correcting J-S42's premise); void is its other mode.

Standalone unit run has no portal: portal:best resolves to axis, except a street hood whose main spine is the course S0 drew and built the outline round; ring hood's outer-band radials end on the margin line; bridgehead and crossroads never eligible. Sky unit run: landings' attach vertices and deck ends of laid crossing sites are its only portals (template portals kind landing and bridge), never counted in SeamReport.portalsTotal.

S9b per district in lineage order on the generation worker as S10a's block hook, after S10a (i) (field-driving classes and institutions below a block) and before (ii) field pass 2 (J-V1.40): compute three quotas, type blocks in two phases (quota-driven squares, greens, manors; weighted draw for remaining small blocks), writing content, squareType, voidCorner. Runs only while fabric.extensionWeight > 0 (parity presets: every block ordinary); under NG per V1-3.15.

S9b candidate blocks: D's L2 built blocks whose interior is not wall_strip, reserved, green, landmark or rim_strip (S8 typed those, §4.6 step 8 (d)), not an intramural garden, holding no S10a (i) item (field-driving class e.g. tannery, midden, prison; institution below a block incl. SIZE compound and GUILD hall), holding no fixed input; untyped stay ordinary; every draw on hood.dispatch; deck plots are never candidates (not blocks).

Band S9b reads per block = the band §4.7 S10 (2) reads: pass-1 field band at generation; in every re-derivation over standing plots (epoch, replace close-up, content edit) the block's manifested band (II.3; item 31, J-A31.43) so a fallen-field block keeps its mansion's manor; quotas stay district-level at D's value; hood pin gates read the field band (II.3).

Quotas: inhabitants N = Σ allocation household rows x roster mean household size at each band; squares Q_sq = max(0, N/1 000 x haPer1000(value) x kind[D.kind] x 10 000 - squaresM2) m² from squares.quota (base table, BCR-32; J-V1.39), value = D's pass-1 value (row interpolated); defaults haPer1000 squalid 0.05, poor 0.05, modest 0.07, comfortable 0.08, prosperous 0.10, rich 0.12; kind factors market 1.5, central 1.3, temple 1.2, gate 1.2 (ours; S4 (d) band 0.03-0.15 median 0.08 over all square sources, §13.7).

Greens Q_gr = max(0, G_D - Σ D's S7b green claims), G_D = §4.9's public green for D (parks row at band and planned intent, greens toggle floor rates): the sub-block part met here with whole small blocks.

Manors M = min(round(manorBlockShare(band) x N_ord), H_top); N_ord candidate blocks in manor fit band; H_top = allocated households whose band lies inside D's provisional band range (§4.5 (5), pass-1 mean) and >= prosperous, x class mix probability (§4.7 S10b, item 71) of a compound-arrangement class at each band centre. Defaults manorBlockShare 0 up to modest, comfortable 0.02, prosperous 0.06, rich 0.12 (ours; NG measured 6-11 % anchor, profile-neighbourhood.md §3.3); 0 for secular standalone.

Square type split q_t ∝ base_t x factor: forecourt 0.2 x (1 + 2 mix.religion) only where a church, temple or GUILD hall stands on an S3 or S7b reservation touching D and has no §4.8 forecourt; bridgehead 0.3 when a bridge portal bounds D else 0; trading 0.4 when kind market else 0.05 x (1 + sectors.trade); crossroads 0.2 x (1 + 2 trade); well 0.3; Q_t = q_t x Q_sq after normalising. A trading square is never a market: no stalls, no market rank, never a market Reservation, outside item 24's count and separation (J-V1.44).

Square sites: block area <= min(2 x smallBlockM2, 5 000 m²) [sq.maxM2], smallBlockM2 = eLo²/2 (ref:NG 1.2.2 small-block rule code); forecourt at generation only against a landmark on a reservation: reservation's boundary side on its widest frontage way, block shares that way and centroid within 60 m [sq.forecourtM] of that side's midpoint; in a re-derivation the landmark's committed main entrance within 60 m and a shared frontage way; a church/temple below a block never takes an S9b forecourt (its forecourt is §4.7 S11's forecourt yard part); bridgehead corner within 40 m [sq.bridgeM] of a part-0 bridge-end junction; trading and crossroads a corner at a junction with >= 3 part-0 arms, one tier 1 (through, primary) or two tier 2 (secondary, quay; §8.5 tiers); well a corner at a junction with a tier-1 or tier-2 arm.

Square filling per type in order forecourt, bridgehead, trading, crossroads, well: candidates by score (siting distance asc, area nearest Q_t remaining, sunnier (lower shade at centroid, g 102 (d)), flatter (lower area-weighted mean unlevelled slope; ours, extension), block id), taken while Q_t remains and area <= 1.5 x Q_t remaining [sq.overTake]; unmet quota rolls to next type; last remainder reported stage2.squares.unmet (F-DISPATCH). Template plazas already count in squaresM2; a square template's plaza takes trading when kind market, forecourt when a landmark reservation's widest side faces it, else crossroads.

Greens: candidates of area <= 1.5 x D's median block area [green.maxMedian], no frontage on a tier-1 part-0 way, >= 2 x eHi [green.spacingEHi] from every green; score = (1 + intent.greenery) / (1 + d_c/eHi) x siting (d_c distance to D's pole; siting = V1-3.5.5 push product with the sensitivity row of D's modal household class); taken in score order while Q_gr remains and area <= 1.5 x Q_gr remaining: content green.

Manor fit band: block area in [1.0, 3.0] x [manor.fitLow, manor.fitHigh] the plot-area budget of the largest compound class with nonzero weight at D's upper band (§4.7 S11 designation template size budget); candidates weighted prestige x spacing x sun x siting: prestige = §4.7 S10b prestige rows over frontages; spacing = min(1, d_m / (2 x eHi)) [manor.spacingEHi], d_m to nearest manor block or landmark reservation, a weight never a floor (ref:NG 1.2.2 manor spacing code; BCR-22 (a)).

Manor sun = 1 - manor.sunWeight x shade(centroid) [manor.sunWeight 0.5, ours, extension]; shade(x) = pass-1 terrain and wall mask OR-ed with every live island's strip onto the ground (V05 §2.3a), strips evaluated once per shade evaluation (generation, re-derivation from S10a or earlier, epoch V05 §3.19 (6)) at S9b's first read by the same pure call field pass 2 makes, and held (no strip computed twice); on a sky arena shade(x) = V05 shadeSky(x) on the 32 m lattice, no sky reader reads the ground pass-1 mask.

Manor siting = Π(1 - push) over blocks S10a (i) filled, push = weight of derived family row fam/nuisance/<n>/L<level> (V11 §2.4) for each nuisance the placed class emits and compound class is sensitive to, when within that row's radius at the emitter's level (block edge to edge), else 0; clamped [0,1]; extension (g 103 (a)); weight-1 row keeps every manor out of its radius. M blocks drawn without replacement by weight on hood.dispatch keyed by district lineage with pick ordinal as creation index, weights recomputed after each pick: content manor.

Phase 2 small blocks: every untyped candidate with area <= smallBlockM2 draws content from the band row's small weights (interpolated): squalid 0.80 ordinary/0.20 yard/0 green, poor 0.70/0.25/0.05, modest 0.60/0.30/0.10, comfortable 0.50/0.35/0.15, prosperous 0.45/0.30/0.25, rich 0.40/0.25/0.35 (ours; NG empties every small block, 0-3 % empty, profile-neighbourhood.md §3.3; NG preset does; calibrated at M5 on NG panel pairs); green weight x V1-3.5.4 siting product; draw on hood.dispatch keyed by block pick ordinal 0; yard paving (yardPaved) same key pick ordinal 1.

A ringCentre block draws among feasible {square (plain or siting type), green, manor} at equal odds (II.2 centre rule; pick ordinal 0); manor feasible only in the fit band with a compound class allowed; green only when greenery rows allow greens. Phase-2 over-quota typing allowed up to 1.5 x each quota [dispatch.overQuota]; beyond it ordinary.

Court greening (§4.9 row): S12b plants a block's court residue as a green with trees with probability squalid 0.10, poor 0.20, modest 0.35, comfortable 0.45, prosperous 0.60, rich 0.80, x (0.5 + D's greenery value), x 1.5 for leafy standalone, clamped [0,1], drawn on greenery keyed by block (ours; NG 23-58 % anchor, item 58 (b)); extension (0 in parity presets); an ungreened court stays bare court ground; a court a RetainingWall crosses is greened or not by one draw, a greened one plants every level piece (terraced garden).

Seam guard (S3): a block whose frontage on soft seams (way and field runs shared with another district) is >= 30 % [guard.softShare] is a manor or green candidate only when the district across has a pass-1 band within one band [guard.bands] of D's at the seam's boundary samples (S3's band §13.7: Δ median frontage <= 25 %, Δ plot area <= 35 %, Δ storeys <= 1).

Land in the programme: S2's land estimate multiplies each band's plot land by (1 + λ_b), λ_b = sq_b + gr_b + yd_b (sq_b sub-block share of squares.quota over plot land per 1 000 inhabitants; gr_b sub-block green share of §4.9 rows; yd_b = small-block share 0.12 [land.smallShare] (ours, measured on B-CITY at M5) x (small.yard + small.green)); S7b (1) capacity subtracts expected dispatch land (Q_sq + Q_gr + yard expectation) and in reconcile the template land; a manor block holds one household and compound, its expected capacity loss (row capacity less one) also subtracted.
T-V1-12: on B-CITY 0 households unplaced because of a dispatched block or template (F-SITING shows none), per template class. Fallback: λ_b + 0.05 and re-run; V1-3.3.7's for template land.

Downstream per content: ordinary base everywhere, court greened by V1-3.5.7; manor: S10a one household of D's top band inside D's band range with its members (servants are members §10.3, no extra allocation), S10 all residential plots joined by §4.7 S10 (7) join law, S10b/S11 class mix among compound classes only (item 71 renormalised) and compound site plan with enclosure (§4.7 S11), S12b compound yard planting, name its house's (§10.4); square: capacity 0, no plots, one L3 residue face kind square (paved, commons), centrepiece on pin.centrepiece by SquareRow.centrepiece at face pole (skipped where an aqueduct terminal is the centrepiece), no stalls (item 24), HoodPlace, drawn in road role; green: capacity 0, one residue face kind green, green Greenery owned by commons, grove layout by §4.9 small-face park rule, §4.9 parks row admits it at any size (BCR-10), HoodPlace; yard: capacity 0, one residue face yard_common paved with probability yardPaved (poor 0.7 to rich 0.4) else grassed, no model pin, grassed: yard planting, HoodPlace local.

SquareRow.centrepiece defaults: forecourt cross 0.7 / statue 0.3; crossroads market cross 0.5 / well 0.3 / fountain 0.2; bridgehead statue 0.5 / cross 0.5; trading market cross 0.8 / fountain 0.2; well well 0.7 / pump 0.2 / trough 0.1; plain as well.

F-DISPATCH revert rung: after S10a (ii) re-homes households outside D's band range (§4.5 (5)), a manor block whose district holds no household of the block's band range reverts to ordinary, reported stage2.dispatch.manorReverted; never left empty.

Epochs: the hood.fabric participant runs S9b's rule on blocks an epoch creates outside a growth run's S10a hook and on due blocks rung 3 redevelops; a re-cut block otherwise keeps content; a standing square, green or manor block is a survivor.

Fixed inputs: S9b never types a fixed input's block square, green, manor or yard, and a re-derivation (replace close-up, content edit scope, epoch) keeps its plot and site (§7.2): (1) locked, pinned, assigned or dossier-backed plot; (2) a SIZE record's compound (g 108 (a)); (3) a GUILD record's hall; (4) a catacomb's source cemetery (V04 UndergroundSystem.sources under g 109 (k)(2) as revised ~20:05): churchyard part's plot, separate burial ground face, monastery burial face, quarry ossuary surface head, plus the plot holding the church owning a sourcing churchyard and the plot holding the catacomb's entrance AccessPoint (extramural cemetery in hinterland, never typed); (5) a declared RetainingWall (a line every re-derivation keeps and every seed respects); (6) a raised part's under-deck strip with piers (a hole no re-derivation plots). At generation (2),(3) are S10a (i) blocks (not candidates); (4) exists only in re-derivation (V04 systems laid after ground plots).

Ladder records (g 108): QUARTER record whose district is D makes D's identity the dossier's (item 72 (3); identitySource dossier), read by S7c identity term, panel, title; members elsewhere keep districts; GUILD hall on a reservation is a σ-bearing landmark for S9b's forecourt; COUNT members are ordinary allocation rows keyed #k (DR9, J-A74.73); no double counting (108 (c)): each member counted once in its plot's district; membersHere + Σ elsewhere = membersTotal = record count.

Context features, every district whatever its fabric (S2 (a) coverage matrix reads them): (1) Waterfront (water run >= 60 m [feature.runM]): S8 lays a bank path (path-class spine along the shore setback inner line, parallel at onEdge with path width) when kind docks/riverbank or band >= comfortable and no noxious water trade (profile emits water pollution, V11 §2.3) allocated and no quay way already along; else rear-plot water rule: plots with rear line within dBar of shore setback extend to it and take a shore yard part (§4.7 S10 (6)) with water access edge; a quay template spine satisfies it; a closure-only water arc is a water run.

(2) Wall-side (walled wall run >= 60 m: full or parapet stretch): intervallum where the era row has one and stretch is full (§4.8); else the base's rear-plot behaviour (S8 lanes end on the inner setback line, plots back onto the wall strip); a wallside template adds the wall street.

(3) Slope: a lane, alley, cul_de_sac or path whose slopeP95 (§2.4, written by S9 from the unlevelled terrain, BCR-6; levelling never rewrites it; a terrain stroke re-samples it) exceeds its class's rampMaxGrade in V11's ways.crossing (item 110 (a) way-class rule; lane, alley, cul-de-sac 12 %, path 15 %) is stepped, one threshold stated once (J-V1.72): S14 draws step ticks at district band and finer; naming reads stepped; no model field. A stepped lane may be carried on vaults (II.7.6 vaultSlope, base's and V04's), not drawn or read here. A way crossing a RetainingWall carries a stair or ramp interval (base way-class rule, item 110 (a)) never changing shape, slopeP95 or name; drawn by way.stair.

(4) Bridge approach: §4.6 step 7 portal gap keeps lanes off a bridge end; bridgehead squares and template read it (part-0 deck over water); a raised road's ramp/stair end takes the portal gap extended over its rise. (5) Gate approach: base gate plaza (§4.8), nothing added; an aqueduct arch through a curtain and a raised gate at deck level are wall openings, not gates (no gate portal, plaza or wall-side feature). (6) Sky: no portals but landing attaches; outline seams sky (hard); rim strip along them, margin band only where a run has no rim strip.

(7) Barrier edges (g 106 (a)(f)): a boundary run on a barrier-closure arc typed by its barrier kind (J-VI.3's six): shore -> water; cliff and gorge -> cliff; marsh -> new hard type marsh; enceinte (earlier ring's curtain) -> wall with that enceinte's stretch class; sheer (island rim) never types a ground seam (V05 §3.21). cliff or marsh run takes the rear-plot rule, never a wall street; panel names it ('the cliff is the wall here', g 106 (g)).

(8) Terraced wards (g 110 (a)): a district whose terrace.asks holds is terraced; the base's S10-S11 levelling levels each plot to its fronting street, so a base-produced wall holds the rear line once the step passes terrace.stepMinCm and the slope terrace.slopeMin; this volume produces no wall there (one producer per wall line; J-V1.61); where slope.meanPct in [8 %, 100 x terrace.slopeMin) the stepped row lays contour streets, no edge wall (walls false), base walls only levelled units steeper than slopeMin. Along D's edge the base district-edge source raises the ward-edge wall by BCR-42 with this volume's inputs (terraceState, terracedEdges). S2 (a) coverage gains row 'terraced district x ward-edge wall, or none with its reason (below slope threshold, no soft backing run, no step)'.

S13a local-place step (@plat/hood registration, two passes around the way names): (a) creation pass before ways are named creates/keeps one HoodPlace (kind, host, lineage, no name) per square, green or yard block; every court residue of area >= court.nameMinM2 (200 m², ours), one per residue even where a RetainingWall crosses it (labelled on its largest level piece); a square or park template's or void square's plaza (hosted by plaza reservation block or, for a void, the junction's largest corner block); (b) S13a names the ways reading these records; (c) naming pass names each place via §10.4 on naming keyed by place lineage from V11 naming.place conditioned on kind, squareType, centrepiece pin kind, adjacent landmark, dominant trade family of fronting plots (σ-weighted >= 0.3), D's identity row, proper-name source for courts and yards; never a way's name (no cycle); uniqueness §9.6 per district per kind.

HoodPlace knowledge defaults from hood.placeKnowledge: square and green public, court and yard local (a court's name shows to the public only at the neighbourhood band and finer, §9.2; item 30); a dossier naming claim may name a place (§7.7 item 82), name then dossier-owned; LabelEntity kind place, lod district and neighbourhood bands for squares and greens, neighbourhood band for courts and yards, spine candidates by §9.3 area rule; the step is extension (runs only while fabric.extensionWeight > 0; parity presets create no places); court names only a block's court residue (§4.7 S10 (6)): a footprint's court (V02 yard part court, BCR-V2-24: manor enclosed court, ovalCourt arena floor) is never a HoodPlace.

Opening pass (J-V1.76), run by the underground tail after systems and AccessPoints are laid, selecting by V04 record fields never kind alone (mouth is also sewer outfall, culvert inlet, quarry adit end, skylight): one opening HoodPlace (1) per public opening (AccessPoint source opening, role access, V04 §3.5.7 (e)), subtype its kind sinkhole, mouth, collapsed_shaft, ruin_entrance (f item 554; V04 BCR-29, V01 BCR-37 merged); a skylight (mouth role light) makes no place; (2) per catacomb entrance (AccessPoint kind stair, source system, cause.system a catacomb system, V04 §3.5.1 (9), incl. quarry ossuary stair) subtype catacomb. No other access makes a place (sewer mouth, quarry adit, grating, neighbourhood or lifeline stair keep symbols only). Named from naming.place with opening kind feature; knownTo the AccessPoint's; lives as long as host while the step runs.

Catacomb entrance only on cemetery ground (g 109 (k)(2) revised ~20:05): churchyard part of a church, temple or cathedral plot, never inside the footprint of a church-class building (crypt column always or basement; V03 J-V3.73); a separate burial ground face; a monastery burial face; an extramural cemetery face in the hinterland; or at CITY and METROPOLIS only a quarry ossuary's surface head (V04 §3.5.1 (9)); its place carries its catacomb's name, knowledge the AccessPoint's. No crypt gets a place or a pin (crypt = Basement.crypt, V03 §3.7.4, BCR-V3-20; J-VI.17 H33); a crypt joined to a catacomb by a (3b) link adds no second entrance. A building's dug access gets no place (hosted by building or basement: plan draws its head, V03 3.7.2 (5); opening in a yard: symbol on its plot); an unexcavated void puts nothing on the surface.

A place made by hand: T11 name tool on an unnamed court residue, yard or square creates its HoodPlace with the typed name, setAttr(name) on a new place minted from the event's seq; lifecycle and undo are HoodPlace's.

Way-naming context (BCR-16) per way at S13a: shape ring (ring course), stepped (V1-3.6 (3)), curved when a fillet arc spans >= 30 % [name.curvedShare] of length, bent when a corner >= 15° [name.bentDeg], else straight; to = kind of node or place it leads to (gate, market, bridge, church forecourt, castle, harbour, named square or well) from Way.from/Way.to and HoodPlace records at its ends; landmark = reservation σ >= 5 within 50 m [name.landmarkM] of frontage; trade = class family of >= 0.3 [name.tradeShare] of σ-weighted fronting uses (never a quarter, g 104 (h)(3), 107 (e)); band; districtIdentity; water; slopePct; placeOnIt; terraceIndex (V11 naming.way may guard Upper/Middle/Lower Terrace). Raised road takes shape, to, landmark only, kind word the base's; aqueduct no context; a crossing interval never changes shape (no name shift).

V11's grammar rows guard on these features with weights, no strict priority; two lanes of one trade in one district get distinct names by §9.6 uniqueness; context derived at S13a from eager records so names stay eager model data (§4.10); features land at M1; M5's squares and places give some ways new to or placeOnIt, a declared M5 shift of those names (§13.3 shift record).

Way surfaces (BCR-6): at S10a's end after field pass 2 every way without an edited surface takes way.surface's value for class, era row and band of its fronting blocks (area-weighted pass-2 value, both sides). Defaults (ours): through, primary paved (setts) at comfortable+ from the high medieval else cobble; secondary cobble at modest+ else dirt; lane, alley, cul_de_sac cobble at comfortable+ else dirt; track, path dirt; quay paved; pier planks; bridge paved stone / planks timber (Bridge.kind); ford dirt. Raised road takes the base's value from its record (masonry paved, timber planks, V11 raisedWays.structure); aqueduct no surface. hatched road programs read it; MFCG draws none. Epoch re-derives past the hysteresis (§4.5); a way bounding a re-derived district reads both sides so surface and naming record belong to that district's seam exception (BCR-33); replace dry run lists each shared way whose surface or name changes.

District naming features (BCR-16): §10.4's district naming (V11 naming.district) reads fabric (hood.templates row), hasManorBlock, hasGreenBlock, ringCentre (square/green/manor), terraced (terrace.asks), small (area below the lower third of the town's district areas; standalone: small chip); V11 rows guard with weights never strict priority; T-V1-24 checks name-feature consistency.

Close-up trigger (§4.1 policy): under elaborate 'click', a click on a district at city or district band derives its close-up and raises its buildings' wings rung (II.4); a click on a building at these bands is this click, selecting the building and opening its panel without rooms or plan (V03 §4.5; V02 §3.11); under 'view' every district with a visible tile at neighbourhood band derives within V1-6's budget; outline close-up derives those of districts and hinterland faces it meets and raises the wings rung of every building inside, centre-out from the outline centroid. Runs in the derivation pool (or generation worker with pool off), never the tile worker; delivers marks as a DisplayDelta of group D (§8.9); opening/closing/reopening leaves the model digest unchanged (II.5).

Hood pins per block in lineage order (outline close-up: each hinterland face in face order), each site on pin.decor keyed by the block with stage component STAGE_VIEW and site ordinal as pick ordinal, order gate, kind, size, angle. (1) Sites: court (court residues in order); plotYard (plots' yard parts yard, garden, court (footprint court except an ovalCourt arena floor, no pin), forecourt, churchyard of area >= 30 m² [pin.siteMinM2]); yardBlock and square: four edge sites (OBB corners inset 3 m [pin.edgeInsetM]) and the pole when no model centrepiece; green: pole and two next clearance maxima (§3.8 spine reader); hinterland cemetery (pole and four edge sites), fieldEdge (two corners nearest a way), outsideYard (outside plot yard parts >= 30 m²). Site point = face pole of inaccessibility else next clearance maximum; a court residue crossed by a RetainingWall = one site per level piece (pieces < pin.siteMinM2 dropped); no site on a deck plot or under-deck strip.

(2) Prior picks: before a block's first site every model pin in the block (S11 decoration rows, centrepiece, singleton) counts as a prior pick of its kind (decay applied); a per-district singleton kind (bandstand, statue, monument) standing in D as a model pin is removed from D's hood rows; an aqueduct terminal outlet in or fronting a square counts as a prior fountain pick. (3) Gate p_r = gate_r(band) x siteFactor x pinGate x identity_r x (1 + shadeGain_r x shade(site)); band at site's plot or block (field band, II.3); siteFactor 1 for square, yardBlock, green; pin.courtFactor (0.2) for court, plotYard, hinterland (J-V1.43); identity from placed identity row; shade item 102's (sky: shadeSky); site holds a pin when u < min(0.6, 1 - Π(1 - p_r)) [pin.cap].

(4) Kind: weighted pick over rows with nonzero p_r, weight r.weight x decay_r, decay_r starting at 1 per block and divided by 10 after r is picked (II.3 rule; ref:NG 1.2.2 pin decay code, P20); scope pin.decayScope: block by default, district under NG.

(5) Placement: size lerp(sizeM, u); pin at site point when its disc (size/2 + clearanceM) clears every footprint, entrance reserve, model pin disc, drawn ground-access symbol disc (only accesses on a ground face outside every footprint draw one), hood pin placed, way corridor, raised-way pier footprint and under-deck strip, every retaining-wall line (half-width + clearanceM); else next clearance maximum; else no pin (debug report only). Angle = host face OBB axis + 90° x floor(2u). (6) Overrides applied last.

Entrance reserve (J-V1.75, J-V1.96): outside each building's main entrance and each side, rear, yard or service entrance (§2.6 roles; a concealed use's door among them, rectangle never drawn), a rectangle on the entrance's footprint side at offsetCm outward, from the base's eager Entrance records (never the lazy composition), widthM[1] wide and depthM[1] deep of V02's porch kind rows (main: largest over PorchKindRows with outside true; others: the hood row's, secondary porch kind; composition.json shipped from M3a-V2 so the reserve stands from M5); where Basement.access is external, the main entrance's rectangle again outward from the footprint side nearest V03 basementDoor(b), centred on its projection (none where basementDoor(b) null: base trapdoor fallback); for each AccessPoint hosted by a building with neither basement nor ground(b) (V03 3.3), the hood row's rectangle outward from the side where stackAccessDoor(b,a) lies centred on its at (a well access opens at its well pin, no rectangle; a building on a deck hosts no head). Holds porch, secondary porch, stoop, outside basement stair and stack access door whichever rungs are derived, so the close-up is a pure function of committed state in any order.
T-V1-26 measures close-up purity in any order of click, wings rung and plan; fallback: reserve depth doubled, re-measured.

Default hood.pins rows (ours, calibratable, extension; gates at square/yardBlock/green sites, x 0.2 at court/plotYard/hinterland): well (court, plotYard, yardBlock, square, cemetery; 0.35 at poor falling to 0.10 at rich, 0.07 to 0.02 in a court); pump (plotYard, yardBlock; 0.15 to 0.05); trough (square, yardBlock, fieldEdge; 0.10); fountain (square, court; 0.02 to 0.30; shadeGain -0.5); large tree (court, plotYard, yardBlock, green, cemetery, fieldEdge; 0.10 to 0.35 x (0.5 + greenery)); statue (square, court; 0 to 0.10); monument (square, cemetery; 0.05); bandstand (green, square; 0 below prosperous, 0.05; shadeGain -0.5); cross (square, cemetery, fieldEdge; 0.05, x 3 religious identity); shrine (court, plotYard, fieldEdge; 0.05, x 2 religious). Underground rows V04's (none shipped: underground close-up draws no hood pins); sky arena reads the ground rows.

T-V1-31: pins per 100 buildings per kind and template within 3 x NG's for the default preset and within NG's band under NG; fallback pin.courtFactor scales all court and yard gates by one factor to meet the ceiling.

Close-up cache: derived content (HoodPins only; names, squares, greens, places are eager model data; ground AccessPoint symbols drawn from the model) is one elaboration chunk of rung closeup per district and one per hinterland L1 face an outline opens (§2.9), keyed by it and its inputs digest: leaf digests of blocks, plots, yard parts, court residues, model pins, ground AccessPoints (building-hosted included), footprints, Entrance records, Basement.access, basementDoor(b) value, each stack-hosted access's stackAccessDoor(b,a) value and ground(b), the PorchKindRow slice of composition.json, every RetainingWall, raised strip and pier on D's faces, owned deck plots with buildings, CloseupRecord (or default params), the hood.pins slice cited, every Block.overrides. <= 32 KB per district [closeup.chunkKB]; counted in §12.8's elaboration cache and LRU-evicted to absent (pure function, nothing lost).

Staleness: a batch changing any input sets the district's closeup record stale (§2.8) with the change marker at the city band (§8.5); cached pins stay on view until the next click re-derives from committed state never the cache (§4.1); a stale close-up under 'view' re-derives on its tile request; no canonical prior (only authored content is Block.overrides, re-applied).

Overrides: an instance event on a hood pin writes §2.7's override row on its block; op, ordinal (hood:<n> generated, u<n> add) and style (InstanceStyle with pinKind BCR-34 adds, so restyle can turn a well into a fountain, add names its kind) are the event's; resolution §8.10's law unchanged: by ordinal while lineage unchanged and generated position within 0.5 x spacing of recorded point; else by position to nearest unclaimed same-kind pin within 0.5 x spacing; else orphaned and reported; spacing = 2 x clearanceM + sizeM[1] of its row; superseded block's rows move to supersededBy successor.

Persistence: the first hood-pin edit inside a close-up (instance event on a hood pin or params change) is preceded by a closeup event writing CloseupRecord (params and table version) into the closeups block of the model digest (II.4); a later closeup event replaces the params (undo restores); every other close-up element is a base entity edited with no closeup event (lane name, plot, building, square centrepiece model pin, place name; BCR-23, BCR-12 (d)).

Frame and surroundings: opening frames the view by §9.5's framing rule restricted to D's footprints and owned decks (outline close-up: the outline); neighbours draw base marks at neighbourhood band to the frame's edge, never cut (§8.6), under the style's optional closeup.vignette (none default, fade, plateau).
An underground district opens as a refine close-up drawing no hood pins (V04 ships no underground rows); a sky district opens like a ground one on its island's arena; neither changes the ground.

Ground access symbols (J-V1.74): every ground AccessPoint whose ground.host is a ground face (corridor, square, yard, outside face, catacomb entrance's burial face) in the opened area and whose ground.at lies outside every footprint is drawn at ground.at in the hatched pins slot (V1-5.1.3 slot 10): grating, neighbourhood or lifeline stair, sinkhole, cave mouth, sewer outfall or culvert mouth, collapsed shaft, ruin entrance, catacomb entrance, and a cellar stair, shaft, ladder, hatch or broken-through well opening in a yard; sized by access.<accessSymbolKind>M; drawn in the form §8.2's access states row gives its state (stored locked with a bar; bricked solid in wall incl. landfall and host closures, V04 §3.10) or while its element is closed the derived reading (sealed -> bricked; collapsed as a trace with rubble stipple; II.7.4, II.6; J-V1.93).

An access hosted by a building or basement, or whose ground.at is inside a footprint (catacomb stair in a cemetery chapel), draws no surface symbol: roof covers it at neighbourhood band, building plan draws its head at building band (V03 3.7.2 (5), 3.7.3, 5.1; secret head by 5.4); one mark per access; an arch vault's door is the base's infill drawing, no symbol; §9.2 admission filters by knownTo (yard access local at neighbourhood band for a public key; secret only at building band to a key holding it); unexcavated void has no AccessPoint (g 109 (j)(2)); symbols drawn from the model, never stored in the chunk; hood pins clear their discs.

AccessSymbolKind = Exclude<AccessPoint.kind, door> or catacomb; accessSymbolKind(a) (@plat/hood, derived never stored) = catacomb for a catacomb entrance (kind stair, source system, cause.system catacomb) else a.kind; values: base AccessPoint.kind as f item 554 extends it less door plus catacomb: twelve (stair, ladder, hatch, shaft, well, cellar_stair, grating, mouth, sinkhole, collapsed_shaft, ruin_entrance, catacomb); keys V1-5.1.2's drawing and size column access.<kind>M; hood.constants' access.*M columns equal this set, held by T-V1-4's registry test (not a TotalityRule), so enum and columns change together (J-V1.100).

Outline close-up (J-V1.45): a view action, no event, no model change: user draws a rectangle or lasso or picks a named site from the reader's sites query (cemetery, quarry, mill, catacomb source, shrine); view derives the refine close-up of every district met and for the part outside every district the hinterland pseudo-district's L1 faces inside it, raises the wings rung of every building inside centre-out, frames to the outline; hinterland close-up chunked per L1 face using ground rows with sites cemetery, fieldEdge, outsideYard; a hood-pin edit there takes a closeup event on the hinterland pseudo-district (one CloseupRecord); unit run not used; an outline over a harbour opens the decks it meets with their owning districts; a quarter declaration stays the way to make a new district.

Replace close-up is a model edit (II.4): one undo group of setAttr(D.fabric, r) (and setAttr(D.fabricParams.k, v)) then regenerate({ids:[D]}, 'keep'); effective scope = §7.3 item 1's district scope from S8 (tree scoping) with the seam exception extended by BCR-33 to surface and naming record of D's bounding ways, plus S10a (i) and S9b for D's blocks, S10a's distribution for D (Allocation unchanged), S10-S12b for D, town-wide S12c (derived), S13a within scope, plus cross-arena consequences of V04 §4.3's ground-edit row and V05 §4.3's island re-read (cited, predicted by the oracle).

Replace fixed inputs (§7.2): locked, pinned, assigned, dossier-backed entities in D (a sky island's institution released for one event only by a re-searched claim, V1-3.10.3 (6)(c)) and V1-3.5.12's (SIZE compound, GUILD hall, catacomb source cemetery with owning church plot and entrance plot, declared retaining wall, under-deck strip): faces stay, template lays round them as holes, S9b never types them away (J-V1.46).

Replace dry run (§7.1) runs the whole re-derivation on the overlay and returns: ghost of new ways and blocks (live.ghost, §8.2) with count badge (plots, households, buildings); fate report (kept, carried, orphaned); renames of case (4) (§7.3 item 4) incl. each shared way whose surface or name changes; each generated retaining wall added/removed/moved and each declared wall kept; as information each neighbouring wall whose derived step changes by >= terrace.profileNoticeCm (50 cm); template fallback bend in one line; for a stagnant catacomb whose extent lies under a plot the fates demolish or clear, the blockLifted notice {system, plots, cause: event seq} which V04 reads from the logged fate report to resume growth by least disruption; cross-arena fates with underground or sky on. Successions go to SeamReport.superseded (II.1 (4)); budget V1-6's.

A targeted edit of a catacomb's source (retyping the churchyard plot, demolishing the owning church, turning a burial ground into houses) is allowed (item 22 least disruption; item 101 R2): dry run lists the source's closure among the fates and names it in one line (V04 §3.5.1 (8): complex frozen, no growth, fill unchanged, galleries kept); a catacomb never shrinks (g 109 (k)(4)-(5)). A refine close-up emits no notice and moves nothing.

Unit run: a request whose boundary has no committed fabric runs the pipeline as a unit on its own arena (own overlay, no other writer, merged in lineage order, §4.1 unit sense); request carries no seam, context, params, closeup; the runner builds each district's DistrictContext and SeamContract once its partition exists (after S6 from HoodRecipe; after V1-3.10.3 step 2 from the hand-over) and returns districts in partition order; two callers at generation, V1-3.10.3 (6) names those after it.

Standalone S0 resolves the recipe on blueprint.features (appended after S0's existing draws, §6.1) in order: kind when absent from hood.kinds over DistrictKind only: central 0.25, craft 0.25, market 0.15, temple 0.15, riverbank 0.05 (river edge only), docks 0.05 (sea or canal edge only), gate 0.05 (wall edge only), shanty 0.05 (only intent.wealth <= 0.2), non-admitted rows drop and renormalise; wealth is the slider's never a kind (T1 great houses card = any kind at wealth 0.9 planned 0.5; slum card shanty at wealth 0.1); title identity stays item 72's derived one.

Standalone S0 size: size chip sets buildings to about 85, 700 or 1 050 (NG C8 bands); else buildings; else areaHa; else uniform in the kind row's areaHa band (defaults 6-20 ha; shanty 4-12); a buildings target sets areaHa = buildings x plotArea(band) / 0.62 / 10 000 (0.62 = §4.2 S2's dense-core plot share). Fabric when auto by V1-3.3.5. Outline: drawn polygon or named template as given; auto by fabric (NG B1; J-V1.42): bent-cut star, ring star_round, street street_strip (main-street course S0 draws first and S8 lays as main spine), square plaza_frame, context row by kind row outline weights (default star 0.6, disc 0.15, lozenge 0.1, d_shape 0.1, spindle 0.05; crescent only by request); scaled to area. Tags: leafy greenery 0.9 and court greening x 1.5; secular no landmark anchors, manorBlockShare 0.

Standalone S1: frame = outline box + 30 % a side [hood.frameMargin]; flat terrain at datum 0 unless edges.slope: plane tilted at pct along bearing plus S0 rolling fBm (§4.2 S1 (1)); relief class hilly when pct >= 100 x terrace.slopeMin else rolling. Terraces with no slope (T1 Terraces card or fabric stepped) sets edges.slope to hood.hillsidePct (20 %) falling toward the outward normal of the outline's longest side (auto outline: the side S0 drew), named in one line; card never bent to organic for want of slope (J-V1.71). edges.water: boundary run whose outward normal lies within ± 60° [hood.edgeDeg] of bearing becomes a shore (sea/canal: L0 water face fills frame beyond, §4.2 S1 (2) routine; river: channel of the river row's width at context rung along the run, far bank inside frame).

Standalone S2: virtual host town = S2's roster for a town of contextRung's target population with the recipe's intent (demand per class x band only, never materialised). One-district allocation (computed by S7b in step 6 once field pass 1 gives capacity per band): L_hood = outline built land (area x 0.62), L_town = virtual town plot land; each dispersed class takes round(demand_c x L_hood / L_town x affinity[family(c)] / Σ̄) (Σ̄ normalises affinities over dispersed demand); households fill residential capacity by band from field pass 1 shares; singular and district-defining classes enter only through the kind row's anchors (none religious when secular); hood population = household members (reported; title subtitle).

Standalone S3-lite: outline from §4.2 S1 (2) closed-outline routine scaled (drawn polygon as given) as the arena's L1 border chain (border role), seams type frame, hard; edges.wall makes the run facing that bearing an open Enceinte chain (kind inner) whose strips S7 cuts (§4.8), typing it wall. An outline below 4 x eLo² is scaled up about its centroid to that area with a one-line bend, never refused (item 101 R2).

Standalone S6: one district = outline face; kind from S0; field pass 1 with characterOffset = intent.wealth - 0.5 plus kind offset, kernels of what exists, ε; FieldBands cuts are the band set's default cuts: one cut per band boundary at cumulative default household shares c_i mapped c -> 0.1 + 0.75c onto [0.1, 0.85]; the six-band default set keeps its authored row 0.12, 0.25, 0.45, 0.62, 0.80 (ours; J-V1.9).

Standalone step 6: S7 only with a wall edge; S7b one-district allocation persisted as the district's Allocation (less the void part), claims (anchors larger than a block, green quota) cut by claimSubFace, S7c inside it with template land; then S7b (6) and (7) with V04's forecast (V04 §3.3; V04 BCR-19) at contextRung after the one-district allocation, P7's cap reading the one-district allocation's poorest-band households (J-V1.92); with Features.sewers false and undercity forbid only (6)(d)'s void-dwelling part allocates: P7 voidDwellingHouseholds of the poorest band capped at forecastSafety x forecast, taken from the allocation into the underground pseudo-district's Allocation, placed below by V04 T3 F6; population unchanged; freed surface capacity typed by S10b's reconcile as yards, greens or vacant plots; F6 misses go to T8 (V04 §3.7a), reported. Then S8 (axis anchors or street course), S9, S10a (i), S9b, S10a (ii)-(iii), S10 (0) margin band along the whole border (no plot fronts the outline), S10-S12b, S12c, S13a (district name = hood name, title label), S14.

Standalone layers and history (J-V1.36; J-V1.77): Recipe.product hood fixes layers through the inputs V04 and V05 read, which the hood's S0 writes (only V04 §3.1's hood line also reads Recipe.product): islands off (S0 resolves recipe.layers.islands to off, any other value resolved and reported; V05 §3.2 (1) gate fails, S7b (5) no allocation); sewers off (Features.sewers false: U-NET commits nothing, P1-P4 nothing, U-FRONT only F6 over the void part); undercity never (circumstance slice undercity forbid: P6 none, U-CITY never runs); rest of tail and the one catacomb are V04 §3.1's hood line (J-V4.105, T-V4-75), cited; decision here: no quarries, generated vaults or buried town; epochs not offered for a hood in V06's first build; raised ways none generated (no route solver, no water balance), a declared one honoured. T1's hood card shows no layer toggles. A standalone document is an ordinary document for every edit, export, undo, close-up.

Standalone outline rows (BCR-13; ref:NG 1.2.2 hood outline code; code-neighbourhood.md §2.1), each on blueprint.features, scaled to area: star n = 4 + floor(8(1 - bell4)) vertices (4-12, mostly 9-12), vertex i at angle 2π(i + m3)/n radius 0.35 + 0.65 x m3 (0.35 floor ours, hood.starRadiusFloor), one corner-cutting pass, rotated min-area box axis-aligned, stretched to aspect 0.4 + 0.6u, turned ± 45° (+ at 0.3), fBm detail none, F-OUTLINE clamp and repair apply; star_round as star with radius 0.5 + 0.5 x m3, aspect 1 - 0.6 x bell4, a random subset of 3..n-1 corners kept sharp.

street_strip: main-street course first at bearing ± 45° (+ at 0.3) plus a centred bell up to ± 45°, from -L/2 to +L/2 through a middle control point within L/2 of centre, resampled into 3 + floor(5u) segments jittered sideways up to half a segment, with probability (n-1)/n smoothed by 4 - floor(n/2) passes; strip of width L x (0.3 + 0.5 x bell4) round it, vertices jittered, two end vertices each side pulled toward course ends by an m3 share; L solved so strip area is the target. plaza_frame: plaza (coin drawn here) at centre; at 0.3 a jittered rectangle three to four plaza sides wide plus one eHi offset from the plaza; else a star of 4-6 vertices (rectangular plaza) or 4-7 (round) at plaza radius x (2 + u) (round (4 + u)) + eHi, one corner-cutting pass.

Sky island unit run (J-V1.49) inputs skyHandover(doc, island) (V05 §2.3: land face, rim strip, claims (institution's and landings'), landings with attach vertices, river, sky Allocation, field, context districtKind, districtHa, fabricHint, fabricPrior); this runner is the hand-over's one caller; on the generation worker after the ground's S10 (0), beside the hinterland unit, each island in slot order: (1) no S1 (SKY wrote L0 land, water, terrain, V05 §3.8); (2) unit outline = land face less rim strip, claims are holes; district partition k = skyDistrictCount = clamp(ceil(allocated plot land / (sky.plotShare x districtHa)), 1, 3) (districtHa V05's; J-V5.45); for k > 1 §4.6's bent cut with stop test 'stop when the arena holds k faces, cutting the largest first', cuts are secondary ways (soft way seams); each district's kind = context.districtKind (sky-island, or the institution row's on the face receiving its claim).

Sky unit run (3) field = SkyHandover.field (raster, mean, density, greenery), never recomputed from h(S_carried); town's FieldBands cuts apply. (4) S7b split: island allocation divided among districts in proportion to capacity less each one's template land, institution claim cut in its face; S7c per district, each row's weight x fabricPrior when the row is fabricHint else x 1 (a prior, never forced); S8 with each landing attach a gate-ranked portal (+2) and each laid crossing-site deck end a bridge portal (+1), each must be reached by a seed or lane (unreached = F-TEMPLATE validation failure, last rung lays a lane); S9, S10a (i), S9b, S10a (ii)-(iii), S10 (0) (margin band only on land-face runs without a rim strip; the rim strip never cut or plotted), S10-S12b in the island overlay.

Island crossing sites (J-V1.91): a site qualifies when both deck_end vertices lie on the boundary of the unit outline face (both banks border built land, neither a claim nor the rim strip). After S7c and before seeds, one L1 batch lays for each qualifying site in Bridge address order its span: own L1 edge between deck ends with structural deck role beside way, secondary at 0.9 x top of secondary width band (mean of w_tpl's range; no draw); this batch is the way that uses the site (no S4/S5 on an island). Each deck end is a template portal kind bridge of the district whose face it bounds (shared vertex: smaller address), ranked secondary bridge (3 + 1), read by portal:bridge and portal:best, must be reached (F-TEMPLATE last rung lays a lane).

After S8 and before S9 one L1 batch removes the span of every site with an unreached deck end (site stays a site, reported in requestedVsBuilt 'the river crossing at {site} left unbridged: no street reaches its far bank'; a street reaching the other end stays, ending at the bank) and builds every other span by §4.8's bridge rule: deckCm from two bank elevations by §2.6's datum step (sampler levelledGroundCm on the island's key, BCR-V5-30: island raster since S10 has levelled no plot; dispatch and raster fallback built in W8, f item 309 M5 part) plus clearance row, kind and piers as S7 sets on the ground, so S10's deck-plot rule and S11's DeckContext (V02 §3.16 (1),(5); X28) read a built deck (BCR-45); furniture laid by §4.8 in the unit's closing L1 batch (no S7). Deck plots (none on a ford) belong to the district V1-3.17.6 (1) names (on an island Bridge.deck[0]'s); S7b split counts expected deck capacity (BCR-4 (b)); capacity for a removed span or a ford is surplus typed by S10b's reconcile. Non-qualifying sites stay unlaid sites. Landfall fates are V05's (§3.16 (7), §3.22 (6)).

Cross-arena pulls: the island's S10b reads a class on another arena by BCR-V5-16's route distance (skyRoute, V05 §3.20 (1)); at generation reads a ground provider at the block its S10a allocation holds (V05 §3.20 (1),(12)(a)), never the pool's placed plots (placements pool-independent); after generation reads both arenas' placed plots.

Rim walk (J-V1.81, J-V1.90): plantRimWalk(doc, island) (@plat/hood) is pure over the committed rim strip (rim_strip face, inner setback line) and §4.9's street-tree row, draws nothing (trees instanced at render at row spacing, §8.10); writes one esplanade Greenery on the strip face and one street_trees Greenery along the inner setback line (along names the strip with no way, BCR-10 (c); a tree every 10-14 m); lays no way; pair keyed by island derivation unit and strip; the pair found is retired by §6.3 carry-over in the same batch (succeeded within hysteresis radius else tombstoned), so exactly one pair after every call; unchanged strip rewrites nothing (J-DET-2). Callers: unit run once after its districts' S12b before S12c (generation and every (6)(a) run); every strip re-lay event (V05 §4.2 resize, rim reshape) once in its commit after V05's island L1 batch and any district re-derivation. A district's S12b never plants the rim strip. Households the unit cannot house go to V05's F-SKY-UNIT.

Sky unit run (5): the town's S12c and S13a include the island's districts (names unique town-wide §9.6); run returns district ids in partition order, SKY-F writes SkyIsland.districts (V05 §3.12), SeamReport with portalsTotal 0 and landingsReached.

(6)(a) After generation (J-V1.90): no scoped mode (every run partitions the whole island); callers V05 raiseIsland (at an epoch by its sky.islands participant, V05 §3.15 (5); after generation by convert raiseIsland incl. T5 sky declaration, V05 §4.2) and New random on an island (regenerate island scope newRandom) run steps 1-5 inside the calling commit on the island overlay where V05's sequence calls the hand-over, cross-arena pulls reading both arenas' placed plots; draws carry the calling commit's key components (epoch's; island's advanced reroll) so replay reproduces; Re-derive from SKY, S7b or earlier runs the unit run at generation's slot; each run belongs to its calling commit, undo restores the island's districts whole.

(6)(b) Carry-over: a run over an island with content re-derives it as a replace close-up does (§6.3 carry-over; locked, pinned, assigned, declared, dossier-backed and V1-3.5.12 fixed inputs kept as holes; one the re-drawn outline no longer covers carried or orphaned and listed among fates, never silently dropped; successions in SeamReport.superseded); districts keep derivation unit (island, S6, partition face order), so an identical partition keeps lineages; a newly raised island only mints.
