Segment count after collinear merging before M7 (single, towerHouse, pass-throughs 1; T 2; H 3; cross 2; closed ring its edge count) written by M13 to MassingRef.segments. M6 merged into M5.

M7 blocks (rectilinear families and a plotRing's gate range): k drawn in blocks (creation index 2); candidates with weights: midpoint of a range >= 3w long (1, or 2 on main or gate), free end of a range (1), outer corner of a butt joint (1.5 closed, 1 otherwise); drawn by weight without replacement; per block lb = w x U(1, 1.6) along host, db = w x U(1, 1.4) across (proud by (db - w)/2 each side); accept when inside H, 1 m from every accepted block and tower, each remaining host piece >= max(w/2, 2 m) (shorter absorbed into the block); accepted splits its host into up to two pieces with the host's role and new keys (rect pieces of a rect host; quad pieces of a quad host keeping the mitred end and ending square on the block); block a rect wing role block aligned with its host's eave; at a corner replaces the corner square; pieces and block tile the union (pairing §2.6 rule 4 (ii)); piece-end vertices on the block's side recorded in its corners (§2.6 rule 1); block roof always hip (item 59 ADOPTED; J-V2.3), ridge along the longer of lb, db, ends inset by WingRoleRow.hipInset x span.

M8 towers (collision set holds the wings, item 59): k drawn in towers (creation index 3), shape by towerShape; candidates: (a) every convex corner of the union where two ranges meet and each free corner of a range (weight 2 on rectCourt, plotRing, U, fantasy closed; 1 otherwise); (b) midpoint of each free end (1); (c) midpoint of the gate or main range's street side only with chance gateTower; (d) tower on a block (centroid of each accepted block, weight towerOnBlock, 0 default, square); radius r = w x towerRadiusW drawn; (a)-(c) centre outward by 0.35r along the corner bisector or side normal; ring side count by TowerShapeRow radius bracket (round 12 below 2 m, 16 below 4 m, 24 above; square 4 aligned with host; octagon 8 one side parallel), dmath vertices snapped. Accepted only if (i) inside H; (ii) area share inside the wings' union in [0.2, 0.6]; (iii) centre inside no wing deeper than 0.35r from its boundary; (iv) 0.5 m from every other tower and block; (v) seed contract (§2.6): every tower vertex >= attractCm from every wing side it does not cross and vice versa, else centre moves once by 2 x attractCm outward and re-tested.

M8 (d) acceptance: a square of side min(lb, db) x U(0.5, 0.8) centred on the block, inside the block ring inset by towerOnBlockInsetM (0.3 m), 0.5 m from other towers; contained in its block (clip order after its container, §2.6 containment rule), its room inside the block's piece; M11 raises it until its eave stands above the block's ridge. Candidates tried in drawn order until k accepted or none remain (fewer accepted reported, never retried). Stair turret: chance turret, one turret radius U(1.2, 1.8) m at a re-entrant corner (inner corner of L, T, H, U, cross), same tests with share band [0.25, 0.75]; role turret.

M8 (e) template towers (church, cathedral, cloister rows and any template row with westTowers[1] > 0 or crossingTower > 0): west end = free end of the template's nave part (nave or the longest part) whose ridge end lies farthest toward world west (-x); west tower count = the attached tower/towers structure's drawn count (M8b) raised to the row's westTowers[0] (a cathedral always has two), else a draw in westTowers; one west tower a square of side w_n x U(0.45, 0.6) centred on the west end's midpoint standing out 0.35 x side; two at the west end's corners each standing out diagonally 0.35 x side; crossing tower (chance crossingTower, where the template has part crossing, BCR-V3-13 names) a square of the crossing's shorter side less 2 x towerOnBlockInsetM, contained in the crossing part; template towers pass tests (i), (iv), (v) (west towers also (ii)); a failing one moves inward by attractCm steps at most 4, then dropped and reported. Towers and turrets are polygon wings (square tower a 4-vertex aligned polygon), first in the canonical wing order (J-V2.4).

M8b attached structures (BCR-V2-29), each template structure whose roleKeys row says attach main arrives in BuildingInput.attached with S11's drawn count: wheel (watermill wheel housing): rect wing role service, one storey, width U(2, 3) m, length along the water side min(main range's water-side length - 1 m, 6 m), centred, reaching from the main range's water-side wall to H's boundary on the water side (at most wheelReachM 4 m), roof shed high against the mill house; needs the water axis frame, without a water edge laid on the rear side and reported. sails (windmill): no wing, main family forced to towerHouse with no range (windmill override sets shape weights), sails a §8.10 decoration. westTower: the count M8 (e) reads. churchPorch: rect wing role service, one storey, width U(3, 4.5) m, depth U(3, 5) m, on the main entrance's side of the nave centred on the door, inside H; where laid, the entrance hint names its outer side and the composer lays no porch there.

M8b absorbed (a court institution's ranges): no geometry; the count raises the main family's least range count; M10's budget for the main slot takes the absorbed shares. On an ovalCourt (an arena's gates; J-V2.88) an absorbed structure raises no range count: its budget share joins the main slot's; the drawn gate count g (2-4, V11 §3.6.1) sets the passages: the first two are M5's major-axis gate passages; a third turns the seating wing of the minor-axis chord (n/4 - 1, n/4) or (3n/4 - 1, 3n/4) (centred on the minor axis, n a multiple of 4) nearer the access into a one-floor gate passage, façade keeping its role; a fourth the other; massOval reads g from BuildingInput.attached (2 where absent) so the M3a builder lays the same bytes. An attached wing passes M13's checks like any wing; a failing one is dropped and reported, the building kept.

M9 back range: with chance backRange (creation index 4), host = main range (a row: the front quad); rear side = host ring side whose outward normal has the largest +v component, independent of the ridge (J-V2.40): a row quad side 4 (rear chain) on gable- or eaves-fronted rows, a detached host the side farthest from the access; attaching run = that side's longest straight run (chain: longest sub-run with direction varying <= 5°); width wb = clamp(backWidthM, 3 m, run - 0.6 m); length lb = clamp(backLenM, 2 m, reach - 1 m), reach = free depth of the back region behind the run (row: V2 §3.4 step 5's back region; else H); a row's stands flush against one party wall (a coin), a detached house's flush against the side nearer the larger side yard; rect wing role back abutting (butt) the host's rear side, vertices inserted into the host ring; floors host's less one (>= 1); roof shed (high against host) when wb <= 3.5 m else gable along its length.

M10 size budget (J-V2.35): A = union area (sum of tiled wings less towers' overlaps, measured exactly by the kernel boolean only when towers exist); target band [lo, hi] = [p10, p90] x footprintShare_i / count_i x buildingScale x sizeFactor ([p10, p90] = template footprintM2 at the significance-shifted value; where p10 = p50 = p90, [sizeBandLo x p50, sizeBandHi x p50] with sizeBandLo/Hi = 0.7 and 1.45 fixed (V11 §3.6.1 derivation ratios; SCC-R0C-3); footprintShare_i the structure's share (V11 role table; absent: main slot 0.6 when other structures are drawn else 1, other slots equal parts of the rest) plus absorbed shares; count_i the drawn count; sizeFactor the SIZE ladder step's (item 108) else 1). Claim-sized (J-V2.87): where the row carries claimShare or the template's footprintM2 is 'the claim's' (V11 §3.6.1 cathedral, cloister, castle families, precinct institutions), [lo, hi] = claimShare x area(H) x sizeFactor (row's claimShare else constants claimLo, claimHi 0.35, 0.6); on a deck plot the deck row's band; narrowed by drift areaPct; cap = coverageMax x area(H); the whole band is slotBand (@plat/plots) read by M3, ST0, ST8, M10.

M10 ladder: (1) if A > 1.1 x min(hi, cap): every M5 path length scaled by sqrt(min(hi, cap)/A) with M5's clamp lower bounds lowered to the family's M3 least, M5-M9 re-run once with the same draws; (2) still over: drop blocks, then towers; (3) still over: reverse lattice rectCourt, plotRing, regularCourt, starCourt -> U -> L -> single; H -> T -> single; cross -> T -> single; gridWalk, chordArc -> L -> single; towerHouse -> the tower alone; stepped -> single (ST8); ovalCourt -> rectCourt -> U -> L -> single, re-running M5-M9 at each step on massing/attempt=a continuing M14's counter; (4) end of lattice still over: accept and report overBudget by class. If A < 0.9 x lo: path lengths scale up by min(sqrt(lo/A), largest factor keeping the massing in Rr) once; still under: accept and report (underSize and JOIN are the mutator's, never the massing's).

M11 heights: main floors fm = template floors interpolated along the value, rounded stochastically (creation index 5: floor(x + u)), clamped into template and drift ranges; each wing floors = fm + a draw in WingRoleRow.storeyDelta (block blockStoreyDelta; tower/turret towerStoreyDelta above the tallest wing it overlaps), >= 1; all ranges of one closed or oblique path share fm. Tower storeys: a tower of a family whose HeightsRow carries towerStoreys (church, chapel, cathedral, cloister, tower, castle; V11 §3.6.4) takes floors uniformly in that range (creation index 5 after fm), each of towerStoreyCm (BCR-V2-26; else storeyCm.upper). Heights from V11's HeightsRow keyed by template family (J-V2.33): eaveCm = storeyCm.ground + (floors - 1) x storeyCm.upper (+ parapetCm on flat); ridgeCm: gable and hip eave + pitch x span/2 (quad: mean of end sides), shed eave + pitch x span at high, pyramid and cone eave + towerPitch x r, tent eave + pitch x r, flat eave.

One pitch rule (J-V2.33): range pitch = HeightsRow.roofPitch x (ClimateRow.roof.pitch / pitchRef) clamped [0.3, 1.8], ClimateRow the site's (§4.9, V11 §2.8), pitchRef the temperate-deciduous row's roof.pitch; towers TowerShapeRow.pitch; spires as M12; never a material's (item 19). A tower's or turret's floors raised further until its eave >= the highest wing roof point inside its ring (tower on a block above its ridge; occlusion rule V2 §5.2). A wing spanning a passage keeps the base's two-floor minimum (§2.5 Passage). An arcade wing keeps its storeys, ground storey open (dashed, exported open, outside capacity's ground storey). Under a vault (underground layer, V04 chamber ceiling incl. an arch vault's soffit under a raised way, X29): floors clamped so the eave stays >= vaultClampCm (30 cm) below it, reported vaultClamp. ovalCourt: façade ring shares fm; each seating wing solid (floors 0) with eaveCm = storeyCm.ground and ridgeCm = the façade's eaveCm; gate passage wing floors 1, same eave and ridge. baseCm = base deriveBase called by S11 after the massing (crypt lift raises ground wings over the basement's ring; stacked building: rebaseStack, BCR-V2-32). Building Heights: towerCm highest tower or turret ridge above baseCm (absent without one); eaveCm, ridgeCm maxima over other wings; stacked building: the envelope of V2 §3.15.2 incl. floors.

M12 roofs: range roles hip with chance hipShare else gable (one draw per closed or oblique path, one per wing otherwise; creation index 6); where ClimateRow.roof.form is flat (arid town) every range, block and back range takes flat with the family's parapetCm and no dormers; block always hip; towers cone (round) or pyramid (square, octagon), or with chance towerFlat (square, octagonal) flat with parapetCm (battlemented); spires: a tower of a family whose HeightsRow carries spireFactor takes a cone or pyramid spire of rise spireFactor x (eaveCm - baseCm), stored as the RoofSpec.pitch giving that rise over its radius; back as M9; shelter as M0; @underground forces flat. Cupola (creation index 7): with its chance a kind by weights on the main range (the longest main or gate range) written to MassingRef.cupola (derived solid at the ridge midpoint, never in Heights, never a caster). ovalCourt: façade flat with parapetCm, no draw; seating and gate-passage wings shed with high the side on P1 (outward), pitch = rise over span from M11. Ridge axis: along the path segment for a range; along the host for a block unless db > lb; a row quad ridgeAxis 1 (gable to street) with probability smoothstep((gableToStreetMaxFrontM + 1.5 - frontage) / 3) (own; share calibrated to NG's measured 36 % under parity, V2 §7.4).

M13 snap and validate: every point snaps by §3.2's placement rule; a ring edge shorter than minEdge (25 cm) merges its end into its start; every wing vertex within the hot pixel of another wing's side inserted into it (§2.6 rule 1). Checks (exact on lattice points): every ring simple and counter-clockwise; every wing inside H; non-tower wings tile (pairing §2.6 rule 4 (ii); stepped: ground wings only, wings with on by ST6's containment); M8 (v) for towers; each wing >= 4 m² and each side >= minEdge; the laid range count before M7 lies in MassingFamilyRow.wings and every joint of its joints kind (J-V2.57; every family has its row incl. stepped and ovalCourt); ovalCourt: P0, P1, P2 simple and CCW, every edge >= minEdge, P2's least width >= courtMinM. Order and keys: towers and turrets (acceptance order), ranges in path order (gate else main first), blocks, back range, M8b attached; keys 0..n-1, nextWingKey = n (canonical order by construction); segments written. Entrance hint: the gate wing else main (church porch's outer side where laid), its eave side with the largest positive -v component (forecourt U: back range's; towerHouse without range: the square tower's front side), kept only if >= entranceHintMinCos (cos 60°) else null. A failing check is an M14 attempt.

M14 ladder (F-MASSING; per building, never whole-map): rung 0 attempts 0, 1, 2 of the drawn family (concern cap 3), attempt a on massing/attempt=a; rung 1 each other feasible family by descending weight, one attempt each, continuing the attempt counter; rung 2 single with w = max(0.8 x wingWidthM[0], 3 m); rung 3 baseOutline (base rectangle in H, guaranteed by §2.6 with F-SITEPLAN above it); every rung past 0 counted per class in the generation report; no building refused; no retry beyond the building.

compose(input, outline, 'wings', k) is a pure function of the wings rung's recorded inputs (wingsInputs: base wings, main entrance, massing reference, row slices, the porch's neighbourhood on the plot) and its own streams: (1) one Wing {base} per non-tower base wing in key order, one ComposedTower {base} per tower or turret wing; ring, heights, roof, spans read from the base wing, so the stage-3 contract (BCR-V2-22: union of composed wings and towers equals the outline's union; each composed wing reaches exactly its base wing's storeys) holds by construction; (2) courts = footprint face holes in ring order; (3) dormer rows on compose.dormers; (4) porch and secondary porch on compose.porch; (5) validation (F-COMPOSE, BCR-V2-16): each dormer inside its facet clear of every valley, hip, tower, block (roofscape regions); each porch inside the plot clear of other buildings, of the building's own other wings (stack's stair 0, an attached porch wing) and of every way; failures take V2 §3.13's ladder; nothing the composer makes is model data until an edit stores it.

facadeBays (the one rhythm every reader shares; every side, J-V2.93): on an eave side usable run = side length less endMarginM (1.2 m; constants row, only home) at each end, less the projection of every tower ring, block and other wing meeting it widened by 0.6 m, less the reach of each valley ending on the side computed in integer cm by §6.5: for wing X whose ridge meets wing Y's roof e = floor((X.ridgeCm - Y.eaveCm) x Y.halfSpanCm / Y.riseCm) (never from the float roofscape, J-V2.25; byte-identical on every host, T-V2-13); run cut into nb = max(1, floor(run / bayM)) equal bays (bayM 3.6 m own), each {atCm centre from the side's first vertex, widthCm}. Other sides of rect or quad wings (gable end, free part along a butt joint): same less the valley term; a non-positive run has no bay. Polygon wings (tower, turret): bays round the ring's free perimeter (boundary less parts inside or within 0.6 m of another wing's ring), each maximal free arc cut into max(1, floor(arc / bayM)) bays by arc length (arc < bayM/2 none); facadeBays returns bays whose centres lie on that side. Pure, no draw; read by dormer positions (eaves), V03 W2 windows on every side, §8.4 lit windows when no plan, §8.10 decorative chimneys (eave sides; bay line nearest each end, hearths of them).

Decorative chimneys on exposed roof only: at a bay line of a host wing's eave, up-slope by half the span; host a storeyed wing whose roof there is exposed (never solid; never inside the ring of a wing standing on the host); on a stacked building hearths placed on the top storeyed wing first (bay lines nearest each end, alternating), then the exposed terrace band of the storeyed wing below (bay lines whose chimney point lies outside every wing on it), and so down the stack; a count left with no exposed bay line dropped and reported (hearthsDropped).

Dormer rows: a wing takes dormers only if its role allows (WingRoleRow.dormers: main, range, cross, gate, block), its roof is gable or hip (never under flat climate roofs) with pitch >= DormerKindRow.minPitch (0.7), and HeightsRow.attic is true (BCR-V2-26) or it has >= 2 floors. Per eave side (creation index 2 x key + eave on compose.dormers; nb and run from facadeBays): (1) n = clamp(round(perTenM x run/10 x U(0.75, 1.25)), 0, nb); (2) entrance gable on the main entrance's eave side with chance dormer.entranceGable: one entranceGable dormer width U(2.4, 3.6) m clamped to its bay, in the bay containing the main entrance (counts in n); (3) kinds by dormer.kinds; a warehouse family puts exactly one hoist dormer on each eave facing an access edge (outward normal component toward the access >= entranceHintMinCos), in the bay nearest that eave's centre; (4) width U(widthM) clamped to bay width - gapM (0.4 m); (5) positions dormerPositions (no draw): n bays symmetric about the run's centre (n = nb all; otherwise centre bay first when nb odd, then outward in pairs; odd remainder on even nb to the main-entrance side, else first side in ring order); a dormer whose plan rectangle (width x depthShare x span/2 up the slope, set back 0.3 m for dormer, at the eave for wallGable, entranceGable, hoist) meets a valley region, tower ring, cupola or other dormer is dropped (count falls, reported).

Precedence against the plan: before a plan exists the rows are the dormers; once the plan rung has derived a plan an unedited DormerRow's count is the plan's count of top-storey roofed rooms with exterior demand under that eave (V03 W4) clamped to nb, kind and widthCm kept, positions by dormerPositions; an edited row stays a fixed input the plan honours; the drawing never shows a dormer the plan contradicts, a user's dormer edit always wins. Dormers never project past the eave line (J-V2.7): FM's projecting cross-gables would leave footprint and plot; the real projecting bay is a block (M7).

Porch: only on the wing carrying the main entrance where WingRoleRow.porch admits (main, gate, range, cross, block; not tower, turret, back, service: a towerHouse entered through its tower or a church through its porch wing takes none); side and offset the main entrance's (base rule 3, re-read after every carry); d = free distance from the door point along the side's outward normal to the first of the plot's boundary, another footprint of the plot, or a footpath or forecourt yard part edge reaching a way (measured on the plot's own rings). Feasible: recessed where host depth >= 3 m + depthM[0]; hood where d >= depthM[0] + clearanceM (0.3 m); gabled, halfRound, twoStorey where d >= depthM[0] + clearanceM, side >= widthM[0] + 0.6 m, twoStorey needs >= 2 floors. One draw (creation index 0 on compose.porch) over porch weights restricted to feasible and none; width U(widthM) clamped to the side's free part (no other wing abuts; BCR-V2-38) less 0.6 m; depth U(depthM) clamped to d - clearanceM (outside) or host depth less 3 m (recessed); halfRound depth = width/2 with width/2 <= d - clearanceM; a flush row front (d = 0) takes recessed or none. Porch ring derived (rectangle on the side at the offset, outward or inward; halfRound half-disc radius width/2 centred on the door on the side's outer line, dmath arc with TowerShapeRow's round bracket side count halved, >= 6 segments); heights one storey (storeyCm.ground) and rise pitch x width/2 (twoStorey two storeys; halfRound half-cone at TowerShapeRow round pitch); drawn and lit where compositions are drawn; adds nothing to model heights.

Secondary porch (J-V2.44): with chance secondaryPorch (creation index 1 on compose.porch) one hood at the side, rear or yard entrance (§2.6 Entrance.role) with the largest d among those where a hood is feasible, ties by entrance ordinal; size by PorchKindRow.hood; 0 in default rows (one porch at the main door), calibrated under FM (up to three porches per building).

rooms rung derived only as the plan rung's input (compose(..., rooms) after wings on the plan-deriving click), never alone under view (J-V2.9); each room a Room (§2.6) with storey, composed wing's base key (a tower's room its tower wing's key) and a role V03's programme rows name (these four roles must exist there); all rooms inside one seed piece at their storey (stage-3 contract): each avoids every tower ring (shortened away else omitted) and keeps attractCm from every side it does not share. The rung reads the occupants (item 28 (f); J-V2.36): rooms cells at the occupants' band; recorded inputs include the occupants' band row and household count (BCR-V2-13): a band change or re-division marks it stale; hall and chapel emitted only where the interior-ladder row at the occupants' band gives unit form house (one household) or the class is an institution whose programme names a hall (inn common room, guild or town hall, market hall upper hall, barracks mess); a rich manor fallen to the poor band has no hall ring (T-V2-35), returning restores the as-built rooms exactly; gate hall and tower rooms stay at every band.

Hall: in the main wing (closed family: range opposite the gate) eave to eave, length U(hallLenShare) x the wing's ridge length clamped to [1.4w, length - 2 m] then to the programme's area (class programme hall row [min, max] x interior-ladder sizeFactor at the occupants' band, by shortening its length never its width) where the class's RoomProgramRow hall rule is loaded (V03's rows from M6-P's P1); before those rows land (M6b) clamped by [1.4w, length - 2 m] alone and reported per building (hallUnclamped; J-V2.95); low end = the door it is entered by: the main entrance on the main wing at door offset - hallDoorBackM (1.5 m; cross-passage bay) clamped inside the wing; else a court door on the main range's court side at the offset nearest the gate hall's axis (derived opening the plan rung opens); runs toward the range's farther end; ground storey; role hall.

Gate hall (closed families): in the gate wing eave to eave, width U(gateHallM) centred on the main entrance's offset, shifted to keep gateHallJointGapM (0.5 m) from a joint; ground storey; role gatehall; the plan rung opens an arch at both ends (street and court). ovalCourt: laid in the main gate's façade wing and continuing through its gate-passage seating wing to the floor (two gatehall rooms sharing an arch on P1); the opposite major-axis passage wing holds a second gatehall room (outer end a door into the façade's main wing, or an arch where an access edge faces it); each minor-axis seating wing turned into a gate passage holds a gatehall room with an arch through its façade wing; façade ring's plan is V03's (V3C-78). Chapel (chance rooms.chapel under the hall rule): open family at the free end of the range whose ridge is nearest world east (+x); closed ring at the east end of the range whose ridge is nearest east, from its joint; eave to eave, length w x U(1, 1.5), ground storey (first storey where the ground storey there is the hall); role chapel. Tower rooms: per composed tower one room per storey (ring less earlier overlapping towers in clip order; on a block inside the block's piece); role towerRoom.

Room ids are the base's room:<building>/<level>/<i>, i in order hall, gate hall, chapel, then tower rooms by tower key; the plan rung passes them as fixed rings (§3.4 transient arena) and places stair cores against their walls; every room editable by setComposition room (on or off, extent along the host's ridge, bent to the nearest lawful extent by V2 §3.13 (3)); an edited room is a fixed input of the rung (edited), kept while its host keeps its key.

Mutation wing step (item 18) in the base mutator (§4.7 S11: match by role, subtract -> convert -> adapt -> add, siteplan.mutate stream, MutationSteps, exact reversal): W1 target family = target designation's composition row at the manifested band; the source family stays if it has weight > 0 in the target row and is feasible on the current hint (S11 re-fit with other kept parts fixed); else one draw on siteplan.mutate over target families reachable from the source by MassingGrowthRow and the anchored-lay table and feasible (M3), weighted by the target row; stepped feasibility anchored: kept main range's shorter side >= tierMinSideM + 2 x insetM[0] and ST0's least stair reserve fitting in H in front of it (none for internal), else stepped leaves the set. W2 seeds: growth row keep all (every source range in the target path), main, mainAndOne (main and longest other, ties by key), none (only when the source's main has no compatible role in the target by §4.7's compatibility table; keep what it can as other slots or subtract, never re-roll the plot).

W3 anchored lay (J-V2.11): the target family's M5 construction in anchored mode with its frame fixed on the kept main range (u along its ridge, v away from its access-side eave, front that eave), parameters solved so kept ranges are exactly slabs of the target; added ranges that do not fit shrink, then are dropped (degrading to the largest feasible sub-family by the growth table), then the base's step 3 (JOIN by S10 (7) or the template's underSize) decides, never a fresh roll.

Anchored-lay table (source -> target; kept; construction): single -> L (main; kept range is the front slab Lf; arm at the coin's end with the sunlit choice, Ls drawn, abutting); single -> T (main; cross slab through the kept hall's end; hall adapted shortened by w_c); single -> H (main; cross slabs both ends, hall shortened by w_c each); single -> U (main; kept range is the through front range, arms Ls running +v); single -> cross (main; kept range runs through, cross slab through its middle Lc drawn as two pieces); single -> rectCourt (main; kept range is the gate range Lf, Ld drawn, rear and two sides added, rear takes main); single -> towerHouse (main; tower at the kept range's front corner nearer the larger side yard, square abutting, round/octagon overlapping 0.35 x t/2); single -> gridWalk (main; pitch p = kept length / k, k = max(1, round(kept length / p0)); kept range first segment, walk continues from its far end); single -> plotRing, regularCourt, starCourt, chordArc (main; reachable only when the kept length is within ± 15 % of the target's side at the current hint; target laid with that side on the kept range; else removed); L -> U (all; second arm at the front range's other end of the kept arm's length); L -> rectCourt (all; front is gate, kept arm one side, opposite side and rear close the court at the kept arm's length); L -> T, H (main; cross slab(s) through the front range's end(s), range shortened by w_c, kept arm subtracted); T -> H (all; second cross slab, hall shortened); U -> rectCourt (all; closing range across the arms' far ends).

Anchored-lay table (cont.): rectCourt -> U, U -> L, H -> T, L/T/cross -> single, any closed -> U or L (mainAndOne or main; ranges not kept subtracted highest keys first; a hall shortened by a subtracted cross-wing regains length where H allows); towerHouse -> single (main; tower subtracted; a towerHouse with no range keeps the tower as a part and lays single beside it); gridWalk -> L, single (first two segments or first kept, rest subtracted); any closed or fantasy -> another (main; anchor either; only within the ± 15 % side rule); baseOutline -> any (main; the base builder's bar is the kept range as single's rows); row -> row (all; quad kept, only back range and storeys change); template <-> any other: never reachable (a template building changes only by the compatibility table's keep, convert or subtract, §4.7); single -> stepped (the only source; main; kept range's four corners are tier 0 via layTiers anchored mode, stack, stairs, top laid with the target row's cells and drawTiers on siteplan.mutate; V2 §3.15.5); stepped -> single (main; tier 0 kept as main, every stacked wing and stair subtracted highest keys first, roof and floors by W5, a solid tier 0 becomes storeyed with solid cleared; onward by single's rows); stepped -> stepped (all; tiers up to the target's count kept, W4 subtracts above (shrine first), W6 adds tiers on top with the stack's step while ST3's side test passes, their stairs, the shrine where the target's top is one).

W3b arrangement change (item 108; J-V2.13 scoped): a row building whose target template's arrangement is compound (brewer's shopfront becoming a brewery's works-noxious yard) keeps its quad byte-identical as the compound's frontage slot (role shop-house or house by the target's structures) and the target's main structure is added as another slot by the base compound packer behind it (JOIN by S10 (7) where the budget asks); reverse (compound -> row) subtracts the added slots and restores the quad's role; J-V2.13's 'a row building never changes family' holds for every change keeping the row arrangement.

W4 subtract: source wings with no role in the target, towers or blocks above the target row's maximum (highest keys first), unless locked or edited (kept, reported). W5 adapt: kept wings' floors move into the target's band one storey per step; on a deck plot clamped to the deck's maxFloors as M11 clamps at generation; a roof kind the target's WingRoleRow disallows changes to its first allowed kind. W6 add: blocks, towers, turret, back range and attached structures to the target row's counts by M7-M9 and M8b on the new massing, draws on siteplan.mutate keyed as V2 §3.12; added wings take keys from nextWingKey; canonical order restored before commit. Digging down (item 109 (j)(3)(i); J-V2.39): an added wing whose ring newly lies over a sealed cavern, ruin chamber or gallery within reach of its dig floor draws once for an access down keyed (building lineage, dig, void system's kind, wing key) on the sewer concern in V04's T2b stage (draw and access kind V04's C4-52; chance V11 §3.23.7 DigRule by class and depth, SCC-22).

W7 record: each wing step a MutationStep part kind wing (address ('wing', building, key) and role), storey for a floors change, roof for a roof kind change, and one slot step role massing carrying MassingRef before and after (segments rewritten); kept wings keep keys and bytes (T-V2-15); subtracted keys never re-used. W8 composition: unstored wings rung marked stale, re-derives at next click (kept wings' dormer rows unchanged, draws keyed by wing key); a stored composition re-matched inside the event: composed wings of subtracted keys dropped (fates), kept keys kept (edited dormer row kept while eave within ± 10 %, else orphaned and listed in §7.3's orphan table with two actions), added keys composed on the spot on the committed massing. W9 reversal the base's (inverse steps restore exactly while the leaf digest is the record's result; else a forward mutation toward the former designation runs, reported). Re-rolls: regenerate rung wings advances #wings (dormer counts, kinds, porches re-draw; massing unchanged, T-V2-14); rung rooms advances #rooms (hall length, chapel); New random on the building's plot or block re-derives the massing (S11) with the plot's reroll (§6.1).

Concerns (next append-only u16 ids): massing (geometry concern, non-rerollable by salt, attempt cap 3, readers S11 and every operator re-deriving S11 on a plot; keyed by the building's entity key with S11's stage id; creation indices 0 family and width and sunlit coins' base draws, 1 family lengths, sides, walk, 2 blocks, 3 towers, turret, template towers, 4 back range and M8b attached wings, 5 floors then tower storeys, 6 roofs and towers' flat tops, 7 cupola, 8 stepped tiers' count, shape, step, top, stair width, grade, shrine (no aspect), 9 tiers' heights in tier order; ovalCourt width at 0, semi-axis factor, axis ratio, seating depth at 1); compose.dormers, compose.porch (geometry, non-rerollable, attempt cap 0, keyed with #wings folded (§6.1 rung rule); index 2 x key + eave per dormer row, 0 porch, 1 secondary porch); compose.rooms (keyed with #wings and #rooms folded; 0 hall, 1 gate hall, 2 chapel).

Draws in edits and mutations (stated once; J-V2.18): the designation mutator draws on siteplan.mutate: W1's family draw with creation index the causing event's seq and ordinal 0; W6's draws with index the event's seq and the new wing's key as ordinal; a setMassing family op draws exactly so (replayable); every other setMassing op and every setComposition op draws nothing (an omitted value takes the row's central value: range midpoint, heaviest weight; stochastically rounded count round-half-up of the central value); a W6 wing over a sealed void draws its access on V04's sewer key, never these streams; the bends draw nothing (deterministic), except a bend to a family op (tiers on a non-stepped building) draws as a family op; a stepped mutation's drawTiers takes its two streams on siteplan.mutate with the event's seq and ordinals nextWingKey (index-8 group) and nextWingKey + 1 (heights).

Arithmetic: massing and composer use + - x / and sqrt only (§6.5) and dmath's cos and sin for regular polygon vertices (regularCourt, towers, half-round porch, §1.7 dmath); every result snaps by the placement rule; metre draws converted to integer cm before construction; facadeBays' valley reaches integer; the roofscape is view data in float64 under the renderer's CPU reference (§6.5 (9)). Order: candidates enumerated in a fixed geometric order (union ring order from its lowest vertex, then ranges in path order) before any weighted draw; weighted draws use §14's Rng weighted-pick helper. Stability: same state gives same massing and composition on every host (T-V2-13); a New random of a finer rung never changes a coarser one (§6.1); the elaboration cache can be dropped any time (§2.9).

F-MASSING = V2 §3.5's M14 (rungs 0-3 per building, base rectangle last), M10's reverse-lattice steps on the same attempt counter; a failing template tower or attached wing dropped and reported, building kept; for stepped the ladder runs inside massStepped (TierFailure an attempt, then the single fallback, then the base rectangle). F-COMPOSE (per building at derivation, reported to the view report, counted by T-V2-18, never an error): (1) a failing dormer dropped; (2) a porch whose space fails takes the next feasible kind then none (secondary porch none); (3) a composer room the seed contract would refuse (outside its piece, or a vertex within attractCm of an unshared side) shortened once by 2 x attractCm away from the offender, then omitted (V03's A2 (11) places that role, S23-27); (4) any other stage-3 contract failure (a bug by construction) returns the identity composition (composed wings and towers one to one, no dormer, no porch, no room), which satisfies the contract, and files the building in the report; a porch meeting one of the building's own other wings takes (2)'s ladder narrowed first to the free part of its side.
File g's base mechanisms are the coherence pass's (prosperity driver, siting profile, supply web, wall closure, ladder table); V2 §3.14 designs only their building part, citing g's item for the rest.

Sunlight (item 102 (b)(d)(e)): (a) a building's shade casters are its base wings' prisms (ring from baseCm to eave; over its ring the roof's rise: gable or hip ridge prism, a tower's cone or spire only over its own ring); these are item 102's epoch casters (at an epoch §4.11 the previous epoch's buildings enter the daylight raster through them); no stage-3 wing is a generation-time caster (buildings never feed the term they are sited by); the composition (dormers, porches, cupola) never casts in the model; cross-volume: V06 §3.4 rasterises per wing, not one height per footprint. (b) The rich seek the sun at building scale: M5's sunlit choice (J-V2.38). (c) Over time: a wing added or raised at an epoch changes the next epoch's casters only; V06 owns the drift.

Custom institutions (item 104; V11 §3.13): compose as the class DR24 resolves (archetype, category, tags, library fields or fallback; V08, V11 §3.13.2) through the ordinary chain; (a) landmarkLevel and economicWeight act through significance; (b) the ruined landmark (ruined-landmark -> generic-other) massed by its class's row then takes the ruined existence at its site (roof none; §2.8 decline states; V2 §5.1); (c) subsumption (item 104 (h)(5); item 108 source subsumption): the subsuming kind's template takes each subsumed kind's structures as extra slots (names by roleKeys, shares added to the compound's budget), nothing merged into one wing; (d) custom supply chains place members, never shapes.

Split works-and-shop sites (item 105 (h); J-V2.54): one institution on two plots: the branchOf use's building composes by split.shop, the works building by split.works (V11 §2.3), each an ordinary building (composed, mutated, undone by W1-W9); a merge-back (clerk's or author's declaration, or V06's re-evaluation) is two designation mutations inside one event: the works plot toward the class's unsplit template family (shop structure added by W6 as a frontage slot) and the shop plot toward vacancy (base subtract steps), both in EditBase.mutations and reversed together (undo restores both byte for byte, T-V2-39).

Ladders (item 108; J-V2.55): COUNT, QUARTER, GUILD members are ordinary buildings of the lesser class (LadderStepRow.memberClass) each by its own chain; a GUILD's hall composes as the hall family; a SIZE building composes as the greater class's family with sizeFactor in M10's budget (and σ's rank in step 3) so 'city granaries' are one compound of several stores; an upgrade keeps the existing building as member #1 (row arrangement kept: W1-W9; row -> compound: W3b); a demotion keeps the member nearest its demand and reverses added slots; as-built bytes return (T-V2-40).

Dig floor (item 109 (j); V02 is its producer, read by V04's access draw): baseCm - Basement.floors x cellar.depthCm with a basement (raised crypt's floor for a raised one), else baseCm; baseCm includes a half basement's raise (half cellar's floor = datum less half the depth; BCR-V2-28); a building on a deck plot has no dig floor and never draws; a wing with on never draws; a quay on the bank (surfaceCm null) is ground and has one. Who digs: a building draws its access once when built (draw V04's C4-52; chance V11 §3.23.7 DigRule, SCC-22); a wing the mutator adds over a sealed void draws once for that wing (W6); a setMassing op draws nothing (a user declares addUndergroundAccess, item 66); a replacement building (new lineage) draws as new (J-V2.39).

cryptSeedWings(b) (stated once; J-V2.92): for a building with template part names (BaseWing.partName, BCR-V3-13) the wings named chancel, else apse, else crossing; else for a stepped building its tier 0 (tier wing with no on); else the one storeyed ground wing (no on, not solid) of role main, range or cross whose ridge has the end with the largest world x (farthest east), ties by lowest key; else none (empty list: V03 places the crypt under the third of the region farthest from the main entrance, V03 3.7.4 step 1); returns wing keys; exported by @plat/plots beside massStepped; called by §2.6's basement function (BCR-V3-20 crypt ring; BCR-V2-28 lift and half raise on wings over the basement's ring); read by V03's crypt placement, T-V2-36, T-V2-53. The crypt is Basement.crypt (BCR-V3-20, derived by §2.6 from V11's crypt column); V02 owns the wet-ground lift and the half raise. After every basement re-derivation (setMassing commit step 3, a designation mutation, a terrain change) an always-class crypt (cathedral, great temple, a building a dossier crypt record binds to) is kept with no condition; a basement-class church keeps its drawn crypt while its class stays in the church family; a mutation out of that family drops it through re-derivation, contents to V03/V04's closure, never silently.

Cathedral's crypt never refused (J-V2.46): ladder with no refusal rung: full crypt; half-sunk where the full floor would lie below the water table or the plot is low (wings over it raised by cellar.depthCm/2, BCR-V2-28, floor at datum less half depth); raised-choir crypt (Basement.kind raised) where even a half floor would lie below the water table or on a damp or flood plot: floor at max(lowest terrain sample under its ring, water table + crypt.freeboardCm), the ground storey of ground wings over the basement's ring lifted to clear the basement by crypt.clearCm (250 cm; the seed wings over a crypt-only basement; every ground wing over the whole inset V03 gives a crypt no stair reaches, V03 §3.7.4, S23R6-02), written by the basement step as those wings' Heights.baseCm with steps at the crypt ring's edge (V03 plans choir stairs, V3C-61 (4)). Inside a solid platform (V2C-68): seed wing a solid tier 0 of height >= crypt.clearCm + 100 cm: crypt inside tier 0 (floor as above, vault >= 100 cm under tier 0's top), no lift (stair 0 and stack keep heights); any other ground wing over the ring lifted as above; the lift applies only to a lower or storeyed tier 0 and then through rebaseStack. On a sky island the rim-slab vault is V05's form of the ladder. (e) Size and rank not V02's (cryptM2, rank via §2.6 with V11, BCR-V3-20). (f) Catacombs never V02's: no V02 path sources, moves, re-sources or shrinks one (item 109 (k)(2)(4)); V02's footprint and basement floor are an obstacle input to (k)(5)'s stagnation; a V02 demolition or replacement lifts that block; a crypt joins a catacomb only by V04's (3b) link.

Siting-profile columns shaping a building (item 103): none save two: emits.smoke >= 2 adds one decorative stack per level above 1 to the row's hearths (forge, kiln, brewhouse, dyer's chimney; §8.10 drawn until a plan exists); needs.runningWater selects the water axis for the main slot (M2); every other column is S10b's and the solver's (V11 §2.3); materials texture and colour.

A stepped building is reached only by name: a class whose designation template's composition key is one of V2 §3.15.4's rows (V11's specialisations, X17), a setMassing {family stepped} (or a tiers op bent to it) or a mutation toward such a row; no default, family, override or role row lists stepped (no-op pin, T-V2-50). One exported function decides the bytes (J-V2.80): M5 calls massStepped and the base outline builder calls the same massStepped from M3a (BCR-V2-39) with the same row, band, streams, so a pre-M6 stepped building keeps its bytes when stage 3 registers (T-V2-46); massStepped owns frame, band, draws, attempts, fallbacks; layTiers owns only the geometry and is what the tiers op, the mutator's anchored lay and V04's ruins call.

massStepped(input, row, band, k) in order: (1) frontage frame (V2 §3.4 steps 1-2); (2) slotBand -> lo, hi, cap (stepped rows carry claimShare: claimShare x area(H) x sizeFactor); (3) ST0, infeasible -> step 6 reported steppedInfeasible; (4) for attempt a = 0, 1, 2 (massing cap 3): drawTiers on massing creation indices 8 and 9 (a = 0) or massing/attempt=a's 8 and 9; layTiers at scale 1; ST8; an accepted TierLay converted to wings and MassingRef (ST7 order and keys) and returned; a TierFailure reported with step and detail, next attempt; (5) attempts exhausted -> step 6; (6) the single fallback (ST8's construction), then if its checks fail the base outline rectangle in H (M14 rungs 2 and 3). storeys = class HeightsRow.storeyCm; pitch, parapetCm, plinthCm = M11's pitch rule, the family's parapet, §2.6's plinth.

ST0 feasibility (M3 for stepped): at least draws n0 = count[0], d0 = insetM[0], sw0 = stairWidthM[0], ĝ = stairGrade[1] (steepest: least run), least heights h_k (solid solidHeightM[0] x taper^k, storeyed storeys.groundCm); least stair reserve r0 (axial (h0 + plinthCm)/ĝ, flights sw0 + stairClearM, internal 0); least front insets f_k, k = 1..n0-1 (axial max(d0, h_k/ĝ + landingM), flights max(d0, sw0 + stairClearM), internal d0); least top width t0 = tierMinSideM (flights max(tierMinSideM, h_{n0-1}/ĝ + landingM)). rect: Wmin = t0 + 2(n0-1)d0, Dmin = r0 + Σ f_k + (n0-1)d0 + tierMinSideM; feasible when W >= Wmin and D >= Dmin; Amin = Wmin x (Dmin - r0) + sw0 x r0. round or octagonal: least inradius ρ = tierMinSideM/2 + Σ max(d0, f_k); feasible when min(W, D - r0)/2 x cos(π/m) >= ρ (m side count: 8 or round bracket); Amin = m ρ² tan(π/m) + sw0 x r0; infeasible also when Amin > 1.1 x hi. Anchored mode (mutator W1): anchor's shorter side >= tierMinSideM + 2d0 and least reserve r0 of width sw0 fits inside H in front of the anchor's front side (none for internal).

ST1 draws (drawTiers): on s8 in order n uniform on count's integers; shape by weights; d = U(insetM); top by weights; sw = U(stairWidthM); g = U(stairGrade); for a shrine top its floors (uniform integer in shrine.floors), U(shrine.insetShare), roof kind by shrine.roofs. On s9 per tier k in order: solid tier (every tier under solid all; tier 0 only under lower) heightCm_k = U(solidHeightM) x taper^k rounded to the cm, floors_k = 0; storeyed floors_k = max(1, floor(U(tierFloors) x taper^k + u)) (u a second uniform), heightCm_k = storeys.groundCm + (floors_k - 1) x storeys.upperCm (each stacked tier's first storey a principal one, J-V2.85), never a parapet here (ST4 adds it). No aspect drawn (J-V2.86). All drawn once; ST8's re-lays and anchored mode re-use them (a shrink never shifts a draw). V04 draws the same list on its ruin stream.

ST2 tier 0 and stair reserve: reserve r at the front (-v side) of Rr: axial (heightCm0 + plinthCm)/g, flights sw + stairClearM, internal and none 0; the stack's own proportion (J-V2.86): W_need = t + 2(n-1)d, D_need = Σ d_k + (n-1)d + tierMinSideM (ST0's closed form at the drawn values), laid aspect = clamp(W_need / D_need, aspect cell); tier 0 in [0, W] x [r, D]: rect W0 = min(W, aspect x (D - r)) x scale, D0 = min(D - r, W0 / aspect), centred on u = W/2, front on v = r; round a regular ring with TowerShapeRow round side count, circumradius R0 = min(W, D - r)/2 x scale, centred, one side parallel to u nearest the front; octagon an 8-gon same circumradius and phase; every tier of a round or octagonal stack keeps tier 0's side count (concentric offsets vertex for vertex). D-front: under axial a round or octagonal ring's front chords within (sw + 2 x stairClearM)/2 of the centre line replaced by one straight edge (chord between the ring's crossings of u = c ± (sw + 2 x stairClearM)/2 on its front half). Anchored mode: tier 0 is the anchor as given (a kept range's four corners, extra vertices leaving with subtracted wings; or the tiers op's re-laid ring), reserve sought in front inside the region, else stair form falls back (never the ring). Flights: tier 0's front face >= (heightCm0 + plinthCm)/g + landingM else fallback.

ST3 tiers above (J-V2.74): for k = 1..n-1 front inset d_k: axial max(d, heightCm_k/g + landingM), flights max(d, sw + stairClearM), internal and none d; rect: tier k's ring = tier k-1's corners moved inward by d on back and sides and d_k on the front; round or octagonal: concentric, inradius reduced by max(d, d_k) all round (regular), same side count, then D-front under axial; on = tier k-1; the stack ends at tier k-1 where tier k's shorter side (polygon: twice its inradius) would fall below tierMinSideM or, for flights, its front face below heightCm_k/g + landingM; truncated counts tiers not laid (reported tiersTruncated). Stair fallback: with fewer than two tiers laid, re-run from ST2 with the next form of input.forms (absent: the row's form then axial -> flights -> internal; internal only where tier 0 is storeyed; a round or octagonal stack skips flights; none only where input.forms names it (an edit's bend) and tier 0 solid); past the last form layTiers returns TierFailure {noSecondTier, ST3}; the form laid is TierLay.stairs.

ST4 roofs and heights (J-V2.75): every tier but the top: lowerRoof flat (roof flat with parapetCm, ridgeCm = eaveCm, walkable terrace) or pent (hip rect, pyramid octagon, cone round, pitch p_k = min(pitch, pentShare x storeys.groundCm / d), ridgeCm = eaveCm + p_k x d: the band between the ring and the ring above, V2 §5.2 step 3's band facets); pent needs equal insets (internal or none form where every d_k = d; load check and tiers op bend). Top tier (whichever tier the lay ended on): flat and shrine top roof flat with parapetCm; roofed hip (rect) at the pitch rule's pitch, pyramid (octagon) or cone (round) at TowerShapeRow's pitch, ridge by M11's formulas. Each tier eaveCm = heightCm_k plus parapetCm on every flat-roofed tier solid or storeyed (so deckLevel subtracts exactly), Heights.floors = floors_k, solid where floors_k = 0. Shrine: top tier's ring moved inward by insetShare x its shorter side on every side (rect in a rect stack, regular ring otherwise), laid only where area >= 4 m² and each side >= 2 m else top becomes flat (shrineDropped); on = top tier; floors and roof as drawn; storeys groundCm then upperCm; role shrine.

ST5 stairs: axial: width min(sw, tier k's straight front edge length); stair k the rect of that width centred on the centre line along v, reaching from tier k's front face toward the front by run_k = rise_k / g (rise_k = heightCm_k for k >= 1, heightCm0 + plinthCm for k = 0; re-read by rebaseStack); stair 0 on the ground in the reserve (no on), stair k >= 1 on tier k-1's front terrace (on = tier k-1), rest of the front inset a landing before its foot. Flights: stair k the rect of length run_k along u and width sw along v against tier k's front face, on the ground (k = 0) or tier k-1's terrace; stair 0's foot at the face's left end (seen from front) climbing +u; for k >= 1 the foot is the point of tier k's front face nearest stair k-1's head, moved along the face only as far as the flight needs, climbing toward the end with more room. Every stair role stair, solid, roof shed with high its ring side at the upper end, eaveCm 0, ridgeCm = rise_k. Internal: no stair wing, V03's cores climb inside (X18). None (sealed): no stair wing, no way up; a storeyed shrine or tier on it is reached by nothing and V03 flags W_TIER_UNREACHED.

ST6 snap and validate (M13 for stepped): every ring snapped; every stair vertex lying on a tier ring's side inserted into that ring (§2.6 rule 1: stair 0's head vertices into tier 0's front side, stair k's into tier k's, a flight's back vertices into its face) so contact is exact and a carry keeps it; ground wings (tier 0, stair 0) tile; every wing with on inside the ring of its support (exact orient2d), boundary >= minEdge from that ring's except a stair whose foot lies on the terrace edge; wings standing on one wing pairwise interior-disjoint (stair k abuts tier k on shared vertices); each stair rise/run <= g x 1.01; stairChain connects the ground to the top terrace for axial and flights; a regular ring stays regular except its D-front edge; every wing >= 4 m², every side >= minEdge; failure returns TierFailure {check, ST6, detail}.

ST7 order, keys, hint: keys 0..m-1 in the order tier 0, stair 0, tier 1, stair 1, ..., tier n-1, stair n-1, then the shrine (no stairs under internal or none); no tower, so canonical order holds; nextWingKey = m; massStepped writes MassingRef.family stepped, segments 1, row, grammar, entrance, stack (shape, stairs, lowerRoof, top, insetCm, grade, truncated). Hint: a solid tier 0 under axial or flights: stair 0's outer side (axial: the side at its foot; flights: its -v side), so the main entrance is the stair's foot and the plan roots at the first landing door (BCR-V2-41); a storeyed tier 0: tier 0's front side, the door on its free part (BCR-V2-38); under none: tier 0's front side, an entrance opening nothing (BCR-V2-41).

ST8 size budget (M10 for stepped, inside massStepped): A = area of tier 0 ∪ stair 0, A_t tier 0's, A_s stair 0's; over 1.1 x min(hi, cap): where A_s >= min(hi, cap) the single fallback at once; else scale <- scale x sqrt((min(hi, cap) - A_s) / A_t) and layTiers re-runs once with the same draws (tiers may truncate; only tier 0's size moves the footprint); still over or a TierFailure: the next attempt, at the end the single fallback. Under 0.9 x lo: scale grows once by the least of sqrt(lo / A) and the largest factor keeping tier 0 and the reserve in Rr. Single fallback (no draw, so M3a and M6 builders agree): w = max(0.8 x wingWidthM[0], 3 m), L = clamp(min(hi, cap) / w, 1.2w, W), slab [u0 + (W - L)/2, u0 + (W + L)/2] x [v0, v0 + w] (single along the frontage), role main, roof flat with parapet, floors the template's least; MassingRef.family single, reported steppedFallback; failing M13's checks the base rectangle. A stepped row is never read on a deck (V2 §3.16's rows admit no stepped; family stepped there bends to single).

rebaseStack (J-V2.81): every path re-basing a wing of a stacked building calls it for the whole building, never the per-wing step: S11's datum step, a setMassing commit, a tier height edit, §7.3 (a) 4's terrain operator (whenever any ground wing is on a changed sample), §7.4's warp and moveVertex, carry rule (2), the crypt lift, a deck's re-base. Steps: (1) ground wings by the terrain rule (BCR-V2-32's levelledGroundCm samples with BCR-V2-42's wall-side move, so a levelling re-bases through S11's datum step); a ground wing's user-edited baseCm (J-DET-24's kept fate) kept and carries the stack; (2) each wing with on in stack order (after its support, whatever the keys), baseCm = deckLevel of its support; (3) each stair's ridgeCm re-set to its true rise (stair 0 deckLevel(tier 0) - stair0.baseCm; stair k deckLevel(tier k) - deckLevel(tier k-1)); where it exceeds g x run x 1.1 it is kept and reported stairSteep; the run is never re-laid by the datum pass (J-V2.2: the massing owns every ring); (4) envelope: Building.heights.baseCm least baseCm of ground wings; eaveCm, ridgeCm maxima over non-tower wings of w.baseCm + w.eaveCm - baseCm and w.baseCm + w.ridgeCm - baseCm (read by §8.4's caster ceiling and V05's clearance, X20); floors = 1 + max storeyRange(w)[1] over storeyed wings, 0 with none; every other building keeps M11's rule byte for byte (J-V2.78).

Stacks' storeys, rooms, composer, chimneys, shadows: a tier reaches storeyRange's storeys (solid none; storeyed from the storey above the one it stands on; level 0 the lowest storeyed level so a solid pyramid's shrine is storey 0; BCR-V2-33: capacity, Storey.level, Storey.wings read it); each tier's first storey a principal floor of storeyCm.ground (J-V2.85; V03 floorCm reads the tier's ground and upper heights, X18); the composer composes every tier, stair, shrine one to one; tier, shrine, stair admit no dormer; porch only at a storeyed tier 0's main door clamped to the free part and clear of stair 0 (tier admits one, stair none: a solid stack's door takes none); rooms rung emits no hall, gate hall, chapel or tower room; decorative chimneys only on exposed roof; plan chimneys drawn at Chimney.levels' top; V03 plans each storeyed tier and the shrine, landing door on landingSide (X18). One shadow per tier: every tier, stair, shrine its own caster (prism from its own baseCm to its eave with its roof's rise; §8.4 per wing), shadows nest (item 110 (f); T-V2-44).

Stacks' crypts and basements: a stepped building's basement lies under its ground wings (tier 0) whatever storeys they reach (BCR-V2-33); an always-crypt class built in tiers seeds its crypt with tier 0; on wet ground a solid tier 0 >= crypt.clearCm + 100 cm holds its raised crypt inside the platform with no lift (a storeyed annex over the whole inset lifted, V03 §3.7.4); a lower or storeyed tier 0 takes the lift through rebaseStack; where no ground wing is storeyed (V03 ground(b) absent: a solid tier 0 with no storeyed annex) the basement's access is external (BCR-V2-33 extension with §13.2 T29-4, J-A29.25; S23R3-03), its door at V03's basementDoor(b) (tomb door, or the wall side where the stack stands against a retaining wall; a platform crypt entered by the same door at its own floor); a storeyed ground wing beside a solid tier 0 (annex, arena façade ring) joins the basement by its core or trapdoor fallback, never outside (V03 J-V3.88).

roofscape(building, composition?): planar pairwise non-overlapping facets covering the footprint (and a porch outside), derived at read in the tile worker (float64, renderer CPU reference) and generation worker (exports), stores and draws nothing. (1) Ends (resolveEnds): each ridged wing's two ends (sides 1 and 3 for ridgeAxis 0, 2 and 4 for 1) classed in order: open if a tower ring covers it; party on a plot party-wall edge; mitre if shared vertex for vertex with another wing's end; along another wing Y's side (butt): wall when Y.eaveCm >= X.ridgeCm - 10, gable when X.ridgeCm > Y.ridgeCm + 10, else valley; a free end hip on a hip roof, gable otherwise; a block's side partly shared with a piece's end classed on the shared part. (2) Ridge lines: base ridge (rect: ends' midpoints; quad: arc-length midpoints of its ridgeAxis chains), hip pulls the end inward by WingRoleRow.hipInset x span (0.5 ranges; a block's FM entry 0.25 until calibrated keeps a ridge half its short side, never a pyramid), collapsing to the centre only when the wing is no longer than 2 x hipInset x span; valley extends it into Y by e = (X.ridgeCm - Y.eaveCm) / Y.slope; gable, party, mitre, wall, open leave it at the end's midpoint (mitre: the path vertex).

roofscape (3) facets per wing: gable/hip two long facets eave to ridge plus a hip triangle at each hip end; a valley end's facets continue into Y up to the valley lines (plan projections of X's facet planes meeting Y's near facet plane, clipped to Y's footprint; where X's eave is below Y's the valley starts where X's facet reaches Y's eave height); shed one facet low eave to high side; pyramid and cone one triangle per ring edge to the apex over the centroid; pent band facets (J-V2.75): for a pent wing x and wing y on it (concentric, equal insets, same vertex count) one planar facet per side i from x's side at x.eaveCm to y's side i at x.ridgeCm, neighbours sharing the vertex-to-vertex edge as hip line, round or octagonal per edge, nothing inside y's ring (ridgeCm = eaveCm + p x d meets the tier above's wall); a pent-kind roof with nothing on it laid as the top's roof (ST4); tent as a cone at its pitch; spire a cone or pyramid at spire pitch; flat one facet at eave height with an inner parapet line where parapetCm > 0; dome four latitude bands of planar quads (triangles at apex), rise = ring mean radius x domeRise (1.0), band rings scaled by cos of latitude (15°, 37.5°, 60°, 82.5° by dmath); plain (F-SKELETON downgrade) one flat facet, no lines; none no facet (excluded from tiling, drawn by states rows); skeleton the base's validated straight-skeleton faces (§3.8) with plain downgrade; cupola a small solid at its range's ridge midpoint (square plan side 0.3 x width, drum 0.25 x that side, dome/tip (cone rise 2 x half side)/pyramid) extra facets part cupola, never in Heights; every facet vertex carries z (cm above the lowest baseCm).

roofscape chimneys (§8.6, §8.10): a decorative chimney (no plan) at its host point on its host facet; a plan chimney (§2.6 Chimney) drawn on the roof or terrace facet over Chimney.column of the wing holding storey Chimney.levels[1] whose ring contains the column (a lower tier's stack carried up rises from the top of the stack, V3C-68 (2)); a chimney whose column lies inside the ring of a wing standing on that wing (stored plan not yet re-cut) is not drawn, reported chimneyCovered until the plan re-derives. (4) Occlusion: each valley region removed from Y's facets; each tower ring removed from every other facet (M11 guarantees the tower's eave is above); each ring of a wing standing on another removed from its support's facets; a dormer's plan rectangle removed from its host facet and replaced by its own facets (dormer/wallGable two facets from its front edge to a short ridge perpendicular to the host's, depthShare up the slope; hoist with a flat front; entranceGable two facets whose ridge runs to the host's ridge); porches add facets (hood one thin facet; gabled, twoStorey two facets with ridge square to the wall; halfRound half-cone triangles per arc segment to the apex on the wall line; recessed none, a notch line in the eave); result tiles footprint ∪ porches less roof-none wings (T-V2-9); cupola facets over it, excluded from tiling. (5) Lines: ridges, hips, valleys, eaves, wall end lines, tower seams (every other ring vertex's edge for a cone with >= 16 sides, every edge for a pyramid). (6) Order: porch, wing (stack order), dormer, tower facets, then lines.

χ̃ (provisional character): item 72's character vector computed from DistrictContext before S7c (V1-3.2), read by fabric selection and S9b; never the final χ.
DistrictContext: the read-only per-district context S7c and S9b read (shade, terrace, chains, frontage, relief, class shares, contextRung).
fabric (District.fabric, fabricParams): the layout kind S7c chooses per district, one of NG's four templates, seven context templates, or the base's own fill.
TemplateRow (table hood.templates): the editable row per template (requires.* eligibility, weights, primitives), §7.6.
template face: the face of a district a template layout is laid in, cut by seed primitives.
seed primitive: spine, ring, plaza or fan, the four building blocks of the template machine.
templateLandM2(D, row): the land a template claims in S7b (1) (BCR-4 (b)).
HoodPlace: a named local place (square, green, yard, court) of a neighbourhood (BCR-5).
hood pin (HoodPin, HoodPinRow): a derived point feature S9b places in a block (well, shrine, fountain), drawn through §8.1 marks (BCR-34).
close-up (CloseupParams, CloseupRecord): the persisted elaboration of one district or outline at neighbourhood detail (BCR-11, BCR-12); closing or reopening never alters the town.
outline close-up: a close-up on a drawn outline with no district under it (V1-3.8.9).
unit run: the generation path for a close-up with no base under it (standalone neighbourhood document; each sky island's districts).

standalone neighbourhood document (Recipe.product = 'hood'): a document holding one neighbourhood generated by the unit run; also written 'standalone hood', 'hood document' and 'lone neighbourhood document'.
pseudo-district: the one-district allocation the unit run makes for a standalone document or an underground void part (S7b (6)(d)).
plantRimWalk: the island rim-walk planter the unit run calls (also resize and rim reshape).
NG preset: the zeroing parity preset selecting Neighbourhood Generator's own rules, its entries on hood.constants alone (BCR-46).
hood.constants: the one settings row every numeric rule of V01 reads (item 23).
terraceState(D) = DistrictContext.terrace: declared, relief row or S1 site primitive (item 110 (a)).
contour series: the stepped row's terrace contour lines (with a ravine's two flanks) item 110 (a) builds.
under-deck strip: the strip under a raised way's deck S7b (1) and §4.6's holed laws treat as claimed.
hatched: V01's style family (the NG look) for close-ups; draws a stack in stack order and stair treads by stairTreads.
fabricSignature(outline): the fabric signature of an outline (read by V04's ruins, II.7.5 (2)).
SeamReport: the seams between a template face and the base's fill (portals, ring-radial stagger, dispatch seam guard).
entrance reserve: the rectangle S9b keeps free in front of a main entrance (and an external basement's door), reading PorchKindRow widthM, depthM, outside.
massing: stage 3's plan of a building's base wings (outline() M0-M14), recorded as BaseWing[] and Building.massing.
composition: the lazy composer result (wings and rooms rungs) over a massing; stored only when edited.
base wing (BaseWing) and composed wing (Wing.base): the massing's wing record keyed by wing key, and the composition's wing that names its base wing and carries nothing of its own.
wing role (WingRole): main, range, part, tier, shrine, stair (and the seating, gate passage of ovalCourt).
wing key: a wing's stable ordinal, never changed or re-used; edit paths and streams name the wing by it (Building.nextWingKey).
MassingRef: Building.massing (family, row, grammar, entrance hint, segments, stack).
massing family (MassingFamilyId): the vocabulary of plans (single, L, T, H, U, rectCourt, the five FM families, stepped, ovalCourt, ...).
resolution chain: the order in which a building finds its CompositionRow (designation template's composition, classFamily, templateFamily, default).
slotBand: the size band of a stepped slot from the slot hint and claim share.
facadeBays(wing, side, bayM): the bays of a wing side (integer), in @plat/plots.
roofscape: the building-wide roof plan from all wings at once (ends, valleys, walls, towers resolved; planar non-overlapping facets).
stack, tier, stack order: wings standing on others (BaseWing.on), tier 0 the ground wings, stack order supports before their stacked wings.
solid wing (BaseWing.solid) and sealed stack: a wing with floors 0 (no storey, room or capacity); a stack with stair form none.
stack helpers deckLevel, storeyRange, stairChain, landingSide: derived-at-read functions in @plat/plots.
approach strip: stair 0's derived approach region (stair reserve width, landingM deep in front of stair 0's foot; under internal in front of the main entrance; none under none), stated in V2 §4.6.
rebaseStack(b, ground): the one building datum pass for a stacked building.
cryptSeedWings(b) (seed wings) and the raised/half-sunk crypt: the wings a derived crypt is seeded under; the wet-ground forms of the no-refusal crypt ladder.
DeckContext and deck plot: a plot built on a deck host (mole, pier, quay platform, bridge) and its context (host, kind, surface height, landmark).
bend: the named alternative outcome replacing every structural refusal (item 101 R2), with a bend id.
fantasyShapes: the model control admitting Fantasy Manor's families among composed buildings.
identity composition: the composer's fallback (composed wings and towers one to one, no dormer, porch or room).
B-MASS and the free-frame harness: V02's bench fixture set and the FM parity harness (plat/bench/fm-parity/).
wingsInputs: exactly the inputs of the wings rung's staleness digest.

A1 resolution inputs: designation template programme key k (V11 §3.6.1: class id; custom institution's resolved class V11 §3.13; ladder GUILD/SIZE greater tier's class V11 §3.12; village v. key V07 §2.4, V11 §2.9); BuildingSlot.role (§4.7 S11) and whether it is the main slot; half h (shop when Use.branchOf set, works when another building's use names this use in branchOf, else both; item 105 (h)); occupants' band b (Plot.fieldBand); recipe era e (§7.7 layer 1). At every level a row whose for.era is e wins over the era-less row at the same key (J-V3.78).

A1 main slot resolves by first match: (1) class-id row whose for.use is Use.specialisation under k, else under '*'; (2) class-id row for.cls = k, no for.use; (3) where h is not both and the row reached has no half cells, or no row reached: family row of V11 split.works or split.shop for k (by h); otherwise family row of k's templateFamily (v. key: row its V02 composition.classFamily key names, reported via); (4) building-class row of §2.6 Building.class; (5) fallback house class row when the building houses a household, else warehouse. Another slot resolves by 2.4's slot-row order. A row's room with half other than both and h is dropped. No use and no household -> vacant programme. Row, level, slot, half, era, vacant -> PlanReport.programmeSource. A concealed use resolves its own row by the same rule for A2 (6).

Band cells: authored four-column cell reads poor/modest/prosperous/rich (squalid = poor, comfortable = modest); continuous cells (areas, sizeFactor, furnish.density) interpolate linearly along the field value between the centres of the two bands it lies between (§4.5 centres); discrete cells switch at the cut.

Pattern precedence: at a band whose ladder form is lodging, apartment or room, the ladder row's circulation.patterns replace the resolved row's upper and top cells (first listed weight 2, each other weight 1); the resolved row governs every other cell.

A2 lists: ProgramRooms built in order (1)-(7), (9), (10), (11); (8) runs after A6; each carries origin, rule (row index in that list), scope, priority, and the resolved row's cells overriding the role table's.

A2 (1) units: per household in address order, its unit's rooms at the ladder row's form (scope unit, hard, origin ladder); unitOneRoom: one room of role room whose area triple is the sum of the form's unit-room triples; unitHearth false: cooking place carries no hearth (H1 skips). (1') live-in household (Building.dwelling, §4.7 S10b; J-V3.32): form = ladder form capped at dwelling, rooms marked liveIn for A5 (a). (2) shared rooms: ladder row's shared roles the resolved row's shared cell admits, scope shared, soft, origin ladder.

A2 (3) staff rooms of the owners' unit (form house or dwelling whose principal chamber is largest; ties by household address) by ladder staff.count: const n rooms or one per n principal chambers (chamber or solar rooms); area = sizeShare x target of the owners' principal chamber (largest chamber, solar or hall); service, soft, origin staff. (3b) workplace sleep-in: beds = ceil(workers.max x staffSleepIn), workers from V11 BuildingClassRow.staff at band b; beds >= 3 -> dormitory x ceil(beds/8); beds 1-2 -> staff chamber x beds; soft, origin sleepIn, storey rule top then upper; a journeymen slot's slot row holds the dormitory instead.

A2 (4) class and use rooms at band b, half-filtered, origin programme (vacant: vacant). A dwelling row's own rooms need form house: for dwelling rows (class house, cottage, row_house, manor; families dwelling-row, dwelling-detached, dwelling-compound, farm; village v.yeoman_house, v.parsonage, v.manor_house, and v.cottage, v.hovel via class rows; every slot row taking one of them) own rooms apply only where the ladder form at band b is house; otherwise units (1) and shared (2) replace them, as V02's rooms rung withholds hall and chapel (V02 §3.8, J-V2.36), and fill still runs; every other row keeps its own rooms at every band. Count laws per §10.2: const, perHousehold, perStorey (one per storey the rule admits), perCapacity (named capacity summed over sub-locations / perRoom, rounded up; guest room 2, dormitory 8, cell 1 by default), perSubLocation; a fractional count draws once on plan.program.

A2 (5) sub-locations: per SubLocation in id order, keys = its tags in order then cap:+largest capacity key (ties leisure, tempResidential, guestWorker, studying, working); roles of the first key with a SubLocationRoleRow; hosted by the first (4) room in list order whose role is among them and whose hosted count < role hosts; else adds a ProgramRoom of the first mapped role (soft, origin subLocation); store only when no key maps (reported); A2 writes ProgramRoom.subLocation, P5 copies to Room.subLocation; a custom service inside its provider (item 104 (h)(5)) arrives as such a sub-location with SF tags.

A2 (6) concealed rooms: per concealed use in id order, rooms of its resolved row marked concealed (§10.2 RoomRuleRow.concealed); none marked -> back room x 1 (hard) and strongroom x 1 (soft, basement preferred where one exists); flagged concealed, scope service, origin concealed. (7) declared rooms: Building.declaredRooms in list order, role x count, hard, origin declared, storey = declared exact level where given else role's; scope role's.

A2 (9) crypt: exactly when Basement.crypt exists: crypt x 1, hard, storey -1, area its ring, origin crypt, whatever class, band or vacancy; where the rank capped it, undercroft x 1 as well (hard, storey -1, area the capped bays' ring, origin crypt, rule 1). (10) access host rooms: per hosted access whose host roles name no room of the lists above on the head's storey class: cellar (basement head) or store (ground head) at min area, hard, origin access; none for a head with storey null and none on a crypt-only basement (heads hosted in its undercroft or crypt; J-V3.119).

A2 (11) composer rooms: each Composition.rooms room (V02 hall, gatehall, chapel, towerRoom) takes the first unmatched ProgramRoom of its role on its storey (area becomes the ring's); unmatched adds a ProgramRoom (hard, area its ring, origin composer). Omitted composer room (V02 §3.13 F-COMPOSE (3)): a composed gate wing with no gatehall room adds gatehall (hard, origin composer, rule -1, wing key) whose fixed ring E2 lays across the wing eave to eave, width = lower bound of V02 CompositionRow.rooms.gateHallM at the occupants' band, centred on main entrance offset (else wing midpoint), clipped to its seed piece and moved along the wing on the module until it keeps minEdge (§3.4) from every side it does not share; no lawful position -> area target of the gatehouse triple allocated to that wing (reported composerRoom, tier 2); a composed tower missing towerRoom on a storey it reaches adds one (hard, composer, rule -1, area its seed piece, ring role). So the court keeps O1 (b)'s arches and T28-2's reach.

A2 (8) entrance anchors (after A5 and A6): per entrance in ordinal order whose storey is not null (a solid stack's main entrance opens nothing; S6's root landing door takes its place with that door's storey), the first ProgramRoom on the entrance's storey not already anchoring, whose role is in the EntranceAnchorRow list in list order, takes anchor.entrance (crossPassage resolved at the cut: to the cross-passage strip where drawn else next entry; firstGround; concealedFirst); a room anchors one entrance only unless two inward points fall in one seed piece; no candidate -> stair hall at min area added (circulation, hard, origin entrance); every fall reported in PlanReport.anchors.

A3 sizes: areaM2 = role triple (or resolved override) x ladder sizeFactor at the value; a ring role takes its ring's area as min, target, max. Unit floor: where the sum of a unit's targets < unitFloorM2 of its form, every unit room scaled by floor / sum (min, target, max together). Provenance of the floor and the room role's 9 m2: own, general historical knowledge, not corpus-witnessed (item 104 (f)); floor measured at P6 (2.4 measure line, T-V3-35 (i)-(ii)); room area on that line too (written at M2b by V12 default line, restated at P1), measured at P6, never tuned (capacity reads its min from M2b).

A4 storey capacities: cap(s) = area(pieces(s)) - sum fixed rings on s - circulation(s) in area2; fixed rings those of 3.1 step 2 (stacks subtracted when A5 (c) places them); circulation(s) = area(pieces(s)) x num/den of the resolved circulation cell (integers; A6's ring counts inside), at least one landing (landingCm x the core's flight width) on every storey the core serves above its first; the crypt's piece is outside cap(-1) (holds the crypt alone).

A5 (a) units first (F-PLAN tier 0; deterministic, no draw): a storey is claimed when a hard non-unit room of the resolved row has that storey class; a house unit takes every storey above the basement; dwelling units take whole storeys in address order from the lowest unclaimed storey up (one each where storeys >= units; else split by wing in key order where wings >= units; else side by side around a lobby, 3.5 lodgings); live-in unit takes the lowest storey above the use's hard rooms with capacity, spilling upward; with no upper storey stays on ground marked farFromEntrance; lodging/apartment/room units pack first-fit from the top storey down (poorest highest), perStorey(s) = floor(cap(s)/unitArea), falling to the next poorer form (tier 0) until every household fits; a claimed storey tried last in every rule; when even room does not fit the no-abort ladder runs (3.9).

A5 (b) hard non-unit rooms by storey rule: ground (level 0 = lowest storeyed level, V2C-61), top (highest storeyed level), basement (-1), upper (lowest storey above 0 with capacity), notBasement, any and belowTop (storey with most capacity left among admitted, ties lower), declared exact level; a room whose rule admits no storey the building has is dropped (soft, tier 0) or delivered by tier 5 (hard); on a building with no storeyed wing it is dropped, hard or soft, with no tier, information solidMonument, listed in PlanReport.owed with no tier (T28-1's exception as BCR-V3-14 words it); a shortfall runs ladder step (ii).

A5 (c) hearths first among the wings: every allocated room needing a hearth (H1) takes its wing now by (e); then H1-H3 place stacks and cap(s) of every storey a stack crosses falls by its ring. (d) soft rooms by priority then list order; staff rooms by ladder staff.placement in order (attic top storey; basement; service = storey holding a service or back wing, BCR-V2-01), never on a storey holding the owners' principal rooms while another allowed storey has capacity; sleep-in staff top then upper downward; other soft rooms onto allowed storey with most capacity left (ties lower); a soft room fitting nowhere dropped (tier 0, reported), the unit's hearth room never (falls with its form); a storey class whose only positive-weight pattern is nave holds one target per seed piece, soft non-anchored extras go to another storey with capacity in level order before 3.5's strips.

A5 (e) wing choice inside a storey, first rule that decides: (1) an anchor names the wing (entrance inward point, stack, core bay, access head, composer room); (2) hard adjacency: direct or corridor -> partner's wing; under -> storey below its target's, under it; to core -> core's wing; to entrance:main or entrance:yard -> wing holding that entrance; (3) concealed room -> concealed entrance's wing, else wing holding the use's service rooms; (4) farFromEntrance -> wing farthest from main entrance's inward point; (5) WingAffinityRow first wing role the storey has with capacity (part:<name> wing carrying that template part name); (6) wing piece with largest remaining area; ties by wing key.

A5 (f) fill: per storey in level order, while spare capacity >= smallest target of the resolved fill list, fill rooms added cycling the list at target (soft, origin fill); a fill room is scope unit of the storey's household where every unit room on that storey belongs to one household, else service; after the cut a piece above its role's max keeps it (oversize, reported), never split below a min. Output: per storey and wing piece, an ordered list of targets.
