Editing: everything a village has is editable with item 101's twelve tools (§7.1 authoring toolkit); village adds no thirteenth tool — two parameters and one sugar event (BCR-V7-19); every declaration held (§7.2) until its author changes it, bent to the nearest lawful form by its dry run otherwise (item 101 R2).

Twelve tools on a village: T1 intend — site card with form, water, palisade, field system, organic roads, orchards, forest, field factor; size = population; density and wealth sliders; events recipe intent at creation, afterwards Adjust / Re-derive on VillageRequest; a form edit making a held forest_strip unlawful bent to open_field with a note; derived by S0. T2 ground — reshape ground, draw brook or pond, move course-first river knots (WaterBody.controls), draw a terrace (item 110 (a): faces under the stroke levelled and walled along its edge, field terrace or lynchet included; J-V7.87); events setField(terrain), warp, drawWater, moveCourseKnot, terrace stroke (V09 terrace sugar) whose edge is a drawn RetainingWall where step > terrace.stepMinCm, held; derived by S1 operators, S10-S11 levelling inside perimeter, hinterland unit outside. T3 wall — palisade, bank and ditch, stone circuit; add gate; river, cliff or marsh closes it; retaining wall held never an enclosure; drawWall kind palisade/earthwork/inner/retaining (high side by drawing direction or ground; plots crossed re-levelled; ways crossed become stair or ramp by §3.8a (7)); points form derives the village trace (VS3 smoothing and pull, closing when ends meet); stretch end snaps to a barrier within reach, barrier arcs shown (item 106 (g), V09 snapping); placeGate; derived by VS3 steps 5-6, S7. T4 road — draw road, lane, track between points or walk from a point; raised way or aqueduct (any rung); drawWay with class; walk {headingCdeg, class road/track, maxLengthM?} (dry run runs one tracker, branches off, stores laid spine resolved); raised true or aqueduct class by points only (walk with raised bent to points form with a note); count badge; derived by S4 router (points) or VS4 tracker (walk); raised by base raised-part commit.

Tools cont.: T5 quarter — at a village rung declare an end by lassoing its houses (item 101 R4), kind and name; anchor defaults to most significant entity inside (church, manor, mill, open space, else lasso centroid) or picked; sugar quarter expands to declareEnd with boundary (BCR-V7-19); count badge; derived by VS8. T6 place — heart, church, mill, manor, well, centrepiece; assign a use; on a deck face (pier head or widened bridge) a store, net shed, boat shed, toll house or chapel; placeAt (heart = placeAt of VillagePlan.heart, heartSource edit), assign, build; on a deck face S10b's request path with deckOk in the village reading (dwelling there bent to nearest toft with a note); derived by VS1 (heart), S10b (mill bent to nearest mill seat). T7 roster — list what the village must hold; with a dossier the author may only place (§7.1); S10b claims-first. T8 fill — brush more/fewer houses, draw a green, brush class mix; setField(density), drawGreen kind green (green Reservation and Greenery); S10a quotas and slot race in touched blocks. T9 shape — split/join tofts, build on a close, move a house, set croft depth, change a furlong's strips; split, join, build, moveFootprint, setAttr (yard parts, furrowAxisCdeg, rotation.slot), drawFootprint. T10 hold — lock, pin, revert, regenerate; New random on a block re-races slots, on the plan redraws auto draws; rerollLayer('village.track') re-grows roads; rerollLayer('forest') re-draws crowns. T11 name — setAttr(name) on VillageEnd, VillageField, reservation, way; moveLabel, hideLabel, group. T12 dress — painterly or ink; fields, relief, spotlight, shade map, underground (unexcavated voids, V09 toggle); setStyle, setLayer, paintGround. delete (V09 §4.3) — remove a raised way: declared = V09 delete of its declaration; carried generated = C6-39 suppression (reason key in log), dry run 'the town will not rebuild this aqueduct; undo brings it back'.

Other village edits: land conversion by hand = convert with retypeLand (file f item 209 absorbing BCR-V7-22; ST-25) under T2's land-use chip; retiring, effacing, reopening a way by hand = convert with retireWay/effaceWay/reopenWay (BCR-V7-32 (b)) under T4's way chip, dry run keeps every live plot's access (a stretch that is some plot's only access stays in use with a note); underground edited with V04's tools and events (drawTunnel, drawChamber with system ruin or cavern, addUndergroundAccess, closure states; V04 §4), lifecycle and undo V04's; a church's crypt is its building's basement (V02, V03 events). Count badge (item 101 R14): dry runs of declareEnd, drawGreen, density brush, raised way add/removal, retaining wall, terrace stroke show plots, households, buildings touched. Supply links (item 105 (j)) pinned, moved or cut by base link events through V09's link view, stored map-side, never written to the dossier (a cut bakehouse-mill link makes flour an import). Author split: T6 assign of the shop to a second plot with branchOf naming the works' use (BCR-V7-24), held, merged back by inverse. Item 110 declarations (drawn wall, terrace stroke, declared raised way, placed deck plot) held through Regenerate (keep); generated wall edited by setAttr of material or by drawing over (drawn wall wins); deck widened by setAttr of width (face buildable).

New event forms (BCR-V7-19): EditEvent gains {t: 'declareEnd'; anchor?: Id or PointCm (absent: most significant entity inside boundary); boundary?: PolygonCm; kind: VillageEnd kind; name?} (sugar quarter expands to it at a village rung; creates a declared VillageEnd keyed by the event's address, held); drawWay gains optional walk {headingCdeg; class road/track; maxLengthM?} (one tracker from points[0] by VS4 step rules, branches off; laid spine resolved into points at dry run); walk and raised are exclusive (bent to the points form with a note, item 101 R2); retypeLand is V06's EvolveOp member, one op for both volumes (file f item 209; ST-25): {op: 'retypeLand'; landUse; to: LandUse kind; crop?; rotation? {scheme, slot}}. setAttr reaches VillagePlan.form, .roads, .nuclei, .character.*, VillageRequest.*, Reservation.kind between green and plaza, Enceinte.kind among village kinds, VillageField.name and .kind, VillageEnd.name, each with base dry run, fate report, inverse (§7.1, §7.4).

Locality per village edit (§7.3): heart moved / form or road topology changed / nuclei edited -> from VS1; settlement VS1-VS8 and S7-S11 on the district; hinterland only on faces the perimeter move touches; locked/pinned held, declared re-placed; coarse 'the village is re-laid around the new heart; N houses move'. Character -> VS4, network and after in the district. Density brush -> S10a, touched blocks (quotas re-allocated among themselves, sum kept; re-raced), 'N houses in the brushed blocks'. drawGreen -> VS4 open-space step for the green only then VS6-S11, blocks overlapped or fronting. drawWall (village kinds) -> VS3's form then S7, the wall's band cleared and re-cut, gates where ways cross. drawWay (points or walk) -> VS6 on faces it splits. declareEnd -> VS8, ends only (count badge). Class placed/assigned -> S10b request path, target plot and relocated occupants (§4.7). Market hall claim or fair field moved (T6 placeAt of its member) -> VS4 claim step along the rim or VS5 fair step at the point; open space remainder and hall plot, or fair field face and commons around (S12a). Field system changed -> S12a, hinterland faces, outlying farmsteads re-sited, nothing inside perimeter. retypeLand, rotation.slot, furrowAxisCdeg -> hinterland unit on that face. retireWay/effaceWay/reopenWay -> the network's readers of that way, way alone (no live plot's access from a hollow way; a reopened way's runs raced again only by regrowth). New random on a block -> that block. rerollLayer('village.track') -> VS4 as character edit. T3 retaining -> S10-S11 in plots crossed (re-levelled, re-cut; stair or ramp for a crossed way). T2 terrace stroke -> S10-S11 inside, hinterland unit outside. T4 raised way added -> §3.5a (10) (blocks re-raced with quotas kept, shortfall to neighbours; faces re-cut; feet joined; well coverage). Raised way removed -> strip blocks re-raced, faces re-cut, V04 vaults removed same commit. Deck plot placed -> S10b request path on the deck face. Deck widened -> S10 on the deck face ('the pier head can now hold a shed'). Coarse edits declared coarse by dry run (§7.3); a density stroke never moves a quota outside its blocks.

Edit lifecycle (§7.4 columns): declareEnd — event (sugar quarter); VS8, labels, exports; log; held (lasso plots re-joined every re-derivation; never merged or capped); inverse removes the end; event schema version, an event without boundary reads a point declaration. drawWay with walk — event with resolved spine stored; VS6 on split faces; log; never re-walked (spine is the recorded input); inverse removes the way, faces re-joined; as drawWay. retypeLand (one lifecycle row with V06's, file f item 209) — convert or epoch op; S12b, hinterland unit, render; log or epoch record; kept; conversion's undo record; new op kind versioned. retireWay/effaceWay/reopenWay — event or epoch op; network readers (hollow way read by none), hollow_way role, GeoJSON hollow_ways; kept; conversion undo; new op kinds. setAttr on VillagePlan, VillageRequest, VillageField, VillageEnd — event; §2.6 rows; log; recorded value read on regenerate; inverse. Village density stroke — setField(density); S10a, race; log (strokes); composited onto recomputed raster (§7.2); stroke inverse. drawGreen (kind green) — held (declared); inverse. drawWall retaining; T2 terrace stroke — event; S10-S11 levelling, hinterland unit, render, exports, clerk; log; held; inverse; older document nothing. drawWay raised or aqueduct — event; §3.5a stages, V04 arch-vault source; log; held, feet re-joined at every derivation; inverse. Raised way removal (V09 delete; C6-39 suppression) — event; declaration layer (raised), V6 §3.19 ledger from first CITY epoch; log (reason key for a generated way); held through Regenerate (keep), every village epoch and both hand-offs; inverse restores way and vaults with their ids. Deck plot placed; deck widened — event; S10b, V02 DeckContext, render; log; held while its deck stands, falls with its deck and re-offered when rebuilt; inverse.

Clerk's view (V10 over §11.2's tool API): reads the same records a person sees (VillagePlan, ends, fields, palisade, dossier facts); proposes with the twelve tools as dry runs shown as ghosts (J-A101.74). Describe-to-map returns a skeleton, e.g. 'a green village by a ford...' -> intend (VILLAGE, 600 people, form green, water stream), place (v.parish_church, high ground within 200 m of heart), place (v.watermill), intend (field system open_field), never a picture. 'Why is this here' answers from rows that pulled it: heart from VS1 score terms; house from slot density, rim multiplier, block quota; class from §2.4 profile, relation and coverage rows, signature pairs fired (item 103 (e)); wood from §3.9 suitability incl. shade (item 102 (f)); custom institution from resolved profile sources (item 104 (a)); trade from links and goods (item 105 (j)) or coverage and spacing; market hall from its claim; fair field from its record; pin from forcing record or VS8 row and epoch (provenance; SR4-01, TV-03); unwalled side from the barrier arc (item 106 (g)); ladder record from its members; underground from V04 records (V10 rows): unexcavated void, access cause, dwelling from its access; crypt or its absence; burial face; strip holding's holder; hollow way's disuse epoch; item 110 (V10 rows): generated wall from platform step ('the ground falls 22 % here'), carried raised way from reason and year, removal, absence ('villages never build them; you may draw one'), pier head, scarp.

Painterly family: the village opens in 'painterly' (base reserves the slot, §8.2; V07 builds it at all four bands); every other family draws a village from the same display list (§8.1), ink one click away (J-V7.25); style sheet is data (roles, programs, layer order, palette on §8.2 targets, item 69; own colours never VG's, §17.1). Programs (PaintProgram in §8.2's registry): Ground: ground ramp by relief class and moisture over paper tone; base hillshade (multiply shade side, add lit side, at 0.5 and 0.25 strength); relief tier on (contours, hachures or grass marks by the sheet's relief option; grass default: short slope-aligned ticks alternately longer/shorter, light or dark by facing). Water: water-band law of §8.3's census (W x (i/N)^1.5, N = 3), stony edge as a pair of jittered strokes along every shore, one tide line on flowing water and two on still water and sea (ref:VG water look, D5, geometry only). Ways: through wide, street narrow, lanes narrower, tracks dotted (dash 1 % of width, gap two widths), driveways as flared patches, junction corner fills where roads meet at > 26 deg; fords a pale band with stepping marks; hollow ways a sunken double hairline with inner shade; way.edgeFade: a road leaving the frame turns over its last fadeM (60 m) into a dotted trail whose dot spacing widens x1.4 per dot; bridge.shadow = deck.shadow for a part-0 bridge (offset band along §8.4's sun, offset = deck height x sun cotangent); pier head = widened plank deck; way.stair: step ticks one per stairTickM (0.3 m) of run, tick side toward low end (V1 I110-2); way.ramp: tapered wedge tint darkest at low end.

Painterly cont.: Fields: each furlong in its crop tone with bounded jitter; strips as furrow strokes along furrowAxisCdeg at strip width, dashed from a small set of patterns, headlands plain; enclosed fields hedged by hedgerow instances (§8.10); orchards rows of crowns (jittered grid, §4.9); meadow fine stipple, commons coarse; great-field boundaries faint dashed at township band. Woods: crown.bands (rim band of full crowns, one or two muted bands offset inward at mutedMix 0.35 toward fill tone, solid interior billowed thicket fill); crown.groupShade (each crown shaded away from light; touching crowns shaded as one mass; per-crown radial gradient a sheet option, off in ink); crowns from §8.10 instances on render.instances (never stored), rerollLayer('forest') redraws them alone. Palisade: thick dark line with stake ticks every 1.5 m outside; earthwork bank of short hachures toward the ditch with the ditch a thin water-toned or dark line outside; inner stone circuit as ink's wall symbol at half width; gates a gap with two posts or a gatehouse footprint; light stretch at half weight (wattle thin line with cross-hatches, low bank sparse hachures, parapet stone symbol at a third width); barrier anchor post dot (palisade, earthwork) or small tower (stone); closing arcs drawn only as their barrier; the wall layer's 'show circuit' option (V09) traces them faint dashed.

Conventions: 'the base' is docs/ARCHITECTURE.md with amendments c, d, e folded in and file g items 102-110 as the coherence pass applies them; a § points into the base, 'V08 §' into this volume; SettlementForge field names and values quoted freely (owner's own project; amendments d, gate 2); no SF code excerpted; nothing from SF's map programs or map designs used; BCR-V8-n (§10), J-V8.n (§9), T-V8-n (§7).

Plain words: SF gets a Map tab on every settlement page; first opened by someone with GM rights, the map is drawn from the dossier (every listed institution sited sensibly, population fills the right number of houses, walls, gates, harbour and quarters match; everything unsaid derived by the map's rules from the same seed); the map never writes back into the dossier. On change (DM event, decree, week, season, year) the map compares the new dossier with facts it carries, works out what changed, reads each change's week from the dossier's receipts, changes the town as little as it can; history panel says what moved and why in SF's words ('bankrupt', 'destroyed by disaster'); after the DM advances time campaign maps catch up one by one in the background; a map opened before its turn catches up at once.

Plain words: custom institutions and chains from SF's homebrew library arrive like built-in ones; the map reads scene type, category and tags and (when handed over) the fuller library entry; an active supply chain laid out as one working line (raw material at its field or quarry, workshops stepping inward, seller near the market); renaming a custom item changes nothing; revising moves it only as far as needed. 'Blacksmiths (3-10)' drawn as several smithies, a guild as its hall with workshops, a 'district' as a quarter, never twice when SF lists the smaller form; SF supply chains tie mills, bakeries, markets together, a weakened chain pulls less; a coastal town whose record names a war or hostile sea partner walls its quays; a storm leaves damage where it struck; ancient ruins, magical node, ley lines or a magical past put an older town's ruins beneath; mines and mountains make caverns likelier; catacombs only under cemeteries, never under churches, only from a town upward; the cathedral always has the largest crypt; a cemetery the record closes stops its catacomb growing; nothing lost below.

Plain words: in a city (10 000 people or more) whose record lists its water system the map may carry an aqueduct on arches from a spring or river in reach to the city's conduit house, and a raised road may link a citadel, palace or cathedral on high ground; a town gets these only if the DM draws them; they are the map's own additions, removable by the DM and staying removed through later updates; the history panel says why each was built; a toll bridge gets a stream to cross, never a bridge over dry land.

Plain words: DM sees and edits everything, co-DM edits too; players never receive the DM's map file or SF's record: their Map tab shows pictures of the town as the party knows it (unlearned place drawn but not named), redrawn after every DM save and reveal ('Reveal to the party'; 'See what the players see' switch); gallery and public pictures show only public names, SF-veiled words veiled; SF's AI assistant reads the map, answers 'where is the tannery and why', proposes changes as ghosts the DM accepts or drops; a player's assistant reads only the party's known places.

Plain words: the map program runs in its own frame on its own web address (as SF's realm map does), none of its code beside SF's accounts or payments; each map stored by SF next to its settlement, never inside the dossier, as a saved file plus the list of changes since, 'with two older copies kept as backups'. An unreadable dossier, an unknown SF version, or a settlement shrunk below the town floor never breaks the map: it shows the last good town with a plain note ('This map is held as it was. The settlement's record could not be read.'), loses nothing, catches up when a readable dossier arrives; 'A settlement under 1 500 people waits for the village product, which will plug into the same doorway; when it exists, a town that shrinks into a village, or a village that grows into a town, keeps one map.' Map record: the host is the store (§11.3); for SF one map record per settlement map in its own row keyed by settlement id and map id, never inside the dossier's data blob (would ride every save, sync and public projection at about ten times the dossier's size; research/sf/dossier-seam.md C-6; J-V8.3); type published by @plat/bridge-client as the host's storage contract; module never touches storage. The host never computes anything it stores (C8-04): every encoded event, head, sequence number and snapshot field arrives in a message; the host compares only strings it was handed (a proposal's baseLogHead against the logHead it holds; J-V8.46).

MapRecord.status semantics: current = lastOffer.dossierHash equals the dossier the host holds and the result committed; stale = host holds a newer dossier than lastOffer; refreshing = a live refresh lease (refreshing.until in the future; an expired lease is free and status reads stale); held = last offer refused, held says why (§3.9). Written only through the client's store calls (§3.7, §3.14), each a compare-and-set conditioned on the logHead the host holds (or party.rev for the party), so two writers never interleave; party starts {tier public, places [], rev 0} at create.

A binding row's life: create — creation writes one row per dossier element placed or carried (collective members #1..#n; a ladder lesser merged into its greater becomes a row of the greater's members, or an alias row on a new-thing greater, or the row on the churchyard cross a pin lesser binds at a village rung; SR5-01); absorb writes a row per addition; read — factTier (§2.8), the diff, the oracle's answers (§4.4); persist — dossier block (§2.9) outside the model digest; regenerate — scoped regeneration re-places members under their addresses (§6.3), rows never change; undo — a dossier event is no undo target (§7.4); a map undo that would un-place a dossier element refused (§7.7 item 2); migrate — rebuilt from the log's dossier events at first load (§7.5); adapter remap or line migration re-keys rows by §3.8 and writes line_migrated; a row whose element is removed keeps key and entity (retired assignment) so a re-opening re-binds to its former building (F6).

A cemetery closes, so its catacomb stagnates: a burial or monastery record turning ruined, removed or destroyed, or closed by an institutionHistory fate, closes its placed burial faces at the change's week (F2 fates); V04 holds the catacomb under a closed face stagnant (extent kept, growth stopped, nothing lost; item 109 (k)(5); blockedBy); a reopening (F6) resumes growth by least disruption. A church's fate touches only its crypt: a church or cathedral ruined, removed or destroyed ruins or vacates its building and crypt (V02, V03); a catacomb feels it only through an existing crypt join (join takes the base's closure state; extent and growth unchanged); a churchyard stays a burial face while its church plot keeps the churchyard part, ruined or not, closing only when the plot is cleared and re-used by least disruption (J-V8.53). A tier change is not a closure: a promotion adds the new tier's burial record beside the old one (research/sf/dossier-generation.md tier-shift row), item 108 (c)'s merge makes the lesser a member, no face closes; when a lesser leaves the list in the absorb that adds its greater (burial pairs graveyard REPLACEMENT over burial_ground (hamlet to village), parish_burial_grounds COUNT over both (village to town), burial_grounds_and_charnel_house SIZE over all three (town to city); V11 §3.12, SS-26, SS-45), the port re-binds the lesser's faces to the greater's key (rebind, noted ladder_promoted), never a remove; a demotion below TOWN removes no catacomb (V04's ratchet; V06 and V07 maintenance mode). New cemeteries seated by S10b's least disruption; one begins a catacomb only where V04's count allows. Deaths: a plague or plague_onset condition or stressor standing at an epoch, and a calamity's deaths in its CalamityRef, are that epoch's burial input for item 109 (k)(4)'s capped growth (V04 §3.10).

Embed (1) SF's side: the Map tab is a lazy chunk imported by nothing eager (SF's first paint unchanged; C-10, E-8), holding SF's mount component and @plat/bridge-client (<= 12 KB gzipped with the party viewer, §6); a player's tab (audience player) calls mountParty: reads the record's partyPictures into the client's small pan-and-zoom viewer, no frame, module or message (§3.14; C8-01); the DM's and co-DM's tab calls mount: reads the map record, draws the viewer key's thumbnail at once as a static image if one exists (J-V8.24), creates one iframe src = moduleOrigin + embedPath + '#p=2', sandbox 'allow-scripts allow-same-origin allow-downloads' (no top navigation, pop-ups or forms), allow '', referrerpolicy no-referrer, sized to the tab (J-V8.7); SF's CSP adds the module origin to frame-src; allow-same-origin is the module's OWN origin (workers and cache), granting nothing on SF's origin; mount refuses any audience word other than dm and co-dm before a frame exists. (2) Module's side: the module origin serves static files only: embed.html (second entry point of @plat/app, host mode: no file operations (fileMenu false), no DocResolver, bridge-driven; BCR-V8-3), lazily loaded chunks of the current output version and the retained N−1 and N−2 (§6.4), fonts, the stamp-tile asset; headers: Content-Security-Policy default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; worker-src 'self' blob:; img-src 'self' data: blob:; connect-src 'self' <the clerk origins>; frame-ancestors <SF's app origins>, where the clerk origins are a deployment row by V10's configuration (V10 §3.17): none under C ('SettlementForge's own assistant, the default recommended here') and under off; the proxy's origin (one of SF's app origins on the embed's allowlist) under B; the provider's API origin under A; no cross-origin isolation headers (§11.2); Cache-Control immutable on hashed chunks; the module holds no account, cookie or secret, trusts only messages whose origin is on its allowlist and whose source is its parent window (§11.3).

Embed (3) Boot: embed.html binds WindowPostMessageTransport to window.parent with the allowlist, sends module.status {booting}, starts the generation worker, the derivation pool (up to three workers, §4.1) and the tile worker, loads model packages of the current output version, sends ready {outputVersions, schemaVersion, protocol 2, adapters [{line, version}]} (BCR-V8-1); client flushes queued messages in order (§11.3); ready within bootTimeoutMs (20 s) or the client re-creates the frame once; a second miss leaves the thumbnail with the note 'the map could not start' and a retry button (§3.9 B1). (4) Load: client sends doc.load {bytes: snapshot, role, session, audience} (module re-derives role and key from audience by §14's table, takes the lower; J-V8.29) then doc.apply {baseLogHead: snapshot.logHead, events: tail}; module opens the snapshot (§2.9 steps 1-5: frozen view outside the window, corrupt cache replayed, verification in background), folds the tail, draws; first live frame replaces the thumbnail; an older snapshot.outputVersion inside the window replays exactly under its own version and module.status {upgrade-available} goes to an owner's client only (§3.8). (5) Offer: client decides whether to offer (§3.2) and commits the result (§3.3). (6) Switching settlements: MapSession.switchTo(spec) (same fields as mount; C8-40) reuses the frame: close on the handle, then load and offer the next record; boot paid once per page (J-V8.30); one document live per frame; previous one's memory released before the next is opened (§12.8 per document).

X12); exportFormats (by §5.4 (2): every format §11.1's key rules admit for the frame's role and key, saved to the user's device); fileMenu false; historyFilter unset (only owner and editor frames at secret); {places} = names admitted by the key list is called with (effectiveKey(), V9 §2.10; SR2-23), targets their entity ids; each place read by query(h, {kind entity, dossierKey} or {kind entity, id}, {admitAs}) (BCR-V9-36, BCR-V10-22), a collective by each member key <key>#k; withheld neither named nor targeted; null named by its key with no target; a reveal or hide line left with no place not listed (SR2-24; J-V8.106); answers cached keyed by knowledge key, dropped when a line is added and when the document's head moves (doc.changed ApiEvent of the handler's one subscribe, registered at each doc.load, released at close and switchTo), firing onChange (SR3-13 (c); J-V8.110); list with an uncached key returns only place-less lines (host.partyTier, host.picturesDrawn), starts reads, fires onChange on answer (J-V8.109); no key subscription of its own (the shell re-lists on onEffectiveKey, V9 §4.10); one line host.picturesDrawn 'Party pictures last drawn {time}' from partyPicturesAt; list starts empty at each doc.load (first party value is the baseline), never persisted (J-V8.58; J-V8.93)); newDocuments 'download' (V9 §3.9 host-mode rule; a copy of a dossier-bound document is detached, V6 §4.4; J-V8.93). (c) host.state: handler keeps the latest party, backups, partyPicturesAt in session memory; playersView and the header's toggle set ViewOpts.viewAs via setViewOpts (BCR-V9-23) through view.set (§11.3), clear with viewAs undefined. (d) Selection: reveal and hide carry the frame's current selection (entity ids forwarded in entity.selected, §5.4 (4)) as binding key when dossier-bound (Identity.dossier), else address. The handler lives as long as the frame and survives switchTo; host.state memory replaced after the next doc.load, historyLines cleared, players' view switched off at every load.

Offer decision and coalescing: the host cannot compute the fact hash, so it compares raw dossiers: hashDossier = SHA-256 (Web Crypto) of canonical JSON (keys sorted by code point, no insignificant whitespace, numbers as JavaScript prints them), lower-case hex; the DM's or co-DM's client offers when hashDossier(dossier) != record.lastOffer.dossierHash or when the record is held (every new dossier is a retry), never otherwise; a player's page never offers; the port decides at the fact level (J-V8.4): differences only outside the carried facts (generation log, prose, simulationTrace, never-read keys) return unchanged and the host stores the new lastOffer with nothing appended (T-V8-6). Coalescing (J-V8.23): at most one offer in flight per session; a newer dossier replaces any queued one; when the in-flight result returns the newest is offered against the new head; the client counts skipped versions in its report field coalesced (client-side; no port note; C8-34); skipped versions lose nothing (the port diffs carried facts against the newest; each change's week from receipts, §4.11 (2)); an element appearing and vanishing between offers is never seen (same answer as SF's end-state).

Port leader: the port runs inside the module (generation worker, beside the document), never in SF's bundle (J-V8.1); only an editing role (DM owner or co-DM editor) holds the document, dossier and a port; a player holds neither (C8-01; J-V8.2 revised); digest, creation, absorb are pure functions of (document, dossier, HostContext, adapter and table versions), so every editing client computes the same events; every port event carries reserved session host:port (C8-15; BCR-V8-19) so events are byte-identical whichever editor computed them (T-V8-3) and no user's undo stack holds one. Creation (no map record): host mints mapId, sends dossier.offer {create {mapId}}; module runs digest -> creation (§14: blueprint, creation prefix, binding, carried facts) -> generate(blueprint, {docId: mapId, prefix}) (BCR-V8-2; J-V8.13); replies dossier.result {created, created: SnapshotBlock, factHash, report} (.plat bytes with logHead, lastSeq, outputVersion, schemaVersion, documentDigest computed by the module; C8-04); host calls MapStore.create as handed ('exists' -> another client won; reload the stored record, byte-identical by determinism, T-V8-3), writes the two thumbnails and renders the first party picture set. Absorb (a record exists): digest -> absorb(doc, digest, host) (§14; steps §3.5-§3.6), dry-run on the working state (§7.1; never refused by map locks or pins, applied around them, §7.7 items 2, 5), replies dossier.result {absorbed, baseLogHead, events, encoded, seqAfter, logHeadAfter, factHash, week, report} WITHOUT folding; host treats it as a doc.changed: if baseLogHead is current it commits (MapStore.commitEvents), sets its head to logHeadAfter, fans doc.apply out to every open session incl. the sender (which folds; §11.3 convergence); else doc.rejected {stale} and the module re-runs absorb on the new head (bounded: three attempts, then module.status {error} and a retry at the next offer). Verification by every editor (C8-37): an editing client folding a doc.apply with host:port events and holding the same dossier (last offer's hash equals the result's dossierHash) re-runs absorb on the pre-apply state and compares encodings; a difference is a port mismatch (module.status {error, detail host.verify.mismatch}, §3.9 B20, a report line naming the first differing event); never blocks the fold (T-V8-8). Two editors at once: both compute the same events; the host accepts the first, answers the second stale; the second's re-run finds nothing left (unchanged); no election protocol; the log's single head is the arbiter (J-V8.2).

Refresh queue (J-V8.6): after SF commits an advance, the host marks refreshPending on every map record whose dossier changed (hashDossier) and calls MapHost.refresh(queue) from the DM's page; the client creates ONE hidden frame (embed.html#p=2&mode=refresh: no tile worker, no view, no thumbnail pass until the end) processing the queue serially in campaign order, one document at a time: take the record's refresh lease (setStatus refreshing {by session, until now + 60 s}; refused when another live lease holds it; C8-30) -> doc.load + tail -> dossier.offer -> commit -> compact if the tail exceeds its threshold (§3.7) -> render the two thumbnails and party picture set (tile worker started for this step only) -> release lease with status current and refreshPending cleared -> close document, release memory -> next; lease renewed after each step, expires on its own (a dead page's lease expires within 60 s; record reads stale meanwhile). Scheduling: runs while the DM is not interacting with a map frame (paused on pointer or key input in any visible map session, resumes 5 s after the last), yields between maps, stops on AbortSignal. Page memory (C8-23): the refresh frame does not start while a visible map frame holds a CITY or METROPOLIS document; runs when the Map tab is closed or the visible document is a TOWN (at most one CITY or METROPOLIS document per page; §6 page row); queue persisted by refreshPending (next page resumes); a map opened in a visible tab while queued is absorbed there first and dropped from the queue; serial keeps memory at one rung's line (§12.8) plus the frame's fixed cost (a campaign of 20 CITY maps after a year in about 1.5 minutes of background work incl. party sets, §6).

digest(raw, host) steps (§14 item 2's duties; all pure): (1) adapter: AdapterRegistry.select(raw, {line: host.line, bound}); refusal ends (E_LINE_UNSUPPORTED); (2) limits: a bounded walk measures bytes of keys and strings, depth, list lengths against the manifest's limits; over any -> E_UNKNOWN_SHAPE with a size_limit note naming the first limit (T-V8-20); no string longer than maxString copied; (3) shape: every requiredKeys key present with the types read (id 's_' + 16 hex, name non-empty string, tier a string, population an integer in [0, 1e7] (0 a deserted settlement routed by §3.6 (7); SS-21), institutions an array, _seed present); failure -> E_UNKNOWN_SHAPE listing up to 20 violations; an extra top-level key never a failure (C8-03): read-false optional or unnamed key dropped into ignored with ignored_key; the hand-made teaching file fails here (§14); (4) records: each institution, power, notable, condition, calamity checked for required fields (a name; an institution a category string; numbers finite); a failing record QUARANTINED (kept out of the digest, its key when formable listed in DossierBinding.quarantined with the reason, quarantined_record note), the rest proceeds (J-V8.8; §3.9 B4); the diff never removes a quarantined key; a quarantine whose key cannot be formed holds every absent institution key (C8-12).

digest step (5) keys, grammar, class: name grammar and ladder step (§3.5.1); §7.7 item 12's key law with housing records set aside for DR7 by their @housing row; CLASS LOOKUP CHAIN (DR24): (a) renamedFrom -> kinds row of the slug of its CURRENT name; (b) else its kind (catalogue key) -> its kinds row; (c) else the slug of its name as a catalogue key; (d) else the tags rung (C8-33): tags mapping through tags to exactly one family whose generic class exists -> that class, noted unmapped_kind with rung tags; (e) else its category's generic class, noted unmapped_kind — for (d), (e) the note written after the fold, its class the class building the record at the document's rung (§4.6; §3.6 (4); at a village rung V07 §3.11 step 4's tag fallback; SR4-07); (f) a CUSTOM record's class and profile NOT decided at digest (SS-12; J-VI.20): (b)-(e) do not run; the digest carries inputs (custom scene tokens, group, keyword keys; tags; category; admitted custom-def fact) and item 104 (a)'s resolution with V11 §3.13.1's rungs (author's map declaration for its localUid, archetype, category, tags, definition fields, keywords with their class cell, then generic-other) decides at fold; custom_resolved written after that fold naming the deciding rung; a pseudo-class kinds row routes the record to its reader with no roster class (@absent to S2, SS-10); a catalogue record's siting-profile family = kinds row family when set, else tags families (item 103 (a); combination rule in §10.2), else its generic class's own; political role carried as given (DR12, J-V8.45).

digest step (6) powers, notables, circumstances, economy: standings = power / sum power rounded to 1/10 000; controlled list via the line's stable part (§7.7 item 12); relations from powerStructure.factionRelationships one per unordered pair with type and direction words (relations row at the put); notables' workplace and power resolved by name (absent, noted name_unjoined); deposits; every listed condition whatever its status; stressors normalised (stressors, else stress, one object or list: each {type} a condition cond:stress:<type>, source stressor, severity 0.5, no weeks; C8-09); quarters; government and security; economy: each activeChains[] into economy.chains (resource joined to a listed deposit by resourceKey, processors by the name rule, outputs via goodWords, upstreamChains as chain:cat: keys, status via chainStatus; C8-06); tradeDependencies into economy.dependencies (institution by name, severity via dependencySeverity); primaryExports, primaryImports with necessityImports, transit into economy.goods via goodWords; calamities keyed calamity:<tick>:<slug(name)>, severity by calamitySeverity over deaths and population at its week (latest populationHistory at or before, else current), targets by name (C8-09); sea threats by threats row; ruin evidence by ruinEvidence row; latitude by DR-V8.1; never-read keys dropped into ignored (§7.7 item 1); severities round to 1/1 000 and percentages to 1/100 (J-V8.17). Name resolution (chain processors, dependency institutions, calamity targets; C8-06 (3)): exact name -> key; else KIND FAMILY (names with count range and qualifiers removed, case-folded, last word's plural folded to singular: -ies -> -y, -es after s, x, z, ch, sh, else final -s) -> the one record of that family (several: first in dossier order, noted name_ambiguous); else unjoined, kept by name, noted chain_node_unjoined (research mapping row 46: 2 585 of 3 381 processor names join exactly; kind family measured by T-V8-34); goods words by V11 §3.13.5 matching; no match noted unmapped_good (SR1-26). (7) custom content: §3.13's steps. (8) ladder merges: §3.5.1 (c). (9) seed: settlement.seed = H32('plat:sf-seed' || _seed) (§14 item 2); _seed and _config go no further.

The diff (absorb's first step): carried facts vs the new digest under the same keys, key by key in code-point order, skipping every quarantined key (C8-12; a quarantine without a formable key holds every carried institution key absent from the new digest, one quarantine_hold note). Per kind (key only new / only carried / fields compared -> op): settlement: —; — (a different settlement key refuses, E_OTHER_SETTLEMENT); population -> population; tierWord -> tier (F8); name -> rename (title only). institution: add (F1); under a key carried as removed or ruined -> reopen (F6); a greater whose lesser is carried -> add, the lesser's members re-bound as the greater's where the greater's thing is the lesser's, else the greater placed new and the lesser's key bound as at a first reading (§3.5.1 (c), (d); SR5-01) / remove with fate vanished (SF never deletes, research V48) unless a ladder promotion re-binds it or a quarantine holds it / state, fate, inactive -> state (F2, F3, F5 by item 14, fates first); impairments -> state (F4); name with a demotion or upgrade receipt -> rename + class re-read (F15, F3), an upgrade to a REPLACEMENT greater of a new thing places it new under the key and re-points the key's row (SR5-01); kind, category, tags, role, step, lesserOf, popQualifier, openTop -> attr (re-designation, item 18); count -> attr (members added or removed); knownTo, facets -> attr (§7.7 item 7). power: add / remove / standing, governing, controlled -> power (epoch data); name with rename-faction -> rename (relation keys re-keyed); category -> attr. relation: add -> PowerRelation put / remove -> retire / kind, trend, sign, strength, hidden -> attr. notable: add -> Person put; a reroll's new key whose name and role equal a vanished key's -> rename (re-bound) / remove -> retire / role, institution, power, status -> attr; replaced naming a carried notable -> rename (successor re-bound, F17). condition: add -> ConditionOverlay put / remove -> retire at its week / severity, severityBand, status, untilWeek -> state. resource: add -> DepositSite put / remove -> state removed / state -> state (F13). quarter: add -> naming claim (§7.7 item 16) / remove -> unassign / phrase, landmarks -> attr. government: name -> attr (kind by government table; F11), governingPower -> power. trade: partners, links, relationships, goods -> attr (F14); income shares -> attr. port-values: any field -> attr riding the next epoch's slice. deity: key, name -> attr (F16). chain: add / remove / any field -> attr, response epoch (no map event; web re-derives links at next epoch; DR-V8.5; V06 dossier phase). dependency: as chain. calamity: add -> event in the epoch covering its week (DR-V8.6, §3.6 (3)) / nothing (a calamity leaving the capped history list never undone; J-V8.54) / none (immutable). evidence: kinds -> attr, response epoch (V04 re-evaluates at next epoch). institution custom part: custom.contentHash -> attr cause custom_revision (item 104 (e)); custom.scene, .group, .keywords, .required -> attr. custom-chain: add -> CustomChainRecord put / remove -> retired / active -> state (item 104 (h)(7)); nodes, exports, imports -> attr. custom-service: add -> put / remove -> retire / provider, serviceCategory -> attr. custom-def: add / kept when the offer carries no library; remove (response none, noted custom_library_dropped) when its definition's revision changed and no admitted entry for the new revision came (§3.13 (8)) / any field -> attr cause custom_library only when the entry's revision equals the dossier's. Equal after rounding -> no change; a change affecting no rule (a notable's importance) still updates carried via the ledger event and report, no map event.

Chains' links (item 105 (i); DR-V8.5; C8-06): SF's chains become links of item 105's supply web between bound members, DERIVED at every placement and epoch by the base web (item 105 (a): never stored) from carried chain and dependency facts; the port stores only facts. DR-V8.5: map fact = supply links between the chains' bound members, goods and weights; inputs economy.chains (processors resolved, outputs via goodWords, upstream, neutral status), economy.dependencies, economy.goods, entrepot; rule item 105 (a)-(h)'s web at S10a/S10b and every epoch, each link x V11's siting.web.chainStatus of its chain's status; an entrepot chain's ends item 104 (b)'s import and export pulls via the store at the gate or quay facing the partner; no chance; bar: every chain with two joined members yields a link, an impaired chain's pull = status factor x a running one's, an entrepot end pulls toward the gate or quay facing its partner (T-V8-35). A processor joining nothing binds nothing and never invents a building, reported chain_node_unjoined. Coverage pull inside a collective range (item 103 (f); BCR-V8-12): DR9 draws a collective record's placed count inside the dossier's range from S2's per-capita rows; where the class carries a coverage row the coverage target (clamped into the range) is a weighted option beside the per-capita value; range = dossier fact, count inside = map fact (J-V8.20).

DR-V8.1 latitude row (item 102; BCR-V8-11; 'numbered by the coherence pass: V01, V05, V06 and V08 each propose a row'): map fact = the site latitude the model-side sun reads (item 102 (a)); inputs the realm block's cell.latDeg (optional), site.culture via tables/dossier/cultures, else 50 deg N; rule: the port writes it into Intent.latitudeDeg at creation (BCR-V8-11); a later or changed latitude is a port-values change carried into the next epoch's slice (PortValues.latitudeDeg); V05's model sampler reads the latitude in force (§2.5 resolution rule); §8.4's path mode reads it for views; no chance; bar: a dossier map's population-weighted mean band within one band of its wealth row with the sun term on (T73-7 unchanged; T-V8-22). SF usually places a settlement on its realm map after generating it (C-9), so a map is created with the culture's latitude and receives the realm's later (C8-21); the later value enters at the next epoch and item 102 (e)'s drift moves field and uses by the engine's lag (J-V8.34 revised); a DM sets it now by adjust (§7.1) with its own fate report; a document made before Intent.latitudeDeg existed reads 50 deg (§7.5 migration default).

Name grammar (the base's T9 extended, BCR-V8-5; in order): (1) (lo-hi+) -> count [lo, hi], openTop true (members may exceed hi up to V11's per-kind-and-rung cap, reported; Parish churches (50-100+)); (2) (lo-hi) -> count [lo, hi] (Taverns (5-20)); (3) (n+ only) -> popQualifier n (a population floor kept in the label, never a count; Cathedral (10,000+ only)); (4) every other parenthesised group -> its case-folded words appended to qualifiers ((guild), (red light district), (divine, 1st level)); digits may carry thousands separators; kindLabel = name with groups 1 and 2 removed and trimmed; a housing-stock record is told by its @housing kinds row, not the grammar.

Step type: V11's dossier.ladders row for the record's kind (catalogId, else name slug) gives step and lesser; with no row the qualifiers row over the record's qualifiers in order (first with a step); none with a count range -> COUNT; else no step. An unnumbered COUNT, QUARTER or GUILD record takes V11's range column (range at the kind's lowest tier) x its rungScale only at rungs above that tier (V11 §3.12); at a village rung (THORP, HAMLET, VILLAGE) an unnumbered record takes V07 §2.4's range row for its step type and member class (village.json rules.ladders.ranges keyed by step type with the qualifier as label; V07 SR1-16, J-V7.105), else V11's range unscaled (SS-08); a kind whose qualifier names a step V11's table lacks is noted ladder_unknown; a record whose kind is a greater of the committed ladderPairs the catalogue does not list is read as a plain record, noted uncatalogued_step (V11 §3.12).

No double counting (item 108 (c)): where a greater and a lesser of one ladder row are both in the dossier, the lesser gets mergedInto = the greater's key: not placed on its own, its range not added, the roster's per-capita members of that class ARE the greater's members, its binding key an alias row on the greater's member #1 (SIZE and REPLACEMENT: the greater's building — save a pin-record lesser, which V11 §3.12's row keeps as a pin of the greater's plot: parish_church over wayside_shrine binds the shrine's key to the churchyard cross, laid by V07 §3.10's pin-record rule at a village rung (VS8 at generation, village.records at an epoch or absorb; V07 §2.4, §3.10, §3.12 item 4; SR4-01, SR5-01), while at a base rung (no churchyard cross laid) it aliases the church building; the target chosen where the merge is first read — creation, or the absorb or epoch bringing the pair — and kept across a later rung change (§3.10; SR4-06; J-V8.111)), noted ladder_merged. A pair meeting over time (SR5-01; J-V8.113), lesser already placed and greater arriving beside it: (1) greater's thing is the lesser's (every COUNT, QUARTER, GUILD, SIZE, and REPLACEMENT rows keeping the lesser's thing: graveyard over burial_ground (face re-bound), wizard_s_tower over hedge_wizard (house becomes the tower), mages_guild over wizard_s_tower (tower binds the guild's hall), professional_city_watch over town_watch (posts carry on), cathedral_10_000_only over parish_church (church converted in place with its crypt, V6 §3.9.11)): lesser's placed members re-bound as the greater's #1..#n (nearest its demand first; a rebind each, no address change), DR9 adds members up to the greater's count by least disruption, nothing closes; (2) a lesser with no thing of its own (@none or @office: citizen_militia, traveling_performers, traveling_hedge_wizard, gates_if_walled, priest_resident): greater placed as any added record, lesser's key an alias row on member #1; (3) every other REPLACEMENT greater is a new thing placed new in the absorb or epoch bringing it (a building by DR9, an assign of its member (§3.6 (5)), at a village rung via V07's records placement item 4; a @wall greater by the fortification's dossier path (DR2 walls; V6 §3.7.6 (4); at a village rung V07 §3.11's palisade REPLACEMENT)), the lesser's key binding as at a first reading, its row re-pointed by one rebind (fold re-points, §3.6 (5)), noted ladder_merged (ladder_promoted under (d)): (i) a building lesser (fish_market over fishmonger): alias row on the greater's building (village: rim hall, V07 §3.12 (b)), the shop keeping its use unbound; (ii) a pin-record lesser: at a village rung the churchyard cross laid in that batch after the church, at a base rung an alias row on the church, the lesser's former pin standing unbound (a pin lesser whose row keeps no pin — wayside_shrine under cathedral_10_000_only — takes an alias row on the greater's building); (iii) a @wall lesser (town_walls over palisade or palisade_or_earthworks and the wall rows above): alias row on the enceinte the fortification path yields; the superseded ring keeps no binding.

Guild halls (V11 §3.12; SS-23; J-V8.83): a GUILD record's hall binds as one member #k of a craft_guilds_* COUNT record (categories family craft) or merchant_guilds_* COUNT record (family trade) in the same dossier, noted ladder_merged: the GUILD records of that family take members #1..#m in dossier order; the COUNT record's placed count = max(DR9's draw, m), above its range's top only when the GUILD records alone exceed it (noted count_over_range); no further hall; at an absorb a hall already placed is re-bound as #k (rebind, no address change), never duplicated; a COUNT record leaving the list releases its bound halls back to their GUILD records (a rebind each), so no hall closes by a change of wording; a GUILD record of another family, or with no such COUNT record, keeps its own hall; fixtures' cases: the three metropolises' two church ranges and metropolis-3's two cathedral records (§2.6a (3)).

Steps over time (item 108 (d)): a promotedFrom receipt (upgraded_by_reconstruction) keeps the record's one key (§7.7 item 12's F15 re-binding; the line keeps the old kind's catalogId); greater's thing is the lesser's ((c) first case): re-keys the singular record's binding row to the greater's #1 (rebind), DR9 adds the rest inside the new range by least disruption; greater a new thing ((c) third case; SR5-01; J-V8.114): placed new under the record's key (village: V07 §3.12 item 4) and the binding row re-pointed from the lesser's former thing to it (rebind); one key binds one thing (J-V8.111), the former thing left standing unbound (fishmonger's shop keeps its use; roadside shrine standing; a palisade the new ring superseded decaying by its persistence rows); a pin the row keeps (churchyard cross of parish_church over wayside_shrine at a village rung) laid in that batch by V07 §3.10's pin-record rule for the record, keyed by its binding key and provenance the record, with no binding row of its own; a lesser leaving the list in the same absorb that adds its greater with no receipt is read the same way (promotion, ladder_promoted, never removal plus addition). A demotedFrom receipt (demoted_by_disaster) keeps the member nearest its demand as the singular record (re-bound) and closes the rest by the receipt's fate (F2; a calamity's ruins stand as ruins); a burial record's demotion or promotion follows the same rules (no burial face closes by wording; §2.6a (4)). Custom content (item 108 (e)): a custom record whose admitted library entry lists subsumes is SIZE when the subsumed kinds belong to another V11 family, GUILD when a craft of its own family, SIZE when unknown; its lesser = subsumed kinds, merged by (c).

Re-check against the ladder file (CONFIRMED; C8-07 (2)): SF's ladder data at the pinned commit (src/data/institutionLadders.js at 5d699cc68, blob 91f6e2bd..., read as data, nothing copied) compared with V11 §3.12's rows: agreements (every row V11 marks ladder or subsumption); rows V11 marked inferred that the file holds (craft_guilds_100_150, merchant_guilds_50_100, banking_houses, banking_district with pawnbroker, gambling_halls, gambling_district, multiple_criminal_factions, multiple_adventurers_guilds with hireling_hall, slave_market_district, carriers_guild, cartographer_s_guild, large_prison, mages_district with mages_guild, alchemist_shop, alchemist_quarter, thieves_guild_powerful with black_market_bazaar and contract_killer, mint_official with assay_office, international_trade_center over caravan_masters_exchange and caravaneer_s_post); disagreements (hospital_network's lessers are almshouse and foundling_home; dungeon_delving_supply_district's lesser is bowyers_fletchers_guild); pairs the file holds that V11 lacked (wayside shrine -> parish church; water source -> multiple water sources; traveling performers -> theaters; hedge wizard and traveling hedge wizard -> wizard's tower; wizard's tower -> mages' guild; carriers' guild -> caravan masters' exchange; academy of magic, assassins' guild, auction house, gladiatorial school, printing house, great library, major port, specialized metalworkers, caravaneer's post, chroniclers' exchange, whisper market, black market, thieves' guild chapter over their named lessers; major hospital over almshouse); rows V11 infers that the file lacks (parish_churches_50_100, multiple_monasteries, major_monasteries_5_10, great_cathedral, burial_grounds_and_charnel_house, ...) stay inferred (dossiers list both forms); every fix a table change handed to revise-V11 (X1), reported by R2 when a baseline moves. (V11 now carries hospital_network COUNT over almshouse, foundling_home and dungeon_delving_supply_district QUARTER over bowyers_fletchers_guild: X1 landed.)

Changes to events (1) Dating: each change reads its receipt row (§7.7 item 13): the first receipt present gives cause, fate and week by §4.11's rungs; HostContext.week the last rung; no rung -> week null and an unreceipted_change note; V08's kinds dated by rows F-V8-1..F-V8-7 of tables/dossier/receipts (BCR-V8-20): a relation by its powers' pulse week when stamped, else arrival; port-values by arrival riding the next epoch; a custom definition by arrival; a chain (custom or SF's) by arrival; a dependency by arrival; a calamity by its own tick (a receipt); the evidence singleton by arrival riding the next epoch. (2) Order: by week (null last), then decrees before other sources, then the dossier's own record order, then binding key. (3) Epochs by the cadence (§4.11 (4); C8-31; J-V8.55): from the last epoch's week W0 (its EpochRecord, else creation week) to the absorb's week W1 (latest dated week, else HostContext.week, else W0): an epoch at every calendar year end W with W mod 52 = 0 in (W0, W1] (sf445 calendar); an epoch at the first week the population leaves the last epoch's populationTarget ±5 % (from populationHistory; with none at W1 when outside), the reference moving to that epoch's target so every crossing adds its own epoch; an epoch at the week of each newly carried calamity no other epoch falls on; each epoch's populationTarget = population at its week (latest populationHistory at or before, else linear between W0's target and W1's population, rounded to a person); circumstances = the new digest's slices (trade, economy, powers, government, port): SF keeps no interior history (V52, V56), every catch-up epoch reads the end state, declared (J-V8.25). Calamities (DR-V8.6 = V06's DR-V6.1, the same row: V06 the reader, V08 the inputs): each newly carried calamity is one entry {week, kind 'calamity', calamity: CalamityRef} in EpochInputs.events of the epoch at its week, CalamityRef = {id: its key, name, type, severity, targets: use ids of resolved bound targets, deaths} (deaths for V04's burial growth; X3); its F5 targets' dossier events at the same week ride the same epoch's EpochInputs.dossier so V06's hazard phase strikes them in place; an unjoined target dropped, noted calamity_unplaced; the calamity-to-hazard mapping is V06's table (J-V6.70).

(4) Ledger event (J-V8.14; C8-12, C8-13): the absorb's first event is one dossierFacts {changes, quarantined, notes, notesCleared} (BCR-V8-6): every DossierChange with full before and after carried facts and the WHOLE quarantine list after this absorb, author host, no model effect; folding sets carried[key] = after per change, DossierBinding.quarantined to the list, appends {seq, week W1, factHash, changeIds} to absorbed and removes changeIds older than the newest 64 (the dossier block rebuilt from the log by folding these events alone, equal to the stored block at every seq, §2.9); creation's prefix opens with the same event, every fact an add. Port's notes (SS-44; J-V8.98): notes holds in order this run's event-class notes and those standing notes whose identity DossierBinding.notes does not hold; notesCleared the identities of standing notes this run no longer writes; report-class notes never enter the log; folding sets DossierBinding.notes to the old list less notesCleared plus the standing notes of notes, identity order; no model rule reads either. custom_resolved and low_confidence notes of custom records added or revised are written after the dry run's fold and appended to notes before encoding (dry run's result stands; every editor's re-run computes the same bytes); they are event notes (live resolution is the why card's, V10 WhyAnswer.profile, V9 §2.7 chips). Every unmapped_kind note (standing) likewise written after the fold (dry run's at absorb, generate's at creation, loaded state for unchanged), its class the class building the record there (SR4-07; J-V8.112), before notes and notesCleared are computed, so a note whose built class changed at a rung change is cleared and written anew at the next port run. An unchanged digest writes no event; its notes reach the host's report only.

(5) Emission by receipt row response: assign -> assign of a dossier-backed assignment (§7.7 One path: S10b's dossier request, least-disruption order; at a rung of a product declaring a records placement that placement first, V6 §2.1 ProductDeclEpoch.records, V07 §3.12; SR5-06); unassign -> unassign; status -> setAttr of the assignment's state (and memberState for a collective by DR25); setAttr -> setAttr of the named path (re-designation mutates by §4.7 S11); rebind -> setAttr of the bound entity's dossier ref to the new key (fold re-points the binding row; no address changes, §6.3; BCR-V8-8), also for a ladder promotion, a relation re-keyed with its power and a notable re-bound after a reroll; a staged record -> dossierRecord (stressors' overlays among them); a count change -> assign of added members as dispersed additions or setAttr of memberState removed on the members DR25 picks (siting keyed by the assignment and the event's seq); epoch and every slice-level change (port-values, a chain, a dependency, the evidence singleton) -> the epoch of (3); a calamity -> (3)'s event; none -> nothing beyond the ledger; each emitted event carries its DossierChange in EditBase.dossierChange and the binding key in EditBase.dossier (§7.1). (6) Placement in the log; the session: element events fold as standalone events at their week between the epochs of (3); one dated exactly at an epoch's week rides that epoch's EpochInputs.dossier (§7.7 item 6); undated ones follow the last epoch, applied finished (no Works); all take seq from nextSeq in this order, author host, reserved session host:port, never a user's session, no group (C8-15; BCR-V8-19); envelope session the same (§11.3 Logging).

Refusals at absorb: a digest whose population routes outside the base ladder with no registered product (§3.10) refuses the whole absorb (§7.7 item 15), as does E_OTHER_SETTLEMENT; nothing emitted, map held (§3.9). Deserted settlement (SS-21): with the village product registered, a population of 0 at an ABSORB routes to THORP and V07's desertion (V07 §2.1, §3.12; an outcome, never a refusal): a village-product document runs it at the epoch directly, a base-product document reaches it through V07 §2.1's fold, 0 below the band's lower edge (J-V8.85); at a CREATION population 0 refused E_RUNG_UNAVAILABLE naming the floor (V07 §2.1); with no village product registered 0 is held like any population below 1 500 (B7).

Persistence (C8-04; J-V8.46): every encoded event, seq, head and snapshot field the store holds arrives in a message (doc.changed and dossier.result carry encoded, seqAfter, logHeadAfter; dossier.result.created and doc.snapshot.ready carry the whole SnapshotBlock); the host verifies only that a proposal's baseLogHead equals its head, stores the rest as handed, never decodes a byte, hashes an event or computes a head (T-V8-5 against a store that cannot). Commit: every committed event (user edit, absorb events, undo) appended via MapStore.commitEvents; stale -> doc.rejected {stale} (§11.3); an absorb's commit also writes absorbed and lastOffer in the same compare-and-set. Compaction (J-V8.5; C8-05, C8-29): when the tail passes 256 events or 256 KB, and at every created, upgrade and rebase, the committing editing client sends doc.snapshot and calls MapStore.replaceSnapshot with the reply's SnapshotBlock; precondition: snapshot logHead is the record's head or the logHeadAfter of an event in its tail (an edit committed meanwhile does not refuse it); the store keeps the tail's suffix, moves the old snapshot to backups[0] with the removed segment as tailAfter (C8-27), keeps backups[1] without its segment, drops older ones, one transaction; a snapshot whose head is in neither place is stale (restore or new map replaced the log) and discarded, the next commit's threshold check retries; the snapshot's canonical bytes include the whole log (§2.9) so nothing is lost; doc.snapshot is an editing role's message, not an export (E_HOST_FORMAT n/a). Load: snapshot plus tail replays exactly (T-V8-5).

Thumbnails: after each committed absorb and each compaction the committing client (or refresh queue) requests two 512-px PNGs — public key (anonymous and gallery fallback; exportPicture knowledge {tier public, places []}, J-V8.92) and secret (DM's; no knowledge) — at the city band with the document's style and a fixed sun (§11.1), stored with putThumbnails; shown before the frame is ready and after a failed boot; players' pictures are §3.14's party set. Backups and restore (J-V8.44; C8-28): backups hold the two previous snapshots; 'restore previous map' (§4.2) refuses a backup whose docId differs from mapId; else makes backups[0] the snapshot with an empty tail (swapped-out snapshot becoming backups[0]), then every open session gets a fresh doc.load (module.status {loading} between); the next offer absorbs the current dossier forward (dossier stays the truth; only the map's own edits since that snapshot lost; the dialog lists them). Local draft mirror (V09's; C8-35): in host mode only a draft mirror in the module origin's storage keyed by document id (V09 §3.8 (6)): unsent edits of a session, replayed at load only when its base head is the record's head or an event's logHeadAfter in the loaded tail, else discarded with 'unsaved changes from an earlier version of this map were dropped'; the mirror persists inside SF's page only when the module origin is same-site with SF's app ('Q1's recommendation (a subdomain of SettlementForge's own domain) meets it'); on another site it lives for the session only. Sizes (host quota per map): snapshot within §2.9's budget (TOWN <= 0.6 MB, CITY <= 3 MB, METROPOLIS <= 8 MB), tail <= 256 KB between compactions, two backups (newer with one tail segment <= 256 KB), two thumbnails <= 150 KB each, party set (§6: <= 2, 6, 12 MB); at CITY <= 15.9 MB worst case, typically about 8 MB.

Versions (ours): output version (§6.4): a stored document inside the retention window replays exactly under its own version; the owner's client gets module.status {upgrade-available} and the upgrade dialog with §7.5's diff; an accepted upgrade is an ordinary event over the bridge, compacted at once; players' pictures keep the stored version's drawing until the DM upgrades (J-V8.22); the owner's 'Update the map engine' action (§4.2) is the host's upgrade request V06 names for a document whose epochs carried dossier events (V6 §3.15), never upgraded by anything else; outside the window the document opens as §2.9's frozen view for everyone, the owner offered frozenImport rebase by V9 §3.14 (b)'s 'Edit it with this version', committed through doc.changed, then the client sends doc.snapshot (XV-V9-24); schema version: a newer document opens read-only (§2.9 step 1), an older module serving a newer document is a deployment error reported in module.status {error}; dossier row sets: absorb reads tables/dossier/* at the DOCUMENT's pinned versions (§2.9 tablePins), a new table version reaches a document only through upgrade. SF's side: a dossier carries schemaVersion, simulationVersion, generatorVersion; the same seed gives different dossiers on two lines at one generatorVersion, so the LINE names an adapter; the port never re-generates a dossier or reads SF code; SF's internal migrations reach the map only as a changed dossier shape.

New adapter version on the same line: at the next absorb, when binding.adapter.version differs from the running adapter's, the port first RE-BASELINES: per carried key, a difference confined to fields the new manifest's remaps list for that fromVersion is recorded in the ledger event with cause {kind adapter_remap} and response none (no map event), noted adapter_remap; every other difference is a real change absorbed as usual (J-V8.10); an adapter version changing a field's meaning without listing it fails T-V8-10 on the re-cut fixtures. New SF line (§14 item 1): one new adapter folder with its manifest; fixtures re-cut by the same scripts; fromLines declares how an older line's binding keys map (identity when the key law is unchanged); a document bound to line A receiving a dossier the registry gives to line B: B's fromLines entry for A re-keys the binding rows (a rebind setAttr per changed key, no address changes), binding.adapter becomes B's, line_migrated noted, absorb proceeds by the re-baseline with B's remaps for A; no fromLines entry for A -> E_LINE_UNSUPPORTED, held (J-V8.11). Release of a line: §8.3's checklist runs creation and absorb bars on the new line's fixtures, the cross-line migration on the old line's pairs, T-V8-10 and T-V8-11.

Failure handling (no failure discards or re-rolls a stored map, §5): a held map shows its last committed state with host.status.held and its reason row (the refusal's held note msg, a host.held.* row, stored as MapRecord.held.reason), status held, every later dossier a retry; words written once (host.held.*, host.recovered.*, host.verify.* here; host.status.*, host.party.* in §5.1; host.note.* in §4.6; SS-44); a refusal at CREATION shows host.status.notCreated and the reason row in the thumbnail slot; E_RUNG_UNAVAILABLE's row by case: .village below the floor with no village product registered, .cap above 120 000 ({cap}), .empty a creation at population 0. Rows: B1 frame does not start (no ready within 20 s): re-create once -> stored thumbnail with retry; host.status.failed. B2 no reply (replyTimeoutMs): re-create frame and re-load -> thumbnail on second miss; host.status.stopped. B3 too big, too deep or not the line's shape (§3.5 steps 2-3): refuse E_UNKNOWN_SHAPE -> held; host.held.E_UNKNOWN_SHAPE 'The settlement's record could not be read.' (size_limit note in the host's report). B4 one malformed record (step 4): quarantine, absorb the rest; quarantined element keeps its last carried state (at creation not placed), retried every offer; host.note.quarantined_record. B5 no registered adapter accepts or the named line refuses (select): E_LINE_UNSUPPORTED naming candidates -> held (several accepting = B19); host.held.E_LINE_UNSUPPORTED 'This SettlementForge version is not supported by the map yet.' B6 another settlement's dossier: E_OTHER_SETTLEMENT -> held (catches a host bug); 'This record belongs to another settlement.' B7 population leaves the base ladder with no product (router §3.10): E_RUNG_UNAVAILABLE naming village product or cap -> held (creation: no map, thumbnail slot says why); with the village product registered 0 at an absorb routes to THORP and V07's desertion, at creation 0 refused naming the floor (V07 §2.1; §3.6 (7); SS-21); texts .village 'Villages are drawn by the village map, which is coming later.', .cap 'Settlements of more than {cap} people are larger than the map draws.', .empty 'The settlement's record lists no inhabitants.' B8 head moved under an absorb (doc.rejected stale): re-run absorb three times -> module.status {error}, retried next offer; nothing or host.status.absorbing. B9 store compare-and-set fails: reload, re-apply as B8.

Failure rows cont.: B10 snapshot damaged or root mismatch (§2.9 step 3): §2.9's corrupt-cache replay from recipe and log -> if undecodable, backups[0] plus its tailAfter segment plus the current tail (exact) -> backups[1] absorbing forward, map edits since it lost and listed -> a new map from the current dossier, reported; module.status.detail beside ready: rungs 1-2 host.recovered.rebuilt 'The saved copy was damaged and has been rebuilt.'; rung 3 host.recovered.lost 'The saved copy was damaged and rebuilt from an older one; {n} of the map's changes were lost.' (lost edits listed in the report, V9 §5.7); rung 4 as B11. B11 map record gone (the host detects a mapId its store no longer holds; else it simply has none and makes one): a NEW map from the current dossier under a new mapId, one creation of the current state (§7.7 One path; item 22 (c) allows it to differ); old layout not recoverable (J-V8.43); host.recovered.newMap 'The saved map was lost, so a new one was made from the settlement's current record.' B12 absorb over its disruption budget (draft reroll, J-M11; §7.7 item 5 dry run): least-disruptive sites, reported over budget; the disruption report. B13 host restored an earlier dossier (factHash equals an earlier absorbed entry): F22 forward convergence (§7.7 item 5); host.note.state_matches_absorbed with the residue. B14 upgrade cannot copy a pack (§7.5 cap): keep the old model; upgrade dialog's message. B15 settlement deleted in SF: host deletes the map record; nothing in the module. B16 hostile string in a name: never executed (text rendering; every export escapes, §11.1 inert bar). B17 quarantined record whose key cannot be formed: every carried institution key absent from the new digest held (no remove), quarantine_hold, until readable (C8-12). B18 party pictures missing or older than the map: the viewer shows what is stored captioned with its week; the next editing session or refresh sends party.render (new set or unchanged); host.party.notOpened or host.party.asOf. B19 two adapters accept a new settlement's dossier, no line named: newest registered line, recorded, line_defaulted. B20 an editor's re-run differs (§3.3 verification): the applied log stands, mismatch reported with the first differing event (C8-37); module.status.detail beside error, editors only: host.verify.mismatch 'A map update did not match when it was checked; it has been reported.'

Village-tier hand-off: LadderRouter.route(population) (§1.1) is the one decision of which product builds a population; the village product registers its ProductDecl in StrategyRegistry.products (V07 §2.1; BCR-V7-11), the one registration of file f item 202; the port registers nothing and consults LadderRouter: at creation which product and rung build the population, at every absorb only whether the population lies in a registered range (SS-19, SS-28); the product's rungs, range, stages, strategies are V07's (not restated). With no village product registered, a population below 1 500 is refused (§7.7 item 15) and a mapped town shrinking below 1 500 is held at its last state (B7) until the population returns above 1 500 (then the next absorb diffs everything since in one pass). With it registered: a village-sized dossier is created on the village rung rows (V07 §3.11); a crossing is §4.11's rung change as BCR-V7-26 states it (the product at an epoch is V07 §2.1's fold with handoff.band: town to village and village to base only when an epoch's target leaves the band; inside it the previous product runs on its own rung row; SS-20); everything the epoch builds follows that product's stages; standing fabric survives (§6.3); population 0 at an absorb is V07's desertion (SS-21); one document, one seed, one history across both products (J-V8.12); V07 owns what the village builds and its fold; V08 owns the port's consultation and the one-document rule, tested by T-V8-19 with a test ProductDecl.

Staged records from the digest: Conditions and stressors (C8-09, C8-10 (c)): each digest condition put as a ConditionOverlay (cond:<id>; archetype, severity, sinceWeek, untilWeek) whatever its status (stable, worsening, easing; only live conditions listed); weeks from ticks: W = HostContext.week, else the latest tick of populationHistory, else 0 at creation; sinceWeek = round(W − duration.elapsedTicks); untilWeek = round(W + duration.expiresAtTicks − duration.elapsedTicks) (reading expiresAtTicks as the whole length; PLAUSIBLE: a generated condition carries elapsedTicks 3.25, expiresAtTicks 6 at tick 0); measurement: untilWeek within ±1 week across town-1's and city-1's one-week, one-season, one-year ticks (T-V8-18); pre-decided fallback if it drifts: untilWeek = expiresAtTicks read as an absolute tick; a condition no longer listed retired at the absorb's week; each stressor put under cond:stress:<type> (archetype its type, severity 0.5, sinceWeek its first absorb's week, no untilWeek), retired when no longer listed; effects by the conditions row (tint via §8.2's thematic rows, Works factors via DR21, activity scalars and dials at the next epoch); stressors add no EpochInputs.events entry (one path: the overlay; J-V8.56). Deposits (C8-18): each listed deposit put as a DepositSite (res:<key>; family by the deposits row, state); derived fields S12a's: reading the prefix's deposit puts ahead (BCR-V8-22) S12a draws the bearing on hinterland.outside keyed by the deposit key (realm block's bearing wins when given), writes bearingCdeg; the land use writes landUse (both derived, recomputed on regeneration, never in the event; DR19); a state change is a put at its week, converting the land use at the next epoch (§4.11); magical_node and ancient_ruins sites follow the deposits row and V04's ruinCentre(); a derived site res:derived:<landuse> by the same row (SR2-04).

Staged records cont.: Power relations (C8-10 (a)): each unordered pair put as a PowerRelation with the relations row's neutral kind, sign, strength x trend factor and hidden flag (BCR-V8-26 adds sign and hidden); §4.5's typing reads the prefix's relation puts ahead (BCR-V8-22) as a soft adjacency row (attraction positive, repulsion negative); item 72's political component reads them; a hidden relation never named on a public view (DR20). Notables: each put as a dossier-backed Person (npc:<id>) pinned whole, Posting at workplaceKey's element, Membership in powerKey's power, housed by §2.7's rule in the district of its institution or its power's seat (names joining nothing: governing power's seat district, noted name_unjoined); a successor (replaced names a carried notable) put with the old person's house and posting, old record retired (F17); dead or gone retired, the house stays a house; a reroll (C8-39; J-M11; F21's receipt): a vanished npc: key whose name and role equal a new key's is re-bound (rebind, noted npc_rebound) keeping house and posting; other vanished keys retired, the new put. History: at creation only Recipe.history = {ageYears: history.age, scars} (one scar per event by historyScars with yearsAgo and severity); never updated (ageYears never advanced by the host's weeks, §2.7); magical events to ruin evidence. Per-settlement values: PortValues (crime by crime row, importPct = foodImportPct / 100, foodChain = foodChains, legitimacy, threats by threats row, latitudeDeg null in the creation slice where Intent.latitudeDeg holds DR-V8.1's value; a later realm latitude fills it) in the creation slice and each epoch's slice.

Custom kinds (C8-17): the dossier's custom definitions are PortRows.customKinds rows DERIVED at read time: the table's rows (empty in the base) overlaid by one row per carried custom institution (kind = its definition id; no fallbackClass: the class is item 104 (a)'s resolution at fold, BCR-V11-26, J-VI.20; SS-37), and only from its carried custom-def fact (admitted library entry): economicWeight and criticality by the customWeights row (a dossier row set, not calibratable; J-V8.108), defenseRoles and powerAuthorities (the entry's defenseRole and authority) (BCR-V8-29); nothing written into the recipe's params (a revision changes them through its own setAttr's fold, no editTable, avoiding item 22's reshuffle). Realm block (J-V8.27; C8-21; BCR-V8-24): the client's realmBlockFrom(placements) computes host-side without module code from the campaign's placements (the settlement's and partners' realm positions), realm map scale and latitude scale, and the campaign's spatial digest (cell terrain, river, coast words) — nothing else of campaign state: each partner's bearingCdeg = round(100 x atan2(dx, −dy) in degrees) mod 36 000 (realm y grows southward), distanceM = hypot(dx, dy) x mPerRealmUnit, the cell, latDeg = degAtY0 − y x degPerUnitY when the latitude scale is given; used as §7.7 layer 2 states (true bearings, north first) and as DR-V8.1's first input; sent with an offer only when the settlement is placed on the realm. Audience in use: the client maps SF audience words via §14's table: DM's page mounts with dm (owner, secret), co-DM's with co-dm (editor, secret); a player's page never mounts a frame (party set and party gazetteer); anonymous, gallery and DM-full shares get picture exports only (§5.3); module takes the lower of told role and audience word (J-V8.29). Display names (J-V8.28): for a public picture the host computes with its own public-projection filter the veiled text of every name to veil and passes displayNames (binding key -> text) with that one export request; the module draws them for that export only (§11.1; T85-3 via the bridge, T-V8-16).
