Proposal cards (ProposalView): AI mark, reason line, active variation's counts, bends, fates, renames, findings, effects under What else changes as the fates sheet draws them (V9 §4.20.7), a removal's info.remove.holds line, variation chips with V10's labels and thumbnails (each its own preview); Accept (Enter) → accept; Accept these lines (roster) → acceptLines; Try again → retry; Drop → drop; Why → why card of what it makes; once accepted Undo and, on a removal no longer the latest group, Put it back (rebuild), each worded by its label; focusing a chip calls focus and draws its ghost (one proposal ghost at a time); a proposal whose town moved on shows refuse.stale with its buttons (Show the new preview = focus; Show me why) and Ask again (V10 §3.11; retry, clerk.alt.stale.retry). Refusals (RefusalView): card text and each action as a button worded by its label, a select without one as id chips.

Card-only drawer — a host's proposal (V10 §3.17; V08 §4.4 (3)): in host mode with clerkMode off or host the slot is kind host: no Assistant button, nothing sent to a model from the frame; a TurnView whose proposal has source 'host' arriving on turns (the harness takes it from ClerkMount.host.proposals) opens the drawer in card-only mode: that card alone (AI mark clerk.host.mark naming the host's assistant via HostSlots.hostName, reason, chips, counts, bends, fates, renames, findings, What else changes, Accept, Drop, Why) with no message box, prompts, first-opening cards, menu, settings or meter and no Try again; Accept → accept (V10 §4.2); Drop → drop; harness answers via ClerkMount.host.answer; drawer closes on either; a newer host proposal replaces the card; a moved town shows refuse.stale without Ask again; a viewer never receives one (§11.2 refuses a viewer's preview); with clerkMode builtin a host proposal is drawn in the full drawer as a turn with no user words (V10 §2.6).

Creation preview (V10 §3.11 (3), §5.1): while a creation proposal waits the map region shows the active variation's scratch document read-only (ClerkMount.showScratch) under a banner 'Preview — not your map yet' with variation chips, Accept and Back to my town; tools disabled; Accept follows V10 §4.2 (3): when the current town is the untouched empty-state town the view moves to the new town (old stays in Recent towns), otherwise the new document opens beside (openNewDocument: new tab and Recent entry) with a toast; host mode follows newDocuments though no creation proposal arises there. Meter: drawer foot 'This month: about ${usd} of ${cap}' from usage(); past V10's warnShare bend tone (clerk.cap.warn); at the cap clerk.cap.reached shows and the message box is disabled until the month turns or the cap is raised.

Asking why: the why card's Ask the assistant (hidden when no clerk enabled) sends on V10's why entry with the WhyAnswer attached and opens the drawer. Asking how and handing over a list (J-V9.89): How do I …? (drawer menu and Help, shown only when a clerk is configured and on) opens the drawer on V10's help entry (placeholder 'How do I …?'), send(question, 'help'); the answer's closing useTool action drawn as its button (clerk.alt.help.useTool) running by the dispatch (tool active with options strip); next message returns to the drawer entry; Ask the assistant to place these (under T7's paste box, clerk configured and on) sends on V10's roster entry with the text attached as roster, as Paste a list does, and opens the drawer; with no clerk or clerk off neither control shows.

Start a new map from this (J-SS2.4; J-V9.93): drawer menu, standalone only — puts the message box in creation mode for its next message: line clerk.newMap.line ('Describe the new town — this one stays as it is') above the box; send(text, 'drawer', {newMap: true}) which V10 §3.1 (4) reads as the user's choice of creation mode (XV-V9-22); proposal previews under the banner; Accept opens the new document beside the current (not the empty-state town); Esc or the item again returns to ordinary mode; after sending it returns by itself; in host mode the item is hidden and no turn enters creation mode (the frame's document is never the empty-state town; V10 §3.1 (4)'s first condition is standalone's).

Knowledge and roles: the session reads under the view's role and View as — the effective key from ClerkMount.effectiveKey; a viewer's drawer reads and asks why but receives no proposal (declarations answered by refuse.viewer, V10 §3.16); a change of the effective key clears the conversation by V10 §3.12 (6) (clerk.view.cleared). Apply-then-undo is V10 §4.4's setting (ClerkSettings.applyMode, off by default): applied card with clerk.applied and the other variations as chips; every case V10 §4.4 never applies arrives as a preview. Saving: Save these changes as a skeleton (edit mode the document's own skeleton, V10 §3.15; creation mode the transcript's skeleton, V10 §5.3); Copy conversation; export 'Assistant conversation (JSON)'; conversation kept as V10 §2.7 rules (memory by default, device store while 'Keep history' is on; J-V9.10 as amended by J-V9.34); What the assistant sees opens V10 §5.4's read-only view of what was sent.

Touch, pen and small screens (J-V9.9, confirmed by §13.4's first-five-minutes sessions; evidence research/ux/tool-survey.md §6): wide (≥ 1024 CSS px) and medium (600-1023 px and ≥ 480 px high) get every tool; narrow (< 600 px wide or < 480 px high) is a viewer with light edits: map, gazetteer and features in view, layers and thematic views, View as, history (restore and copy), T1, T5 (seed and click-inside only), T6, T7, T10, T11, T12 (style, tint, furniture, light), every export, share and the clerk drawer; T2, T3, T4, T8, warps and T9's geometry drags not offered (rail slots greyed with refuse.phone) while T9's Shape tab forms (storeys, roof, class) work; tables editor and advanced panel read-only lists on narrow.

Coarse-pointer gestures: tap = click; long press (500 ms, no movement beyond 8 px) = context menu; two-finger drag = pan; pinch = zoom; one-finger drag on empty map pans when no drawing tool is active, draws when one is; free placement (Alt) = a second finger held while the first draws; double-tap = zoom to the thing's band; modifier idioms (shift+click New random, ctrl/cmd+click reset, alt+click lock) are context-panel buttons; hit targets and handles ≥ 44 × 44 CSS px; snap radius 22 px; tooltips on a long press on a control. Hit stack by touch: a tap on the selected thing with more under it selects the next down, long-press menu lists Select below; on narrow a raised way, span, deck plot and stepped building can be selected, named (T11) and deleted with V9 §4.20.3's pending card, not drawn. Pen is a fine pointer, pressure not read (brush strength from its slider, replay device-independent), barrel button = right-click. Fallback (§13.4): if tablet participants fail where pointer users pass, AppPrefs.touch.editFabric defaults false for coarse pointers, hiding L3-L4 geometry edits (T8, T9 drags) and the guide says so. Cursor sun (§8.4): with no pointer hovering, the sheet's fixed sun (§1.2); on touch a one-finger drag with the Light chip held moves the sun (view input, never logged).

Keyboard: keymap.json (§14) keeps every base binding (A, B, D, N, L, T, M, W then 1-8 kernels, G, F, R, Esc, ctrl/cmd+Z, shift+Z, + / −, 0, ?) and adds (each also on a menu or button): 1-9 pick T1-T9 (outside a warp session; T10-T12 by the rail or their keys); alt+Enter toggles the selection's lock (T10); F2 renames (T11); S opens the dress panel (T12); Enter accepts the pending ghost or focused variation, else MFCG's idiom (empty state: new town replaces the untouched one; after a declaration Same kind, new seed opens a new document beside, toast names the town left in Recent); [ and ] cycle variations; Tab/shift+Tab cycle handles, arrows move the focused handle 1 m (shift 10 m), Enter commits; Delete/Backspace deletes the selection (previewed; at once only when nothing beyond changes, else pending card; dossier-backed → Not here, rejectSite); H history panel; E export dialog; ctrl/cmd+S downloads a copy of the .plat; ctrl/cmd+O opens a town; Space held pans; X opens the clerk drawer when configured; M base ruler; PageUp/PageDown step the underground band while Below is active (V04's BCR-10) and, while a T4 stroke is drawn on Ground, turn Raised on and off; Shift+F10 and Menu key open the context menu; bindings fire only with map focus (§14), a text field's focus suspends them; rebinding is an AppPrefs.keymapOverrides row.

Advanced panel: every parameter of §7.8's registry (≈ 200), grouped by consuming stage ('Site', 'Programme', 'Streets', 'Districts', 'Plots', 'Buildings', 'Greenery', 'Names', 'Look') with search; each row: label, value with unit, range, the layer that set it (§7.6: 'default', 'preset', 'your preferences', 'this town', 'SettlementForge'), locality badge ('changes nearby' local / 'rebuilds from {stage}'), help link; change = adjust; a Re-derive shows the fates sheet first with an auto restore point. Streets group row 'Raised ways the town builds by itself: as the rules say · none' (item 110 (b)): none = one editTable setting this document's rows of V11's raisedWays table to chance 0, previewed; dry run says offer.raised.standing with Remove them too (grouped delete of each generated one, each suppressed); 'as the rules say' deletes the override rows; row on medium and wide, read-only on narrow.

Tables editor: §7.6's rule tables by group; a table opens as a virtualised grid of keyed rows; cell editor typed by the schema (unit, range, enumeration); per cell provenance (source, date, note) and a chip 'as MFCG does', 'as FTG does' or 'ours' from provenance.source and the extension marker (item 23); edit = editTable previewed (re-derivations and, for the fallback, fates, §7.6); Reset row removes the override; orphans list overrides whose base row changed in a newer table version (old base, new base, user's value) with Keep mine / Take new; Export overrides writes row operations as JSON. Presets dialog: pick a preset (parity presets MFCG and FTG among them, §7.6); Save these settings as a preset = editPreset. 'Apply my current preferences' (§7.6) sends one adjust per changed parameter, grouped, with the fates sheet.

Accessibility beyond §14 (WCAG 2.2 AA chrome, landmarks, keyboard reach, gazetteer as non-visual route, contrast, reduced motion, 100-200 % scaling; T-V9-21 on every new screen): rail is a toolbar with roving tab stop, layer groups labelled groups, button accessible name '{tool}: {hint}'; options strip a toolbar with radiogroup chip sets; ghost spoken once per settled preview through a polite live region (AppPrefs.announcePreviews): 'Preview: temple quarter, 42 plots, 180 households, 38 buildings; 2 of your changes move. Enter to accept, Escape to cancel.' with the first three effects then 'and {n} other changes'; refusal card is a status never an alert; handles by keyboard a listbox ('Corner 3 of 6, 120 m east and 80 m north of the town centre'), arrows 1 m (shift 10 m), Enter commits; no trap (Tab past last handle leaves for the context panel, shift+Tab before first returns to the map region, Esc drops handle focus; T-V9-21 walks it).

Declaring in words: every points-form tool accepts places by name via V9 §4.16's reader — T5 'a temple quarter near the market' (seed at the market's anchor), T4 'a street from the north gate to the harbour', T3 'a wall from the castle to the river', T6 typed locus, T7 list — so every L0-L2 declaration is possible without the canvas; a named target's point is always its EntityCard.anchor (V10 §3.6 rule 1) read by query entity (BCR-V10-1); nothing else snapped (dry-run points-form derivation does the rest, §7.1; V10 §3.6 rule 7), canvas and clerk write the same bytes (T101-3; T-V9-13). Variations tray a radiogroup ('Version 2 of 3: 44 plots, 176 households'); fates sheet a table with headers and a Show per row. Never colour alone: tier chips carry words; link view draws each goods family with its own dash pattern (five patterns) besides colour; shade view steps read out under the pointer; snap highlight and handles keep ≥ 3 : 1 against paper and ink of every shipped sheet (T-V9-21 contrast step). Timing: toasts stay while hovered or focused; long press adjustable 300-1 000 ms (default 500); no action has a time limit.

Locus reader (one small deterministic reader of our own; connective words are parse.* catalogue rows so a locale supplies its own): (1) one place per non-empty line, leading bullet/number/dash dropped; (2) fields: first fitting split wins — 'name: class, locus'; 'name — class — locus' (also '-' or '–' with spaces); 'name (class) locus'; else the whole line is the name and the class guessed from its words ('The Golden Anvil smithy' → smithy); (3) class: words and word pairs matched against V11's label and synonyms cells of the classes the document's rung admits (fold's product and rung, V07 §2.1): base rung the town-and-city rows, V05's sky rows where a sky layer stands, generic rows; village rung the v. rows, town-and-city rows that play themselves there (no villageForm; V11 §3.22; V07 §3.11 step 3) and generic rows, a row with a villageForm answering through its v. row (J-V9.125); exact first, then plural ending removed, then within one letter for words ≥ 5 letters; ties by commonness within the set, a v. row before a town-and-city row at a village rung, then row order; no match → generic 'Other' and the card asks 'What is it?' with a class picker.

Locus reader (cont.): (4) 'in X' → in; 'on X' → on; 'at X' → at; 'near X', 'by X', 'beside X', 'next to X' → near; 'north/south/east/west (side) of X' → near with that side; a connective followed by 'the north/… side of X' keeps its rel and takes that side; X resolved by query({kind 'gazetteer', text: X}): exact name first, then best match whose kind fits a kind word in X ('gate', 'square', 'market', 'harbour', 'bridge'); 'the north gate' = the gate whose bearing from the town centre is nearest north; market and harbour name the principal market and harbour; unresolved X → card asks 'Where is {X}?' with pick-on-map; nothing guessed silently. (5) With a dossier each line must name a dossier element (§7.1's roster rule): the class field becomes an element picker of unplaced elements matching the name. (6) Wording a locus (J-V9.100): rel's connective (first word of parse.rel.<rel>: 'in', 'on', 'at', 'near'), with a side 'the {side} side of' (parse.side, parse.dir.<N/E/S/W>), then the target's name as gazetteer answers at the effective key; a withheld or unnamed target worded by its kind label after 'the' ('the gate'); e.g. 'near the North Gate', 'on the west side of the Market', 'in Tanners' Row'; (4) reads the worded form back to the same Locus for a named target (T-V9-13); readers: refuse.roster.dossier's {locus}, history 'Asked for {name} {locus}', V10's dossier row (V10 §3.16).

Underground records and rules are V04's (V4 §2.2, §3.5.0a, §3.5.1, §3.5.7) and the crypt V03's Basement.crypt (V03 §3.7.4); the panels' explanatory lines are the why rows: excavation reading, ways in, dwellings line, ruin rows, catacomb source, rank, count, entrance, state, burial-face outcome, crypt presence, form, rank and join are the matching rows of the underground and crypt sections of the subject's WhyAnswer (V10 §3.9a) drawn through WhyCardModel.sections with their catalogue keys — one sentence across panel, why card and clerk; the lines quoted in §4.17 name the row each place shows.

Hidden caves and ruins — GM view (item 109 (j)(2)): a cavern or ruin exists whole whether or not reachable; a cluster whose excavation reading is unexcavated (V4 §3.5.7 (g)) is known to nobody in town; the Below group's Show hidden caves and ruins writes the per-viewer view key showUnexcavated (BCR-V9-20; V04's name; J-V9.38), offered (present and settable) only to a view whose knowledge key is tier secret and whose View as shows everything; to any lower key absent and a stored value reads false; on, S14 draws every element of an unexcavated cluster in V04's unexcavated style (dashed kerbs at 40 % alpha, no fill, no light, only its system's label; V4 §5.2) and the legend adds 'Not yet found by anyone in town'; below secret no sealed void is drawn, labelled, listed (gazetteer, features in view), answered by why (unknown address) or exported (V4 §5.2 knowledge rule; BCR-V9-20 for §11.1); at secret a picture export draws sealed voids only with the view's toggle on; GeoJSON and glTF carry them only at secret (GeoJSON excavation: 'unexcavated'); a VTT scene never (V4 §5.5).

System chip (item 109 (g),(h)): on Below, T4 Tunnel and T6 Chamber show a system chip of the town's underground systems by name and kind ('Old Town — buried town', 'the Catacombs of St Aelred's — catacomb', 'Sewers', 'the Deep Caves — cavern', 'Ruins of Ashkar — ruin'), only those the view's key admits, defaulting to the system under the draft's first point else the last used; below them the new systems item 109 admits at the rung: New ruin and New cavern at every rung (item 109 (j)(1)), New catacomb at TOWN and above (item 109 (k)); a crypt is never a system and never listed (J111); mapper emits drawTunnel {system} or drawChamber {system}; a New pick emits drawChamber {system: {newKind}, …}, a closure (§7.3 item 9) creating the UndergroundSystem with its first chamber (BCR-V9-21): a ruin with RuinRecord of source declared and its plan's axis from the drawn chamber (V4 §4.7); a cavern of the site's geology; a catacomb by 4.17.5's bend ladder; a ruin chamber laid on the ruin's axis (bend.ruin.axis) drawn in V04's ruin program (V4 §5.2), legend 'Ruins of an older town' whenever a ruin element is drawn; re-making a run or system is T10's this run / this system.

How people get down here (item 109 (j)(3),(3b)): panels of an access point, a cavern or ruin cluster, a catacomb and an undercity neighbourhood list one line per way in from AccessPoint.cause (V4 §2.2 AccessCause) of the access or the link it reaches through, worded by info.under.cause.<rule> (V09's words); the access symbol differs by cause (XV-V9-4 asks V04's access row). A void reached only through other systems reads 'Reached through the {system} from {access}' — the path is the excavation reading's connection graph from the nearest surface access (V4 §3.5.7 (g)), returned on the cluster as fact under/wayIn (XV-V9-4); Show the way in highlights every step (live.selection), lists steps with bands, switching the drawn band as the user steps; a sealed void reads info.under.sealed with Add a way down, plus info.under.deep when its top lies deeper than DigRule.maxM below every footprint over it (item 109 (j)(5)).
`dig` — line: "{building} dug a way down when it was built." (with an `event`: "… when it was rebuilt in {year}") — symbol: a stepped arrow [line 2353]

`opening` — line: by kind: "A sinkhole opens here." · "A cave mouth opens here." · "A collapsed shaft leads down here." · "The ruins' old entrance opens here." · "A skylight opens into the cave here." — symbol: a ragged ring [line 2354]
`overlap` — line: "The {system} broke into it in {year}." ("… when it was dug" at generation) — symbol: a broken wall [line 2355]
`mineBreach` — line: "The miners of {working} broke into it." — symbol: a broken wall [line 2356]
`lifeline` — line: "The people below dug this way out to {place}." — symbol: a stair [line 2357]
`edit` — line: "You opened this way down." — symbol: its kind's, with the declared pin [line 2358]
`dossier` — line: "SettlementForge's record puts a way in here." — symbol: its kind's [line 2359]
`crypt` — line: "Reached from {church}'s crypt." (J111) — symbol: an arched door [line 2360]

`system` — line: a catacomb's: "The stair down from {cemetery}." (at V1C-09's opening place, in its chapel where one stands); another system's: "The {system}'s own way in." — symbol: a stair [line 2361]
`neighbourhood` — line: "A street stair down to the {neighbourhood}." — symbol: a stair [line 2362]
`basement` — line: "{building}'s cellar opens into it." — symbol: a stepped arrow [line 2363]
`legacy` — line: "From an older version of the town." — symbol: its kind's [line 2364]

Editing a way down (T9 and T6): Brick it up → setAttr(access, 'state', 'bricked'); Lock it / Open it → state locked / open; Who knows this way down → knownTo chips; dragging its opening → setAttr(access, 'ground.at', p) re-hosted by pointLocate (outside II.7.3's admitted ground the refusal card carries Show me why); dragging its underground end → moveVertex on its access_point vertex; Delete → delete; a change closing a cluster's last way in previews the dwellings that empty (fate.access.lastWay, V04 §4.3) before Accept.

Dwellings only after a way in (item 109 (j)(4) with R2; BCR-V9-22; J-V9.40): a declaration putting dwellings in an unexcavated cluster (T5 quarter or boundary on a void part, T6 placeAt of a dwelling class on a void plot, a clerk proposal of either) is expanded as a closure making the way in: (1) a dug access from the nearest ground building above the cluster (plan distance from the cluster's nearest element to its footprint, ties by address) whose dig floor lies within DigRule.maxM (20 m) of that element's top — cellar_stair or shaft by V4 §3.5.7 (d), source dig, cause edit — bend.under.accessDug; (2) else a public opening at the nearest candidate of V4 §3.5.7 (e)'s kinds, chance waived, cause edit, bend.under.accessOpening; (3) else a public opening of kind collapsed_shaft at the public-ground point (V4 §1.2) over the cluster nearest in plan to its shallowest element, cause edit (file f item 372's note; J-VI.4), bend.under.accessOpening; (4) else (no public ground over it and every footprint beyond DigRule.maxM) the dry run bends the declaration onto ground part 0 over the same footprint (quarter or boundary same outline on part 0; placeAt the part-0 plot), bend.under.noAccess with Add a way down and Show me why (item 101 R2; J-V9.102); way in and dwellings one group, one undo — no dwelling ever stands in a sealed void (T-V9-38).

The bends' alternatives (J-V9.112): with step 1's bend the dry run lists in PreviewResult.alternatives the further buildings step 1 qualifies, in its order, at most three (BCR-V9-22); Use another building is shown while one is untried: re-previews the group [addUndergroundAccess {building}, the declaration] (access first, no target, so BCR-V9-22's grouped-access rule takes the cluster element nearest that footprint and the declaration's closure adds no access), card keeps bend.under.accessDug with {building}; each press steps to the next, button goes when none left; Accept commits one undo step; the clerk's propose carries the same events, one per listed building, labelled 'Dig down from {building} instead' (J-V9.118); steps 2 and 3 run only when no building qualifies, so bend.under.accessOpening offers Show the way in and Show me why.

Catacomb panel (item 109 (k)(1)-(6) as revised ~20:05, J111): name by V04's label (V4 §5.4): 'the Catacombs of {cemetery}', a churchyard's by its church, 'the Ossuary of {quarter}'; 'Under {burial face}' with Show and the source in words ('the churchyard of {church}', 'the burial ground', 'the cemetery outside {gate}', 'the {network} ground outside {gate}', 'the monastery's burial ground', 'an old quarry turned ossuary', 'from an older version of the town' legacy); rank 'The largest catacomb in {town}' at rank 1 else '{n} of {count}'; count by V4 §3.5.1 (3): 'A town has one catacomb.' or '{town} is a city with {churches} churches, so it may have {count} catacombs.' (churches as V04 counts them, a collective record once); with overCount info.catacomb.overCount; entrance 'The stair down from {cemetery}' (V1C-09's opening place, in its chapel where one stands) with Show, other ways by 4.17.3.

Catacomb Over time tab: extent (extentFloorM2, m²) with a line chart per epoch (V06 history frames) whose values never fall (T-V9-34); this epoch's growth vs cap ('grew {a} m² of at most {cap} m²' from lastGrowth.addedM2 and V04's cap); state from blockedBy — growing (empty), stopped (holds sourceClosed; info.catacomb.stopped), stagnant otherwise with each cause in V09's words (info.catacomb.blocked.<cause>): reach 'It has reached as far as its diggers go', wet 'The ground beyond is too wet', system 'Another tunnel is in the way', foundation 'Deep foundations are in the way', wallStrip 'The town wall's footing is in the way', depth 'The rock lies too deep', rank 'It may not outgrow the Catacombs of {largest}'; ossuary fill as a bar captioned info.catacomb.stagnant while stagnant, with a stepper (setAttr fill; lowering allowed and undoable; the next stagnation raises it, V4 §3.5.1 (7)); underground view draws ossuaries denser as fill rises (V4 §5.2).

Crypt on a church's panel: every church-class building's panel has a Below line from Basement.crypt (V03 §3.7.4): 'Crypt, {m²} m²'; cathedral 'Crypt, {m²} m², the largest in {town}' — always present (V02 no-refusal ladder, V2 §3.14.5); V03's wet-ground fold 'floor vaults (wet ground)', V02's raised form 'a raised-choir crypt'; Show opens the plan at the basement storey; with the crypt join (AccessPoint cause crypt) adds 'Opens into the Catacombs of {name}' with Show the way in; a church without a crypt reads 'No crypt' with Add a crypt where its class's crypt column admits one (setAttr of the basement's crypt, V03); a crypt is never listed as an underground system. Cemetery panel (churchyard part, cemetery-class use, Cemetery network ground, monastery burial yard): 'Catacombs below: {name}' with Show and entrance; or 'No catacomb below' with the reason from V04's candidate pass read from the face's why (path catacomb; XV-V9-4): 'the town's one catacomb lies under {other}', '{town} may have {count}, and they lie under {others}', 'the ground is too wet', 'it is younger than a century', 'chance'.

Bends, none refused (R2; J-V9.39) for drawChamber {system: {newKind: 'catacomb'}} via BCR-V9-21's ladder: (a) centroid inside a church-class footprint → setAttr(building, 'basement/crypt/ring', drawn ring clipped to the crypt region), no chamber; a building without a basement gets volume 3's crypt ladder (full, then half, then raised; V03 §4.2, V3C-75), ghost names the form ('a half-sunk crypt under {church}'); one undo; bend.catacomb.church offering 'Start a catacomb under {its churchyard, or the nearest burial face}'; (b) burial face with the count reached → within V04's accessReachM of an existing complex's element it joins (bend.catacomb.join), else a charnel vault (one ossuary chamber of the dug system under that face, capped at charnelMaxM2; bend.catacomb.charnel offering 'Join it to the Catacombs of {name}', a drawTunnel to the complex's nearest element); (c) below TOWN → charnel vault (bend.catacomb.belowTown); (d) no burial face, or a worked-out quarry below CITY → chamber stays as drawn in the dug system (bend.catacomb.noGround offering 'Start it under {nearest burial face}', moving it to that face's centroid; nearest by distance, ties by address); a worked-out quarry at CITY or METROPOLIS within V04's ossuaryReachM is a lawful source (quarry ossuary); (e) crypt edits: removing the cathedral's crypt (setRoomRole away, basement none, a dissolving mergeRooms) bent to keep it at its smallest lawful size (bend.crypt.cathedral); enlarging another church's crypt past the cathedral's clamped just short (bend.crypt.largest offering 'Enlarge the cathedral's crypt too', a two-event group); another church's crypt removable freely, and if it carried the join the fates list 'The way from {church}'s crypt into the catacombs closes.'; V03 computes (e) (XV-V9-5).

Author's removal (item 109 (k)(4); J-V4.56): deleting catacomb galleries is allowed: badge and fates say fate.catacomb.removed, the extent floor drops by the deleted area and deleted nodes are tombstoned (growth never digs them again); undo restores both; a seal keeps the extent ('Sealed galleries stay part of the catacomb.'). Plain words, what it is: 'Assistant (AI)' in the program, the clerk in this design; optional helper in a drawer; four things only: reads the map and answers; explains why anything is where it is (with alternatives considered); builds — turns described towns or pasted lists into the same twelve tools; checks a plan before commit.

Plain words, how it feels: nothing changes the map by itself; every suggestion is a ghost with one line saying what and why, counts of plots, households, buildings, anything moved, and up to three versions; accept, try again or drop; an accepted suggestion is one undo step; follow-ups ('make the lower city denser') are new suggestions; where a rule says no (fixed by SettlementForge or locked) it says so and offers the nearest possible things as buttons.

Plain words, item 110: proposes viaducts, aqueducts on arches, terraces, a fort at a mole's head, stepped tiers exactly as the canvas tools would; explains a generated raised way's reason ('it crosses the gorge, a 34 m drop') and absences ('a town builds them only once it is a city; you may draw one'); before a removal shows every consequence ('the road goes round by the lower bridge; the fountain on the square loses its water'); once accepted the town never builds it back; 'put it back' returns it; never adds a raised way, terrace or retaining wall and never removes anything unless asked.

Plain words, what it never does: never draws a picture — writes only the tools' declarations (movable, reshapable, re-rollable; exports say which parts were drawn, derived or proposed); never invents SettlementForge facts (places what the dossier lists, never adds, removes or renames); never tells a view what it may not know (a player's assistant sees as the player; a secret guild's name never reaches it; a hidden function behind a shop front does not exist for it); a hidden house is 'a building'; unfound caves and ruins do not exist below the GM; View as limits the assistant too; explains the underground (ways down, sealed caves, crypts vs catacombs, stagnating catacombs); answers history questions and distances ('about 340 m by street'); any SettlementForge claim must come from the map, else greyed 'not found on the map'; 'a village' gives a village once that product is installed.

Plain words, turning it on and cost: off until opened, labelled AI everywhere; 'runs on Claude, Anthropic's model, over the internet: in the standalone program you paste your own Anthropic API key (it stays on your machine), or the program that embeds the map — SettlementForge, say — provides the connection, or uses its own assistant instead'; a question costs a few cents, a building request tens of cents; a monthly limit, the drawer shows spend; settings (model, spend) belong to the device, a shared map never changes them; without the assistant every tool and feature works the same. What leaves the machine: messages and a written description of the map filtered to the view's knowledge (district names, landmarks, roads, walls in words and bearings); never the map file, an image, a withheld secret, or the key to anyone but Anthropic (or the chosen host); conversations in memory unless kept; accepted changes live in the map's history.

Turn steps: (1) Gate — enabled, consent set, keyState ok (configuration A) or the host's transport live (B), backend ready, month's spend under cap, role allows the route (a viewer may read and ask why; every declaration tool answers role); otherwise end at once with the matching refusal (offline, key, budget, role). (2) Segment — the route's live segment or a new one (V10 §3.2). (3) Map sync — if logHead moved, describe the change (V10 §3.2). (4) Mode (converse only) — creation when the document holds only its creation prefix and nothing is declared (the untouched empty-state town, R7) or when attach.newMap was sent (V9 §2.10, §4.11; standalone only); otherwise edit; both conditions standalone's: in host mode no turn enters creation mode (XV-V9-22 (c)); the mode is told in the turn's first user message and enforced by the tools. (5) Draft inheritance — a waiting proposal's draft and scratch are inherited ('bigger', 'move it east'), the new proposal supersedes the old (V10 §3.14); a host clerk's waiting proposal is never inherited: a built-in turn supersedes it and tells the host.

Turn step (6) the model loop: request → stream → final message; before anything else the fallback boundary (J-V10.53): when the content holds fallback blocks, every thinking, redacted_thinking and tool_use block before the last one is removed from what is appended (text blocks and everything after the boundary kept; the fallback block itself dropped), and only tool_use blocks after it are calls; each declined attempt recorded in ClerkTurn.declined with its stop_details.category (null when none); then by stop_reason: end_turn finishes; tool_use runs the post-boundary calls and appends the cleaned assistant content and one user message holding every tool_result block, then loops; refusal (the whole fallback chain declined) ends with the model refusal and category; max_tokens and pause_turn follow V10 §3.19; the loop stops at the route's maxCalls, wallClockS, the turn cap in US dollars or the user's Stop. (7) Finalise: grounding check with claims and action steps (V10 §3.13) with at most repairRounds repair requests; proposal assembly when the draft holds an applied item; reply blocks; transcript entry; usage. Progress: one plain line per step — 'Thinking about your request…' when a thinking block starts (display stays omitted); per tool call a fixed line ('Reading the map', 'Looking up why the tannery is there', 'Drafting a quarter', 'Trying the draft on a copy of the map', 'Checking the plan against the rules'); the model's short text between calls; a fallback block withdraws the tool lines announced before it ('Trying again with another model'); the model's thinking is never shown.

Request rendered order and caching (a prefix match: tools, system, messages): (1) tools — the route's tools only (clerk.ops.routes.<route>.tools, J-V10.50) in ToolName's fixed order, schemas byte-stable; each route has its own cached prefix (explain two tools, help one); (2) system — one text block, the rendered prompt, explicit cache breakpoint TTL clerk.ops.cache.staticTtl (tools + system one cached prefix for every request of every segment of the route); (3) messages — the segment's list: its first user message opens with the map block (explicit breakpoint TTL tailTtl), then the fenced vocabulary block when the document or host overrides lexicon rows, then the turn's mode line and the user's words; later turns append; top-level automatic caching moves the third breakpoint along the tail; a longer TTL always precedes a shorter one (static 1h after V10 §6.4's switch, map block and tail 5m); (4) settings: model from clerk.ops; thinking adaptive; output_config.effort pinned per route (never varied inside a segment, grounding repair included); max_tokens per route; streaming; the fallback beta and fallbacks 'default' (or V10 §3.17's transport rule); no sampling parameters, no prefill, no forced tool choice.

Short addresses: ids cross the facade as <docId>/<id> (§11.2); the model sees <id> alone; a scratch carries the same address ids as its source (lineage-derived, §6.3), so one short id names one thing on both; the harness restores the prefix of the targeted document. Map updates between turns: the harness keeps log events appended since the segment last saw the document (subscribe's doc.changed and report.changed); before the next request renders them as a delta — one line per event: kind, target's name and address under the key (withheld by registry kind; an event whose every target is absent, an unexcavated element's among them, left out and uncounted), author (user, clerk, host, epoch) — appended, when ≤ cache.deltaTokenLimit tokens, as a mid-conversation system message after the user's words (keeps the cached prefix); a longer delta closes the segment (delta). Segments close on: prompt reaching cache.segmentTokenLimit (length); a change of the effective key (key); a change of clerk.ops, clerk.content or a vocabulary feeding the tool schemas (tables); a delta over its limit (delta); 'new topic' (user); a new segment opens with a fresh brief and only a harness-written memory block (referents with names key-filtered, one line per earlier turn: outcome and proposal reason), never a model-written summary (J-V10.13).

System prompt: a template in @plat/clerk/model (our words) rendered with the shipped and device layers of clerk.content's lexicon, refusal and family-word rows and the vocabulary names; its bytes depend only on those versions (J-V10.38); sections in order with binding rules: (1) who you are — the map's assistant, labelled AI ('clerk' is internal), plain short answers in the user's language (map names as the map has them), no jargon, one line saying what was done; (2) what you can do — read, explain with why, author with the twelve tools, check with check_draft and critique; no pictures, files, web, changes to SettlementForge; (3) nothing applies until the user accepts — say proposed, never made; (4) declare, then derive — only what was asked, at the shallowest layer; never ask the user for a fact the rules can derive (item 20 (h); J-V10.71); in a new town declare the bones, check_draft, read, then place relative, check again; (5) scoped re-rolls only — never the whole town once anything is declared; new names from name (the whole town only when asked); new compass, emblem, trees or decoration from dress; (6) the dossier is the truth and numbers come from tools — state a dossier fact only by quoting a facts row of tier dossier; state a number, date, year, count or distance only as a tool gave it (measure for distances); never add, remove, rename or re-designate a dossier element — end with [[do:refuse:dossier:<id>]] or [[do:refuse:dossier:count:<id>]] (J-V10.70) or [[do:refuse:dossier]]; with a dossier a roster (and a locus place, a one-line roster) places dossier elements only; a new place of the user's own goes at a point or on a plot.

Vocabulary block (J-V10.38): a document's or host's lexicon rows never enter the system prompt; each row validated by schema (every word 1-40 characters of letters, spaces, hyphens and apostrophes in the user's script; field one of the lexicon's; value within range or enumeration); a failing row dropped and reported in 'What the assistant sees'; kept rows appended after the map block between fences <map-vocabulary> … </map-vocabulary>, one row per line 'words → field = value'; document refusal templates are not used at all. (4) Previews: edit mode each variation dry-run on the user's document preview(h, events, {filtered: true}), the active one with the session's view (ghost drawn); equality check: variation 1's preview (counts, fates by address, created addresses, effects' kinds and counts) must equal what the scratch produced while logHead equals forkHead; a mismatch is a defect: the card shows the user's document's own preview, the reply is marked 'the preview differs from what the assistant saw', a previewMismatch record joins the defect store; when the head moved, the check compares counts, fates and effects' kinds and counts only; creation mode each variation is its scratch town shown read-only under 'Preview — not your map yet' (V09 draws it); (5) reason = the reply's first line trimmed to limits.reasonChars, else 'Proposed: ' and the tools used; (6) the proposal becomes pending; an earlier waiting proposal becomes superseded (a host's answered clerk.proposal {status 'dropped'}). Acceptance V10 §4.2; dropping closes the scratch; retry drops the waiting proposal (not inherited) and starts a new turn with the user's last words and the note 'the user asked for another attempt; the previous proposal was: {reason}; propose a different approach'.

Staleness: while a proposal waits, subscribe watches the document; when logHead moves (user edit, host dossier event, another client's edit) every variation is re-previewed at the new head with placeholders re-resolved: if counts, fates, effects' kinds and counts and the resolved created addresses' kinds are unchanged, it keeps waiting under the new baseLogHead; otherwise stale — variations hold the fresh previews, baseLogHead the new head — and the card shows V9 §4.9's refuse.stale row (one sentence for one condition on canvas and clerk, J-V10.94) with its two buttons Show the new preview (runs focus on the active variation) and Show me why (a why of the row's page), beside Ask again (retry, clerk.alt.stale.retry; a new turn noted 'the map changed after the previous proposal: {reason}; propose again on the current map'); a host's card shows refuse.stale and its two buttons alone, answered when it closes; a variation whose events now conflict is removed; a proposal left with none fails with its conflicts shown as refusals.

ColumnSpec {name (dotted field path), row? (settings form row name), type number / integer / bool / string / enum / ref / range / weights / list / object, unit (m / m2 / ha / cm / cdeg / share / weight / people / yr / wk / m3 / lvl / none), range?, enumValues?, ref? (target TableId, value must be a live row key), interp band / step / none (band: interpolated along prosperity between band rows §4.5; step: switches at cut), calibratable, extensionAllowed, presetsRequired?, sumsTo? {group, total, tolerance}}.

Numeric edit outside a column's declared range is clamped to the nearer bound and the editor says so in one line ('set to 3, the most this column allows'; item 101 R2); only a dangling ref or a type error is refused, F-EDIT (§5.2), naming the rule.

presetsRequired: a categorical option cell is refused without a value for each zeroing parity preset whose file ships on the tables that preset requires: MFCG and FTG on every table; VG (from V07 V-M0) only on a table whose readers include a stage ProductDecl('village').stages registers (conditional registrations included; manifest productStages.village); other tables carry no VG entry and under VG resolve to their MFCG entry; NG on no table (resolves as MFCG does).

sumsTo: weights that must sum (a class's powers, sectors; a cover row's weights need not). TotalityRule {kind coversEnum / coversTable / coversManifest, column, of (enum name, TableId, or manifest list 'sf.catalogue@<line>', 'sf.archetypes@<line>'), allowFallback? (row key a miss resolves to, reported)}: a coverage promise compiler checks and CI holds (T-V11-2).

TableSchema {id, file (shipped path under plat/packages/tables/dist/), rowType, key (composite joined by '/'), columns, readers (invalidation map of §7.6; stage readers by StageId: S0-S15 with S5 a group expanded to S5a-S5d; volume ids S7c, S8.seed, S9b (V01), SKY (V05), U-NET, U-SYS, U-ACCESS, U-FRONT, U-CITY, U-LINK, U-RECONCILE, U-FADE (V04), VS1-VS6, VS8 (V07), EVO_PRELUDE..EVO_RAISED (V06 §3.16); module ids only for readers outside the stage graph: @plat/app, @plat/clerk, @plat/docs, @plat/sim, port.digest, tables.compiler, derivePerson (§10.3), rung.wings, rung.plan (V02 §3.1), testkit.bench, @plat/hood (V01 §3.8)), sliceKinds, rowsHome, owner base / V01..V11, parity zeroExtensions / perPreset / untouched, packPatchable (SettingPack rosterPatch/tablePatch §10.4), totality, version (semver: major changed schema, minor declared output shift, patch no output change)}.

Compiler tells stage readers from module readers by the source manifest's stageIds (§3.2.1 step 1); village-read test (step 4), V12 run scope and cost shortcut (V12 §3.7.2 (4), §3.7.7) match StageIds only (J-V11.80).

@plat/tables exports REGISTRY: ReadonlyMap<TableId, TableSchema>, one entry per row of §3.1's catalogue, read by compiler, loader, tables editor, docs generator, provenance audit; a table not in the registry cannot be loaded, patched or edited (loader refuses, F-EDIT); a registry entry without its file fails the build.

Every registry row exists from C0: a row whose rows-home milestone has not landed ships its schema's empty table (rows 0 in manifest), status column unchanged ('written (Vnn)' names the writer, not shipment); compiler holds an empty table's TotalityRules and row invariants from the change shipping its first row; the landing milestone's tests read them so a table still empty past that milestone fails there; a reader meeting an empty table reads no rows, as readers of a staged row read its absent input (row 32) (J-V11.84).

Settings form (roster.settings, raisedWays settings and structure, retaining settings, V01 hood.constants; J-V11.96): beside keyed rows a table may hold single rows named by a fixed key (settings, structure) whose fields are no column of the keyed rows; each field is a ColumnSpec whose row names that row, nested by dotted name (span.maxHeightCm, span.vaultShare.viaduct), with own unit, range, calibratable, extensionAllowed; so every settings cell is a column a V12 register entry names (V12 §3.11) and the editor edits as a cell; key column admits the named keys; a named row holds exactly the columns whose row names it and a keyed row none (T-V11-3); a table that is only a settings row keys that row 'settings'.

Authoring source: JSON5 files, one per row group, under plat/packages/tables/src/<table-id-with-slashes>/; SourceFile {$table, $defaults {provenance, calibratable?} cascading to every cell unless overridden, rows}; SourceRow {key, $extends? (template-family or profile-family row key of the same kind; cells inherited, row overrides), $provenance?, fields}.

Ladder step types (dossier.ladders; item 108): source ladder and subsumption are SF's own pairs as g quotes them (provenance sf:institutionLadders.js@5d699cc68, BCR-V11-21, owner's own program); inferred pairs read from the catalogue's tier names and re-checked by V08 against the ladder file when the port reads it (V08 §3.5; a disagreement is a table fix, reported); an unnumbered COUNT, QUARTER or GUILD record's member range = range column = value at kind's lowest tier; rungScale multiplies it only above that tier ({CITY 2, METROPOLIS 3} TOWN kind, {METROPOLIS 1.5} CITY kind, none METROPOLIS kind; multiple_court_buildings (M) yields 4-10 at METROPOLIS, never 16-40); at a village rung an unnumbered record takes V07 §2.4's range row (village.json rules.ladders.ranges) by V08 §3.5.1 (b) (keyed by step type and the class playing the member class; J-V7.105) else this range unscaled; every member count is S2's per-capita count clamped into the range (108 (b)); a numbered record's own range wins.

A COUNT whose member is a pin (@pin:<kind>) sets a floor only: members = max(range low end, the pin's own coverage count at the rung: V07 §3.10 well rows at village rungs, §4.7 furniture step at base rungs), never clamped to the range top (J-V11.61); SIZE's factor multiplies template footprint and plot budget, sigma's rank and, for a crypted class, cryptM2; identity names the QuarterIdentityRow a QUARTER record claims (T-V11-2); rows never calibrated (range, rungScale, sizeFactor, inferred rows included, §13.9 (7)); a change is a table fix reviewed with V08.

Step semantics: a kind absent from the table is no step; a COUNT's members keyed #k (J-A74.73); a QUARTER record owns its district's members of the class and, by the class's ordinary spread (item 107), members outside it; a GUILD record is one guildhall plus a collective of the trade's members tied to it, its hall bound into a guild COUNT record of the same dossier by V08 §3.5.1 (c) family rule (J-V8.83), never a further hall (108 (c)); SIZE is one building; REPLACEMENT keeps only the greater (108 (a)); no double counting (108 (c)); cemetery_network members are burial faces (V04 §3.5.1 candidates; at METROPOLIS the first in the catacomb order, §3.23.8).

Burial ladder across 1 500 people: burial_ground (T, H) -> graveyard (V) -> parish_burial_grounds (W, a COUNT of church plots' churchyards) -> burial_grounds_and_charnel_house (C, SIZE); a tier change is never a closure: V08 §2.6a (4) re-binds the lesser's face to the greater's key (churchyard keeps lineage and opening year, which V07 §3.12 step 6 carries across the hand-off); no churchyard bound to two records.

V08's re-check against the ladder file (V08 §3.5.1 (f), V08 §13 X1) applied: file rows are ladder or subsumption; hospital_network's and dungeon_delving_supply_district's lessers are the file's; file pairs added as rows (parish_church, multiple_water_sources, theaters, wizard_s_tower, mages_guild, caravan_masters_exchange, major_hospital's almshouse); rows the file lacks but dossiers carry in both forms stay inferred (108 (c) must merge them). Conventions: 'the base' is ARCHITECTURE.md with amendments c, d, e folded in and g items 102-110 (with J110's refinements, J111's crypt and catacomb switch, item 110 (J115) and its raised-ways revision (J116)) as the coherence pass applies them; § points into the base, 'V12 §' into this volume, 'V0n §' into another volume; ids BCR-V12-n (§10), J-V12.n (§9), T-V12-n (§7), Q-V12-n (§11); V12 is an implementer input under §17.1 (1): names no reference class, method, grammar, palette or asset; reference evidence cited by file and section only; every number quoted from a capture is a measured behaviour (§17.1 (6)); the corpus was not read: machinery and process designed from partitioned/README.md's rules alone.

Plain words: V12 sets the rule tables' numbers right and proves it against other generators (MFCG, FTG, Neighbourhood, Village Generator, Fantasy Manor) and later the owner's historical map collection, never changing how the generator works; four loops: (1) measuring references on towns whose seeds were fixed by formula before capture; only numbers cross into the product folder; (2) measuring ours with the very same code; every number has a band by one rule; nightly report 'in band', 'out of band', 'for information'; (3) tuning: a table value changed (never code) by a recorded search on practice towns, checked on a held-out set; each change a new table version declared in release notes; saved towns open exactly as made; (4) the owner's eye: sitting page at each big milestone, pairs ours vs reference, sides hidden, three questions per pair (easier to read, more like a real town, rather use), about 35-45 minutes, can be split; only the owner's answers let a milestone say 'at parity' or 'mastered'.

Plain words: tendencies not guarantees: the harness proves each leaning by counting over many practice towns (rank vs the same town shuffled at random, ties broken by a fair coin; counting members exactly; watching a rate climb as towns grow), rules worked out beforehand so chance almost never passes and a real leaning almost always does; a failing bar re-runs once on fresh towns before anything changes; where the owner's volume states how a bar passes, that wins. Owner's rules stay the owner's (catacomb only under a cemetery, cathedral always crypted, raised ways only in cities): no tuning, fallback or historical map moves them; a historical counter-example goes to the owner as a question with 'keep the rule'; catacombs checked never to shrink on every rebuild (epoch, regeneration, re-derive, New random, upgrade) and to fill ossuaries when they cannot grow.

Plain words: later the historical maps adjust default numbers and bands, never machinery; one historical example proves possible, never common; only a fair pre-chosen sample of measured plans says how common; collection teaches drawing, never naming; its 53 held-back plates never used; MFCG and FTG behaviour stays exactly reachable through the parity presets; historical values arrive as a 'historical' layer and the owner decides at a before-and-after sitting whether it becomes default. Baseline row: rows.py + crossing; read parity, calibrate, check; persist baselines.json; never re-computed in place (a new metric version or build adds a superseding row); undo supersession; migrate schema bump with converter in plat baselines check --migrate. ReferencePin: baseline seat at M-1; pin change back is a new declared baseline shift. ParityReport: plat parity; persist plat/goldens/parity/ (milestone), CI artifacts (nightly); re-run same bytes (§3.13). CalibrationRun: plat calibrate run; read register, compiler (evidence), release notes; persist plat/calibration/runs/; re-running reproduces every evaluation (T-V12-8); undo a revert run restoring from values, itself declared.

Lifecycle CalibrationEntry: created by the seat landing a volume's constant, or §13.7's letter; default line's by plat calibrate register --defaults --milestone <id>; read milestone exits, docs, editor, clerk; persist register.json; statuses recomputed from history by --check; --defaults writes only columns holding a compiled cell and no entry (idempotent), each with a first history row naming the landing milestone and its due from it; a value moved by its owning seat before its due appends one cells row to its provisional not-yet-due default entry or named entry whose cells no run may name; rows a later landing adds append one cells row to any entry; a tuning the golden check refused appends a held row by --hold; --check fails an entry whose last cells row differs from its target's compiled cells or lacks a compiled row key; staged entry's exit and sitting rows advance its stage; undo: history rows appended never removed; a later named line restates a default entry in place (line dropped); migrate: entry without line reads as named; row without cells reads as metrics, panel or status row; entry without stages reads single-stage; row without stage or held reads as before.

The loop at a glance: research side (reads captures; never ships): capture plan -> captures (profiler tools; FTG one per day) -> adapters -> MeasureInput -> plat measure (product code run research-side) -> per-seed rows -> plat baselines aggregate -> rows.py -> candidate baselines.json -> plat baselines check (C1-C10) + checker seat => numbers only => baselines.json -> plat parity -> ParityReport -> out of band -> plat calibrate run (train/holdout) -> table versions, shift records, goldens; panel assembly: renders from plat + reference images -> sitting page -> owner -> answers.json => answers, hashes => plat d5 verdict -> D5Record; corpus (M-CAL only): adapter -> MeasureInput -> plat measure -> frame rows => baselines.json (corpus rows) -> corpus runs -> reconciled preset layer -> sitting M-CAL -> release; the product never reads the research side; research may run the product's released CLI (§13.3); every crossing arrow is a numbers-only file passing §3.3.

MFCG stress settings exist at size 80 only, so B-REF runs no MFCG coast+river town at TOWN or METROPOLIS; the M1 panel's MFCG coast+river pairs take their own exports per rung (§3.9.1), feeding no row; panels' reference identifiers (fm-captures.json, dw-captures.json, vg-seeds.json; numbers and ids only) written research-side by plan.py and cross by §3.3 into plat/goldens/d5/<panel>/, read by plat d5 seeds (BCR-V12-8).

Adapters (research/baselines/adapters/<ref>.py -> inputs/<ref>/<build>/<capture>.metric.geojson): MFCG: JSON export in metres; each exported road a way of class arterial; each footprint and prism a building of class unknown; first wall polygon the city's enclosure and curtain, second the castle curtain and a castle feature; gates are city ring vertices touching a road vertex less those shared with the castle ring (class land); district, square, green, field polygons, river centrelines (with river width), pier segments, sea polygon mapped; shore split (106): ring edges whose two vertices lie on the sea polygon boundary within 0.5 m become closure features class shore, rest stays curtain, ring stays enclosure; ring vertex on a river centreline is a gate of class water; towers are castle ring non-gate vertices plus city ring vertices neither gate, castle-shared, nor inside a shore closure; lanes not exported (lane metrics read the derived street graph §3.4.1). FTG: road graph main -> arterial, district -> street, suburb -> lane; footprints; wall chains and tower points; fields; water outlines; cm to m; no plots (item 49). NG: blocks, lots, buildings from vertex captures, relative; bent-cut signature values are §13.5's recorded measurements entered as trace rows. VG: V07 §7 features; FM: counts file.

Measuring with one implementation: at M-1 seats measure with research-side scripts written from §3.4's definitions (red-team scripts of docs/validation/bench/README.md as starting point); from M1 plat measure is the one implementation: research re-runs every baseline through the released CLI on the same MeasureInput files; T-V12-3 holds the two within each metric's tolerance; where they differ, the seat finds the wrong definition and the product's value replaces the M-1 row as a superseding row with a declared baselineShift (§13.3) naming the metric (J-V12.1); a render metric (recoverability) keeps §16 M-1's cross-check within 0.01 on M1's golden renders; T-V12-3 and T-V12-6 read captures so are research-side checks (check_t3.py, check_t6.py running the released CLI), verdicts reach MilestoneRecord.exitCriteria as evidence strings naming output hash; nothing under plat/ reads a capture (§17.1 (3); T-V12-28).

Writing rows: plat measure writes per-seed values; plat baselines aggregate (product code run research-side) forms each row's values by §3.5.1's estimator and for distribution rows spreadKS; rows.py adds §13.5 provenance (referenceBuild, capture, script, date), sample block, role from §13.5 or the owning volume; script and capture written as research:-prefixed opaque labels (research:baselines/adapters/mfcg.py) the product never resolves (C2).

The crossing: plat baselines check <file> [--previous] runs on every candidate numbers-only file before commit (baselines.json, ftg-captures.json, ng-counts.json, fm-captures.json, dw-captures.json, vg-seeds.json, a panel's answers.json and key.json after reveal, the corpus's frames.json; BCR-V12-8 adds the new ones to §17.1 (4)); until M1 its twin research/baselines/cross_check.py applies the same rules, M1's first product run re-validates the M-1 file (T-V12-1). Checks (each refused on failure): C1 schema (zod plat.baselines/2, §13.6 (9) types); C2 strings (id, metric, supersedes ^[a-z0-9.:/@+_-]{1,120}$; sample.family, sample.captures[], panel seed labels and reference ids ^[A-Za-z0-9.:/@+_-]{1,120}$; builds ^[A-Za-z0-9._:+-]{1,64}$; dates ISO 8601; capture folder name or research: label; script ^research:[a-z0-9_./-]{1,160}$; any other string field refused); C3 notes (<= 200 chars of letters, digits, spaces, .,;:()-/%±≤≥×, passes the scanner); C4 colours (no six-hex-digit sequence); C5 numbers finite, units in the closed list; C6 metrics exist at the row's metricVersion; C7 samples (registered capture/ family, indices from 0; FTG captures equal plan slots in order; panel FM, DW, VG references the plan's in order); C8 corpus (reference corpus:frame:<id> or corpus:map:<16 hex>; evidence present; a target row is a frame row with frameN >= 20 and evidence surveyed; frame in frames.json by an EARLIER CrossingRecord with equal n and digest; no other corpus string); C9 append-only (no row removed or changed; replaced row kept and named by supersedes); C10 scan (§17.1 (5) scanner over the whole file: 0 hits).

A passing file is committed by the baseline seat (research tier) and countersigned by a checker seat reading only the candidate file, the check output and metrics.json (never captures), appending a CrossingRecord; what never crosses whatever the check says: images, geometry, names, colours, a reference's option names beyond numbers and flags, any corpus string other than our D-2 preset keys (J-V12.2).

Two derived features for sources lacking them (MFCG exports no blocks or lanes; a corpus plate may show buildings only): cluster blocks: footprints whose rings lie within g of each other join one cluster (g = 1.0 m metric, 2% of median footprint short side relative); outline = union closed by dilation then erosion of 3 m (metric) or 10% of that short side (relative); derived street graph: inside the outermost curtain (or built area's outline) the complement of cluster blocks reduced to its straight skeleton (§3.8 kernel), spurs < 8 m (metric) or 40% of median short side (relative) pruned, nodes within 2 m merged; a metric reading blocks or lanes on MFCG reads these and the same metric on our side reads the same derivation from our footprints (never true blocks) (blockc.*, sgd.*); our true blocks and ways feed rows whose reference has them (J-V12.5).

Catalogue conventions: where the base defines a measure the row cites it; m = metric scale needed, f = scale-free; every wall row reads the §2.2 enclosure (item 106): inside the outermost curtain = inside the outermost enclosure; curtain ring's area = enclosure's area; along-curtain distances along built stretches only, never across a closure edge (a condition run's end is no stretch end); a main gate is a gate of class land (a water gate, a harbour-mouth chain included, never counts).

Default rules: absFloor shares, ratios, rank statistics 0.02; angles 1 deg; lengths 2% and areas 5% of reference median; densities 5% of it; counts 0.5; Moran's I and Spearman 0.05; entropies 0.05 bits; timings 5%; sign any for Moran's I, Spearman, z, signed angles, positive otherwise; distribution bins: areas log-spaced 24 bins (blocks 50-50 000 m2; buildings 10-2 000 m2; plots 20-5 000 m2) with underflow and overflow; run lengths 5 m bins to 400 m; NN distances 0.25 m bins to 30 m; widths 0.25 m bins to 30 m; tolerance geo, model, trace, counts 1e-9 relative, render 0.01 absolute, M-1 twin comparison 0.5% relative or one unit of last printed digit; stages: ways S3, S4, S5, S8; walls, towers, gates, castle, closures, enclosures S3-S5; districts and squares S3, S6-S7b; blocks S8-S9; plots S8-S10; buildings S10-S11; water, river, pier S1 and S3; green, field, tree S12-S12a; galleries and chambers the underground stages (II.7); retaining walls S10-S11; raised parts, supports, spans S4-S6 (viaducts S4, elevated roads and aqueducts end of S6).

Estimators: a reference's per-seed statistics s1..sn give spread [a, b] and centre c (median): n = 1 -> a = b = c (single); 2 <= n < 10 -> [min, max] (minmax); n >= 10 -> p10 and p90 by linear interpolation (Hyndman and Fan type 7); with n i.i.d. draws [min, max] covers on average (n - 1)/(n + 1) (0.82 at n = 10), so at ten seeds the two aim at the same interval as §13.5's [p10, p90] (J-V12.3).

Scalar target bands: positive metric: lo = min(a x 0.9, c x 0.85), hi = max(b x 1.1, c x 1.15) (union of §13.5's rule and its single-value +-15%; n = 1 reduces exactly to §13.5's single-value rule); then lo <= c - absFloor and hi >= c + absFloor enforced; sign any: w = max(b - a, absFloor), lo = a - 0.1 w, hi = b + 0.1 w; ours = median of our per-seed statistics; a target row passes when lo <= ours <= hi (J-V12.6).

Distribution target bands: reference seed-to-seed spread = p90 (type 7) of two-sample KS distances over its n(n - 1)/2 seed pairs (n = 2 the one value); ours = median over every (our seed j, reference seed i) pair of KS(tj, si); row passes when ours <= 1.25 x that spread (J-V12.7); at n = 1: ceiling = KS critical value c(0.01) x sqrt((n1 + n2)/(n1 n2)), c(0.01) = 1.628, n1 the one reference seed's element count, n2 our median-sized seed's.

Weakness, descriptive and declared exceptions: a weakness row compares ours (median) with its one-sided bound and margin as §13.5 states; a descriptive row is reported and gates nothing; a row whose band §13.5 or a volume declares as an exception (organic turning's 0.5-1.5 x FTG; V02's chi-square and KS clauses for FM's small sample) carries that band as band.override and the report prints 'declared exception'.

J-V12.1: chose one implementation of every metric — the product's plat measure, run research-side on reference and corpus inputs from M1, the M-1 scripts kept only as cross-checked twins — over separate research-side and product-side implementations, because a definition that drifts between the two sides is the silent way a parity number lies

J-V12.2: chose a MeasureInput of numbers, geometry and closed vocabularies only — no names, label text, colours or styles — over carrying names for traceability, because names are creative content the firewall and the corpus's "drawing, never naming" rule both keep out, and the salted ids trace a row well enough

J-V12.3: chose ten reference seeds per matched MFCG size with the min–max estimator below ten seeds and type-7 quantiles from ten, over §13.5's five seeds, because [min, max] of ten draws covers 0.82 of the spread on average — the intent of [p10, p90] — while five cover only 0.67, and the extra exports cost minutes

J-V12.4: chose seed families derived by H32 from structured labels, with a priority-ordered rehash on collision and B-CITY and the goldens formula-derived too, over stored seed lists, because a formula is a pre-registration anyone can recompute from text, and disjoint families keep tuning off the test seeds

J-V12.5: chose to derive cluster blocks and a street graph from footprints alone, identically on ours, for rows whose reference lacks blocks or lanes, over comparing our true blocks with MFCG's reconstructions, because only the same derivation on both sides compares like with like

J-V12.6: chose the scalar band as the union of §13.5's multiplicative band and the ± 15 % single-value band, additive for sign-indefinite metrics and floored by absFloor, over the multiplicative band alone, because a narrow reference spread would otherwise give a band narrower than a single value's, and a zero-centred metric has no multiplicative band

J-V12.7: chose the KS rule as the median of single-seed-against-single-seed distances compared with the reference's pairwise p90, over pooled-against-pooled distances, because the reference's spread is measured seed against seed, and pooling shrinks a distance and flatters ours

J-V12.8: chose the MFCG settings' population as the one whose expected non-hinterland building count equals the reference's median building count — 3.4 persons per building ÷ (1 − the hinterland share measured on B-CITY-lite), solved per rung at each milestone — over the rungs' target populations or 3.4 × the whole count, because §13.6 (3) matches building counts, MFCG exports no farmsteads, and a population off by a third, or by the hinterland's share, would compare towns of different sizes
